product_reviews: ['    Valium is something that probably everyone has heard about but many maynot know the significance of it s usage and effects, whether in the positive or in the negative.Valium is a brand of company called Roche. The only ingredient is a drug called Diazepam. Other brands are also available and they all contain exactly the sameformulation ie. Diazepam.Diazepam is most commonly found in tablet form. However it is also available in capsule, liquid, suppositories and injection forms.It belongs to the group of drugs known as benzodiazepine and it has a wide range of uses. It helps to relieve nervousness and tension, will relax muscles and promote sleep. It can also be used as a muscle relaxant in the treatment of alcohol withdrawal and the relief of epileptic seizures.My experience with Diazepam began after I had a car accident two years ago in West Africa. Due to that accident I broke two ribs, ruptured my chest muscle, cut my head and broke my front tooth.I was prescribed first and foremost a medication called Dyclophenic Acid tablets (Dyclophenac), which was to reduce the intolerable pain that I was suffering from immediately after the accident. Even after taking these tablets I was still in severe pain and found it extremely difficult to sleep because any small movements would send a chilling pain straight through my chest. My doctor thus prescribed diazepam tablets to be taken three times a day. 5mg in the morning, 5mg in the afternoon and 10mg at night.I went through with this dosage for one week and started reducing the dosage on the second week by discontinuing with the 5mg in the afternoon.What I can say from personal experience is that this drug did help me tremendously in sleeping. It is basically a tranquilizer and thus induces a very heavy sleep. This basically numbs the nervous system thus allowing you not to experience your pain.However after 3 weeks of taking diazepam my doctor recommended that I try to discontinue them and see how I felt and if I experienced any sleeping problems. That very night I could not sleep. Nor could I sleep for the next night. Basically my body had become so addicted to diazepam in just three weeks.I worked in a pharmacy in West Africa for 2 years and I know that if I gave up and tried not to fight this addiction it would overwhelm me and I might be addicted for a very long time to come. Also knowing fully well that now was the easiest time to try and break the chain and the longer I waited the more difficult it would become to break.I therefore persisted and withheld my temptation to take diazepam. On the fifth day, after discontinuing it, I got an almost perfect sleep.Overall I can only say that diazepam does have its positive usages, as in my case, but the problem with this drug is that it is so easy to get addicted. My advice would be to try your best not to take this over long periods of time and make your fears, about addiction, known to your GP. It may be possible that he could prescribe something less powerful and therefore less effective, but at the same time less addictive and overall more beneficial to you. After all you wouldn  8217;t want to get over one sickness to find yourself overwhelmed with an addiction of sorts.So all of you out there who use Valium (Diazepam) please be careful.     ', '    My husband used to suffer from dandruff, quite badly in fact. Some days he would have a mini snowstorm build up on his shoulders. And being so dark haired, you couldn  8217;t fail to notice it and it wasn  8217;t really the image he wanted to portray to his new bosses He tried a variety of treatments and specialist shampoos, none really seemed to give long lasting results, the dandruff would be better but would never disappear altogether.He tried Head and Shoulders a few months ago and was quite impressed. Yes, it did remove the dandruff, totally and permanently, and flaky white bits are now a thing of the past. But, and it  8217;s a very BIG but, the shampoo was incredibly harsh on his hair.  So harsh that it seemed to strip his hair of it  8217;s natural shine and body and left it looking dry, lifeless and incredibly dull. The whole texture of his hair has changed, from its usual silky feel to the feel of dry straw. He also suffers from a very itchy scalp and I  8217;m guessing that the chemicals within the shampoo must be fairly strong, or maybe he is just a little allergic to some of the ingredients.The dandruff had disappeared and thankfully seems to be making no effort to come back. So the shampoo does what it says it will on the bottle, it WILL clear your dandruff once and for all. But at what cost? He now has to use gallons of conditioner each time he washes his hair to try and restore some of the shine and softness, but his hair has never felt the same since. And being one who loves to run her fingers through his hair, I too notice the difference. So do I recommend this shampoo? Yes, as a treatment against dandruff, I would say it is the most effective on the market but as a general hair cosmetic shampoo in itself; it just doesn  8217;t do it for me. If you  8217;re as unlucky as Mark, it will strip your hair of all its natural bounce, sheen and vitality. Be wary would be my advice.      ', '    Head and shoulders. How do I loathe this product? Let me count the ways.....During my teens, I, like most of my peers suffered from derranged hormones, unruly skin, spots, dandruff and about anything else that can go wrong. I tried al sorts of shampoos, (although with hindsight I think my dandruff was largely stress induced.)nothing worked, some of them made it worse. I tried head and shoulders then, I ve tried it once since.From the moment you open the bottle, head and shoulders (sorry, but I don t feel it deserves capital letters) it smells chemically. Now, I know most shampoos have icky man made substances in, but its nice if they at least try to mask the smell. This shampoo smells like you could probably disinfect  toilets with it. The only shampoos that smell significantly worse are the ones you have to use to get rid of nits. (another bad memory from teenage years.)Head and shoulders does not get rid of nits however - somehow they are able to survive it.Whilst washing my hair with as little of it as possible, it isn t too bad, appart from the smell. I then get about an hour of reasonably clean hair, and gradually the itching starts. Within three or four hours my scalp is sore, reddenned, itchy and it is as much as I can do not to try and pull my skin off.  By the next day, my skin responds by producing as much oil as it can to protect itself from the shampoo. Result - very oily hair. Oh, and if anything, it made the dandruff worse than it was before I started.I have asked around, being curious (and wanting to know if I m some sort of freak.) My bloke tells me he can only use head and shoulders occasionally or it upsets his scalp as well. My mother and grandmother apparently have both used it and experienced hair loss as a direct result. So far I have not found anyone who likes this product. My suspcion is that its too strong for everyday use, too strong for most skin types as well. It doesn t do much for the condition of your hair, and frankly I can think of little that would recomend it. If you have tried every other anti dandruff product available and none of them have worked, you might want to try this, but until then, I really wouldn t.     ', '    Scrub a dub dub for very clean squeaky hair is my motto.  The shampoo market is littered with many top quality products.  If your girly then (in best Divid Ginola accent)  because I m worth it  Loreal is probaly your kind of thing.  Kid even have the glamourised Johnsons no more tears range with very succelent apple smelling shampoos.I previously had used Pantene pro v with conditioner as it left my hair very soft and had a nice tangy smell to it which stayed on without disappering the next day.  That is until I discovered, well maybe not discovered but decided to try it, Head   Shoulders.  H S did something that my trusty Pantene didn t do it actually made my hair feel cleaner with a louder squeak effect after cleaning.With Pantene although it left my hair nice and soft it would feel very greasy again as soon as I went out, even with multiple lathers.  With H S the feeling of greasiness was eradicated until the next night when I would wash again anyways.I m not going to bore you with the ingredients as this is a op not a fact telling extravaganza so for you interested freaks out there I suggest you read the packaging.  Which leads me on nicely to the packaging side of the Procter   Gamble product.  Head   Shoulders is packaged in a white shampoo bottle, in either a small, medium or large size.  The design is a cool blue streak with coll writing on it.  Not overly impressive but you hardly buy shampoo for the packaging, its the contents that count.More on the actual product itself, as I said wih some lathering and rinsing Head   Shoulders will leave your hair squeaky clean.  The smell of the product is not as vibrant as Pantene but its still a refreshing and clean fragrant.  After washing and rinsing your hair will sometimes feel a bit dry even though the shampoo has a conditioner as a 2in1 combo.  Thats the only quibble I have with Head   Shoulders, it could leave the hair soft like Pantene, but instead it feels kind of wirery and stiff.  The shampoo is also good for dandruff sufferers, so thats a plus, the menthol fragrant is very strong and nice as well, so be on the lookout of the variety you have at your disposal.However don t let that put you off as Head   Shoulders will leave you satisfied.     ', '    Head   Shoulders - remember the adverts - the guy with huge flakes of dandruff on the shoulders of his suit - looked like ash from a volcano  Marvellous  However I do have a more interesting story to share...I have used this since I was a kid and it is true - it does exactly what it says. It reduces and gets rid of dandruff with ease. As long as you follow the instructions and use it on a regular basis.Lets get the shop-talk out of the way It comes in various sizes. I can just use one shampoo to bath n  shower n  wash my hair in when I need to Now all I need is an all-over conditioner to be extra shiney with added bounce (Mmmmmmmm ? ? )D :)     ', '    A few years ago I had a snowflake problem and I tried this shampoo. I thought the smell was awful but figured who cares as long as it works.Nice blue color and lathers nice so this is a plus in my book and the price was comparable to similar products.I used several bottles of this and yes it took away the flakes but I didn t like the smell of my hair as that medicine smell stayed with me.It did however give my hair body so another plus.I guess the only bad thing I can say about it is the smell.Do I stil use it? ', '    This is the best anti-dandruff shampoo on the market in my opinion, it cannot be beaten. ', '    Now, I   m going to let you in on a secret, but first you   ve got to promise me two things.  First of all, please don   t laugh, this really isn   t a funny subject.  Secondly, you can   t tell anyone, and I mean anyone about this.  Not you spouse, lover, mother, dog and certainly not Mrs. Smythe from No. 36, she   d have it spread around the world quicker than Concorde can fly.  No doubt she   d post the story on one of those damned opinion websites, and then where would my reputation be?  In tatters So, will you promise me?OK, then I   ll tell you, I suffer from dandruff.Oi   Stop sniggering, I thought you promised me you wouldn   t laugh.  Really, it   s not a funny subject, I try and take pride in my appearance and it   s not as if I don;t wash my hair everyday.  I use good quality shampoos and conditioner, I rinse my head thoroughly after washing it, yet still when I run my fingers through my hair I   m in danger of causing snowdrifts in the middle of June   Believe me, that is quite embarrassing.  Well, I suppose it gives Railtrack a better excuse than leaves on the line, they can just blame me for sticking my head out of the window and causing a blizzard Anyway, as I   ve said, it   s a bit of an embarrassing problem, especially as I do all I can to try and ensure I don   t get dandruff.  But what exactly is dandruff?  Well, if you already know or don   t really care, I   d skip this big, I try and make things as humorous as I can but it   s a bit tricky when it comes to the science.  So if facts bore you (I try never to let them get in the way of a good story )  I   d skip the next couple of paragraphs.  But it you want to become a dandruff anorak, then read on.....*******So, what is dandruff?  Well, contrary to popular belief it   s not just a dry scalp.  OK, a dry scalp will make your head a little bit on the flaky side, but although it looks similar it   s not technically dandruff.   Dandruff is really a chronic scalp condition characterised by excessive flaking of the scalp and is also associated with itching and redness of the scalp.  The keyword here is    excessive   .  Everyone   s head sheds skin in much the same way as your body is continually shedding skin.  Around 80  of all dust in your house will be made up of dead skin cells, nice thought eh   People with dandruff suffer from an accelerated rate of skin shedding from the head, resulting in noticeable flakes of skin, or dandruff.  The flakes from dandruff tend to be a little bit bigger than those from a person with just a dry scalp, they are white in colour and slightly oily looking as opposed to the smaller, drier flakes from a person with a dry scalp condition.  Don   t they both sound really attractive  So, I   ve educated you in what exactly dandruff is, I   m sure you   ll sleep easier tonight now you know, but what causes it?  Well, I can give you a fascinating insight into that too It is thought dandruff is caused by a fungus found on nearly everyones  scalp called Malassezia (try saying that when you   ve had a pint or two ).  This fungus munches away on the natural oils found in your scalp and can create byproducts and acid that in some people irritate the scalp and speed up the shedding of those dead skin cells.  Everyone   s tolerance to this fungus is different, those people with a lower tolerance are more inclined to suffer from dandruff.  Unfortunately, I must have a low tolerance to that greedy little bugger, hence I suffer from dandruff.I   m in good company though, as it   s estimated that dandruff and dry scalp condition will affect over 70  of the European population at some time, so stop sniggering, you could succumb sometime in the future   Pay attention to the rest of this article and you might find out how to treat it.******OK, that   s the science bit over and done with, so for those of you who skipped that bit, welcome back   If you   ve been paying attention you should now know what dandruff is and what causes it, but what can we do about it apart from always wearing white clothing and trying not shake your head all day?  The good news is it can be treated and you can make dandruff go away just by using a simple shampoo.  So finally, after 750 words of pure waffle, I   m getting to the crux of this review   Yes, all that build up was for (drum roll please......) my dandruff controlling shampoo of choice.......Head and Shoulders.I   m sure you   ve all heard of it, lets face it the ads have been going for years, those ones with Ulrika and Emma Forbes    I don   t have dandruff, just great looking hair      I hate to be a marketing as for the company, they   re not paying me enough, but it really does work.So, time for a bit more science, how does Head and Shoulders get rid of dandruff?  Well, seeing as the cause of dandruff is a fungus, it makes sense to put something in the shampoo that will reduce the amount of fungus on the scalp.  Head and Shoulders contains an anit-fungal ingredient called Pyrithione Zinc, a patented formula that   s supposed to help get rid of dandruff.As I   ve said above, it really does work.  A few days of using this stuff and my dandruff goes away completely.  No more snowstorms when I shake my head, no more blizzards if I sneeze and I don   t need to carry a vacuum with me to brush of my shoulders every few minutes   One of the problems with this fungus is that it   s very difficult to eradicate completely.  Head and Shoulders keeps it under control, but does not kill it off altogether, so if you stop using it completely you will soon find those flakes building again until you   re back to square one.  It   s not all bad news though, once you have got the dandruff under control you don   t have to use Head and Shoulders every day.  Once or twice a week in place of your usual shampoo is usually enough to keep the dandruff at bay.  This is great for all you girlies (and guys ) who are addicted to a certain shampoo, I certainly know my girlfriend couldn   t live permanently without her Frizz-ease shampoo Having said this, using Head and Shoulders everyday isn   t such a bad thing as I was surprised to discover it really is a very good quality shampoo in its own right, without taking into account the dandruff controlling properties.  I find it leaves my hair really squeaky clean and easy to manage, OK, I   ll admit I   ve not really got huge amounts of hair to manage (no, I   m not bald, I just like to keep my hair short ) but it really does compare very favourably with other shampoos I   ve used such as Charles Worthington and the Tricologie range from Boots, both of which cost twice as much as Head and Shoulders.  I know it   s not as trendy as these names, and there   s a certain stigma involved in using Head and Shoulders, but if you can get over that it really is a good shampoo.  I hate to admit it, but for once a TV advert is right, I really DON   T have dandruff, just great looking hair     There is now quite a range of different types of Head and Shoulders shampoo for all types of hair :-Classic CleanClassic Clean 2in1Extra FullnessSmooth and Silky 2in1Dry Scalp CareRefreshPersonally I   m a traditionalist and stick with Classic Clean, but you   ve no excuse for not using it if you have difficult hair, give it a go, if nothing else it will certainly help the weather  (those snowstorms, keep up )Now remember your promise, don   t tell anyone about this, I don   t want it leaking out onto the internet www.headandshoulders.comAround 2.29 for 200ml from most chemists, supermarkets and high street toiletry stores.     ', '    This product may cure your dandruff problem but not always in an acceptable manner. Now. I may be running the risk of incurring some libel law that will be swooped upon by Proctor   Gamble s lawyers (although you can guarantee that there won t be any flakes gently sifting down from behing them) but I ve head this from enough seperate sources, from people who should be in a position to know, that this is the truth of it s success. Nature can be cruel and humiliating at times.So, here I am after my last failed attempt with a anti-dandruff shampoo having to stock up on the Head   Shoulders normal range (nice smell, good lather, leaves the hair feeling clean and not sticky, although you do notice a distinct whistling of the wind around the hair roots once you re aware of how this stuff works) and prepare to remove the pesky flaking layer once and for all.Great performance from a dandruff shampoo. Just a shame my dermaetological bits have to die so brutally in the process.      ', '    DANDRUFFDandruff is a condition affecting the scalp. What happens when you have dandruff is that the process I just explained speeds up to twice the normal rate so more dead cells are shed and pushed to the surface, there are so many cells that they go into clumps and this is what makes them visible. (If you have dandruff there are countless websites out there which can explain in greater detail such as www.netdoctor.co.uk or www.coolnurse.com) INTRODUCTIONI am reviewing the  Head   Shoulders  for normal hair or  Classic Clean  as it is now known. I would advise it s use...     ', '    There is a disease stalking the land that dare not speak its name. Despite the great majority of the population suffering at some time or another, nobody every seems to actually have it - dandruff, that is.Head and Shoulders is a dandruff treatment shampoo from Proctor and Gamble. What more is there to say? Well, I think that I probably need to pad out this opinion a little more, so here goes  8230;What  8217;s this dandruff anyway?~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Dandruff is a condition where the scalp flakes to a noticeable degree. The flakes are usually white in colour and range in size up to a couple of millimetres. The main cause of dandruff is thought to be the fungus malassezia. This fungus is normally present without problems on the scalp but in dandruff sufferers it goes into overdrive and causes the symptoms with which most of us are familiar.So what can you do about it?~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Treatment falls into three groups; antifungal, to kill of the root cause, antiproliferative, to reduce the production of cells, and keratolytic, which break down the flakes so that the effects are less noticeable.The most common antifungal treatments are pyrithione zinc and selenium sulphide. The former is the active ingredient in Head   Shoulders Classic, the latter in Head and Shoulders Intensive. Which one to use really depends on the individual, use whichever works for you.The only common antiproliferative treatment is coal tar and was universally used before the introduction of the antifungal treatments. The two disadvantages of this therapy are that it treats only the symptoms and not the underlying cause and the strong smell of the oil itself. This is the basis of all the popular   8216;medicated  8217; shampoos of the sixties and earlier (e.g. Vosene). Since the coal tar is strongly brown in colour the shampoos tend to be also.The final class of treatment is the keratolytics, the most common of which is salicylic acid. This is, of course, the same chemical used in Aspirin. It is not widely used in retail shampoos although it is sometimes prescribed for direct application. It also treats only the symptoms and can have serious side-effects if used to frequently or in too high a concentration.  8230;Back to Head and Shoulders~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Head and Shoulders has been produced since 1965 but only became widely available in the UK in the early seventies. The advertising marked a radical shift in emphasis for anti-dandruff shampoos. Previous brands had been marketed as utility or family shampoos   8211; stressing their   8216;medicated  8217; nature. To an extent this was forced by the coal tar basis of the shampoos which caused a uniformly strong smell and brown colour. The leading brand in Britain was Vosene, which was generally advertised with bubbly laughing children and as little mention of dandruff as possible.Head and Shoulders was launched with a marketing campaign based on the use of glamorous celebrities (admittedly rather   8216;B  8217; list) and models and stressing the effectiveness of the treatment in maintaining the proper image. Black seemed to be the only colour to wear which seemed a perverse choice for dandruff sufferers but made the point. Ulrika was, of course, one of the celebrities used.The shampoo itself is blue and creamy (opalescent, supposedly) and has a mildly fresh scent that is neutral enough to be unisex in application. The original packaging featured a long slender neck with vaguely   8216;shoulder  8217; shaped body to the bottle. This has now been superseded by the very squared style that is common to most shampoos. The bottle has the flip-top that is almost universal nowadays in these products. (Incidentally, am I the only person who has nightmare visions of opening my suitcase to find it full of freshly squeezed shampoo? I much preferred the security of screw-tops when travelling).What  8217;s in the bottle?~~~~~~~~~~~~~I don  8217;t propose to list all the ingredients here. I don  8217;t believe that there is much value to a straight list without explanation of what the various chemicals do. I have checked through all the ingredients (tedious job that it was) but if I were to reproduce that work the op would run to an extra page or two of A4. Those (few) people who have specific allergies will be all too familiar with checking labels.The active ingredient in H S Classic/Classic 2 in 1 in pyrithione zinc, the antifungal agent described above. The rest of the ingredients form the shampoo base.The chemicals fall into a few major groups. The largest single ingredient is water (or   8216;aqua  8217; as it commonly appears in lists). This serves both as a solvent for the other chemicals and a bulking agent. Bulking agents are used so that the correct dosage of chemicals can be easily applied, for example it would be possible to make a shampoo requiring only a few drops to be applied but this would make it difficult to apply evenly and in the proper concentrations. Anionic surfactants are the next major group and are basically detergents. If you look closely you will find the same chemicals in shampoo, washing up liquid, dishwasher detergents and so on although in different combinations and concentrations. Next up are foaming agents; these are special surfactants that are there to produce lots of foam. The foam actually has no effect other than reassuring the user that something is happening. You will next find chemicals that are known are   8216;pearling agents  8217;, these give the creamy or opalescent appearance to the liquid (rather than having a clear appearance).Next we find chemical such as sodium chloride (that many will recognise as table salt) these are used as water softeners to help the detergents dissolve and to avoid adverse reactions with the chemicals present in hard water supplies.The final elements are perfume and colour, which have the properties you would expect.But does it work?~~~~~~~~~~~In general it does work in controlling dandruff. I have found it to be consistently effective over many years. For those who find that the Classic doesn  8217;t work, try a shampoo, such as H S Intensive, that uses selenium sulphide as its active ingredient. One or the other should do the trick.The problem with dandruff treatments is that they do need to be continued. Since the fungus that is responsible is a normal inhabitant of the scalp the problems tend to recur when the treatment is stopped. In my experience you can lay off for up to a week, if you prefer to use another shampoo for daily washing, but it is very individual. There are also many different factors that can affect dandruff so it may be that having cleared it once it may never return, or maybe only at stressful times, for example.Some users report that they find the shampoo a little too harsh for everyday use. I have to say that this is not my experience, but you may want to alternate with a milder shampoo. The ingredients used in H S have been recently reformulated so if you have tried it before and been unhappy, now may be the time to try again.Conclusion or   8230; I think that  8217;s well over 120 words~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Head and Shoulders is generally an effective treatment for dandruff and I don  8217;t have any problems with it as an everyday shampoo. However as a result of using the product my hair suffered severe dryness. I say that it was a result of using the product as it was something I had never suffered to any great degree before. This was rather frustrating as it meant that I had swapped one problem for another. Because of this I then had to buy yet another product to ensure my hair kept its condition whilst using Head and Shoulders so at the time I was not particularly impressed ( At the time there was not a variant of Head and Shoulders for dry/damaged hair). The product itself is good at what it does so I will recommend it but I think that people should be aware that because of the strength of the shampoo there are potential problems to be associated with Head and Shoulders for the individual.     ', '          The first step is to admit you have a dandruff problem  If it looks as if it s been snowing outside, then that pretty much gives it away. But I could imagine it being very embarrassing having to buy an anti-dandruff shampoo in a crowded shop. But so many people without dandruff use head   shoulders shampoo, it doesn t seem embarrassing at all   Why do people without dandfruff use an anit-dandruff shampoo, especially when there are so many other shampoos available?  It actually prevents dandruff. If you haven t got it, and don t want it, then use head   shoulders to make sure that this won t happen. It has a fresh fragrance that lasts for a long time. It really annoys me when I buy a shampoo that claims to leave your hair smelling like lime or coconut, but just washes out.  It is unisex. The smell is suitable for male   female, and the simple yet eyecatching packaging is as well. Plus, on the advert, there are men and women, all sharing their personal experiences of the shampoo  It is more than just a smell, as it leaves your hair soft, clean and shiny. It is available in a range of styles, from shampoo and condition in one, to shampoo especially for greasy hair.  And most importantly, if you have dandruff, after just a few washes it will be noticably less. After a few weeks it should be gone    Finally, don t fbe too embarrassed to buy it   There is nothing more embarrassing than having flakes of skin shedding on dark clothing, and having to subtly wipe them off.     ', '        The first time that i purchased this was by chance, just wanted to try something new. I wouldnt say that i am prone to having dry skin, but i felt a noticable difference in the feel of my skin after i had used it. My skin felt really smooth, and i mean really smooth   This may be a good body wash to try if you have sensitive skin as it is ph balanced. There is a slight smell to this, but it is very subtle, but it does smell very nice, sort of a fresh, clean smell. A good thing about this bodywash is that a little amount does go far, it also lathers up very well. It is reasonably priced, around average compared to other body washes. I would definately recommend this to smoothen your skin, but not if you like body washes that have a strong scent to them, as this one does not.             ', '    I remember the first time I smelt this product, it was unbelievable, the staying power of the product was huge, at last I found a product that was timeless, you could wear it to the beach, out at night or just relaxing around the house. It s top notes are exact of what I always wanted from a smell, yet so many girls asked me what I was wearing. I come from a medium sized town in Australia when many people are graced by the designer brands such as Versace, Hugo Boss, Gucci, Tommy Hilfiger and YSL products yet they give little time into the classics like this product Joop, I wore Joop Homme for nearly 2 years and I haven t found a parfum for men that I liked or could wear for such a long time without getting bored of it or thinking that it s time to change. Classic Rated 5 star     ', '    Cool effect eyeshadow cream seems to be the latest make-up idea so I thought I would try it out.  I am constantly looking for a lilac shade as I tend to be drawn to pale purple clothes so I tried their lavender shade.  There are two other shades available in silver and gold.Initially there is definetly a cooling affect when applied to the lids which is quite pleasant. The cream did feel smoother and the shimmer effect was stronger but as usual the price was higher at around    6.  Personally I preferred L Oreals cream colour which could be applied directly to the lids but Maybelline do provide a satisfactory cheaper alternative.     ', '    From a young age, I was diagnosed with acute ezcema on both of my hands. I remember going through cream after cream, searching through what the doctors advised me to use. ', '    Having being unfortunate enough to suffer from problem skin since my teens, there isn t a spot treatment product that I haven t tried After many disappointing results I came across Oxy 10 and have never turned back.The product comes in a tiny white bottle and is available from Boots, I believe that its only available from over the counter, however don t take my word for that, but thats how I always buy it, I think its because of the powerful ingredients that are in it such as benzoyl peroxide so make sure that you don t have an allergy to this before purchasing.When I first applied the cream to my skin there was a slight tingling however this soon went, the spots clear up really quickly, the only thing that I wasn t keen on was that the cream actually brings the spots to a head before drying them so don t apply this cream before going out becuse during the night you will end up with a rather attractive yellow head I tend to apply before I go to bed and the skin is generally dried up by the morning, again a problem being that the skin does get dry but removes the spots, what a choice spotty skin or dry skin   personally I d go for the dry skin...     ', '    As a thirty-something year old, I shouldn t really ought to get blackheads, but, hey, life s not fair, is it? Unfortunately, in spite of vigorous cleansing, the blackheads were back in 2 days and needed doing all over again, making it a pretty expensive job.  But, the price can be brought down if you shop around - Quality Save offer Blackout liquid for about    3 and at the moment, expiry date October 2001 was setting me back a mere 99p      ', '    Me and my boyfriend bought this whilst we ere shopping in sainsbury  8217;s yesterday, I got home feeling tired, so I went upstairs to run a bath pouring a tiny amount of this into the bath, I left it as I changed and went back into the bathroom to see bubbles galore. ', '    The first time I tried this product i was plesently suprised. The smell was inviting and i cound not was to get in to the bath.When I used it on my body my skin really tingled and felt refreshed.I very good product which leaves you skin fresh and soft. I have purchased this product a few time and i have tried other product which are similar but none of them really compare to it. I did really go in to the shop to buy this product I just notice it was new and decided to try it and I am glad I did I would recommend it to anybody. Its a great wake up call in the morning. So have an orange start to your day.     ', '    My daughter s hair is quite thick and none of the children s shampoos worked well on it, leaving it limp and lank.While out shopping one day I spotted a half price offer on Timotei shine and strength shampoo which is formulated for frequent use on normal hair.It has the normal shampoo ingredients with extracts of wild herbs, ginseng and lemon tree blossom and smells really fresh and light. ', '    Yes Tommy might be an expensive line but so is every other fragrance these days, not to be rude but for all the guys out there that wear this one just because the girls love it, get one girl into bed then they have made their money back on it. Well Tommy is simply a classic, released nearly four years ago and sales still strong in the US, Australia and UK today, this is the fragrance for the laid back cool fresh scented guy. It has that lovely sporty scent top note about it and is a definite girl grabber. Literally girls noses will be on your neck as you walk past them. For the ladies out there, this is a huge one to buy your guy, but depending on what he likes. Not all guys like the sporty, citrus smelling aftershaves yet some like the more business like smell. When I worked in fragrance spritzing two years ago for Tommy, Aramis and DKNY this one was the biggest puller of girls. more girls came up and purchased this one for themselves than they bought the ladies version. I highly recommend this one to anyone who likes the sporty scented aftershave with classic girl pulling draw cards. The bottle lasts ages and will keep people asking you, Do you wear Tommy?? That s it from me, this is a top 5 ftershave on my cards, is it yours or not, that s up to you to decide.      ', '    Because I have to take so many medications for medical reasons, my hair becomes very dry and brittle.  There were many times that my hair would actually feel like straw and it was getting very difficult to even comb.  A few months ago I came across this product and I am so thankful that I did.  My hair is once again soft, shinny, and easy to manage.Downfall: I did find that if I did not use it everyday that it would loose its effect.Ingredients: water steryl alcohol xychopenasiloxane cotlagen biotin Panthenyl ethyl glutamin acid benzyl alcohol fragrance methychlorosothiazolinone Methyisothiazolinone cytyl alcohol dimethylamine ethe* dimethiconThis product should be used:If you have dry and damage hair.You Want:Conditioning that will help to replenish moisture to you drying hair and will help to prevent split ends.How to Use:Apply VS Moisturizing Daily to your hair after shampooing.  Let is sit for five minutes, and then rinse with cool water.  It is important to remember to use the cool water and not hot.I would recommend this product to anyone who is willing to use it on a daily basis.  If it is something that you only want to use once in a while, it is not going to work as well.     ', '    My boyfriend wears Opium and I really can t stand it, and trust me fellas, I m not the only one   I won t go near my man when he s got it on, which is probably the reason he wears it in the first place   To be fair, its not bad enough to keep me away from him,but within seconds my head starts pounding and I m ready for a lie down, and, no thats not just the effect he has on me I wouldn t mind if it was bargain basement stuff, if he d got it from a dodgy guy on the street but there are so many other fragrances for men which smell gorgeous, why spend your money on something that smells like I you just conconcted it yourself in the bathroom?   It s just far too overpowering, fine if you re trying to mask the fact that you ve just been rolling about in a rubbish dump but, surely fragrances are meant to be more subtle than that?   Blokes, wouldn t you rather a lovely young lady leaned in close to you to ask  what is that gorgeous fragrance you re wearing?  rather than passing out from half a mile away? I don t mean to offend any fans of Opium, fragrances are a personal choice, I realise that but from a female point of view, please, if you have to wear it, go easy      ', '    The results are in  Pure O2 is a breath of fresh air for the skin.I love the light airy foam and the way it left my skin feeling softer and looking more radiant with its delivery of pure oxygen to my skin.This is the first time that I have ever used a foam treatment. It is so easy to use, goes on very easy and dries quickly. It does feel really good and seems to improve the texture of my face.I loved the beautiful glow and the softness to the look and feel of my skin.It is the perfect daytime complement to the Retroactive Cream I already use.What Avon says :  Anew Pure 02 Oxygenating Youth SPF 15 Complex / First ever  lighter-than-air  anti-aging facial treatment that increases the delivery   use of pure, life-giving oxygen to skin / Exclusive Energie-Cell-System increases the delivery   use of fresh oxygen to skin. / skin stays looking younger, healthier, glowing with energy / First ever anti-ging foam  / 1.7 fl oz / for all ages,all skin types-even sensitive I have a very sensitive skin, and I didn t feel anything wrong with this product.My skin looked like a  paper craft  before using Pure O2, and now, I couldn t forget to use it every day. It so comfortable   I am 35 years old, and I look like 30  Do you believe that ? ?      ', '    I personally have never used a cream on my face. But noticed that recently my skin was a little flakey. So I decided to try one. The lady in the shop recommended this as I have never used a cream before plus in the past if I ve changed my soap/cleanser it has brought me out in a rash/pimples. The clarins gentle day cream is purely for very sensitive to sensitive skin.I like the idea and design of the bottle. Its easy to spot on the Clarins shelving as its peach in colour unlike the original clarins which is red. It has a pump action which is great. I find two pumps supplies me with enough cream for my face and neck. Its smooth creamy texture goes on easily and is absorbed effectively. It has a light pleasent refreshing scent.I paid    25 for this cream although I have been informed it is cheaper on Pharmacy2uk.Even though Clarins are a little expensive they re worth every penny.Clarins gentle day cream suits my skin down to the ground. When I first went out looking for a cream I thought it would take a few different makes, I was so delighted when I found the perfect cream for my face. I would highly recommend it,especially if its your first cream. I use it now every day,it leaves my skin moist, soft and refreshed, I don t know what I did without it.     ', '    My husband use s aquatonic deodorant and bodyspray. They are both by faberge.The deodorant comes in a 200ml tin, which is blue and green. The bodyspray comes in 150ml tin. They both cost    2.99 each, which is quite expensive, but smells very nice. The smell is nice, and is quite strong but not overpowering though. The smell lasts quite a while too once you have put it on.They sometimes do an offer on aquatonic of buy one and get one free. This offer they do at morrisons, so when they do I usually get one of each for my husband and stock up on them.Before you use them, you should shake them and spray them on your body about 15cm s away from your body.They are highly flammable, so do not put it in direct sunlight or near someone who is smoking.The ingrediants for anyone that is interested are (deodorant)ButaneIsobutanePropaneCyclomethiconeparfumdisteardimonium HectoriteMentholThe ingrediants for the body spray are:-Alcohol DenatButaneIsobutanePropaneparfumIsopropyl MyristateMentholThe deodorant is effective but if you go jogging, running, or excersie, then expect the deodorant not to work very well. I have seen them both cheaper in other shops, so you do need to look around really.It is expensive, but they both last quite a while though. My husband has them for about a month, maybe longer, before we need to buy more.I d recommend any man to use this as it smells lovely.     ', '    For anyone who hasn t tried the massage bars made by Lush thet are unusual as they come in a solid form. To use them, you just rub gently between your palms to melt the bar into oil with the heat of your hands and apply  The beauty of this is that they are very portable ( no great clunky bottles) and simple to use ie. can t be knocked over. Also of cousre, it saves on wasteful packaging.Fever is one of the newest massage products made by this firm and promises a scent evocative of the 50 s. It does smell gorgeous, very floral and retro. It does remind me a little of the Flower Market fragrance they used to make for any Lush devotees out there I would recommend this either as a massage bar to use with a loved one or as an after bath body oil, which is my personal preference for this particular product, as I think the scent is very feminine, so if your loved one happens to be male then one of their other massage bars may be better ( I think  Bewitched  is a good all rounder). I am a lover of Lush stuff and can t wait to try anything new of theirs. Go on, have a go - beats anything ( or almost) that Ann Summers can offer at this price  Currently,    2.95 per. bar.     ', '    Having been a fan of Nivea most of my life, probably because my mother always had a tub on the go in the days before Nivea expanded its range into more complex products, and after seeing it advertised, I was keen to try Visage All Day Aqua, especially, as it claimed 24 hour continuous moisturising.Upon opening the pot I was amazed to see that the cream was not the usual boring white but blue  Upon applying, (just a small amount is required), my skin felt quite cool, and what I can only described as invigoratingly refreshed.After reading the ingredients listing, I discovered that it contains an active ingredient combination, which claims to   8220;intensively moisturise and strengthen the skin  8221; called   8220;Aquaspheres  8221;.  This combination comprises: Glycerine which gives immediate, intensive moisturisation of the upper layers of the epidermis. Fucogel which prevents the skin from drying out and Liposome encapsulated natural moisturising factor or (NMF) for short   8211; apparently, this NMF fills up the skin  8217;s own moisture depots and binds water into the horny layer   8211; very scientific  It also contains minerals to help your skin store the moisture, Vitamin E and those wonderful UVA and UVB filters.I have been using this product now for several weeks and can honestly say, I cannot see an obvious difference in the mirror (probably take a lot more than a pot of face cream anyway) but the texture of my skin does feel softer.I bought my 50m jar from Tesco and it cost    6.99 which I thought was a good price, considering the cost of an equivalent product from other leading brands.     ', '    Ever since I have been dressing myself (no jokes please from those of you that know my sense of/ lack of style ) and part of the routine has included all over moisturising. Way back then, it was the   8220;odd  8221; thing to do. But now most people wear sun screen within their cosmetics and include a facial treatment in a their daily routine in a never-ending battle to maintain youthful, healthy skin   8211; without a doubt moisture is the key. I brought Oil of Olay Moisturising Body Wash because I wanted a change from my usual brand of shower gel. Over the last few months, shower products have been drying out my skin, leaving it feeling itchy and rough. The Oil of Olay Moisturising Body Wash appealed to me because Oil of Olay have a good reputation in skincare. The Body wash smelled very fresh and clean and lathered really quickly. The bonus for long legged people like myself is that a little goes a long way, so at 3.99 for 300ml, it is good value for money. I have been using it for several weeks now and my skin feels so much better, softer and less dry. I saw some results straight away. After the first use, my skin was brighter and slightly smoother and after about a week my skin was less dry and finer areas of dry skin were no longer visible. Most of the time I used a   8220;buff pad  8221; to lather the Body Wash (I don  8217;t know what they really are called but they are those plastics things that look like your granny  8217;s hairnet and work up even the weakest soap into a great big mass of foam). It is definitely a must try bath product.      ', '    Having seen Pond  8217;s Clear Pore strips advertised in a well-known woman  8217;s magazine, I apprehensively bought a pack from a high street chemist. I had previously tried Biore  8217;s Deep Cleansing Facial strips, which I thought were quite expensive at    7.50 for a pack of six, especially as I was not completely satisfied with the results. However, never being one to give in easily, I tried the Pond  8217;s strips.What They Do==========These strips are designed for used on the nose and chin to unblock clogged pores and remove blackheads, whiteheads, and general dirt, oil and debris, which these areas can be prone to. Instructions for UseI followed the instructions outlined on the box, which are:1. Moist the area to be treated with water, i.e. chin or noise   8211; the water is necessary to activate the ingredients on the strip.2. Apply the strip ensuring that it is firmly pressed down ensuring that the strip makes contact with the skin and that all air bubbles are removed.3. Wait fifteen minutes, or until the strip has turned stiff and feels dry to the touch.4. Remove.Note: If the strip is extremely dry and hard to remove, moisten it with a little water, which will help removal.Results=====I was pleased with the final result   8211; I did not at first believe how much unseen dirt was clogging my pores   8211; although after use, the area treated stung for a short while, my skin felt quite soft and smooth to the touch, and it also felt cleansed.Where you can buy them===================Pond  8217;s Clear Pore strips can be purchased from major supermarkets, Boots the Chemists www.wellbeing.com for    9.99 or over the Internet from Pharmacy2U www.pharmacy2u.co.uk where they are usually cheaper at    4.99.Don  8217;t take my word for it, try them for yourself.      ']

This opinion is really for the fellas out there, but no doubt you will all take an interest, as if you  8217;re anything like my lady, then you  8217;re forever nicking your bloke  8217;s razor to do whatever it is you do with it.My missus tells me it  8217;s to shave her legs, but I have my suspicions  ~ ~ Shaving is a subject that is very close to my heart, (not to mention my face) as it  8217;s an exercise that I  8217;ve had to carry out on an almost daily basis for about the past 36 years or so, ever since the day my voice broke, and my facial hair started sprouting all over the place.I know that there are tried and proven methods of stopping this hair growth in its tracks, but becoming a eunuch was never really on the cards as far as I was concerned.Over the years my beard growth has got heavier, to the extent that if I am going out for the evening, or contemplating any naughty business with her indoors, I actually have to shave again in the evening. The claim is that the first of the blades removes the heavy hair growth, the next blade removes what the first one has missed, and the last blade (the new one) administers the   8220;coup de grace  8221;, and wipes out any remnants of facial hair entirely.Well, much as it pains me to have to say so, I have to admit that it is all true.The removable razor head swivels and turns to conform itself to every little nook, cranny, and wrinkle on your face, (well, on MY face) and has a lubricating strip to ensure that it glides with ease. I used to get around a week out of my old Contour, so if it  8217;s as good as that I  8217;ll be happy enough.As I said, the razor cost me    5.99 (Irish Punts) and along with the flashy looking razor itself I also got a plastic holder, and a spare replacement blade.Now I  8217;m no mug, and checked the cost of replacement cartridges before I even bought it, and it has to be said that they are relatively expensive when compared to other blades on the shelves.A pack of four blades costs    6.59, and this compares with    2.59 for a pack of five blades for my old Contour.But so what   If I get a month out of a pack (a cartridge per week) then it  8217;s only costing me    1.65 a week to get the best and most pleasurable shaving experience of my entire life. ', '    As I mentioned in a previous op that occasionally I go a week without shaving, normally cause all I   m doing is work and don   t really see the point in being cleanly shaven behind a desk. ', '    I bought this razor for my husband twice, as the first one he lost, for    3.49 from Boots and it came with 2 free blades. ', '    This is another review on something I was bought for chirstmas. It wasn t pretty. I ve definatly found the blade of choice for me.Thanks for the read.     ', '    Having to shave every day can be such a chore. I am sure this is a coincidence, I mean do you think my Daughter would use my razor??     ', '    Let s get one thing straight. I grudge paying over the odds for toiletries. ', '    When i got my electric razor, i new it was time for me to have to give up my normal everyday shaving razor, but i was gutted because i had used this for nearly a year now, and i had not had a razor as good as this.The Mach 3, is probably the best shaver available in the UK, that is not a electronic one.The mach 3 itself was introduced into the UK in 1998, and since has become one of the best brought razors on the market.The first thing you notice about these, is that they are 3 blades per razor blade itself. But if you want a clean, nice feeling, and to make yourself feel fresh afterwards and not to be cut to shreds, then i would recommend this totally.Thank you for taking the time to read and rate this.Michael xx      ', '    Unfortunately, no, fortunately for me, I can  8217;t include results of self-experiments as I  8217;m not a hairy type, not even for UK Ireland standards where many more women shave their legs than in Germany, I trust my husband who chanced upon MACH3 - I had bought it for him by mistake - and has been faithful to the product ever since.For the readers who don  8217;t know German and the ones who slept during their German lessons: The title of my op is not bad IMHO, no, to be honest, it  8217;s dead brill IMNHO, it  8217;s a play with words:   8216;macht  8217;s gut  8217; meaning in German   8216;does it well  8217;, echoing the name of the product and stressing at the same time the name Mach, which should be pronounced the German way as Ernst Mach was an Austrian, i.e.   8216;a  8217; like the   8216;u  8217; in bus,   8216;ch  8217; like the   8216;ch  8217; in Loch (Ness). Don  8217;t believe British/American encyclopedias which tell you otherwise What has Ernst Mach (1836-1916) got to do with razor blades? Nothing really; he was a physicist and philosopher, born in Brno, Bohemia, Professor at the German University in Prague and Vienna. An aeroplane has the velocity of Mach3 when it is travelling at three times the speed of sound as measured in the prevailing atmosphere.Men, picture yourselves in the bathroom very early in the morning, preferably after a short night, does who/what looks out of the mirror resemble a Mach3 pilot? The brand name is a very clever advertising trick, hinting at and implying a dynamic force and deluding the consumers into thinking that by using a gadget with such a name something of this dynamic force might rub off What does a MACH3 razor offer?-  a rubberized contour grip for better handling-  an indicator lubricating strip signals when you  8217;re no longer experiencing the optimal       MACH3 shave-  the open-flow cartridge is designed for easy rinsing-  a single-point cartridge docking for easy, error-free loading-  a new forward pivot design so the blades are always in an optimal shaving position    (To answer the most FAQ: This means that MACH3 cartridges don  8217;t fit into any    other type of razor, sorry )-  three specially positioned blades to shave progressively closer in a single stroke, you    take one stroke, MACH3 takes three-  and a new generation of blades  Gillette has reengineered the blades themselves, the   first major blade innovation since 1960. The patented DLC (TM) comfort edges are    thinner than any other Gillette blade edge and cut beard hairs more easily.Who do you have to thank for all this? King C. Gillette (1855-1932), of course, who founded the company in Boston on September, 28th 1901 (congratulations on the 100th anniversary ), which is now the global market leader in nearly a dozen major consumer products categories, principally in the grooming, portable power and oral care business and which delivers its goods in over 200 countries and territories.Who remembers that he was also a great utopian thinker who envisioned a city so huge that nearly all the residents of 20th century North America could be housed in its high-rise buildings and enjoy life under its glass atriums?   8220;Metropolis  8221;, on the shores of Lake Ontario, N.Y., was meant to be clean, efficient and pollution-free. ', '    The village I grew up in boasted an old-fashioned corner shop, a newsagents, a pub, a railway station, a cobbler  8217;s shop and a barbers. Not a hairdressers - a barbers, one which proudly exhibited a traditional red and white pole. Barbers have a celebrated and very impressive history and in primitive times, they were the leading religious men of their tribes because people believed that good and bad spirits entered the body through your hair and that the bad spirits could only be driven out by someone cutting your hair. The barber was the main player who arranged all the marriages and baptized the children. In the Middle Ages, barbers were actually surgeons who practiced    8216;bloodletting  8217; to cure disease. In fact, the predecessor of the barber  8217;s pole was two spiral ribbons painted around the pole to represent two long bandages, one twisted around the arm before bleeding and the other used to bind it afterward.The barber in our village had a job description, which no longer included bloodletting but he was still a prominent member of our society and he did a roaring trade in shaves. I can clearly recall the queues on Saturday Mornings for a short back and sides and a shave with a cobalt steel   8216;cut throat  8217; razor which he sharpened on a stone called a hone and stroked up and down against linen on a leather strop. He had a machine, which dispensed warm shaving cream and there were plenty of steaming hot towels, which he used to swathe his customer  8217;s faces in after he  8217;d finished the shave.  I was too young to shave in those days but the whole process fascinated me. I don  8217;t suppose anybody goes to the barbers for a shave anymore, but I think I  8217;ve found the modern day equivalent, the Gillette Mach3, the first triple-blade razor, which was first introduced in 1998 and which has become the world s leading razor. Alright, fellow grooming adventurers, let’s talk about the Gillette Mach 3 razor — the trusty sidekick that promises to turn your shaving saga from “ouch” to “ahh” with a few slick moves.

First off, swapping blades on this bad boy is a breeze thanks to its single-point cartridge docking system. No fumbling, no finger gymnastics—just a quick click and you’re back in the game. And if you’re like me, tired of razors that clog faster than your inbox, the Mach 3’s design keeps hair from gumming up the works, making cleanup a snap. Bonus points for saving you from that awkward “why is this razor so gross?” moment.

Now, the real magic happens with its swivel head and spring mechanism. It’s like the razor has a built-in GPS for your face, hugging every contour with the grace of a ballerina—well, a ballerina who’s really into smooth skin. This means fewer nicks and less irritation, even if your skin screams “sensitive!” at the mere sight of a blade. The three-blade system glides so effortlessly, you might forget you’re shaving and not performing a delicate dance.

Speaking of smooth, the lubricating strip is the unsung hero here, helping the razor glide like it’s on a slip ‘n slide, reducing razor burn and leaving your skin feeling pampered rather than punished. Plus, the blades last longer than your average disposable, so while the price might make you raise an eyebrow, the durability makes it a worthy investment.

Oh, and it’s not just for the gents—ladies, this razor handles legs and other delicate areas with equal finesse. The grip is comfy and secure, and the stylish, well-weighted design means you’re in control, not the other way around.

If you want a quick, close, and hassle-free shave without the drama, the Mach 3 is your new best friend. Just don’t be surprised if you start looking forward to shaving—yes, really.

The nasty smell you get form sweat isn   t actually your sweat smelling. Human sweat hardly smells at all, and, in fact, it   s not that bad. The bad smell you get is from the microbes that live on your skin that produce it, as they metabolise your sweat (it   s the same with wind by the way     it   s the microbes in your gut that make it). All PitRok does is stop these microbes producing the smell. Cunning or what? It doesn   t kill the little beasties     without them, you   d get very uncomfortable very quickly. ', '    Well, I didn t think that I would ever be writing a review on a deodorant but every so often you discover a product that is so good that you feel that you have to let everybody know about it. PitRok is one of these products and what is more I discovered it first on Ciao via digitalburn s excellent review.So what is the big deal then? Well, whether you like it or not we all need something to stop those nasty smells building up and offending those around us. To this end, most people use deodorants or anti-perspirants or both. The problem I have had in the past is that most such products tend to give me a rash and to be frank most of them smell pretty disgusting themselves - all icky sticky sweet and yucky.Deodorants tend to work by masking the smell. They overpower the bodily smell with some chemical or floral smell which aims to confuse the nose of passers by but more often than not just creates a new smell which still has the subtle undertones of sweat.Anti-perspirants work by preventing the sweat glands from functioning. You don t sweat so you don t smell. But hey - shouldn t we be sweating? Doesn t it have a purpose? The answer is  yes  and by preventing sweating you are interfering with your body s natural functions and preventing the flushing of toxins.Another common problem with these chemical conconctions is that they damage your clothes, leaving nasty rings or even rotting them - so what are they doing to your skin? The truth is that very many people suffer adverse reactions to deodorants and anti-perspirants in the form of itching and rash, sometimes severe.Many such products contain quite nasty substances, a common one being Aluminium Chlorohydrate, or aluminium chloride which acts by constricting the pores of the skin. It is one of several aluminium salts employed by the cosmetics industry. It is a chemically active form of chlorine which is emulsified enabling it to plug and close underarm pores. When this compound comes into contact with organic matter (e.g. skin tissue) the chlorine attacks and breaks down chemically. Aluminium chloride has a corrosive effect on the skin, respiratory tract and eyes. The toxic affect is caused by the evolution of hydrochloric acid when the product is exposed to moist air. The resulting respiratory difficulties can vary from mild irritation to coughing. Nice eh?But all is not lost - this is where PitRok comes in.PitRok is a totally natural bacteriosatic deodorant. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re on the lookout for a natural deodorant that’s gentle yet effective, PitRok might just be worth a try—especially if you have sensitive skin or shave regularly. What stands out immediately is that PitRok doesn’t irritate the skin or clog pores, which is a big plus for anyone prone to sensitivity or breakouts. Unlike many conventional deodorants loaded with chemicals, alcohol, or aluminum chlorohydrate, PitRok is made entirely from mineral salts, making it a clean, chemical-free option that supports your body’s natural toxin removal.

Application is straightforward and even a bit satisfying: just wet the crystal and glide it smoothly over damp skin. No sticky residue or harsh sensations here. It’s fragrance-free, so if you’re sensitive to strong scents or prefer to layer your own perfume, this deodorant won’t interfere or leave any scent behind.

Now, PitRok doesn’t stop sweat—it lets your body do its thing—but it neutralizes the bacteria that cause odor, which is the main goal for many of us. This means you stay fresh without blocking your natural sweating process, which some find healthier and more comfortable.

One thing to note is availability; you won’t find PitRok in every supermarket aisle. It’s mostly available online or in health food stores, so a bit of planning is needed before you stock up. However, the initial price might seem higher than drugstore brands, but it lasts much longer, making it a cost-effective choice in the long run.

Bonus points: PitRok is endorsed by the Vegetarian Society and is environmentally friendly, aligning well with a natural, ethical lifestyle.

In summary, if you want a no-nonsense, natural deodorant that’s kind to sensitive skin, odor-effective, and long-lasting, PitRok delivers. Just don’t expect it to stop sweating, and be ready to order it online. For those who prioritize clean ingredients and practicality over flashy branding, this is a solid pick.
