product_reviews: ['    ~ ~ OK girls. This opinion is really for the fellas out there, but no doubt you will all take an interest, as if you  8217;re anything like my lady, then you  8217;re forever nicking your bloke  8217;s razor to do whatever it is you do with it.My missus tells me it  8217;s to shave her legs, but I have my suspicions  ~ ~ Shaving is a subject that is very close to my heart, (not to mention my face) as it  8217;s an exercise that I  8217;ve had to carry out on an almost daily basis for about the past 36 years or so, ever since the day my voice broke, and my facial hair started sprouting all over the place.I know that there are tried and proven methods of stopping this hair growth in its tracks, but becoming a eunuch was never really on the cards as far as I was concerned.Over the years my beard growth has got heavier, to the extent that if I am going out for the evening, or contemplating any naughty business with her indoors, I actually have to shave again in the evening. (She says my whiskers give her a rash   Imagine.)~ ~ Up until the beginning of this week, my weapon of choice for scraping the old bristles was the Gillette Contour Plus razor.This is a twin-bladed device, and has given me many years of faithful and stout service, without hacking the old features to total ribbons.But the advent of the non-paying categories here at Ciao last month has meant I have found myself reading an avalanche of opinions recently about toiletries, shampoos, deodorants, and razors. (not to mention the new food and drink section)One razor that seems to be almost universally praised by nearly all the Ciaoites is the new one from Gillette, called the   8220;Mach 3  8221;.This razor is the next logical step by Gillette after the twin-bladed Contour, and instead of two blades, this one has no less than three. ~ ~ While I was doing the weekly supermarket shop at the beginning of the week, and looking for some replacement blades for my Contour Plus, I spotted this new   8220;wonder weapon  8221; prominently displayed on the shelves, and for a mere    5.99. So being the fickle and flirty fella that I am, I decided on the spot that I was going to try out this new fangled invention, if only to prove to myself that it couldn  8217;t possibly improve on my old faithful Contour.Oh, how wrong can a person be? Joy of joys, and all sorts of wonderful and flowing complimentary adjectives. This razor is quite simply the best I have ever used, and shaves the old   8220;boat race  8221; so effectively that afterwards I find it hard to believe there were any whiskers there at all.In fact, the only shave I know that is better is a   8220;hot towel  8221; shave at a barber  8217;s shop in central Dublin, with an old-fashioned cut-throat razor. (You can hardly get a barber to do this for you these days, because of the huge increase in their insurance since the advent of AIDS and all sorts of other nasty diseases that can be spread by infected blood.)~ ~ Anyway. Back to the razor in question, the Mach 3.I  8217;m sure that most of you have seen the somewhat gushing and over the top TV adverts by Gillette claiming that this is the nearest a man will ever get to turning his face into a passable imitation of a baby  8217;s bottom.In fact, if I  8217;m totally honest, these ads probably put me off purchasing the Mach 3 more than anything else, if for no better reason than to foil the admen  8217;s attempts to inveigle me into buying. The claim is that the first of the blades removes the heavy hair growth, the next blade removes what the first one has missed, and the last blade (the new one) administers the   8220;coup de grace  8221;, and wipes out any remnants of facial hair entirely.Well, much as it pains me to have to say so, I have to admit that it is all true.The removable razor head swivels and turns to conform itself to every little nook, cranny, and wrinkle on your face, (well, on MY face) and has a lubricating strip to ensure that it glides with ease. There is no sensation of   8220;scraping  8221; that is normally associated with shaving, and the whole exercise is so hassle and pain free that you start to wonder if it is actually shaving you at all. That is, until you see and feel the wonderful results.~ ~ I don  8217;t know yet how long each of the blades will last, but I  8217;ve had half a dozen shaves from the original blade now, with no signs of it dulling or losing its edge. I used to get around a week out of my old Contour, so if it  8217;s as good as that I  8217;ll be happy enough.As I said, the razor cost me    5.99 (Irish Punts) and along with the flashy looking razor itself I also got a plastic holder, and a spare replacement blade.Now I  8217;m no mug, and checked the cost of replacement cartridges before I even bought it, and it has to be said that they are relatively expensive when compared to other blades on the shelves.A pack of four blades costs    6.59, and this compares with    2.59 for a pack of five blades for my old Contour.But so what   If I get a month out of a pack (a cartridge per week) then it  8217;s only costing me    1.65 a week to get the best and most pleasurable shaving experience of my entire life. That  8217;s cheap as far as I  8217;m concerned.A big well done to the research and development department at Gillette from the   8220;mad cabbie  8221;. How long, I wonder, until we have the   8220;four blade  8221; razor.But then how exactly do you improve on perfection?     ', '    As I mentioned in a previous op that occasionally I go a week without shaving, normally cause all I   m doing is work and don   t really see the point in being cleanly shaven behind a desk. So unless someone is coming to see me I don   t bother but recently having to replace my regular Wilkinson Sword razor, so I headed for Cost Co and picked up one of these Mach 3   s as they were the only ones they had. And with shaving being one of those things every man needs to do here   s what I found. A wet shave is one of those pains of the day where after getting up you really cant be bothered to gather all your stuff together but usually I find it provides a better finish than with an electric razor. So The Mach 3 seemed like the perfect instrument especially after all the advertising about it being the best a man can get and all that.The Gillette Mach 3 is one of the market leaders in disposable razors being the pioneers of the three blade technology. The scientific reasoning behind this 3 blade system id to provide you with a closer shave, cutting closer to the grain. The green strip is designed to prevent irritation in anyway, however I   ve found this not to be the case.Of course it does prevent the irritation, but I have to say I   m very disappointed with the closeness of the shave. It left big clumps of stubble all over my face even when I use a brand new blade. The other major problem I have is when I do have a few days growth it drags over the top of the hair yanking it out rather than a smooth pleasant feel. This is totally unlike the Wilkinson, which I always found gave the closest possible shave even if I hadn   t shaved for a few days.The cost as well is a bit of a put off, although the first time you buy one you get the silver razor in a nice little holder with 2 disposable blades. You can get them for about    3.10 from Sainsburys.co.uk but cost roughly the same everywhere. Once the 2 blades run out you have the option of either 4 for    3.80 and 8 for    7.50. This does seem a tad expensive but is in line with the others on the market. The one saving grace here is the fact the blades do last a decent length of time usually just over the month so you don   t have to buy new ones too often.The three blade system really should make the Mach 3 into a better razor with the idea of the closer shave really appealing. Although it does do it occasionally it really isn   t enough to justify the cost of the razor, which isn   t as near to the quality of the Wilkinson Sword. After this shave the skin feels quite stubbly  and I really don   t have the sort of finish I was looking for. So overall Gillette Mach 3 is certainly not the best a man can get and infact is actually quite a normal unimpressive razor. The price is its first downfall but its mainly in the finished quality that the razor really lacks. I think rather than lumber on with this poor quality shave and constant stubble patches, I   ll head back to the Wilkinson when I   ve finished the remaining blades off.     ', '    I bought this razor for my husband twice, as the first one he lost, for    3.49 from Boots and it came with 2 free blades. The Gillette mach 3 razor is a fantastic razor it leaves my husband with a great smooth shave and the razor blades are cheapish too. The mach 3 razor has three blades so it cuts the stubble down effectively in one stroke of the razor and my husband doesn t cut himself with this razor.My opinion of the Gillette Mach 3 razor is that it is a great razor for men and is a great buy. I would recommend this razor for men because it leaves the face feeling smooth it does the job perfectly and there are no faults with this razor.      ', '    This is another review on something I was bought for chirstmas. My granny gave me a mach 3 razor gift set type thing for chirstmas and although I m always happy to recieve gifts I already had a razor I was comfortable with. So in a way it was seen as something that would save me a few quid when I d run out of my wilkinsons protector. I have a lot of sympathy for women who have to shave their legs, I can only imagine how annoying this must get. But facial hair is a real pain, for at least the next 30 years or so ( assuming I don t choose to try and grow a dodgey beard ) I ll have to shave every day, every other day at the most. It is therefore very important for me to have something that is not only quick to use but also comfortable. Like I said previously I used Wilkinson sword s protector 3d diamond. I was happy, I didn t know there was anything better so I just made do. I was wrong.Lets start with a few boring facts, the razor handle thingy comes in the standard design, comfortable rubber handle with a connecting mechanism at the top to allow you to attach the different blades. Each of the blades themselves have the patented 3 blade system ( without any guard rails, although I don t think they help at all ). This supposably makes shaving faster and more efficient and this is what they use as their main selling point. In truth I didn t see much difference from my previous razor that had only two. In all honesty, the first time I used this razor I thought I had slit a huge hole in my face. The first stroke was as usual but the second one was different, there was very little resistance to the blade and I assumed this must have been due a cut I had made. Thankfully I was wrong, I had discoverd by far the best thing about this blade. A small solid blue line on the top of the blade had released some kind of gel. This sounds strange but its true, when this little bar ( just above the actual blades) gets wet it releases a gel that lubricates the face on use. With each stroke it got easier until my face was coverd in a very thin layer of a clear gel. This is a brilliant feature. There is no more worries about irritated the skin with multiple strokes as the razor glides over the face easily. All the men out there reading this just try it and see, you ll love it. The gel smelt good in a stereotypical masculine way and washes off with just normal water. The shave itself was very close indeed, I didn t need to shave for 3 days following my first use of this ( believe me, thats a good length of time ). Each blade lasted about 3/4 uses before it was feeling blunt and I changed. This isn t too bad a record and the little bar that provides the gel provided adequate lubrication for each of the uses. The only bad point I found using this was the cost of buying replacements. Its just short of    5 for a set of 3 blades and using a simple bit of maths that means you get about 36 days of that freshly shaven feeling for about    5. It might not sound like a lot but to a student its quite a lot and works out at about    50 a year.The true quality of this product was only brought home to me last night when I ran out of my mach 3 blades and had to use my spare protector 3d razor. It wasn t pretty. I ve definatly found the blade of choice for me.Thanks for the read.     ', '    Having to shave every day can be such a chore. Just think of all those extra minutes I could have in bed every morning if I didn   t have to shave, but unfortunately I am one of those people that needs to shave every day. Until recently I used to use an electric shaver because I thought it was easier and quicker but that was before I discovered the Gillette Mach 3 razor.The Gillette Mach 3 razor has been around for quite a while. It was launched in 1998 as the world   s first triple blade razor and has since become the world   s most successful razor, but what is the secret of its phenomenal success? To begin with its initial success can be put down to some very clever marketing and advertising, but beyond the hype there has to be a decent product to keep people coming back. I have friends who are on their fourth or fifth Mach 3 razors but as I said earlier I have only just acquired my first.The Design FeaturesIt has a forward pivot movement for a closer more comfortable shaveIt has a single point cartridge docking for easy loadingIt has an indicator-lubricating strip, which lets you know when you are no longer experiencing the optimal shave.It has open cartridge architecture for easy cleaning.It has an Ergonomic handle design for improved handling.General AppearanceThe Mach 3 has a very trendy and modern appearance. It is packaged in a turquoise and black case with the razor held inside a transparent bubble. It is very light and easy to control; there is a rubber grip on the handle, which also prevents it slipping out of your hand.PerformancePersonally it is quite unlike anything that I have experienced before. The shave is very close and without any cuts or nips. It leaves the skin feeling soft and refreshed. In fact so close is the shave that I now need only shave once a day in the morning. Following each shave the Mach 3 is very easy to clean.Value for MoneyI paid    3.99 for my Mach 3 razor from Wilkinson   s, which came with 2 spare blades. The cost of replacement blades are however quite expensive so be warned. The cost at Asda is currently as followsPack of 4 blades =    3.96Pack of 8 blades =    6.90SummaryOverall the Mach 3 is an excellent razor, which really does live up to and beyond its expectations. There are cheaper razors on the market but I think you   d be hard pushed to find one better than this. Thank you Gillette     ', '    This is a great razor. The look of it is very modern and fresh. the razor has three blades which are designed to lessen pressure on the face and therfor reduce the likelyhood of you cutting yourself. This combined with the swivel head mean that you get a close shave, though there is a reduced chance of you cutting yourself.    this product can be combined with others in the gillets range for example the shaving gel, to lessen further the chances, whilst ensuring a close shave. I found it easy to use, and relatively inexpensive at in and around    3.50 for the razor and about    1 for the blades.     Would advise this product to anyone, due to its ease of use and also its price. An excellent buy     ', '    I have sensitive skin and therefore alternate between wet and dry (electric) shaving. Wet shaving has often been a problem for me, I tend to cut very easily and also get a rash from wet shaving. I am left with two choices; either grow a beard (not for me) or alternate between wet and dry shaving. I first bought the Gillette mach 3 when I needed a new razor. I tend to try new ones in the hope that one day I will find a razor that will be better than anything I have tried in the past does. To be honest I could not see how three blades could be better than two, once the beard has gone it has gone. I am happy to be able to report that although these are expensive the results really are well worth it.I compliment these blades by using a shaving gel rather than the ordinary foam. The gel tends to assist in moisturising the beard and skin. I have now been using the mach 3 for a few months and have found I have not yet cut myself whilst shaving. Hmmmm I wonder if I have just tempted fate.They glide over the skin easier than a conventional blade and also easier than a twin blade system.I have found that cleaning the hair from between the blades presents no problems. This is unlike some single or twin blades where the hair tends to clog up and can effectively reduce the life of the blade. The mach 3 does not seem to suffer this problem.Changing the blade is easy just place the old head in the space on the pack (although this is in keeping with most razors, I do like this as it keeps little fingers and sharp objects apart), press the button on the handle to disconnect and then place the handle over a new blade press and hey presto  The only downfall is the cost, they are not the cheapest blades on the market.Having said that, they do last a long time and I like the idea that I have not cut myself using this system.Since my eldest Daughter moved out I have also found that the blades life expectancy has been increased by a long way. I am sure this is a coincidence, I mean do you think my Daughter would use my razor??     ', '    Let s get one thing straight. I grudge paying over the odds for toiletries. After all, we blokes have to shave because if we don t, we look and feel grubby. Especially me - I m not a hairy bloke. My wife has more hair on her arms than I do - and no, she s not desperately hairy either  If I let my  beard  grow, it spends at least a fortnight growing into a thoroughly unimpressive mass of stubble, complete with bald patches  Consequently, I need to shave, because I d spend too long growing a beard that would look half decent.If I was ruthless, I d stick to the good old Gilette Sensor. It gave me a pretty good shave. But the thing about the Mach 3 is that it genuinely is worth the extra over the Sensor.At between    4 and    5 for 4 blades, I reckon it s incredibly expensive, but I pay it because it s COMPARATIVELY good value. Your first one (ie with the razor itself) will set you back about the same (   5ish) including 2 blades.The handle is well designed - good grip shape and those nice rubberised grooves that are so in vogue with designers these days. It s basically bulletproof and unless you lose it you won t have to buy another.The shave is quick and comfortable - no skin irritation here - and the blades last well. Although that may be something to do with my soft, downy hair  My only concern is that the  original  Mach 3 will go the same way as the original Sensor. It s clear why this happened - Gillette want people to buy their newest, most profitable product. It became increasingly difficult for me to get normal non-Excel blades, and as I said before, I grudged paying the extra for no appreciable benefit. The Mach 3 Turbo is out now ( Turbo ??? I ask you - whatever will those marketing characters come up with next...?), and I predict that over the next couple of years, standard Mach 3 blades will be harder to come by.For folks who do get razor-burn, here are a couple of wee tips:-  Never shave first thing in the morning - at the very least have a shower first, or shave last thing at night instead if your hair s growth-rate allows it.-  Experiment a lot with different foams/gels/oils. My favourite is King of Shaves - either the oil or the gel. Also, they have a lot more advice for comfortable shaves on their bottles/tubes Though it pains me to say it, the Mach 3 is one toiletry product that I believe represents good value for money. But only relatively...     ', '    When i got my electric razor, i new it was time for me to have to give up my normal everyday shaving razor, but i was gutted because i had used this for nearly a year now, and i had not had a razor as good as this.The Mach 3, is probably the best shaver available in the UK, that is not a electronic one.The mach 3 itself was introduced into the UK in 1998, and since has become one of the best brought razors on the market.The first thing you notice about these, is that they are 3 blades per razor blade itself.  This is to give you a closer shave and to make it more easy for you to remove every little hair on your chin.When i first used this, i was also using Gillette Shaving Foam, which again is one of the best by the way.  When you do shave using this product, it is so easy to do.If you have ever used normal everyday throw away razors, you will know what i mean when i say burn, kill, rip, and pull.  Yep these 4 words come into it everyday, as these always happen when you do use dodgy throw away razors.  This is why the Mach 3 is so good.When you take a sweep of your chin, or face, there is no ripping sensation like with other razors, no burning feeling after you have shaved, and no killing feeling as you shave, it really is a clean, easy shave. ', '    So you re probably wondering what some young un like me, who only shaves once or twice a week is doing writing a review on a product which already has 108 to its name?Well, I m a little behind everyone else, in that I never use the latest thing because they re always more expensive. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re weighing the Gillette Mach 3 razor, here’s the lowdown from folks who’ve taken it for a spin—warts and all, with a dash of my own skeptical eye. First off, yes, those replacement blades come with a price tag that might make your wallet wince compared to other brands. But many users argue that the quality and longevity justify the splurge—think of it as investing in a shave that lasts longer and feels smoother, rather than swapping blades every other week like a frantic barber.

The Mach 3’s triple blade tech isn’t just marketing fluff; it genuinely cuts down the number of strokes needed, which means fewer nicks and less irritation—a blessing if you’re prone to razor burn or have sensitive skin. The lubricating strip combined with the spring-mounted head lets the razor glide over your face like a well-oiled dance partner, adapting to your contours and delivering a close, refreshing shave that leaves stubble in the dust.

Now, about the advertising—some users find Gillette’s hype a bit over the top, bordering on “too good to be true.” I get it; the slick commercials can feel like they’re selling you a magic wand rather than a razor. But the consensus is that the product largely lives up to its promises, which is more than I can say for many beauty ads.

If you’re a bargain hunter like me, the upfront blade cost might sting, but the durability—sharpness lasting two weeks or more—means fewer purchases over time. So, it’s a classic case of paying a bit more now to save later. Just don’t expect this to be the eco-friendly hero of your grooming kit; sustainability isn’t its selling point.

In short, the Mach 3 is a solid performer for those who want a close, comfortable shave without constant blade swaps—just be ready to pay a premium for that convenience and quality.

Yes, of course everyone s hair lightens in the sunshine, as does mine, and obviously the actual light you are in affects how your hair looks, but I am being serious, one minute it s really blonde, the next it goes to a dark blonde/light brown colour, and other times I m strawberry blonde with even a hint of ginger occassionally. But, as with any shampoo, don t use every wash as it could make your hair greasy. I am absolutly sick of this miserable weather  K xxx        ', '    Shopping is a necessity, whether it is on the internet or in person, and although I have tried Tesco.net I prefer to drive the few miles and walk around the store as you sometimes see bargains, and I love bargains especially the BOGOF variety Those of you who have read my Timotei Anti-dandruff shampoo review know why I had to use it instead of my normal shampoo, but I quickly put the new bottle of shampoo in the bathroom ready for the next hair wash, and my other bottle of Timotei did not disappoint either.*BOTTLE*Size about 18cm high, with a narrow base in a golden yellow pearlised plastic, with a more orange gold pearly flip lid. Even though I ll be a red dot for years on Ciao, I m going for Gold for my hair colour      ', '    This shampoo is meant for Blonde to light brown hair, I have what I would like to call strawberry blonde hair     that is it was once very ginger and over the years is now only a very pale ginger     thank god   So I hoped that this shampoo would help my hair as it is supposed to help lighten the natural colour of your hair and embolden highlights.**PACKAGING**This shampoo comes in a what I presume is supposed to be a golden colour bottle, The main body of the bottle is a yellow metallically colour and the lid is a deeper shade of yellow, almost orange. There are other varieties of this shampoo available, but to be honest I don   t know what they are and how good they are, but if they are half as good as this one, then I would recommend giving them a try.**CONTACT**Lever Faberge Ltd, Freepost, Admail 1000, London SW1A 2XXTel: 0800 085 2720     ', '    Being quite proud of the fact that I am a natural blonde, I regularly try different products to maintain the glossiness and blondeness of it. ', '    The first shampoo I remember using as a kid was chamomile shampoo, the Garnier one (I don   t think it is available here). Obviously there was not one bottle of shampoo for each member of the family (yet), and the majority of children (2 out of  3) being blond, and my hair not being jet black either, I used chamomile shampoo too. Later I realized that chamomile was known for its lightening properties on light hair, so I started using it again because my hair had become too dark to my liking. The result was not that obvious, and anyway I had to stop using it because I thought I was allergic to chamomile, as it made my scalp very itchy. Fast forward, last June I read about Timotei Golden Highlights in some newspaper, and decided to look for it in Boots, where I found it, on offer. I think it was    2.29 for the shampoo, and I got the conditioner free. The bottle of shampoo is nice and curvy. Its base is wider than its top, so it is quite stable. The lid is at the top (no, this is not as obvious as it sounds) and is of the flip-up kind. It differs from the rest of the bottle, as it is pale golden orange, while the bottle is pale yellow. It looks as though there is a bit missing at the front of the lid, but of course it is done on purpose, to help you open the lid using your thumb, very practical as it means it is no nail-breaking operation. The plastic the 250ml bottle is made of is not see through, so I have to hold the bottle in front of the light to see how much is left, blinding myself for 5 minutes in the process. It is quite easy to use all the shampoo, as you can squeeze the bottle without too much effort.The blurb both on the front and on the back of the bottle is in English AND French, which means there is a lot of writing. At the top, it says    Highlights innovation    written in black on a gold-yellow background. Well, chamomile has been used in shampoos for a while, but they must be claiming their formula is better, plus new products tend to be more appealing to us consumers.Then comes the name of the brand, Timotei, written in a nice font (do you reckon they might tell me which font it is they used if I phoned them on their free UK helpline 0800 085 2861, or they might be nicer over in Ireland on     not free-- 1850 40 40 60) and in black.The main feature at the front of the bottle is a large drawing of a flower, which must be chamomile (although it looks more like a daisy to me), with its white petals and orangy-yellow centre, and just a hint of its green leaves.A yellow circle, in the    approved    stamp fashion, says    Sun kissed camomile   , then an orange rectangle says    Natural extract   . Finally, at the very bottom, it says that the shampoo is to be used on    Blonde to light brown hair   . At the back, it gives more precision :    Natural, highlighted or colored blonde to light brown hair   , that widens the spectrum.I had decided to use this shampoo, but I also had decided to dye my hair first. The result was very disappointing, as the permanent    light brown    dye made my hair darker than it was before I dyed it, I always have trouble deciding what color my hair is.    dark brown at the back with blond strands and light red highlights, getting lighter in the summer    would be a pretty accurate description. ', '    Having had blond hair as a child I had steadily seen my hair get darker over the years until it reached the light brown colour it is now. ', '    Recently I ve become quite addicted to Collection 2000, I have many of their products, so when I needed some new foundation , I instantly went to my Collection 2000 stand.The good thing about this foundation is not just the price, at just    1.79, my expectations weren t exactly what you would call high, but I knew it wouldn t let me down. Users with blonde or light brown hair have noticed that their highlights become more visible over time, thanks to the natural camomile extract that gradually lightens hair. While it won’t replace a professional lightening treatment, it’s a nice, low-commitment option to brighten your hair gradually and maintain softness and manageability.

In summary, if you want a gentle, natural, and wallet-friendly shampoo that subtly enhances your highlights while keeping your hair healthy and shiny, Timotei Golden Highlights Camomile Shampoo fits the bill. Just be patient with the gradual effect and enjoy the softness and shine it brings along the way.

product_reviews: ['    I joined this book club late last year, as I buy books on a very regular basis, to provide me with some light relief while commuting, and thought it would save me some money.I ordered my introductory books (I seem to recall 5 books for 99p or soemthing similar) they duly arrived within a few days(well 4 of them did with a replacement for one that was out of stock)I have not received another book yet (on my counting) it has been five months since I ordered and paid for this introductory offer. I regularly receive a statement of account asking for payment for the editors choice that has been despatched. I have not yet received any further books, and have tried to sort out the mess with QPD to no avail. I have confirmed my address (which they have correct as I receive my statement of account) on several occasions, via telephone and email but have made no progress in tracking down the mysterious disappearing books. QPDs attitude seems to be that they have despatched them so I must have received them  I continue to attempt to resolve the mystery. Their regular 2 for    xx and    3 for xx deals are good value, if you have an interest in the volumes on offer. Were it not for the disappearing books I would be content with the service but until this is resolved I really cannot recommend this club.      ', '    I   ve been a member of Quality Paperbacks Direct (QPD) for about 6 months now so I probably have had adequate experience of the company to write an accurate opinion on the subject.  I   ve also noticed their advertising on the internet becoming more and more rigorous so I   d like to take the opportunity to advise all my peers in the Ciao community against the gimmicks of QPD.Firstly, what is QPD?QPD stands for Quality Paperbacks Direct and is a company which offers a wide range of titles all in paperback form at up to   off the recommended retail price.  Unlike on the high street where you usually have to wait a few months for a recently published hardback book to be printed in paperback, but QPD offers exclusive paperback editions so you avoid the wait. How do I join?QPD offer a very enticing introductory offer of 5 books for    5 (including p p) and also a free document case.  I was thrilled by this amazing offer and ordered a selection of books, some fiction and some reference to help with my English Literature degree.  Your choice of introductory titles can be taken from a wide range which are listed on the site under the following categories: cult reading, light reading, literary fiction, non-fiction, prizewinners, thrillers, true lives and QPD recommends. I have just visited the site and there is a current choice of 94 titles for new members which, in my opinion, is quite an extensive selection.  QPD also invites new members through advertisements in magazines and papers.  Whilst the offer is usually the same, the choice of titles is less broad so I would definitely recommend consulting the website before making your final selection of 5 books.  When will I receive my books?My first order came in just over 2 weeks which seemed a decent enough delivery period. Subsequent orders though have taken well over 4 weeks on occasions to reach me and I   m beginning to find myself somewhat disillusioned with the level of service I am (or am not) receiving from QPD.Your commitmentWell of course as with anything that appears to be to good to be true     it probably is. With QPD you are committed to buying a further 5 books from the company during your first year of membership.  Otherwise, you will be charged the full recommended retail price for your first order.  Be warned though, the lowest price books and sale items    do not count towards your club commitment    and so fulfilling your commitment may turn out to be quite expensive. Making payment on your accountI have set up my account online so I pay over their secure server using my debit card.  You pay after receiving and approving your books which is good and you also receive a detailed monthly statement which is very helpful.  Alternative payment methods include sending a cheque or postal order, paying over the counter at a bank or with a debit / credit card over the phone.Customer ServicesAs I said earlier, now I am a member, my orders seem to take weeks on end (literally) to reach me. I have had one set of books that never arrived and I e-mailed the customer service department regarding this.  They offered little help and simply sent me a form to fill in to confirm I hadn   t received the order.  I have done this and am still awaiting a response from them.  My overall impressionsThe introductory offer from QPD seems like excellent value for money but the 5 book commitment means you will be paying for your first order at the end of the day.  The service I have received has been poor and books take a long time to arrive.  I therefore wouldn   t suggest using QPD to buy books for gifts or research purposes as you can   t guarantee that they will arrive in time.  Whilst their offer of    exclusive paperbacks    seems enticing, beware of the paper quality as this is often quite poor in comparison to shop bought books.  Also make sure you reject the monthly editor   s choice if you don   t wan to be bombarded with unwanted books.  I do this online which is quick and easy or you can do it using their automated telephone service or by post.  If you forget, you will have to pay to return the unwanted goods which cost    2 last time I checked.Overall I   ve not been impressed at all with QPD.  I   m hoping to fulfill my commitment after next payday and then I will end my membership as soon as possible.  Stick to somewhere like bookpeople.co.uk who offer the bargains without he commitment instead.           ', '    Oh no, you re thinking, another mail order book club with those hidden catches - but for once this isn t the case QPD - Quality Paperbacks Direct - delivered the goods all right. I responded to one of those many magazine back page advertisements as it seemed to good to be true and too good to pass up. The introductory offer was 3 paperback books for    1 each plus postage (   2.95) - a total of    5.95 for three non-abridged paperbacks?? Yes  Really I selected my order - a book on law, a Halliwells film guide and a Learn How to do Everything book and posted off the form. Within about 10 days I received the order - well packed, exactly what I wanted and good quality - the same versions you can buy in the High Street. I made a saving of about    40 Here comes the good part  Like most book clubs they send a monthly catalogue to you with an Editors Recommendation which you can accept by not responding or reject by responding ( you can do this online too). And that s it - no obligation to buy ANY further books whatsoever. Most of these clubs require you to buy a minimum of, say, 6 regular price books in the first year or similar but this club holds no such obligation. After receiving your introductory books you need never buy anything from them again.I can only presume that they can afford to operate this way by having built up such an enthusistic and loyal customer base due to their competitive prices and good service.Well worth a look.     ', '    A few people have already written ops on QPD, and all three describe it as a genuine no-commitment club.  Well   8211; sorry   8211; that  8217;s where you  8217;re wrong.  It may have been a no-commitment club when you joined, when I joined, when my mother joined   8211; but now things are very different indeed   I  8217;ll tell you about my and my ex-boyfriend  8217;s (Stuart) experiences to prove the point.My mum had joined QPD a couple of years back, and had been very happy with it.  So when I saw an advert in the Radio Times, saying choose five books for 99p each, plus postage of    2.95, and that you would NEVER have to buy another book again, I thought great   8211; I will definitely join this, as I love reading, and this was before my big win on streetsonline.  The books I chose were varied, the name QPD simply means Quality Paperbacks Direct.  I seem to remember buying   8216;Charlotte Gray  8217; by Sebastian Faulks,   8216;Life isn  8217;t all ha ha he he  8217; by Meera Syal, and a new biography of Shakespeare by Anthony Holden, plus Stuart chose two others.  My experience of QPD was good   8211; the books arrived relatively quickly, within three weeks (although they can often be sent a lot quicker than this from the net), and paying less than eight pounds for such books was a major bargain.  They are sent out by the delivery firm White Arrow, who will call back if you are not in, although you are also given the choice on the form when you join if there is a safe place where they can leave the books.  For example, I live in a house which has been converted into 5 flats, so it  8217;s pretty safe just to leave them outside my own door.  Each month I was then sent the QPD catalogue, with no obligation to buy anything   8211; and actually I never have bought anything, because as I mentioned, I won    1000 of credit with streetsonline and so that is still keeping me in books   You do have to make sure you cancel the editor  8217;s choice each month however   8211; but this is very easy and there are three ways to do it.  You can either ring the national rate number, and do it automatically simply by typing in your membership number and pressing a few buttons.  Mind you, I find that fairly frequently, this number has technical difficulties   It  8217;s just as well then that they have a website as well, you can log on here with your membership number to start with, and then you are given a user name, and from here you can choose to buy books, or to reject the editor  8217;s choice   8211; you then get an email confirming that it is rejected.  There is also the option to cancel by post   8211; but why pay the cost of a stamp when the internet way is probably for many people much cheaper?  I also prefer getting the email confirming my rejection   8211; then if they do ever send me the book, I can prove it was rejected.  This has never happened yet though So what sort of books can you buy each month?  Well, the magazine is actually pretty good, with a variety of newly published books   8211; take this month for example, there is a special offer on Peter Ackroyd  8217;s   8220;London the Biography  8221;   8211; down from    25 to    12.50   8211; so even with postage added this a great bargain.  Of course, they are not all as good a bargain as this   Authors this month featured in the 32 page magazine include David Lodge, Sebastian Faulks, Simon Schama, Martin Amis, Margaret Atwood, and there are pages on crime, romance, lifestyle, and cooking.  There really is something for everyone here, and you can buy all these books in paperback for much less than the hardback versions which are being sold in the shops.  If Trampus  8217; review on Jamie Oliver has whetted your appetite, then as a QPD paperback,   8220;The Naked Chef  8221; is only 8.99.  You notice the savings mount up if you buy a few books at a time, otherwise the 2.95 postage can limit the savings you  8217;ll make.  The quality of the books, since they are QPD paperbacks is also ever so slightly inferior at times   8211; paper quality for example is not quite as good as you might be used to   8211; a bit thinner usually.  However, this is not really a major consideration of mine To pay, you can either send a cheque off to QPD, ring and quote your credit card number (they don  8217;t take switch yet) or use the internet   8211; again, I believe this to be the easiest way, and you can check up on the progress of any orders this way too.  It  8217;s nice to be able to browse through the little magazine, and then go on line and order, having already decided what you will be buying.  The magazine itself is quite interesting too - sometimes giving a bit of biographical information about partiuclar authors, and giving brief reviews of the books featured.So   8211; you  8217;re probably thinking this sounds like a fairly good idea   8211; but maybe aren  8217;t sure, because with the likes of Amazon etc, would you really be saving that much money?  But   8211; oh yes, there  8217;s no commitment, so you can try it and see   8211; nothing to lose   Well at least in theory.  Thing is, QPD have moved away from this no-commitment policy.  My mum got sent a form saying that if she recommended a friend to the club she too would receive a free book, so my ex decided to join himself.  We all read the form, checked it was no commitment still (mum and I in particular are always very sceptical of things which seem too good to be true) and so Stuart joined.  However, a year letter, he was getting letters from QPD telling him if he didn  8217;t meet the commitment he would have to pay in full for the five books he had ordered when he joined   8211; totalling around    75    He tried to say that he joined under a no-commitment scheme, but was informed that that no longer existed, and that since he had no proof that was how he joined, he would have to pay the full charge or order 6 new books   8211; 6     Most other book clubs I have joined require you to buy only 4 in the first year   8211; Mango for example being an example of this (and is run by the same group as well )My mum then phoned to see if she could sort it out (Stuart was always a bit of a wuss) but was told that seeing as Stuart had no proof he had joined the no commitment scheme, he would simply have to buy the books.  In a way, this was his fault, since he should have kept the welcoming letter which set out the terms and conditions, but he was sure, as we were, it was the same scheme as us he had joined.  It was a pretty sneaky trick of QPD to change their scheme   Mum ended up cancelling her membership as the QPD customer service woman was so rude   Stuart ended up paying for 6 books   8211; and even then, one of the ones he was sent was one totally different to the one he had ordered.  So   8211; it certainly seems as if QPD have changed their scheme, and to be honest, because of this, I wouldn  8217;t really recommend them to anyone   8211; sure, the books are cheaper, and the introductory offer is fantastic, but do you really want to be tied to buy 6 books in your first year? What if your financial situation changes?  What if you see the books you want cheaper elsewhere   8211; and now, with all the internet booksellers, this can so easily happen.  I would say if you are a genuine booklover, shop around   8211; the deals at QPD are no better than elsewhere, and books can often arrive quicker from the internet as well   8211; 24hrs from Amazon as opposed to 3 weeks with QPD.       ', '    It is a year since I joined Quality Paperbacks Direct (QPD) and so I thought it was time for a review.As the title of this opinion suggests there really are no strings attached. You tick 5 books priced at 99p each and then send off the flyer to:QPD,Guild House,Farnsby StreetSwindon XSN99 9XI sent off for 5 books to the value of    52.95 - it cost me    5.00 including postage and packaging. The books were of good quality and I received them within 14 days. The range of books is very wide from popular fiction to non-fictional autobiographies. There are literary sections, thrillers, romances and recent best sellers. What you see in Waterstones is here, delivered to your door. I think it reasonable to pay    6-7 for a paperback novel (the hardbacks are    11-12 - but have patience and wait for the soft copy) and they very often have good deals for buying from the same author or ordering more than one book at a time. This is more than most bookshops offer. My last order was for 8 books (2 sets of 4 for    9.99 a set) with postage and packaging it all came to    22.33 and they even included a complementory book.Since joining I have received a newsletter every month with a club magazine - all you do if you do not want to order or to receive the Editor s choice is to put a cross in the box and send the form back. It will cost you a second class stamp. Remember to cancel the Editor s choice or they will send it to you. You can of course send it back but this involves phoning the Account and Order line which is a nightmare and requesting return postage.The Customer Account and Order line on 0870 1650165 is a major downfall. It is automated i.e dial 1 for account details, dial 2 for ordering, dial 3 for insanity and dial M for Murder - sorry but they drive me insane and if by chance your enquiry does not come under the categories selected then you are stuffed because they don t have a hold the line for an operator option. Grrrrrrrrr.Having said that I have only had one cause to use the  quot;NO-help quot; line and that was because the newsletter got lost and I recieved the EC. A word of warning it cost    2.00 to return an item unless it is their mistake. The line is open Mon. to Fri. 8.30am -11.30pm. Saturdays 8.30 -4.20pm - why it is only those times when it is automated I don t know - maybe robots need their beauty sleep.The invoices are clear and easy to understand - the items and the prices clearly indicated with how much your account owes. You can order and pay by phone if your blood pressure can stand it - 08701650165; you can do it on the net apparently but as there is no website detail this seems unlikely. You can fax them when the boss is out on 08701650222. Or you can do as I do and post them a cheque written out to QPD after choosing from the magazine.They can set up a direct debit or telebanking option or you can use your credit card. They want you to pay within a certain timeframe which is usually within 10 days of receiving your statement. There is a late payment fee if you are overdue.The postage and packaging on a normal order is    2.35. The return of goods comes under your Statutory Rights thing and should be withing 28 days of purchse.I have been pleased with my purchases - 13 more books in the last year. I have taken advantage of the reduced price for 2 books by the same author - usually c.   12 for the two. They arrive promptly via White Arrow - so somebody signs for them and they aren t left to go soggy on the doorstep.If you are not satisfied you can cancel your membership by writing to them at;QPDGuild House,Farnsby Street,Swindon XSN99 9XXBut I won t be writing as they have served me well.Thanks for reading. Mel     ', '    I love reading.  I enjoy it so much and often find myself going through two or three books a month.  Unfortunately though, being a student I cannot often afford to buy the latest releases, so I have to rely on either second hand copies or hand-me-downs.All of this was about to change though, as three weeks ago, I came across www.qpd.co.uk.  QPD stands for Quality Paperbacks Direct and the company is a part of BCA, which is the largest mail-order book company in Europe.  Just to give you an idea of its size, BCA runs other companies such as BOL, Just Good Books and FSF Book Club besides QPD.Registering is easy, as you can register online, or via their premium rate number and what is best is that you get your books before you even pay, so you have to be 18 or over.  (I am not but they don   t know that )The first thing that attracted me to QPD was probably the introductory offer.  Like other companies in the BCA group, QPD offers a truly unbelievable bargain to join, but stings you with a commitment to buy five more books within your first year of membership or face paying the full RRP of your introductory offer, of which mine was over    50.For my introductory offer, I was allowed to choose 5 books for    5 from a selection.  This price included delivery and a free gift, which is currently a document case.  I chose five of the best books available: Jamie   s Kitchen, The King of Torts, Man and Boy, The Good Women of China and About a Boy.  All of the books arrived in excellent condition and were delivered by a courier.  My books arrived within about two weeks of joining.When your books arrive you are obliged to set up an Internet account with your member number and you also must pay for your books within ten days of signing for your package.  In your introductory case, included are many different catalogues of books, which, might I add offer very cheap products and other documents informing you of ways to pay and other adverts and stuff.The whole reason why QPD is so cheap is that they sell paperback versions of the best books.  Taking for example one of my books called The King of Torts by John Grisham     this is meant to be a thick hardback but instead, I was sent a paperback version, which I was just as happy with and more than usual, QPD will have many new releases before they are even released.  Additionally, the company orders in bulk, which must save them a fare whack.After you have joined, been sent your introductory books and other information, you will be allowed to buy from an even bigger range of games, books, films, and computer software.  I personally have found the range to be outstanding and prices are generally between 30  and 80  cheaper than other retailers.Ordering online is simple.  You just log in and add books you your basket like you would in a normal online retailer.  You also pay a flat fee of    2.99 delivery no matter how many books you order.  Remember, you must buy five more books within the first year of membership and some lower priced books do not count towards your five-book commitment     but these books clearly state this.You are sent a members catalogue and order form once a month, from which you can also order.  This is just as simple and payment can be sent with your order or ten days after receipt of it.  They accept cheques or postal orders and the four major credit cards, Switch, Delta, Visa and MasterCard.  Unfortunately, they do not accept Solo or Visa Electron yet Customer service is AWFUL.  You usually get a reply within 2 weeks via email but you are ALWAYS given the right information.  The telephone line must be the same for all BCA companies because the telephonist gives some pretty general information and you can be waiting for hours.  They have access to all your account details so you are always able to check your details if you cannot access the Internet.Overall, I would recommend ordering and managing your account online, because you can order, pay and enquire about anything in an instant.  You can also see your statements and previous payments.  The website is clearly laid out and the website is the same format as all BCA company websites I would recommend the company, because if you are intending to buy loads of books the commitment will not affect you anyway, but if you do not want commitment, but still want cheap books, try www.bookpeople.co.uk.     ', '    I have been a member of QPD (Quality Paperbacks Direct) for about five years now, and have to say, its not bad.  It is a genuine  quot;no commitment quot; book club, which supplies paperback equivalents of newly published hardbacks, in all categories of adult fiction (and a few typical book club nonfiction categories like health, well being, etc).  Generally the books are  quot;literary quot; rather than  quot;popular quot;, but if you want the latest Hanif Kureshi, Barbara Kingsolver, Jonathan Coe, PD James etc, then this is the place for you.  The paperbacks are usually  quot;large format quot; which I think means that they take the innards of the hardback and just re-cover it - I could be wrong here, but they certainly look and feel like the hardbacks with a soft cover on.  The magazine is quite a nice read, although the reviews are more in the way of advertising blurb than honest assesments of the book - however, these probably supplement reviews you ve read elsewhere so maybe it doesn t matter all that much.The prices aren t bad. I suppose they re typically about one pound more than the eventual paperback edition will be (about 7.99 would be typical price), but you don t have to wait a year for it to come out.  So you get to read the latest releases, while the reviews are still appearing in the papers, but for a significant reduction.  As with all book clubs, the catch is the postage and packing, which usually adds on another 2.95 or so.  The price however does not escalate if you order more than one book at a time so there s an economy of scale here.  Very often there are good deals offered too - for example, I just bought Jonathan Coe s new book The Rotter s Club and got his previous paperback as well for about another four pounds, and I didn t pay have to pay double postage either.  If you don t want the editors selection, its quite easy to reject it - either send the reply slip back to them or go on the website, log in and click  quot;Reject Editors choice quot;.  What could be easier.  The website is reasonable, but nothing like as good as amazon of course, but then that s not really comparing like with like.If you order a book and don t like it, you can return it, but as usual with book clubs, you don t get the postage back.  I suppose the biggest recommendation for a book club is that in the time I ve been a member I ve never been mis-billed, I ve never been sent the editors choice when I didn t want it, and I ve never had the wrong book sent to me.  And this includes periods of up to six months or so when I ve not ordered anything at all.       ', '    I am very confused by the recent comment written by weebagpus about the QPD bookclub and whether there is any further commitment to buy or not.I had been a member a few years ago and recently received an invitation to rejoin with the offer that I describe below. This was on March 1st and all the literature I have got, stresses that there is no commitment to buy another book.My only thought might be that they have different offers for different people, i.e. if they are trying to tempt you back, then they give the no commitment offer as you have bought books in the past. However if you are a new member then there might be some obligation. Clearly you are right that people need to be very careful.In the past when books have been sent incorrectly and they have implied that I ordered them I just kept them until they prepaid labels. It usually takes a bit of time and you keep on having to email them to remind them but it usually works in the end. Anyway here s my opinion on QPDQPD or quality paperbacks direct has been around for a few years but has recently launched an online web site. The biggest advantage it has is that you get a good opening offer, we got 6 books for    5 including, River Cafe 2 and Bridet Jones Diary, good offers in a monthly magazine and most importantly, no commitment to ever buy another book. One of the books we chose as part of our opening offer wasn t in stock so they gave us a    10 voucher to redeem against any future books. As the name suggests all the books are paperback but they are released in paperback a long time before they appear in paperback in the shop. For example Sebastian Foulkes new novel  On Green Dolphin Street  which has only just come out in hardback is already available in paperback for    8.98 as compared with the hardback price of    16.99.If you choose to buy his novels  Birdsong  and  The Girl at Lion D Or   at the same time you get all three for    14.99. Other books that have been available in recent months include Pat Barker   Border Crossing  Amy Tan   The Bonesetters Daughter  Frank McCourt   Angelas Ashes  Margaret Atwood  The Blind Assassin  plus many others Although you receive a magazine each month and have to accept or cancel the editors choice, there is no time limit for which you have to remain a member and you dont have to purchase any other books The web site is well set out and you can check your orders, pay on line plus all the other things you might need to do and if all else fails you can revert to the post       ', '    This is one of the better book clubs around. I was drawn to the club because there was no commitment which was a welcome relief. The offer I got was 5 books for a    1 each which I thought was fantastic.Whenever I order a book they arrive in great condition and if it is too large for a postbox is delivered by a courier. Each month the catalogue comes with 5 or more offer leaflets which really do offer substantial savings. The main catalogue is well catagorised and some good savings are to be made. There are frequent offers such as buy two books and get White Teeth for    2.99. QPD doesn t just sell fiction books. They also do cookery,kids, humour etc. All the usual types of books found in a book club I have never felt pressured into ordering a book because there has never been any commitments to fulfil. If you don t want the editors choice then just return the order form with a cross in the editors choice box. Orders can also be placed online although the site is a bit basic. I have never ordered from this site before so I couldn t comment on it.My only real criticism is that because they are hardbacks converted specially to paperback for the club the books are usually larger then regular paperbacks. This makes them harder to carry around but is a small sacrifice to pay for the savings you get and the chance to be one of the first to have a particular book in paperback.All in all a very good book club.     ', '    QPD. Not a fruitiers wet dream where all those of a fruitful disposition can buy their ideal Quinces, Pears and Damsons.  Nor is it a club for Queens Persistently in Drag.  Unfortunately.  No, QPD stands simply for Quality Paperbacks Direct and it supplies - you guessed it - quality papers, direct from the printer to you, dear reader (oops, sorry - got a touch of the Jane Austen s then )I am a bibliophile, unable to walk past a Waterstones (or any other bookshop), without coming out with an armful of  must have  books, which tempted me away from the narrow path of financial frugality by looking, well, interesting.  There are members of this Ciao enclave who can vouch for this, having witnessed a Medusa biblio-feeding frenzy.  Not pretty, but those of you familiar with  Trainspotting  are aware of the uglier side of addiction.  Believe me, books and heroin are not that different.Anyway, QPD.  Why did I join?  Like most people, I was tempted by one of those lovely offers they place in the magazine supplements of the weekend braodsheets.  I was especially tempted becasue they were offering to sell me David Crystal s fantastic  Cambridge Encyclopaedia of the English Language  at the unmissable price of    3:00, instead of the less appealing, habe-to-think-about-it-twice price of    25:00.  Who could resist? Certainly not a sad, late-twenties English teacher with a cash flow problem, a teaching A level English Language without a clue problem, and a penchant for small bearded Welsh chaps who look not unlike Merlin. So, I joined QPD and I really have not looked back ever since.  Every month or so they send you a truly no obligation club magazine filled with all sorts of fiction, poetry, biographies and all sorts of other goodies just crying out to you to give them a go.  In addition to the editor s choice of the month (which is always a bargain, saving you in the region of    20:00 on a tempting twosome of recently published titles), they very often to  Two for    9:99  offers on a range of fiction.  Even the single editions tend to be reasonably priced (Example: paperback edition of  The Blind Assassin  by Margaret Atwood at    8:99, compared to the hard back price of    16:99).  The only problem with QPD editions, and this is a problem commented on by my finnickity, Virgo-ascendant beloved of a husband, rathe than a personal complaint, is that many QPD editions come in less than conventional sizes, causing a lack of height uniformity on your bookshelves.  personally, I quite like this eclectic array, but, well .... some people ....?In terms of quality of service, I can honestly say I have had absolutely no problems with this book club.  Overy six weeks or so I place my order (see below), and two weeks later I come home to find an exciting little package waiting for me, filled with exciting treasures, and undiscovered worlds.  MMMMMMMM - wonderful On the whole I very rarely bother with a written order form, preferring instead to order my books / pay my bill, via th telephone helpline.  This automated service is simple and efficient and, in my experience has only one drawback: for some reason it does not operate at the weekends.  I don t quite see why this should be, seeing as it s automated and doesn t require bodies, but .... well, maybe it s more complex than I have any right to assume.However, the greatest joy for me about being in  The Club  is the fact that, as my title, suggests, it really does enable you the reader to broaden your literary horizons and try literature that maybe you would never have contemplated picking up off the shelf in your local bookshop.  I find the  blurb  printed beneath each fron cover illustration informative and enticing and, yes, it makes me add the code of that particular publucation to my arms-length sized shopping list.  Without QPD I would never have known what an excellent book  Blonde  by Joyce Carol Oates is.  I would not have been intoxicated by the yummilicious language of Joanne Harris   Chocolat  and  Blackberry Wine .  And I would never have received  Marabou Stork Nightmares  as a freebie for being such a well-paying customer.  Hmmmmm, then again, maybe QPD isn t such a good thing afterall .....I wholeheartedly recommend this book club to all of you out there who find the rows of books in bookshops quite daunting.  I also recommend QPD for those of you who don t quite know where to start to find something  a bit different  from your normal read that will still be something you will enjoy. The books are excellent value and the range is excellent.  Only problem - anyone here any good at putting up bookshelves??          ']

Reading some of the other reviews, the fact that they are not guide books has been levied as a criticism but I think that this is meeting the point somewhat. **Personality Traits:**
- **Book Lover:** The user has a deep passion for reading, often consuming multiple books a month. This indicates a strong appreciation for literature and storytelling.
- **Bargain Hunter:** The user actively seeks out deals and discounts, demonstrating a practical and budget-conscious mindset.
