The difference, even from the 363 ink to 364 is breathtaking.  Obviously the quality of the printer also needs to be taken into consideration when printing but with a good printer and 364 inks you can now start to produce laser printer quality documents but with the cost of inkjet consumables.     ', '    If there   s one thing that bugs me about ink cartridges it   s that when one of the colours runs out you have to replace the whole cartridge. No matter if you still have plenty of red and blue ink, if you   ve been printing plenty of yellow rich pictures then there is no way around it, and you have to waste the lot. This is a pricey and wasteful approach to printer cartridge management, especially in this day of recycling and frugal awareness where we are all trying to make the pennies stretch just that little bit further. Thankfully HP 364 ink cartridges offer a solution to this, thanks to the clever idea of having different cartridges for each colour     that way when you use all of the blue ink before the red or yellow you simple replace it individually, eliminating ink waste at a stroke. I cannot believe I have only just started using a printer and cartridges like this, and dread to think how much perfectly good ink I have had to dispose of while using the old style cartridges. Installing the Cartridges Usually I only have to think about changing ink cartridges and I end up covered in the stuff. It   s not that I   m particularly clumsy, and I know my way around printers and computing hardware, I just for some reason get it on my fingers, hand and face no matter how careful I am. Thankfully this hard to clean up messiness seems to be in the past now, thanks to some simple click and press installation. For my HP Photosmart printer there are five cartridges to install     the usual black, magenta, cyan and yellow are joined by a cartridge called Photo-black, which I am reliably informed is used to elicit professional print lab quality pictures, while resisting smudging, fading and water damage. To install, all you have to do is remove an orange plastic tab from the cartridge and slot it into the corresponding port in the printer, where a reassuring click confirms proper installation. Depending on the printer model some even show a video demonstration on the touch screen to walk you through the process; it really doesn   t get any simpler than that  Once the cartridges are installed you have the option to calibrate or print a test page to make sure all of the cartridges are fitted and working as they should be. During use Ink levels are displayed on screen and on the printers display, and they seem pretty accurate in displaying the correct levels. You get a warning when the cartridge is getting low, and then another when it is about to run out altogether     after receiving this second warning I printed a picture just to test how accurate these level indicators were, and sure enough half way through the print job the yellow ink faded and then ran out. Original Cartridges Vs Compatible  Of course there are compatible cartridges available for my printer, costing a couple of pound less than the original cartridges. But, original HP 364 cartridges are not the most expensive cartridges as it is, and for me the thought of saving a couple of pound per cartridge is outweighed by the assurance of using original cartridges as appose to inferior ones; better, sharper pictures are a price well worth paying. Plus, on a couple of adverts for compatible cartridges I   ve seen you actually have to remove the chips from an original cartridge and fit it to the compatible ones to enable them to work     far too much messing about as far as I am concerned, especially with inferior print quality. Safe to say that on this occasion original is definitely the best as far as I am concerned. Print Quality So, we know how to install them, but how is the print quality? They can be the easiest cartridges to install in the world but that would count for nothing if the colours are washed out or text is blurred and feint. Luckily I have a quantity of photographs to print out so I set to work with gusto. On printing my first picture I am struck by just how quickly the ink dries on the paper; no more trying to pick up the freshly printed photographs by the edges for fear of blurring, these pictures are completely dry and ready to handle straight from the printer. My joy at not having to wait a couple of minutes is heightened when I get to see the results up close. The colour replication is stunning     the first picture is of my three dogs frolicking in a field and the picture really brings the image to life. It is quite hard to explain just how good the printed picture is, but I can make out shades of green and even blades of grass as well as the hues of the sunlight and cloud and the effects on the picture. This printed memento of the occasion is far more accurate than the picture as it is portrayed on a computer screen or digital photo frame, much closer to the living image itself; in fact I am almost getting hay fever just looking at it  Inspired by these impressive results I embark on something of a printing frenzy, first by getting around to a number of letters that were well overdue. Again the results were impressive, with crisp, clean lettering, no fading and of course instant dryness and no smudges. For my next test I embark on printing a number of pictures and text on different quality papers, up until now I have been using high quality photo paper so I was interested to see if the same results could be replicated on cheaper paper. Thankfully the results were good; text and pictures remained sharp and true, with no seepage of the images or crinkling of paper that you might expect. Final Thoughts So, it   s safe to say I am impressed with the set of cartridges I have been testing. Ease of use coupled with crisp and rich colours and the elimination of any waste means my pictures and documents look sharper and more professional than ever. Despite some fairly heavy printing over the past couple of weeks all of the cartridges are still showing as three quarters full, meaning I won   t have to be purchasing new ones for a while yet, mainly because each cartridge boasts a three hundred page yield, with the exception of the Photo black which states roughly half of that. A quick browse of the Hewlett Packard preferred consumables retailers list shows cartridges can be purchased for around the    6 mark, so they are not going to break the bank when they do have to be replaced. Nothing other than the full five stars from me, now I   m off to find some more pictures to print      ']

product_reviews: ['    After my house was set on fire in August last year one of the things I needed replacing was my laptop which I used as an integral part of my own personal work. In November with life finally getting back to normal we had a look around the usual places, PC World, Comet, Curry s and the settled on the Dell Inspiron 1545 from Tesco (I can t remember the price though I think it was around the    400 mark at the time). The insurance had been nice enough to send us an interim payment for the stuff lost in the blaze and as we were still living with the grandparents at the time it seemed to make sense to sort things out that we needed other than furniture (which we ended up getting donated to use anyway). The laptop, which comes in a selection of colours including Black, Blue and Red, was selected in the Red colour with the    top    (the outside of the monitor) being the only part that actually is coloured. The    inside    (inside of the monitor, the keyboard and the bottom of the laptop) is all in black no matter what colour you seem to pick. The colour may seem like a silly place to start but it was how Dell were advertising them a while back, they were using the choice of colour as the way to let your personalise your laptop (like everyone else who bought the same colour...).The laptop came with windows 7, a built in webcam and various Dell based software, most of which was a little irritating to start with, such as the Dell tool bar at the top of the screen. Though after getting back online for the first time since the fire it took only a few minutes to download the programs that made the laptop feel like it was really mine at last. Installs of Open Office, Opera, VLC player, Firefox, Sopcast and the ilk. It was then that the laptop was finally personalised, it was mine at last and still running like a dream.The spec of the laptop was relatively impressive for the price I was paying, it had 4GB of RAM allowing it to quickly run pretty much anything I d be using in super quick speed. I m not one for running huge resource hogging games though it was nice to know the RAM would cope with pretty much any game I was likely to play. The    Windows Experience Index    gave the RAM a score of 5.8 when I checked a few minutes ago (from a possible 7.9) and it s currently running a media application, 2 browsers, a messaging service, various office applications and has shown no slowdown at all despite repeatedly flicking between them. With my old laptop it d take up to 3 or 4 seconds to change programs so this has been a great move forward in terms of usability and speed. Much like the RAM the Processor also scored 5.8 with the 2.3Ghz Pentium dual Core processor. Like the RAM this meant to laptop was a mile ahead of my previous Laptop, for some this speed may be    acceptable    though for someone like myself who isn t using intensive programs the processor is fine with not lag. Combined together they make the laptop quick and easy. This is also the case from the 5.9 scoring    Primary Hard Disk    which shows that the things save to the hard disk swiftly, from games, to music, from documents to installed software. In terms of speed the laptop is quick enough for anyone using it as a general laptop.Where spec lets it down is the graphics. The general graphics are rated as a very moderate 4.0 whilst the gaming graphics are rated as poorly as 3.4. As I don t play many games this hasn t bothered me at all, though if your a gamer I d advise you looking somewhere else for your gaming laptop with much better graphics. If your just wanting to play things like Football manager I can t see this posing you any major problems, though if you want to run the newest most powerful FPS at absolute maximum this isn t the laptop for you.So away from the internal specification, the keyboard, although feeling a little bit    fragile    has yet to give me any problems at all (and has been used, used and used some more) with easily 60+ hours a week usage since the first week of November 2010. The mouse (touch pad) has been the most trouble out of everything, it occasionally plays up and refuses to go where I want it to until I restart the laptop using keys. Presumably this is caused by a software error of sorts and could be fixed via going into the task manager and closing the effected task though a restart is easily enough. This flaw seems to hit once every 16 hours or so with out a shut down so shouldn t be much of a problem for most folks.One of the few    weird    things with the laptop is the use of the    Fn    key. Generally laptops I ve used have used the    Fn    key to get a secondary use out of the F keys, this uses the    Fn    key to actually operate the F function. One of these problems did require a reinstall of Vista (something I haven t had to do on my own machine), but that proved to be easy to do - I just used the DVD that came with the computer, left it running overnight and in the morning, it was all working again, with the bonus that none of my family s files were lost in the reinstall, so I didn t even have to restore things from backup.Like other Inspiron laptops, the computer feels reasonably solid, weighing about 2.5kg. The finish is very shiny and doesn t feel cheap. The TrueLife screen offers excellent viewing quality, but is very reflective. I found the widescreen ratio to be a little bit hard to get used to - the screen is shorter and wider, so you have to page down more often.The computer connected easily to the wireless router, which was just as well because the Ethernet port came loose after only a few months. The battery life wasn t fantastic, but if you mainly use it plugged in, then this isn t an issue. The keyboard was much like any other laptop keyboard - obviously the keys don t go down as far as a regular keyboard that comes with a desktop and sound a bit clicky, but that s par for the course for a laptop. It came with 3 USB ports and a card reader that I haven t used but claims to be 8 in 1.This computer will probably struggle with the latest games, but if you want something that will run Office, play CDs and DVDs, watch online TV, browse the internet or similar, then this is fine. All in all, this is a nice entry level laptop.(Cross posted from dooyoo.com)      ', '     I have used Dell Inspiron 1545 for a couple of months. I m glad I made right decision. My friend who works in computer filed suggested me this one after asking me my demand for a laptop.First , I would like to say , it can totally meet all requirements I expected from a good laptop. I use it to write articles especially for my blog, to send and receive emails, to talk on MSN and Skype with my family and friends abroad. It never let me down. I also used it to watch TV including the programs on BBC Iplayer. Compared to my desk computer, I can feel the speed on my laptop was faster and the stability of the network was better. Second, it has nice overall design. Slim, Simple and sleek. You have three colors to choose . I chose the black one that matches from outside to inside. The keyboard  has all the necessary controls that I used often.Last ,but not least, I think it is a great laptop for the price. I used to have a dell, and decided to go with another because you can t beat the performance for the price. The main items provided by Inspiron 1545 are Intel Celeron Dual core, Windows Vista(home premium including media),15.6in widescreen and 2048MB memory. I especially like the wireless functions. It gave me more freedom when I moved from one room to another room. Overall, fabulous laptop for enjoyable experience. also see on dooyoo.co.uk     ', '    I purchased the Dell Inspiron 1545 laptop back in January for my daughter s birthday. I had a limited budget but wanted to get her something with decent enough spec for playing computer games should she wish to do this, and a large hard drive as she is a big fan of making videos on her digital camera and downloading music - two things which can eat up hard drive space.I did a fair bit of research before purchasing and decided I wanted to get the best spec I possibly could for my money and the Inspiron ticked all the boxes. I paid    399 in January 2009 in Currys for the laptop which was the absolute limit on my budget.The Dell I purchased has a dark blue coloured lid, however the rest of it is a shiny piano black which looks lovely. I would have preferred metal for the mousepad area - it feels sturdier and doesn t seem to attract the dust the way the piano black plastic does - however that s a small quibble. The screen is widescreen and measures 15.6 inches and overall it s pretty lightweight and easy to carry about if you wish to do so.So - what came in the box?As well as the laptop there was an instruction manual, mains lead, Dell restoration CD-ROMs and a CD-ROM for Works 9.The laptop had Windows Vista Premium pre-installed - and I worried that this might be a challenge for me as it was my introduction to Vista - however setting the machine up was a piece of cake.I merely switched it on and dealt with a few prompts as Vista set up and then the computer was up and running. It has wifi installed and this picked up my wireless connection without any problems - and once I entered the security details for my network we were home and dry and online in no time When I was researching laptops I learned that you really need a minimum of 2GB RAM to run Vista properly, so this was another factor to consider when deciding the spec I needed for her laptop.The laptop had a trial version of MacAfee installed but I decided to ignore this and installed AVG instead as my daughter is more familiar with it. I also decided to install the Works program that came with the laptop rather than Office as she really only needs a word processing program at the moment. I was concerned she may find it hard to use at first but we had no such worries.What I really noticed about this little beauty was the speed - it loads really quickly and smoothly. The processor is an Intel Core 2 Duo 2.00 Ghz and there is 3GB RAM. This combination makes the Inspiron easily the fastest computer in the house - making me green with envy So onto the litmus test - did my daughter like it? Well yes - she loved it  She was really pleased to have this compact little laptop in her bedroom instead of the old desktop computer she had had in the past. She loved how she didn t need a wireless adaptor, the speed, and everything about it  The laptop has a large hard drive of 250 GB but this is half full already - just over 3 months since she got it, so I can foresee me having to get an external hard drive for her in the future.I had worried about her learning how to use Vista, but like all 12 year olds, she picked it up far quicker than I did, so my fears were unfounded.There are three USB ports, which so far I have found sufficient. The laptop does have speakers but they are a bit on the tinny side and given my daughter listens to a lot of music on her computer, I got her some USB powered speakers which offer fantastic sound quality.The laptop also has an integral SD card reader which is invaluable for my daughter as she can easily upload photos and videos from her camera and also copy music onto the SD card she uses in her new Nintendo DSi.There is a CD/DVD RW drive which works a treat - my daughter thoroughly enjoys making music CDs up using it and has also burned the occasional DVD featuring some of her many video clips. She can also watch DVDs on the laptop but hasn t used the laptop this way - she prefers to watch her DVDs on TV. It also came with Windows Media Center already installed which was an extra bonus as my daughter was already familiar with this from her old desktop computer and was delighted to still be able to use it for her videos, photos and music.The Inspiron I purchased does not have a built-in webcam but this feature is available on some models.The one thing we haven t tested is the battery life - Dell claim it s 2 hours however. As my daughter hasn t removed it from her bedroom since she got it I cannot tell you for sure. As she just recently broke the screen on my Samsung laptop, resulting in a large repair bill, she is probably too scared to move this one I am really pleased with the Dell Inspiron 1545 and think it s a really good buy for children or students as it s easy to use, fast to load and has a large hard drive but is available at a good price for the spec offered.I do advise getting some half decent speakers to use with it however and cleaning it regularly - the piano black doesn t half attract the dust and show up fingerprints.Overall this is a good machine for the money and it can be found in various outlets right now, including Currys, Tesco and Dell online.**Previously published on dooyoo by me under the same user name.**     ', '    I got this Dell inspiron 1545 laptop back in late 2009 after hearing nothing but good reviews about the model and loved the fact there was lots of different colours available. I chose to get the flamingo pink colour which is a darkish pink.I bought my laptop online directly from Dell and if i remember correctly it was    499, this includes the built in webcam and the colour which were    50 each.The laptop looks great and it s got a really shiny tint to the screen and the casing looks like it has a high gloss finish. At first i was paranoid about getting fingerprints on it etc but have soon got into it. Although mine s the pink, only the back of the screen is pink. The keyboard and edging of the screen and the bottom of the laptop are all black. It s modern looking and has a great quality 15.6 inch LCD widescreen display, which is nice and clear and makes viewing videos and pictures that bit more detailed.The keyboard is the usual standard QWERTY layout and is simple to use, not taking much time to get used to atall. There s various labeled shortcut keys at the top which include volume and internet connection which are handy but i rarely use them as it s easy to forget they re there The laptop came with a charger and mains cable which is easy to connect. Unfortunetly one of my dogs chewed my first one up and Dell kindly replaced it as i still had a number of months left on my warranty.Once i d recieved my laptop via courier, i turned it on and followed the on screen instructions. It arrived fully charged and i simply had to follow the instructions that came with the laptop. Firstly i had to enter a few details and wait for the operating system to install. This took around 20 minutes and i was soon logged into the laptop. I was then able to customize my settings etc and install any drivers, such as the webcam and internet etc. Once connected to the internet i followed the instructions included in the instruction booklet to register my laptop as belonging to myself.My laptop came with Windows vista premium installed but if you buy via the website you ll have options to customize which operating system you like, with windows 7 adding alot more onto the price than windows vista. I personally am happy with windows vista but for those who aren t keen the option of different operating systems are available.The laptop overall has loads of features. Mine has an 1.3mp webcam which i paid extra for. It s simple to use but not great as it doesn t cope with bright light very well  Otherwise it s fine to use.My laptop has 465GB which i paid extra for. I think the lowest GB is 250, the GB s are seperated into a recovery feature which stores all of your details incase the laptop needs resetting, and the rest go into  Computer , storing your music/pictures and videos etc.There s aso a CD player in the side which also acts as a DVD burner.A sample installation of Microsoft office was installed on my laptop and it worked great but i personally prefer Wordpad so uninstalled it.The downside to this laptop is the fact that it seems to overheat quite easily even when placed on a cool wooden surface, when it overheats it usually turns itself off which can be frustrating if you re in the middle of something. It s also not a very versatile laptop, as it weighs in at almost 3kg. I used to take it out and about to do writing etc on but gave up in the end as it weighed me down  The battery life also isn t good as if you re watching videos etc it seems to dicrease quickly Connection to the internet is easy, i have wireless now but started off just plugging it into my Virgin media internet box via an ethernet cable. There are 3 USB slots, 2 on the left side and 1 on the right. These can be used to connect memory sticks, laptops, ipods, etc and are simple to use. Once you ve plugged your item in it will usually install the drivers automatically.I d reccomend it to anyone who wants a basic laptop. I don t think it s be great for gaming as playing the Sims on it usually sucks the energy out of it, makes it lag and sometimes crash. I m happy with it and it personally does everything that i need, the sound quality is decent and the preinstalled programmes are basic, with windows media player etc. It s perfect for most day to day use but i wouldn t reccomend it if you need to take it out and about with you. I personally think it was well worth the price       ', '          I d been on the hunt for a laptop since last August, as I needed one for my Post 16 studies and the desktop was getitng a bit crowded. After extensive researching, I came across the Dell Inspiron 1545 on the Currys  website, reduced from    499.99 to    399. It was a little over my budget, but it just meant that I d have to give more of my birthday money to my parents. Specifications  500 GB HD Windows 7 Home Premium Intel    Pentium    Dual Core T4400 (2.2 GHz) 15.6 Widescreen 3GB Memory 7-in-1 memory card reader 3 USB 2.0 ports WiFi 802.11b/g Webcam 1.3 megapixel (I think) 4-cell lithium-ion battery  Intel High Definition Audio 2.0 Cherry Red colour (pink, black, white and green also available) Laptop When I first looked at it, I realised it was quite sturdy. Many other laptops I have used have been quite flimsy and have easily been damaged, but this one seems durable.The laptop has a gloss finish which, unfortunately, does attract fingerprints and dust. However, it s nothing that a simple wipe with a cloth after every use can t fix. The keyboard lacks the numerical keys that a desktop laptop would have to the right of the letters, but the other number/character keys are fine. I never used the other number keys anyway. The speakers are just above the QWERTY keyboard, as well as the power button. At least you re less likely to  accidently  switch it on  The speakers produce high quality audio, compared to the desktop downstairs. I haven t yet played any media at a high volume, so how it performs then I have no idea.The various ports and slots are dotted around the laptop, on the left and right sides and also at the front. The charger slot is on the left, so it doesn t get in the way. That was something that I noticed after using my Dad s Toshiba, as that charger part was very bulky.I personally love the look of this laptop. I wanted something with a bit of colour and before I could only find Sony Vaio s, but no way on Earth was I going to spend    800+ on a laptop that has a lower or equal spec. to this one  How It Runs I was very impressed with the speed of everything  The set-up was quick, logging on and off is quick, and the speed which the laptop gets going at once logged on is superb  Before, I had to wait five minutes until I could even attempt to open the Internet Browser (that might have something to do with the fact the desktop had 5 users, 80GB HD, 512MB Ram)   Now, I am connected to the Internet within fifteen seconds  None of the applications  lag , and downloading/uploading is also fast. I have downloaded a few programs such as AVG, Ad-Aware and Open Office and I ve had no issues with their functions or the speed at which they run at. I don t know what else to say here, apart from everything runs smoothly and quickly  Ease Of Use I use computers on a regular basis and I know my way around, so regardless of this being a Windows 7 laptop, I got around the functions almost straightaway. It s simple to use, it s just the new functions like the bar on top of the screen and some of the menus that could possibly cause confusion. The only thing that gave me a bit of trouble was the touchpad mouse. Sometimes it likes to highlight things or click on certain links when I m only trying to move it to another part of the screen. I m faithful to the wire or wireless mice, but as I use this while sitting on my bed, I can t really whip it out. It s probably a fault on my part because I m not used to this type of mouse. Features Games, games and more games. Not just the basic ones like Solitaire, but I m lucky enough to receive games like Bejeweled and some other perculiar titles. I don t really use these, so whether they were there or not wouldn t really bother me.There s Windows Internet Explorer 7 too. We, of course, have Windows Media Player which is completely different to the version 11 I ve been using for absolutely ages  Even the webcam had numerous things on it, such as different frames and colours. They are a bit pointless, but nevertheless it s there if you ever want to make yourself look like a clownfish There s a 60 day trial of Microsoft Works 2007, but I use Open Office as it s permanent (and free ). There s other programs related to Windows and Dell, but I haven t ventured in and had a look. All in all, you get the basics and you ll either have to buy or download anything else you want or need.  For the price, there could have been a few more useful things on there  Seller I just thought I d mention this. Bought this laptop from Currys, and although the people are doing their job, I didn t exactly appreciate the hard sell. They were helpful talking about the laptop, but they were trying to flog unnecessary things and it was coming to the point where we nearly didn t make the purchase. I think that next time we ll order it off the Internet so we don t have this issue  We did manage to get a laptop bag   wireless mouse thrown in for    20 (even though they were adamant not to reduce it from    24.99, but seeing as we didn t want the other stuff, they hesitantly chucked it in anyway). Battery Life Well, there are two power options: Balanced and Power Saver. To be honest, one just makes the screen lighter, and the other keeps it darker. They both gobble battery power up very quickly, so the charger always has to be plugged in otherwise it would cut out halfway through when I m working  Without the charger, it would stand maxiumum an hour and a half. Enough time to check your emails or Facebook a few times, but not time for writing an essay or a report. A little disappointing, but then again I don t think that the battery life of many laptops is that spectacular. Just don t lose/break the charger  Wireless Fantastic. My room is on the the third floor, and I get between a 2 and a 4 for the signal (out of 5). It hasn t cut out on me either. Overall Verdict Despite its flaws, I love this laptop. The colour, the look of it, the speed, everything apart from the gloss. They could have just had the gloss on the lid, and have matte inside. I believe the price was excellent, just right for what it was. I think    500 would have been a bit too much. If I could, I would have gone to Dell direct, but when I  built  everything, it was way over    600  Currys  do disappoint me, but hopefully my laptop doesn t break down so I don t have to return and get a lecture about not buying their  data storer  software      ']

If you’re looking for a dependable, no-nonsense laptop that covers everyday needs without breaking the bank, the Dell Inspiron 1545 is worth considering. From my experience and what others have noted, this model strikes a solid balance between practicality and value—especially for students or families who want a straightforward machine for web browsing, word processing, and watching DVDs.

One of the standout features is its durability. The Inspiron 1545 feels robust and can handle the usual bumps and daily wear without issues, which is reassuring if you’re not always gentle with your gear. It also runs smoothly on Windows 7, with a noticeable performance boost if you’re upgrading from Vista, and it doesn’t overheat or crash even during more demanding tasks like video editing. So, reliability is definitely a strong point here.

Typing is comfortable thanks to a well-designed keyboard with handy shortcut keys, making it easier to get through work or study sessions. The screen is bright and clear, though the glossy finish tends to attract fingerprints and can be reflective, which might be a minor annoyance if you often work in bright environments.

On the downside, the built-in speakers are just okay—fine for casual use but don’t expect rich sound for music or movies. Also, this laptop isn’t built for gaming or heavy graphics work, so if you need power for those tasks, you’ll want to look elsewhere.

Overall, the Dell Inspiron 1545 offers good value for its price, especially if you prioritize ease of use, durability, and solid everyday performance over flashy specs. It’s a practical choice that delivers what it promises without unnecessary complexity—perfect for anyone who wants a reliable, user-friendly laptop without overspending.

product_reviews: ['    For a while now AMD processors have began to threaten Intel s dominence of the processor market. Untill last year their offerings have mainly been directed at the lower end of the processor market. Enter the Athlon Thunderbird. The latest offering from AMD catches the eye immediatly with its comparitivly lower price. This however is not reflected in performance with a 1.GHz thunderbird clocking in as fast if not faster than the 1.2 intel offering.All is not smiles and roses however as the Athlon does have some minor draw backs. Firstly it s hot - All processors are hot but this ones red hot, and needs to be kept cool with plenty of air passing through.Secondly its compatibility does throw up the odd problem. If you are upgrading to an Athlon be awear that it needs more power which means to be on the safe side most users will need to upgrade their power supply or even invest in a new case.Along the hardware lines their have also  been some reported cases of conflicts with some makes of the G-force graphics cards. Causing repeated crashes despite using up to date drivers.These are considerations worth a thought as a basic rule if you are upgrading yourself be careful AMD will help you out with any problems so let them know what components you intend to use together before you buy. If you are buying a new Athlon thunderbird system then use a reputable dealer - most know the precautions to take and will not sell you a system with an incompatible graphics card and will also provide adiquate cooling for your machine - Theirs always the sharks or a mate of a mate who builds them in his guarage - they might have problems.Overall the performance of the Athlon Thunderbird for the money is well worth a go - just think it through      ', '    After years as the underdog, AMD s Athlon processor finally helped AMD to bite significantly into Intel s dominance of the PC processor market. Today still, the vast majority of new PC s are sold using Intel s  Pentium  processors, but the clever money is on Athlon powered PC s.The Althlon Thunderbird is a cheaper version of the full blown Athlon processor - noticeably cheaper, but still packing similar sort of performance. These processors have proved to be considerably better than Intel s Pentium III, and solid performers against the Pentium IV. Intel Pentium IV s beat equivalent Athlon s in terms of performance, but only video editors and graphic designers are likely to notice any difference. This is because today s PC s have processors so powerful it is the software which is having to catch up. Indeed, Hard disk and memory speeds make a greater difference to PC performance than an 800Mhz processor compared to a 1Ghz chip.I bought an Athlon Thunderbird when I was building new PC, for two reasons. 1. The performance/cost factory makes the Thunderbird an absolute bargain. 2. They are very easy to install.Athlons have become a firm favourite with overclockers, because they are easy to  overclock  and robust, and many graphic card manufactures have developed drivers specifically to take advantage of Athlon processors.It s difficult not to recommend the Athlon Thunderbird. It is a performance bargain and if AMD continue to nibble into Intel s monopoly of the processor market, then that can only be a good thing for consumers.     ', '    So people now want the fastest chips that are out there. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re weighing the AMD Thunderbird against Intel’s offerings, here’s a detailed breakdown that aligns with what matters most: performance, value, and thermal management. The Thunderbird’s combined 384K L1 and L2 on-die cache runs at twice the speed of Intel’s cache, which translates into noticeably faster real-world performance—especially when compared to Pentium 3 and 4 CPUs at the same clock speed. This architectural advantage makes it a compelling choice for gaming and multimedia tasks where cache efficiency can bottleneck throughput.

From a value perspective, the Thunderbird is significantly cheaper than equivalent Intel processors, delivering superior bang for your buck. For DIY builders like us, this means you can allocate budget savings toward other components, like a better GPU or faster RAM, without sacrificing CPU performance.

Overclocking enthusiasts will appreciate that the Thunderbird tends to run cooler than previous AMD generations, increasing the likelihood of stable overclocks. However, it’s important to note that effective overclocking demands additional cooling solutions—stock coolers won’t cut it. If you’re inexperienced, I’d advise caution here; pushing the chip without proper thermal management risks instability or hardware damage.

On the flip side, while the Thunderbird excels in raw performance and cost-efficiency, it does require attention to cooling and compatibility. Make sure your motherboard supports the Thunderbird socket and that your case airflow is adequate. Also, the overclocking headroom, though promising, isn’t a plug-and-play feature—it’s for users comfortable with tweaking voltages and fan curves.

In summary, the AMD Thunderbird offers a smart balance of speed, affordability, and thermal efficiency, making it a standout choice for value-conscious builders who want solid gaming and multimedia performance without Intel’s premium price tag. Just be prepared to invest in cooling if you plan to push it beyond stock speeds.

product_reviews: ['    The time had come. My little cheap printer, which came with my computer, had finally given out on me so it was now time to purchase a low cost printer.  My criterion was simple: I wanted a low cost, quality colour Inkjet printer from a company with a good reputation for reliability and support.  I am not a mechanical person at all so I really need something which was going to be super easy to operate.  This was a couple of years ago now. I went out not really knowing what I was going to buy and ended up coming home with the Hewlett Packard HP DeskJet 930C printer and    135 less in the bank lol.I took the printer home and opened the box. Inside were the printer, power cord, colour print cartridge, black print cartridge, print software, users guide and Quick Start Poster.  Be forewarned, the printer does not come with an interface cable. The printer was very easy to set up. It can be connected with parallel or USB hook-up.  The software was very easy to load. You just put the CD in the CD-ROM and it guides you step by step from there. In a matter of minutes the software was loaded on my computer, ready for use. Just about any software system will work with this printer as far as I know, but the best operating system is of course Windows. As far as word processing programs are concerned, I found the Microsoft Office package works the best. Word, Excel, and even PowerPoint have given me no problems whatsoever. The top of the printer lifts up, making ink replacement super easy. Even a mechanical dummy like myself can do that with no problems. On opening the top cover of the printer, the print head moves automatically to the middle of the printer, you just slip the old one out and the new ones goes right into its place by pulling it from the top corner downwards. You can also check how much ink you have left in your ink cartridges. It will tell you when the ink is low and when you should have more ink ready to replace your cartridges. Replacement ink cartridges are expensive     approx    20 for black and approx    22-   25 for colour. I recently purchased a refill kit for both the colour and black cartridges, but, as yet, I haven t had the occasion to use them, so I don t know how they will work out. If I were redesigning this printer, I would make the black ink cartridge twice the size it currently is. I think it was designed for colour printing, as the colour cartridge is quite large. So, be prepared to spend money on colour cartridges if you are going to use this printer as a colour printer. If needed, you can calibrate the printer, which will give you the best possible print. It is automatically done for you when you replace the ink, but if it is misaligned you can do this and it will take care of it. It takes about two minutes and will use one sheet of paper. If your printing comes out streaked the print cartridges may need cleaned. This will take about two minutes and only uses one sheet of paper. I used to have paper jams all the time with my previous printer but this rarely happens now. I have found if I try to load the tray with too much paper it will jam. If this happens it can be cleared by pushing the paper jam button situated on the top right hand side. I keep the paper in the tray relatively low and I have found it works out much better (the 930 can only hold 100 sheets of A4 paper).  You can set the type of print you would like your printer to print in. You can use draft to save time and ink, normal for most types of everyday printing and best gives you the highest print quality. This printer has some nice features: you can print in Portrait, which will be a vertical print out, Landscape to print horizontally, or Mirror Image to reverse the print image. You can set it to automatically print two-sided documents. When printing a two-sided document you can select the Book method, which allows you to bind the pages on the side or Tablet if it will be bound at the top. You can also print in different shades of grey. By a simple click of your mouse, you can easily change the brightness when needed or add extra drying time. It has the ability to print envelopes, transparencies, banners, cards, labels and sheets.Oh, and did I say it was quiet? You won   t believe how quiet this printer is. My old printer was loud. This one prints so quietly, it is almost silent - it could easily be mistaken for a laser. I have printed scanned photos onto photo paper and was extremely impressed with the quality I got: they are vibrant without being too glossy. The PhotoRetII technology really helps with shadows, layering, and textures. The 930C has the option to use a higher resolution when printing photos, 2400 x 1200 dpi. I printed my pictures out using this, and they are great  The printer however is slow when printing out photographs, but the quality of the printed picture is unbelievable; it really looks as if it was developed from a negative. I still cannot believe the pictures I print come from an inkjet printer.Design-wise the printer is 17 inches wide and 10 inches deep. Extending the paper tray adds 6 inches to the depth. The paper feeds in at the bottom and returns there - a design I find superior to the top-loaders. In humid weather top-loaders tend to allow the paper to curl and flop over. In the HP DeskJet 930C this will not be a problem, since the paper is lying flat. This unit is stable; it does not shake or rattle, like most Canons or Lexmarks. The 930 s small footprint measuring 44x40x19.5cm and curvaceous design do not look out of place at home. Its understated grey plastic casing accompanied by a further three protruding grey buttons does little to contradict this assumption.  The paper tray even folds up against the printer, to prevent dust from having its wicked way when the printer is not in use. This creates more desk space (a nice touch). This tray is of a fragile build, which is a cause for concern. It is flimsy and brittle to touch, I feel once the tray is down it is safer to stay that way.Buttons   Lights: The buttons and lights are located on the top right of the printer. Cancel Button ~ has an X on top of it, use it to cancel something that is currently printing Resume Button   Light ~ the light will flash when you need to put in paper or if you have a paper jam, use the button when you want to re-start the printing Power Button   Light ~ turn the printer on and off, when the light above the button is flashing the printer is in process of printing On the downside, communication between the printer and the computer is not the speediest or the most reliable. Sometimes it is virtually impossible to work on another document when printing .pdf files or high-resolution digital images from Photoshop. Printing a text file is fine though and I find it far easier to take a break and have a cup of coffee   biscuit when printing graphic-intensive files.Just the Specs Please:  information taken from owner   s manual for those technically minded: Print Technology: The HP 930c utilises HP PhotoREt III printer language, which yields a black resolution of up to 600 dpi (dots per inch) and colour resolution of up to Up to 2400 x 1200 dpi (on premium photo paper). Memory: 4 MB RAM OS Compatibility: Windows 3.1x (Enhanced Mode only)/95/98/Me, Windows NT 4.0 Workstation/Server/2000 Professional, plus support for MS-DOS applications (through Windows 98, 95, and 3.1x), and Mac OS 8.1 or above (USB-connect Macintosh only). Paper Handling:     Up to 100 sheets of paper (16 to 24lbs), plain, inkjet, photo     Up to 20 sheets of banner paper (16 to 24lbs)    Up to 15 envelopes (20 to 24lbs); A2 Invitation, 4.375 in x 5.75 in.     Up to 30 index or business cards (110lbs), 3x5 in; 4x6 in; 5x5 in.     Up to 25 transparencies    Up to 20 sheets of labels Print Speeds: Up to 9 ppm (pages per minute) black, mixed Text with Colour Graphics 7.5 ppm Printer Interface: IEEE-1284-Centronics parallel compatible; Universal Serial Bus (Microsoft    Windows 98, Windows 2000 Professional and Mac OS 8.1 and above). Printing Resolutions: Black TrueType Text Resolution: Draft: 300 x 600 dpi ~ Normal   Best: 600 x 600 dpi Colour Resolution: Draft: 300 x 600 dpi ~ Normal   Best: PhotoREt Photo Paper: PhotoREt 2400 x 1200 dpi Weight: 12.6 pounds without print cartridges Dimensions: 17.34 inches wide x 7.72 inches high x 15.76 inches deep (tray down with paper) or 9.85 inches deep with tray up Ink Cartridges: Black HP45 (approx cost    20) Tri-Colour HP78 (approx cost    22-   25) So that s it -- nothing but good stuff. I have had no problems with this printer. It has been used daily for 4 years and it just keeps chugging out quality prints. The 930C is worth every penny and a bit more.  Thanks for reading.     ', '    I paid    150 for my HP 930c in September 2000 when the model was new. Since then I ve seen them priced as low as    70 in the Viking Direct sales catalogues, great value for money for the printer itself.The quality of the printed material is excellent if I use the correct cartridges. I have tried refill kits and compatible cartridges but the quality isn t quite as good. They are adequate for most things but not for master copies that go on to be photo copied or printed. Refill kits for the coloured cartridges were a disaster, my printer won t work using them. I normally pay around    20 for black cartridges though I have seen them on sale for up to    28, and get approximately 240 A4 sheets from one cartridge. I have no idea how many sheets a coloured cartidge would produce if used all the time, certainly not many if variations of the most popular colour blue was used regualarly. What I found annoying was that the same black cartridges were used for the 930 as the 820 which I upgraded from, but the colour cartridges were different. Higher priced and containing less ink. When I bought the new printer the cartridges were  short  cartridges with only a small amount of ink in. Meaning that I had to go out and buy new cartridges a week later, much quicker than expected. A change from when I bought the 820, those cartridges were standard.The first colour cartridge that I bought was    29.99,    6.00 more than I had been paying. That cartridge ran out within a few weeks, faster than any previous coloured cartridge that I d used as I mostly print in black ink except for a small logo on my letterheads. I went to buy another and the price had risen to    39.99 in every shop in the town. I bought one begrudgingly, the printer had come to a standstill. I was told by one of the assistants that the cost of cartridges were so high because they and not the printers make the profits for the companies. Such a steep rise seemed more like profiteering to me.I turned the colour off but the cartridge nearly empty warning came all too soon. I scoured the internet and every discount catalogue that I could get my hands on. Everywhere the price was at least    39.99. I ordered one to be delivered 3 days later but in the meantime the old cartridge ran out. My printer came to a standstill again - just as I had completed a big design order for a very good customer and needed to print off the master copies for him. It was 2 days before I was able to go into town so I was completely stuck.Furious because I couldn t complete for my customer as planned I emailed Hewlett Packard and complained about there being less ink in these cartridges and the hefty price increase. I finally got an email back one week later. They told me to do what I had already done and turn off colour printing. They also told me that even with it turned off small amounts of the coloured ink is used with every black print out, so eventually even if you don t use colour the cartridges will run out.About 9 months ago the price of coloured cartridges dropped again to between    25 and    30 (sigh of relief ) As I didn t see any dramatic price increase or drop on any of their other cartridges I am left wondering why there was such a price hike on that particular model.A cable wasn t included with this purchase, but fortunately I hadn t thrown my old printer away and was able to use the cable from that which had been supplied with the 830. I think that  extra  should always be supplied with every purchase. Imagine buying a computer and printer together and finding that you have to trek out again to buy a cable before you can connect your printer to your computer and can use it. Always a good idea to check when buying if you need a cable.The feed on the 930 is better than the 820 but I still have problems occasionally when more than one page is drawn in at a time. When that happens the print starts lower on the sheet and part of what is meant to be on one sheet goes on several. Sometimes up to 10 sheets, wasting a lot of paper.Another problem that I have is wider margins or unprintable areas on the right hand side of A4 landscape pages. Or wider margins at the bottom of A4 portrait. I have tried many times without succeeding to alter the unprintable areas following the instructions. That could be me so if anybody knows how to do it I would be grateful for  simple  instructions.Despite the problems I like this printer because of the printed quality and its reliability. The speed isn t brilliant but that isn t important to me. HP deskjets are tough printers, my first one churned out an unbelievable amount before it broke down after 2 years use. That might not sound long but for most of the time I was printing at least 1,000 A4 pages a week. I don t print as much now because I acquired a cheaper to run photo copier to do the donkey work, but I still use it a lot and 18 months later its running like new.     ', '    Okay, to start with I work in the computer trade, so I see products come and go. At work we do lots of point of sale displays, which are usually A4 sized with a large colourful header and some bullet points in large black text.I can without hesitation recommend the Hewlett Packard 930C for its excellent print quality and speed. The documents are printed directly from Photoshop 5 and the results on cheap copier paper are fantastic.But for a real test I printed out a picture of my baby son (for testing purposes, honestly ). The picture was taken on a Kodak 200 Plus at high resolution and printed directly from internet explorer, on copier paper with the HP cranked right up to the highest print quality (1200 DPI, I believe).The finished picture was excellent, and I now keep it to show customers how good the printer can be even on cheap A4 paper.Now I m gutted  I went out and bought an Epson 700 Photo about a year or so ago, and the comparision between the two, well the Epson has 2 extra ink colours, so the skin tones should be better. They are not. The Epson takes much longer to print, an A4 picture can take upto 25 mins, where as the HP 930C can do the same picture in around 7mins. So, if you re printing a few pictures the time saved is alot The downside to this printer (HP930C) is that the cartridges are expensive. The colour cartridge can cost between    20 -    28 and the black can cost about the same. But to justify this, when you change the cartridge you get a new print head, so therefore the print quality is the same as the day you bought it  Unlike Epson where if the heads get blocked, you re looking at a hefty bill You can get non genuine cartridges but I have generally found these to be of inferior quality.If you think this is the printer for you, the only consideration is do you spend the extra and go for the 950C or even the 970CXI. Well, the latter models have full size paper trays, where as the 930c has a folding tray, which is handy if you have limited desk space. Also the 950 and 970 are slightly faster and the 970CXI is optimised more so for photo work.Personally I would go for the 930C, it is at a great price point (around    110) it s compact when folded up and very, very quiet. So much so, that you sometimes have to check if it s running  Something Epson users don t need to do I have decided to update this review due to feedback from other Ciao  users (thanks for your input ) The main reason I have not quoted any pages per minute for this printer is because I have never found an absolute standard for testing them. I personally print mainly  read me  files which are just plain text and large colour photos anything from A5 to A4 size. Almost every printer that I have used in the last 12-24 months have all taken at least 7-10 minutes for a high quality A4 image and text files usually take upto a minute for Windows (mainly due to Windows having to initialise the printer driver).I know this won t help most of you if you really must have the fastest printer available but if like me and many other homeusers, quality and reliability mean a great deal more than quantity and speed  Thanks for readingMikeTime for another update (16.1.2002)To answer a few questions that have appeared on the comments section.Firstly, yes you can use refill cartridges or refill kits, they seem to work well, but only refill the cartridges 2 or 3 times, or you may experience head blockages and impared print quality.  This may not happen to all users, but is a recommendation from a few refill kit manufacturers.The use of refills can invalidate your warranty, so please do read your instruction manuals and small print.I have also found that although HP have stopped UK manufacturers from producing cloned cartridges (they use old HP cases and refill them) it is possible to buy new cloned cartridges from overseas, if you are willing to pay the extra postage. These cartridges are very cheap as HP cannot charge for copyright usage.I have not given much technical specification here as I believe that a review should tell you a lot more than a bunch of figures that are compiled in laboratory conditions. Real use and experiences are far more important, in my opinion. If you really want the full blown tech spec, then please go to www.hp.comAlso pricing is difficult to put in a review as the price changes weekly as newer and faster units become available. It would be fair to say that this is an outstanding printer in the sub    100 section.     ', '    Hewllet Packard is well respected in the computer community and probably one of the best, or should I say, most highly respected brand of printers. Why? Probably due to the quality of their printers and the fact that they seem to go on and on and don  8217;t give you too much hassle. Oh they had a few problems with the HP 500 series etc but when it came to the 560, then the very widely used 640 HP were getting their name around and now, most companies that I know use HP printers. The HP930c is probably the best printer I have seen to date from HP. It looks nice (have you notice how everything seems to be going curvy in the world of computing? s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
The HP Deskjet 930c stands out as a solid choice for home and moderate use, especially for users who prioritize print quality and reliability without breaking the bank. Installation is notably straightforward, with clear instructions and automatic cartridge alignment that simplify setup—a definite plus for those who value ease of use. Connectivity options are versatile, supporting both USB and parallel ports across a wide range of operating systems, which adds to its practical appeal.

Print quality is a highlight: the 930c produces sharp, high-quality photos even on inexpensive copier paper, and it includes a handy selection of sample specialty papers to experiment with. While print speed is reasonable—expect around 7 minutes for detailed A4 images—it’s well-suited for family or casual photo printing rather than professional workloads.

However, a critical consideration is the cost and consumption of ink cartridges. Official HP color cartridges are expensive and contain less ink compared to previous models, which impacts overall cost-effectiveness. Moreover, the printer uses color ink even when printing black and white documents, leading to more frequent cartridge replacements. Attempts to use refill kits or compatible cartridges often result in inferior print quality and can cause printer malfunctions, undermining long-term value.

On the support front, HP’s customer service is prompt and helpful, complemented by extensive online resources and manuals—an important factor for users who appreciate reliable after-sales support.

In summary, the HP Deskjet 930c offers excellent print quality and dependable performance at a good price point, making it a pragmatic choice for families and moderate users focused on photo printing. Yet, the high cost and ink consumption of official cartridges limit its appeal for heavy or professional use. For those who weigh print quality and ease of use heavily but remain cost-conscious, this printer strikes a reasonable balance, provided you stick to genuine HP supplies.

product_reviews: ['    I bought my current PC from Time Computers in 2000 and my Epson Stylus Color 300 printer came with it.The Epson Stylus Color 300 is an ink jet colour printer. It looks quite sleek for its age, but is probably quite bulky by today s standards as most printers nowadays tend to be much smaller.The print quality is generally satisfactory and I cannot really fault it. Sometimes the quality of print-outs will appear slightly grainy, but this is normally resolved if you clean the ink filter first. The crispness and clarity of pictures and photographs is very good, and this is thanks to Epson s Perfect Picture Imaging System and a high-resolution 720 dpi (dots per inch) micro piezo print head. The printer is quite easy to use. Apart from the on/off button, there are two main buttons - one to load/eject the paper, the other to clean the print head before printing commences. It also has three lights which turn on or flash according to the printer status. There is a convenient on-screen status monitor that lets you monitor ink levels and printer status, so you know how much ink you have left. When it comes to changing the cartridge, there is a warning on-screen and the  cleaning  light on the printer itself will come on to let you know that cartridge needs replacing. Loading a new ink cartridge is fairly straightforward, and I m sure if I can do it, anyone can  You simply press the cleaning button for three seconds until the cartridge clamp is in position, open the printer cover and insert the cartridge. However, be warned that if you remove a cartridge before the ink runs out, it may become unusable. I have had several problems with this, because sometimes the printer will not recognise that you have loaded a new cartridge and still claim that you are out of ink  This leaves you with no other choice but to take the cartridge out and start again - and risk the printer not accepting the new cartridge Price-wise, ink cartridges cost between    15-   20 and can be bought in most good stationery shops. You can buy black ink cartridges on their own or black and colour ink cartridges combined. I tend to buy black and colour cartridges because I do a fair amount of colour printing, However, buying these comes at a cost, because if one colour runs out, you have to buy a whole new cartridge, even if there is ink remaining in the cartridge  Notwithstanding this particular problem, the printer is generally economical when it comes to ink consumption, and I find that a cartridge can last between 3-6 months, depending on how frequently I choose  to print.Unfortunately, despite the excellent print quality and sparing use of ink, the Epson Stylus Color 300 has a lot of bad points, and one of them is the printing speed. It prints very slowly indeed and a page can take up to 5 minutes to print, which, I m sure you ll agree, is quite poor. It is also quite noisy when it prints and certainly much noisier than most modern day ink jet printers.Furthermore, I have had constant problems with the sheet loading facility. The standard sheet feeder is supposed to hold up to 100 A4 sheets and load them one by one, and when I first started using the printer, this was indeed the case. But over time, the sheet feeder has begun to malfunction, to such an extent that now if I tried to load even just a few pages, the printer would try to load them all in one go, thus causing a blockage  Since I ve had the printer, I ve experienced numerous other problems - none really that serious in nature, but frustrating nonetheless. Quite often when you load the paper, the printer decides to eject a blank piece of paper, rather than print the document you ve asked it to print. This is very annoying, but is normally resolved by switching the printer off and starting again. On other occasions, the printer prints a page of gobbledegook (normally random letters and characters) bearing no relationship to the actual document I ve asked it to print. There doesn t appear to be any apparent reason for this, but conveniently it seems to occur when you re trying to print off an essay in time for an imminent deadline Given the plethora of different printers now available, I would be surprised if the Stylus Color 300 is still being sold. If it is, I still wouldn t recommend it as it has far too many faults, and the bad points sadly outweigh the good. Overall, I rate this printer 3 stars out of 5.Thanks for reading. ', '    this lap top is the best my dads ever had from work, its got every thing i need, windows xp, dvd player, a nice amout of ram 256mb the battery isnt the best with roughly 3 hours on it, but cos i cant take it out of the house its perfect,  the processor speed is nice i think its roughly 1.5 which is lovely, the color of the lap is nice, mine is silver on the inside, and black on the out side with some silver, this lap top beats all, the advantages of this lap top is downloads are made much quicker, the software and the OS is easy for everyone to use, i love the speed it gets when its on the net when im downloading software and chatting on the net, i love this lap top, because my dad works for the council he gets to pick which lap top he wants, i went to the nearest computer shop and i trialed the lap tops and luckily i was able to find this lap top, and thankfully my dad was able to get it from work. i really do recommend this pc, the looks the speed, the style it has is defintely 2005+ this laptop is definetly a must have, its the easiest way to be good with computers, with out actually knowing what to do,      ', '    After months of struggle with my Manager and IT department, I was finally allowed to upgrade my standard company PC, to a faster model with more memory, better processor, and larger hard drive capacity. The Epson Stylus Color 300 presents a mixed bag for users who value practicality and performance, especially in printing tasks. From a cost-effectiveness standpoint, the printer is fairly economical for infrequent use, as ink consumption remains reasonable when printing occasionally. However, the expense of ink cartridges is a notable downside—cartridges must be fully replaced even if only one color runs out, which can quickly add up and impact overall value.

In terms of print quality, the Stylus Color 300 performs well with black and white documents, delivering crisp and clear results. Colour printing is satisfactory for everyday needs, but those expecting high-quality photo prints might be disappointed; colour photos tend to appear grainy and lack the sharpness that more advanced models provide. This aligns with the printer’s positioning as a budget-friendly, entry-level device rather than a professional photo printer.

Ease of use is a strong point here. The printer’s compact size and minimal physical controls make it approachable for first-time users, with most settings conveniently managed through the included software. This software is quite helpful, offering control over print quality, colour adjustments, and ink levels, which adds a layer of user-friendly customization. The comprehensive and clear instruction manual further supports a smooth setup and operation experience.

On the flip side, performance speed is a clear limitation. Printing can be slow, often taking several minutes per page, which may frustrate users with higher volume or time-sensitive printing needs. Given this, the Epson Stylus Color 300 is best suited for casual users or those with modest printing demands rather than heavy or professional workloads.

In summary, if you prioritize ease of use, compact design, and decent black-and-white printing on a budget, this printer is a reasonable choice. But if you require fast output or high-quality colour photos, it’s worth considering alternatives that better match those needs.
