product_reviews: ['    To those who haven t seen Lost already, watch it  Go out and buy the DVD s or borrow them from someone else and start watching. But make sure you watch from the beginning of the series and don t jump in the middle. This series is absolutely brilliant  It is wonderfully written, with amazing characters, some interesting ideas and a plotline that grabs you and makes sure keep going to the end. It s hard to say much about the plot without giving too much away. The series is written so that there are hundreds of mysteries. Some are posed in one episode and solved by the end of it, some are solved several episodes later, some we re still waiting for the answers. This is the sort of series where you re desperate to know what s going on, but at the same time don t want anyone to spoil it for you, so I ll try not to.The basic plot is that a plane crashed, stranding about forty people on an unknown island. They soon find out that the plane was off-course so anyone looking for them will be in the wrong place, so they have to come up with other ideas for how to get found. At the same time, they have to work together to survive on the island, which is not what it seems. As they spend their time on the island, they uncover more mysteries and learn more about each other. The storyline has clearly been well planned out. When something is revealed, you can see loads of clues to it that are only visible with hindsight. The plot is going to somewhere definite, somewhere the creators have all worked out. I just have no clue where it might be. I was amazingly proud that I guessed the surprise at the end of episode three (or episode four, depending on whether you count the pilot as one or two episodes) during the previous episode. The idea that forty people might survive a plane crash pretty much uninjured is rather hard to believe, which puts you right in the mood for everything else the story throws at you. The whole storyline points at something not normal guiding the characters. One of them believes that they were all brought to the island by destiny and, looking at how their lives are all connected, I might believe it. Each episode focuses on a single character. It shows flashbacks of their life before the island that shed insights onto how they behave now. It seems there are ties between all of the characters. One might own the company another works for or a character could have once had a drink with the father of another. The characters are nicely different, each with their own backgrounds. There are a lot of Americans in the group, but the plane was to LA so that s built into the plot. But there are also Australians, an Iraqi and a couple of Koreans who don t speak English. Some are likeable, some aren t, but all have well thought out backstories that give their behaviour plausibility. The main characters include: Jack, a surgeon and in some ways the leader of the group.Kate, whose background remains largely a mystery, but I have a few theories. Locke, definitely a mystery. A brilliant character who adds to the story every time he appears. Sawyer, who looks out for himself and no one else. Sayid, who knows a lot about electronics.Hurley, who is absolutely my favourite character. Like everyone else, he has his secrets but he is also a wonderfully cheerful soul with some brilliant lines. There are a lot more but this is just a selection. Most of the actors are relative unknowns, with the exception of Dominic Monaghan who plays Charlie, a failed rock star. This means you re not thinking of the characters in terms of who they ve played in films or other TV shows. There are some great effects in this show. I m not just talking special effects, although the plane crash was awesome. There is a scene from the point of view of one of the Koreans when lots of people are talking. The sound is a huge jumble taking odd words from each of the other characters to give an incomprehensible mess. I think this is an amazing way of getting across the difficulty of being stuck with people who you just can t understand. I think the whole series is masterfully done. I m going to be watching until the end. I would recommend it to anyone, though be warned, you will get hooked. Don t start watching unless you are willing to be stuck waiting for answers until they bring the series to an end (I think five seasons are planned for, but I m not sure). Even if you think that it s not your sort of series, give it a try, you might be surprised. There s a lot more hype over Lost than any other TV show I can think of, so that ought to say something. People wouldn t be talking about it this much if it didn t have something special.      ', '      Channel 4 s  Lost  produced by ABC TV has been airing for 14 weeks now. If you haven t seen it yet then I am here to tell you what you re missing   Lost is the tale of 48 passengers who are stranded after Oceanic flight 815 from Sydney to LA crashed onto an island, presumed to be somewhere in the Pacific Ocean (the series is filmed in Hawaii). At the time of the crash they were heading off course and lost radio contact and therefore no-one knows their exact whereabouts. To date the survivors have been on the island for around three weeks and they have just about given up any hope of being rescued. This short time on the island sure has been eventful though and each of the main characters has an illicit story to tell.   So far the survivors have scavenged the wreckage for anything remotely useful and have burn the bodies of the dead. They have explored much of the island and have found water in addition to hunting boar, fishing and growing fruit themselves. Although they have tried to signal for help using the planes radio this was unsuccessful and now the batteries are dead. After living on the beach for a while a small group moved inland to the caves, closer to fresh water and out of the intense tropical sun. However, others decided to stay at the beach, to keep a fire going and to keep an eye out for signs of rescue. In addition some of the survivors are scared to move into the jungle because of the little matter of the  monster  which lives out there and the bears. Early on the group shot a polar bear? and there have since been a number of other sightings since.... These are just some of the weird things that have happened on the Island.... ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~The Characters~~~~~~~~~~~~~~  Each episode focuses on one character in particular and their history is shown through a series of flashbacks which entwine with the current events.   Although there are 48 individuals currently stranded on the island there are a core group of individuals who feature more prominently that the others. These are:Jack (Matthew Fox)   The main male character is Jack, a doctor, who has become the natural leader of the group and who is constantly called upon for aid and advice. Jack was on the flight after going to Australia to attempt to fix things up with his Father, after reporting him to the medical consul for practising medicine while under the influence. However he was too late, his dad drank himself to death before he arrived. The coffin was on the plane and Jack found it... only to discover it was empty...Kate  (Evangeline Lilly).  Kate, the main female character, is a fugitive who was being escorted out of Australia by the police after being caught on the run. Her escort survived the crash but died soon afterwards revealing her secret to Jack. Otherwise Kate has so far managed to hide her status from the majority of the other survivors. She is gutsy, passionate and strong willed and has bonded best with both Jack and Sawyer. Charlie (Dominic Monaghan). Religious bassist of ex-band Drive Shaft, Charlie was in Australian to attempt to persuade her brother to re-join in him the rock and roll lifestyle. Charlie was addicted to cocaine when he arrived in the island and has been through a harsh withdrawal. Charlie has bonded best with Clare and the two of them recently underwent a shocking ordeal.... Sayid (Naveen Andrews). Iraqi Sayid is an ex serviceman, whose history lies in torturing people for information. He has taken on the roll as the intellectual of the group, mapping the island and attempting to understand coded documents he  acquired  . He is currently starting a love affair with Shannon although he is known best for his quarrels with Sawyer. Locke  (Terry O Quinn). John Locke was in Australia to follow his dream of completing a WalkAbout. The company sent him back after discovering he was in a wheelchair. Miraculously when the plane crashed Locke re-gained the use of his legs. He believes that they are all on the Island for a purpose. Locke is now the main hunter and explorer of the Island, together with Boone. He is a fearless and strong character who always has a few words of wisdom for those in need. Sawyer (Josh Holloway). Token bad boy, Sawyer is hated by the majority of the others for his disruptive and petty ways and consequently spends much time alone at the beach. He has particular issues with Sayid because of his race and is secretly in love with Kate. Hurley (Jorge Garcia). Token fat boy of the island any everybody s friend. Hurley s history has yet to be revealed on the show, although I happen to know that he is a millionaire after a huge lottery win, although he is prone to bad luck Clare  (Emelie de Ravin). Clare was eight months pregnant when the plane crashed. She was on the way to America to hand her baby over to adoptive parents, after her boyfriend left her. The couple were recommended by a psychic who insisted that she must raise the baby herself. is it possible he knew the plane would crash?Shanon (Maggie Grace). Spoil rich kid Shannon, step sister to Boon, is used to a plush lifestyle and getting her own way. Her reaction to the crash is to sunbath on the beach and just to take take take, although recently she has started to pull her weight, helping to translate French documents with Sayid. Boon (Ian Somerhalder). Boon has been harbouring secret feelings for Shannon for years. He went to Australia to rescue her from a supposed violent relationship and initially he is very over-protective of her. Although his exploration with Locke has recently caused him to lose interest. Sun  (Yunjin Kim) and Jin  (Daniel Dae Kim). This Korean couple have so far had little to do with the other survivors. Sun can speak English although her husband doesn t know. He treats her badly and insists that she cover up at all times. Micheal (Harold Perrineau) and his nine year old son Walter (Malcolm David Kelly) The pair have only recently met. After Walters mother died, Walter was entrusted back to Micheal s care after years apart and they are struggling to get to know and respect each other again. Micheal is currently putting all his energy into the building of a raft which he hopes will help to get them off the island. ~~~~~~~~~~~~Recent Events ~~~~~~~~~~~~  To complicate things further there is a French women living on the Island who has been there for 16 years. During his exploration of the island Sayid ran into the women named Danielle (Mira Furlan), who was part of a shipwrecked research team. She told him about the  others  and warned  him of the dangers the island holds. So far this intense encounter has been her only appearance although we can be sure that she will be back. The survivors have also recently discovered that in addition to the French women they are  not alone  on the island. This was established after creating a log and comparing it to the pilots passenger log. A mystery survivor  Ethan  (William Mapother) was discovered too late, he kidnapped Clare and Charlie with dire consequences... In addition Locke and Boon have discovered a hatch buried in the jungle floor, except they can t figure out how to open it to see what s inside.....~~~~~~~~~My Opinion~~~~~~~~~  You only have to watch this show once be become completely addicted. It is enthralling and full of suspense, with loads of scary, shocking and down right unbelievable moments that will keep you tuning in for more. The characters are vivid, interesting and endearing and there is bound to be someone you can identify with. My biggest qualm has to be the fact that on the whole all of the characters are stunning with perfect hair and makeup which seems rather unlikely when one is stranded on a desert island but hey, this is American drama and that is the American way.  On the whole this is a great drama, the best show on TV at the moment in my eyes and I currently await Wednesday nights with logging. If you haven t seen it you really should tune in ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~When can I see it?~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~   Lost  is currently shown between 10-11pm, Wednesdays on 4 and to date there  are a remaining 10 episodes left of the first series. Each episode is actually really only half an hour long and adverts fill the remaining space, which I find hugely annoying. If you have E4 you can also watch the next episode immediately after.   The first season is now also available to buy on DVD.  But the show doesn t end there. A second series will also be hitting our screens although I have no idea when.   If you want to know more check out http://abc.go.com/primetime/lost/episodes/117.html       ', '    Just before the first series of lost came out I was hooked it was something that the advert made it look really good and the reviews that it had were excellent so I had to watch it. Unfortunately I watched the whole of the first series where they then moved it to sky so it was harder to watch, but I still watched it and it was one of the best series that I had seen.It then turned out that the story that was great was being dragged through about being stuck on the island, I then also read that they were having four or five series and to have to carry on watching this with the same plot of being stuck on the island was starting to wear thin as this island seemed to have everything on it just that no one could ever find them, so it was a little farfetched to say the least. So half way through season two I stopped watching it.Lost is about Forty-eight survivors that were in a plane crash in the middle of the pacific and are stranded on a strange island, although this island is not what it seems with strange creatures and some people that live on the island.The survivors also have their own deep dark secrets that they all have too and when everyone tries to pull together to get rescued there are some events and stories that no one expected along the way. There are a lot more cast members but these are a few of the main characters.This is worth a watch it is just a very long series and if you have the time and the patience this is one to watch as it has some great actors in it that put on a great performance and do a really great job in the roles that they were cast.My favourite character is Charlie the rock star he has overcome so many things on this island and yet makes every effort to help whilst struggling with his addiction.     ', '    At first I was sceptical of this television show, I did not believe the hype, so I was not anxious to watch the first episode. Eventually however, I was persuaded to give it a try by someone who claimed to be  addicted to it . I did give it a try, and am glad I did, I enjoyed it - though I did not thing it justified my persuader s feelings towards it. However, since then I have gotten into it more, and whilst I wouldn t say that I m addicted to it, I definitely do look forward to the next episode For those of you that somehow don t yet know, Lost is the tale of a commercial flight from Sydney to L.A. that lost radio contact, veered  a thousand miles  off course, and crashed on a pacific island. This crash was devastating, and by rights should have obliterated everyone onboard, however, this is a mysterious island, which seems to have a force of its own, so 47 people did survive. These lost passengers live on the island, slowly uncovering and discovering its mysteries, awaiting a rescue that doesn t look likely to ever happen. Apparently, Lost had the most expensive television debut in history, the first (double length) episode costing  5million to produce [I like the pun in the title of the first episode, The Pilot, as it is a pilot episode and an episode about the aeroplane pilot..]. This enormous investment was obviously a massive gamble, but it definitely was worth it in my opinion, the production values are amazing  We see massive explosions, real bits of ripped apart aeroplane, good special effects too, as we see one man get sucked into a surviving jet engine, impossibly still whirring like crazy. This is all shot on-location in beautiful Hawaii, on the beach no less. These stunning features make it seem like you re watching an actual movie rather than just a show on television, and make Lost an innovative breath of fresh air into the stagnant airwaves populated by solely in-studio sit-coms. Of course, production values aren t everything in a presentation, one needs content as well  Well, Lost certainly has that. Each episode, right from the very beginning with the dramatic plane crash scene, is packed full of action, plot twists, interesting facts, character development, and new and exciting situations. As the island is so mysterious and  seemingly  unpopulated, there is much for the lost passengers to explore and encounter for our entertainment, and every episode features at least one flash back into a characters past, so we learn interesting things about each of the people marooned on this tropical paradise. These flashbacks help to break up the action and keep us interested, as sometimes it is like several stories on the go at once. As the cast discovers new things the whole time, and there is still much to explore, I expect the storyline to keep me riveted for a while yet to come   However, Lost isn t entirely perfect. Sometimes the show seems like it doesn t really know where its going, like it is bringing up all these questions that need answering but which it doesn t have any answers to. I saw an interview with the directors, and they themselves said they don t really know where it s going; they re basically making it up as they go along - they said they only finish writing each episode a few weeks before it is aired  This fact, and also the hundreds of plot twists sometimes leave us feeling a bit dazed and confused. As so much is going on in each episode, and there are so many episodes, it is also very easy to forget what has happened previously, forget little details that turn out to be important when they are referenced later. This too can leave us a little bit bewildered and frustrated.Another bad point linked with the previous one is that the story seems a little slow in developing, which is frustrating as each week we hope for answers to the interesting questions about the story the previous episode posed, only to have a show that has nothing to do with it  I suppose its one way to keep viewers watching, but it can be frustrating. Also, some of the episodes are a lot weaker than others, some of them have almost nothing going on, not even any significant character development. I would say that Lost is one of the most dangerously exciting television shows in recent history, it is in a league of its own, there is nothing anything like it. If you missed it when it was first broadcast, I recommend getting hold of a copy  This way you wouldn t have to wait weeks for the bits you want to see.For whilst Lost could do with some of its creases being ironed out, and could definitely be improved, I still love being lost in Lost.     ', '    Anyone who watches Channel 4 can t have failed to notice them plugging their latest American import  Lost  quite heavily. First there were the enigmatic teaser trailers, with a bunch of people dancing on a desert island beach. Even now, the stars of the show feature heavily on those things where celebrities answer question (their biggest fault, what they d like to do before they die, favourite food).  Lost  was apparently quite a big hit in the US, so it s unsurprising it received quite a lot of hype before being shown here. So far, it s seemed pretty justified too.The basic premise, for those living under a rock, is that the show charts the lives of 40-odd survivors of a plane crash on an unknown Pacific island. They were en route from Australia to LA, but diverted after problems - hence the plane crashed way off course, and the chance of rescue - or even where they are - is unknown.There s a quite extensive cast of characters, some we see more of than others. I can t list them all, but for the benefit of anyone who hasn t seen the early episodes I ll introduce the main ones:Jack Shepherd (Matthew Fox) - a doctor who seemingly by default takes charge, probably the  main character  in so far as there is one.Kate Ryan (Evangeline Lilly) - the  female star , though like everyone she habours past secrets, and hers are darker than most.Charlie Pace (Dominic Monaghan) - former bassist with one-hit wonders Drive Shaft, a bit weird and a druggie. One of my favourites, because he adds a comic touch.Hugo  Hurley  Reyes (Jorge Garcia) - the token big fat guy, and another for comic moments.Sayid Jarrah (Naveen Andrews) - a former Iraqi Republican Guard, makes some suspicious of him, but he has some useful skills for survival.James  Sawyer  Ford (Josh Holloway) - a cynical, out-for-himself chap whose first reaction is to loot the wreckage, and trade what he finds for profit.John Locke (Terry O Quinn) - something of the strange and mysterious old man, who always seems to know a bit more than he lets on (is it a coincidence he shares his name with probably the greatest English philosopher ever?), something of a survivalist, which makes him a useful hunter.Walt Lloyd (Malcolm David Kelly) - the only child, was just about to begin life with his father Michael Dawson (Harold Perrineau) after his mother s death.Shannon Rutherford (Maggie Grace) - spoilt little rich girl, whose first responses to the crash are to give herself a pedicure and sunbathe in her bikini, because she d  just been through a difficult time  - to the disgust of her step-brother Boone (Ian Somerhalder)Jin-Soo Kwon (Daniel Dae Kim) and his wife Sun-Soo (Yunjin Kim) - a Korean couple who don t seem to speak English, and keep much to themselves, despite some attempts to break the language/culture barrier.Claire Littleton (Emelie de Ravin) - eight months pregnant, which could be a burden in the struggle to survive.Plenty more about the characters is available online (even on Wikipedia) but I ve avoided the many fan sites and such for fear of spoilers. I know one of my flatmates has already seen trailers of all the episodes of the series, and thus has a good idea what happens.Each show chronicles a day or two in the lives of the islanders, and the struggles they face - finding food or water, dealing with group conflict, plans to seek rescue - but also focuses on the past of one character in particular, which is revealed through the show in flashbacks to before. It s an interesting technique. I think it s particularly effective, because the problem for many TV shows is that the viewers don t know the characters. In Lost, it works so well because, with a few exceptions, they don t know each other either - we learn about them only gradually, through their actions and what they reveal about their past.It s very clever at times, how little details are fitted in - for example, in one of the early episodes focusing on Locke, we learn why he reacts as he does after the crash, and the secret of his past. The acting also is very good. It s hard to say how people would react to such an extreme environment, but everyone seems to fit their characters well (probably helped by the fact they were nearly all unknowns, at least to me - so like, say, Friends, you now think of them just as that character).I wasn t too convinced by the actual plane crash effects, shown mostly in the first episode. Not that I know what a real crash would be like anyway, it just didn t seem  real  enough - which probably means it was more realistic than how it  should  look (i.e. bigger explosions, etc). Then again, this is only a TV series, not a Hollywood blockbuster, and the effects weren t that bad. It s a minor quibble now that s past - everything else about the island has looked pretty much spot on. What s particularly effective is how they create at times a sense of wonder or fear. The survivors don t know what s out there on the island, and in the first night in particular - assailed by unfamiliar noises - that was very clear.I suppose the most unrealistic feature is simply the cast - who despite the token few foreigners, blacks, fat person and such are disproportionately  beautiful people , but then as any Hollyoaks viewer knows, that never hurt on TV    I think the success of the series (aside from this fact) is largely owed to the universal themes - dealing with adversity, hope, past secrets, human nature and the whole  Lord Of The Flies /building a new society scenario. The island, you get the feeling, could be either a heaven or hell, depending on their actions - reminiscent of the Leonardo diCaprio film  The Beach  in this respect. ', '    For all of those who have been watching the series on terrestial TV, boy are you in for the ride of your life I had missed the very first episode as my hubby had taken control of the TV that night, now he doesn t get a look in.A plane crashes into an remote island... and somehow over 40 people and a dog survive?? ', '    WARNING: Even though I ve taken every effort not to include too much plot, there are a few minor spoilers contained within. Read on at your own risk THE PLOT=========Oceanic flight 815 hits turbulence and loses radio contact an hour into the flight. It s already a thousand miles off course when it goes down; any search party sent to look for survivors would be looking in the wrong place. The plane crashes on a tropical island, and amazingly 48 passengers survive. This eclectic group try and adapt to their new lives in this situation. Learning new skills to survive and living on a diet of fish and wild boar. Sounds from the jungle could indicate they are not the only people on the island WHY IT S GOOD==============A man in a suit regains consciousness in a bamboo forest, a dog runs past him. The man gets up and runs through the trees until he comes out onto a paradise beach. Only it s not paradise, there are dead bodies and dying bodies spread all over the sand. There s a jet engine that s still running and the wreckage of a plane everywhere. This opening scene to Lost really says a lot about the programme; a man in a suit lying on the ground in a forest...  How did he get there? Who is he? Where is he? What in the world is that dog doing there?  Confusion, intrigue and suspense are what make Lost so watchable.Within the first five minutes of episode one a man gets sucked into the jet engine, exploding all over the beach, which tells us early on that this is not your usual TV show. It s shocking and surprising, anything could happen. It also tells us that the producers have spent lots of money making it, because the special effects wouldn t look out of place in a big Hollywood production. Another huge pull of Lost is that it looks so good. Combining great camera work, interesting editing and the fact that it s on location in Honolulu makes for a beautiful programme.The show focuses on 14 individuals (although one of them makes a permanent exit half-way through season 1  ) and in each episode more of the islanders lives are lived out for us, but we also learn more about these people by seeing their back story told through flash backs. This is why Lost is such an addictive programme: we learn so much about the characters that we care about them. There would be no intrigue or suspense if we didn t care  The main characters are all very interesting and have great back stories. The fact that I ve changed who I thought was my favourite character about 10 times is testament to how good the characters are Each episode provides enough new information to keep you hooked, but always without giving too much away. Usually when we are given resolution to a major mystery that has been building over several episodes, it will leave new and bigger questions in its place. Each episode lasts an hour (42 minutes without ads ), and features one of the leads for that time; I think this works really well in slowly revealing more about the characters and adding depth to their stories.THE CHARACTERS================Here are my current favourite three:1) Sawyer played by Josh Holloway. He s done some bad things in his past and therefore thinks that he deserves everyone s hate, and he encourages people to hate him - he doesn t get that the island is a fresh start for everyone. Two things I love about Sawyer, firstly his accent and secondly the developing relationship he has with Kate.2) John Locke played by Terry O Quinn. A man of faith, he believes that everyone is on the island for a specific reason and that the island bought them there - I think he may be right 3) Charlie played by Dominic Monaghan. The only cast member I had seen before, famous for playing Merry Brandybuck in the Lord of the Rings (and less famous for being Hetty Wainthropp s assistant). He s a very realistic character, he makes good and noble decisions, but then in the next scene he can make a huge blunder. He s in a rock band from Manchester, his brother is called Liam, and they both take loads of drugs - sounds familiar WHY IT S NOT SO GOOD=====================There are certain things about Lost which I find slightly irritating. American TV is full of beautiful actors and actresses - I accept this, but even after months of being stranded on a desert island? Clothes perfectly ironed, make-up brilliant, hair from Vidal Sassoon - and that s just the men  It s almost laughable that by the end of season 1, Jack (the shows main man) has a five o clock shadow, and the same length hair he started with. This is only a slight annoyance that I ve learnt to live with I wish that the flow of information was a little quicker sometimes. Without wanting to give too much of the plot away, two of the characters find a hatch on the island, and for about 9 episodes try and figure out how to get in it. To start with there was much excitement,  perhaps they ll manage to open it in this episode  I thought. Then I started to get frustrated,  just get it open, so I can see what s down there , followed by,  do I really care what s down there.  This opinion was shared by our American cousins, as the reaction to the first seasons climax was met with disappointment as not enough was revealed. The producers took this feedback and made an absolutely killer start to season 2, with the first 5 episodes resolving practically the whole first series.CONCLUSION============This is a truly great TV show, unlike anything I ve seen before. It s on Channel 4 on a Wednesday night at 10pm, and be warned that it does get a little frustrating towards the end of the season, but its well worth seeing it through to the end. I watched the whole thing in a week, and I think this is the best way to do it, some episodes are a bit slow and I d be gutted if I d waited a whole week for it  So buy the DVD, get a friend with quick internet to download it, or keep patience with channel 4 - but however you get it, make sure you get lost      ', '    Have you been watching it? well HAVE YOU? if you havnt, then you have been missing out on probably one of the best things to come out of America this year.The beginning:- There is a plane crash on a deserted island and all the survivors are stranded. You have to give it a watch Stups. watch out for the numbers      ', '    Lost premiered on Channel 4 on August 10th this year. It arrived in a wave of hype, it was in every magazine, there were loads of TV spots. Channel 4 even showed a fancy commercial in the cinemas for it. Needless to say all the fuss worked as around six million people tuned in that night. But within weeks that number had dropped and it s easy to see why.But before I get into that let me explain a bit about the show. A plane crashes on a remote island. Among the survivors are people with different personalities, people with secrets, people who are just background extras. Together they must all work as a unit in order to survive and hope that help will come. But this island is full of mystery, at night there are crashing trees and the sound of an unknown creature. During the day there are just conflicts between the survivors. Over the space of 24 episodes we find out a little more about each of the main characters, their back-stories and why they were on that plane. This is intercut with the advancing plot of what is on the island and whether the creature is indeed a creature.I could go into more detail but like most TV shows of this nature, the less you know before you watch the better.I have to admit that I ve actually seen the first season of Lost already. I simply couldn t wait till February of nest year to see the conclusion on TV. Instead I bought the Region 1 DVD boxset, which is available, online for around    30. It s a far better way of watching the series as you can take it at your own pace and not have to wade through the advertising breaks.So is the show worthy of the hype after all is said and done? The honest answer is no, while the show is well made and intriguing it s also incredibly frustrating and ultimately under whelming. I like the characters in the show. Jack the doctor is a good voice of reason, you have a number of good looking women while there is a sense of danger in a few of the blokes on the island. Thankfully there s also a little comic relief from the fat guy. But everyone s back-story just get s drawn out. This is the reason why you ve had many people give up on watching it. In the first few episodes you get the idea that every week will deal with one characters story, once that s done they would then move on to the good stuff. Instead we get everyone s story, then we get a little more and then a little more. The island stuff is really small change in comparison and that s a shame as this is where the good stuff happens. Around the mid-way point of the season you get some great plot twists that keep you intrigued. It s also around this point that you get the feeling the creators knew a second season was getting made. Therefore everything you re teased with ends up being unresolved. I can t really say any more than that without going into specifics. Of course that would ruin it for anyone that is still watching.After watching the whole season I had a feeling of being cheated. I knew what I had seen was good television but it was nothing what I had expected. It promised so much and then didn t actually deliver on it. You have to compare it to similar US TV shows and say it s not as good. For example 24 is far better than this for telling a story over the course of 24 episodes. It slowly cranks up the tension as every episode goes on before resolving itself in the final episode. Lost producer JJ Abraham s Alias is also better than Lost, certainly in it s first two seasons. I ve spoken to a few people that are hooked on Lost and I do tell then it s a bit of a damp squib. I ve also talked to people that have stopped watching and they ve agreed that things get a little tired and samey.Will I watch Season 2? Probably but I won t be excited about it. I ll tune in just to see is anything carried over from season one gets resolved. If it doesn t then it s really just a cocktease of a programme designed to keep you intrigued and keep the viewing figures up.You have been warned.     ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re diving into *Lost*, you’re in for a wild ride that’s often hailed as one of America’s best recent TV dramas. The show’s originality shines through its intriguing premise: a diverse group of plane crash survivors stranded on a mysterious island, each episode peeling back layers of their backstories through flashbacks. This character-driven approach is a major strength—watching characters like the cheeky bad boy Sawyer or the initially selfish but evolving Shannon adds rich emotional texture that makes you genuinely care about their fates.

The plot is brilliantly crafted, packed with hundreds of mysteries that keep you guessing. A standout moment is the discovery of the hatch, which builds suspense over several episodes and deepens the island’s enigma. However, be prepared for some pacing quirks—at times, the show lingers too long on flashbacks, which can slow down the momentum and feel a bit tiring if you prefer a faster narrative flow.

Season one’s finale left some viewers wanting more resolution, but season two picks up the pace and delivers better payoff, rewarding your patience. Given the complex storytelling and numerous characters, it’s best to watch *Lost* from the very beginning to avoid confusion and fully appreciate the intricate connections and fan theories that have fueled passionate discussions.

Emotionally, the series doesn’t shy away from tearjerker moments, so keep tissues handy. Overall, *Lost* offers a compelling blend of drama, suspense, and humor—especially through witty character interactions—that should satisfy your curiosity and analytical mind while keeping you entertained. Just be ready for a slow burn at times, and you’ll find it a rewarding journey into one of TV’s most talked-about mysteries.

product_reviews: ['    To those who haven t seen Lost already, watch it  Go out and buy the DVD s or borrow them from someone else and start watching. But make sure you watch from the beginning of the series and don t jump in the middle. This series is absolutely brilliant  It is wonderfully written, with amazing characters, some interesting ideas and a plotline that grabs you and makes sure keep going to the end. It s hard to say much about the plot without giving too much away. The series is written so that there are hundreds of mysteries. Some are posed in one episode and solved by the end of it, some are solved several episodes later, some we re still waiting for the answers. This is the sort of series where you re desperate to know what s going on, but at the same time don t want anyone to spoil it for you, so I ll try not to.The basic plot is that a plane crashed, stranding about forty people on an unknown island. They soon find out that the plane was off-course so anyone looking for them will be in the wrong place, so they have to come up with other ideas for how to get found. At the same time, they have to work together to survive on the island, which is not what it seems. As they spend their time on the island, they uncover more mysteries and learn more about each other. The storyline has clearly been well planned out. When something is revealed, you can see loads of clues to it that are only visible with hindsight. The plot is going to somewhere definite, somewhere the creators have all worked out. I just have no clue where it might be. I was amazingly proud that I guessed the surprise at the end of episode three (or episode four, depending on whether you count the pilot as one or two episodes) during the previous episode. The idea that forty people might survive a plane crash pretty much uninjured is rather hard to believe, which puts you right in the mood for everything else the story throws at you. The whole storyline points at something not normal guiding the characters. One of them believes that they were all brought to the island by destiny and, looking at how their lives are all connected, I might believe it. Each episode focuses on a single character. It shows flashbacks of their life before the island that shed insights onto how they behave now. It seems there are ties between all of the characters. One might own the company another works for or a character could have once had a drink with the father of another. The characters are nicely different, each with their own backgrounds. There are a lot of Americans in the group, but the plane was to LA so that s built into the plot. But there are also Australians, an Iraqi and a couple of Koreans who don t speak English. Some are likeable, some aren t, but all have well thought out backstories that give their behaviour plausibility. The main characters include: Jack, a surgeon and in some ways the leader of the group.Kate, whose background remains largely a mystery, but I have a few theories. Locke, definitely a mystery. A brilliant character who adds to the story every time he appears. Sawyer, who looks out for himself and no one else. Sayid, who knows a lot about electronics.Hurley, who is absolutely my favourite character. Like everyone else, he has his secrets but he is also a wonderfully cheerful soul with some brilliant lines. There are a lot more but this is just a selection. Most of the actors are relative unknowns, with the exception of Dominic Monaghan who plays Charlie, a failed rock star. This means you re not thinking of the characters in terms of who they ve played in films or other TV shows. There are some great effects in this show. I m not just talking special effects, although the plane crash was awesome. There is a scene from the point of view of one of the Koreans when lots of people are talking. The sound is a huge jumble taking odd words from each of the other characters to give an incomprehensible mess. I think this is an amazing way of getting across the difficulty of being stuck with people who you just can t understand. I think the whole series is masterfully done. I m going to be watching until the end. I would recommend it to anyone, though be warned, you will get hooked. Don t start watching unless you are willing to be stuck waiting for answers until they bring the series to an end (I think five seasons are planned for, but I m not sure). Even if you think that it s not your sort of series, give it a try, you might be surprised. There s a lot more hype over Lost than any other TV show I can think of, so that ought to say something. People wouldn t be talking about it this much if it didn t have something special.      ', '      Channel 4 s  Lost  produced by ABC TV has been airing for 14 weeks now. If you haven t seen it yet then I am here to tell you what you re missing   Lost is the tale of 48 passengers who are stranded after Oceanic flight 815 from Sydney to LA crashed onto an island, presumed to be somewhere in the Pacific Ocean (the series is filmed in Hawaii). At the time of the crash they were heading off course and lost radio contact and therefore no-one knows their exact whereabouts. To date the survivors have been on the island for around three weeks and they have just about given up any hope of being rescued. This short time on the island sure has been eventful though and each of the main characters has an illicit story to tell.   So far the survivors have scavenged the wreckage for anything remotely useful and have burn the bodies of the dead. They have explored much of the island and have found water in addition to hunting boar, fishing and growing fruit themselves. Although they have tried to signal for help using the planes radio this was unsuccessful and now the batteries are dead. After living on the beach for a while a small group moved inland to the caves, closer to fresh water and out of the intense tropical sun. However, others decided to stay at the beach, to keep a fire going and to keep an eye out for signs of rescue. In addition some of the survivors are scared to move into the jungle because of the little matter of the  monster  which lives out there and the bears. Early on the group shot a polar bear? and there have since been a number of other sightings since.... These are just some of the weird things that have happened on the Island.... ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~The Characters~~~~~~~~~~~~~~  Each episode focuses on one character in particular and their history is shown through a series of flashbacks which entwine with the current events.   Although there are 48 individuals currently stranded on the island there are a core group of individuals who feature more prominently that the others. These are:Jack (Matthew Fox)   The main male character is Jack, a doctor, who has become the natural leader of the group and who is constantly called upon for aid and advice. Jack was on the flight after going to Australia to attempt to fix things up with his Father, after reporting him to the medical consul for practising medicine while under the influence. However he was too late, his dad drank himself to death before he arrived. The coffin was on the plane and Jack found it... only to discover it was empty...Kate  (Evangeline Lilly).  Kate, the main female character, is a fugitive who was being escorted out of Australia by the police after being caught on the run. Her escort survived the crash but died soon afterwards revealing her secret to Jack. Otherwise Kate has so far managed to hide her status from the majority of the other survivors. She is gutsy, passionate and strong willed and has bonded best with both Jack and Sawyer. Charlie (Dominic Monaghan). Religious bassist of ex-band Drive Shaft, Charlie was in Australian to attempt to persuade her brother to re-join in him the rock and roll lifestyle. Charlie was addicted to cocaine when he arrived in the island and has been through a harsh withdrawal. Charlie has bonded best with Clare and the two of them recently underwent a shocking ordeal.... Sayid (Naveen Andrews). Iraqi Sayid is an ex serviceman, whose history lies in torturing people for information. He has taken on the roll as the intellectual of the group, mapping the island and attempting to understand coded documents he  acquired  . He is currently starting a love affair with Shannon although he is known best for his quarrels with Sawyer. Locke  (Terry O Quinn). John Locke was in Australia to follow his dream of completing a WalkAbout. The company sent him back after discovering he was in a wheelchair. Miraculously when the plane crashed Locke re-gained the use of his legs. He believes that they are all on the Island for a purpose. Locke is now the main hunter and explorer of the Island, together with Boone. He is a fearless and strong character who always has a few words of wisdom for those in need. Sawyer (Josh Holloway). Token bad boy, Sawyer is hated by the majority of the others for his disruptive and petty ways and consequently spends much time alone at the beach. He has particular issues with Sayid because of his race and is secretly in love with Kate. Hurley (Jorge Garcia). Token fat boy of the island any everybody s friend. Hurley s history has yet to be revealed on the show, although I happen to know that he is a millionaire after a huge lottery win, although he is prone to bad luck Clare  (Emelie de Ravin). Clare was eight months pregnant when the plane crashed. She was on the way to America to hand her baby over to adoptive parents, after her boyfriend left her. The couple were recommended by a psychic who insisted that she must raise the baby herself. is it possible he knew the plane would crash?Shanon (Maggie Grace). Spoil rich kid Shannon, step sister to Boon, is used to a plush lifestyle and getting her own way. Her reaction to the crash is to sunbath on the beach and just to take take take, although recently she has started to pull her weight, helping to translate French documents with Sayid. Boon (Ian Somerhalder). Boon has been harbouring secret feelings for Shannon for years. He went to Australia to rescue her from a supposed violent relationship and initially he is very over-protective of her. Although his exploration with Locke has recently caused him to lose interest. Sun  (Yunjin Kim) and Jin  (Daniel Dae Kim). This Korean couple have so far had little to do with the other survivors. Sun can speak English although her husband doesn t know. He treats her badly and insists that she cover up at all times. Micheal (Harold Perrineau) and his nine year old son Walter (Malcolm David Kelly) The pair have only recently met. After Walters mother died, Walter was entrusted back to Micheal s care after years apart and they are struggling to get to know and respect each other again. Micheal is currently putting all his energy into the building of a raft which he hopes will help to get them off the island. ~~~~~~~~~~~~Recent Events ~~~~~~~~~~~~  To complicate things further there is a French women living on the Island who has been there for 16 years. During his exploration of the island Sayid ran into the women named Danielle (Mira Furlan), who was part of a shipwrecked research team. She told him about the  others  and warned  him of the dangers the island holds. So far this intense encounter has been her only appearance although we can be sure that she will be back. The survivors have also recently discovered that in addition to the French women they are  not alone  on the island. This was established after creating a log and comparing it to the pilots passenger log. A mystery survivor  Ethan  (William Mapother) was discovered too late, he kidnapped Clare and Charlie with dire consequences... In addition Locke and Boon have discovered a hatch buried in the jungle floor, except they can t figure out how to open it to see what s inside.....~~~~~~~~~My Opinion~~~~~~~~~  You only have to watch this show once be become completely addicted. It is enthralling and full of suspense, with loads of scary, shocking and down right unbelievable moments that will keep you tuning in for more. The characters are vivid, interesting and endearing and there is bound to be someone you can identify with. My biggest qualm has to be the fact that on the whole all of the characters are stunning with perfect hair and makeup which seems rather unlikely when one is stranded on a desert island but hey, this is American drama and that is the American way.  On the whole this is a great drama, the best show on TV at the moment in my eyes and I currently await Wednesday nights with logging. If you haven t seen it you really should tune in ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~When can I see it?~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~   Lost  is currently shown between 10-11pm, Wednesdays on 4 and to date there  are a remaining 10 episodes left of the first series. Each episode is actually really only half an hour long and adverts fill the remaining space, which I find hugely annoying. If you have E4 you can also watch the next episode immediately after.   The first season is now also available to buy on DVD.  But the show doesn t end there. A second series will also be hitting our screens although I have no idea when.   If you want to know more check out http://abc.go.com/primetime/lost/episodes/117.html       ', '    Just before the first series of lost came out I was hooked it was something that the advert made it look really good and the reviews that it had were excellent so I had to watch it. ', '    At first I was sceptical of this television show, I did not believe the hype, so I was not anxious to watch the first episode. Eventually however, I was persuaded to give it a try by someone who claimed to be  addicted to it . I did give it a try, and am glad I did, I enjoyed it - though I did not thing it justified my persuader s feelings towards it. However, since then I have gotten into it more, and whilst I wouldn t say that I m addicted to it, I definitely do look forward to the next episode For those of you that somehow don t yet know, Lost is the tale of a commercial flight from Sydney to L.A. that lost radio contact, veered  a thousand miles  off course, and crashed on a pacific island. This crash was devastating, and by rights should have obliterated everyone onboard, however, this is a mysterious island, which seems to have a force of its own, so 47 people did survive. These lost passengers live on the island, slowly uncovering and discovering its mysteries, awaiting a rescue that doesn t look likely to ever happen. Apparently, Lost had the most expensive television debut in history, the first (double length) episode costing  5million to produce [I like the pun in the title of the first episode, The Pilot, as it is a pilot episode and an episode about the aeroplane pilot..]. This enormous investment was obviously a massive gamble, but it definitely was worth it in my opinion, the production values are amazing  We see massive explosions, real bits of ripped apart aeroplane, good special effects too, as we see one man get sucked into a surviving jet engine, impossibly still whirring like crazy. This is all shot on-location in beautiful Hawaii, on the beach no less. These stunning features make it seem like you re watching an actual movie rather than just a show on television, and make Lost an innovative breath of fresh air into the stagnant airwaves populated by solely in-studio sit-coms. Of course, production values aren t everything in a presentation, one needs content as well  Well, Lost certainly has that. Each episode, right from the very beginning with the dramatic plane crash scene, is packed full of action, plot twists, interesting facts, character development, and new and exciting situations. As the island is so mysterious and  seemingly  unpopulated, there is much for the lost passengers to explore and encounter for our entertainment, and every episode features at least one flash back into a characters past, so we learn interesting things about each of the people marooned on this tropical paradise. These flashbacks help to break up the action and keep us interested, as sometimes it is like several stories on the go at once. As the cast discovers new things the whole time, and there is still much to explore, I expect the storyline to keep me riveted for a while yet to come   However, Lost isn t entirely perfect. Sometimes the show seems like it doesn t really know where its going, like it is bringing up all these questions that need answering but which it doesn t have any answers to. I saw an interview with the directors, and they themselves said they don t really know where it s going; they re basically making it up as they go along - they said they only finish writing each episode a few weeks before it is aired  This fact, and also the hundreds of plot twists sometimes leave us feeling a bit dazed and confused. As so much is going on in each episode, and there are so many episodes, it is also very easy to forget what has happened previously, forget little details that turn out to be important when they are referenced later. I know one of my flatmates has already seen trailers of all the episodes of the series, and thus has a good idea what happens.Each show chronicles a day or two in the lives of the islanders, and the struggles they face - finding food or water, dealing with group conflict, plans to seek rescue - but also focuses on the past of one character in particular, which is revealed through the show in flashbacks to before. It s an interesting technique. I think it s particularly effective, because the problem for many TV shows is that the viewers don t know the characters. In Lost, it works so well because, with a few exceptions, they don t know each other either - we learn about them only gradually, through their actions and what they reveal about their past.It s very clever at times, how little details are fitted in - for example, in one of the early episodes focusing on Locke, we learn why he reacts as he does after the crash, and the secret of his past. It s hard to say how people would react to such an extreme environment, but everyone seems to fit their characters well (probably helped by the fact they were nearly all unknowns, at least to me - so like, say, Friends, you now think of them just as that character).I wasn t too convinced by the actual plane crash effects, shown mostly in the first episode. It s a minor quibble now that s past - everything else about the island has looked pretty much spot on. What s particularly effective is how they create at times a sense of wonder or fear. The island, you get the feeling, could be either a heaven or hell, depending on their actions - reminiscent of the Leonardo diCaprio film  The Beach  in this respect. With so much left unknown, or to be uncovered only gradually, you can believe pretty much what you want, and that s part of the fun, piecing together your own theories.For my money, one of the best things on TV at the moment. Needless to say all the fuss worked as around six million people tuned in that night. But within weeks that number had dropped and it s easy to see why.But before I get into that let me explain a bit about the show. A plane crashes on a remote island. Among the survivors are people with different personalities, people with secrets, people who are just background extras. Together they must all work as a unit in order to survive and hope that help will come. But this island is full of mystery, at night there are crashing trees and the sound of an unknown creature. During the day there are just conflicts between the survivors. Over the space of 24 episodes we find out a little more about each of the main characters, their back-stories and why they were on that plane. This is intercut with the advancing plot of what is on the island and whether the creature is indeed a creature.I could go into more detail but like most TV shows of this nature, the less you know before you watch the better.I have to admit that I ve actually seen the first season of Lost already. I simply couldn t wait till February of nest year to see the conclusion on TV. Instead I bought the Region 1 DVD boxset, which is available, online for around    30. The honest answer is no, while the show is well made and intriguing it s also incredibly frustrating and ultimately under whelming. I like the characters in the show. Around the mid-way point of the season you get some great plot twists that keep you intrigued. It s also around this point that you get the feeling the creators knew a second season was getting made. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
“Lost” stands out as a richly layered series that expertly blends mystery, survival, and deep character exploration—elements that will surely satisfy your analytical and emotionally engaged nature. The show’s intense opening scenes immediately plunge viewers into confusion and suspense, setting a compelling tone that hooks you from the start. Its narrative structure, focusing on individual characters through flashbacks, offers a fascinating psychological depth, revealing complex backstories like Charlie’s struggle with addiction or Boone’s evolving protectiveness toward Shannon. These arcs provide the emotional resonance and character development you value, though be warned: episodes heavy on flashbacks can sometimes slow the main plot and feel repetitive.

The island itself is a character—mysterious and dangerous, with threats ranging from a monstrous creature to polar bears—adding a thrilling survival dimension. Characters like Locke, the enigmatic hunter who believes in the island’s purpose, and Jack, the natural leader and doctor, anchor the group’s dynamics with contrasting worldviews and leadership styles. Meanwhile, interpersonal tensions, such as Michael and Walt’s strained father-son relationship or Sun and Jin’s cultural and language barriers, enrich the narrative with relatable human struggles.

However, your critical eye will likely notice the show’s unrealistic portrayal of the survivors’ appearance; the cast remains disproportionately attractive and well-groomed despite harsh conditions, which can momentarily break immersion. Also, the series’ penchant for unresolved mysteries and gradual revelations is a double-edged sword—it keeps you theorizing and engaged but may frustrate if you prefer clear resolutions.

Overall, “Lost” is widely regarded as a landmark TV show, praised for its originality and universal themes of hope and adversity. Watching it sequentially is essential to fully appreciate the intricate character development and plot twists. If you enjoy dissecting complex narratives with emotionally rich characters set against a suspenseful survival backdrop, “Lost” offers a rewarding, if occasionally imperfect, viewing experience.

Or are you a cynic who thinks that anybody claiming to have such a gift is nothing more than a charlatan, a con-artist, out to exploit the more vulnerable members of society? We each have our own opinions on the subject, of course, but how would you feel if a small plastic gadget that you can hold in the palm of your hand were to claim to be able to read your thoughts? You d laugh, naturally. There s just one snag - it happens to be true, the gadget in question being an innocuous looking little toy called 20Q.No, we didn t believe it either, and when my son suggested we try out his new toy after Christmas lunch, we agreed, if only to kill ten minutes or so before tackling the mountain of washing-up. (The toy that is, not my son.)20Q is manufactured by Radica Games Ltd, and it s a lightweight, plastic-covered device, about the size of a tennis ball, except that it s a bit flatter. It then goes on to ask nineteen further questions, through which you navigate, using any one of the four buttons I mentioned earlier. Some of the questions are quite specific, such as  can it be found in an office? , while others are more vague.  Is it bigger than a microwave oven?  or  is it heavier than a pound of butter?  are valid enough questions, narrowing the possibilities down to a mere several million, but when you have only twenty chances to get it right, are the answers to those questions really going to help? The point is, there s no sense of achievement in beating it by means of cheating, and believe it or not, you ll actually find yourself wanting it to get the answer right, and to be able to marvel at the sheer genius of this little gadget.It ll also drive you to the brink of insanity, as it did us. The darned thing still managed to come up with the correct answers and it finally dawned on us just how daft we must seem, grown adults believing this toy was conspiring against us The point is, this wonderful little piece of technology gave us, and continues to provide the whole family with hours of entertainment.
