Favourite toy or not, our Singing Alfie now resides in the bottom of the toybox, and the only interaction he gets now is a hearty kick when another toy sets him off. Maybe Alfie belongs in a family with a higher level of resilience to noise, but for us, his plus points were sadly overshadowed by thirteen little words sung to the tune of twinkle twinkle little star Little Singing Alfie retails at around    8.99 in most good toy shops and takes three AA batteries (these should be optional in my opinion  )     ', '    My friend had a new baby last year so she saw this and thought it looked good.This play gym is suitable to use from birth upwards, it has loads of activities, different types of  materials,velvety to the touch ,it has rattles and it also has a Tigger that hangs with his tail down to where you put your baby in the centre of a hollow material covered ring so that when your baby reaches Tigger his tummy squeakes.There is a bright yellow beehive that has a mirror on it so baby can see his reflection.There are also crinkley leaves and loads of bright colours. This gym comes in four parts.1.Play mat2.Material covered inflatable ring.3. Frame  that has Tigger and Beehive activity toys. 4.Musical chimeAll of the above can be used seperatley in there own way you do not have to use them all together and they are machine washable which is a really good feature because new born babies are sick a lot so you can just throw it in the washing machine. I think this is a little pricey its    39.99 ,but very versatile,bright and colourful.Very useful item to have.       ', '    I used this play gym form when my baby was about 4 month until he was about 8 months. which is a very short period of time concidering it cost    40. The advantages includ that it is stimulating for the baby to look aty and it also improves eye to han co-ordination and play skills. i also liked that fact that when my little boy was just about learning to sit up on his own he didnt like to be led on his back and using this play gym i could sit him up nd the high sides would support his back. most play gyms have much lower sides. i do think that the gym goes well if you have decorated you nursery with traditional colours as it is mainly pastel colours.The disadvantages are again it is not very good value for money just due to the fact that your baby will only be using it or around 5 months. also there is not enough tunes and sound and the colours are not really bright and varied. i would advise a new mum or dad to purchase a cheaper play mat or gym with more colours and stimulation nd attachments. although not to spare on the safty. this gym mat is very safe compared to others that we looked at. also this is not particularly easy to store.     ', '    I recently gave this product to my neice as she has a hard time settleing down at night on her own. She loves Winnie the Pooh, therefore I had to buy it.   The design is so attractive to young children, The design is a soft bodied Winnie the Pooh who is laying down with his head on a pillow and his sweet little friend piglet is lying next to him cuddleing a bee. To get Winnie to sing a lullaby named Lullabee, you have to press the blue cloud on his pillow, or, you can press a button on the remote control that comes with the toy. The remote control is so easy to operate and is very useful.After Winnie the Pooh sings Lullabee, the music changes to play a variety of classical music, and also plays some nature sounds. I find the nightlight in the pillow very useful as my neice doesn t like her room to be too dark. And you don t have to worry about turning the light off on the pillow as it gradually reduces as the music gets quiter and calmer.Winnie the Pooh Sing Me To Sleep Lullaby Soother requires 3 AA  batteries in the toy itself and also requires 3 AA in the remote control. At just    19.99 this toy is great value for money and is available from Argos, Woolworths and most other nursery toy shops.     ', '    Wow, wet and wobblies toy.I was playing in our nursery class today with toys from the interactive toy box. I found the wet and wobblies . These toys are a set of 4 Jellyfish they are a motorized bath toy set. They are made by WOW toys. There is daddy jelly fish, a blue jellyfish that has a cheerful face. Daddy jellyfish is a scoop that has 3 holes, so be careful the water does not come out. Little sister jelly fish is yellow and red. She has a green head, the green head is a plunger push it and she will squirt water. Mummy jelly fish yellow with a smiling face has baby attached to her by a string. Pull out the baby jelly fish and he wobbles and shakes back to his mummy. I played mostly with mummy and baby jelly fish as we did not have water play. The child I was with enjoyed watching the jelly fish move and pulled the baby jelly fish away from mummy to watch him wobbling back. This toy is good for motor skills and cause and reaction. After a few times the child I was with would anticipate that baby jelly fish would return to mummy.This makes a good bath or water tray toy. A good size for tot to play with. Attractive colours too.  These toys were available on line but recently Wow toys have stopped on line trading. You can however buy this in many toy shops see http://www.wowtoys.com/Web/Pages/WOW-Stockists.jsp for a list. This wet and wobbly set of toys costs    9.99 which I think a reasonable price. Have fun playing with your children and their toys. Mary     ', '    for me bickiepegs teething biscuits really are a great thing, my son is 7mths and has been using them for quite a while. he has no teeth at the moment but we will get there soon i hope there is still the conflict of the sleepless nights which nothing can cure yet. UNFORTUNATELY lol so what are they? well they are 9 little biscuits which are made from wheat flour, wheat germ and water. they are made into a long stick shape which a little hole in the top which is for the lace that you get which can be put onto your childs wrist. they are quite safe but with all things you shouldn t leave you child alone with them incase they choke.where are they from? you can buy them from pretty much all places {i.e. chemists to supermarkets} they price from around    1.30 there are 9 in the box with 2 white laces , you do get a little leaflet to tell you the ins and outs of the products and other products by bickiepegs.recommended?absolutely, they are better than the boring old teething rings and other bits you can get as these have a nice taste, just like normal biscuits and cost next to nothing to by. these was recommended to me by my mum health visitor and quite a few friends too that have had little ones too. sorry if review isn t up to scratch its been a while lol i ll get back into it soon. let me know if i ve missed anyting or if you have any advice on making it better please do leave me a message in my guestbook. lou xx     ', '     I anticipate that you will all know about Bob the builder a children   s TV and book series character. There are many toys of the characters in this. One is  Skip,  a friction toy from Born to play. Skip is a lime green vehicle with a yellow skip attached to the back. The toy measures Height: 11cm Length: 17cm .  Skip is suitable for a 3 year old and over to play with and will be popular amongst Bob the builder fans up to 6 or 7 years old . You should be able to buy this toy for about    6. Amazon is selling it for    5.89. http://www.duncanstoychest.co.uk is selling for    7.99. The front of the vehicle like other friction bob the builder toys has googly eyes which jiggle when Skip is zooming along the floor. Skip has a friction engine which will when reved up make Skip zoom across the floor quite fast. Skip will work on the carpet but moves faster on a hard floor . The attached skip will swing down and is detachable press the sides together and the skip will be released. This toy is really quite robust. Easy to play with. Your Childs imagination will come into play the scenarios are endless. Have some toy bricks or some dried pasta shapes some sand or soil and your child can fill the skip up and move it around. The children I know love this toy and play happily with it and the other Bob the builder friction toys. This toy has been around for several years so you might be able to pick it up second hand, as I said its quite robust so a second hand model should be in fair condition . Go on have fun playing with this toy. Mary     ', '    Little Children are fascinated by washing machines. I have known many babies pacified by watching the washing go round and round. However this washing machine is not for really washing it is a toy, no need to panic when your little ones touch the buttons on it.You can buy this toy washing machine for your Childs house play from the E L C it costs    12.50. Your two year old should be happy playing with this. My grandson had a similar one when he was two. . I have seen this  toy washing machines in house corners in an educational /play setting. A child up to eight year old will probably still enjoy playing with it  This washing machine is a blue plastic .It has a clear circular door that is trimmed with red. The buttons on the front for switching it on, changing programmers are red too. There is a little soap dispenser draw that you can open too. This machine  measures  H27cm x W24.5cm x D17cm Your child can put their dolls clothes into the washing machine drum close the door, push the red button and the drum will turn and make realistic noises. This washing machine needs 3 c batteries to make it work. This toy is good as it promotes imaginative play. If this is in the house corner at nursery it will help promote good social play, learning how to share. The use of the buttons will help practice fine motor skills success will be rewarded by the sounds of water.Yes this is a good toy there are other similar washing machines by other manufactures. This one is fairly durable, needs to be it gets dropped often. Enjoy playing with your child and their toys.     ', '    I was playing Duplo trains the other day and we constructed the red Duplo Bridge. Although recommended for a 2 year old a 2 year old will need some assistance building it.  Duplo suggest this is suitable for a child up to 5 I think they are right. Probably a 6 or even 7 year old might play with this bridge and the train set. There are 26 pieces in the box for the bridge The Bridge when constructed measures 42 inches long 10 inches tall.There are brick supports for the bridge to raise it above other tracks, a road or a pretend river. There is track for the approach slopes to the bridge. And red rail guards so that your duplo train does not fall of the bridge. Everything you need to construct a sturdy bridge is here. All you need is some Duplo trains none are included in the set.I am not sure if this bridge is still available as I can not find it in an on line shop. I think it will retail for about    15.This bridge makes a good addition to that duplo train set, compatible with the Thomas set or the standard set of duplo .   I really like Lego Duplo let is a hardwearing conjoining brick. The bricks are fairly easy to put together the colours bright and attractive. Educationally Duplo bricks are good. They encourage fine motor skills and imaginary play. Can be used for colour recognition and basic maths counting. Good for language development too.  Remember to play with your child some of the time as they will benefit from this, use the names for colour count the bricks use words like high and low.So would I recommend this Duplo Bridge? Yes     ', '    Little Tikes make lots of good plastic toys. This pink playhouse is one of many playhouses that they make. I supervise play in this outdoor house most days at the moment. This house is suitable for 2 to 7 year olds.  The house is a really good solid plastic. Although it is this house can be moved  by adults children can not knock it over . 2 adults can move this house to change the position in the garden.This playhouse can be cleaned with hot soapy water.  This house is a pretty pink with a blue grey roof.This house measuring 127cm L   x   104cm W   x   131cm H is a fair size for 2or 3 children .I have known 5 children get inside it  .  The white door is big enough that an adult can get inside with a bit of a squeeze.  There are 4 windows these have white shutters on which the children can open and close. A child can just about climb squeeze out of a window. Inside the house there is some plastic equipment fixed to the back wall a sink with swivel faucet, stovetop with clicking knobs and push-button play phone.  Children enjoy having their own house a place to hide a place to play. I think this is a good house shame its pink for me really but there are others identical apart from the colour. You can buy this toy from http://www.littletikes.co.uk it costs    279 . due to its longevity I think this price is ok . You would possibly pick up a second hand one somewhere in good condition. Have fun playing with your children they would love a playhouse      ', '    Jungle puzzles from Orchard toys. In this green box there are 6 jungle themed puzzles. The six 2 piece puzzles in this box   are a Zebra, a monkey, a crocodile, a Rhinoceros a monkey and an elephant.Each puzzle about 14 cm x14 cm . There are only 2 pieces to each puzzle this makes them suitable for a baby aged over 18 months old. These puzzle animals are bright, cheerful friendly looking. They are made out of a durable recycled board with a wipe clean finish.The puzzles are not straight sided, they are slightly shaped. Each animal puzzle is cut in approximately half one side has a female joining part one the male part, these fit into each other fairly easily. I have worked with children who enjoy these puzzles. They help develop hand eye coordination.. These puzzles will help your child gain knowledge and understanding of the world by seeing the different animals identifying their legs , heads eyes , mouths ears. They will help their speech and language , learning the names of the animals, You can say the sounds the animal makes your child will enjoy watching /listening to you imitate a monkey or using your arm as an elephants trunk , maybe snapping your hands like a crocodiles mouth. Puzzles are good for helping your child develop their concentration skills. These 2 piece jungle animal puzzles are good they are an ideal first puzzle. Orchard toys make good quality hard wearing toys. This box of puzzles are available from http:www.amazon for    4.89 the RRP    6.00      ', '    Lets go shopping no not at Tesco s today but lets play Orchards shopping trolley.This game is a matching memory game.Each of you has a card shaped like a shopping trolleythe trolly is divided into8 squares, each of you is given a shopping list of eight items There are 32 cards about 2cm sq  with the  pictures of items of shopping printed in small case on them . The name of the item is also printed on the card The cards are a firm stiff card covered in a gloss so it is easy to wipe clean. This game can be played as a simple matching game with all the cards turned upright and everyone just collect those to match the items on the shopping list.If I am playing with a group of children I will hold up the card to show them and ask who has the.. Orange (an exampleThe winner is obviosly the person who fills their shopping basket with the things from their shopping list first.I need not show the children the pictuire on the card , just tell them the name of the shopping item. It could be played with all the shopping item cards in the centre and one turned over at a time and the child matching it to their shopping list .I find this game good for encoraging matching skills . As it has the names of the items as well as the pictures it helps with word recognition and reading skills.There is also a version of this game with the items in French, so good for an early french lesson. The children I work with enjoy playing this game. I think a child of 3 would like playing this on an easy level as a matching game.     ', '    This is a small set from playmobil that goes with the new (2008) Playmobil Circus range, and it would go well with the circus tent (set 4230) or as a stand alone item.The clown is a detailed little figure for which we paid    3.95 at John Lewis.  He has moveable limbs and hands like all playmobil figures and his little blue hat, complete with an umbrella is removable as are his fantastic clown shoes.  In the small box you get the clown and the flower.The real fun from this set comes from the flower he is holding - it has a little plastic reservoir hidden at the back which can be filled by water quite easily (my 5 year old can manage it).  When you squeeze the back of the flower water comes out.  As you can imagine this is great fun Playmobil have designed this well as it does appeal to children, but you can t put so much water in it that you cause too much damage.  My two daughters both love this little clown and I think Playmobil have struck the right note of producing an item which is simple but great fun.  I have found that the playmobil people are great for encouraging imaginative play - this little clown has been on all kinds of adventures - they stand up to play well and are well constructed.Like all playmobil items if you lose any of the little bits you can contact playmobil and they are replaceable.The rest of the playmobil circus sets are great too - I particularly recommend set 4231 - the clown band with real sound effects, which would go very well with this little set.This clown is bound to bring lots of fun and laughter into your house - recommended.      ', '    Playmobil make many small plastic toys. These toys are good for creating play scenes. There are many people figures of all walks of life also many Animals. The playmobil toy I am talking about today is the panda family.Playmobil have been making toys for over 25 years. Their toys are all a good quality sturdy and will last a many play hours. They are suitable either for a child care centre /nursery/school or for home. There is a playmobil zoo and many other animal sets the panda family would make a great stand alone toy or an addition to another playmobil toy. The playmobil family set consists of a grass green base this measures approx 5 inches by 3 inches. There are a few plastic tufts of green grass that stand on this base. Also there are two bamboo trees and a bush the tallest is about 9 inches high. This set has 3 panda s a daddy panda a mummy panda and a baby panda. The adult pandas a good size to fit in a Childs hand and for them to manipulate. The baby Panda maybe a bit small and if I had a young child who puts everything in their mouths I might remove this from the play scene unless I was watching all the time.   Your child can place panda in the trees and create an imaginary world. The pandas have friendly features and look loveable.  These Pandas would make an ideal present to a child aged between 3 and 8  . They would make a good addition to the playmobile zoo . This toy costs somewhere between    9 and    10 .    8.99p at http://www.edirectory.co.uk/pf/880/default/d/playmobil/mt/c/rid/13451/pn/H    10.02p at http://www.worldwideshoppingmall.co.uk/toys/playmobil-panda-family.asp. Yes I would recommend this toy to a child . Thanks for reading Mary     ', '    Play Mobil 4496 tractor and hay trailer.Come play on the farm with me, ok it s only a farm play scene I have set up its harvest time isn t it. Play Mobil make a great red tractor and green hay trailer. There are 4 bales of plastic hay to load into the trailer .There is a farm worker with a red safety hard hat, he can drive the trailer or use the plastic pitchfork provided. One side or the green trailer can be flipped down so he can load/unload the hay bales easily. There is a scoop at the front of the tractor which can be raised and lowered.Play mobile toys are a good size the farmer 2.4 inches tall fits a Childs hand perfectly. The tractor, I did not measure it but it s a chunky tractor easy to push.Plenty of play value with this toy. Practicing those motor skills, developing imagination, learning a little about harvesting (who knows maybe your child will go on to be a farmer) This toy is a good toy. Playmobil make strong toys will last many play hours. This can be used in conjunction with other play Mobil toys.  Easy to wash just use hot soapy water. This toys RRP is    21.95 but available for    18.95 at http://www.kerrisontoys.co.uk/playmobil-tractor-with-trailer-4496-p-1841.ht ml . I note Amazon selling for    19 .95 a lot of other on line shops have it for about    19.00. This tractor is recommended age for a four year old to play with. . I would certainly recommend this toy for your child. .     ', '    At my school we have not only the learning resources shopping basket full of lunch foods, but the shopping basket full of breakfast food too. I guess they were both bought together. This set of breakfast foods comes in a blue plastic basket a bit like a supermarket basket.  This measures 10.75L x 5.25W.  In this basket includes 2 fried eggs, 2 bacon slices, a muffin, pancake, and a bowl of strawberries, a glass of orange juice, and 13 pieces in total. These of course are made of a soft unbreakable non toxic vinyl plastic.This set is rather good the food quite realistic looking and realistically sized too. This set is very strong will last many play hours.  It will most probably get tasted and chewed by your youngsters but apart from the odd tooth mark it is as I said very strong. When it gets dirty just wash in warm soapy water.An excellent toy for imaginary play. Your children can pretend to buy the food at the shop using the basket, or they can pretend to be having breakfast at home or in a caf   . This toy is good for your child s social skills sharing playing with others. It could also be used as a prop for early math s counting, sharing. Also for language development, use the names of the foods.  You can use this as a prop to talk about healthy eating. You could add some of those miniature boxes of cereal to it empty just stuff them with paper they are quite sturdy.This toy costs    13.99p from http://www.kbtoys.comWould I recommend this toy? Yes children love to play tea parties.  The same price from https://www.rapidonline.com                                                                                                                          16.50 from http://www.learningresources.co.uk/ Would I recommend this toy ? Well yes but its expensive     ', '    Introduction==========Settlers of Catan is an excellent strategy board game which is simple enough to appeal to a wide variety of people while still being strategically compulsive. Created in 1995, Settlers is the first (and only) German board game to have worldwide success. Settlers appeals to people who would not usually want to play a longer strategy game and has a real pick up and play quality.Box Contents===========Lots of bits in here, included in the box are a large number of hexagonal tiles, two packs of cards (one development, one resources), four sets of wooden playing pieces (roads, cities, settlements), two dice and a pretty well designed rule book. The tiles are all in perforated sheets and need to be popped out, this will take about ten minutes the first time you play.The Objective===========Like most good games, the objective is simple. Players use resources to build towns and cities, a town is worth one victory point and a city two. Once a player has ten victory points then the game is over. Victory points can also be gained by having the longest road, the largest army, or from certain development cards.The Setup=========The gameboard is different every time, the hexagonal tiles are shuffled and then laid out in concentric rings. 1 in the centre 6 surrounding it and 12 in the third ring. Each of the tiles is of one of five types, Forest (which makes wood), Pasture (which makes sheep), Quarry (which makes brick), Field (which makes grain) and Mountain (which makes ore) There is also one desert tile. The board is then surrounded by water tiles some of which are ports. Once this is done a counter is put on each tile with a number on it, these numbers          Pictures of Settlers of Catan     ', '    Are you scared of mice, will you scream and stand on a chair? Don   t worry this is only a little clockwork mouse. You can buy this clockwork mouse in either white or grey. It   s only little about 5cm long. The mouse has a little wind up key on his side, wind this up and his plastic form will scurry about your house.  He scurries about in horizontal and semi vertical delectations.  The mouse has a little tail and beady black eyes and a black dot for his nose When wound up this mouse will dash across the floor or along a table best not on a deep pile carpet.  This clockwork mouse its quite fun, it   s a pocket money toy costs RRP    1.75 but I have seen this mouse for less. These mice are available from shops which sell small pocket money toys our local chemist has some. You might find these in a museum shop too This mouse is suitable for children aged over 3. A 3 year old a bit young I think they need some fine finger control to wind then up. These mice would be fun as stocking filler or similar.This clockwork mouse its quite fun, it   s a pocket money toy costs RRP    1.75 but I have seen this mouse for less. These mice are available from shops which sell small pocket money toys our local chemist has some. You might find these in a museum shop too Tobar is abased in Suffolk it sources pocket money toys, gifts and gadgets, clockwork toys. They sell them to trade customers in trays for display. I have seem these in several shops     ', '    I bought this cot toy as I wanted something which my baby would find familiar and soothing at bedtime.  What I did get with this was an annoying tune which thankfully only lasted five minutes and had no volume control.  The images it projects look nothing like the picture shows in the argos catalogue.  The beauty of this device however, is that it is noise activated so if your baby is still not asleep within five minutes (not many babies are) and he/she starts crying because the music has stopped, then it will start up again.My baby found this far from soothing, mainly I think because it was at one volume level which was quite loud - not what you want when you re trying to drop off to sleep This toy looks attractive, it is made of a hard plastic casing which has a picture of winnie the pooh in a moonlit scene with Piglet and Tigger and projects images of butterflies, bees and stars mainly (which can also be seen lit up on the actual toy).  It costs around    18.99 and can be purchased from most places.  It takes 4 AA batteries and fits very securely to the cot.  If, like my baby, yours is first in a moses basket, it can be free-standing on a flat surface to achieve the same projected images on the ceiling.I personally took this toy back and exchanged it for the Fisher Price Ocean Wonders Aquariam which I am very pleased with and will review at a later date.     ', '    I Bought this toy,with great trepidation for my 5yr old last xmas,from woolworths for around    15.00. I wasn,t sure he would actually play with it at home,as he always went straight to it everytime we entered the shop, and you know what children are like it s more fun playing with it in the shop .Well  he just loves it  You use the joystick to fly around the globe whilst it makes an engine noise, you can then stop it at a certain destination,push the big blue button and it will tell you where you have landed. it has three levels to try,for either the animals, the continents or the oceans and seas,it also gets you to fly and find places and land that it has chosen .The bright blue colours and wonderful big buttons along with flying pilot make this educational toy fun,and the wee ones won`t even know that they are learning anything II`ts amazing he know knows the animals,seas ,oceans and continents better than i do know  I would definitely recomend this to anyone who is thinking of buying this,or who has never seen it before to go check it out,you wont be disappointed .Thank you VTech youve come up trumps with the goods again.Good luck to all you budding pilots out there.Check out ciao`s toy department for further details.And most the most important thing of all, Don t forget it needs 4AA sized batteries to make it work.The battery compartment is on the underside of the dome shaped grey stand.This toy is very durable and can withstand hard knocks and bangs. As Cameron so nicely pointed out to me.I do belive that it will bring years of entertainment, to your child and because of its durability, could well be handed down to generations to come.     ']

- **Playful and Fun-Loving:** Enjoys playful interactions and values humor, as seen in their reviews that often include light-hearted commentary.
- **Detail-Oriented:** Provides thorough descriptions and analyses of products, indicating a meticulous approach to reviewing and sharing experiences.

**Core Interests:**
- **Child Development:** Focuses on toys and games that promote learning, creativity, and physical development in children.
- **Family Activities:** Values products that can be enjoyed by the whole family, particularly those that encourage bonding and interaction.
- **Educational Toys:** Shows a preference for toys that have educational value, helping children learn through play.

**Expression Habits/Style:**
- **Descriptive and Engaging:** Uses vivid descriptions and personal anecdotes to convey experiences with products, making reviews relatable and engaging.

- **Humorous Touch:** Incorporates humor and light-heartedness into reviews, making them enjoyable to read.

- **Educational Value:** Considers the learning opportunities a product provides, particularly in developing skills like fine motor control and cognitive abilities.
- **Durability and Safety:** Emphasizes the importance of safety and durability in toys, especially those intended for young children.

**Shopping Behavior:**
- **Value-Conscious:** Looks for good deals and value for money, often comparing prices and seeking out sales or discounts.
- **Brand Awareness:** Shows a preference for reputable brands known for quality and safety, such as Lego and LeapFrog.
- **Research-Oriented:** Engages in thorough research before making purchases, often reading reviews and seeking recommendations.

**Aspects of Products Interested In:**
- **Interactive Features:** Prefers toys that offer interactive elements, such as sounds, lights, and movement, which enhance play experiences.
- **Versatility:** Values products that can be used in multiple ways or that grow with the child, providing long-term engagement.
- **Aesthetic Appeal:** Appreciates colorful and visually appealing designs that attract children’s attention and stimulate their imagination.

### Summary
The user is a thoughtful and engaged parent who values educational and interactive toys that promote child development. They express their experiences in a detailed, humorous, and relatable manner, focusing on functionality, safety, and value for money. Their shopping behavior reflects a careful consideration of product quality and brand reputation, making them a discerning consumer in the realm of children's products.

That said, if you’re after versatility and a richer experience, the online version of 20Q tends to be more dynamic and engaging than the handheld device. It offers more variety in gameplay, which might appeal to kids who quickly master the physical toy. Still, for under £10, the handheld 20Q offers excellent value, combining educational fun with affordability—a rare find in today’s market.

In summary, 20Q is a smart, interactive toy that balances simplicity with clever design, making it a solid choice for families who want a playful, educational game that’s easy to use and brings everyone together. ', '    Sorry guys I know this is a game that EVERYONE knows about and most people have played but I eventually bought it for my daughter today and had to do a bit of a review on it...For anyone out there that has been in hibernation for the last couple of decades, this is what Twister is all about.  The game that ties you up in knots  Basically as it says on the box, the last one standing wins     This game consists of a plastic mat with 6 of each of 4 different coloured large dots and a spinner.  You have to spread the mat out on the floor and get spinning   The spinner has different options on it for where you put your limbs on the plastic mat ie.  left hand, right hand, left foot and right foot and the seperate colours.  It depends on the different options that the spinner throws at you as to how difficult a position you end up in   The idea is to get between 2-4 players on the mat (although can be fun but difficult with more ) and try to stay upright the longest.  You have one person spinning the spinner and shouting out the moves (the ref), or if there are only two players you can shout out moves without using the spinner, to the other player.  The game should normally last around 10 minutes.  The rules are:  Only one hand or foot per circle   The first player there occupies the circle.    Once you ve made your move, you cant move again unless the ref gives permission to move a limb to let another player through.  If all six circles of one colour are taken, spin again  If the ref calls a hand/foot colour combination you re already doing, you must move your hand or foot to a different circle of the same colour (if all six are taken, spin again)  If a knee or an elbow lands on the mat, or you fall over (as I have done many times ) you re out.There are many ways of playing apart from the basic game.  They are as follows:Twisting TurnsI think this is the basic game where the ref shouts out the moves and players take it in turns to make the moves on the mat. As soon as one player falls over or touches the mat with a knee or elbow, the other team has won.Twister TournamentEach team plays every other team in the league.  Keep score of victories and defeats to see which team will triumph Twister knockoutPlay Twister the knockout challenge way.  The winning team stays on the mat and takes on new contenders until all the teams have played.  The last team standing wins.I think that this game is absolutely fantastic. It is a great party entertainment and it can be played by children or adults. (As long as they are not suffering from a bad back) The idea of the game couldn t be easier. One player is the referee and spins the spinner. It lands on a colour and a body part, which means that the player has to put that body part on that coloured circle. Simple as that  The idea is to twist and turn until one player falls to the ground or puts a body part like their knee or bum on the mat. That player is out  The game requires quite a lot of strength but mainly depends on how scrambled up you get This is a very fun game especially for parties with your friends because you can have a real laugh, and it only takes a second to set up. I think it is worth the money because it is quite cheap and you can have loads of fun and you won t get bored of it. The game is for 2 or more players and it is for children 6 years or above. Another great game from MB       ', '    Take a few 10 to 12 year olds, 1 plastic sheet and a spinner on a board and you have the recipe for a fun filled evening. Well at least a fun filled half hour. Add a few more games and the whole evening may be fun. The game of twister is an oldie but goodie. I say this as someone who doesn t actually play but watches. I used to play this as a youngster but I think I have grown to old. The aim of the game is to get into as tangled a mess as possible. Each player takes it in turn to put either a hand or a foot onto a coloured circle. The part of the body placed and the colour to place it on depends on the spinner. You are not allowed to share colours, this might involve some streaching. What is more you have to keep yourself up on all fours no falling over (easier said than done). It does not take long for bodies to be tangled and giggles to take over. Before long everyone is in a tangled heap on the floor. I have watched some youngsters playing this game who never smile in absolute hysterics. Not all of them want to play, you can t blame them as it is a contact sport and youth can be very funny about their bodies. This is not a sophisticated game. This will not appeal to every one, though with a drink inside you it becomes more acceptable. It would be no good for any one who is not able to bend in all directions, but for the age range I mentioned it is a great game. If you are a bit more sedate then there is a table top edition which just involves using hands on the table, there are after dinner mints also involved. The original Twister is widely available in toy shops, ours came from Argos and it costs    9.99 The table top version tends to be a christmas option available in Woolworths at Christmas I think it cost about    4.     ', '     This has got to be the best game I have ever played. I would say the more you have playing it the better .  You have a large mat with about ten circles in it with around five colours. With it comes a board with what looks like a clock. You spin it and it lands on a colour. With that the board tells you if you put a hand or a foot down. Before you know it, your in such a twist with loads of other people s arms and legs over you or under you end up falling over .  The first person to fall is out. I would tell anyone to buy this whatever age you are. if you are older, get afew drinks down you then play it .  You can buy this game from places like Woolworths for around 10.00.  Happy playing, I hope you have ago .     ', '    Who would think that such a simple game would bring so much entertainment    You are provide with a square mat with a row of red, yellow, green and blue dots.  For your ten quid you also get a piece of cardboard sectioned into parts such as right hand red or left foot blue, with a spinner attached.Sounds like a quality game doesn  8217;t it  So here  8217;s what to do.Someone is nominated   8220;spinner  8221; and gets control of the quality piece of cardboard and spins the spinner.  Player one then has to follow the directions, if right hand red is spun they must put their right hand on a red dot.  Easy to begin with because you have a wide choice of dots.  The second player then waits for their spin to be red out and again, follows the directions.A simple game to learn but not simple to play   Once you  8217;ve had a few spins you are all completely tangled up and eventually everyone will fall down in a big heap with legs and arms sticking out everywhere.  Hilarious and painful   More hilarious for the people watching though.This is definitely a party game.  The more people there the better, everyone doesn  8217;t necessary have to be playing, just there putting off the people balancing on one foot and leaning against someone elses bum. To make the game a great deal more interesting I suggest getting completely drunk first (assuming that you are old enough to).  The game then usually lasts one round but turns out to be a lot funnier.This is probably not a good game to play if you have a phobia of feet because you will probably end up with someones big toe in your ear.  If you insist that everyone wears their socks you slip around on the mat, this could be classed as a good thing or a bad thing, depends if you are the one in play or the one watching.  Playing on a wooden floor is never a good idea, the mat may not slip around as much as it does on carpet but it does hurt a lot more when you all fall over.  One way around this is to make sure you are on the top though   Another time to definitely make sure you are on the top is if you have your fifteen stone friend playing as well.  Ow.So you can see that this game brings much entertainment, for ten quid you can  8217;t go wrong.       ', '    This is the ideal game for a party. It s really good fun, easy to play and causes great hilarity  The rules are easy enough to learn- simply stand on a plastic sheet with coloured circles printed on it, withyour feet on 2 colours. Then spin a dial to see if you have to move your left or right hand or foot to one of the colours. The first one collapsed in a heap on the floor is declared as the looser and has to spin the dial in the next round as punishment At every party this game is brought out as it s a really good conversation maker and you can t help but laugh at all the scrapes people manage to get into. People dive over other people and, well,  twist  around about 1cm off the ground before toppling over, taking all teh rest of the people with them It s suitable for people age about 8+ and can be played with from 3 to about 8 people. I find the more people, the more funny it is, but it is still enjoyable with 3 people. Also try and play with people about your age- it s too easy if you re challanging a 5 year old.My hints for playing are: If you get the chance then rest your weight on someones leg as it makes them collapse easily. Never go underneath someone as they re likely to sit on you  always make sure the person with the dial isn t cheating- and if you re on the dial then deliberately set people up- it makes it more interesting Overall I say if you don t have it then most definately go out and buy this game as it s pretty inexpensive, last ages, can be played with lots of people and is really good fun for all ages      ', '    Twister a suitable family game that most children play, but thats not always the case. Many a time have me and my friends come back from a night on the town, drunk as skunks and played twister.The aim of the game is to spin and place the item of the body its says on the colour it says. Its a lot of fun but you get twisted and tucked into many different position next to other people, which many oversexed people enjoy.The game is good fun if you are in sound mind and body and able to twist. The game last until there is one person left who has nt fell down. This game gives you a good excuse to get close to somebody you fancy and get in there.If children are reading this just ignore what i said above and you play a nice game of twister with the coloured circles.Parents I would by your kids this game, and then you can take it off them at night.     ', '    If you bring one game out at a party, it has got to be twister. Great fun for all ages, so can be played at all parties, occasions or general gatherings.It can be played with 2-4 people. Twister is pretty cheap to buy at around 12.99 (pounds).It consists of a  large plastic mat, and a cardboard spinner. The game is quite hard to explain in words but in practice is extremley easy and picked up very fast. The game is a very hands on and active game which will cause many laugh with young and old alike. My one tip for you when playing is- GET FLEXIBLE. If you don t have twister i would suggest buying it for christams and living up your parties       ', '    I know Twister is really classed as a childrens game but I find that adults have much more fun. For children it s fun and helps with their co-ordination though it s best if the age groups aren t mixed as the little ones get crushed. The main thing it teaches children is left and right, left hand on yellow, right leg on red. For adults though it s pure fun, especially at a party when the drinks have been flowing  All concept of left and right go out of the window and the main aim is to remain on your feet  The game never really seems to get played properly as it normally ends in a fit of giggles or a twisted ankle. Buy it for your kids then have a go yourself.     ', '    Naked people should not play twister in glasshouses, believe me.  Twister is a highly entertaining game, which really should not be classed as a children s game   Twister involves spinning a pointer on a piece of card with coloured segments.  You take note of which coloured segment the pointer points to and then have to do what it says   It is played on a massive slippery, plastic sheet with coloured circles on a white background.  The pointer tells you to put, for example, your right foot on a red circle etc.  It is a game for 2 to as many people as you can fit on the sheet   The more people you have on there the more fun it is  It is a great game which can entertain both sober and drunk people, children and elderly people  It is a wonderful party game, to get everyone to get to know each other  You can learn alot about people by playing it.  There is no way people can not end up laughing when you are on top of one person and beneath another, in a totally bizarre situation  Good game to play with people you fancy It will only cost you    9.99 and is great value for money   It is officially for ages 6 and up, presumably people under 6 haven t got long enough arms and legs      ', '    Twister is wasted on children because they can actually contort themselves enough to put that last  right foot yellow , and you can t laugh at kids falling over coz that s mean.On the other hand - get a bunch of friends around, add a splash of alcohol, take away the inhibitions and you have yourself a party.Speaking from personal experience, when I went downstairs to the neighbouring flat, little did I know what was in store. The alcohol was flowing freely, lots of people were there, and then the host whipped out a twister mat.It all went mad after that.Arm someone with a camera while playing this - you re sure of getting some interesting photos of people with their faces in other people s crotches.If you want to be nasty, put a dollop of cooking oil on the mat and watch as the person that inadvertantly steps on it brings the whole mass of intertangled limbs crashing down.Then there is of course the infamous...the oft-dreamed about...*N*a*k*e*d* Twister...I don t know anyone that s done it or would even be willing to do that....if you have...or if you know of anyone, please leave a comment - how on EARTH did the situation arise? ?      ', '    I can t believe they put this game in the children s section   I suppose you could get a load of kids playing it and they d all have quite a good laugh, but how much more fun is it to play whilst under the influence of our great friend - Alcohol   ???    That s right, have you ever played  Drunken Twister , with lots of alcohol to hand and plenty of friends, both male and female ??  ? If you haven t, then I would definitely recommend it   You have such a laugh it s soooo funny, honestly  I played it at a party where there were loads of us, all very drunk, and I can tell you it is way better then any time that I have played it sober   I had so much fun that evening, although I must say I did decide that I d had enough when it began to turn into  drunken NAKED Twister           ', '    I wouldnt say twister was a childrens game because it could end up trying 2 get 1 leg on one side of the sheet and the other on the other side, which would be very difficult for small children.I think its much better to play with teenagers and adults especially when had a few drinks, you never know what positions you could end up in with the person you fancy  Ciao does say its a childrens game so i should keep this clean. Its great fun for all the family and can be hilariously funny at times when you are spread across the twister mat.The object of the game is to say up right for the longest and when its your turn you spin the spinner and that will determine where you put your hands or feet.     ', '    This game may be painfully when you are trying to stretch your body so you can get to the red circle   However it is a simple game where you spin a board and whatever you land on you have to put your hand or foot on one of the different coloured circles  It is a fun game to play at a party with lots of people but you can however play it as a couple when you are on your own   I will leave it to your imagination  Definitely a game to get and it is such a reasonable price       ', '    Twister is a fantastic game that is the main event of most children s parties...and a few adults. How To PlayTwister is a game for three or more people: two (or more) will be playing the game and one spinning the board. There is a mat, on which the game is played with numerous different colour spots. These are Yellow, Blue, Red and Green. I first played twister when I was very young so it can be fun for all ages. The basic idea of twister is, that you have a plastic mat, at least two people. On that mat there are different coloured circles, you have another person not in the action of the game telling you where to place your feet and hands, this is don  8217;t by spinning a dial on a little board, where the dial lands tells you where to put your hands or feet etc. the game is over when there is only one person left standing, this sounds easy but can be very hard.This is a very fun game and suitable for all ages, it is only around 15 pounds and can be found in most good toyshops around the nation. I would recommend this game to everyone that enjoys a good time.         ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re looking for a family game that’s a guaranteed hit across generations, Twister is a classic worth revisiting. It’s an inexpensive, widely available game that offers excellent value—durable enough to survive countless family gatherings and parties. The setup couldn’t be simpler: a colorful mat dotted with circles and a spinner to call out your next move. This straightforward design makes it easy for kids and adults alike to jump right in without a lengthy rulebook.

What really makes Twister shine is the sheer fun and laughter it sparks. Picture a room full of family members tangled up in a hilarious human knot, giggling uncontrollably as they try to maintain their balance. It’s a fantastic icebreaker that gets everyone interacting, breaking down barriers between kids and adults. The more players you have, the wilder and more chaotic the game becomes—perfect for those who enjoy a bit of friendly competition and physical silliness.

For those nostalgic about childhood games, Twister brings back that carefree spirit while still feeling fresh and lively. It’s especially entertaining at parties, and if you’re playing with a group of adults, a little added cheer (like some drinks) can turn the fun up a notch. However, keep in mind that the game’s physical nature might not suit everyone, especially if you prefer less active or more strategic gameplay.

In summary, Twister is a family-friendly, interactive game that delivers hours of laughter and bonding without breaking the bank. product_reviews: ['    My Furby still can   t speak any English yet, but she has started doing an impression of a telephone:    Bring Bring...Bring Bring...   , belching loudly, and farting after I have fed her. I don   t know whether this is a reflection on me or on the Furby. When I first got her, carefully unscrewed the battery compartment in her plastic base,and installed four long-life AA batteries, she told me her name was Mee Mee -    Me Mee Mee   . Having played with my Furby for a few weeks now, I can see where she got her name from: Furbys do sleep, but when they are awake they almost equal a small child in their constant attention-seeking behaviour. If you don   t pay them any attention or feed them regularly by placing a spoon or finger in the    beak    - never use real food or drink though -they will call out to you in Furbish , such as    kah mee-mee a-tay    - I   m very hungry, or    nee-tye kah    - Tickle me. Although Furbys can be a little needy, their huge long-lashed eyes are hard to resist, and they will encourage you to pet them by saying phrases such as    doo-moh may-lah kah    - Please hug me. Furbish is not too hard to learn, although you will need to keep consulting the English-Furbish phrasebook for a while until you get used to the language. Furbys will spontaneously go to sleep when they are    tired   , perhaps saying    wee-tee kah way-loh    - Sing me to sleep - and will often snore loudly for a few seconds, leaning forwards and closing their eyes. If you want your Furby to go to sleep before you go completely bananas, you can either cover her eyes for a few seconds, or try petting her on the back sensor several times, which will result in her humming twinkle twinkle little star and falling asleep. There is a way of putting the Furby into a deep sleep to shut it down so that she can only be awoken by being turned upside down, which involves a lot of clapping and pressing of sensors. If this seems like too much trouble, you can buy a Furby Sleepy Time Cloud Bed for    6.99, and sit your Furby in it, which will send it into a deep sleep straight away. The Sleepy Time Cloud Bed takes 2 AAA batteries. Mee Mee has long fur the same colour as a silver-backed gorilla, one of the most majestic and beautiful mammals on Earth. Whilst Mee Mee cannot be described as majestic, she is beautiful in her own way with rich deep brown eyes, and she really is very endearing, especially when she says things like    kah may-may u-nye    - I love you. You can play games with your Furby, and teach them to respond to you. One rewarding game is to tickle the Furby   s stomach: if the Furby responds by giving you a kiss, you can reinforce this behaviour by rubbing her back. This works because there are a number of different sensors built into each Furby   s body. There is a pressure sensor in her back, and one where the stomach would be if Furbys had stomachs. Another sensor allows the Furby to    hear    loud noises, such as clapping hands, or music, and the Furby can be sent to sleep by covering the infra-red light sensor just above her eyes. These sensors are what make the Furby capable of interacting with you or other Furbys, and it is the infra-red light sensor that enables Furbys to interact with each other by sending and receiving signals. A microphone in the Furby   s stomach enables her to respond verbally to input from the user. The belch and fart noises are said to be there to widen the appeal of the Furby from girls to boys, and, I am relieved to say, not learned from my own habits. Why did I get a Furby? I read lily7star   s moving opinion on guinea pigs, The Perfect Pets, and decided that although I had wanted a guinea pig or similar small pet for years, it just wasn   t practical to get one with a small person in the house, as they tend to be a little rough with small animals. My mother found this out the hard way when looking after Genevieve the guinea pig at a nursery. Genevieve was one stressed out guinea pig. There was also the problem that to be fair to the guinea pig it would need a companion, and after that fiasco with what I thought were the world   s first gay mice - I had asked for two boys - I was reluctant to take any chances. A Furby seemed like the ideal solution. The only nourishment it will need will be new batteries every once in a while, and if I get bored with it I can always shove it in the back of a cupboard without anyone phoning the RSPCA. FURBY RESOURCES The official web site for Furbys is www.furby.com (an American site), which has online Furby related games, and mainly promotional pages. There is a link on this site to Tiger   s online store (www.tigertoys.com/store.html) where you can buy French, Japanese, Italian or German Furbys, which suggested to me that Furbys do not really learn to speak human languages, but are pre-programmed with all that they will ever say. The four stages of development that the Furby is supposed to go through during its transition from childhood to adulthood are probably just different levels of the Furby   s behaviour patterns that are released or made accessible over a set time, or duration of activity period. International shoppers are welcome, but it is easy to get Furbys in the UK, unless you go in for  rare  or special edition Furbys, which are not so easy to get in Britain. According to an article by (I believe) Denis Susac in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) section of About.com (http://ai.about.com/compute/ai/library/weekly/aa101398.htm) each Furby is pre-programmed with 160 English and Furbish words and sounds. He also states that these existing words and sounds are eventually combined, using positive reinforcement feedback from the Furby   s sensors, into up to 1000 phases, triggered by input from the sensors. This enables the Furby to appear to learn English (or whatever language it is pre-programmed to speak), while in reality it is just pre-programmed to introduce English words alongside the Furbish that it initially speaks. Also on the AI section of About.com is a page of links to other virtual pets, which Furby enthusiasts may find of interest (http://ai.about.com/compute/ai/cs/virtualpets/index.htm). An interesting site to go to if you want to see what a Furby is made of is the Furby Autopsy site http://www.phobe.com/furby/, which has pictures of a Furby skinned to reveal the T-800 Terminator-like skeleton without its outer layer of fur fabric. It bears more than a passing resemblance to Gonzo off the Muppets, but much prettier. A description of the inner workings of the Furby is given on this site, but there is not much information about the Central processing Unit (CPU) and Read Only Memory (ROM) that make the Furby work, mainly because Tiger have protected their intellectual property rights over the workings of the Furby by covering it with glue, so that it cannot be hacked easily. A site that will give you more information on the inner workings of Furbys is Hack Furby, (http://www.homestead.com/hackfurby/). Some of the    easter eggs    or surprise features (from easter egg hunt) hidden in the Furby   s CPU and ROM are detailed here, such as how to make your Furby burp - like I need help to make Mee Mee belch?   I would advise that you do not let children visit the discussion group on the Hack Furby site, as some of the posts contain some offensive language. The paperback Furby Official Trainers Guide (Sandwich Islands Publishing Co., ISBN: 1884364268), by J Douglas Arnold and Mark Elies is available from Amazon.co.uk for    8.27, and usually ships within 1-2 weeks. I tried some other online bookshops, but none of them had this title in their database. WHERE TO BUY YOUR FURBY The best place to buy a Furby is a toyshop where you can examine the Furby before you buy it. Prices seem to be fairly uniform (there was no difference between Index, Argos or the independent Toymaster toy shop where I bought my Furby from. The problem with buying from a shop like Index or Argos is that you usually don   t get to see the Furby before you buy it, in order to select a colour that you like (there are many different colours available), and in the Autumn, the peak toy buying period, these shops tend to be jam packed with shoppers. On the high street the price of a Furby is approximately    20-   25. BUYING FURBIES ON THE HIGH STREET AND ONLINE A Furby is a Interactive toy, suitable for age 6 and upwards. Batteries should cost approximately    3.00 for 4. Furby Babies can talk and play games. Furby Babies speak English and Furbish, and have animated eyes ears and mouths. Furby Babies can interact with other Furby Babies, Furbys, Gizmos and Shelbys. Furby Babies come in avariety of pastel colours. If the Furby Baby is interacting with a Furby, the Furby must initiate the  conversation . Gizmos can talk, play games and learn tricks. Gizmos can interact with other Gizmos, Furby Babies, Furbys, and Shelbys. The Gizmo has animated eyes ears and mouth, and can speak English and Furbish. Gizmos talk in the actual voice of Gizmo from the film  Gremlins . It takes 4 AA batteries, and these are not supplied with the toy. Batteries should cost approximately    3.00 for 4. Shelbys can talk and play games. Shelbys speak English, Shelbish and Furbish, and have animated eyes that move up and down and from side to side. They also have animated mouths and antenna. Shelbys can interact with other Shelbys, Furbys, Furby Babies and Gizmos. The Shelby is a furry creature in a shell, and comes in a variety of colours. Shelbys take 4 AA batteries, and these are not supplied with the toy. Batteries should cost approximately    3.00 for 4. ', '    While many Furbies by now have been sold, broken, been put to sleep, or even chucked in the dustbin never to be seen again, my Furby (Ko-Ko) is right next to me now, talking away, laughing, dancing and burping   I have to admit he has been asleep on my window shelf for the last couple of years  8230;  8230;.but he is happy to be alive again   So why did these little computer run critters become so popular so quickly and then fall off the edge of the earth sooner than you can say next Christmas? Well now I have my Furby out again, seeing him happy, I am really sorry I left him asleep for all that time.  I forgot what a time waster little Ko-Ko can be A WHAT?A Furby can only be described as a mechanical fluffy alien type thing?  My Furby is a lovely mix of all different greys.  Like all Furbies he has a long fluffy white mane along his back and a small fluffy tummy.  He has lovely big brown eyes and a little beak like mouth.  The eyes and mouth move when he talks and when he is asleep he also closes his eyes.  Just above his eyes there is a sensor which can sense what you are doing to the poor lad, such as throwing him up and down or kissing him.  A Furby sits around 20 centimetres high and has a moveable black plastic bottom which is stands on, this moves so the Furby can dance.  One last point, which makes me realise that maybe Furbies originated from birds, is that Furbys have soft feet, similar to a bird  8217;s foot.  WHAT IS THE POINT OF THEM?Many see Furbies as a children  8217;s toy, however Furbies in their peak of popularity were bought by parents  8230;  8230;..for themselves   They were even banned from some offices for making too much noise or remembering and repeating some conversations they had previously heard.  They are more than a simple toy, they learn and develop the more you handle, speak and play with them.  WHAT DO THEY DO?When you first see a Furby you will think awwww they are so cute, so quiet, put the batteries in and you are in for a shock    8220;Me Ko-Ko  8221;   8220;Du Du  8221;   8220;me like  8221; will fill your ears. Your Furby will be speaking furbish, a Furbish to English dictionary is included with your furby so you can try to understand him.  Eventually the more and more you play with him, he will learn English  They learn more and more as you play and love them, so the first thing to do is get acquainted with your new found friend.  Tickle his tummy (which includes a sensor) and stroke the back of his mane (includes another sensor) I find when I stroke his mane I have to touch a certain spot for him to feel it.  When he does he normally makes a very strange sound, but gives the impression of contentment   When you tickle his tummy he usually laughs and giggles.  After you first get acquainted the chances are that you will hear a   8220;waaa  8221; sound coming from your furby.  While this is happening his little mouth will be opening up.  This means food time.  If you look inside the Furby  8217;s little mouth he has a red tongue, and by pressing this he will say   8220;yum yum  8221; meaning he is enjoying his food.  If you want the Furby to sleep you can cover his eyes (sensor) for around10-15 seconds and he will begin to snore and fall asleep.  You can also try stroking his back around 10 times to calm him to sleep, or you can place him in a dark room for around10 seconds and he will fall asleep.  The Furby will not wake up until you lift him and give him a hug.  I have never found my Furby to wake up alone, however he may just be lazy   That is the basic functions of the Furby, to be loved.  However as you read the manual you can begin to see that the Furby does more than you would imagine GAMESTo get your Furby to play you need to follow a sequence of tickles, eye covering etc.To make sure that the Furby will carry out a game, you must wait for the Furby to stop moving before commencing the next sequence.  Example if he is laughing do not expect him to understand if you cover his eyes.  You must wait until he is quiet.  If he doesn  8217;t listen you can rock is slowly for side to side and he will   It is recommended that you wait 3-5 seconds after each command.FURBY SAYSA game very similar to Simon Says.  Your Furby will tell you what activities to dio and you have to carry them out   For example your Furby may say   8220;Tickle, light, sound  8221; and you have to tickle your Furbys tummy, cover his eyes and clap.The game consists of four different patterns.I still haven  8217;t got my Furby to play this yet ASK FURBYThis is a good game, where you can ask your Furby secrets After you follow the sequence your Furby will say   8220;Ooh too mah  8221; which means ask.  When you have asked the question, stroke your Furby  8217;s back and he will state the answer. However if you don  8217;t speak within 20 seconds he will state   8220;I  8217;m done  8221; and the sequence will have to be done again.HIDE AND SEEKThe classic game of hide and seek can be played with your Furby   After the sequence has been done he will state   8220;Hide Me  8221; Your friend goes and hides your Furby and you try and find him. When you find him, turn him upside down and he will state   8220;me done  8221;TRICKSYou can teach your furby to do tricks, however I find this very complicated and have no idea why I cant   The sequence is quite complicated, but I will keep trying.DANCINGYour Furby can learn to dance, all you need to do is clap your hands of play music and the little chappy will dance and laugh I have not included all the different sequences you have to go through to get your Furby to perform a certain way as these are all included in the manual that you are given with your Furby.  So whatever you do DON  8217;T throw the manual away COMMUNICATING WITH OTHER FURBIESYour Furby will not only talk to you he also likes to meet critters like himself.  Unfortunately Ko-Ko has never met another Furby so does not know what his people look like.  Don  8217;t worry as the little chap seems happy enough   When your Furbies first meet, they may not hit if off but keep trying.  Eventually they will be dancing together and talking happily.  Your Furby doesn  8217;t just have to mix with one of his kind at a time, he can chat to as many as you like SETTING UPNow before you all run off to get your Furbies out of the cupboard, let me remind you about a few things that you will need to do to get your Furby back to the land of the living. The box is in a hexagon shape and has pictures of children playing with their Furbies.  The words   8220;Electronic Furby  8221; are all over the packaging. It really will fill in any spare time you have, its fun to have him around again, I wonder how long the fad will last though??A Furby is a highly recommended toy.Remember that Furbies are a toy and mechanical sounds are normal      ', '    Firstly, I should perhaps point out that I haven t lost the plot... although some might say I never had it    Neither have I made a dire spelling mistake in my opinion title. Dah doo-ay is Furbish for big fun. Furbish, for those not familiar with the Furby craze, is the language spoken by Furbies and Furby Babies. (Not to be confused with gibberish, the language spoken by parents suffering Furby overload.) So, what is a Furby? An electronic pet, of sorts. About 4 inches tall, Furby is a furry  blob  with the ability to try the patience of a saint and push the sane right over the edge. The saving grace of this companion from hell? It runs on 4 AA batteries, that fortunately run out of power quite frequently. Now I ve got the harassed parent grumble out of the way, let s start again. Furbies, and the latest addition Furby Babies, are cute interactive toys. They communicate with each other, Gizmo s, and Shelby s. With the aid of the dictionary supplied, your Furby can communicate with you too. They come in a vast array of colours and there have been some  theme  Furbies such as a Christmas one. To bring Furby to life, you need batteries and a screwdriver. Loosen the battery compartment cover, insert 4 AA s, tighten up the screw and Furby is born. Listen carefully and Furby should tell you his name. (I say  his  name because only a male could be this annoying.) So, what will Furby do? Not too much at the outset of his life, but he may want a lot of attention. Keep the dictionary close by as all requests will initially be made in Furbish. A cry of  a-tay  indicates that Furby is hungry. Feed him by putting a finger in his mouth and leave it there until he s done,  toh-dye . Listen to what he says next and try to suffice his needs. As Furby gets older (in terms of length of play rather than ownership) he will do more. He will start to speak English, have the ability to play games when prompted by some simple commands, and will even be able to sing to you. It is claimed that Furbies can say more than 800 phrases, but I would imagine a lot of them end up forgotten, shoved in the back of a cupboard, before reaching their full potential. One of my favourite activities with a fully matured Furby is to hold him upside down for a while. You ll be greeted with a pitiful wail of  Me scared  and some whimpering. It kind of makes you feel in control If you have the pleasure (?) of living in a multi-furby household like I do, then sit them in a circle and let them chatter to each other. It s quite amusing until they all decide they want feeding. The good side though is that as soon as one goes to sleep the others follow suit so peace quiet and sanity are restored... eventually. At the full price of around    20 (plus the cost of batteries), Furby is not the cheapest toy on the market, but shop around and you ll find them cheaper - Toys R Us often sell them at less than    10 and Halfpriceorless.com periodically stock them too. Furby sadly is not the most robust of play things. A concussed Furby sounds like a strangled cat, so try to avoid dropping him... unless you have a seriously sadistic streak in you. Treat him with care and you should get many hours of enjoyment from him before the novelty wears off. (The official line on battery duration is 15-20 hours play time per set of 4 AAs). You can get further details about Furby himself from Furbyland - The official Furby website, which can be found at www.furby.com (Furby toys are produced by Tiger Electronics, a division of Hasbro, and details on other products by these manufacturers can be found at www.tigertoys.com or www.hasbro.com)     ', '    Furbies are very cute and cuddly. They can talk, eat, sleep, sing and learn languages. They cost around    30, so are they worth it? Well, at first, I thought aww, they look so cute  Then I asked my Mum if I could get one. She said maybe, but I got one, so did my brother and sister. Furbies require 3 AA batteries, so we had to buy those as well. I thought they were really good at first, but then one day my Furby said a word that it had never said to me before. ', '    These are the worst toys ever, to any potential buyers of Furby  8217;s, I wouldn  8217;t recommend them and I think they were the worst    30 I have ever spent in my life. ', '    I bought a Furby for a friend this Christmas, as she had given away her last one to a visiting child. Furbys are not just for kids you see, they can be entertaining for housebound adults. ', '      I m gonna bounce....... boing boing boing..... ', '    I have been using Pampers now for over 4 years, at one point I had both of my children in them at the same time, now that was expensive.
