product_reviews: ['    In an ideal world pets would benefit from free health care, but we all know this will never happen, with not enough money for humans it would be unrealistic.In television lala land Animal Hospital or Pet Rescue would sort out any problems in the blink of an eye. Well excuse my cynicism but in my experience expecting the RSPCA to rescue a stray or ill cat without a television crew as back up is as unlikely to happen as me winning the lottery. In my area the PDSA (Peoples Dispensary for Sick Animals) runs a scheme for people on benefits or low incomes, and very worthy it is too, but where does this leave the average working person. It seems if you don  8217;t fit into the category of being financially able to afford infinite vets bills, on benefits or low incomes and so benefit form the PDSA scheme, the average working person on an average working wage has to foot the bill themselves, even if they are financially unable to. It  8217;s the same with prescriptions (but that  8217;s another opinion and I shouldn  8217;t even start on that here). This coupled with the fact that illness and tragedy can strike even the most beloved pet, persuaded me to seek animal insurance for my Golden Retriever Molly. Retrievers unfortunately are susceptible to some inherited conditions such as hip and eye problems, despite being in sound health, when Molly was 6 I finally got round to considering her middle age and health care, thus began the search for a reasonable policy. I made my initial inquiries by phone, contacting several companies and discussing prices, type of cover and clauses. Personally I like to talk to humans in these matters as opposed to other research methods and I found, despite the varying cost of policies, one factor in particular made me choose Petplan, that was most companies stop paying for treatment of a condition after a 12 month period. This is obviously unhelpful if your animal develops an ongoing problem like diabetes, eczema or arthritis. Petplan however agrees that as long as the owner continues the policy, they will operate a   8216;covered for life policy  8217; and will continue to pay for claims of the same illness until the animal  8217;s old age. Obviously premiums rise with age, but I still considered this the best company to suit my particular needs. Of course it is important to instigate insurance before any medical conditions developed. How to contact Petplan Phone ~ Telephone 020 8580 8080 Fax ~ Fax 020 8580 8001 Internet ~ www.petplan.co.uk/default.asp Post ~ Computer House, Great West Road, Brentford, Middlesex TW8 9DX Incentives Upon joining Petplan, I received a year  8217;s free subscription to Petsafe worth    14.99, this is 24 hour monitoring service for lost cats and dogs. The owners contact details are registered with Petsafe and the animal wears an identifying disc on their collar with a contact number. Although Molly is micro chipped, I felt Petsafe was a good idea as it allowed any member of the public who finds her to see a contact number, after all micro chips are not read by the human eye and although she wears a disc saying she is micro chipped, I felt a backup plan was still a good idea. This incentive was carried over to the 2nd year of cover and I  8217;m hoping it continues. I checked the web page recently and found the incentive at the moment is one month  8217;s premium free, I personally prefer the Petsafe incentive. Cost Petsafe covers different animals, i.e. cats, dogs and rabbits. Prices are based on the area you live in and are identified by your postcode. Dogs are then catergorised by breed and age. Prices and excesses vary according to all this information and the plan that you choose. Payments can be made monthly be direct debit and I chose this option. Everything was done over the phone and the documents followed within a week. There was a 14-day cooling off period in which I could cancel the policy if I changed my mind. Molly was 6 when first insured and her premiums were as follows ~ 1st Year 1 payment of    13.45 11 payments of    12.45 2nd year 1 payment of    14.05 11 payments of    12.94 This was a Budget Low Xs policy and gave the following cover ~ Vets fees for illness and injury, including hospitalisation, referral and complementary medicines ~    4000 with an excess of    50 Boarding and Kennel fees or homecare with a friend if you are hospitalised for more than 4 days ~    250 no excess Advertising and rewards ~ If your pet gets lost or stolen, Petplan will pay for local newspaper advertising and a reward ~    250 no excess 3rd party liability ~ If your dog causes damage or injury and you are held legally liable ~    1,000,000 excess    250 Death from Injury or Illness Losing a pet is a great sadness but Petplan will refund the purchase price (see exclusions). The excess applies to each individual claim, i.e. different conditions would require the owner to pay the excess on each condition, if the condition requires numerous treatments, only one excess is paid. I noticed my excess for vets fees rose by    5 the 2nd year to    55. Exclusions Any illness or injury that first occurred before the policy commenced, therefore it is important to start cover before chronic diseases are diagnosed. Any amount for death resulting from an illness or disease in a pet age 8 or over (fees for the illness itself still covered). Cosmetic dentistry Any treatment in connection with pregnancy or giving birth. The cost of killing or controlling fleas. Prescribed foods. My experience of a claim Last year, during my first year of cover, Molly became ill; she was sleepy and quiet, vomited after meals for 3 days and generally not herself. An examination by the vet proved worrying when the vet thought she felt something in Molly  8217;s abdomen. She immediately took blood tests, and sedated her for an x-ray. The suspected diagnosis was a tumor or a foreign body. Luckily the x-ray showed some sort of foreign body that had passed into the large intestine. The vet prescribed laxatives and it was hoped Molly would pass the offending article with a little help from mother nature. If she did not or became more seriously ill an operation to remove the foreign body would have been necessary. I dread to think of what the cost would have been but luckily I knew the insurance would cover it. It was a relief to be able to say to the vet  Do whatever you have to . The following day Molly   8216;passed  8217; the foreign body, it was a Dishcloth. The total vets bill was    380. I initially had to pay the vet and then claim the money back from Petplan minus the excess. I filled in the claim form and left it with the vet to fill in their part and send to Petplan for me. I thought this was the end of the matter but I was wrong. Four days later Molly vomited again twice, once more I returned to the vet who thought this was probably due to gastric irritation caused by the dishcloth and prescribed some antacid type tablets to calm her tummy. As this was related to the first incident I knew there would be no excess and my    18 bill was covered by Petplan, again I left the claim form with the vets receptionist. One week later I received a cheque for    330, the cost of the first treatment less the    50 excess, now by my records Petplan now owed me    18 for the 2nd consultation. Imagine my surprise when a week later I received a cheque for    348, the total cost of both treatments less the    50 excess. It seemed the vets receptionist had not realised the first claim had been sent and sent the whole claim again. Petplan had failed to notice this error and paid out twice. Now despite friends saying I was stupid and should keep quiet, I had this fear that one day they would find out and maybe even refuse to pay up on future claims, this led me to believe that honesty was the best policy and I phoned Petplan and told them. I must admit to being annoyed when they asked me to return the first cheque, I explained I had already banked it. They then suggested I return the 2nd cheque and they would send me one for    18. I informed them I would tear up the 2nd cheque, they could also put a stop on it to cover themselves and send me the    18, I was annoyed that despite my honesty no one said thank you for bringing this to our attention or offered to send a prepaid envelope to return the cheque. My only criticism therefore is perhaps a little more gratitude that I was trying to give them money back would have seemed appropriate. Despite that hiccup, which after all being paid twice is better than not being paid at all, I  8217;m glad I chose Petplan. The one time Molly needed veterinary care that would have been very expensive for me, I was able to say to the vet   8216;Do whatever you have to  8217; and not worry about the bill. Without the insurance I would still have agreed to treatment but would then have struggled to pay the fees. I believe this makes the monthly premiums worthwhile and intend to continue with this plan.      ', '    I have cats. Anyone that knows me will tell you that I love my cats and because I love them I have insurance cover to ensure that they are never denied veterinary help should it ever be required. So I have choosen to insure with Petplan, which has become a necessary investment in the future health and well being of my animalsPetplan is simple is simple to use and it offers cover for life, which in effect means that should you have an animal that becomes ill with a condition that will effect it for life, then Petplan will pay all veterinary fees for life on the proviso that you keep up payments on which ever cover plan you decide to take out. You must also ensure that  the animal has an annual health check and innoculations.Petplan has on offer various schemes to cover cats, dogs, rabbits and horses, details of which are easily accessible from their website which is easily located by typing Petplan into your browser or as an alternative you can phone direct for details or to request an information pack. Leaflets are also usually available in  at any vets surgery. It was also possible until earlier this month that if you bought a pedigree pet from a reputable breeder, then you would be given a free six week Petplan cover note which was validated over the phone before you left the breeders premises so giving you peace of mind. However due to changes concerning unfair practices breeders are no longer allowed to offer this facility. Be aware though that you will amongst other documents be given a telephone number which if called will still give the six week free insurance, but it is up to you the pet owner to call and validate it and it should be done on the day of purchase. This valuable insurance also comes with the promise that should your pet become ill or injured during its duration that you can obtain a continuation of this insurance without incurring any additional costs and I can vouch for this as I had the misfortune to buy a kitten that became ill, so ill that he almost died.When you phone for a continuation of a free insurance or apply by phone or on line for a new insurance or you will be offered a number of different options. In the case of cats and dogs the options are simple, you simply select cross breed or pedigree and then select whichever level of cover you require for your pet.Cover options include    Full settlemeny of Vet fees (Amounts are varaible dependant of the plan selected)    In the case of Dogs, third party cover should your pet injure anyone or cause damage.    Boarding fees should you need to go into hospital or require homecare with a friend.    Advertising and rewards should your pet stray or become lost.    A payment to cover loss of your pet due to theft or straying.    Holiday Cancellation if caused by your pet becoming seriously ill.A full description of all the above is available both online and in the written information packs.You can if you wish also adjust the level of your payments by selecting a Budget plan, which can reduce payments but has the downside of leaving you to pay 25  of every bill submitted. A full instant quotation facility is available on line where you simply enter your details together with those of your pet (Or you can enquire by phone.) and within seconds you are presented with a quotation. Should you decide to proceed with the insurance you then have to set up your preferred method of payment by selecting from direct debit, credit or debit card options. You will also be asked if you wish to contribute one pound to an animal charity.Within days of completing your sign up you will receive from Petplan a pack containing your policy and a leaflet containing a clear explanation of the wording of the policy. A claim form is provided in case you should ever need one, you can also download a printable claim form from the Petplan website.Now everything is set up and heaven forbid you find you have a sick animal, what do you do. Simple take your pet to the vet together with your claim form with the relevant details of both you and your pet filled in, the vet does the rest including submitting the form and provided the treatment is more expensive than the excess on you policy, in my case    60 then everything is covered. You must decide together with your vet at this point as to whether you will pay the bill and wait for Petplan to reimburse you or whether the vet will take care of everything so that you need not pay a penny. It is also worth pointing out that should the initial consultation fee come to a figure less than the excess levied on the policy that should you need to return to the vet with your pet for a follow up examination so taking the fee above the excess then you can still claim.Things of course can and do go wrong so watch out for the pitfalls. As I said earlier I have a kitten that is ill, he went to the vets and they diagnosed an upper respiratory infection and treated him accordingly. He also had diarrhoea and it was decided that the one illness caused the other. This diagnosis turned out to be wrong and so another course of treatment was started and again the vet filled out the relevant forms and sent them to Petplan. At the time I was paying the bills myself with reimbursement from Petplan so when Petplan received the second claim form with a different illness on it they refused to pay as the bill was below the excess.No amount of arguing on my part would sway Petplan so it was back to the vet and it was pointed out to him that I was paying for his incorrect diagnosis. As a result the vet took up my case with Petplan and the outstanding money was returned to me.By now my kitten was getting no better in fact he was slipping away and I took him away from the vets after telling them a few home truths when they said they could do no more for him. I then took him to see a vet miles away from home who is deemed an expert on cats and who surprisingly belongs to the same practice.  He took it on himself to liase with a University that has a department specialising in cat related illnesses and they decided that a course of a drug not licensed for animals was the best course of action in this particular case. The vet in question did warn me that as the drug was unlicensed that Petplan may not pay for it but he offered to deal direct with them rather than me making any payment and to my surprise Petplan have honoured their commitment to pay for a condition for life and so little Sven has received the drug with no cost to me.Up to now Sven s treatment has cost just under a thousand pounds which to be honest I would have found hard to find. So for a modest outlay of just under seven pounds a month I have both peace of mind and more importantly health care for my kitten so giving him a chance of survival. I might add at this point that some of my other cats are insured with a rival scheme, so would I recommend Petplan against the rival, well in all honesty I don t know as I have never had to make a claim on their plan but I will say that I do recommend Petplan which has proven it s worth and should I, (which is always a possibility) acquire other pets then Petplan will be my first choice of insurer in the future.Apply on line at the moment and the first months insurance is free and you are also intitled to a years free membership of Petsafe which provides a tag with a unique number which is then attached to your pets collar so providing a way to become reunited should your pet ever strayPlease never put off insuring your pets, yes I know there are excellent schemes such as the Peoples Dispensary for Sick Animals where treatment is free but free treatment is limited to those who cannot afford it. Never let your pets suffer, join a scheme such as this because you never know what will happen tomorrow.Vets Breeders and Animal Charities all recommend Petplan and so do I.Contact detailsTel 0800 1070204http://www.petplan.co.uk/Thanks for reading    Bigbaz 2005     ', '    Pet Plan certainly aren t the cheapest pet insurer, but they are one of the best   The main bonus that puts them ahead of the rest is their  cover for life .  This means that each year, following the excess payment (mine is currently    45), the animal is covered for continuing illnesses.  Many insurance companies only pay out for the same disease for one year only, or up to a certain amount.  If your animal is diagnosed with a long term illness, this can mean disaster with these companies, as you will shortly find yourself paying the bills even though you thought your pet was insured.Pet Plan insure cats, dogs, horses and rabbits (there may be more that I am not aware of). You have to pay the vets up front yourself and then claim the money back.  You can pay Pet Plan yearly or monthly by direct debit. They do not pay for pregnancy, speying, grooming, cremation, dental work, or home visits.As you can tell I have been very impressed with Pet Plan and all of my pets are insured with them.  One of my Pekingese was diagnosed as having auto-immune disease and they have paid out nearly    1,000 so far.  Due to their  cover for life  I am ensured of continuing cover for the rest of his life.Their telephone number is 0845 0178000UPDATE------I have just got my renewal for this year with a note saying that when my dog reaches 10 later this year, I will have to pay the excess (increased to    50) PLUS 35  of each claim.  This makes the insurance a lot less cost effective.  However, Pet Plan justify the charge as they say 60  of dogs over 10 years old make a claim.  I shall be continuing.     ', '    Our collie sadly died in January this year which left a gaping hole in our lives ,so we decided we should get a replacement. We wanted to get a rescued dog, so we began ringing round the kennels in the area(you would not believe how hard it is to rescue a dog ,rules on kids,gardens,age etc) anyway we found the dog we wanted at the Blue Cross,  after taking it for walks and having our home checked out we finally got our new dog (A lurcher called Corn ,don`t ask me where they got the name). To the point, included with our new dog came a trial period of six weeks free insurance with Petplan for which we signed up ,always having planned to take out insurance anyway. A month later we had not decided whether to carry on with Petplan or to go to one of the many other companies selling pet insurance, however this decision was taken out of our hands when Corn stuck her foot in a rabbit hole while flying full tilt across a field, the result being one broken leg. This was going to be long and expensive and as our six week trial was almost up and there was no way that Corns recovery was going to be completed we had no choice but to sign up with Petplan.Corns treatment lasted for three weeks and incuded four trips to the vets at a total cost of    240.00 of which we have recieved    192.00 back from Petplan in the form of two cheques two weeks after Corns last visit to the vet.So this is our experience of Petplan to date. This is how it works .When you fill in the Petplan application form you are asked whether it is for a cat, dog, or rabbit and then for the age of your pet, breed and your postcode, all of which have a bearing on how much your premiums will be. An excess is applied to all policies and is different depending on wich policy you have chosen to take out.As an example ours worked out as follows. age of dog, 6 months breed, crossbreed Post code, IP  monthly payment    12. 40This will drop by    1 a month once we have had her neutered.What do you get for your money? Depending on which plan you take out benefits could include Vets feesThird party liability (If your dog bites someone) Boarding kennels (If the owner is hospitalised) Advertising and reward (if your dog gets lost) Death from illness or injury Loss by theft or strayingThese are the benefits for a dog but I should imagine cat and rabbit cover is similar.How to make a claim . This could be inportant if your dog got a long term illness such as arthritis or diabetes as you will be able to make on going claims.  Overall although it is quite expensive when compared with other companis we are happy with the cover  petplan gives us and with the speed they handle claims.     ', '    Insurance from Pet Plan eased our families pain of losing Toby to Rat Poisoning.  Whilst Toby was with the vet being treated, the costs were increasing.  Having the safety of the insurance meant that we did not have to worry about the cost.  Finally when the end came, the vet, knowing we were insured made everything go smoothly and dealt directly with Pet Plan.  Just to have that little thing out of the way meant it remained out of mind.  We were able to ensure we could give the relevant time for a pining Ollie, who had been left alone.They were able to provide everything necessary from the outset, and they did so without putting pressure on us. Ollie is still going and is still covered     ', '    If you have ever had a pet you will know just how expensive it is, food, treats, collar and lead, plus the trips to the vets, and boy are they expensive.After my partner bought me a miniature longhaired dachshund I decided to get her insured as the vet bills are very expensive and it was going to cost an arm and a leg for her injections.I decided to ring around a few pet insurers but the one that stood out the most for me was petplan, there are several plans to meet just about everybody   s needs, I got the company to send me out some more details of the plans so I could decide which one suited me.~~~~~~~~~~~~***************************~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Around 4/5 days later I received a big brown envelope containing the info on petplan insurance.On one of the leaflets it said the very best for your dog so I started to read more.There was stuff about why you should have pet insurance, and answers to questions like  do many people claim on their pet insurance? and what cover for life actually means .~~~~~~~~~~~~~**************************~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Work out the best level of the plan for you by the type of dog you have and the area you live in (are you surrounded by fields or main roads). s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re considering Petplan Insurance for your pet, here’s a detailed look based on key insights that matter for a financially savvy and caring pet owner like yourself.

Petplan offers a variety of plans—Budget, Standard, and Supreme—allowing you to tailor coverage to your needs and budget. One standout feature is their “cover for life” policy, which continues to pay for ongoing or chronic conditions as long as you maintain the policy. This is a significant advantage over many competitors who limit coverage for a condition to 12 months or a capped amount, providing real peace of mind when managing long-term pet health issues.

The policy starts immediately upon agreement, and documents arrive quickly, making the sign-up process smooth. Plus, their website and phone support are user-friendly, helping you get quotes and enroll without hassle. Discounts for insuring multiple pets add value if you have more than one furry family member.

However, be aware of some important exclusions: pre-existing conditions, cosmetic dentistry, pregnancy or birth-related treatments, flea control, prescribed foods, and routine injections or neutering are not covered. Also, for older pets (typically over 8 or 10 years), coverage for death from illness may be limited, and excess amounts or contribution percentages can increase annually, which could impact your long-term costs.

A practical benefit is that Petplan charges only one excess per condition, even if multiple treatments are needed, which can save money during extended care. Claims are generally settled quickly—often within a week—and Petplan rarely refuses payouts, which is reassuring. That said, you must pay the vet upfront and claim reimbursement afterward, so budgeting for that is essential.

On the downside, some users report that customer service can be bureaucratic or ungrateful, especially when dealing with overpayments or errors, so patience may be required.

Overall, while Petplan tends to be pricier than some alternatives, many find the comprehensive coverage, reliable claims handling, and ongoing condition support justify the cost—especially if you prioritize your pet’s well-being and want financial security without surprises.

Then read on   WHO?TSB merged with Lloyds back in 1995 to form Lloyds TSB Group plc, I can t believe it s already been 13 years (I still referred to it as TSB by accident until 2 or 3 years ago). But it wasn t until mid 1999 that TSB and Lloyds Bank branches in England and Wales were actually re-branded as Lloyds TSB.WHY ME?I ve been a current account holder with Lloyds TSB since 1986, except then it was just TSB or Trustee Savings Bank (as was it s full name). What I liked about TSB even back then was that fact that it was online real-time banking, i.e. if you made a deposit anywhere in the UK at another branch of TSB it would show up on your account instantly, whereas as far as I m aware back then, other banks wouldn t show the deposit amount on your account till about 3 days later. I don t use my    200 overdraft facility at all (although I feel safe that it s there). I always pay my credit card bills in full so I don t pay any interest. I regularly get letters saying my credit limit on my credit cards has been increased - as I m a good customer, why not? Except that they expect me to get greedy and use more money than I can afford to pay back in one month and thereby have to pay interest. No, not me, not anymore THE ACCOUNTSFirstly there s the Classic with Vantage Current account. The whole company seems to be broken down into small sections and if you get a problem they will all start to blame the other departments and tell you to speak to someone else. I would not recommend this bank to anyone who is looking for more then just a savings account. What   s more they have very poor interest on their accounts, unless you apply for their online accounts but these seem to have more clauses then I   ve had hot dinners      ', '    My student bank account is with Lloyds TSB and has one of the largest over drafts of all the banks at one thousand five hundred pounds interest free which can go up to one thousand seven hundred and fifty but thats when they start charging the normal interest rate. One draw back is that to open the account you need to deposite one hundred pounds, which for some students will be tricky to find. They also sign you up to their credit card the asset card so plenty of opportunity for blagging cash back at spar. No real problems, although if your university financial admisistrators are as useless as Aberwyshites and you end up getting billed for tuition fees 3 times in one term you ll end up being charged by the bank thirty quid a time.     ', '    I have been a customer of Lloyds for all 20 years of my life, then when I was 18 I became a student... student eBank suddenly became public enemy No.2 after NTL (public enemy No.1)  I had recently recieved my latest card offerings before I was 18 - a cash card and a cheque card.  Become a student I then recieve the credit card (with its self increasing limit - until they asked me why I had such a huge limit) and the Debit Card x 3 in 2 weeks, and not all of them worked. End less phone calls and visits to the bank proved fruitless to get a pin number and to be told which card I should use.  Only when I made several offical complaints to which I recieved no replys did things begin to sort themselves out.  I got    50 to say sorry and promised no more hassle.A year later I need to go over my overdraft for a short period of time, this was aranged over the phone, but still took a while to sort out... no really big problems. 8 Months later I need to the same, this time due to the ineffency (sic) of the branch staff two, 2 hour visits are made, to get a temporary increase on the overdraft, yet they still only made it for a couple of weeks so it ended before I got paid... when I gave them documented proof of when I d get paid and how much.  I have had many over niggly problems, such as statements not turning up, change of address problems, missing money etc...As soon as I can afford to I think I ll change banks.     ', '    Yellow pages in hand I decided to get a few quotes for the home and contents insurance, I was suprised by just how much the Lloyds TSB service saved me. They act as brokers so have access to many different companies. The service was quick and easy to arrange the cover. Details were taken over the phone together with credit card payment to gain cover. Full policy documents were sent out the same day to confirm cover and conditions. I even got a    20 gift voucher as a new customer. The most suprising thing was that Lloyds TSB could actually offer the cheapest quote. High street banks are not normally associated with offering good value.     ', '    Having been with LLoyds for 17 years I now find myself being in the position of having to change banks.Apparently statistics say you re more likely to get divorced than change your bank...so it s a major step. I m basically fed up with the bad service I ve recieved over the last few months. On my part I ve been a good customer, stayed in credit / within my overdraft, taken out loans with them and have had a steady account. The rest of the post is fine so the problem must lie with the bank. The staff are generally very good, but there doesn t seem to be anyone there who can give you the answers you need, the advice and help given varies but has been without results. Anyway this customer is taking his business elsewhere.     ', '    I have an ordinary, bog-standard, run-of-the-mill bank account with Lloyds TSB.And what can I say, the interest rates are appauling. Nationwide have a system where you get a Flexi Account, and then you can do online banking. Nationwide, offer a huge amount of interest (currently 6.75 ). This is soooo much more than I got before, and the only difference in access to money is that it takes one day to transfer money back into the Flexi Account to take out.     ']
filtered_hist_vote_written: ['    I have had an interesting conversation with a girl at Reality this morning. I got home to find a card advising me that they had tried to deliver something to me but hadn t been able to, so would redeliver within the next three days. That was April 23rd, so 3 days would mean up to and including April 26th, right?Well, no. The card says 3 days. Their phoneline says 3 days.What they mean is 3 working days.The card is terribly misleading. All I was offered as comfort was  I will make a note of it . No card was left when the courier tried to deliver, 5 days later.The courier/delivery industry in this country is an utter shambles. Reality is just the worst of a very bad bunch.It seems that getting the correct item delivered to the correct address on the correct day is beyond these companies.     ', '    I find the Bank of Scotland completely disagreeable.  Initially the sales people are more interested in getting your business than actually trying to help get the best deal.  Fair enough? They work for Bank of Scotland but at the very least i would like honesty, and someone who is knowledgable about their products.  For example to do what they say they will or atleast to recieve what you sign for  But they re only human    We can all make mistakes.What i dont understand is how they can t rectify them.  I was put on endless hold lines and still noone could help.  The kept giving me the same jargon but no answers.  Fine  But if you confront people they re more likely to help?  You would think so but no  A sales advisor couldn t find sand if he was sent to the beach.  He promised me he would talk to the manager and phone me back next day. Two days later i had to phone him and he had still not sorted it out.All in all i think these people are terrible and that the customer service is less than very poor.  I certainly would not recommend that anyone should go with them.  In My opinion they are cowboys who should go back to basics and treat their customers with respect.     ', '    Having worked for Debenhams, I am among the people who put their ethics and morals aside and pushed this card to customers for all its worth, with a lot of success. From a sale s adviser s point of view, it s fairly easy to sell: Would you like to open an account and save 10  NOW and for a WHOLE WEEK ? Not only that, but it s easy to open (providing you re dealing with a competent member of staff); there is a high acceptance rate from GE Capital, the bank that deals with the account; you save 10  or more throughout the year at various  mega days  and account evenings (but you may have noticed there is practically always a sale on at Debenhams anyway).Sounds good?Well, these are the bonuses, but how about the limitations? As with other credit cards, there is no annual charge, and the minimum payment I believe is 5  or    5. But with Debenhmans you have 30  interest to pay on any outstanding balances. Say you cannot afford to clear the balance one month, any savings you have made previously are wiped out straight away  So why bother? I would say stick to a normal credit card that gives you cashback or air miles or something. Better still, take advantage of the free Nectar card and save at Debenhams that way, by accumulating points.      ', '    I started with HSBC when I was about 14, and converted to a student account about 18 months ago when I started at university. Due to mess ups by the Student Loans Company, I used the overdraft facility of    1000 straight away, and had absolutely no problem. With the bank account there is a choice of    50 or a 3 year student railcard as an incentive. I took the railcard, but already had one that was valid for another six months. So HSBC, helpful as ever, delayed the railcard and automatically sent me one the VERY SAME WEEK that my first one expired.I also have Val, my personal finance advisor. She works in my local HSBC at home, but I can go into any HSBC and call her for free if I get into any money problems.Since last summer I have also had an HSBC Mastercard. The APR is 3 , so when I have maxed it to the limit (   500) I only have to pay back    15 a month.Pure genius - gives me money to spend on better things such as beer and parties.Go to HSBC for student accounts      ', '    I have written an opinion about this Courier Service (Interlink) in Ciao Cafe. I was not sure how to move that opinion under a different heading, where it would be more suited. I requested help from Ciao team (may be from the wrong person ) and still waiting for a response.I am not  for  or  against  this Courier Service - I mean ....writing two opinions about one product could be a bit too much for a person who has written 4 opinions in 10 months   I will tell you why I have done it. As I could not find this product, I requested it as a  new product , when I received an email that ....this has been added, I felt guilty and thought of writing down something. Please forget if you have already seen / read my previous opinion  This courier service offers very reasonable price for International large size parcels as compared to UPS, Royal mail  that was the reason I used this service. A 20 kg parcel costed me    185 to send to New Delhi by this courier (which was quoted by other companies from    250-   580).The staff at receiving stations and rontline staff for telephone enquiries do not provide the correct information, may be the Company does not provide adequate training to answer queries other than the very routine ones.International section staff (London office) are extremely unrealiable, they deny what they have said to you two days back  faxes are lost  Customer Care Staff and Manager- reasonably reliable, you have to support your views by documentation. Do not make phone complaints, never remembered Give time bound requests to answer your queries- everything in writing, letters by recorded delivery.     ', '    I applied for my Mint card about 2 weeks ago, and I am writing this review to tell everyone how thrilled I have been with their service so far. I chose this card by comparing rates for balance transfers     this one is 0  until Feb 2005. As far as I know Mint is an internet only operation.I applied online, which was a simple process, at the end of which I was told immediately that my application had been accepted, and what my credit limit would be. I received the credit agreement two days later, and after returning this it was only another couple of days before I received a confirmation that my balance transfer had been carried out. I had cause to contact customer services to check out a detail of the credit agreement, and found them friendly and helpful, plus there was no waiting in a queue.My card and pin number also arrived very quickly, and the activation process was straightforward. I found the customer services staff polite and helpful. I chose Mint   s MC2 card     the one with the curve which you might have seen on the TV. Mint warn you that you may not be able to use this card in ticket machines etc. but if this is a problem you can choose an ordinary shaped card. I wish everything in life could be as well organised as Mint appear to be     no hold-ups, no hassles, no having to chase them around. Everything just turned up like it should.      ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
Lloyds TSB presents a mixed bag for anyone serious about banking with transparency and solid customer service. On the positive side, branch-level staff tend to be friendly and helpful, which can make in-person visits less painful. The bank also invests in comprehensive training for its employees on legal compliance and customer protection—something that should, in theory, translate into better service and safeguards for customers.

However, the reality often falls short. Call centre staff frequently provide incorrect or misleading information, likely due to insufficient training or over-reliance on rigid computer systems. This disconnect is compounded by poor communication between departments and centralized admin centers, leaving customers caught in frustrating loops. Charges at Lloyds TSB are another sore point: fees for account services, overdrafts, and statement requests are notably high and often applied automatically without clear explanation. While small charges might be refunded at the branch manager’s discretion, this feels more like a band-aid than a customer-first policy.

What stands out is Lloyds TSB’s apparent prioritization of revenue over customer satisfaction. The impersonal nature of fees and the inconsistent service quality suggest a bank more focused on profit than on building trust or transparency. For a customer who values clear, honest communication and cost-effective banking, Lloyds TSB’s approach can be disappointing and frustrating.

In summary, if you’re looking for a bank with friendly face-to-face service and solid legal safeguards, Lloyds TSB might work—but be prepared for high fees, inconsistent advice, and a system that often feels more interested in your money than your experience. Approach with caution, and don’t hesitate to question charges or seek clarity, because the bank’s default isn’t always in your favor.

product_reviews: ['    Premium Bonds have had a varied reputation. Born against considerable political opposition, they have now been around for fifty years. In some eyes they are considered    naff        something that used to be given to the kids for christening presents, but which are now    old hat   , boring, expensive.However they are one of the secret weapons of the successful entrepreneur. Premium Bonds are a government backed security and as such your initial investment is safe. The prizes are tax free. If you read the serious financial papers or talk to a personal investment advisor in these days of very low interest and inflation rates generally, many will suggest a holding of Premium Bonds as a hedge in an all-round balanced portfolio. Although the nominal interest rate may be low, it is still quite competitive compared with the average Building Society and beats the Banks. Capital invested in Premium Bonds has stayed stable (except for inflation) over the last three or four years unlike money invested in shares.Unlike the National Lottery there is only one draw a month. However your money is still there after the draw even if you haven   t won anything. Statistically your chances of winning a prize are quite a lot higher with Premium Bonds. There is no doubt that the more you have the more likely you are to win (regardless of the publicity otherwise). Take a look at the distribution of the higher level prizes from the December 2002 Prize Draw in comparison with the prize winner   s actual holding.   National Savings - Prize winners December 2002Prize          Bond No        Total Holding   Area   1,000,000   61KF029460      6,650   NORTH YORKSHIRE   100,000     78PN 903645     19,000  BRISTOL   100,000     65DE 621819     20,000  ESSEX   50,000      32GN 517278     18,901  WEST GLAMORGAN   50,000      23QH 007647     7,005   WEST MIDLANDS   25,000      8TC 254288      5,000   GALASHIELS   25,000      37YT 684449     1,050   CO DOWN   25,000      24NW 034532     20,000  HAMPSHIRE   25,000      14BE 837046     19,000  CHESHIRE   25,000      1ED 650558      20,000  LB of ISLINGTON   25,000      72ZN 774067     20,000  SURREY   25,000      74BP 600893     20,000  KENTA LITTLE HISTORYPremium Savings Bonds were launched by Harold MacMillan, then Chancellor of the Exchequer,  in the Budget of 1956 amid much opposition. Harold Wilson went on record in June 1956 saying:  Now Britain s strength, freedom and solvency apparently depends on the proceeds of a squalid raffle . The first draw took place on 2 June 1957.The actual draw is carried out by ERNIE (Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment) which  took 10 days in 1957 to carry out the first draw. ERNIE is not a computer so it cannot be programmed to favour any particular range of numbers. A new ERNIE was built in 1973 and this was replaced by a new model which was built in 1988. The current draws take about six hours. The numbers generated by ERNIE are regularly checked each month by the Government Actuary, who is independent of National Savings and Investments, to ensure every draw is entirely random. No test so far has ever shown any evidence that this is not the case.The    1 million jackpot was introduced in April 1994.WHO CAN BUY BONDS?Any adult over the age of sixteen years can be a Premium Bond holder. After the first application for purchase has been made a Bond Holder registration number is issued.Special arrangements are available for children under the age of sixteen years as they may not buy or hold Bonds in their own name. Bonds may be purchased by parents and the Holder   s Card is issued to the parent by proxy for the child. Grandparents may also buy bonds for a grandchild. Prior to the child   s sixteenth birthday, the Holder   s Card must be signed by the child and witnessed by the parent and a new Card issued. The Bonds become the property of the child by law.Special arrangements also apply for an individual who has granted a power of attorney to another in financial matters or where the individual is subject to the Court of Protection. In this circumstance the subject   s receiver may buy and hold bonds on behalf of the named person.Bonds cannot be bequeathed, given away or transferred to another person. On death, a special dispensation will allow the estate to leave the Bonds in up to twelve further consecutive draws and any winnings are added to the estate. On the first anniversary of the death, the Bonds are repaid to the estate.  HOW DO YOU BUY BONDS?Bonds are purchased in    1 units with a minimum single purchase of    100. Above that level, increments of    10 are allowed. When this lower purchase limit was introduced some years ago it was generally felt that the attraction of Premium Bonds was on the wane and this limit had been set too high. This has not proved to be the case. Units are purchased in consecutive numbers, represented by the certificate (for example a    100 bond certificate may represent bonds 77AX 120001 to 77AX 120100).Premium Bonds are bought by application to the National Savings and Investments Department  (NS I) - a government agency. Forms are available at Post Offices who will also accept the completed form and money. The completed form may also be returned to the Department by mail with a cheque.  Forms can be downloaded and printed from the web site (www.nsandi.com). On occasions, existing Bond holders and prize winners may be invited to subscribe to further Bonds by telephone with payment by Switch.There is a maximum personal holding of    20,000. [This limit was raised to    30,000 in June 2003 - ADC]HOW DO YOU WIN?Every current Bond is entered into the Prize Draw which takes place at the beginning of each calendar month. A current Bond is one which was purchased at least one full calendar month prior to the current draw and which remains uncashed.Bond numbers are drawn randomly by ERNIE as mentioned above. Winning numbers are published in the London Gazette and also on the NS I web site. Prizes are sent out by crossed mandate to the winners     usually by the fifteenth of the month. The certificate notes which Bond actually won the prize.If you do not wish to take your prize as cash, it is possible to arrange for the money to be used to buy a new Bond which is then entered into the next but one prize draw. This is the only exception to buying Bonds with a value of less than    100. If the reinvestment takes the holding above    30,000 the excess is returned to the Bond holder.   THE PRIZE FUND.A monthly prize fund is allocated so that there is one prize for every 28,500    1 units in the draw. Each    1 Bond has a separate and equal chance of winning a prize. This means that the odds of any    1 unit winning a prize in a monthly draw are 28,500 to 1.Money is invested by the Department and is underwritten by HM Treasury. A nominal interest is paid into the prize fund which varies with the general base rate. The current interest rate is 2.4  . 5  of the prize fund goes to    higher    value awards, 7.5  goes to    medium awards and 87.5  goes to    lower    value awards.The draw in December 2002 had an estimated prize fund of    35.1 million. This was distributed as follows:Prize band Prize value No. of prizesHigher value:    1.8 million                    1 million 1            100,000 2             50,000         2             25,000         6            10,000   15             5,000   31 Medium value:    2.6 million                  1,000         1,053            500         3,159 Lower value:    30.7 million              100         2,739             50      608,848 Total:    35.1 million1    (Table reproduced from the NS I Web site)[The actual valuation, division of the prize fund and percentage chances for each bond do vary according to the nominal interest rate. Up to date values are printed with the official documentation - ADC (Aug 2003)]THE GAME STRATEGY.The official guidelines suggest that with the maximum holding (   30,000) and with average luck, anyone should win about ten prizes a year. Most of these will be    50 but there is always the chance of a larger win.It should be obvious that the best time to purchase new Bonds is on the last working day of the month (a Bond bought on January 31st will enter its first draw on March 1st). The best time to cash in Bonds is on the second day of the month. PERSONAL EXPERIENCESBefore his death, my father held the full    20,000 worth of Premium Bonds. In the last year of his life he had thirteen wins totally    950. His estate left the Bonds in place for a further twelve months and there were another seven monthly wins. I bought my first Bonds in 1985. I do not hold anywhere near the maximum number of Bonds but have had six monthly wins since July 2002 giving me an equivalent interest rate of 4    . The purchase dates of the winning Bonds have varied across the years since then. In fact the reinvested prize from one winning Bond won another prize in its first prize draw. The kids are given Bonds for Birthday and Christmas presents over the years and between them see two or three wins per year.  THE BOTTOM LINE.Premium Bonds: An investment vehicle for the serious saver, for parents to provide for a child   s future, to put aside for a rainy day. An alternative to the Building Society Deposit account. A gambler   s vehicle for the one who likes an occasional flutter     an alternative to the Lottery     but who is happy not to see his stake disappear each time. ', '           It Could Be You (but it probably won t be)  I assume that most people are like me and have an ISA. What Are Premium Bonds  Premium bonds are UK government backed bonds issued under the national savings and investment scheme and have been around since 1956. Instead of putting your money in a bank and gaining interest on it with premium bonds you effectively buy a bond from the goverment and instead of interest being paid on your money the bond goes into a kind of lottery whereby you have the chance to win  prizes . These prizes are paid instead of interest and range from    25 to one million pounds and the draw takes place every month at the start of the month. Each bond you own is worth    1 and theoretically everyone has a chance of winning but obviously the more bonds that you own the more likely you are to win a prize. The amount of prizes that are allocated every month are based on the bank of England base rate so at the moment when the inteest rates are so low there are less monthly prizes than there was two years ago when the interest rate was higher. The pluses of premium bonds are that any money that you put into premium bonds is completely safe and guarenteed by the government. The chance to win a prize every month is obviously a big incentive and any money that you win is considered to be tax free. The minuses of premium bonds is that in order to really win any prizes you really need to have quite a high amount of money staked. Also there is no guarentee that you will ever win anything whereas at least in a bank you are guarenteed a set amount of interest even if it is quite small at the minute. Another big thing to consider is depreciation. If you put    10,000 into premium bonds and leave it for 5 years and dont win any big prizes then with the rise in the cost of living    10,000 is worth less than it was when you put the money in.  Where To Buy Bonds  You can purchase premium bonds from the post office or online direct from the NSandI website. The minimum amount of bonds that you can purchase is    100 and the maximum that you can hold at any one time is    30,000. If you are buying them at the post office you will have to fill in a form and show some ID. Anyone can buy premium bonds but you do need to be over the age of 16 to hold them. You can t pay for them with credit cards and they can only be bought online with a debit card held in your own name. The process of buying and receiving the bonds is pretty straight forward and once you have paid for them you should have the bond within a week or so. One word of warning for anyone thinking of buying them is to wait until the end of the month before purchasing them because the bond won t go into the draw for one month after buying them so if you buy them at the beginning of the month then you will have to wait over 7 weeks befre they are eligable to win anything.  The Bonds  Once you have bought your bond then you will receive it through the post usually in my experience within a week. Owning the bonds has changed quite radically over the last few months as has how they now issue the bonds. Before you would receive a seperate bond for each amount that you invested. For example if you invested    1000 in January and then    500 in Febuary you would have two seperate bonds that contained the amount and the numbers of the bonds. You were supposed to keep these safe as you needed the numbers on them and you were also supposed to send back the bonds when you were cashing them in. They have now stopped issuing seperate bonds and when you now invest they just send you a new statement stating the amount of bonds you hold and your details and you can now destroy all your old bonds as this one sheet of paper contains everything you need to know. This obviously makes things easier not having loads of different pieces of paper to keep track of but I did enjoy collecting the bonds and seeing how many that I had managed to accumulate.  Cashing In and The Prizes  Cashing in your investment has now also been simplified. Before you needed to fill in a form and write down all the numbers of all the bonds you were cashing in and send it back to NSandI. The process could be time consuming but when they received the form they were pretty good about getting the money in my account within a few days. They have now set up an online account for premium bonds where you can have your money released into your bank account with just the press of a few buttons. There are still a few kinks with the system as far as I can see and I have now locked myself out of it three times which is not only extremely annoying but also time consuming as they need to send me a new password through the post and in the mean time I can t access my account. The prizes are what most people want to know about and these have also recently been changed. There used to be two one million prizes a month but this has been reduced to just one prize of a million and the lowest prize used to be    50 but this has also been reduced to    25. Also because the prize fund is linked to interest rates the amound of prizes on offer has been significantly reduced meaning there is less chance of winning anything in a month. If you do win a prize you used to have the option of either getting the money sent to you by cheque or else you could choose to reinvest the money and in that case they would send you a new bond. With the new system it is much better not having loads of smaller bonds sent to you and I think that you can also now have your winnings put into your bank which never used to be an option.  My Exerience of Premium Bonds  My experience of premium has been quite a positive one however this isn t the case for the majority of people I know who have invested in them. When I first invested in them my original investment was quite high and there was hardly a month went by that I didn t win at least    50 and usually it was more in the region of    150 -    250 and my largest prize was    1000. However when the interest rates were lowered and NSandI reduced the prize fund my winnings started becoming scarcer until it got to the point that I was going a few months at a time without winning anything. When this happened I decided it was time to put my money somewhere else especially as when I counted out my winnings I had made more than 5 times what I would have made in a high interest paying savings account. I still have a decent amount invested in premium bonds now that would be making me a small but steady stream of interest in the bank and I still win the odd    25 but nowhere near what I used to and I am now under what I would be making in a savings account even with the low paying rate. It is the thought of maybe winning a large prize however remote that possibility is that keeps me from withdrawing all my money from them. For his small chane I am willing to write off the small amount extra that I would get from the bank. If anyone was to ask me whether or not they should invest their money in premium bonds then I would say to look into it carefully first as there are definately pros and cons to them. Realistically unless you have a large holding you are unlikely to ever win a decent prize and could easily go a year without winning even    25. It is all based on luck and whilst my luck was good for a long time with them my sister for instance barely won anything whilst she had money invested. The novelty and excitment of checking the NSandI website every month to see if I have won is still there but unlike in the beginning I am usually left disapointed. There is a reason that they are popular and over 1/3rd of the UK population own some bonds but for me it probably has more ot do with the heavy advertising that NSandI do rather than how good the product actually is. ', '      There are two times in a man s life when he should not speculate: when he can t afford it, and when he can  - Mark Twain.Premium Bonds are a curious affair; part investment and part gamble, they are an almost-lottery run through National Savings and Investments, and backed by the government itself. I had until recently paid scant attention to them, until a chance conversation with my mother revealed that I had in fact owned a set of Premium Bonds since my 1st birthday, when my parents decided that some money given as a gift by my grandparents would be better placed into the bonds than into the savings account that they had opened for me. Having suddenly discovered this new dimension to my investment portfolio, I headed off to find out more about them.The Premium Bond scheme was started back in 1956, it turned out, when the government tried to encourage more people to save money for the future by operating what amounts to a risk-free lottery. When they were first offered, this system actually caused quite a bit of controversy, and they were even opposed by the Church s Committee, who rejected them because of the element of gambling involved. Most of you will be used to using savings accounts where interest is paid on the money you place into the account, usually annually, and you get whatever is left of the interest after the taxman has pocketed his share (unless you are lucky enough to be a registered non-taxpayer). However, Premium Bonds are a very different type of savings scheme, as they don t pay you interest. Instead, every    1 you invest in the scheme gets you a unique bond number that is entered each month into a prize draw where there are around a million prizes to be won, ranging in value from the top two prizes of    1 million to the smallest prizes of    50, all of which are awarded tax free. The numbers are drawn by the famous ERNIE (electronic random number indicator equipment), which randomly selects numbers to be compared to bonds. The sum given away each month is equivalent to the total interest that would otherwise be paid to all bond holders, and therefore varies according to the amount invested in bonds. The scheme is open to everyone aged over 16, although parents can buy Premium Bonds in the name of their children if they are younger, as happened in my case. When my parents bought the bonds for me back in 1979 the minimum investment was just    1, and the money they invested for me was (they tell me) a considerable investment into the scheme for the time, giving me multiple chances to win each month. Over time the irresistible force that is inflation has seen the minimum investment rise to where it currently stands at    100 (or    50 per month by standing order if you join the regular savers programme).A million prizes a month sounds a lot, doesn t it? Well, I thought so too until I read on and found out that there are currently 23 million bond holders owning    26 billion worth of bonds. Each bond has an equal chance of winning a prize, although the odds vary over time as the amount invested and the equivalent interest rate fluctuate. The way such figures are calculated is a shadowy procedure carried out by the Treasury, and according the National Savings and Investments website, your current odds of any one bond winning a prize are 24,000 to 1 (the odds were 11,000 to 1 back in 1993). By way of comparison, the odds of any    1 ticket winning a prize in the UK Lotto are 54 to 1, and the odds of any    1 ticket winning the jackpot in the same game are 14 million to 1. Mind you, there were only    4 billion invested in the bonds in the early 1990s - the explosive growth in bond ownership has seen the remaining    22 billion added over the past decade or so, thanks largely to the introduction of the    1 million jackpot, but also because they are increasingly seen as a safe alternative to diminishing savings account returns due to low interest rates. The big difference between Premium Bonds and games like the Lotto, though, is that with Premium Bonds your capital is safe; if you don t win one month, your bond numbers are kept and entered into every subsequent draw for as long as you own the bonds. This is why the scheme appeals to many people - it seems to offer a  safe  way of gambling, as you can t actually lose your stake. Obviously, the more money you invest in Premium Bonds, the greater your chance of winning one of the prizes, although there is a maximum investment limit of    30,000 per person. According to financial writer Jasmine Birtles in her book  A Bit on the Side , the odds of winning the    1 million jackpot if you have the maximum amount invested is 770,000 to 1, but you could expect an average of 12 prizes a year from this investment. She calculates this to be equivalent to a tax-free return of 2.15 , although the National Savings and Investments website cites the equivalent interest rate as 3.15  and independent financial advice website Motley Fool works it out at 3 . Should you be the lucky winner of one of these prizes, you will be notified by letter, or by representative if you beat the odds to win the jackpot. However, we all know how erratic the post is, and that coupled with the fact that people do irrational things like move house means that there are millions of pounds worth of unclaimed prizes from Premium Bonds, dating back over the years (500,000 prizes totalling    30 million according to the BBC). There is no deadline for a prize to be claimed, so if you have won a prize it will be kept waiting for you however long it takes you to claim it. The National Savings and Investment website (www.nsandi.com) has a handy checker on it for your bond numbers if you suspect you may be due one of those prizes, and I duly typed in mine once my parents had relinquished the bonds to me to see if there were any unknown prizes lurking out there. Needless to say, I had won nothing. In the 27 years that I have held Premium Bonds (or 327 monthly draws up to the time of writing), I have not had a single penny back on the investment. Mind you, that is nothing compared to the remarkable record that my parents have amassed between them - they have both held Premium Bonds for at least 40 years and neither of them has ever won, either. My mother jokes that we are storing up our luck to win the jackpot one month, but I am starting to wonder if Karma is trying to tell us something. If  average luck  dictates that you should get about a 3  return on your money per year, then after 27 years I should have expected (if my maths serves me correctly) to have nearly doubled the original investment bought for me on my 1st birthday by now. If the money had been put into my savings account I would have got a dull but reliable annual return on the money over time - none of the excitement of having a letter from ERNIE certainly, but I would definitely have had a growth in my money and it would have been a higher return than the 3  offered by Premium Bonds to boot. Premium Bonds are undoubtedly popular and are probably fun if you ever manage to win something. They also claim to be the only investment option that is 100  safe as they are backed by the Treasury itself, so it is secure and reliable. If you like a gamble, then they are certainly a tempting opportunity and many people may find the idea of winning prizes to be more appealing than the thought of getting interest, especially as there is no payment to the taxman with a prize. I can see all these advantages, but it seems my family just don t have  average luck  and with both interest rates and the stock markets rising, I think my Premium Bond capital might just be better invested elsewhere. I just can t see a future for me and ERNIE, I m afraid.For more information or to buy Premium Bonds, visit: www.nsandi.com       ', '    I like premium bonds. ', '    Until a couple of years ago I had heard of Premium Bonds, but had little idea about what they were and how they worked. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
National Savings and Investments (NS&I) Premium Bonds present a unique, low-risk way to engage with savings, backed securely by the UK Treasury. This government guarantee ensures your initial capital is safe and accessible at any time, which is a significant reassurance for cautious investors prioritizing capital preservation. The minimum buy-in is £100, with a maximum holding of £30,000 per person, making it accessible but limiting for those seeking to grow larger sums.

However, Premium Bonds differ fundamentally from traditional savings or investment products because they do not pay interest. Instead, they offer a chance to win tax-free prizes ranging from £50 up to £1,000,000. While this introduces an element of excitement and “gamble,” it also means returns are unpredictable and statistically low. Many investors may never win despite long-term holdings, while others might experience frequent small wins. This variability makes Premium Bonds more suitable for those who enjoy the thrill of a lottery-like system rather than investors seeking steady, guaranteed growth.

From a value-for-money perspective, Premium Bonds are not ideal if your primary goal is capital growth. They function better as a fun, risk-free supplement to a diversified portfolio rather than a core savings vehicle. The tax-free nature of winnings and the option to automatically reinvest prizes add convenience and some appeal, but the lack of interest and low odds of winning limit their effectiveness as a serious investment.

In summary, NS&I Premium Bonds offer a secure, government-backed product with the novelty of prize draws, appealing to those who value capital safety and occasional excitement. However, for prudent investors focused on predictable returns and growth, they should be considered a supplementary option rather than a primary savings strategy. Transparency about the odds and clear terms make them straightforward, but the inherent unpredictability of returns requires careful consideration aligned with your financial goals.

product_reviews: ['    I have just got an Egg Loan. I went to them to pay off an Overdraft - my Bank is ripping me off in Charges to pay Directors Fees and expanding abroad. GrrrI thought of Egg first, as I got an Egg card many years ago, when it was still a bit of a novelty to apply on-line. They were an offshoot of the Prudentail and were targetting the  young  market - whenever I called their Call Centre there was pop music playing in the background.Egg have grown up a bit since then and although at one point they made a bad move expanding into France, they are still innovative and competative.I first went to the egg.co.uk web site where you can do an instant calculation of monthly repayments. There are useful sections to explain their T Cs.I went straight to  apply for a Loan  and logged in using my existing details.After completing the on-line Application, I got a message saying that they needed to speak to me and I was given the opportunity of a time slot.  This did not surprise me as on-line I was asked to verify personal details such as Pay and Outgoings which were blank and they said they would need to validate this. I got a call back immediately from Matthew. This was a good start as a couple of months ago I got a mailshot offering a  special  loan, I rang the number for 25 mins and got no answer. I then rang the number on my Egg Card and they disputed that I would have to wait that long and announced it was not a  special  offer but the typical rate.Matthew was very humorous but thorough. Last time they were pushing sickness and unemployment cover, which when added to the headline  low  APR made it uncompetative, so I wondered what would happen this time. I explained that we have family BUPA and have sickness pay at work. He explained that he would offer a tailored package which turned out to have less extras than last time. I then began to wonder if thats why they call you back, as on-line you can decline all optional extras and I am sure insurance is very profitable for them.Matthew went through all the details, explained that you can pay this off early without penalty, it was an attractive rate and unsecured. I am old enough to have had a few Loans in my time and he was thorough.He then hit the  decision  key and I was accepted. I am sure you are aware of credit scoring, you get points for being married, having a phone, steady job etc and points deducted for arrears, late payments. Different Companies have different ways of scoring. I got my credit profile from Experian, one of the two big credit reference agencies, and I know my record is not AA++, I recommend you do this sometime, its frightening what they know about you.He explained the process for crediting this to my Account and the paperwork which would be sent out. (Last time the paperwork did not arrive and I had to chase it).So this time I had a very positive experience and I can recommend Egg as being professional, although I would think carefully about the Insurance extras and whether they are appropriate to you. They seem to be flexible. The High Street Banks are taking the proverbial with their APR rates and the Consolidators often add surcharges or insist that the Loan is secured on your house.Now I will have to just be responsible and not spend it too soon......     ', '    If you are thinking of getting a personal loan I can thoroughly recommend Egg as your lender. my colleague just signed up with them to borrow a small sum and I have, as always been thoroughly impressed with both the product and the service. ~~~~ Calculator ~~~~ Before applying for a loan visit the Egg website and head on over to the Loans section. Here you will find a loan calculator to help you decide how much you wish to borrow and over what period. The calculator allows you to enter how much you want to borrow; then either the Period you want to borrow over of the amount of monthly payments you can afford; you can also chose any payment protection options you require. Once you have entered the required information into the calculator you press the calculate button and you are given a loan illustration showing how much you will be paying and the number of payments you need to make. ~~~~ Budget Planner ~~~~ To work out how much you can afford to pay each month for a loan use the budget planner. Here you input details of all your monthly income and all your monthly expenses. To help you remember all your monthly outgoings there is a huge list of commitments that most people have. Simply input in the relevant boxes all your outgoings, the list is really great and includes all the regular utilities (gas, electric etc.) as well as things like holidays and going out and travel to and from work. When you have input all the information press the proceed button and your total spare cash is calculated, helping you to decide just how much you can afford to pay for your loan. ~~~~ Great Rates ~~~ At present Egg are offering the following rates for loans.    1000 to    2499 @ 16.5  APR    2500 to    4999 @ 14.5  APR    5000 to    9999 @ 10.7  APR    10000 to    15000 @ 9.9  APR These are very competitive rates, using Moneyextra.com I did a comparison for the amount he wished to borrow and only 2 lenders offered better interest rates. He chose to go with Egg as they offer more flexibility. ~~~~ Optional loan payment protection ~~~~ Whenever you take out a loan you are offered payment protection. With Egg you can choose the sort of payment protection you require. The options are Accident and sickness Unemployment or death Or any combination of these but life cover cannot be taken on its own. If you choose to protect against unemployment, accident or sickness you can also choose the deferment period (the time before you can claim). The deferment period can be either 30, 90 or 180 days. The amount you will need to pay for your payment protection is calculated according to the options you choose. ~~~~ Payment Breaks ~~~~~ Once you have been making your loan repayments for six months you can take a payment holiday of up to three months. The payment holidays can be taken in any 12 month period. This can be really handy if you find you need extra cash for a short period. After all you never know when you can suddenly get a huge drain on your finances, so you always have the peace of mind that can be gained from the ability to take a payment holiday. ~~~~ Overpayments ~~~~ With an Egg loan you can make an overpayment any time you want. Should you come into some money you can pay off a lump sum. Maybe you ll get lucky and earn a little extra through overtime, you can pay a little extra off of your Egg Loan. ~~~~ No Early Repayment Penalties ~~~~ Should you find yourself in a position to pay off your whole loan, you are able to do so. Some lenders charge an early repayment penalty to make up for the interest they won t get when you pay off your loan early. ~~~~ Interest Calculated Daily ~~~~ This is a huge advantage if you are able to make overpayments to your loan. Instead of being charged interest for a month after you have paid, you are only paying interest on what you owe each day. ~~~~ Increase and Decrease Payments ~~~~ As I have already mentioned you can overpay your loan at any time. You can also arrange to make a higher monthly payment permanently if you have got a nice big pay rise. Similarly if your circumstances have left you with a reduced income you can make arrangements to reduce your monthly payments and pay your loan over a longer period. ~~~~~ Online Application ~~~~ You complete all your application details online and you may get a decision within minutes. Egg were in contact the day after the application to confirm a few details and then tell you wether or not your application was successful over the phone. ~~~~ Money In a Week ~~~~ Once your application has been accepted Egg post you the completed forms for you to sign. If you sign and send them straight back your money will be in your nominated bank account within the week. You can also specify a date by which you want the money transferred, this can be up to 3 months away. ~~~~ Choose Your Repayment Date ~~~~ You tell Egg which day of the month you wish them to collect your monthly payments. The collection will commence once you have the money, when your next nominated date comes up. This allows you to make sure the payments are collected just after payday. ~~~~ The bottom Line ~~~~ I helped my colleague to choose Egg because the flexible options are just what he needed at the moment. In the next 18 months he is expecting two payouts which will allow him to pay chunks off of the loan. We found a slightly better rate elsewhere but the flexibility he wanted wasn t there so he went to Egg instead. Also I have Egg shares, which I m hoping will one day be worth what I paid for them so every bit of business they get helps me       ', '    After making a decision to buy a new car, (see my previous op )  I shopped around for the best loan deal I could find that suited me. The most obvious places, like my bank, or the place I was buying my car from did not offer anything favourable to me.  What I was looking for was a loan where I could be flexible, i.e. be able to pay off lump sums when I can afford it, or increase my monthly payments or take a month off maybe now and then. Two familiar names came up, Egg, and Cahoot.The Cahoot site didn  8217;t load for me,  I am an impatient sort, so they lost my business straight away. So anyway, the loan was approved. I received direct debit papers in the very next days post. I now have the cash waiting in my bank account in anticipation of the 28th of September when alflavor will be blasting around the streets in a MCC Smart Passion  I will update as and when I use any features of the loan, such as using a lump sum to decrease the debt. Well you never know, I may win Bananalotto or Tombola      ', '    I would just like to share my experiences of Egg Loans with you.  To start, go to www.egg.co.uk and choose the personal loans section.  The registration process is comprehensive (takes about 15 minutes all up) but you have the option to continue later if you don t have much time. Once you have submitted the form, they tell you that you will hear in 2 days and I heard in exactly that.  Much to my relief, they accepted my application with an APR of 11.5 .  Now, I should say that this was very important as I m a young lady who has had some rather crazy times with money and hence have landed myself over the course of time in some trouble financially.  Although I m better now, I obviously still have a negative credit rating as I get turned down for everything that I apply for - although I could manage repayments easily.  I applied without success for loans with smile, if.com, halifax and also all the main banks (although I didn t particularly want loans from them as their APRs are so high ). They offer loans from    1,000 to    15,000.  The Egg Loan has also won the Money Facts gold award for the most flexible unsecured loan.Once they approved my loan, the paperwork arrived 2 days later.  I signed the form and chose how and when I wished the payment to arrive - either via cheque, straight into my account.  This was all that the paperwork consisted of as the loan application was completed online.  Once again, 2 days later I received notification that the money had been sent to my bank.  This has to have been the cleanest process I have ever had when dealing with money   The whole process took a week and a half I highly recommend egg for loans if you wish a no-fuss, hassle free loan procedure. ', '    I am sure there are many people like me out there - we pay loan and credit card payments without stopping to consider whether we can find a better deal.Four months ago, I received a letter from egg inviting me to apply for a loan.
