product_reviews: ['          IntroductionBaked Beans are an item that can be found in everybody   s food cupboard, they are a versatile product that can be eaten hot on toast or as part of a meal or on a cooked breakfast or used in stews or shepherds pie or eaten cold from the can if the fancy takes you.Baked beans are made by stewing haricot beans in a tomato based sauce; they are a good source of fibre and can be counted as one of your five a day. The product I am reviewing today is Tesco Value baked Beans in Tomato Sauce.PackagingThe packaging is quite attractive for a value product; the paper label is glued around the metal can and can be removed for recycling. On the label there is the Tesco value logo on the front with Baked Beans in Tomato sauce written boldly in white writing on a red band, in the background there is a picture of beans, looking quite vividly orange also on the front of the can (can a circular can have a front?) there is an at a glance nutritional information band. On the back of the can there are the cooking instructions for various power microwaves and also hob cooking instructions. There is also a more detailed nutritional breakdown, storage instructions in case you don   t finish the can, a list of ingredients and contact information. All this information is also written on the back in Polish, Czechoslovakian, Hungarian and Slovakian.The can is made of recyclable steel so can be de-labelled, washed out, crushed and put in your recycling box or taken to your local recycling centre.The contentsOnce you have carefully opened the can with a can opener (no fancy ring pull for us value customers) and poured the contents in to a microwavable dish the beans are cooked in a matter of minutes and ready to serve with a Bacon and Eggs or Chips and Fish Fingers or on a humble slice of toast. On the back of the can it is advised not to boil the beans.The beans can also be warmed up in a pan on the hob on a medium heat. When I warmed the Beans up on the hob my children wanted to know what I was doing with them, I think I must use the microwave too often.The beans themselves are a creamy colour and an oval shape about the size of pea gravel. The sauce the beans are cooked in is sweet and tastes of tomatoes with a little tang and compliments the creaminess of the beans. The ratio of Beans to sauce is perfect.  The beans have just the right amount of bite to them, neither to soft nor to hard. There is nothing worse than a can of little bullets. The sauce has just the right consistency not thick like tomato ketchup nor to runny like water.The Value Beans now contain 50  less salt than they used to.Ingredients and Nutritional InformationHaricot beans (44 ), Tomato Paste (26 ), Water, Sugar, Glucose-Fructose Syrup, Modified Maize Starch, Salt, Onion Powder, Paprika, Flavourings.The recipe contains no nuts but cannot be guaranteed nut free.Half a can 210g contains 105 calories, 8.8g protein, 15.5g carbohydrates of which 8.6g sugars, o.6g fat of which 0.2g saturates, 9.2g fibre and 0.5g sodium.ConclusionThese value beans are just as good as Heinz Beans, and priced at    0.29 a can they are much better value and handy to have in the cupboard so you don   t starve in the two days before pay day. I always buy value beans as I don   t see the point of paying extra to have a fancy brand name in the cupboard and with the packaging on Tesco value beans they don   t look as down market as some value brands.I can not write about baked beans without mentioning the good old fashioned childhood rhyme which goes as follows (sing along if you wish)    Beans, Beans good for the heart, the more you eat the more you fart   Baked Beans are well known for causing excess flatus (being grown up now) due to fermentation cause during digestion.Thank you for reading.     ', '    Being a bit of a baked bean snob but with the credit crunch biting I decided to attempt a switch over from my much loved (and tried and tested) Heinz baked beans and give Tesco   s Value Baked Beans a go.  My fears of course being that at a cost of 29p for 420g I would receive a severely compromised Baked Bean experience.  Especially when in comparison Heinz Baked Beans cost a whopping 64p for 415g.  I mean we all know the saying    you get what you pay for    and with such a dramatic difference between value and premium this was bound to be the case here, right?I set out to find out  Tesco   s Venture into Own Brands Founded by Jack Cohen in 1919 Tesco   s is the UK   s largest supermarket chain and the third largest in the world based on revenues.  As of Feb 2010 there were 455 Tesco superstores located in the UK with a further 1130 Tesco express stores (not bad from a store that began life as a stall to sell surplus groceries at Well Street Market, in London).Tesco   s have diversified into other commercial markets including the stocking of their own label products within their stores.The sheer size of Tesco   s as a buyer, combined with the lack of need to market and promote its own label products, will mean that they are able to produce and sell similar quality merchandise at a reduced price to other manufacturers.  Theoretically with Tesco s being one of the largest food product purchasers you would think their value beans would be cheaper than other supermarkets however having had a look around they are all very similarly priced (suggesting that these may indeed still be a bit of a loss leader product).   I asked myself could this be the cause of the price difference for their value beans or is it purely a matter of quality reduction? The Value Beans These Baked Beans, are based around the promise of cooked Haricot beans in a sweet tomato sauce and are generally used as an accompaniment for meals or used as ingredients within a recipe.  They are often believed to be a good source of protein and although there is some contained within, it is really the fibre that make these quite good for you (if you overlook the salt and sugar contents that is).  They can be a little hard on the digestive system though (for some with embarrassing side effects )The tin itself does not sport the more luxurious feature of a ring pull for easy opening.  Slightly frustrating          Pictures of Tesco Value Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce     ', '    Now I reckon I am a connoisseur of baked beans. Only because, in the days when a bag of batter scraps from the local chippy was free and wages were low;   I spent the first few years of my time away from home and the luxury of mum   s home cooking, eating baked beans on toast, mainly for tea and occasionally as my main midday meal. Then, of course, Heinz had little or no competition.I still enjoy the occasional snack of beans on toast, but nothing near as frequently as in my youth, and I have shed the reputation of being the only member of the family whose most important kitchen implements were a saucepan and tin opener.Before I get down to giving my opinion of Tesco Value beans, I would like to tell a little of what I have learned about baked beans in general.The first and surprising piece of info I discovered in a lecture by a nutritionist long ago, was that a meal of Baked Beans on toast was a perfectly balanced meal. Yep. Just baked beans on toast, for it contained a perfect balance of vitamins, minerals and fibre. To add egg, bacon or anything else would make it a less well-balanced meal; therefore, it is not surprising that I did so well on that meagre meal for so long?A perfect balance in a meal is the same as a perfect balance in cake making. Too much or too little of one ingredient and the balance has been altered and cake ruined.Having said that, it would not be wise or healthy to live on beans on toast entirely.The minerals contained in the baked haricot beans are calcium, iron, magnesium, phosphorous, potassium, zinc, copper, manganese selenium and fluorine. The vitamin content is A, C, K, B6 and Folate.There are no unhealthy trans fatty acids present or cholesterol.Heinz now has considerable competition to their traditional baked beans, and I have tried most of them, Tesco own brand included. I paid 29p for a 420g tin of Tesco brand baked beans, much less than for Heinz or Branston brands.Tesco Baked beansContents: I have listed the contents of the haricot beans, but a tin of baked beans, whatever the brand, contains a few more additives, such as tomato paste, sugar from corn syrup, onion, Sodium, pepper, spices and paprika flavourings. It is the quality and amounts of these additions that separate the quality and taste between different brands.Tesco Value baked beans main ingredients consist of 44  beans and 26  tomato paste. Compare this with another leading brand which contain  51  beans and 34  tomatoesThe most disturbing discovery I made, when reading all the writing on the label a little more thoroughly than usual,     and this is where I briefly go off on a tangent - is that the additives contains artificial sweeteners. Without diving head long into a boring chemistry lecture, I have to say that although the contents on the label do state that the sugar is a glucose-fructose syrup. What is not clear is that this syrup is a manufactured sweetener with different properties to that of ordinary sugar (sucrose) which is also a glucose-fructose compound. However the former is made from cornstarch and has a completely different structure, and properties, to that of the sucrose, it   s ratio of glucose: fructose is 45:55 whereas sucrose is a 50:50 ratio. In short, the sugar added to baked beans is commonly described as HFCS (High-fructose corn syrup) an unnatural, man-made sugar substitute, cheaper to produce and use than sucrose extracted from sugar cane and beet.Recent research into HFCS suggests that it enhances the appetite, significantly contributes to obesity and increases the deposition of fat around vital organs in the body. This sweetener is also found in a multitude of other foodstuffs. Ketchup, Yogurts, soft drinks, to name but a few. I have added this extra bit of info here because I thought it the perfect place to increase public awareness of the uses of unnatural sugars being added to our food and that some manufacturers are hiding the facts in the name of economy at the expense of health.Hats off to Tesco though, for honestly describing their sugar content as    glucose -fructose syrup.   Heinz, incidentally disguise the fact that they use HFCS by listing their sweetening ingredient as    sugars.    Frightening, is it not?Back to Tesco value baked beans.All that is required to make a perfectly balanced snack then is a saucepan, or microwave, one tin opener and a toaster. Real butter or butter substitute, and of course a tin of baked beans.The beans, as everyone knows are already cooked (hence the name - baked beans - and so they can be eaten straight from the tin. However I wouldn t advise that, the edge of the can is extremely sharp and might catch your knuckles as you delve for the last bean.To make a warm snack, empty the baked beans into the saucepan and heat to a temperature that suits. Some prefer them warm, others - hot.  Make and liberally butter some toast, pour the beans over the toast and tuck in - Simple.Although it is recommended that the beans are not brought to the boil, I tend to ignore that bit of advice, in the name of comfort, because it is my belief that, by bringing the beans just to the boil, it does     putting it as delicately as possible - eliminate the    Flatulence-factor.      Either that or my digestive system is better than most.I find the taste of microwaved baked beans not as good as those heated in a saucepan, probably because I tend to overheat them in the microwave.If not all the contents can be used after opening the tin, the remainder should be transferred to a dish, covered and refrigerated.For anyone interested in the approximate calorific value of a typical beans on toast snack: The calorific value of half the contents (210g) is 105 calories. Two slices of bread would be approximately another 200 calories, plus about 100 calories for the butter, depending on which butter and how much is used.My opinionI admire Tesco   s deceptively honest description of the ingredients in their Value Baked beans.I have not yet found a cheaper tin of baked beans, but my feeling is that you do get what you pay for. 29p is good value, but, when comparing it with other brands, the tomato paste was more watery, and a tad too salty for my liking.For the purpose of this review, I have splashed out on a small tin of Heinz baked beans to demonstrate the difference in colour of the sauces the vast difference in the amount of liquid in each.In the Tesco Value beans the calorific value per 100g is on 45 Kcal. In the well-known brands it is around 79 Kcal per 100g. Tesco do sell better quality tins of baked beans, similar in quality and price to that of other brands.The Taste testWith the Tesco Value beans the taste of  paprika in the sauce was very dominant.Perhaps this was because the balance of sauce and beans was a little too uneven and the sauce flavour overpowered the beans.In conclusion then, The Tesco Value baked beans are lower in price, calories and quality, higher in liquid content. The taste is ok, but not as good as Heinz I have to say.     ', '    Tesco Value Baked Beans in Tomato SauceOver the past number of years we have tried many Tesco Value products and have found it to be a bit of a hit and miss process. Whilst some of the value products certainly are great value, others fall into the category of    you get what you pay for   . Luckily, though, even if a Tesco product turns out terrible, you never break the bank as all the value range are really low priced with some products coming in at only a few pence. This particular product; Tesco Value Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce, comes in at only    0.29p for a 420g tin, so again, the bank has not been broken. *****************VALUE BEANS*****************One of the facts which always stand out with value products is the packaging. These value products are always very noticeable by the plain white packaging with blues and reds in the corner. Recently, Tesco have changed the packaging on many products to hide the fact that they are the value items, and have made them a little bit more colourful, though to be honest, they still look very plain compared to other products of the more expensive range, though in my opinion in a lot of products, you pay over the odds for the packaging. With the value items, you pay for the contents and at such a low price, does it really matter so much that the packaging will not be winning any artistic awards? It has the necessary information on the tin with a large image of the beans inside, (though slightly misleading as it looks nothing like the actual product), and as far as I am concerned, this is all that is needed. What is important is the contents. So the question is; Are the contents as cheap as the price and packaging, or are they great value for money?Firstly, as expected, the tin has not come into the modern day and therefore does not have the easy to open ring-pull mechanism so it is back to the tin openers with this can of beans. Once opened, though, you are ready to go. Unlike some cans of baked beans which have thousands of ingredients, this can only has the bare minimum;Haricot Beans (44 ), Tomato Pur   e (26 ) ,Water ,Sugar ,Modified Maize Starch ,Glucose ,Salt ,Fructose ,Flavouring ,Onion Powder ,Paprika ,Vegetable Oil.And the Nutritional information is (per 100g);Fat = 0.4gSaturates = traceFibre =3.6gSodium* = 0.3g*Salt Equivalent 0.8gAnd now with the formalities out of the way, it is time for the real test *******************TESTING TESTING*******************The very first thing I noticed with this product when tipping it all into the bowl is the sheer amount of sauce. Not only were the beans drowned in sauce, the sauce was also very thin compared to brands such as Heinz. It was also very light in colour which mirrored the actual colour of the beans themselves. This did not change when heated up, either. If anything, the sauce became even thinner and the beans even lighter, though there were still a substantial amount of beans in the tin. It was not filled to the brim with beans as there was no room after all the sauce, though I half expected only half a tin of value beans and so was pleasantly surprised. There was enough to cover about two people for a side helping of beans with a meal or for lunch on toast. I doubt very much that it would stretch very well to more than two people, though. The beans were also a decent size, if a little smaller than other brands though barely noticeable.  Although the appearance of the beans is nothing to shout out about, the aroma is completely different. It is much more of a fuller flavoured aroma and you could be forgiven into thinking that this tin of beans was in fact a more expensive brand where the smell is concerned. And now for the most important test. The taste test  There is no point having a lovely smell if the taste does not match up to it, so does the taste exceed all expectations? Well, not really, though it is not terrible either. The beans themselves were quite soft, though perhaps a little harder than a Heinz branded tin. There was no need for a large amount of chewing, though I did find that the texture was a little abrasive on the tongue. This in itself put me off of these to begin with, although my husband found them absolutely fine. He had also added some spices to the sauce to enhance the flavour, and when I tried his, I found that with the added spice, the beans started to take on a new meaning. Without the added spice, the beans were a little bland. The tomato flavouring was very weak and had more of a watery taste and texture to it. By adding the spices, it gave the sauce something extra and tasted lovely (I believe it was some kind of barbeque seasoning my husband used if you wanted to try this ). I thought that the beans would be more salty as it does have a high amount of salt in the tin, though this is one thing I was happy about as I could not taste any salt there which shouldn   t be. The sheer amount of sauce does create a little bit of a problem when eating such meals as beans on toast, or even just as a side on a main meal, as the juice soaks right through the toast making it soggy, or runs right off of the plate. The beans are big enough, however, to sieve any unwanted juice though I would recommend doing this after you have heated the beans up as we did this before hand and the bland flavour got even blander without the sauce. It may be a thin, nearly tasteless sauce, though obviously the small amount of flavour is in the sauce so without it you might as well eat plain beans which come out harder without the sauce. *******************FINAL WORDS*******************It is difficult not to compare this products with the more expensive brands such as Heinz as when I was eating the beans, all I kept thinking was    I wish I had bought the Heinz tin   . As mentioned at the beginning of this review, buying Tesco Value products is very hit and miss, and in my opinion, this particular product is definitely a miss. The taste is very bland, and the beans are slightly harder than Heinz brands and the excess of sauce is really a waste (if you can call it a waste at this low price?). The scent and the price are the redeeming factors to this product, though in my opinion, this really isn   t enough. Yes, at    0.29p the bank certainly isn   t broken and there is a lack of products that fall in this price range, though personally I would rather spend that little bit more and enjoy a much fuller Baked Bean experience  Sorry, Tesco, but this Value item just does not live up to scratch        ', '           Tesco Value Baked Beans In Tomato Sauce I like baked beans, I always have, especially with a full English which I enjoy now and again. Unfortunately my wife can t stand them so as a result we did not eat them very often until Heinz recently started selling them in mini plastic tubs, I bought a pack of four of these and she can now pop one in the microwave when we have a full English and there is just enough for one person. I occasionally like beans on toast for my lunch but have always had Heinz until yesterday, I must have mentioned to Karen, my wife, that the product of the week was Tesco value beans so she had picked a tin up specially, oh so sad  Packaging The Tesco value packaging has come on a bit in recent years, what was once a very dull and bland red, white and blue label is now, well, red, white and blue predominantly however there is at least a picture of some beans in the background now. The front of the tin has the Tesco value logo at the top, the name of the tin contents, in this case baked beans in tomato sauce, across the middle and the main nutritional information across the bottom, which I think is a very good idea and should maybe be adopted by a few other food makers. This information is all on a background of baked beans as mentioned previously. There are also a couple of graphics at the top of the tin stating great taste (a matter of opinion) and new recipe. It also states the weight of the contents (420g) and then further around the tin are the ingredients and nutritional information etc.. well enough      ', '    Tesco Value baked Beans used to be used as a loss leader, meaning they would be sold at a lot less than cost in order to entice you into the store where you would then spend lots of pennies on other goods which might be higher priced than in Asda or Sainsburys.When I first started buying these they were sold for literally pennies, sometimes as low as 3p or 4p and I used to buy a minimum of 12 cans at a time.I m not a fan of beans in general so I tend to use these to bulk out other foods such as casserole, curry, bolognaise and so on when I m a bit short of meat, and in those kind of situations they re really good, the sauce is quite mild so you can add a bit of seasoning and stock to get a reasonable dish and the beans taste of whatever you ve cooked them in.I know a lot of people, students especially, stereotypically live on a diet of beans on toast, and if money is tight, these beans are still good value at 29p. However, if you want them to taste like Heinz you need to be aware of a few tricks.Firstly, the sauce is a lot more watery than Heinz, so when you heat them up, don t do it in the microwave, instead tip the whole can into a frying pan and let it simmer for a few minutes to thicken up the sauce. This also tend to soften the beans slightly as they seem a bit undercooked if you eat them raw, whereas Heinz ones can just be spooned straight out of the can.Secondly, you need to add a little flavouring to the beans, a dash of Worcestershire sauce is always good, with a pinch of salt and a very small sprinkle of sugar. You can also use a little soy sauce but be careful it diesn t get too salty.You will now have transformed your cheap, nasty, value beans into something more reminiscent of a  premium  brand but  at half the cost.Overall, these beans are nothing special but they are very versatile. You can use them to bulk out a less substantial meal and with a bit of creativity you can get them tasting yummy as well.If, however, you just want something you can eat out of the can then go straight to Heinz, do not pass go, do not collect    200.     ', '    This product,  Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce  is sold by  Tesco  in their  Value  range.TasteThe taste of baked beans happens to be one of my favourites, particularly the partially viscous sauce. The beans are soft and easy to chew and go hand in hand with quite practically any meal, especially toast, in my experience. Perhaps the best thing about these beans is the juice, it is delicious and it is one of the few food leftovers that I will actually attempt to mop up with a piece of bread. That s rare for me, so if that s not saying that it s tasty, I don t know what will.However, the taste is almost comparable to the Heinz Baked Beans, but alas, not quite. I still think that there is a definitive taste to Heinz, perhaps I am just being biased towards the bigger company, but there s something about their sauce and the textures of their beans that really beat any competitor for the production of beans. However, even though I d quite happily snatch your rather expensive can of Heinz Baked Beans off of you, I can still happily sit down with these on my plate and still find myself frantically clawing at the remaining sauce with a tasty slice of thick, white bread.The taste isn t quite comparable to the taste of Heinz Baked Beans, but it s pretty darned close.SmellThe smell of Baked Beans is always pleasant. At least it is for me, if you hate the things than it is probably the smell of dread. For me, the smell of these beans is great, it s a slow moving smell which I can only define as the  baked bean  smell. There has yet to be a comparable smell, and this can of baked beans is most certainly no different. It s lovely, and you know it s lovely when you get to a point where you can almost taste it on the tip of your tongue just by smelling it s cooking odour. The smell of Baked Beans is one of the best smells around, and these particular Baked Beans are most certainly no different.PackagingPlain and simple is how Tesco Value rolls, it is just a can with a piece of paper wrapped around it. Albeit there is nothing too fancy about the beans that would require extravagant, floating strips of ribbon with bright, illuminating lights on them and a speaker that announces the name of the product to you as you approach. However, it would be nice if they handled the packaging with a little bit more care, I often found that some of the Baked Beans on the stand where damaged, bruised and dented. It s not something I ve come to expect from food, and it certainly doesn t help Tescos image, still, it s cheap and it s cheerful, so I can t complain over a small mishap.Product QualityHere I go, about to compare the product to Heinz Baked Beans yet again. The taste can only hope to reach the quality of the Heinz Baked Beans, as the sauce doesn t have quite the right viscosity to it for it to have the same self-indulgent, succulent taste to it. The smell is just like any other can of baked bean, brilliant and soothing and the quality of packaging just a little below average, with a few bumps, dents and bruises, but that doesn t affect the quality of the all-important taste too much. As a competitor against Heinz Baked Beans, this is almost an effective competitor. I still prefer Heinz though.Value for MoneyThis is Tesco Value, they will offer you a product similar to the Heinz Brand for a price as cheap as    1 or less. It s fantastic really, because there is very little that is heavily flawed about these baked beans, and so it is always a financial positive to have these in your basket instead of Heinz. You could find that they don t give the sensation to your taste buds that Heinz do, but for the money that you are paying, it is most certainly worth it. The price of the can and the contents must have been really cheap, because if it wasn t, I don t understand how they re not paying you to take them.In conclusion, I d always take Heinz instead of Tesco Value Baked Beans, but the Tesco Value Baked Beans are certainly better in price, even if not in style. I d highly recommend these beans to anyone who needs a little bit of a cheap price tag, but, like me, still loves their baked beans. A good alternative to Heinz, but the taste and packaging departments could still do slightly better. Still, it s better than nothing. I give this product a total of four out of a possible five stars.     ']

If you’re weighing up Tesco Value Baked Beans in Tomato Sauce against pricier brands like Heinz, here’s a balanced take that might help you decide—especially if you’re budget-conscious but still care about taste and nutrition.

First off, Tesco’s beans offer solid value for money. They’re significantly cheaper than Heinz, making them a handy cupboard staple for families or anyone watching their spending. The beans themselves have a creamy texture—not too mushy, not too firm—which works well in stews or casseroles. However, if you’re planning to enjoy them solo or on toast, be warned: the sauce tends to be thinner and runnier than Heinz’s, which some find less satisfying.

Taste-wise, opinions split. Some find Tesco’s beans just as tasty and richly colored as Heinz, even noting a more intense tomato flavor compared to beans from other countries. Others feel they fall short in quality and flavor depth, with smaller beans and a thinner sauce that can feel watery. So, if you’re nostalgic for that classic Heinz experience, Tesco might not fully hit the mark.

On the health front, Tesco has made strides by cutting salt content by 50%, though some still find the salt and sugar levels a bit high. The inclusion of glucose-fructose syrup (high-fructose corn syrup) as a sweetener raises eyebrows for those mindful of added sugars. That said, these beans remain a good source of fiber and count as one of your five-a-day, which is a nice nutritional bonus.

Packaging is straightforward but clear, with easy-to-read nutritional info—always a plus for the detail-oriented shopper. Overall, Tesco Value Baked Beans are a practical, budget-friendly option that won’t break the bank, especially if you’re flexible about sauce consistency and don’t mind a sweeter edge. Just don’t expect a gourmet upgrade from your usual Heinz toast topping!

product_reviews: ['    Bought my Gameboy Advance yesterday from a specialist shop in Cleveleys and I am not in any way dissappointed. I was worried about the battery life - well it has been going for 20 hours and the light is only just showing red (it warns you when it has only a few hours left by changing colour) it weighs just enougth but not too much and just smells of good nintendo design.I got the mario game and f-zero, and agin was worried that I had forked out for a handheld Snes, not such a bad thing but hardly cutting edge. No worries here either, both games are absolutely top notch and look better than their older counterparts. Mario advance is a bit of a rehash, with bits from all the mario games stuck in , but it plays well, is colourful and has that Wow factor even now after continued play.F-Zero has to be seen to be beleived, just stop reading this and go buy one        ', '    After reading ciao opinions on the Game boy advance, I decided that I got to have one. It was a big step up from the game boy original I had nearly five years ago. The release date was last Friday (I believe), and I began to check out prices a few days earlier. Woolworth  8217;s were selling theirs at    89.99, which was the same price for a fair few Internet companies. I then tried a price comparison site and was awarded with a few companies offering it for    79.99; I chose to buy it from BOL. Within two days of ordering, there was a knock on the door. Upon opening, the postman handed me a small well-packaged box. I guessed what it was, so immediately ripped into the packaging, and saw the inside box. Opening the box revealed-my new white game boy advance. I was surprised that it included batteries, but alas no new games for me to try. Never the less, I had some old games, which I got with my original game boy, so went to hunt those out.Now for those of you who are technically minded here are some of the specifications for the console:     CPU - 32-Bit ARM with embedded memory     Memory - 32 Kbytes + 96 Kbytes VRAM (in CPU), 256 Kbytes WRAM (external of CPU)     Screen - 2.9 quot; TFT reflective screen 240x160 resolution 40.8mm x 61.2mm screen size 32,768 possible colours 511 simultaneous colours in character mode; 32,768 simultaneous colours in bitmap mode     Size - Width 144.5mm Depth 24.5mm Height 24.5mm     Weight - 140g     Batteries - 2 AA batteries     Battery life - 15 hours     Cartridges - Cartridge format Game Boy and Game Boy Colour compatibleNow if that hasn  8217;t interested you, then you  8217;re with me  8230;basically apart from the battery life etc, it means nothing to me.So what differences are there between this and the old game boy I had? Well there are a few. Firstly, the appearance of the console is totally different. It is lighter and smaller than the game boy original. The screen is bigger. It also has the L and R buttons that are familiar to the Nintendo 64 console.  You can link up with other consoles to play with other people. You even have the option of obtaining an adaptor so you play on electric rather than batteries (although the company insist on you buying their adaptor). You can also get accessories for it, including: Communication cable and game boy printer (thought I quite can  8217;t understand yet why you would actually want a printer).You can change the screen colours on the original game boy cartridges, for example by pressing up it will change it to brown, while up and a will make the screen colour red. This is quite entertaining, but bear in mind that you need to press the said buttons when the screen is loading.By pressing the L button while playing, the screen is enlarged to the biggest it can, while pressing R can bring it back to the smaller size. The screen is a bit clearer on my original game boy games than it was on the original, however I can  8217;t comment on the colour games. So is it worth the change? Well, I am glad I did   8211; but to be honest the change is not worth it if you are happy with your old system (although it does obviously have advantages). So why did I change? Simple I treated myself before I go into hospital for some operations (even though this might be a while off), and I had a spare amount of cash to buy it with. As with all the game systems there is a small chance that it may bring on a fit. The company reckon this to be 1 in 4000.  I have just bought some new games for the advanced game boy. And they are really something else, the clarity of the view screen is brilliant. That said though Nintendo gameboy advance still has the similar darkened screen to its predicessors. However, with the right games (which I think at present are limited) it was a great swap.     ', '    As with all consoles, they become outdated, I wonder how long the GBA will last.  The original GB (yes the big bulky white brick) lasted for 10 years and I still see people playing on them.  The GBP probaly was the most shortlived because of the arrival of the GBC.  Now that the GBA has arrived on the scene, coupled with its compatibility to play both original GB and GBC games as well as playing the new small GBA carts, they will be no need to purchase a old Game Boy console.  Price cuts on older machines to clear stock has already commenced.With the foreword out the way lets focus on the star of the show.  The GBA is technologically the most advanced heldheld console in the world, outshining even the 32-bit golden oldies such as the Mega Drive and the mighty SNES.  First the price point, very reasonable, in the UK it should be easily found for    80 or less.  My model is the Japanese one for which I paid just over    60.The games are very overpriced in the UK.  New games are    35-   30, this is ridiculous as the same money could buy 3 DC games   I know that the cartridges are expensive to produce but still they are too overpriced.The console itself is very well made.  They are available in a variety of colours, a clear violet, pink, white and purple.  More are schelduled and some are already out in the land of the rising sun, the variations being different coloured buttons.  The screen gives a high resolution crisp colour display.  One fault of the screen is that it is too dark and needs to be played in well lit areas.  This could have been sorted out with a backlight option.The next fault are the button arrangements. they are simply too compacted and those with big hands will struggle to control both the shoulder and normal controls at once.The games of present are great, with Mario Kart Advance and Final Fight One leading the way, the future looks bright, the future looks orange. Oops wrong product One question just to ponder, how long will the GBA last before the next toy is released.     ', '    Way back in 1989 the world saw the release of the biggest computer console in history. It was not however a home console but one that you could hold in your hand.....The Game Boy. Since then this little gem as gone on to sell about 110,000,000 units with the help of updates such as the Game Boy Pocket and the Game Boy Colour and games such as  Tetris  and the recent phenomenon that is  Pokemon . What s more the Gameboy managed to achieve its success with less than impressive graphics. So now, 12 years later, we are about to get the sequel to the Gameboy, The Gameboy Advance.     Already released in Japan, where in a matter of weeks it has sold very well, the Gameboy Advance features 32  bit  gaphics and capabilities of producing effects considerably better than Nintendo s home console  The SNES . It is also backwards compatible with all  Gameboy  and  Gameboy Colour  games giving users already 1000+ games to choose from.    Its size is about that of the  Gameboy colour  but its design is quite different. Instead of being help upright like the original it is help horizontally. It features all the same buttons as the first gameboy but also with the introduction of left and right shoulder buttons that make conversions of classic SNES games a reality. There s also a difference in the screen sizes with the Gameboy Advance having a screen 1.5 times the size of the Gameboy colour.    There are already several high quality games on the release list of the Gameboy Advance including a super Mario Bros. game and F-Zero-X due for release on the day of the GBA s release, due sometime this summer. However the game everyone is really looking forward to is Super Mario Kart Advance. it promises to be an improvement on Super Mario Kart for the SNES which many consider to be the best game on that system.    Although all the signs point to the Gameboy Advance being a classic only time will tell if it meets with the expectations of the gaming community. It is however an almost sure fire big seller as it will attract the massive user base of the GameBoy original plus many new gamers. I for one can t wait.         ', '    I knew my wife had been after a Nintendo Gameboy Advance for quite a while so I got her one as an anniversary present - and guess what? I can t stop playing the damn thing now    It s not the newest handheld games machine on the market by any means, but even today it s not too shabby. I m not going to bore you with technical details however as they re largely irrelevant (I could tell you that it uses a 32-bit RISC processor but how many people would know that RISC stood for  quot;Reduced Instruction Set Chip quot;, or that it was first used in the Acorn Archimedes    and even then, how many people would really care? ?). What I will do is give you a pros and cons list, which I think will be far more helpful. (If you really must have the technical specs. Visit http://www.nintendo.com/techspecgba.) Pros Readily available and cheap, I saw it on Amazon for about ?65 new, though availability of the GBA new will no doubt reduce as Nintendo try to promote their newer models. I got mine (er    my wife s, I mean    of course   ) second hand for ?60 including 3 games (Mario Kart Super Circuit, Road to Westlemania - well it was thrown in for free, I didn t actually want it - and the Gameboy Colour version of Super Mario Bros). Which leads me to another two pros    1 - Backward compatibility - if you have a load of Gameboy / Gameboy colour games already you don t need to throw them away - you can still play them on GBA. They won t be enhanced in any way of course but you can still play them. 2 - There s a thriving second-hand game market out there for GBA, which is just as well since new games range from about ?15-?35, which I think is a bit steep for a handheld game. Multiplayer option - up to 4 GBAs can be connected. Massive selection of games available, first or second hand. Proven technology that works and has had the bugs fixed. Decent control system (I found the extra buttons on top a little fiddly to use but otherwise it s quite intuitive.) Surprisingly good battery life (quoted in the manual as 10 hours for a rechargeable battery but we tried it on a normal AA battery - it takes 2 - and got about 20 hours life out of it). Cons Not exactly the cutting edge of technology these days. You have to get the GBA in exactly the right position to be able to see the screen properly. Some of the games will of course be rather rudimentary by today s standards. Sooner or later companies will stop developing new games for it. You can t plug it into the mains. ', '    I thought it was about time I put my newly acquired gadget down and write an op on it   So here are my views on the great little device from Nintendo:~Memory Lane~During the last decade many large gaming companies such as Sega, Atari and Neo Geo have contributed their feeble attempts to the market, failing miserably in one way or the other.  The Atari Lynx was the successor many years ago, but faded away due to it   s small range of games and low battery life.  The Sega Game Gear was to follow, with it   s vast range of titles, but soon died a slow death over the years, due to it   s poor    Master System    processor, which couldn   t cope with the ever-increasing progress of technology.  Then came Neo Geo Handheld, which appeared on the shelves a couple of years back, then disappeared almost straight afterwards, due to a lack in interest from  software developers.  In the year of 1999 the Nintendo Gameboy Advance was born and introduced to the UK, boasting a 32 Mb processor. With a vast array of titles and support for their older Gameboy systems, the GBA was sure to stay and has done so till today, where it still remains the most powerful handheld games console to date, selling over 110 million systems. ~Packaging~The GBA sits snugly in it   s small laminated box, which measures approximately twice the size of the GBA in terms of mass.  The front of the box shows an angled view of the system, with the word    Gameboy    shown on the screen in an un-realistic way.  The picture is displayed an attempt to convince people that the screen is well lit - this is not the case, as the GBA system DOES NOT feature an internal light   The colour of the GBA corresponds to the colour of the system contained within the box to prevent confusion.  The reverse of the box describes the features of the system in three different languages as well as a small picture showing the connectivity possibilities with the Nintendo Gamecube system.On opening the box you will find a warning and maintenance information sheet and 2 instruction booklets - each one covering various languages.  An additional sheet is included in the box displaying a small range of games available for the GBA besides screen shots of each game.  The reverse of the leaflet show the possibilities of the GBA Link Cable.~Gameboy Advance Design~The main difference between the GBA and standard Gameboy / Gameboy Colour, besides the 32 Bit capabilities, is the horizontal orientation.  The large 2.9 inch TFT colour LCD screen lies prominently in the centre of the unit, which boasts a 50  increase in size in comparison the older Gameboy system.  The direction pad, start button and select button to the left of the screen. The    A         B    buttons, speaker and power light are located at the right of the screen, with    Left    and    Right    shoulder buttons at the top of the unit.  The shoulder buttons adopt the same principle as console game pads, which adds more flexibility to game play, especially in the case of driving games, such as F-zero.  The extension port and accessory fixation slots also reside at the top of the unit, with the volume dial, headphone jack and power switch located at the bottom of the console.  The extension port is used to connect up to 4 GBA   s together for multi player gaming and the accessory fixation slots are used to attach such things as (much needed) lights and screen magnifiers. Weighing 140g the GBA unit measures 135mm in width, 80mm in height and 25mm in depth.  Unlike many other handheld consoles the GBA has a sturdy feel, which feels solid whilst held in the hand - peace of mind if you happen to be a little clumsy  The console adopts the classic square handheld device shape, which happens to look better, rather than    feel    better. I have found after prolonged gaming, my fingers begin to ache and the    pins and needles    feeling sets in soon after, forcing me to put the console down.  It   s times like this I yearn for the comfortable feel of a Sony Playstation or Megadrive game pad with a screen in the middle   The unit may feel more comfortable to those with smaller hands, such as children which the console is generally aimed towards.  Fortunately this problem can be overcome by the attachment of the    hand grip    accessories, which fit on either side of the GBA, giving it a more bulky feel.The 240 by 160 pixel (38,000 pixels) screen is capable of displaying 32,768 colours simultaneously.  To put this into more basic terms, the quality of the picture is that of a high definition television   The original Gameboy fails miserably in comparison to the GBA.  No longer do we have to put up with blurred dots in high speed games, as the GBA handles graphics in a crisp, fluent manner.  As mentioned earlier the screen does not incorporate a light, which incidentally happens to be the systems biggest drawback.  Without the assistance of an external light/magnifier accessory or internal  quot;afterburner quot; light, it is rather difficult to see the screen in all it   s glory.  Even under a bright light the GBA must be aimed at the correct angle to obtain full viewing capabilities.  If you intend to play your GBA at night or in dim light, it   s really essential that you purchase this accessory. Personally I think Nintendo should have though twice before releasing this console without a light.  The main reason for the system   s non-existent light is battery consumption, but in my opinion I   d rather sacrifice a couple of hours battery life for improved screen viewing, and after all, most GBA owners use a re-chargeable battery pack.There are many GBA colours available including: clear, clear blue, clear pink, purple, black and platinum, as well as many other snazzy designs from companies on the Internet.  Whatever your choice of colour, you are sure to find accessories in the same colour to match your console.~Music to the Ears~The GBA offers 4 channels of crisp quality sound through it   s built in speaker.  The quality of sound is excellent in comparison to the older Gameboy systems.  Instead of various pitches of    beeps    our ears are now greeted with fully fledged music and speech.  Classic games such as Street Fighter 2 let out the cries and chants from players when executing special moves, much like original arcade version and most football games feature live commentary, adding extra realism to the games.  Though the sound quality of the GBA is very impressive, the system only features one speaker, which gives you monaural sound and the volume is rather low, even when turned up to maximum.  To get the most from the GBA sound system, it is advisable to purchase some quality headphones to enjoy the full aural experience.~Game overview~There are literally hundreds of games available for the GBA, from puzzle games to beat em    up   s.  Many classic games such as Mario Kart and Mario World have been re-vamped to take full advantage of the GBA   s capabilities.  The overall quality of the games is truly amazing - quality which is not expected to that of a handheld gaming device.  In the case of the original Gameboy, the games were usually played    on the move    and had little lasting appeal for home play, especially when you had a TV console which provided more depth and playability. When the GBA was first launched I assumed the system was basically a handheld Super Nintendo, but boy was I wrong   In the case of the GBA you will find yourself pulled in to games which can even match the performance of games found on the Nintendo 64 system.  Boasting Mode 7 (rotation FX), multi-scrolling and superb animation, GBA games rarely fall short of  N64 quality, though a small handful of games have suffered miserably - looking less impressive than a older Super Nintendo game.  The small (and I mean small) amount of poor games usually arise from a conversion.  For example the 3D worlds of Tony Hawks Pro Skater and Dave Mirraz BMX, are slimmed down to a 2.5 scrolling landscape, as opposed to multi camera angles.  Nevertheless, some of these conversions have made their mark as great games on the GBA system.All games come in the GBA   s small cartridge form and feature a save facility, for saving your progress in long games.  The quality if the games is truly amazing, when you take the size of the cartridge into consideration.  Each cartridge measures approximately 6cm in length and 3cm in width  - now hows that for technology Games can be purchased from    15.00 to    40.00 depending on the size and age of the game.  There are some great bargains to be had at Play.com, where you will find a vast selection of GBA games at the lowest possible prices.  Other web sites may offer you reduce prices on used game as well as accessories for your GBA.  Shop around before you buy and most of all contact me and I   ll give you my short opinion on the game before your buy ~Connectivity possibilities~One great feature of the GBA is the ability to connect it to a maximum of 3 more GBA consoles for multi player gaming.  This is achieved by using the    Multi player Link    or a combination of Multi Player Links, in the case of 3 or 4 players playing a game.  The Multi Player link works via the extension port of the GBA from which information is transmitted and received between the systems.  Some games require that each player has the game cartridge plugged into their GBA for multi player, whilst other special games, require that only one person needs to own the original game cartridge, from which the game information is sent to the other players.  Though this is an excellent feature, the single cartridge multi player games, often only offer a limited amount of game usage, for example you may only race on one track in a racing game, and all players must use the same car.  Being able to do this is a great little bonus, even though the game access is limited - after all the GBA is a games console not a multi-tasking PC The future is set to release games for the GBA which work in unison with the Nintendo Gamecube (and vise-versa)  via the GBA   s extension port.  In effect the GBA works as an extra Gamecube controller from which tactics and moves can be planned on the GBA screen, out of view from the other player ~Gameboy compatibility~Owners of the original Gameboy / Gameboy Colour will be pleased to hear that the GBA supports these games too  Of course original Gameboy games are not converted to GBA colours, but you have the option to change the shades of grey to a single different colour ~Power up ~The GBA is powered by 2 AA batteries, which last approximately 15 hours, though I have powered my console for over 17 hours on the Maxell batteries which were supplied with it. For those of you who do now want to fork out the cash for new batteries every week, third-party re-chargeable battery packs are available for various companies at very low prices.  This battery can be charged via a mains adaptor at 3 volts, to provide hours of un-interrupted gaming. ~Gameboy Advance Accessories   Extras~There are many accessories available for the GBA, both from Nintendo and third party companies.  Official Nintendo accessories tend to be a little more expensive than those offered by other companies. It is important to note that if you use third party accessories with your GBA your warranty may be voided, if it is evident to Nintendo that you have used such products.I recommend the first accessories you purchase should be some form of light / magnifier, which allows you to play your GBA in dimly lit rooms or in the dark and a re-chargeable battery pack, to save on disposable battery costs. The linker also allows you to send information and save it to your PC, which is very useful for saving games. Of course the Flash Linker can only be used to make a    back-up    copy of games that you have purchased and any miss-use may be illegal  ;o)~Prices~The Gameboy Advance console can be purchased in high street shops for around    70.00, but I recommend searching various suppliers on the Internet before parting with your cash. ', '    On the 11th June 2001 the Game Boy Advance was launched in America. The console has since been releases here in the UK on the 22nd of the same month. Hype for the system is high being heralded as the   8220;Future of Portable Gaming  8221;. Anyone who has walked down a commercial area in the last week or two will know about this release   8211; if you don  8217;t now you will soon (very soon as you are reading this opinion ). Big things lie ahead for this small console   8211; but just how bright is the future for the GBA? Is the hype well deserved or somewhat miss placed? These questions are the same ones I aim to answer in the next few paragraphs.In 1989 Nintendo launches a new handheld console   8211; the original Game Boy. After 12 years of ups and downs in the life of the GB and several separate carnations the Game Boy is still there at the top of the handheld console war. Now the best selling console ever having sold over 80 million units worldwide as of 1999. The ride has not always been easy for the handheld wonder though   8211; it has been offered competition from Sega (Game Gear), Lynx, Bandai and Neo Geo. The Game Boy now takes the shape of three different incarnations: The original game boy, the Pocket Game Boy and the Game Boy Colour. Ready to meet the new member of the Game Boy family? Keep reading:The new GBA is the most powerful Game Boy ever and also, by pure coincidence, the most advanced (see the link with the name?) handheld console. The GBA has a 32-bit processor   8211; equal to that of a PlayStation. The basics have been changed this time as the GBA adapts a horizontal position rather than the more traditional vertical look. This radical change in the design of the system means that the console is easier to hold and hand cramps occur less   8211; meaning you can play longer in complete comfort. The screen is now 50  bigger than any of the previous GB and can display an impressive 32,768 colours. The screen itself measures 2.9  8221; and has a new special covering to reduce glare (we all know how useful that will be ). The buttons will be familiar to those who have owned a previous GB with Start, Select, A and B buttons all being present and correct. However, the new additions of shoulder buttons on the top of the GBA are reminiscent of Nintendo  8217;s SNES days. The whole GBA is very handheld at only 140g and is very comfortable to hold for long periods of time. 2AA batteries will last about 15 to 20 hours of game play which is very impressive considering how long the same batteries last other portable devices such as CD and MiniDisc players. The games themselves now come on cartridges that are 50  smaller than the old bulkier ones of days gone by. The sound of the console is also very impressive with digital quality sound that can only really be appreciated with headphones. The only thing that could have been included that isn  8217;t here is a backlight. However there are 2 main reasons for this exclusion, the first being it may push the price of the console up driving it away from its target audience and the power consumption of the console would look less impressive.In a nod towards other Game Boy systems and the fact that about 7  of the world population owns a GB the GBA is also backwards compatible. This means that even at launch the GBA has literally hundreds of class A games. However when playing old games the cartridge will stick out but really who cares   8211; you  8217;ve got a GBA. With new games you can use the bigger screen to your advantage with the wide screen option using the L and R shoulder buttons. I have also heard that US and Japanese games will work on UK consoles and vice versa but I am unable to confirm this at the present time.The GBA has a wide selection of brilliant games from launch including: Super Mario Advance - The classic Mario 2 from the NES, with crisper graphics and some great 4-player options. With the added bonus of the original Mario game thrown in for good measure. F-Zero Maximum Velocity   8211; An old SNES favourite speeded up and with better graphics are more options. Tony Hawk  8217;s Pro Skater 2   8211; Probably the most anticipated game. This really is the game to show off your GBA with. This version contains everything from the PS version with a few other options.Chu Chu Rocket - Yes the Dreamcast game on the GBA, it looks frantic and if you liked it on the DC you will be totally addicted again. Rayman Advance - This game looks fantastic and feels like Rayman on the PSReady to Rumble - A boxing simulator, with some stunning graphics and great game play (allegedly). GT Advance Championship Racing   8211; Always the racing game  8230; this has 32 courses and 48 cars to play with  Most of the games that have been confirmed for launch on 22nd June, but there are many more that will be arriving soon afterwards: Mario Kart, Street Fighter II, Final Fight One, X-Men, Sonic the Hedgehog, Napoleon, Golden Sun The potential of this console is very good. From launch most of the games will be ports from the SNES and why not as the SNES was possibly the best console ever created. As time passes and developers get to grips with what the GBA can do, there will be some new games that will be very unique and special. The list of developers is already very long and includes some big names such as Sega (Sonic), Activision (Tony Hawks), THQ (Smackdown ), Squaresoft (Final Fantasy) and Konami (ISS, Metal Gear Solid). The chance to play multiplayer games is now more accessible than ever. You can now link up to 4 consoles together and play multiplayer games while only requiring one game cartridge. However if you do have more than one cartridge it  8217;s worth using them as extra game options and better graphics will be present with the extra cartridge(s).At the E3 exhibition that has just finished in Los Angeles Nintendo stated their plans to let users join their GBA  8217;s to the new Next Generation console the GAMECUBE. In essence the GBA can be used as a controller, meaning that you can see things on your screen that other players won  8217;t be able to  Imagine playing games like Perfect Dark and Golden Eye and not being able to see your opponent  8217;s radar, nice  Nintendo are also working on a Mobile Telephone link to its consoles, it is questionable if this will happen anywhere outside of Japan, where calls are so cheap, but it would be great if it ever did. Do you remember the Barcode Battler? Well Nintendo are working on what is called E-Card reader. Which is probably going to be used in a new Pokemon game, in essence you get cards and scan them into the GBA with the special scanner. This will give new options and information, something to watch out for.The GBA is available is 3 different colours, these colours being indigo (purple), arctic (white) and glacier (clear blue). Clear red may also be available but, as was the case in the US, you may have to wait a little longer for this but the clear red is being advertised among the other 3 colours for the UK.Surely such a brilliant new console with so much potential will cost you?? This is the beauty of it. The retail price of the unit is    80 but certain shops have pushed their prices up to nearer    90. However, if you shop around and are wise with your money then bargains are to be had. Try EB and Dixons for bundle deals as well gameplay.com for consoles at the original    80 price tag and cheaper games (I  8217;ve heard about games going for    23ish online).The GBA is not intended to rival the PlayStation and it cant compete in terms of 3D game play etc just as the PSone can  8217;t compete for a place as a handheld console even with a screen. It is unfair to compare the GBA to a PlayStation, they are both 32-bit, but they are different consoles for different purposes   8211; one is truly handheld and the other is an adapted home console.The Game Boy Advance is truly the new must have handheld with such a bright present and an even promising looking future. 700,000 units all ready sold in Japan  8230;. But back to the British bit, now in the good old U.S.A they think that our humour is strange (well actual I think all of the world think our humour is strange), but still British Humour like The Royal Family and Alan Partridge is god DAMN FUNNY, there is no dout about it and in Worms the whole of game is based upon British humour, I mean which U.S.A game would use member s called Sponge and Spam which are quirky yet funny. But the concept of blowing up worms doesn t seem funny but sick and a little twisted but this game is just laughter all the way with the extremely funny cut scene s and the intro where a worn gets suited up to the teeth with weapons and then falls over and everything goes starts to fire (Looks better than me explaining it). If you haven t played Worms then the best out of the series is Worms united because it doesn t go as far as the next two in the series and is just that tiny bit better than the original, with more things to do in single player mode. It is not just a game it is British humour in a game       Long live worms     ', '    I bought Crazy taxi when i first bought my playstation 2 on boxing day 2001.  The game came as part of a package along with gran turismo, since them i have played on my ps2 everyday since i bought it and can honestly say it was the best 250 pounds i have ever spend.  However it moght have been the best 250 poungds spent but the crazy taxi has got to be the biggest mistake of my life , as it is really boring and restricting.  You only have a choice of 2 diffrent options of original and arcade of which you can work for 3 minutes,  five minutes or ten minutes. and there is also a mini game section where you can complete some small missions, for example collect 5 passengers and take them to there chosen location.  after you have completed the mini games there is nothing else that you can do with this game except repeat what you have alreay done.  There are no new cars to be won on completing any of the missions and there are no new drivers that you can win.Overall this game is weak and has no incentive for anyone to want to buy the game never mind want to complete it.  I have recently found out that it was original written for the dreamcast which we all know was a complete flop for sega and so was the game.     ', '    This is an excellent RPG probably the best I ve seen (actually the first ) I grew very atached to this game. Though the game can take absolutly ages to complete the longer u spend on it the more exciting it gets with secret items and equipment to use.I liked how the scenery was set out. These cut scenes deliver vital information about the game and its storyline e.g. Clouds past.Anyhow a brilliant game and I highly recommend it to anybody especially RPG fans    (No doubt though they have already bought a copy)Bye Bye        ', '    This game is an oversized robot game it isn t really very good.  The  Mechs  are o.k. but to be really honest the story line isn t very god.The game is hosted on 4 worlds but when easily passing though the levels at brake neck pace you don t even know which world you are on. Of course there are different terrains but they range from the extreme snow to the grasslands of somewhere forgotton.The battleing is o.k. and at times fun but customising your  Mech  can be really faffy  and time consuming.This game is o.k. and very addictive but this game is only for hardcore fans (not me )     ', '    Moto GP had a high standards to live up to coming from the Namco school of gaming wizardry. With Ridge Racer V coming out nearly a year before moto gp this is practically a second generation PS2 game. It is as anyone who has played the game will tell you very realistic. If you want a decent racing game then wait for the likes of Gran Turismo 3 A-Spec to arrive in the UK at the end of June.     ', '    It s standard procedure these days for follow-ups in series such as Test Drive to simply bring back pretty much the same game just with some updated graphics. Unfortunately, version 6 of this series doesn t buck the trend, and this is no better than Test Drive 5 or 4 or so on - it just looks a little (and not much ) better. You buy yourself a car and take part in races, to earn money to upgrade or replace your car. That s the first point, all the races are one-off and the system lacks any real ambition for the player. The cars don t take damage, so not much braking goes on, and the game is made even more unrealistic when you consider the very poor collision detection engine and the poor physics and handling. The developers still haven t decided to put multiplayer options on either, which seems a very strange decision to me considering the current popularity of such games. You will only really enjoy this game if you just want something you can get into easily, with not much depth.     ', '    The computer version of ITV s Who Wants To Be A Millionare? it comes complete with all the features of the Tv version, 50:50, Phone a friend and ask the audience, and the music as well. Oh before I forget you also get Chris Tarrant. but after a while you just want to get on with answering the questions but there is no way to stop him speaking and you have to go through it all every game. apart from this it is an exellent game and one that i highly recomend you buy. the game has a high score table so you prove to any doubters that you did infact get the million pound question. I have made it to the    500,000 question but then got the million pounder WRONG  oh well at least it wasnt real money.the game cost me    20 when it was released but now should be less as they have bought out a WWTBAM2.     ', '    The gameboy advance has definately advanced on its predessors, gameboy   gameboy colour, but I am not convinced that Nintendo have put very much effort into making it a handheld console which has no comparison. The games are good, with probably the best selection on the market, and there s the added bonus that games from the previous models are playable also. However, I had to ask myself the question after I first bought it,  quot;How hard is it to illuminate the screen? quot;. If you think back to the sega handheld, with its  sonic the hedgehog  and  shinobi  etc. and remember that you could play away in a dark cupboard if you wanted to, you must wonder, why haven t Nintendo done the same to their screen?Nintendo s solution to their have hearted efforts....Game lights which are even more useless.To make matters worse for Nintendo, there is a service on the internet, which can actually amend this problem by inserting internal lighting without changing the design of the gameboy. Now, why didn t Nintendo do that???To be honest, the gameboy advance is the best handheld on the market, and if you are determined to buy one, then this is probably it. Not because of its design however, because of its games. I was disappointed with their meagre efforts to  advance  the gameboy, and would personally prefer a sega handheld if only they had more games.      ', '         This is the best damn protable game console that any company has ever created.  Now, before you buy your gameboy advance you must get it from WHSmiths      In WHSmiths the gameboy advance will cost you    79.99 as oppossed to    89.99   Most shops, no sorry ALL shops will charge you    89.99.The gameboy advance console is like a playstation controller, with a screen.  It has a a   b button as has all of the original gameboys.  It also has a start and select button aswell as the direction key pad.  It has two new buttons L1   R1.  L1 changes the camera view   I havent a clue what R1 does     The screen is 50  bigger that the original gameboys and it has 32 Bit graphics.  This is just a great console and I hope you enjoy it as much as i do.The advantages of this great conosle are;.The graphics.Sleek design.Not too expensive. Small.Battery powered.Loads of accessoriesThe disadvantages of this great console are;.NOTHING     ', '    So this game has some of the well known Nintendo charactes smashing the hell out of  each other. What better could have Nintendo thought of. Best of all you get to kick that Annoying little plumber (Mario) into oblivion or maybe even Pikachu There are 8 characters in total and 4 secret ones which can be unlocked by doing certain tasks. Each character has their own set of special moves. Instead of a health bar like other fighting games, characters have a damage meter, the higher the reading on the damage meter, the easier it is to knock your opponent off. But dont forget to defend against your opponents attacks, or you may get knocked off yourself  There are also 8 stages to fight on with 20 items. My favourite item is the hammer because one hit and, your opponent is off the stage. Bye bye  I will now name each 8 character and their moves, but not the 4 secret characters I m afraid.MARIO:B - Fire ballB and up - super jump punch B and down - mario tornadoD.K:B - giant punchB and up - spinning kongB and down - hand slap SAMUS:B - charge shotB and up - screw attackB and down - bombFOX:B - blaster shotB and up - fire foxB and down - reflectorPIKACHU:B - thunder joltB and up - quick attackB and down - reflectorLINK:B - bomberangB and up - spin attackB and down - bombKIRBY:B - swallowB and up - final cutterB and down - stoneYOSHI:B - egg layB and up - egg throwB and down - ground poundI recommend this game to anyone who owns a Nintendo64 as the game has a wide range of Nintendo characters.     ', '    Overall an excellent, intelligent film with good performances. The other reviews have concentrated on the opening sequence which is nice but a bit obvious visually - but the sound tracking back through time and eventually switching off is a great touch). But the virtuoso performance technically has to be the scene with the young girl running for the medicine cabinet - an apparently innocuous scene but watch it again and try to figure out how they could have done it - the whole scene appears to have been shot through a mirror which is fixed to the bathroom wall, yet starts downstairs and travels upstairs and into the bathroom in one continuous shot. It s a shot Hitchcock would have been proud of and it s always good to see a commercial director showing that he still has some artistic sensibilities and can do more than paint by the numbers.Sometimes the ethical elements of the plot are laid on with a trowel, and John Hurt is far too hammy and out of place from the general atmosphere of the film to be anything other than an annoyance but Jodie Foster gives a strong central performance and the movie hangs together nicely by the end. The arguments about spirituality against science are somewhat contrived but that does little to detract from a genuinely uplifting and inspiring story. Great to see a piece of science fiction that actually treats its viewers as intelligent human beings who can perhaps understand a plot that goes beyond boy rescuing Californian beach volleyball princess from evil emperor while retrieving mysterious plastic crystal and saving the world. Watch it, and restore your faith in earthlings.      ', '    I first bought the original gameboy in 1993 for my birthday and at the time it was the latest craze and every one had to have one.  What appealed to me was the addictive gameplay and of course its portability.Well a modern, colour gameboy was long overdue and at long last Nintendo have produced it.I bought my gameboy for    60 due to it being imported from Japan, but most shops currently sell it for    89.99.  When I first turned it on with Mariokart Advance inside I was amazed at the speed and quality of graphics. It is a 32 bit machine which means it is twice as fast as a SNES, and it s graphics twice as good.  The sound quality is quite good, although could have been better since there is only one speaker.The gameboy Advance now only needs 2 AA batteries and this last for a long time due to the LCD screen.  The layout is now horizontal with the usual A nd B buttons but has added L and R buttons above, rather like the SNES gamepad.The disadvantages with the new gameboy is the lack of a backlight which can strain the eyes and makes gameplay difficult in dim light.  Also the games are way overpriced at    35 each, although it is compatible with any of the previous gameboy games which are usually much cheaper.  Another thing is that most of the games available are old SNES games just revamped which can be annoying. Having said this,I would recommend it to any video games addict, especially gameboy fans. It can liven up many boring journies       ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re eyeing the Nintendo GameBoy Advance, here’s the lowdown from someone who’s both a tech geek and a retro gaming fan. First off, the graphics are a solid step up—smooth, colorful, and flirting with Super Nintendo quality, which is a real treat for those nostalgic for the 16-bit era. Plus, the console’s lightweight, comfy design with well-placed buttons (including those nifty new shoulder buttons) makes for a pleasant handheld experience. It’s also fully backwards compatible with GameBoy and GameBoy Color games, so your old favorites aren’t left behind.

Battery life is decent, running on standard batteries but with options for rechargeable packs and AC adapters—handy for long gaming sessions. And if you’re a fan of variety, the multiple color options add a bit of personal flair.

Now, the not-so-great bits: the screen is a bit of a diva. No backlight or contrast adjustment means you’ll need a good light source to avoid eye strain, especially in dim environments. This omission has frustrated many, and honestly, it’s a missed opportunity by Nintendo. Also, the screen’s reflectiveness can be a pain, making it tricky to see your game without angling just right.

Game-wise, the launch lineup is a mixed bag. There’s a limited selection of exclusive titles, and many games are revamped SNES classics—which might feel like déjà vu if you’re craving fresh adventures. On top of that, the cartridges are tiny and easy to misplace, and the games themselves tend to be pricey, so keep your wallet close.

All told, despite these quirks, the GameBoy Advance stands out as the best handheld console of its time, especially if you value classic gameplay and solid graphics. Just be ready to hunt for good lighting and keep those tiny cartridges in check!
