product_reviews: ['    After playing a demo of Burnout 3: Takedown, I was left astounded as to how they could have made Burnout 2: Point of Impact any better. But they did.Here s some of the news...FEATURESSome of the newer additions to the Burnout series include...Takedowns - the signature of the new generation Burnout. Smash an opponent car into a wall or into traffic, and you can watch and gloat while you get to see the crumpled bodywork flying about, causing havok.CAMERA QUALITYAfter laughing at your adversary s misfortune, the camera flips back flawlessly behind your car, get taken out and you get a slow-mo chance to see your killed car cruising through the sky, to land on a poor, unfortunate soul in another vehicle.SOUNDAlthough I haven t heard the soundtrack (I ve only played the demo), It s been reviewed by others as having more than just racing rock tracks on it. Some hip-hop, for instance. The in-game sound is so realistic, along with the graphics, you can almost smell the burnt rubber and twisted metal.GRAPHICSYou ve seen the case. That s not a photo, more like a game snapshot. Need I say more?BOOSTThe Burnout bar is back, with a twist. You start with a little boost, perform a Takedown and your boost bar with get longer, allowing you to gain more boost, which you will need if you want to beat the exponentially tougher competitors.AFTER-TOUCHAnother little addition is the after-touch control, meaning you can still have a little control over your car after you have stacked it. A well timed tap on the controller allows you to manoevre into the path of a rival car, taking them down with you.PROGRAMMERSCriterion have outdone themselves yet again, but with the addition of EA Games, Burnout 3: Takedown will probably not be equalled for many years yet.RELEASEPlease bear in mind this review was written based on a playable demo from a leading PS2 magazine. I have not played the full game because it will not be on general release until 10th September 2004.I WILL be getting it, and finishing this review later.*****************************************************As promised here is the continuation of this review.Welcome to Burnout 3: TakedownThe first thing that you are presented with when the game has loaded is, predictably, the main menu. This gives you the following options.Burnout 3 World TourSingle EventMultiplayerOnline ModeDriver DetailsBURNOUT 3 WORLD TOURThe Burnout 3 World Tour is the  quot;career mode quot; of B3. There are a handful of races available from the start, but only America is unlocked. Take part in these events to unlock events in Europe and the Far East. SINGLE EVENTQuite simply, single player mode. Here are the events that feature on the WORLD TOUR and the single player.RACEThis is just a simple race. You race against 5 rivals. You must be bad, though, cos if you behave you ll find yourself in 6th place. The aim is to finish 1st.GRAND PRIXNone of these are available at first, but can be unlocked by winning other events. Instead of 1 race, you race for points and at the end of the event (usually 3 or 4 races), the one with the most points wins.ELIMINATORA race event with a twist. The racer in last place at the end of each lap dramatically explodes. This carries on until only one car remains - the winner.BURNING LAPYou get to drive a locked car for this event. The aim is to boost your way round the track and hopefully beat the clock.FACE-OFFRace for a new car. Beat your rival to get their car.ROAD RAGERemember my description of takedowns? Basically you need to do as many as you can in the alloted time without crashing too much. If you crash too many times, the event is over.CRASHCrash mode has gone through some spectacular changes. There is no boost, you need to pick up an icon for that. Multipliers are collectable not automatic. A big addition is the Crashbreaker. Collect a Crahbreaker icon and your car instantly blows up, causing huge damage and giving you the opportunity to aftertouch into more traffic or more collectables. You can also get Crashbreaker when a number of cars have been involved. This number is always given before the event. The Heartbreaker cuts your score in half. Leave Well Alone.MULTIPLAYER MODESRACEROAD RAGETEAM CRUSHTwo players crash at the same time to cause the most havok on the street.DOUBLE IMPACTTwo players crash at the same time to score more than their opponent. This mode includes the score-switcher icon. Pick it up and players swap scores, which can be an advantage if your opponent caused more damage than you or if you picked up the Heartbreaker.PARTY CRASHMuch like Double Impact, but this can be played with one controller, as it is turn-based. Up to 8 players can play this mode.CARSI will not give any info on these. All I will say is look out for the US Circuit Racer, among others.There are more than 60 cars to unlock, over nearly 200 events.AWARDSIf the above doesn t seem too big a challenge, certain actions earn you awards. Win certain events or get enough points and you will win a car. Perform Signature takedowns and you get a photo. Get all photos and you will receive ??? (you didn t think I d tell you did you?). Win Special events, get postcards. Crash mode offers you headline news if your crash was big enough. All I ll say is I got all headlines and love my reward for it (small clue: 4 wheels, ladder, water). DRIVER DETAILSHere you can check your progress, awards, total takedowns, view your cars and save/load.ONLINE PLAYI haven t played this, as I m not connected, but I ve heard that it s better than offline (is that possible?)     ', '    General:Burnout 3 is the game if the year. It is a good improvement from point of impact. Main great feature is the improved crash mode and the very fun world tour with hundreds of eventsRacing:The game itself is very fun. The cool thing is takedowns. These are done by forcing other opponent cars into either the wall, cars, trams, buses or anything else to make them crash. It shows an excellent slow motion of the opponent flying in the air with a big title at the top saying : CAR TAKEDOWN. This is a very satisfying moment. That is why my favourite events are the road rage events (see later on).Crash:This is very fun. A great feature is having small control in slo-moiton of where to send your car if you have just come off a ramp. Also after a certain amount of cars have crashed because of u you will get a crashbreaker which means that if you press the right button you will blow up and also here when you aer flying in the air after u have blown up it is possible to control your car in slo-motion. In the world tour your total is counted up everytime you do a crash and count that as your final one . This total is counted up also to unlock new cars. If you get all 10 crash headlines (you get them for amazing crash totals in one crash) you will get a firetruck muhahahaha (i got it)Road Rage:Oh yeah this is fun dude. Just take them all down. Very satisfying. The point of this in the world tour is to get a certain amount of takedowns in three minutes without crashing yourself aout 3 times but for the more fun people you can just go to single event and play it and get as many as you want (without crashing much). There are basically infinite cars whch go quite slow so it is easy to get takedowns although they can take you down too. My record is 47 takedowns try and beat that. (if you do please say what you got in my guestbook).Burnout world tour:This is the story of the game. All you do is go through specific races or crashes and get as many medals as you can. There are normal races, road rage events, one on ones (face-off), elimination (where at the end of each lap last place gets kicked out of the race), timed run and crashes. There are lots of things and you get to play as cool cars. You build up burnout points that you get from takedowns in races and other special things to get a new car. There are special events which are very hard but if you get gold in all 10 u win a special car. There are also other special cars for getting gold in every race and every crash and other things.Music:i myself have enjoyed the music a lot. I made a list of all the ones i liked and downloaded them. One band on it called The F-Ups i really liked that i even bought the cd on ebay (because it is a US band so it has to be imported). Sometimes i even get slightly distracted by it.Verdict:Gameplay: 10/10Graphics: 10/10Sounds: 10/10Longevity:8/10Overall verdict: 10/10     ', '    [This review is now added on my website - www.ps2-central.co.uk - as part of the website s special Burnout 3: Takedown Feature]Sypnosis:DON   T FIGHT TRAFFIC    DESTROY IT Grab the wheel and hold on as you takedown the competition with the most spectacular smashes this side of Hollywood. Use your car as a weapon and battle to the front of the pack. Live dangerously and indulge your thirst for twisted metal with a dedicated crash mode that rewards you for creating massive pile-ups. While they re fun to play, especially on a Saturday night with a bunch of friends, having a mad competition, I d almost given up playing them by myself when I was bored - they all seemed to consist of the same thing (driving, obviously) but with nothing to liven things up a bit.Burnout 3: Takedown is therefore such a nice refreshing change. Well, read on.MENU*******When you start the game, you ll be taken to a menu where you can choose to start a  quot;campaign quot; style main game, which is in the form of a World Map (more on this in a mo ).Also on this menu are options for single races, which aren t a part of the main game, these are detailed below. The single races are easy enough to find, as are the multiplayer, but the Driver profile menu (where you can view your rewards, medals and new cars and also save or load your personal profile) are awkward. The music is customisable from the Driver Profile menu, so if you really hate or love one track you can turn it off, or choose to play nothing but that. As well as the opposing race cars, you have to contend with ordinary cars, lorries, trams and buses driving in an ordinary way (at least until you came along).  This makes avoiding crashes incredibly hard.Another thing you ll notice is the sheer speed of the game.  It s wonderful to whoosh round the tracks like a bat out of hell, but watch out  Remember those ordinary cars and things on the road? If you ve no idea what I mean, I ve explained Takedowns below.BOOST*********In addition to the normal high speed of the cars you can drive, you also earn something called Boost.  This is a sort of turbo-charged speed-up which you gain for bumping other cars off the track, scraping them, taking corners at high speed, flying off bumps in the road and having near-misses with other cars.If you thought the ordinary speed was fast, using boost (by pressing the R1 button while racing) is just suicidal. CRASH EVENTS*****************You are able to select Crash Events as a single game, as multiplayer, or they will turn up in your World Map. You earn points for first place, second, third and fourth per race, and these points are totted up at the end of each race to give you your current standing, and then added all together at the end of all six races to determine the medals.I find these events quite good, as it means you can still earn a gold medal even if you rarely come first in an actual race, because the points you earn are added up over all the races.  Depending on how the AI cars do, I m usually in with a chance of first overall which I find hard to do with a single race event.ROAD RAGE***************Found only in single race and multiplayer mode but not on your World Map (more s the pity) is the Road Rage events.  Here, you pick a car, pick a road to race on and then proceed to smash the living crap out of your competitors.  Your opponents are indicated by a blue arrow over the top of their cars, and your only objective is to shunt, bash, crash or force them off the road using any means possible.  This is not a race, you don t need to get over any Finish line.  Just get as many takedowns as possible to irritate your friends with your highest score.  The race only ends when the time limit expires or your car explodes You also earn cars while in Road Rage mode.  The total takedowns you get in any one race are added to a Global total, which rewards you with more cars as you hit certain targets.  Takedowns made in the World Map races also add to this total.STANDARD RACING MODE********************************This does exactly what it says on the tin.  To gain a bronze, silver or gold medal and unlock new events or cars you need to get over the finish line in first, second or third place.As I said above, the race track is an ordinary stretch of road with ordinary cars on it as well as your competitors. While you can run your competitors off the road to earn takedowns, and extra Boost, you don t want to be crashing into these ordinary cars, it will lose you a lot of time, and will damage your own car. Mind you, if you re anything like me, once it becomes clear that there s no way to win, I do like driving at high speed into cars I m not supposed to as it gives me a great sense of satisfaction.  Maybe I have a low boredom threshold.........I found these races very hard (when I m trying to play them properly). The AI cars are not the usual run-of-the-mill ones you d get in mnay other racing games.  AI controlled opponents are not daft, they re trying to bump you off the track too, plus they re fast enough to make it very difficult for you to win when playing a race mode competition instead of one where you merely have to destroy as many cars as possible.HEAD-TO-HEAD EVENTS*****************************This type of race, found only in the World Map unless you re playing split-screen against a friend, pits you against a single opponent.  You have to get to the finish line first, and as usual, there are all the other, ordinary cars to look out for.  While this may sound easier than the normal Race mode, it s not.  The opposing car is fast, and seems to have an uncanny ability to sneak up behind you - before you know it, you re sailing up in the air/over a cliff/into a barrier and the other car has zoomed off into the distance. Darn TIME TRIAL EVENTS************************As the title suggests, you have to complete a lap of the racetrack in a certain time to earn medals.  There are differing time limits for bronze, silver and gold, and while you re the only racing car on the track, there are all those pesky Sunday drivers to get in your way and make it hard for you to beat the time limit PLEASE  SHUT THE HELL UP ***********************************So, what s the catch? A game can t be this much fun surely?  Well, the only complaints I personally have are these: firstly, the races are very hard, even the easier ones. That s not too much of a problem though, as practice makes perfect.  The other complaint is the Radio DJ commentary that cuts in at the beginning of each race, and sometimes halfway through. The idea is a good one - give you information in the style of a radio which you d hear in your car.  The problem is, the DJ has the most annoying voice EVER and keeps repeating himself.  He sounds so excited you wonder if the guy supplying the voice had been up on cocaine all night before going to the recording studio......I just want to slap him, or send him a nasty case of laryngitis.  You don t have the option of turning him off either, more s the pity Well, after reading all that, I hope you ve got a good idea of what the game is about - I d definitely recommend it even if you re not usually a fan of driving games, it will liven up another gloomy winters  evening when there s nothing on telly (again).  I haven t really managed to fit in everything about the game - I was planning a section on the rewards you can earn, but there has to be some things for the player to discover for themselves in any game - that s half the fun   I ll leave you to discover them for yourself, should you buy or borrow this game. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
Burnout 3: Takedown stands out as a thrilling arcade-style racer that perfectly balances high-speed excitement with innovative gameplay mechanics. For fans like you who appreciate a fresh alternative to serious sims like Gran Turismo, this game delivers an adrenaline rush with its fantastic sense of speed—especially when boosting after successful takedowns. The core mechanic of “Aftertouch Takedown,” where you control your wreckage to hit opponents post-crash, adds a unique layer of strategy and chaos that keeps races unpredictable and intensely fun.

The game’s diverse event types let you switch between traditional racing and the highly entertaining Crash Mode, where causing spectacular destruction is the goal. Features like Crash Breaker and bonus pickups spice up gameplay variety, while the improved AI ensures opponents actively seek revenge, adding a competitive edge that prevents monotony. The World Tour mode offers over 20 hours of single-player content, rewarding aggressive driving with cash and medals to unlock new vehicles and events—great for those who value replayability and progression.

Graphically, Burnout 3 impresses with detailed environments and visually stunning crash sequences that enhance immersion. The indie rock soundtrack, featuring bands like Franz Ferdinand and the Ramones, complements the game’s energetic vibe perfectly. Multiplayer shines here too, supporting all modes offline and online, making it a fantastic pick for social gaming sessions.

On the downside, some may find the online multiplayer repetitive over time, and the arcade style might not satisfy those craving realistic racing physics. Still, for an enthusiast seeking fast-paced, aggressive racing with innovative mechanics and solid multiplayer, Burnout 3: Takedown offers a highly entertaining and well-rounded experience that’s hard to beat in its genre.

product_reviews: ['    Well, how many times have we complained about hospital waiting lists ? Staff shortages ? General incompetence ? Now we can get a taste of the other side of the issue ... kind of   In the CD-ROM computer game, Theme Hospital, it is up to YOU to build your own hospital, design the layout, hire the staff and have it all finished in time and within a set budget. It is your responsibility to make sure the hospital is well heated, has enough seats, toilets and vending machines - or your patients will suffer   This is my favourite part of the game, as it is fun to see how your design works out.Once the hospital is up and running, there are endless patients to cure. You need to have the right staff and equipment to diagnose the illnesses and be able to treat the patients well enough. This will entail you hiring specialised staff or buying a specific machine to increase the amount of cured patients on your books.The game is interesting, fast moving, exciting and can become addictive. However, I did find it confusing after a while and as the pace quickens, it can actually become quite stressful at times   It certainly gives you an idea of some of the problems faced by the NHS in real life - although I don t think there is an epidemic of Bloaty Head disease yet, thankfully       ', '     No dying in the corridors  comes screeching from reception. A great laugh with very funny comments, and an old game now so should be very cheap to buy.***GAME PLAY***Ok it s old but that doesn t stop it from being an immensely fun game. You are the manager of a hospital and your aim is to of cure a certain number of patients, while staying out of debt. You are stuck with the task of building different rooms in the hospital, they vary from GP s office to Surgery and you will find toilets and staff rooms will make the place  cleaner  :-)***ILLNESSES***No cancer, no heart surgery you will be more worried whether you have popped the bloaty head correctly and whether the patient is cured.  Great creative and original illnesses such as  Bloaty head (mentioned above) - the patients head has expanded and needs to be popped then refilled immediately.    Invisibility - Ok maybe not as original as I thought but still very funny when you see a hat, some glasses and a walking stick moving around the hospital  ***GRAPHICS***The game was released in 1997 so as you can imagine the graphics aren t as good as say  Joint Ops . Though having cartooned graphics does add a sort of childish side to the game. :-) I think this game would have got excellent if it had better graphics.***SOUND***ARGH   The music on this game is horrible. It sounds like a tune that was written by a child in five minutes. Also all the tracks sound the same, so after you have put up with the noise for one track and your thinking maybe the next one will be better...  I found the game was more enjoyable when I had turned the music off and I could just hear the popping noise of heads or a machine blowing up which was much better.***OVERALL***If you can get into the hang of building benches everywhere for people to sit on, it becomes a lot of fun. I would definitely recommend it to any potential buyers and it will be very cheap because of the age of the game.Hope you have funThanks     ', '    Theme Hospital ReviewGame HistoryTheme Hospital was produced by UK developer Bullfrog.   This game was produced as a sequel to the ever so popular Theme park with released in 1994 for Windows 95 and MS-DOS.   Theme park became so successful that it sold over a million copies worldwide and remained for 2 years running a top ten hit within the UK.   Theme Park was an adventure of the day to day running of an amusement park.  Back in those days the game was like no other.  Technology has since been used within Theme Hospital to demonstrate accurate attention to detail which has become Bullfrogs trademark, there is full interaction from the characters and objects of the game, portraying every day tasks of life.   Bullfrog was soon to produce Theme Hospital after its running success with Theme Park.  And so Theme Hospital was born.How to installInstallation is simple, open your CD rom drive and insert the CD, and close again. The installation details will automatically appear. Then you simply choose which directory you wish to install the game to, you may accept the default type option displayed in the directory if you wish or browse, using the browse button to find the required directory. Once you have chosen simply click on OK to continue. Next a panel will appear confirming that it is installing the required components.  After this you will be met by a message asking you the language of the installation.  There are 6 options available; these include English, French, German, Swedish, Italian and Spanish.  Simply choose your required language and then click on the next button.The next box will appear notifying you that the programme will be installed on your hard drive, as well as informing you of the copyright laws and international treaties.  Simply read through the law abiding conditions and select the next key to continue.Next you will be notified that Theme Hospital requires Direct X to play.  Simply choose yes to install, without this the game wont play.  Be sure to read the Direct X terms of licence agreement, if you agree with these rules, simply click yes to continue.The next screen you will come to is the installation type.  Here you are give 3 options:To install the game at minimal (20 mb), typical (30 mb) or full (55 mb) be sure to pick the right one for you, since you may not have a lot of hard drive space on your system.  Make you decision by selecting one, and click next button to continue.Next there will be a screen displayed, and you will see the progress of the installation, and a percentage, this is just basically telling you that the installation is following your commands, and the percentage simply tells you how far the game has installed.  Once the percentage reaches 100 you will be greeted by yet another page notifying you that your setup has been successful, but in order to play you will need to reboot your computer system.  From here you have 2 options     you can choose to reboot or choose to reboot at a later time.  Once selected press the finish button.Should you have chosen the reboot option, then your computer will start to shut down and will notify you of this.Your computer should now restart in the normal way, be sure to wait until the system has fully loaded (mine normally takes 3 minutes) although this could be different depending on your machine system.To load simply find the game programme in your directory (from which you choose to install it).  The programme will be listed under the name Bullfrog.  Once found you will simply see the theme hospital tab, click this and the game will begin.Once loaded the first thing you will see is the Theme Hospital demo which you can choose to watch or not, this includes humorous animation and music.  Simply click the mouse button once to be taken to the first screen.The first thing you will need to do, will be to choose a nickname, this can be anything from your own name or just a simple word.  Once you have chosen a name simply press the enter key.From here you will arrive to a screen which is rather like you are sitting in a lecture.  There is a professor type man who will give you 5 options.You can:Start a new game     this basically takes you to the hospital and allows you to develop and run it to your worst or best ability.Continue previous game     this simply lets you continue on a game you have previously been playing.Load saved game     you  re-load your game from here, the ones which you have savedStart network game     This feature enables 3 other players to take the places of the 3 other hospitals (whom you are competing against).  This can be challenging as each hospital competes to discover new cures and machinery, as well as having your staff poached as well as having your patients attracted to the other competing hospitals.  It can be more realistically challenging than the one-player version. This option is fully functional with network and modem support.Exit     obviously shuts down the game.Simply select start a new game     this will take you to yet another screen which will allow you to change the game settings (making it easier, hard etc).  You can choose one of three levels these being: Easy level (junior) Medium level (doctor) Hard level (consultant).  From this screen you can also select the Tutorial option (should you be a beginner this is highly recommended, as you will learn the basic aspects of the hospital quicker).Selecting the tutorial feature, you will be given help from the tutorial assistant who will show you how to successfully install the main key features (rooms, employ staff, open hospital etc).  Once the tutorial part is complete you can then take full control of the hospital and knowing the basic concepts of the game you will be able to perform the simple tasks.Control panelThe game is played mainly by using the Control panel (situated at the bottom of the screen). The control panel includes the following options: (hovering over the key symbols will tell you a brief description of what they do)Finances     here you can request a loan, view important information such as the hospital value, interest payments etcThere will be a display next to this which will display your bank balance as well as the date and your hospital reputation score.Build room option -  from here you have 4 different types of room (diagnosis, treatment, clinics and fractures) simply select one and it will then list a range of rooms of that type which are available.  To build a chosen room simply select one.  Next you will need to drag out a blue print of how big you want to make the room (the tutorial will explain this in further detail).  Once happy with the desired size simply select the tick button.  Next you will be informed to place a door and windows (since you will need a door to enable patients to enter the room).  Simply place these within the outside of the blue print.  Next you are given the option to equip the room with furniture.  You will see all the types available for that room in a list.  Select from the list the furniture you want (say filling cabinet, desk etc) and in the same way blue print the items in the room (you can also change the angle of the furniture to ensure they aren   t facing the wrong way).  Click the tick button to exit.Furnish corridors     from this option you can choose all sorts of wonderful furnishings in order to put your own individual mark on your hospital.  These items include and range from reception desks to benches to radiators.  Simply select the items in the same way as you did with the rooms and place within the perimeter of the hospital.  All the prices for the items will be individually listed, so should you feel they are too expensive you don   t have to purchase them.Edit rooms/items     this allows you to delete that extra bench or reception desk you have purchased too many of (should money be tight).Hire staff     4 varieties of staff are available here:DoctorsNursesHandymenReceptionists.  Choose one of the categories to view the applicants.  There will be several to choose from and you can read their profiles to ensure you only employ the best.  To employ simply click the gold envelope and they will be added to your pay roll with immediate effect.  Place the member of staff in the designated area (for example a doctor in the GP   s office or the nurse in the ward etc), you can also place the member of staff anywhere within the hospital and they will automatically go about their business themselves.  At all times you can hover over the displayed button options available, should you get stuck.Here you will also be able to view all the staff you have on your books, as well as see when they feel tired or when they have acquired a new skill for instance.  As well as being able to offer them a good gesture and well deserved pay rise (should you wish) or if needs be you can always sack them.Town map     this displays the situation the hospital stands in.  From here you have information regarding how many patients are within the hospital, how many plants/radiators you have.  You can also change the heat of the radiators from here, should the place get to chilly or too hot.Drug casebook     gives you up to date information of illnesses you have cured, as well as any fatalities.  You can also concentrate on more research from here.  You will also be able to view which illness have generated the most profit.Research     from here you can choose which types of cures to invest in.Status     simply gives you information regarding how well your hospital is doing in comparison to other hospitals (these are displayed in graphs).  You can also view patients thoughts from here     such as to see how happy/sad they are, if they are thirsty (if so you can easily invest in more drinks machines) and even if they feel hot or cold within the hospital     in which case given this crucial information you have, you will be able to make decisions to best please them.Charts     here you can view all your in/out goings, including staff wages, number of patients, deaths, cures and of course you reputation score.Policy     this feature allows you to set important decisions     such as: how tired the staff have to be before they are allowed to rest and take a break.  As well as whether to chance patient   s health by either sending them, home or guessing/trying an unproved cure.You can alter these decisions by simply selecting these targets, staff will then follow the desired procedures.Tell me more about what the main game play is about?Have you ever wondered what life would be like working perhaps for the NHS, well now you will have a life like chance with the help of this game.  You will be in charge, making all important life changing decisions.  You will have to ensure the Hospital functions correctly by using careful planning and resources.  Things can go wrong and will go wrong and it   s your job to sort them all out, even if some of the patients do look rather monster like.  It   s your duty and in your best interests to build and maintain a fully functional successfully run hospital.  There are many different types of illnesses within the game, all of which have cures, it   s your neck on the line to ensure you discover and market these valuable cures.   The game is ram packed full of humour but it   s really fun to play.GraphicsI consider the graphic of this game to be excellent.  You can watch the characters of the game interacting very life like and realistically.  For instance watching the GP opening and closing the filing cabinet and putting files away as well as many more humorous, bizarre and realistic actions.What are the goals/tasks of the game?You are competing against other hospitals, to achieve the maximum amount of reputation you can possible.  With each new game you play, at the start of the game, you are notified of a goal you have to achieve in order to complete the level and in order to progress to a bigger and much better hospital. PlanningEnsure you plan every thing you do with attention to detail, everything from furniture to cures.  You need to ensure you attract patients and establish cures, as well as equipping the hospital with the highly qualified staff and features     doing this should bring you financial success.  Tougher quests await you when you attain promotion to more complex hospitals.The plotBuilding a successfully resourced hospital from the ground up.Introduction of getting startedIn order to run you hospital to the highest possible standards requires more than just a good layout.  You need to be aware of important research consequences which will improve not only your drugs but develop new clinics and machinery.  Staff is yet another important factor, deciding who to train to higher level of degree as well as implementing pay rises and the sack.  Overall you need to be prepared for all and everything which is to be thrown at you.   In later levels you won   t have the time, money or resources to do everything at once, so be sure to plan to detail every right move.  Having a plan should benefit your hospital not only financially but will help it to run smoothly, making life easier.EmergenciesAll emergencies appear with no warning and in this game you are faced with several which you will have to deal with:Accident emergency - During times in the game, you will be asked to treat what is called an emergency.  The task will be to treat a number of patients who have a certain illness of some sort, within a certain deadline.  Should you accept, you must be sure to stand by for their arrival, assuring each and every patient gets the exceptional treatment they require.  All emergency patients will arrive at the hospital with the same disease. ', '    Theme Hospital, released in 1997 by Bullfrog, is a relatively simple but addictively fun game that truly stands the test of time. It puts you in complete control of a series of hospitals, working your way up from one larger institution to another. The job gets harder as you move up the ladder, as greater crises and burdens lie in wait to bring you down. It all starts fairly simple. At your first hospital, you just need to set up a general practitioner s office or two, a general diagnostics room, a pharmacy, a psychiatric office, and get your researchers working on new diseases and ways to go about combating them. You ve got to hire doctors, nurses, handymen, and a receptionist - and you get a wide range of folks to choose from. Will you pay top dollar for the efficient GP s and specialists, or will you settle for abrasive, lazy types who smell of cabbage? Cure enough patients, make enough money, and establish a good enough reputation, and job offers for bigger and better assignments will come your way.As you progress, you ll get access to an assortment of fancy diagnostic equipment and treatment clinics. For those hard-to-diagnose cases, there are X-ray rooms, cardiology exams, high-dollar scanners, and the like, and before long you re even ready to build an operating theater and put scalpels in the hands of those crazy doctors of yours. As for the diseases and conditions, they aren t your typical fare: alongside gastrointestinal-type ailments such as the squibs, you have folks with Elvis Complex (who do indeed show up in Elvis leisure suits), invisibility, Bloaty Head (just pop their head and reinflate it), Slack Tongue (chop chop), Baldness (wait ll you see how to cure that), and an assortment of silly afflictions. Of course, you have your basic fractures and uncommon cold cases, as well. Each condition is more funny than serious (especially in terms of how it is contracted), but keeping your hospital up and working efficiently gets to be pretty serious when you ve got patients queued up in the aisles, tired doctors recuperating in the staff lounge, diagnostic machines temporarily down for repair, emergencies bringing in a number of new patients who must be cured quickly if your reputation isn t to suffer, earthquakes shaking things up, and epidemics popping up and wreaking havoc. Patients can be pretty messy, as many of them tend to throw up all over the place. If you don t have enough dependable handymen around to clean up the mess, the Ministry of Health will be all over you. The graphics look surprisingly good even today - although 1997 graphics certainly don t compare to those of recent games. There is a decent variety of looks among patients, and it s almost worth killing a few of them just to watch them ascend to heaven (or, on occasion, drop through the floor on their way to an alternate destination). The game is simple enough for anyone to play and enjoy, although things get pretty challenging as you progress deeper into the game. A lot of games today sacrifice fancy graphics for actual gameplay, but Theme Hospital is the kind of game you enjoy playing years and years after its release. Installing Theme Hospital. -------------------------- Theme Hospital is extremely easy to install, you simply take the disc out of its jewel-casing, insert it in your CD-ROM drive, and the installation program should appear automatically. Just follow the instructions, the game requires Direct X, so install it if you haven t got it. The installation program creates a program called Bullfrog, and adds this to your start menu. Playing Theme Hospital. ----------------------- When the game has loaded, you will have to choose a nickname for yourself, I usually call myself Dr Death, because I normally kill a lot of my patients, not on purpose though. Next a mad professor appears, and pulls down scroll with a picture of a skull, the skull is divided into segments, and each segment, gives you an option, such as load game, new game, quit and continue game. If you start a new game, you are asked whether you have played before, if not tutorial mode is activated, and you will be thoroughly guided through the game. Theme Hospital is played like a board game; you start out as an amateur, and have to progress though different hospitals, gaining experience in each, until you eventually retire with an impressive record and bags of money. Setting up your hospital. ------------------------- The first task is to set up a hospital, gain a good reputation, bank a bit of money and treat fifty percent of the patients. You will need to build a GP s office, which is like a doctor s surgery, the doctor working in here, will examine the patient, and determine what condition they are suffering from. You will also need a General Diagnosis room; this room contains specialist machinery that can examine a patient more thoroughly. A ward is also needed, which must be manned by a nurse. A psychiatric room is used to treat patients with mental problems. A pharmacy is essential as most patients can be treated with drugs. Later on in the game, you will need to build an operating theatre to treat patients with more complex conditions. There are also various clinics that are needed such as an inflation clinic and slack tongue clinic. Your hospital also needs facilities for patients and doctors alike, such as toilets, and staff rooms. The tanoid announcements are invaluable, in this game, as it tells you where your doctors and nurses are needed. Overall I d give this game 8/10 as its not as good as some others(Tiberian Sun for example) but better than   the likes of Solitair What I like most about it is that there s manyt different conditions which you get to decide how to deal with egh slack tougne desiese etc.     ', '    I bought this game when it first came out 3 or 4 years ago and I still love it    it is one of the best games i have ever played    It starts off pretty simple, you build your hospital with a GP s office, a diagnosis room and and ward. but as the game goes on it gets even better. wierd and wonderful dideases like hairy it and jelly something    you get emergencies, earth quakes and rats. it is one of the most addictive and enjoyable games i have ever played. There are many levels, and bonus levels, if you kill enough rats or kill enough people    As you go through the levels you get new rooms, like x-rays, training rooms, and different clinics. this game is definatly worth buying        ', '    I have had this game for several years now, after my brother and I spotted it going for a few pounds at a local computer store, and thought we would give it a try. Immediately I was hooked and still am to this day. The game is (obviously) based on the running of a hospital, in which outrageous diseases are frequently discovered. Basically, you\\ re given the money, (not real of course), and the site, and the rest is up to you. The aim is tobuild the correct rooms for what your patients need, and employ the best staff in order to keep your hospital running smoothy.Targets are set for you to achieve, reputaion, hospital value, and money -wise, in order for you to succeed on to higher levels. Along the way other disruptions such as emergency situations, in which you must cure a certain number of patients with a certain illness in the time allocated to earn you money. Also, in the higher levels, you come across epidemics, which I find particularly amusing as some of the so- called epidemics, only involve a single person.The levels are all pretty repetitive, as is the somewhat annoying receptionists voice, but hey, you can mute her so its all good.... Once you\\ ve built the rooms for your hospital, there isnt much left to do but sit back and wait for something to happen. As you have probably gathered, I own quite an old version. I would highly recommend this game if you want something fun and lighthearted, and I can guarantee I will enjoy playing this for years to come =]     ', '    Theme Hospital is a totally addictable game in which you have to build and manage your own hospital.  Easy, you might think.  But it s not as simple as it sounds  Finding decent employees with qualifications is hard enough.  For each level (of which there are several, increasing in difficulty) there is winning criteria, for example you might have to make    50000, have a reputation of 400 and cure 200 patients. You have to face up to the terribly annoying doctor figure who keeps giving you  quot;advice quot; (critisism, some might call it) on how to do better.  And your hospital s no ordinary hospital.  Oh no   Have you ever heard of illnesses such as  quot;Slack Tongue quot;,  quot;Bloaty Head quot; or  quot;The Squits quot;?  This game has it all.  Theme Hospital is a great game and I d recommend it to anyone, whatever their age      ', '    This game is brilliant  You re given a hospital to build and run - the more patients you cure, the more money you earn; the more money you earn, the quicker you get to the next level.Basically, you have to build up you re hospital so that it has everything the patients would want - toilets, gp s offices, operating theatres, wards etc etc.  Then you have to employ the staff to run it, cleaners etc and keep everything ticking over nicely.Don;t let the place fall to bits, else you ll keep getting epidemics and killing your patients off.  They are a valuable commodity so take care of them.You have to train your staff up too so that you have plentty of surgeons and specialists to look after the patients.  Don t treat the quickly and you ll get a visit from the grim reaper.It s very easy to get the first few levels completed, after that it gets harder and harder as you go on.  It s a good game though - good graphics, amusing noises and varying skill levels.     ', '    This is a really funny game pleasr read on to find out more.Theme Hospital is a game where you have to build your own hospital and cure as many people you can in different towns and citys.  The game involoves building lots of different rooms and employing staff to work in each room.  You must have lots of different rooms to cure different illnesses.  The different illnesses you can get are tv personalities, squits, bloaty head and lots and lots more.  You must try and make money and once you cure enough patients you move onto the next level.  It sounds a little boring I know but it s not it s really fun.  Please comment      ', '    I always thought my dad was a bit of a geek because he spent so much time playing various games here on our PC. That was until he persuaded me to have a bash at Theme Hospital.Theme Hospital is one of several games invented by the company Bullfrog, and is just as addictive as Theme Park, if not more so. Personally, I find Theme Hospital easier to play.For those of you not too familiar with Bullfrog games, Theme Hospital allows you to build your own hospital and then you are responsible for running it. You start off by building your reception desk, toilets and General Diagnosis room, and as you progress through the levels, you are able to build more and more facilities for your patients to use.For beginners, there is a facility on the game which guides you through how to build your hospital and how to hire (and often fire) your staff. This can however get really irritating once you know what you re doing Theme Hospital is really enjoyable, and incredibly funny, especially when the hospital has a raging vomit virus, or an earthquake strikes. I really recommend it if you like taking charge of things, and basically want a giggle  You won t be able to stop playing      ', '    Who wants to be a doctor?  What about a nurse?  No?  Okay then  Let  8217;s play   8216;Who wants to be hospital director   8217;  Yep, with this game you too have the chance to be the big cheese and make lotsa decisions about running a hospital.When the CD loads you are transported to a classroom setting where an old man with a funky white crown of hair points to various options displayed in the form of a skull on a pulley thing attached to the blackboard.  Choose from:New Game,Load Game,Continue last Game,Quit,Network Game.New Game  Pretty self-explanatory really   You basically start a brand new game where you get to choose the level - Junior (easy), GP (medium) or Consultant (hard).  You  8217;ll be asked whether this is your first game (If you click yes, you  8217;ll get a lil guy popping up to tell you what to do every now and again   8211; tutorialish )  You can also choose between high or low resolution.Load Game Choose from one of your 9 saved games and continue playing from where you left off.Continue When you quit your last game it was automatically saved by thelast game  program   8211; you  8217;ll leave off from the moment you quit. Quit DUH Network Play with people on your network or play over the internet (I  8217;veGame  never tried this though, so I can  8217;t really comment). The basic idea of Theme Hospital  8482; is to cure the patients and to complete the tasks given to you by the big guys from the Health Ministry of Theme Hospital  8482;     To progress in the game you must satisfy a number of criteria depending on the hospital you own.  These include the following:Keeping your hospital  8217;s reputation above a certain amount,Having at least X amount of    s in your account,Curing X amount of patients.When you start the game you  8217;ll be given an empty shell of a hospital which you must furnish and staff.  You are given a certain amount of time to do this before your hospital is automatically opened (but you can avoid this a little bit by going to options and setting game to   8220;Slowest  8221;.  Choose rooms from GP  8217;s offices, Pharmacy, General Diagnosis, Ward, Psychiatric room, Operating theatre, and several clinics that become available further on in the game as new illnesses are found.Staff can be chosen from a number of applicants and can be sacked for any reason at any time. I found this game interesting and funny.  The graphics were quite cool and some of the illness the characters had were freaky  The clinic rooms for those illnesses were cool and fun to watch. It  8217;s a good game and you can get it for a good price. The game comes with a detailed instruction manual and a smaller and simpler   8220;Quick Play Guide  8221;.  Both were easy to read and comprehendible to even the least experienced gamers.      ', '    Laugh, I throught I would never start. This has to be one of the funniest games ever. I bought it when it first came out about 3 years ago for    30 after playing the demo, and it is still installed on my PC all though i don t play that often any more as I am now taking a-levels and have no time.The most attractive thing about this game is its humor. I would recoment it to anyone with a sense of humor. From the names of the diseases such as Slack Tough and Uncommon Cold to the PA announcements, every part of this game will have you rolling around with laughter.The game is split into levels of increasing difficulty. Each level must be passed in order to get to the next. Each level has its own win criteria, such as reaching a certain hospital value, a specific number of cures or people treated and cash balance.     ', '    Theme Hospital follows on from the success of Theme Park.  Obviously set in a hospital you have to meet the needs of your patients by providing the various machines required.  The games is not meant to be morbid and as a result many of the machines are rather unusual.  Look out for epidemics with green blobs sticking to the heads of the diseased.  There is always the risk of running out of money.  As I play a lot of these type of games I found it quite easy on medium mode finishing it within a week.The games is good fun to play and can be a good laugh when things go wrong.  If you are planning to be a manager and enjoy making money in games then this should be on your buy list, especially now since it is cheap.     ', '    Theme Hospital is a game of design, money and organisation (oh yes and some luck too). You have to build a hospital from scratch starting with just four walls. You start by building a GP s office and furnishing it. Then go ahead and build more rooms including a pharmacy,  a ward, an operating theatre even a bloaty head department. You ll need to train doctors, please nurses, hire handymen and get the vital receptionist who keeps the place running.The patients that will attend your hospital are not your ordinary run of the mill people. Maybe you ll get someone suffering from hairyitis...have you got an electrolysis room built, if not will you send him to another hospital, send him to the ward or send him to the research department where he ll not leave but your researchers will learn alot to help other sufferers  This may have been around for a while now but it is still a good game. Produced by the people who made Theme Park, the original good build, manage and play game this is suitable for all ages and mentality  I played a demo of this from the Bullfrog homepage and liked it so I went out and got it. It cost me    25 (that was when it first came out)I have found it a very good playable game so go ahead and get it and cure the world of their ills.     ']
filtered_hist_vote_written: ['    This is an unashamed Micro Machines rip off, but this is no bad thing. It takes the Micro Machines game, adds to it and produces a superb game.The premise is simple, race a series of cars around a load of courses. These are real world courses, by which I mean icy tracks or desert locations as opposed to the Micro Machines idea of minaturised locales.The single player game is fun, but this game comes in to its own in multi player.Get 4 people or more sitting round a playstation with this game and you are guaranteed a fun time.The graphics are not great, but do the job well.An old game, if you can find it buy it; you won;t be dissapointed.     ', '    This is the most playable football game ever - and I ve played most of them.An update to Pro Evolution Soccer. It s worth buying even if you have the original. Apart from the updated stats, the animation has been improved, there are more detailed stats, formations and an increased number of moves the player can perform.The crowning achievement is in the playability - it is the closest to real football yet. The AI is very good, now making a few human-like errors. But it s best played in mulitplayer mode. With up to 8 players it is quite incredible.A new training mode adds longevity to the game. It allows you to test your dribbling skills, passing, free-kick taking and more.Additional players and teams may be unlocked by winning tournaments with certain teams, or by reaching a number of points in the training challenges.The commentary on the game is actually quite good this time round, and doesn t repeat itself too often.The various stadiums are well designed, as are the good weather effects.This is the best footbal game yet, make no mistake.     ', '    The playstation is by far the best console at its price as you can get more than just a couple of months play from it, we re talking years.The capability and adaptability from the console is extreme and is worth buying who ever you are. It wont make a difference who you are as their is a game for everyone and it is guarenteed to keep you kids quiet in their rooms fot weeks.The price that its at is very reasnableas the N64 is not any where near as good,it may be faster and have better graphics but the gameplay is poor and the variety of games is poor.     ', '    After some mix ups I finally got to play this game yesterday (27/12/01). Wow. It is really addictive. I promised myself that I would play it for half an hour and before I knew it it was 12pm.      As soon as I saw this product I knew that I had to have it. The shop I bought it from was extremly helpful.The front cover stands out amongst the others probably because on the chart shelves it stands amongst sports, fighting and racing games.      It was very easy to install and didn t need the computer to be restarted which is a big plus point. The game was also very easy to play. There are no buttons that never get used. The help is easy to understand and the tutorial really does help you get used to the program.       I would recommend this product to anyone and everyone as its enjoyable by all the family. Although a little expensive it will keep everyone amused for hours and will make those boring school holidays pass like a dream. All in all buy it     ', '    When I first started this game it thought that I would get bored of it easily, but I was wrong   It has a series of levels in which the hospitals get larger and the game gets trickier.  Its very different to your average computer game.  You have an outline of a hospital and you have to fill it with the appropriate rooms e.g. toilets, staff room, pharmacy.  You then have to hire the appropriate staff e.g. doctors, handymen and furnish the hospital appropriately all before the hospital opens for business   Small tip, remember to hire a secretary  I made this mistake and I had not visitors to your hospital at all   Once a certain amount of patients have been cured (it varies with every level) you get to move onto the next via a letter from your boss asking if you want a promotion   You then move to a larger hospital where the process starts again but you get emergencies where you have to treat some people in a certain length of time for a bonus, you get infestations of rats and new machinery which treats more illnesses.  You get cleanliness awards and you are able to take out loans as long as you pay them back   Overall this is a really fun and addictive game, well worth buying.     ', '    This is probably the best football game ever released on the Playstation. Recently the only choice was between the FIFA games and ISS Pro. The FIFA games were amazing graphically (although a bit jerky if speeded up) but the game play wasn t brilliant and was too easy to score. ISS wasn t great graphically, but was smooth and great to play. What was needed was a cross between the two. This is where  quot;This is football 2 quot; comes in. Graphically it s up with FIFA being very realistic with a lot of attention to detail. It s also very smooth and playable which makes it a great game. There are loads of tournaments and cups to keep you occupied, including the chance to play in season mode in various countries around Europe. A nice touch is that not everything is accessable at the beginning. The more trophies you win the more extras you get, including other tournaments, stadiums and game modes (including invisible player mode which is a great laugh when you re playing your mates after a few beers  ). This keeps the interest alive for a lot longer.Another nice touch is that you can create your own teams to play in exhibition games.Overall this is definately the best footie game around at the moment       ', '    This is my fave F1 game, it beats all others hands down.It has a good mix of realism and fun, its not too realistic to be borong but not too arcadey to only be fun for a minute.The graphics are great, sharp and clear. The options are plentiful and allow a lot of control of how the game plays, including weather, damage etc.Of course, being made in  97 the game is a little out of date, but I still love it. I bought it when it was released and I am still playing it now. The tracks are well detailed, and although the game slows down at time the engine is generally a lot better than the buggy original.Available for only    20 now, this is a must for all F1 fans, it is alot better than all the subsequent games. The pinnacle of F1 games on the PS.     ', '    This was the original Gran Turismo, and like Metal Gear Solid, when this first came out we all loved it The game is simply driving, and claims to be nothing else. It pits you against 5 computer controlled cars in a race to the checkered flag. Doesn t sound special does it? Let me tell you it is.There are over 500 cars to buy, all fully upgradable and tweakable, about 20 course to race around and tens of tournaments to enter. The graphics are amazing, the best on the Playstation at the time, and the replays of the races featured almost photo realistic cars.You start with 10,000 credits, enough to buy a second hand banger  Win a few races, upgrade you car or buy a new one. And so on, till you were driving the beasty Skyline GTO or a brand new Dodge Viper.What made GT great was the realism, the handling and physics were great. It was only let down by a lack of any damage to the cars.Even after all these years, still worth buying      ', '    What an excellent deal here  Basically, you get one sexy looking console with 4 features to it ( Audio CD, DVD, Playstation 1 games and Playstation 2 games) all for    299. I know that looking at that price it seems quite expensive, but if you think about it, buying all of these pleasures seperately, it would cost you a helluva lot more than that  I know it has been said that the DVD  quality is really poor and not worth using, but that is utter crap  I have seen this beast in action and there s no crap going on here   The visual and audio quality are just as good and clear as a domestic DVD player. The other great thing is that it plays not only the new PS2 games but the old PS1 games aswell  Some of the PS1 games even improve their graphic images when put into a PS2 console        ', '    I recently rented this game from blockbusters because I read a review on here saying that it was quite good. I liked it so much that I had to go and buy myself a copy  The hospital is like a hillarious cartoon because everything is so chaotic and you have to keep in control. The receptionist is so funny because she never stops talking, announcing that the hospital is full of litter and a caretaker needs to clean it up. Sometimes the machines break down and you have to fix them.I haven t yet completed Theme Hospital, as I am only on Level 2 at the moment, but it is so addictive. I just can t stop playing it. This is the best game I have ever bought, and I recomend it to everyone who has spare time to kill.I hope you all enjoy playing it as much as I am at the moment.xx Sally xx     ', '    The ultimate game for both Richard Branson and Gerald Corbett   You can run your own trains, buses, planes and ships and make a fair mess of it in the process It s a strange game really. If you have the Deluxe version, you can choose from  of 4 environments which to existing users of the original game is pretty strange. There are pre-set scenarios for you to play with; one of which mirrors the South West (without foot-and-mouth on the farms to our relief).It s dead straightforward to do: build transit systems where you think you can make a profit. Why not have a whole transport exchange in a town, where you can put a train station, bus and cargo station, airport/heliport and a dock together  Quite a big complex to construct.You can get patches for Transport Tycoon, but I found in the original version that they weren t necessary really. You can make a massive profit without cheating really. It s just a case of anticipating demand in areas and allowing for it.This is a great game if you want to plan how a transit system really should work. It might also be the only game of it s kind. Though if you want smaller scale (transit systems in a city), may I recommend Traffic Giant, which you can put in trams and such like. Traffic giant reviews can be found on ciao.com.     ', '    In all my life, never have I had so much fun in a hospital The main idea of the game, for anyone who has not yet played it is this......you are a manager of a hospital and it s up to you to keep a high reputation, a big fat bank account and of course, as many cured patients as possible. This is such an addictive game, once you start a game, you really just can t stop. The very first week I bought the game, I was playing into the very early hours of each morning Seriously, I cannot recommend this game enough. Every PC user should have one. Its like this.. But not to worry, just get one of the handy-men to fix it, asap.I m sure you ll all agree...An overall FANTASTIC game, for those who have.An overall FANTASTIC game, for those who haven t.:)     ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re a fan of simulation games with a quirky twist, *Theme Hospital* is a gem that’s hard to put down. This classic PC title brilliantly blends management strategy with a healthy dose of humor—think eccentric patients sporting bizarre ailments and a receptionist who’s as funny as she is efficient. The game’s charm lies not just in its gameplay but in these lighthearted touches that keep the experience entertaining and fresh.

From a gameplay perspective, *Theme Hospital* nails the addictive formula of building and running your own medical empire. You’ll find yourself obsessively optimizing layouts and staff, all while juggling the cleanliness of your hospital. Yes, cleanliness isn’t just cosmetic here—it’s a core mechanic. Neglect it, and you’ll face hilarious yet gross consequences like piles of vomit and rat infestations, which can tank your reputation and awards. This adds a satisfying layer of challenge and realism that keeps you engaged.

While the graphics are simple by today’s standards, their cartoonish style perfectly complements the game’s humorous tone. The sound design, including quirky patient noises and catchy background music, further enhances the immersive, fun atmosphere.

One thing to keep in mind: the game’s addictive nature means you might lose track of time as you try to perfect your hospital. For those who love simulation and strategy games, this is a huge plus, but casual players might find the micromanagement a bit intense.

Overall, *Theme Hospital* stands out as one of the best sim-type games ever made, offering a unique blend of humor, strategy, and replayability. If you appreciate games that don’t take themselves too seriously but still deliver deep, engaging mechanics, this title is definitely worth your time—and your wallet. Just be prepared to clean up some virtual vomit along the way!

product_reviews: ['    Well, how many times have we complained about hospital waiting lists ? Staff shortages ? General incompetence ? Now we can get a taste of the other side of the issue ... kind of   In the CD-ROM computer game, Theme Hospital, it is up to YOU to build your own hospital, design the layout, hire the staff and have it all finished in time and within a set budget. It is your responsibility to make sure the hospital is well heated, has enough seats, toilets and vending machines - or your patients will suffer   This is my favourite part of the game, as it is fun to see how your design works out.Once the hospital is up and running, there are endless patients to cure. You need to have the right staff and equipment to diagnose the illnesses and be able to treat the patients well enough. ', '    Every so often I frequent games I loved as a child. For whatever reason, I became addicted to them. Whether it be something on one of the older Nintendo consoles, controlling lives (or destroying them) on The Sims, or as in this case, creating and controlling a hospital.The follow-up to Bullfrog s highly successful Theme Park, Theme Hospital allows players to create their own hospital. As the name suggests, the game puts you in the driving seat of running a variety of hospitals.Unlike it s predecessors, such as Theme Park, Theme Hospital takes the concept of management sims a step further, by actually giving you goals to achieve. For those hard-to-diagnose cases, there are X-ray rooms, cardiology exams, high-dollar scanners, and the like, and before long you re even ready to build an operating theater and put scalpels in the hands of those crazy doctors of yours. As for the diseases and conditions, they aren t your typical fare: alongside gastrointestinal-type ailments such as the squibs, you have folks with Elvis Complex (who do indeed show up in Elvis leisure suits), invisibility, Bloaty Head (just pop their head and reinflate it), Slack Tongue (chop chop), Baldness (wait ll you see how to cure that), and an assortment of silly afflictions. Of course, you have your basic fractures and uncommon cold cases, as well. Each condition is more funny than serious (especially in terms of how it is contracted), but keeping your hospital up and working efficiently gets to be pretty serious when you ve got patients queued up in the aisles, tired doctors recuperating in the staff lounge, diagnostic machines temporarily down for repair, emergencies bringing in a number of new patients who must be cured quickly if your reputation isn t to suffer, earthquakes shaking things up, and epidemics popping up and wreaking havoc. Patients can be pretty messy, as many of them tend to throw up all over the place. If you don t have enough dependable handymen around to clean up the mess, the Ministry of Health will be all over you. The graphics look surprisingly good even today - although 1997 graphics certainly don t compare to those of recent games. There is a decent variety of looks among patients, and it s almost worth killing a few of them just to watch them ascend to heaven (or, on occasion, drop through the floor on their way to an alternate destination). The game is simple enough for anyone to play and enjoy, although things get pretty challenging as you progress deeper into the game. A lot of games today sacrifice fancy graphics for actual gameplay, but Theme Hospital is the kind of game you enjoy playing years and years after its release. Can you do a better job than the NHS trusts, well probably is the answer.So what do you do?  The first step with any hospital is to build the rooms into the frame of the building.  You need GP rooms, Psychiatric rooms, wards, pharmacies, a staff room (or your doctors go mad, denoted by a rather amusing graphic of a doctor with hair all over the place), toilets and operating theatre as the pure basics; other rooms become available such as X-ray, scanner etc and as you move up the levels you can have a training room to improve the skills of the haphazard junior doctors.  Moreover, there are some rather strange illnesses, which require special clinics and you need to build these or you will not be able to cure the poor afflicted patients.  (To list them would spoil the progression of the game, as the weird afflictions are revealed as you progress through the levels.)Ok, you have the building and rooms, now you must equip them, with seats, desks, medical equipment, sinks, plants, fire extinguishers etc.  The list goes on and the further you get into the game the more options are available.What no staff.  Yep, a hospital without staff is a rather strange place, so you need to hire doctors, (general, surgeons, psychiatrists) of various levels, (only a consultant can train junior doctors so acquiring one of these is quite important).  It is not just doctors that are required, you need receptionists so patients know where to go and handymen, to clean, maintain the hospital machinery and water your plants.All this requires money, so you need patients, they pay for a consultation and treatment and the more patients you cure the better your reputation, so the more patients you get, the more money you can make and thus the more expensive machinery and treatment rooms you can afford, to charge the patients more money, improve your reputation  and get more patients and more money, the circle goes on.That is the basics, but you can also research new cures for illnesses and buy new buildings to expand your hospital.  As simple as it seems the hospital runs like chaos and you are forced to deal with problems, too many patients, long queues, means more diagnostic rooms being needed.   Doctors sulk and threaten to resign, do you pay them more?  You need surgeons to perform operations, good handymen to make sure the heating works, the problems go on.  All this can become quite absorbing, as your hospital has to cope with emergencies of patients with a certain disease, cure them all make lots of money, be slack and your reputation suffers.  Epidemics spring up, that need containing, or a health officer will slap you with a hefty fine and there are even earthquakes which threaten to destroy all poorly maintained machines, killing all patients in the vicinity.  (These earthquakes are rather annoying as you can get 5 in a year, sorry, not realistic.)  Patients who see vomit will also puke so make sure the handymen are cleaning the place properly.With each hospital you have goals to meet, (i.e. a certain amount of money to make, a certain approval rating, or a number of cures to effect) in all of this you are competing with the other local hospitals for the patients custom and a poorly paying medical insurer can result in poor cash flow, which will necessitate a trip to the bank manager.There is a large deal of management depth to this game and if you like roller coaster tycoon or theme park etc, you will enjoy this.  But what about the game play and graphics.The game play is simple, using a set of point and click drop down menus, which are fairly self explanatory, there are stats to look at as with all management games and you can point and click on members of staff to give them their orders, although they do have a certain degree of self sense in what they do.  The game play cannot be faulted the control engine is simple with nice graphics and could be picked up in 30 minutes of play.The graphics?  This is now an old game, being released in 1997, so the graphics are rather blocky, but they are not bad and do not detract from the game.  The depiction of the strange illnesses and the way they are cured is rather fun and well animated and even by some management games released in the last year or so the graphics do not look that dated.At first Theme Hospital is brilliant, but as the game progresses it becomes repetitive, OK you get new rooms to build and new illnesses to cure, but the basic actions are the same.  Most management simulations suffer from this problem, but Theme Hospital seems to suffer more than most.  But it looks good, plays well and for    9 on budget it is a bargain and will provide you with at least 60-70 hours entertainment before you get bored.  But once you are bored it will stay on your games shelf gathering dust.The manual is well written and provides good guidance in places, listing all that you need to know, although my only criticism is that the manual is a bit simplistic.The game is amusing and lighthearted, with almost cartoon like animation in places and was a groundbreaking release in 1997.  A quick tip, do not hire Geoffrey, you will only get sued   Worth    9 of your money and this is a game that is regarded as a classic, I would not go that far but it is good.  But the imagination involved in the comedy disease situations is great In summary if you like management games, take it, if you hate them, leave it. Well Theme Hospital puts you in charge of running and maintaining a hospital. You have to make sure that your hospital runs smoothly, you must diagnose patients and treat them correctly, and if you kill a patient, then it s on your head, can you ever live it down? Installing Theme Hospital. -------------------------- Theme Hospital is extremely easy to install, you simply take the disc out of its jewel-casing, insert it in your CD-ROM drive, and the installation program should appear automatically. Just follow the instructions, the game requires Direct X, so install it if you haven t got it. The installation program creates a program called Bullfrog, and adds this to your start menu. To play the game, make sure you have the Theme Hospital disc in your CD-ROM drive, click on the start menu, then Bullfrog, then Theme Hospital, and the game automatically loads. Playing Theme Hospital. ----------------------- When the game has loaded, you will have to choose a nickname for yourself, I usually call myself Dr Death, because I normally kill a lot of my patients, not on purpose though. Next a mad professor appears, and pulls down scroll with a picture of a skull, the skull is divided into segments, and each segment, gives you an option, such as load game, new game, quit and continue game. If you start a new game, you are asked whether you have played before, if not tutorial mode is activated, and you will be thoroughly guided through the game. Theme Hospital is played like a board game; you start out as an amateur, and have to progress though different hospitals, gaining experience in each, until you eventually retire with an impressive record and bags of money. Setting up your hospital. ------------------------- The first task is to set up a hospital, gain a good reputation, bank a bit of money and treat fifty percent of the patients. If you succeed, you will be promoted, to a better hospital. When you enter your first hospital, all it consists of is a huge empty space; you now have the task of building the rooms. You will need to build a GP s office, which is like a doctor s surgery, the doctor working in here, will examine the patient, and determine what condition they are suffering from. A psychiatric room is used to treat patients with mental problems. A pharmacy is essential as most patients can be treated with drugs. Later on in the game, you will need to build an operating theatre to treat patients with more complex conditions. There are also various clinics that are needed such as an inflation clinic and slack tongue clinic. Your hospital also needs facilities for patients and doctors alike, such as toilets, and staff rooms. Later on in the game you can train new doctors, in special training rooms, and you can employ researchers to research new conditions, and new drugs. Install a few fire extinguishers, put in a couple of drinks machines, place a few plants around the place to brighten things up, and not forgetting the reception desk, every hospital needs a reception desk. Your hospital cannot operate by its self so you will need to employ doctors, nurses, handymen and receptionists. Opening your hospital. ---------------------- Once you have completely set up your hospital, you are ready to open the floodgates. In Theme Hospital land, the patients problems are not like our, I m telling you, they can develop some very strange complaints. That s about it really, just make sure you treat your patients, don t let your hospital become dirty and ensure that you have all the latest medical machinery. Sound. ------ The music in this game is controlled by a jukebox; you can pick any of the eight tunes, but be warned they will drive you insane after a few minutes. The tanoid announcements are invaluable, in this game, as it tells you where your doctors and nurses are needed. System Requirements. -------------------- You will need Windows 95/98, 75Mhz processor, 16MB Ram, 55 MB of free hard disk space, and a 4x CD-ROM speed. If you have a higher processor, this game is great, you can whizz through all the commands, and there is no waiting around for certain commands.
