product_reviews: ['    The first glucose based product that I can recall was Lucuzade, and it claimed and in fact still claims to give energy to body and brain. Since that far off day in the sixties                  ( yeah I know you were all on better stuff than Lucozade, but you see I was a good boy ) there have followed various versions and products with similar claims. I have tried most of them and really don t feel that much different once I have taken the so called miracle drink, so I stopped purchasing them and went back to good old Lucozade, although I never really took to their claims either.  In the past few years the gimmick has changed from drink to sweet, one such sweet being Dextro Energy, and this is the product I shall review now. I m starting with an open mind, well OK slightly ajar, well to be perfectly truthful I m not expecting very much from this product.  Dextro Energy comes in various flavours, but it is the Original and the Blackcurrant I shall be talking about since these are the only one s I have tried, and indeed been able to find. The Packets for each flavour are almost identical apart from only the colour, the original flavour being an orangey yellow colour and the blackcurrant being a nice purple colour, as one might expect. The packet is perhaps 5 to 6 inches long and each individual sweet 1inch wide by just over a half inch high and one quarter of an inch thick making a decent sized sweet. Although I have never actually counted them I would estimate there to be about 15 sweets in each packet which retails around the 55p mark.  The sweets are all chalky looking with a slight hint of the colour for each particular flavour, and they are very slightly concave in the centre of there nice rectangular shape. On placing an original flavour on into my mouth the first experience I had was that of melting. Any moist part of my mouth was causing the sweet to simply disintegrate in my mouth allowing the sweet liquid to easily flow down my throat and start delivering that lovely glucose to my tiring system. It was causing I kind of moist foam in my mouth which was an odd sensation to say the least, but a nice kind of odd. The sweet taste was not a sugary sweet, not quite that intense. It did not take too long for the whole sweet to dissolve and disappear from my mouth, but the sweet flavour stayed for quite a while.  As I waited in anticipation of the energy rush I ogled the packet containing the Blackcurrant flavour sweets and decided to try one of those. The experience here was the same as previously described, but this time the flavour was stronger and made the whole eating of the sweet much more pleasurable. So now that I had consumed two of these energy tablets as the package claims they are, I would soon be re-charged and ready for anything.  The wait was beginning to tire me so I made a quick cup of coffee which I guessed was probably going to do more for me than the tablet. It was well after finishing the coffee that I made my final decision. I was neither here nor there, didn t feel any more alert, didn t feel any more energetic, just pretty much felt the same as I had before. So I tried another two of the sweets which although had not yet had the desired affect were very nice as a sweet. Too many might make you feel a little sick and maybe even a bit bloated, so I would advise no more than 2 -3 at any one time with a substantial break in between taking anymore.   I continued with my normal routine eager to feel that hit of energy, but alas as the day wore on the hit never arrived and I went home just as knackered as I always do, so to this end I have to conclude that this is just another gimmicky idea, even if it does taste pretty good. I don t by any means feel my 55p had been wasted I did enjoying eating the sweets and in fact may even purchase more at a future date, but certainly not as an aid to boosting my energy levels.     ', '    I have only heard of these recently as my husband had to buy some as he is a diabetic and can have these when his blood sugar levels go down Dextro energy helps to bring his sugar levels up slowly.I m not sure how they taste as i have not had them but the pack says they are orange flavoured with viamin C i m not sure if they come in other flavours.Ther are 14 tablets in a pack and they are quite big in size and thick they are white in colour and have dextro etched on them. When you eat one of these they enter directly to your bloodstream.The ingredients are:dextro (88 ), Maltodextrin, citric acid, flavouring, anti-coking agent, (magnesium of fatty acids, vitamin c.nutrition information per 100genergy 159kj/36kcalprotein 0gcarbohydrate 91gof which sugar 82.6of which dextrose 87gfat 1gfibre 1gsodium 0.1gvitamin c 1.0mgThese are good if you need an energy boost or if you suffer with diabetes and need to carry something around with you incase your sugar levels go to low and you need to bring them up and want to do it slowly.     ', '    Dextro Energy Tablets - Orange flavourThese things have been around for a long time - I used to eat them while still at college so about 6 years at least   I haven t tried them but there are different flavours - I stuck with what I know and got the good old Orange flavour while having a wander around local chemist type shop. Cost me 47p so still not expensive to buy. You can also find them in the bigger supermarkets,  as I ve seen them in Asda and Tesco.What are they for ? Well they re meant to give you a quick fix / boost of energy, they are high in glucose type stuff (Dextrose) which the body turns into energy quickly  to fuel your body, and keep you going. Much the same idea as Lucozade and energy sports type drinks but in  tablet  form.What are they like ?They come in a easy to open handy size small packet and are not like tablets in the usual sense...you don t swallow them....you just eat them.  ( PMSL@the thought of trying to swallow one of these   ) The tablets are off-white sort of colour rectangle shapes with Dextro indented into them. They have a chalky / powdery look and feel to them, but they taste good - like orange flavour. They disintegrate in your mouth pretty quickly and don t taste chalky...they melt away in your mouth nicely leaving the aftertaste of..yep...orange - no nasty aftertaste.Directions: take 1-3 tablets as required, always eat proper meals.Ingredients: Dextrose (82 ), Maltodextrin, Anti-caking Agent (Magnesium Salts Of Fatty Acids), Citric Acid, Vitamin C, Flavouring.Well I dutifully ate 3...and...Not a lot   No magical boost of energy over here. Though upon disregarding instructions completely and munching half a packet of them as I remember doing in the good old days...(also have fond memories of pro-plus seeing me through some though days..lol...bad me.) ...there is a slight boost on eating twice the recommended dosage but nothing spectacular, nothing that a good strong coffee couldn t do for me really. But maybe thats just me.On a more serious note though if you have small kids then I d be sure to keep these things out of sight/reach as they do look and taste like sweets...pretty nice sweets at that.So unless you re going to eat them by the packet-load  - which I wouldn t recommend...they re not really anything fantastic for your average person, don t know if would be more suited to the more sporty people out there, as unlike most energy things this has no caffine. In my humble opinion you d be better off putting the kettle on *or* getting some Lucozade sport drink - which I find perks me up enough to get me through those horrible  I ve got a cold / I m so tired / I feel like poop  kind of days. Though that said at least they ve got vitamin C in there so maybe a good little stand-by for colds, for those who don t want the more caffine based pick-me-up s.Not for me...I ll stick with my Tea / Coffee / Pepsi / Lucozade thanks very much...all tried and tested and get me through a rough day     Thanks for reading, Manda.x     ', '    WHAT ARE THEY AND WHAT S IN THEM?Available in Orange, Lemon, Blackcurrant or Tropical flavour, Dextro Energy tablets are a small, rectangular tablet with a sweet taste and powdery texture.  The company producing them claim they provide an energy boost for after sports, during long drives, for extra concentration at work and to quickly perk you up when you feel your physical or mental energy dipping.IngredientsDextrose (82 ), Maltodextrin, Citric Acid, Anti-caking Agent (Magensium Salts Of Fatty Acids). Vitamin C, Flavouring.Each packet contains 100  of an adult s RDA of Vitamin C - however, be aware that whilst this information may not be deliberately misleading, it is not advisable to take an entire packet at once, so the percentage you will receive of your daily vitamin C per recommended dose (1-3 tablets) is between 7  and 21  - not quite as good, but still a useful supplement.In a small rectangular packet, these fit easily and unobtrusively into a pocket or bag, so are easily carried with you at any time.HOW DO I TAKE THEM?It s recommended to take between one and three tablets at a time, depending on how effective they are for you and how much of a boost you need.  However, rather than taking the entire dose in one go, Dextro Energy advise consumers to take half a tablet every 15 - 20 minutes, up to the maximum recommended dose, as this allows your body to adjust - otherwise your levels simply shoot up and then crash down, leaving you more  sapped  of energy than before.  It s important to make sure that you re eating a balanced diet as well - poor nutrition could be the source of low energy levels.HOW DO THEY WORK?The primary ingredient of Dextro Energy tablets, Dextrose, is a fast acting carbohydrate which, instead of entering the bloodstream after digestion, is immediately absorbed into the bloodstream to give an instant  lift .  I was first introduced to these a few years ago when, suffering from fatigue, my doctor suspected diabetes.  He took blood samples but, while waiting for the results, advised me to take half a tablet when I felt my energy levels dipping.  They did seem to work for me, but I m not sure if this effect was more mental than physical - I ll continue reporting my personal experience in a few moments.ARE THEY UNSUITABLE FOR ANYONE?  ARE THERE ANY RISKS?I ve researched, but can t find any reported cases of serious side effects relating to this product.  Of course, if you have a condition which requires you to monitor your blood sugar levels they probably aren t a wise choice   but I m sure that if you had a condition like this you wouldn t need to be warned   If you take too many you could suffer from nausea or stomach problems, so it s important not to snaffle the whole packet at once.It is vital to remember that long-term fatigue could be a symptom of an underlying medical problem, so you should always mention this to your doctor - don t just struggle through using energy products to help you cope.WHAT DO THEY COST AND WHERE CAN I GET THEM?The tablets cost approximately 45p for a 47g packet and are available from Holland and Barretts, Tescos, Sainsburys, Morrisons and other large supermarket chains.  With such good availability and reasonable price for a packet, I would say these are definitely good value.OK   YOU VE TOLD ME THE FACTS - BUT WHAT DO YOU THINK?First and foremost, I think these are absolutely delicious - dangerously so   It s very hard to limit myself to the recommended 1-3 tablets, as the taste and texture is very similar to that of  Swizzles  lollies or the  Pez  sweets I m sure most people had as children (the ones you load into a canister and then shoot into your mouth - like death by processed sugar).  Though they are a solid tablet, they dissolve very quickly on your tongue with a pleasant gentle fizzing sensation, which adds to the whole enjoyable experience.  Though sweet, they re not overly so and they don t leave an unpleasant aftertaste as some products do.  Personally, I ve only ever tried the orange variety (I found my favourite straight away and have never wanted to stray) but reports from others who have tried the rest of the range are very favourable - apparently they re all as lovely.I mentioned earlier that I was introduced to these a few years while waiting for diabetes test results, and that they did seem to work at the time.  However, I suspect that this was psychological  - I believed that they would work and this tricked my body into perking up.  I ve tried them many times since then and haven t noticed any huge physical effect, although I am aware that they could potentially be improving my concentration levels   something I wouldn t be actively aware of.  I think they key with this product is not to expect the same effects you would get from a product such as Red Bull, which has stimulant properties.  Dextro Energy tablets aren t designed to stimulate as much as to  work behind the scenes  providing a boost when you need it most.  If you want an instant boost you can really feel, I would recommend a product containing caffeine - if you re looking for a healthy method to assist your body, this is an excellent product to try.     ', '    When I was at grammar school it was  The thing  during exams to brag about how many hundreds of hours of revision you did each night, using dextrose energy tablets to sustain you during your midnight toil.I figured that I needed all the help I could get so a I bought a couple of packets of these and took them home.  My desk was covered with my year s notes, text books, library books (No Internet in those far off days of antiquity) and my faithful energy boosters.  We piled into the Tudors and Stuart, Boyles law and quadratic equations until the first yawn.  Not being totally sure if the yawn was induced by tiredness or the intricacies of quadratic equations, I carried on.  After the next yawn I opened the packet and popped a couple of these in my mouth.The taste========A pleasant fruity taste, slightly chalky texture, I found the sweets to be a good size to suck. The effect=========To hear my fellow pupils talk (We weren t students, in those days you had to go to university to be one of those) these were like amphetamines.  Too many and you would be wired for days.  Sadly for me this was not the case.  With the latest Led Zeppelin LP on the turntable (When Stairway to Heaven was newly released, fer chrissake) booming around the room, with my parents hammering on the ceiling below and my sisters moaning about the noise I woke up some hours later.  I had nodded off on my history notes.  Moreover, I had dribbled onto them.  If I looked into the mirror I could clearly read the details and dates of the Tudors clearly imprinted on my cheek.  To this day I can remember the date of the Battle of Bosworth Field and I owe my history O level success to Dextro Energy.  I was forced to wash it off before entering the exam room the next day.All in all, as a sweet these are very pleasant but as an energy boost I found them to be quite useless.  Maybe I have a strange  physiology but they worked better as sleeping tablets for me     ', '    When I was younger I had an undiagnosed, overactive thyroid condition which would raise it s ugly head from time to time. When I was eventually diagnosed my Doctor told me that at times my thyroid had possibly been underactive also and this explained my fluctuating weight and the low energy levels I often had. Until I knew what was theproblem I tried many things in an attempt to stabilise my weight and give me some energy.Amongst the products I tried was Dextro Energy Tablets. These tablets to me taste like large, hard, sherbet sweets. They almost taste like those hard lollipops that used to be called traffic lights. You know the sherbet ones. They are very hard but dissolve quite easily on the tongue and this is usually the recommended way to consume these tablets. They have a dry chalky taste initially. The recommended dose is one to three tablets at a time.Dextro Energy Classic tablets basically consist of:Dextrose (82 )MaltodextrinCitric AcidAnti-caking Agent (Magensium Salts Of Fatty Acids)Vitamin CFlavouringYears ago there was just one flavour-original. These days there are five flavours namely-blackcurrant, lemon, orange, tropical and classic.The ingredients vary slightly in the tropical flavour. This one has added Thiamin and vitamin B6, vitamin B12, Folic Acid and much more. However I do not know how significant the amount of these extra ingredients are.A packet looks quite small and so fits easily into your pocket and, or, handbag. The pack weighs 47g and usually costs 47p so these tablets do appear good value. However I am not so sure. I wonder really how useful products such as this are. I quote my medical history at the start of this review as a cautionary tale. If you have sudden problems such as lack of energy it could simply be too many late nights or alternatively could be the sign of something such as a thyroid disorder or Diabetes. Most of the time it will not be anything significant but it does need checking.These tablets state that they are not a replacement for food and do need to be taken alongside of a healthy diet. They claim to give you a quick boost of energy if you should need that for example for a sports activity. Perhaps in such instances they would do the trick but I doubt it. However there are plenty of high energy, healthy foods which would work just as well.I guess overall these tablets will be ok and not cause you any problems if you are healthy and if you only use them rarely. Taken too often as a replacement for sufficient amounts of healthy food and enough sleep they will not work and may either mask a healthproblem or cause dietary problems.If you have never tried Dextro Energy tablets by all means give them a go. They taste nice if you like a very sweet taste but exercise caution as with all such products.They are on sale at Chemists, some supermarkets and shops such as Boots. They are available over the counter but it would be as well to read any instructions and contra-indications on the pack.Thanks for reading.Copyright Eiley 2007     ', '    Dextro Energy products (formerly Dextro Energen) were first introduced at the Berlin Olympics in 1936, Dextro now provides energy supplements for both athletes and busy people alike. In my younger days I was a dancer, dancing for many hours at a time in my youth, ballet, tap, modern stage, ballroom and Latin American, disco, jazz ballet and contemporary dance to name but a few styles and often I would need an energy fix and my ballet teacher, April advised that I tried Dextro Energy tablets. In those days you could get only orange or original flavours. I favoured the orange ones and a packet was usually found in my dance bag. (My friends tried mine and like them so much they went out and brought packets for themselves).The long established Dextro product comes in a convenient tablet form that I prefer, which makes them handy to carry in the pocket of a sports bag or handbag and also easy to consume. There is 80  dextrose in these tablets and this is the only substance that the brain can absorb directly, thus stimulating the recipient. These glucose tablets are devised and developed to provide an instant source of energy for both mental and physical activity. I found that they really worked for me and gave me that boost when I was flagging. The Dextro range is produced in a factory in Krefeld, Germany and has been producing the pressed tablets for many years. Dextro believes that they are the dextrose tablet leaders. In Germany they have 60  of the dextrose tablet market. They export 30  of production to mainly Europe, including Austria, BeNeLux (Belgium, Nederlands and Luxembourg), Denmark, Finland, Great Britain, Norway and Sweden; also amongst this 30  Hong Kong is a large consumer *Taste*The taste of the orange tablet is a pleasant tangy flavour. The tablet dissolves quickly in the mouth leaving a sweet powdery texture. It is not unpleasant but if you do not like sweet things then this product may not be for you. The powdery texture is that of the compressed glucose. I tend to eat mine in two bites, but Shane, my hubby, like to suck them. I cannot comment on the other flavours in the range, as I have not tried them recently.*Usage*They are often used on an everyday basis, as consumers see lack of energy, as one of the top five health concerns. It helps to boost you when you are flagging.The next use is in sports and other physical activities. It is good for after activity recuperation and during warm downs. I eat these tablets between classes as it gave me a boost before class. Lucozade drinks only made me gassy as did other energy drinks, so I tried to avoid them.Concentration is the final common usage, it is shown that it can reduce driving errors in excess of 80  (source Keul et al, 2001) and for those that suffer energy lapses during the day, the tablets provide that  instant fix    When I need to concentrate that bit harder or last that bit longer, Dextro will keep my brain and body in gear .*Flavours*There are five flavours in the Dextro Energy tablet range:BlackcurrantLemonOrangeOriginalTropical*Availability* Dextro Energy tablets can be found at Boots, Holland and Barrett, Superdrug, Tesco and all good chemists.*Cost*50-55p from most good pharmacies (Allied) containing 10 tablets per packet 47g. In comparison Lucozade tablets cost 47p per packet from Asda.*Other Products*The other products in the range consist of   sticks ,  minis  in a re-sealable box with a  click  lid and  power bars  for  on the go  usage. They are less commonly avalible.*Website*For more information go to http://www.dextro-energy.de/ but this is a German site.     ', '    Dextro energy tablets come in five different flavours which are original, orange, blackcurrant, lemon and tropical.  I haven t tried all of these flavours but have tasted the orange and lemon varieties.  I have done a bit of research on these as well as testing them myself to help in my review.  Before I go any further I would like to make the point that they are not designed to be eaten as sweets.AIMSDextro energy tablets are designed to give a quick energy release to help in endurance sports for example marathon running or other sports which last longer than thirty minutes or so.  These tablets are high in glucose which the body uses as an energy supply to fuel your exercise.  This means that you are topping up your body s glycogen reserves so that you do not run out of energy as you are exercising.PACKAGINGThe packets of dextro energy tablets are white with  dextro energy  written on the packet in a different colour depending on the flavour, for instance the lemon flavour has yellow writing on the packet.  There is a small picture of a man running on the packet to show that this product aids sports performance and also a picture of a man s head as these tablets are also meant to help mental concentration.TABLETSBoth the lemon and the orange flavour tablets are a plain white colour with the word  dextro  imprinted on them.  There is not much of a smell to them unless you have them right under your nose, and even then there is just a very faint smell of either lemen or orange depending on which flavour you have bought.  The tablets have an almost chalky kind of look about them.TASTEThe lemon and orange flavours are both quite pleasant with the lemon personally tasting a bit nicer than the orange.   The flavour of these tablets is not very strong at all with just a hint of lemon or orange.  If you suck these they will melt in your mouth and despite the look they do not taste chalky at all.  When you are exercising vigourolsly and your mouth is dry the dextro energy tablets can be a little harder to eat and a drink of water is then handy.  I would recommend that you drink water rather than a sports drink when using the dextro energy tablets as your stomach may struggle to cope with the demands put on it with a mixture of both sports drink and energy tablets.DO THEY WORK?I would say that these definately work for me.  If  I am going out for a long run I will put two or three dextro energy tablets in my pocket and will eat one about every three miles.  I always feel a boost in my energy levels shortly after so in my opinion yes dextro energy works.  Also if  I eat one before going to the gym I feel I get a boost when im there as well.  I think that dextro energy tablets would help boost your energy in a lot of other sports as well for instance sports like football, rugby and a lot more.OTHER USES1) Mental PerformanceDextro energy tablets are also said to boost your mental performance and alertness.  The brain needs a steady supply of dextrose, and if this supply dwindles it can result in a lack of concentration, so these tablets can help.  While researching these tablets i also found out an interesting fact that while the brain accounts for only 2  of your body weight it uses 20  of the body s whole energy expenditure.  This means that the energy intake from these tablets should help to feed much needed energy to your brain and help concentration levels when you are tired.I tried a couple of dexro energy tablets one day at work when i was feeling particularly tired and i felt that they did help my concentration levels that day but i don t think they would make any difference on a day in which you were up to date with your sleep and refreshed.2) Use For DiabeticsThe use of dextro energy tablets can help diabetics who suffer from mild hypoglycaemia between meals.  This condition could be caused by the wrong calorie intake, alcohal or too high a dosage of insulin.  When warning signs occur like dizziness, fatigue and irritability a fast-absorbed carbohydrate is needed so dextro energy tablets would be perfect to help in this instance.  Obviously check this out with your chemist first who will give you more advice on this matter.AVAILABILITYI buy dextro energy tablets in boots for about 45p per packet.  They are also available in Tesco, Holland   Barrett, Sainsbury s and most local and national pharmacies.NUTRITIONThere are 12 calories, 3.0g carbohydrate and a trace of fat per tablet.  Obviously calorie intake is not really a worry with these as you will be burning a lot more calories through exercise than what you are taking in.CONTACTSYou can contact the makers at:Unilever Bestfoods UKCrawleyRH10 9RQVERDICTI would give dextro energy tablets a rating of 8/10.  They help me for the purpose I need by giving me the extra energy to help me go that little bit further either when i am out for a run or at the gym.  I have tested a similar product from lucozade and the dextro variety definately came out on top meaning I will stick with this brand in the future.  As for helping with mental performance and concentration i am still undecided although it is preferable to having endless cups of coffee i reckon.  Just remember not to eat these as sweets, having just two or three at the most and you will feel the benefit.Thanks for reading my review, all comments welcome.********UPDATE********This is just a small update on my review to say that I have now tried the tropical flavour of these dextro energy tablets and they are now my favourite flavour, even better than the lemon or orange flavours.     ', '    Ciao s  Product Of The Week  is, apparently, an everyday about-the-house kind of product that we can all have a bash at reviewing.  So you ll be as surprised as I was, then, when I discovered - after searching through every cupboard, grubby cubbyhole and even broggling around in my wife s knicker drawer - that I didn t actually have a pack of Dextro Energy Tablets in my home.Having been stumped by last week s  Rolled Gold+ (on USB Memory stick, no less)  by the Rolling Stones, I was determined not to fail again this week at not having such an everyday product around my house, so set off in to town.  Tuesday afternoon was wet and dismal and Newmarket High Street isn t the greatest place to go shopping at the best of times, seeing as it s usually full of wannabe jockeys trying to climb onto the heady heights of a bar stool and real jockeys trying to get you to notice them in their Ferrari 430s and their Lamborghini Gallardos whilst stable girls hover around waiting to get drunk or laid, usually in that order.Eventually, though, having braved the weather, the delivery drivers who like to park on the pavement and the stable girls, my mission was complete.  In my pocket was a splendid, shiny new twin-pack of orange flavoured Dextro Energy tablets purchased from boots for the princely sum of 99p.  It wasn t until I got home and opened the pack to start contemplating my review that I realised that Ciao s Product Of The Week is nothing more than a shameless advertising prank designed to encourage us hapless members of the site to go out and spend more money on a product we don t need in order to lift a flagging vendor s product sales and line Ciao s advertising budget with a few more pieces of gold.Still, in for a penny in for a pound as the saying goes and, having tried numerous other providers of energy-based liquid drinks and snacks such as Red Bull, V, Tescos Value Energy Drink, HappyChap and something from France amusingly called Pschitt, I decided I d give these little tablets a bit of a try.Purchasable in single- or twin-pack variety, not to mention available in a variety of flavours including lemon, blackcurrant, tropical and orange (blimey, it s almost as complicated as buying a pack of Durex condoms these days), Dextro Energy tabs are, compared to much of their competition, a relatively inexpensive method of boosting your energy.  The predominant ingredient is Dextrose, otherwise known to many of us as glucose.  A natural substance, Dextrose is infused straight in to the blood stream which allows for a rapid energy release and therefore does not need to be digested.  This means that the results are more effective.  Or, at least, they should be.I opened my pack of Dextro Energy tablets with a little tingle of excitement and placed the first cube on my tongue.  Fizzy with a faint orangey flavour, the tablet immediately dissolved on my tongue and lasted about as long - and was about as satisfying - as my first sexual encounter.  The second tablet lasted no longer and the third disappeared just as quickly.  In fact, before I knew it I had consumed all fourteen cubes in less than ten minutes and felt as randy as a hibernating squirrel.To be fair to these little tablets, they aren t too bad.  The problem is that they don t deliver a boost of energy in the same way as a Mitsubishi Evo VIII kicks you in the kidneys when the turbo comes to life and the long-term promises do fail to materialise but, if you re feeling a bit low or are starting to yawn whilst driving your car, Dextro Energy tablets will stave off fatigue and keep you going until the next set of tacky motorway services.  Along with carbohydrates such as sugar and dextrose, these tablets also deliver a whacking great surge of Vitamin C.  In total, they offer absolutely no protein, but provide 1549kJ/364kcal of Energy and that equates to roughly the same percentage as that offered by Red Bull.  That, of course, means absolutely nothing to me and seems as complicated as the Offside rule is to girls or explaining what torque means to my mother but still, it sounds good and doesn t rely on Taurine to boost energy levels.I quite like these little tablets.  I ve never found any energy substitute to be particularly suitable, but Dextro Energy don t do too bad a job and aren t ridiculously expensive.  As long, of course, as you don t eat the entire packet in one go.They re safe for diabetes sufferers and apparently two cubes of Dextro Energy correspond to one bread unit which, I think, is a good thing and means you won t die.  Not being a diabetic yet (it seems like I might be one soon as diabetes is now apparently quite trendy amongst the beautiful and the rich) I m not exactly sure what that means but, according to the website, the cubes have become an indispensible  friend in need  for diabetics who recognise the onset of low blood sugar levels.Good for them, then.In short, Dextro Energy tablets are great for a quick uplifting experience without the need for expensive and illegal narcotic substances.  There s no advice on the website or the packaging as to how many you should take in a given period of time, but I d steer clear of consuming the whole packet in less than ten minutes.  The energy boost might be great for a quick two minute fumble under the duvet with your missus at four in the morning, but the resulting fizzy farts are enough to leave questionable stains in your underpants.     ', '    I first remember being introduced to these odd large tablet like energy sweets by my mum when I was a young child.  My mum felt these were better for us than a  normal  packet of sweets.  When I first tried them I didn t think very much of them but can now quite honestly say I am addicted to them THE CLAIMSDextro Energy was first introduced in 1936 when the Olympics were held in Berlin.  It is claimed that Dextro Energy can supply our bodies with energy we may have lost through our busy lifestyles, or for athletes who may need that little extra boost, it is also said to aid concentration.  Dextro Energy is made up of 82  Dextrose, which is basically another name for glucose and a natural form of sugar, usually found in fruit and honey, this is the ingredient which is supposed to give us our energy boost.  Our bodies naturally produce blood sugar, which gives us our energy.  Dextrose does not need to be digested, being absorbed directly into our blood stream and then on to our brains.THE PACKAGINGThis 47g stack of energy sweets is wrapped in a foil and paper wrapper with the little pull and tear strip at the top, which releases the first couple of sweets. These sweets, although hard, once in the mouth have quite a crumbly feel to them, they slowly begin to turn to a sweet, sticky paste before gradually melting away.  I have to admit once I ve had the first one I can t stop until they are all gone, usually devouring the whole packet of 14 sweets in about 30 minutes, which I later regret   Even after eating the whole packet I can honestly say I have never yet felt a boost of energy.  I love these sweets for their flavour and texture and the fact that they are different compared to any other sweets I have tried and I would recommend them but, I would be lying if I was to say that I would recommend them for their energy boosting powers.PRODUCT INFOThe packet weighs roughly 47g and contains 14 sweets.  You have a variety of flavours to choose from - Original (which I would still describe as having a bit of a fruity flavour), Orange, Blackcurrant, Lemon and Tropical, my favourite being the orange ones.  They contain Dextrose, Maltodextrin, Flavouring, Anti-Caking Agent, Citric Acid, Vitamin C and Flavouring.  There are 12 calories per sweet, which isn t too bad I suppose.One thing I do know these can be good for, other than the taste, is for diabetics.  My brother-in-law is a diabetic and I know these can possibly be of benefit if a diabetic is suffering from a hypoglycaemic attack.You can purchase these sweets quite easily in most chemists from 45p - 55p.At lunchtime I decided to go out to my local chemist and buy a packet (55p), just before I dismiss the energy boosting properties completely, and probably because talking about them in detail gave me a bit of a craving   Ok after devouring the packet minus one each for the kids, I suppose I do feel a bit more alert, a bit more in the mood for working, but I don t think I m going to start doing cartwheels around the office.Overall I would definitely recommend these sweets for their flavour and the fact that they probably are slightly more healthy than a normal packet of sweets and yes I do think I probably feel slightly more alert after eating the packet, but cannot guarantee their energy boosting properties.     ', '    Dextrose: Quote from a medical dictionary :-  Better known today as glucose, this sugar is the chief source of energy in the body. Glucose is chemically considered a simple sugar. ', '    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~What are Dextro Energy ??~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Dextro Energy are a brand of energy boosting sweets/tablets which are rather sweet tasting. My favourite ones have to be the blackcurrant because they taste much sweeter and fruitier than the lemon variety.  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Price And Availability~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~I usually buy my packet of Dextro Energy sweets from Semi Chem and they cost 48p for a packet containing approximately 14 sweets, which is fairly cheap, considering most chocolate bars and packets of crisps cost near enough 50p theese days.  I have also saw the Dextro Energy tablets for sale in alot of pharmacies and supermarkets such as Tesco, Morrisons, Boots, et so they aren t only sold in selected retailers which are hard to find, they are almost sold anywhere, but your best to find them in your local pharmacy as it will save you looking around in shops trying to find them.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Do They Really Give You A Burst Of Energy?~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~To be completely honest they don t give me a burst of energy, after taking one or two tablets I dont feel like running a marathon or vigorously cleaning the house. I m sure most mums are like me because they skip breakfast whilst trying to get the kids ready for school, and on the way home the or whilst doing the shopping the awful feeling its you. Dextro Energy tablets present an interesting option for those seeking a quick sugar boost, especially for diabetics managing mild hypoglycaemia. Their primary strength lies in this targeted use, where the rapid absorption of glucose can be genuinely beneficial. For healthy individuals, the tablets are generally safe for occasional use, but it’s important to remain cautious—overreliance might mask underlying health issues rather than address them.

From a practical standpoint, the tablets score well on convenience and sensory appeal. Their small, portable packaging makes them easy to carry during sports or busy days, and the variety of flavors—orange, blackcurrant, lemon, tropical, and classic—adds a pleasant touch that many find enjoyable. The chalky, powdery texture dissolves quickly in the mouth, which some might find agreeable, though it’s a matter of personal preference.

In summary, if you’re looking for a reliable, fast-acting glucose source—particularly for diabetic needs or occasional tiredness—these tablets are worth considering. I had it implanted at the recommendation of my doctor because I can t use contraceptives that use both oestrogen and progesterone, because I suffer migraines which can be made worse by oestrogen, and the implant only uses progesterone.How it works************The active ingredients in the implant is progesterone which works by stopping you from ovulating (releasing an egg) and it also thickens the mucus in the cervix which makes it difficult for sperm to get past.How affective is it***************The implant is effective immediately if you have it fitted whilst on your periods or seven days after insertion if your not. Having it fitted*************Having it fitted is really easy and took about 10 mins.Firstly I had to have a local anaesthetic. Once that had taken effect the doctor made a 1cm cut in my upper arm then the  implant is inserted under the skin using a special tool like a giant injection. The doctor then used butterfly stitches to help the cut heal and bandaged it. I needed to keep the bandage on for 24 hours and after that I needed to use a dressing for a week until the insertion site had healed. It isn t really painful but was a little uncomfortable.Side effects*********Heavier or lighter periods. Then using a long pair of tweezers he removed the implant.I was then bandaged up for 24 hours and needed to use dressing for the next week.My experience *************For the first couple of months after having the implant put in I had no periods at all. Most of you will have seem some of my other ops and will know they are usually of the nice travel / university variety. This, however, is something new. So some questions, then, to ease us in gently (ooo err) What Is Implanon? *************** Implanon is the brand name of the current contraceptive implant available in the UK. Norplant, a similar device, was available in previous years but since this one is no longer being prescribed, if you want an implant then Implanon it is. How Does It Work? **************** It   s a hormonal method but unlike the pill you don   t have to remember to take it every day. Implanon is a contraceptive in the form of a small implant which is inserted under the skin of your upper arm, on the side closest to your body.  It contains the hormone progestogen (which is a synthetic form of the natural female hormone progesterone) which is released into your body at a steady rate for three years. It stops your ovaries from producing eggs and thickens the mucus in your cervix to make it hostile to your boyfriend/husband/lover s friendly sperm.  A doctor has to be trained in the insertion and removal of these implants, so you might find that your own GP doesn t offer this as a method of contraception. This involved asking whether I had planned to have a child in the next three years, as they don t like fitting implants as short-term contraceptives.  The intention is that it will stay in for three years, although it can easily be removed earlier than that if it was necessary - my own view is that if you only wanted it for a year or so, it would be a bit of a waste, and we all know the NHS hates that................don t we? Anyway, getting back on topic, I also had to fill in a medical history questionnaire, and discussthe choice with the doctor so he could be sure that there wasn t another form of contraception which would suit my lifestyle better. They took a urine sample for a pregnancy test at this time too, as it s important that you re not pregnant when the implant is put in as it could damage the foetus. This is a tube 40mm long and 2mm wide (about the size of a hair grip).Afterward it did feel a little bit sore and they applied a pressure bandage to the area to prevent bruising, the pain which I can only describe as being punched in your arm by your younger brother lasted no more than 2 days.The first 5 months I was on top of the moon no periods, no headaches, and no bald patches or weight gain and certainly no babies, then suddenly I got a period which was not a problem it was not painful and no where near as heavy as I remembered, it was when I got to the third week of my period that I became a little distressed ..I went to see my doctor who offered me something to control this but I refused on the grounds that I just did not want to mess with my body and was just happy to know that I was not dying , I have also suffered from some of the other symptoms breast tenderness, and patches of dry skin but nothing like I had experienced with the injections.So okay the everlasting periods are not exactly something to rave about but this does work and as I can not take the pill I personally think that this is the best thing on the market for someone like me, even if I could take the pill I would still opt for something like this as I have the memory of a goldfish with amnesia and having to take something on a regular basis is not a good idea.Obviously if you are going to consider using this kind of contraception do bear in mind that there are side effects and just like the injections were not for me this might not be for you, however I have read several reviews on this and most people seem to get on okay with it.  Another thing to think about as well with the implanon is that after 3 years you do have to have it removed and they will insert it into the other arm which can be difficult unless you re ambidextrous.On a whole I would say that this is the best thing on the market especially if you are like me and cannot take the pill, I have been using this product for just over 5 years now and although I still do suffer with irregular and prolonged periods they are far and few and I think that it is better to put up with them rather than take a chance, I have heard from several people that they are scared of these because of the injection but I can reassure you that my MMR was far more scary and painful than this.     ', '    Firstly, I will explain all you need to know about implanon before giving my controversial, radical opinion on how implanon could help wipe-out teenage pregnancy.What is Implanon? Implanon is a contraceptive implant. The implant is a small flexible rod about the size of a matchstick, which is inserted on the inside of the upper arm. It is sited on the opposite arm to which you write with, just under the skin. On thin people it is slightly visible, but on the majority of people it is unlikely to be visible, but can be felt by gently pushing the site. Oooh no - its not visible on me anymore - I must try and shift a few pounds, I could see it a few months ago.How does it work?The primary action is to stop the body from releasing an ovum (egg) every month.It thickens the mucus in the cervix, so that those pesky little blighters (sperms) can   t get through.It also changes the lining of the womb (the knock on effect is that it alters the bleeding pattern).How effective is it?It is very effective at preventing pregnancy, as no human error can occur once it has been implanted (when I say human error I mean forgotten pills and the like).It is not affected by anti-biotics, diarrhoea or vomiting.It may be affected by certain other drugs -  e.g. anti-epileptic and anti- TB drugs .Who is it suitable for?Women whose bodies cannot tolerate oestrogen.Most women looking for hassle free, reliable, long-term contraception. Scatter brains who forget to take daily contraception.Who isn   t it suitable for?It is not suitable for women with hormone dependent cancers, active thrombosis, severe liver disease, unusual vaginal bleeding or an allergy to the components of the implant.Insertion and removalMust be fitted by a qualified practitioner.The woman must confirm that she isn   t pregnant before insertion.If it is inserted on the 1st day of the menstrual cycle, protection from pregnancy starts from that day. If it is fitted at any other time an additional contraception must be used for the next 7 days.A local anaesthetic is given to numb the skin and then a small incision is made in the arm. The single rod is then inserted into the incision site. The incision is minute, therefore no stitches are needed.A pressure pad and bandage is placed on the arm to reduce bruising and help the site settle, this should be removed after 48 hours. During which time a small layer of tissue forms naturally around the rod holding it in place.Once you   ve had the implanon inserted, you should receive an information card. This should state the date that the implanon needs to be removed. If you don   t receive this, ask the health care practitioner that inserted the implanon for it.The removal is just the same process as the insertion. You can have another implant fitted at the same time as having one removed.The rod needs to be removed after 3 years (although it is believed that this will soon be increased to 5 years). It can be removed sooner than this if you request.Your fertility should resume to its normal level shortly after the removal of the implant. The majority of women will be ovulating within the first three months after the removal of the implanon.AdvantagesAvailable on the NHS.Can be removed at anytime - pre existing fertility returns very quickly.Very effective at reducing the risk of pregnancy.Can cause light periods or the abstinence of periods altogether.Suitable for women who cannot tolerate oestrogen.Not affected by stomach upsets.DisadvantagesSome women experience irregular bleeding patternsWeight gainAcneHeadachesExtreme side affects - mood swings, painful periods and hair loss.Conflicting reports on implanon You only need a follow-up appointment if you are experiencing problems with the implant, it can be checked when you have a routine pap smear. It needs to be checked after 3 months, then yearly.I personally haven   t had mine checked in the two years since its been inserted.* It is safe for breastfeeding women.* It shouldn   t be used for breastfeeding women.I had implanon inserted when my baby was 6 weeks old and I breastfed her for 16 months (Gasp, I hear you cry 16 months - are you mad?). I   m not aware of any effects on my baby.* The effectiveness of implanon is not reduced by variations in weight.* Implanon should not be used in overweight women.My sister-in-law is rather    cuddly   , she had implanon inserted 6 months ago and has been told that her weight makes no difference to the effectiveness of implanon.My ExperienceThe following is a list of contraception   s that I have tried:1. Pill - Pill pregnancy following a bout of tonsillitis (had my tonsils out as soon as I had baby no.1)2. Injections - Split with my husband, didn   t have injection renewed. Husband started to come back round to see baby no.1 - soon I was expecting baby no.2  3. Coil - Had to be removed following infection. NOT of the STD variety. Apparently infections are quite common with the coil.4. Norplant - The old implant which implanon superseded. Had the implant inserted a week before I had the coil removed. Had this removed after 4 years as I wanted baby no.3. Had it removed in the September found out I was expecting in the November.Implanon - I have experienced no problems whatsoever with this. It has been completely hassle free. By far the best contraception that I have experienced.The opinion was as a guide only.  If you require any information on implanon or any other contraception please speak to a qualified health practitioner.My Radical Opinion. I think that it would be a good idea to offer implanon to girls aged around 15. There could be a government campaign targeted at promoting and offering implanon to teenage girls. Possibly sending awareness    workshops    into schools. These workshops could offer advice on love and life as well as giving girls the option to have an implanon implant as a form of contraception.The cost of one implanon is approx.    99, therefore it would be financially viable as this is far cheaper than the true cost of helping a teenage mum raise her baby.Teenage pregnancy is on the increase and has been steadily rising for years. These young women have babies for a variety of reasons including contraception failure, human error and a whole host of other reasons.Where I live it appears that babies are the latest fashion accessory instead of  mobile phones, designer clothes etc. for an alarming number of young girls.I believe that as a nation we need to address the issue and bring our incidence of teenage pregnancy to the lowest in Europe.This opinion wasn   t meant to patronize or offend anyone and I am truly sorry if it has done so. I am aware that there are thousands of responsible teenagers around and I know that there are (and have been) brilliant teenage parents. I   m not letting young boys off the hook, just trying to think of a solution.I look forward to reading your views.     ', '    Hi, As most of you know I had my little boy in July 2002. After I had him I decided that I definatly didn t want any more children for quite a while yet As I was breast feeding my baby, you can only have Progesterone only hormones, which don t change (or stop) your milk, so I started to use the Progesterone only Pill (POP) or the Mini Pill as it is better known. You have to take this at the SAME time every day - I couldn t cope with this so I went to my GP and found out about the Depo Provera injection, which I had (see my Depo Provera Op) On the first night of having the injection, I had quite bad side effects, and I didn t want these again  I made my mind up to try something else.My friend works at the Family Planning Clinic, she told me about Implanon (the contraceptive Implant) I had heard about this before, but never thought anymore about it. I went to my Family Planning Clinic to see if they would give it to me, I had a short discussion in private with the advisor, she took my blood pressure, weighed me and informed me in detail about Implanon. She also gave me a very imformative leaflet all about it. I was made an appointment to have it done, although this was at a different clinic with a GP, as the person who does this has to be specially trained. **A Bit More About It***Implanon is an implant, it is a plastic rod, 4cm in length, and 2mm in diameter. (sounds scary) it is filled with the hormone Progesterone, which is released in tiny amounts over the three years. It is inserted on the inside of your upper arm, Don t worry, you don t feel a thing as they give you a local anasetic to numb the area, It is then inserted via a large needle - if you re scared of needles, don t look  It lasts for three years, when this time is up, you have to have the implant removed (again they numb your arm) if you wish, they can put another one in at this time. It is supposed to be very expensive, therefore, they don t like to remove it before it has run out, however, if after 18 months you decided you wanted a baby, they would, as it is your right.**What They Did To Me**When I went to have my implant put in, I was called into a room with a couch, I was asked if I knew all about it and if I still wanted it done. I did. I lay on the couch and was asked which arm I wrote with, I am right handed so they did it in my left arm (I don t know why) First they cleaned the area, then they got a very fine needle and gave me an injection to numb the area, three minutes later when this had worked, he put in the implant, this is just like a thicker needle, (you can t feel it) He pushed the needle about 4 cm up my arm, then pulled it back out. That was it  He put a plaster and a really tight bandage on (to stop the bruising) When I got home I took off the bandage, (even though I was advised to keep it on for two days) I was lucky, I didn t get a single bit of bruising  I kept the plaster on for three days. During the three days, my arm was a bit weak and I found it hard to pick up heavy things, (like my little boy ) apart from that there were no problems at all. When I took off the plaster there was a tiny little red mark where the needle has gone in (about the size of a small spot) On the fourth day, my arm was completley normal and I could feel the implant when I prodded my arm  Some people think it s disgusting but I like it  Two weeks on and I have forgotten about it  I love it  no pills, no nothing  It doesn t interfere with sex at all, unlike some other methods. I have to go back to the clinic next week, to see how i m getting on about it and to have any questions answered. After this, you only have to go back once a year **Side Effects**Some people complain of headaches and feeling sick.Also bruising after the implant is in place for the first week. I didn t get any **How Effective Is It?**99  although NO-ONE has become pregnant using this, they can only write 99  to protect themselves, against suing incase someone did fall pregnant.**How Long Does It Take To Work?**1 Week, If you are currently using the Depo injection, you are covered straight away **Who Can Have It?**Most healthy peopleBreast Feeding MothersThree weeks after the birth of your child**Who Cant Have It?**People who are very over weight, have cancer or like diseases. **How Much Does It Cost?**Free on the NHSIf you are thinking about this, I would strongly reccomend it  I will definately be using it again  and I can promise you, It DOES NOT HURT Take CareJade x     ', '    I was so pleased when the new Implanon contraceptive came out, I obviously find it very easy to get pregnant as only one of my children was planned and the other two are the results of one forgotten pill and a condom which looked ok, but obviously wasn t. I took the combined pill for quite a few years but used to get really bad headaches with it and the mini pill suited me better but remembering to take it at the same time every day was a chore. So when the now obsolete Norplant implant came out I was only too glad to try it out, and I didn t have any side effects from it, so 5 years not having to worry about contraception was brilliant, when it came to having it taken out I presumed I d be able to have another one put in, but in the mean time they had stopped using it as it didn t suit everybody and at the time there wasn t an alternative implant. So I was really glad when I was told Imlanon was now available, especially as it is only one rod as opposed to the 6 with Norplant. The Implanon, however only lasts for 3 years. It was a lot easier to put in than Norplant, it comes in its own applicator, which looks like a large injection and the implant is inside the metal rod, the doctor puts a small amount of anaesthetic in the top of your arm and when it has taken just pushes the metal rod in your arm and inserts the implant just under your skin, which only takes about five minutes and doesn t hurt. Afterwards it ached a bit, but not much and bruised slightly. You have to go back for a check up after 3 months and then every year.As for side effects they vary from person to person, but in general periods are light or non existant, and as I had no side effects with the Norplant it will most likely be the same with Implanon.     ', '    I had been on the combined pill for over 7 years and I thought my body could do with a break. Being in a long distance relationship, I could afford to go without worrying about contraception for about a year, but moving to the US required me to look again at what was out there. It came down to a choice between the shot and the implant, and as I would have had to pay for the shot here in the US, I went for the implant.***So what is it?***The implant itself is about the size of a matchstick, 40mm by 2mm or thereabouts. It s slightly bendy, and is placed just under the skin in the inside of your upper arm. You leave it in place for 3 years (2 if you re of a heavier build) and it slowly releases hormones into your body.***How does it stop you getting pregnant?***Several ways. It stops eggs from being produced every month, and should one get produced anyway, it thickens the mucus in your cervix to help deter any wandering sperm. Some literature states that it makes the womb lining thinner too. It says it is 99  effective, but I have also read that no one has actually got pregnant on it, when used properly, but they could not say it was 100  for obvious reasons.***What side effects can I expect?***Now here is the difficult bit. I have read reviews here and on other websites about women who had side effects. Me, personally myself, I have had hardly any, but I ll go into that later on. These are some of the side effects you MAY get, and I do mean may: Headaches Heavy periods Long periods Mood swings (some serious) Hair loss Breast tenderness Periods stopping Pimples***How do you get one?***I got mine via the local family planning centre. I had to make an appointment to have a chat with a nurse and tell her why I wanted the implant as opposed to anything else. That appointment was very friendly. I asked her if moving abroad posed a problem (you cannot as of yet get Implanon in the US, so I will have to go back to the UK to get it removed), and she was fine with it. An appointment was made for the implant, but they wanted to put it in when I was on a period. As it turned out I was a week late, so I had to push the appointment forward a week, but that was no problem.***How does it get inserted?***I went to see the doctor, and she took my blood pressure, which was a little high (due to nerves). She took me to another room and lay me on a couch. Another woman was there who was being trained to insert the implants. I was told exactly what would happen and told to relax.First of all, the area was numbed (you seriously don t want this inserted without numbing believe me, and if you don t like needles, look away now and until the doctor tells you you are done ). Needles don t bother me, so when she started with the numbing, I had no problem. She injected me about 6 times in a wheel pattern, but after the first injection I felt nothing. The other woman then opened the packet with the needle and implant in, and the implant fell out. This is not  a good thing . The doctor told her to get another one, which thankfully didn t fall apart. I felt nothing whatsoever when the implant went in, only a little pressure. It was over very quickly, only about 20 seconds, and the doctor put my finger on my arm so I could feel the implant. She then put a pressure bandage on, and told me to get up slowly. I felt a little lightheaded but otherwise fine.I asked her how soon it would work, and she said it should work straight away as I was on my period, but she liked to give it 48 hours for the chemicals to kick in, and to use condoms in the mean time. Off I went with my new toy As it was, the numbing wore off quite quickly, and my arm ached like a mad thing. I had work the next day (data entry) and I couldn t use that arm at all. Even with the pressure bandage I got a huge bruise, and my arm wasn t back to normal for about a month. It says about 3 days to a week for it to heal, but expect longer with some people.***Long terms effects?***I have had the implant for 4 months now. I didn t have a period until last week, and that period was normal. Whether I ll get one every month now, or every 4 months I don t know, but I ll keep you updated. I ve had no other side effects, and it s great  It really does seem to vary from woman to woman though, so don t take my experience as the written rule. I was told at the first appointment I had, that if I had no problem with the combined pill, then it was likely I d have no serious side effects with the implant. So for those ladies out there that have trouble with the pill, you may want to think twice about the implant.***Anything else?***Yup, it s a great party trick, if you press the one end, the other end sticks up and grosses people out  Seriously, expect the area to remain tender for quite a while. Also, check it s there every now and again. Reports have been made of either it not being properly inserted in the first place, or it wandering off slightly. If it s in properly, your body will make an area of tissue around it (because your body sees it as a foreign object and holds it in place so it can t do any harm), and hold it there. Finally, if you do want it taken out, your fertility returns almost straight away, but you need to have a good reason to get it taken out. They cost the NHS a fair bit, so they don t like removing them without just cause.Overall, I would recommend this to anyone not wanting to start a family for at least 3 years, but please do read up on it first, and make sure you understand every aspect of it. Be aware of possible side-effects. If it s good for you, then have lots of fun with it ;)     ', '    Very early on I realised that condoms were not going to work for me. I was with the man who would be come my husband so STDs weren t something I had to worry about. I had 2 fairly happy years having depo provera shots but my doctor made me stop.The next logical option was the implanon contraceptive implant. It lasts for 3 years and is proven to be one of the most effective contraceptives available. Unlike the pill or barrier methods, there is no chance of user error or forgetting to use it. I m on my second implant now and have had 5 years of very light but irregular periods and no worries at all  I m not good at keeping track of my cycle anyway so unfortunately I can t really say how irregular I am. I would estimate at about 2 to 3 months between periods.Having the implant fitted is not pleasant but it s only once every 3 years and, for me at least, infinitely better than getting pregnant. There is a bruise which lasts about a week and having them changed is a bit more surgical but not at all painful. To have the implant fitted is a bit like having a really big injection, you do get a local anaesthetic so it doesn t hurt. When you have it changed the nurse does have to cut with a scalpel, it s a small incision which leaves a scar about the same size as the original insertion scar. The only thing I felt during the procedure was a slight tugging sensation.When the implant is in place you can normally feel it. The nurse will ask you to feel it before she sends you off so you know it s there. My first was shallower than the second so I can t always feel it now. I was lucky in that I haven t ever had any side effects from my contraception.I would recommend to anyone who wants hassle free contraception but remember it is no protection from STDs.     ', '    I was on this pill since I was 14 from Feb 2001-Jan2004. I had no problems with the pill but  I was finding it difficult to remember to take them and this isn t a good thing when you re paranoid about having a baby I discussed changing my contraception with my doctor on a number of occasions and after discussing all the possible options, we decided Implanon would probably be the best option for me. I was given the prescription after blood pressure tests etc and went to collect it...If you aren t currently using this method, are thinking of using it and are scared of needles...DONT open the box I went down to the doctors when I was next on my period taking my boyfriend as support to hold my hand. The doctor was very nice and told me to relax and lie down on those horrible bed thingies  Now... I have a BIG BIG fear of needles and no matter how much they tell you it s just a little sting.... in this case...however much we hate to believe it...it is  They administer a local anaethetic to the area and you feel nothing...zilch  When they inject the implant you feel a little pressure and its not exactly comfortable but since when was having something metal and sharp shoved in your arm comfortable?They then placed a bandage round my arm to reduce bruising and I went home...All the booklets say you may not get a period whilst using this method of contraception and for six weeks...I didnt. Then...one fateful afternoon...it came and it didnt go away for 7 weeks  After a month I went to the doctors but they said to leave it a few more weeks. I went after 6 weeks of starting my period and was told the same thing...so I went to see another doctor who has since prescribed the contraceptive pill as a method of purely regulating my periods. It was horrible and nasty and the worst thing that could have happened (after getting pregnant).I m told the implant is as effective in preventing pregnancy as the pill....in some cases even more so. So where are the benefits? Its easy to insert (ALWAYS GET YOUR DOCTOR OR A PERSON FULLY TRAINED IN THIS AREA OF CONTRACEPTION TO FIT THE DEVICE...yes it comes with instructions but you dont need to use them ). Its also effective for 3 years so you dont need to worry about pregnancy for that time...and to boot...the hormones saved me    3000 in plastic surgery  OK...so a list of side effects    @ for good ~ for bad:@ the hormones can make your breasts grow~ periods may be irregular and/or heavier@periods can be lighter, less painful etc@ ~ which ever way we look at it your periods may stop~ the hormones may cause you to gain weight~the hormones may cause acne@risk of conception is reduced by about 99 ~ Condoms must be used to protect against STDs such as Chlamydia and HIV and AIDSOne thing I will say (as a piece of factual information I have read about hormonal contraceptives which is not intended to lecture etc) is hormonal implants are an abortive method of contraception in that if for some reason the woman ovulates and her egg is fertilised, the  cluster of cells  is expelled with the next period (generally). This is a piece of information from a pro-life website I read whilst researching for ethics. Again, it is not intended as a lecture cos I myself agree totally hormonal contraceptions...I hope if anyone is confused about  their contraception, this review has been of some help. Just remember, condoms should always be your number one priority if there may be a risk of Sexually Transmitted Diseases.     ']

If you’re considering Implanon as a long-term contraceptive, here’s a balanced overview based on user insights that align with my own research and reflections. Implanon is highly effective—over 99% at preventing pregnancy—and it’s especially appealing for those who want reliable, low-maintenance contraception without daily pills. It’s great that it doesn’t interfere with sex or get affected by stomach issues or most medications, which adds peace of mind.

Accessibility-wise, it’s encouraging that Implanon is available free on the NHS in the UK, making it a cost-effective option. However, some younger women or those new to hormonal contraception might face hurdles obtaining it due to healthcare providers’ reluctance, which is a concern I feel needs addressing through better education and awareness.

The implant suits breastfeeding mothers and women who can’t take oestrogen, broadening its usability. On the flip side, it’s not recommended for women with hormone-dependent cancers, severe liver disease, or active thrombosis, so medical consultation is essential.

Side effects vary widely: some users report no issues and find it hassle-free, while others experience irregular bleeding, mood swings, weight gain, insomnia, or acne. Personally, I think it’s important to weigh these possibilities carefully and discuss them with your healthcare provider. The insertion and removal require a minor procedure by trained professionals, usually quick and with minimal discomfort, which is reassuring.

Interestingly, some women notice improved hormonal balance and relief from premenstrual symptoms, which could be a bonus for those struggling with hormonal fluctuations. The implant lasts three years, and fertility returns quickly after removal, making it a flexible option for those planning future pregnancies.

Overall, Implanon stands out as a reliable, long-term contraceptive with some caveats around side effects and access. For anyone considering it, I recommend thorough research and open conversations with healthcare providers to ensure it fits your health profile and lifestyle.

product_reviews: ['    ~ What is Indian Head Massage? ~Indian Head Massage originated, as it s name suggests, in India over a thousand years ago. The origin of shampoo comes from a Hindi word  champi . Being  champi-ed  meant having your head massaged. It began as the way to keep your long hair in beautiful condition and has become a part of daily life.IHM can ease headaches and stress as well as helping to deal with scalp and hair problems. It aids localised blood and lymphatic circulation, relieves eyestrain, boosts the immune system, relieves muscle tension, and helps restore joint movement. They can also relieve tension, fatigue, insomnia, headaches, migraine and sinusitis.~ Why do I have regular Indian Head Massages? ~In the months leading up to my driving test and my January A-Level exams I started having frequent migraines. I used to get them less than once a year but I was now getting them every week. They caused me to be off school for a day, which meant catching up, leading to more stress and therefore more migraines. I was at the point where I was worrying about getting them, which was triggering migraines as well. My mam regularly has aromatherapy treatments and she was talking to the therapist about my migraines. She recommended that I have an Indian Head Massage (IHM). Willing to try anything that might prevent my migraine attacks, I made an appointment. My first IHM was booked for the day before my first driving test. Unfortunately, I had a migraine attack that morning. The appointment was at 4.30pm and I was feeling a bit better so I just managed to get myself there, though I felt pretty ill the whole way through. Due to the fact that I still had the headache, which follows a migraine, the therapist couldn t give an in-depth massage. It still relaxed me immensely though. She recommended that, should I have a migraine on the day of an appointment, I should reschedule.      I now have an IHM every four weeks and so far they seem to be working, although my stress levels have obviously fallen as well which will also help me not getting migraines.~ What happens during the massage? ~When I go for the massage, I have a five-minute consultation with the therapist where we discuss how I have been feeling since my last massage. (The first massage I had the consultation was regarding the frequency of my migraines etc)She then leaves me to get changed and get under the blanket on the bed. I only need to remove my t-shirt and my shoes. I also need to ensure that I am not wearing any earrings, or a necklace etc. When she comes back in she checks I am ok and tells me what she is going to do. Today, as my stress levels have been low recently, she informed me that she would use balancing oil to help maintain the low stress levels.She started by massaging my neck and shoulders. This was very relaxing. She then moves on to massage my head, face and upper arms. It is a very relaxing experience, which relaxes all my senses. There is relaxing music playing in the background and the lights are low. The actual massage lasts 30 minutes. This time flies by, presumably because it is so relaxing.The movements of her hand over my head and face slow down towards the end of the massage. All of the massage is very gentle and soothing.When the massage is finished she leaves the room, to give me time to come back to reality. She returns about five minutes later with a glass of cold water. She then asks me how I am feeling, and leaves to me to get dressed. She tells me just to take my time, as if I get up to quickly I may feel a little bit dizzy. The whole appointment lasts around 45 minutes and it costs    20, I think it is worth every penny  After my massage I feel nice and calm and relaxed and I also feel quite awake and alert.Different places do the massages a bit differently. My mam had an IHM with a different therapist somewhere else. She said she was sitting on a stool, fully clothed and it wasn t very comfortable which made it difficult for her to relax.After the massage my hair looks very greasy as it is full of oils. I usually try and arrange an appointment so that it doesn t matter what my hair looks like so I can leave the oil in over night. It does make my hair feel nice and soft though, it just doesn t look very nice.~ Have I felt the benefits? ~As I have already said I haven t had any migraines recently (touch wood ) I think this is partly due to the massages but also due to my reduced stress levels. When I had my first massage the therapist told me that my neck, head and shoulders were all very tense and heavy. I could feel this as she was massaging me. Today my shoulders didn t feel as tense and she says she can feel the difference. She says my head is still heavy and tense at the back (which is where most of my headaches come from) but my forehead is more relaxed (where lots of my headaches used to come from)~ Do I need to do anything between massage to make it more beneficial?My therapist advices that I put ice on my neck for 10 minutes everyday to reduce the inflammation in my neck and lower head where most of my current headaches come from. When I do this it does feel much nicer.~How will I feel after the massage? ~ You may feel tired or dizzy after the massage though personally I haven t experienced either of these. The IHM makes me feel quite thirsty, this is normal and it advised that you drink lots of water after your appointment. There is also an increased desire to urinate (as the body eliminates toxins and waste materials and also due to the increase in your intake of water). Some people may experience aching muscles but this shouldn t last long.~ Will I continue to have, and do I recommend IHM? ~Absolutely  I hope to continue having IHM every four weeks or so to help keep me relaxed. As I am at school 5 days a week and then at work at the weekend, I sometimes feel as though I never have any time off. The head massage helps me to have an hour off and forget about everything. Also, I am hoping that if I continue to have IHM regularly I won t start getting frequent migraines again in the lead up to my final summer exams. I do feel better in myself since having these Indian Head Massages.Thank you for reading.         ', '    I have written about stress and depression and now for the next few opinions I will talk about different alternative therapies that you can try in order to elevate or reduce the symptoms of these particular conditions.
