', '    This review is about something I learnt at college very recently and now have just received a Diploma in. INDIAN HEAD MASSAGE----------------------------------? What is it?Indian Head massage has been practised traditionally in India for thousands of years and is part of Ayurvedic medicine system.This medicine is one of India s oldest systems. It promotes longevity of life though balancing of Mind, body and spirit.It was used on women traditionally to aid and promote beautiful hair. Oils were used too. They passed their knowledge and massages onto their families.New mothers massage their babies every day until they are the age of three and then they receive one every week. The children then learn and return the massage to their mothers. It becomes a circle and Indian Head massage is practised on all the family members in turn. A gentle man visiting the barbers as part of the treatment will finish off his haircut and shave with a head massage. Indian Head Massages are given on the beaches as part of relaxation by vendors. The whole Indian culture benefits and is seen to be a reason they tend to be more laid back and less stressed.The massage itself differs in different parts of the country and when it was introduced here in the UK by Dr. Narendra Metha in the 1970 s, it also incorporated, not just the head but also the back, upper arms and shoulders, neck and face areas too. This treatment had become westernised.Indian Head massage is a powerful therapy and had a positive effect on the whole person, Mentally and physically and can balance the body s energy centres, know as chakras.It is becoming increasingly popular and has many benefits.? Benefits?In this day and age everything is dictated by time and stress levels increase to all new heights. Indian Head Massage works on this complaint and helps to relax you. It is especially useful for people who work in the office environment as they are very often slumped over the office chair staring at the PC screen all day.Good for tension and relaxation, good for posture and muscle tension and stiffness. It is good for promoting restful sleep, insomnia, healthy hair growth and circulation. It can help skin tone and elasticity and reduces congestion. It eases eyestrain and reduces headaches and gives the person renewed energy and also encourages deep breathing and stimulates lymphatic drainage too.On an emotional level it can bring a feeling of euphoria and wellbeing too. It brings inner calmness and banishes mental fatigue. It aids concentration and rids mental anxiety and stress.Indian Head Massage also works on the energy bases called Chakras. It can help unblock and clear these and give the person rebalanced energy, rid of stagnant energy and revitalise their energy too.All these things are benefits and of course if you have regular treatments then your health will improve vastly.? The treatment?The treatment starts with a 15 minute consultation and introduction to Indian Head Massage. This is to put the client at ease and find out if the treatment will suit their needs. Whether they prefer oils to be used or not. Details are taken and are kept recorded for future reference and to enable me to check if the treatment is effective and whether I can change it to suit the client better. Or to check if a treatment caused a reaction, positively or negatively.Then the client is sat down ready for the treatment.The treatment itself lasts half an hour and any chair with a low back can be used or indeed you can buy a massage chair if you want to appear more professional. The beauty with this type of massage is that it is extremely portable and you can practice anywhere with as little apparatus or as professional as you want.The client does not need to undress and is asked to place feet on the floor to ground themselves and then breath in and out deeply to help oxygen around the body and calm themselves.The massage begins with the grounding process and gentle effleurage movements on the back. There are several types of massaging types and I ll explain these later. Next the upper arms are worked on and then the neck after. The client is requested to either have powder applied to the neck or to raise their collar whilst this is carried out, as the massage shouldn t be carried out on bare skin on skin. This avoids the skin getting hot and avoids the lack of effective massage. Following on next is the head massage its self.This part is where the oils come into play. You can either have the massage done without oils if you prefer or you can choose from one of the ones used to aid healthy hair growth and stimulation. Again I shall go into the different ones later.After the head massage comes the face part and finally the balancing of the higher Chakras. The Throat chakra, the third eye chakra and the crown chakra. After the treatment the client is asked to sit quietly and water is given to flush out the toxins.An aftercare leaflet is given with advice for things to do to promote the treatment you just received and get the full benefit from it.? Aftercare?The most effective way to allow your body to recover from a treatment is to go easy. Rest and try not to exert yourself after.Drink lots of water to flush out toxins and rehydrate the body.Eat light meals as eating heavily will take the energy from rejuvenating the body and use it all up on digesting the food.Try to avoid stimulants like tea, coffee, alcohol and cigarettes. They will hamper the full effects of your treatment.Also deep breathing will compliment your treatment.If you have had oil applied to your hair, there is aftercare for this too.Leaving oil on hair for at least two hours or indeed overnight will really make a difference to the condition of your hair. Often results in a shiny, managable, soft hair and scalp.Letting your hair rest from heat products and chemical treatments will also promote healthy hair too.? Affects after treatment?After receiving a treatment of Indian Head Massage you can feel mostly calm, sleepy, relaxed, a warm and feel rejuvenated.Sometimes though and up to three days after the treatment an affect known as a contra-action occurs.This can be anything from a dizzy feeling, nausea, headache, insomnia and feeling generally zapped of energy. This is the reaction your body can take to the treatment and although it shows that it has an effect it should be noted down in the therapist s records. As to try and ascertain what causes it and can be changes in future treatments. Also Indian Head massage should not be carried out less than three days apart. This allows the body to recover and balance itself.? Oils?In Indian Head massage oils can be used to help the treatment work to its full potential. Applied to the scalp and massaged in to the hair it works both on the inside and on the outside and there are several oils that can be chosen depending on the effect you desire.Sesame oil----------------Is a very popular oil in India. It is a good for balancing and is more suitable in the summer months. It is said to be good for the delay of grey hairs as well as nourishing and protecting the hair.Excellent for dry skin and hair and it contains Iron, phosphorus and calcium. It can also ease muscle stiffness and pain.It can unfortunately irritate sensitive skins though.Coconut Oil----------------Used in Southern India mainly. Comes in block form and melts in the hands before application.Excellent for hair and does really gives hair a glossy finish and shine.Also brilliant for dry and brittle hair and is especially beneficial to those with coloured or treated hair.Mustard Oil---------------Used mainly in the North of India and is a strong smelling oil.More suited for winter months.It is used for people with circulatory problems, colds, muscle stiffness and tension. It can help bring down swelling.It also can apparently cleanse the blood and increase heat and generate warmth.It can be an irritant to sensitive skins though.Olive Oil------------Easily available and is popular. This oil is good for moisturising dry skin and hair also increases body heat and can relieve muscle stiffness and pain.Sweet Almond Oil-------------------------Another popular oil and is easily available. It is high in nutrients, protein and vitamins A,B,D and E.Good for hair and moisturises and protects it.The oil also has a warming effect on the body so helps muscle stiffness and pain.Unfortunately it is not suitable for people with nut allergies.? Massage Movements?There are several types or massage used in the Indian Head massage. Here are the names and the benefits.Effleurage --------------This movement is the introduction to Indian Head Massage.It is also the finish movement.It is used in the linking of movements and continuity. The movement uses the whole of the hand and is gliding, smoothing and stroking action. It can be deep or superficial and is a medium spreader as in the use of oils. It is used in preperation for deeper moves and also aids the removal of dead skin cells.Frictions------------This movement either uses the whole of the hand the heel or the fingers. It is a rubbing movement and is good for localised pressure movements and helps to break down adhesions, frees up restriction in muscle fibres and aids absorption of fluid around muscle joints. It also creates heat.Petrissage---------------Is a deep movement including use of thumbs, heel rolls and finger pulls. It s used to reduce stress and tension, increase circulation and improve muscle tone and elasticity.It helps to remove waste products and promotes fresh oxygen and nutrients to the area.Taptoment----------------This is mainly a drumming action by the fingers on the area.It is brisk and rhythmic, hacking or tapping movement.Alternate hands are used and the move is also light, springy and stimulating.It helps muscle tone and elasticity, stimulates the nervous system and muscle contraction and also increases sweating.? Contra-indications?Unfortunately Indian Head Massage is not suitable for everyone, or sometimes part of the treatment has to be adapted so as not to cause damage.If there is a contra-indication then the therapist can refer the client to their GP with a covering note and seek advice from them. This is mainly to cover the therapist.Cuts, bruising, skin and scalp disorders, recent operations, skin infections and infestations, high temperature or fever, high or low blood pressure, Thrombosis, Heart conditions, recent blood haemorrhage, Nervous system disorders, Epilepsy, Migraine, Head and neck injuries, Diabetes, Cancer, undiagnosed lumps and swellings and intoxication.All of these are considered local or general contra-indications and need guidance from the therapist to follow the right course of action.? My thoughts as a newly qualified therapist?I enjoy the whole experience of Indian Head Massage and during my training I have both received and given Head massages. The feeling is so lovely and relaxing from both ends.I like making people feel calm and relaxed and re-energised and feel like I have helped that person in a way other conventional way of medicine has maybe not been so successful. I like the whole idea of touch and massage as benefitting the person inside and out. And is indeed a complementary therapy I am so glad I have learned and will hopefully use for many years to come on clients and on my own family. ? Further information?You can find any therapist in the yellow pages, or indeed in any alternative clinic up and down the country. They may be part of a hairdresser s salon or beauty salon.Average cost of a treatment is    25 and includes consultation.If you want to learn the art of Indian Head Massage for yourself then I highly recommend you obtain a college guide book and see what courses there are running on the subject.?  My course?I started off by learning an introduction to Anatomy and Physiology .The course lasted twelve weeks.Then I enrolled onto a VTCT Indian Head Massage Diploma level 3. This course lasted twelve weeks too. In this time I completed more anatomy and physiology and also had to complete tasks involving health and safety, Doctors referral letter, a case study and two full Indian head massages in front of the assessor. All of this had to be totally 100 per cent correct. So it was very daunting and quite stressful too.Two exams had to be taken and my work put forward in a portfolio to be verified by an external verifier. I can also now be asked to attend college up to seven months after passing the course to do a further Indian Head Massage to make sure I am totally competent.I have now got my certificate and can now get my Insurance sorted out to start practising.One on the course the materials you need are a beauty tunic and trousers, and oils and white towels.You can also purchase books or indeed borrow from the library.My top book is Indian Head Massage by Helen McGuiness and is pictured at the top of this review. Of course there are many others too.The total cost of my course was    155.? Websites?http://www.vtct.org.uk/welcome.htmhttp://www.fht.org.uk/home.aspI hope you found my review helpful and has given you an insight into this wonderful treatment. Thanks for reading this and looking forward to your comments.Shirley.     ', '    My wife has been on a full day introduction course for the Indian Head Massage. Of course I have been her first   8220;victim  8221; and I must say that I am very impressed by the technique. I am not going to tell you about the history or techniques of this massage, as I don  8217;t know any of the details, you would have to talk to my wife about that. I looked on CIAO just out of curiosity and was pleasantly surprised to find that a category existed about this subject.Let me tell you about my experience. We made sure the children were happy in another room watching a film and set up the room we were going to use will lots of candles and some gentle relaxing music playing in the background. The massage is worked over the upper back, shoulders, head and face. There are many different techniques used over the different parts of the body that are intended to relax the body and release the toxins in the body and to stimulate the inner energy of the mind and soul. During the massage there is colour visualisation and movement of the head to relax the muscles around the head and shoulders. The whole process takes about 30 minutes. Now I am not normally a great believer in these types of   8220;unusual  8221; techniques, but at the end of this massage I did feel very good. I was totally relaxed, but at the same time my mind felt very active. Following the massage it is suggested that you relax for at least an hour, possibly have a bath and drink plenty of water, have no heavy meals and no alcohol. If you have the chance to have one of these massages then I would highly recommend it.      ', '    My local college were holding taster sessions and included in these were the basic techniques of giving an Indian head massage.  I am interested in alternative therapies and although I may not want to become a qualified therapist quite fancied finding out some of the techniques that are used.The course ran for six two hourly lessons for the total price of    54.00.  As this was a taster course no exam was taken at the end.  On the course we learnt not only how to give a head massage but were also able to be a recipient.  We had to practice on each other which often led to fits of laughter or squeals of pain when the giver got a bit over zealous with the probing finger tips.  9679;A Short HistoryThe Indian Head Massage is well known as an ancient art in India.  It has featured in Ayurvedic texts. The three main Ayurvedic texts are the Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita and the Ashtanga Hridaya Samhita.dating back almost 4000 years. Most Western massage treatments do not pay as much attention to the head as to the rest of the body. In India The richer families would have their own personal therapist and these would have even be trusted to help choose the future partner for the bride to be.  9679;BenefitsAn Indian head massage is a great way to relax the muscles of your head, neck and shoulders.  Stresses accumulate daily which have been proven to cause a weakness in the fluids of the brain. An Indian Head Massage is thought to aid the circulation in your brain and also increase concentration. Your respiratory systems are also opened up following an Indian head massage.  9679;Further BenefitsYour hair is supposed to benefit from a regular massage and can become much shinier and healthierStretches the muscles of your neck and shoulders increasing mobility.Gets rid of body waste by stimulating the lymphatic drainage system.Headaches are relieved along with eyestrain.  9679;How Long Does It Take?A full Indian Head Massage will take at least 45 minutes but if you just want a headache relieved this can be as short as 15 minutes.  I have used a short massage to aid my sister s tinnitus and the improvement was quite dramatic.  9679;Do I Get Naked?Well you can if you like but as only the shoulders upwards are covered then it is not necessary and is usually performed through the clothes.  This is of course for a dry massage and if you want oiled as well then the top will have to come off.  Again it depends on whether a full Indian Head Massage is required or just part of.   9679;How Do I Start?I am actually only going to be describe the massage briefly. After all I am not writing a book, just letting you see how easy the basics are and can be added to if you decide to attend your own course which I hope you will.Wear loose comfortable clothing and prepare all your oils if used.Make sure a chair is available for your friend to get comfortable inDecide what oil you are going to massage into the head.  This will depend on whether your friend has dry, greasy, oily or normal hair.I decide to use Olive oil as my particular friend has very dry hair.  She also has mild dandruff so I have added a few drops of tea tree oil to the Olive oil  9679;The TechniquePour a generous amount of oil into the palm of your hand. Gently rub into the crown of the head using your fingertips.Add more oil to the sides of the hair and work your way back towards the crown.Still using your fingertips press quite firmly, in a downward movement.You have to create mild warmth by using small movements over one area.Continue to massage small areas and ensure you always work your way to the crown.When this has all been done we can start on the face.Have your friend close their eyes and stand behind her/himStarting at the sides run your finger through the hair, gently tugging as you work you re way backwards. Repeat this five times at least.Now gently use circular movements in front and above of the ears. Work your way towards the temples and again continue in a circular motion.Working down towards the neckAt the base of the neck you may find the muscles very taughtPlace your thumbs at the nape of the neck and using an up and down motion rub quite firmly.Tilt your friend s head gently backwards and rest it on you thumbs for 20 seconds.Continue by giving the whole area another rub except this time using a circular motion.Leave the oil in the hair for at least eight hours before washing out.  At least four sessions gives the most benefit.This was a very interesting course and I would encourage anyone to attend one of these taster sessions.  If you want to continue onwards to become a qualified therapist you can either do this as a distant learning student or at your local college.  If they don t do the course then request it for next year. The courses are suitable for people with physical disabilities as well as able-bodied students.One-day courses are available at regular dates throughout the year from the Oxford School of Reflexology at the price of    56.00. Details can be found athttp://www.reflexology.aromapost.com/ihm1.htmFor an online course there are many choices available and I found the following link whilst surfing the net. The following company have some special offers http://www.naturalhealthcourses.com/specialoffers.htmAt the moment you can have the choice of five very basic starter self-study courses for    250.00.  The price is normally double this so is a real bargain.A few good books and videos can be purchased from Amazon at prices ranging between    4.99 and    12.99Unless you have spinal disorders or have suffered a head or neck injury this therapy is suitable for all and can even be performed on babies whilst they are lying down.  Care should be taken when using certain oils and if unsure a small test patch should be applied 24hrs before use.  If unsure then extra advice can be sought from your health practitioner.Always check with your doctor first if you have Thrombosis/embolism,Advanced Heart Condition, Diabetes or Epilepsy.  You will probably still be able to proceed but you must get their permission first.  I had to take a letter with me to the college from my doctor when I did my taster sessions. I hope you found this beneficial and thank you for taking the time to read it. Fiona xxx     ', '    A medicine, known as Ayurveda, has been practised for well over three thousand years. This word, Ayurveda comes from Sanskrit, the ancient language of India. When translated it means    science of life    or    knowledge of life    It is a complete healing system, possibly the oldest in the world. It teaches a totally holistic approach, which aims to achieve a balance of mind, body and spirit. This can then promote physical, emotional and spiritual health and also a feeling of well-being. This practice has become known as Indian Head Massage. It does not claim to diagnose or cure ailments but it does help provide the physical and mental conditions to foster good health and prevent illness. This type of massage was, originally brought to this country by Narendra Mehta, a blind physiotherapist, from India. He formalised the Indian Head Massage techniques first at the Mind, Body and Spirit exhibition at Olympia in 1981. This massage can be practiced for monetary gain or purely to give pleasure to those we love. Even babies can be soothed by it   s few basic strokes. These techniques are so simple, yet so effective and a full session need take no longer than a half hour. Mine usually last a little longer. When I give Reflexology treatments I need a couch, candles and relaxing music to create the most beneficial atmosphere and I use special oils. Indian Head Massage needs no more than a chair and hand washing facilities. With ALL massages hygiene is a VERY important factor and particular care should always be taken. A massage may be given to calm, revitalise or uplift. It can create a feeling of relaxed awareness, an exhilarating yet peaceful feeling. This feeling can bring about the benefits of more restful sleep, increased energy and vitality and even relief from stress and mild depression. Although it all sounds a little like MUMBO JUMBO a regular head massage can improve the condition of the hair and the skin, whether oils are used or not, and a fresher, younger and more attractive appearance is produced because a more efficient blood and lymph circulation has been achieved thus providing fresh supplies of oxygen and nutrients to these areas. In this way toxins are speedily removed from the body thereby promoting healthy growth and functioning. After an initial consultation, where all possible contra indications can be discussed, and all non-verbal signs, body language and lack of direct eye contact have been noted, (this feedback could be very important), the massage can proceed. When I have ensured that my client is QUITE comfortable I will begin the massage. After placing my hands over the client s head for a little while I usually start on the upper back. I will roll with my thumbs in a diagonal position over the shoulders and then up the back and then roll them over the top of the shoulders and then stroke with my fingers down over the whole upper back. This is followed by a hitting motion over the muscle at top of the back. I then find the pressure points in the back, and using a circular movement with my thumbs, I will massage these. Lastly I knead and squeeze the top of the shoulders. If you are very tense some of these actions can be a little uncomfortable, but I can assure you I am not being a sadist. You really will feel the benefit later I then do a little massage, ironing and squeezing of the upper arm and then I start on the neck and up under the base of the skull. All these movements are, in many ways similar, just changing a little regarding the type and position of the muscle. Much vibrating, (not as awful as it sound), and frictions are used at the base of the skull. There are many, far too many to go into here, massage techniques used on the scalp. One or two of them are Windscreen wiper, (some of my clients are very enthusiastic about this one, which is a sort of waving backwards and forwards over the ears) Scratching, Hacking and whole hand Friction. I will just let your mind run riot with these. Now you will HAVE to visit, or have one call on you, if only to find out what on earth I am talking about. After stroking back to forehead I move to the face. This is very soothing. The eye-socket and the forehead pressure points are all massaged along with the cheeks, jaw and ears. The massage will then finish, as it started, with me laying my hands just above the client   s head There is much difference for the therapist between Reflexology and Indian Head Massage. The former relies very much on knowing the position of the main organs and glands etc of the body and being able to recognise how the meridians lie, where as, the latter has a lot more faith put into the Auras and the seven Chakras of the body. I expect the one Chakra known to most is the Chakra of the forehead known as the    Third eye   . Indian Head Massage is a little more mystical than Reflexology. After a session the client should be warned to eat a light diet, drink plenty of water or herbal teas and take no alcohol. This advice is also given after other massages. Sometimes when tension is released clients can feel clearing of the thought process, with more oxygen getting to the brain, it will become more active. Regular brushing of the hair, at home, will have a stimulating effect on the scalp and therefore the hair. This is one of the few massages that one can successfully practice on oneself. Narendra Mehta quotes an ancient proverb:  A happy mind is medicine, no better prescription exists.  Your local technical college should run evening classes. I believe it will cost you about    200 in all (including the examination fees) and if you have a basic understanding of anatomy and physiology it should take about 15 weeks. I hope I have not bored you or put you off the idea at all, because I can tell you that an Indian Head Massage is money well spent. It would be foolish for me to have been trained and then let loose on people if I did not know what it felt like, wouldn   t it?      ', '    I had my first Indian Head Massage last week and have found it fantastic I didn   t have to undress     the therapist worked through my thin blouse.She started by working very deeply on my shoulders and upper back, then my arms down to the elbows. Next she worked on my neck, then, of course, the scalp (really thoroughly) then the face, (very soothing) and, finally, she balanced the upper charkas. After that my energy really picked up.I was also shocked at the greasy smell of my hair but had to leave the oil on for at least two hours before I washed it to get any benefit.It was important to drink lots and lots of water afterwards and eat a light diet.She came to my house and charged    15.I   m having another one next week      ', '    I am a qualified Indian Head Massage therapist in Leeds and since I started giving this treatment I have been amazed at how pleasurable and effective people find the therapy. Indian Head Massage the shoulders, back, neck, head and face. It is a most pleasurable and therapeutic programme which concentrates on the areas most vulnerable to stress and tension. This therapy induces peace, tranquillity and promotes high levels of alertness and concentration. It also aids sleep and stimulates lymphatic drainage. Ghandi had a daily massage, believing it boosted his energy levels whilst also keeping him in touch with his spiritual mind. To anyone who is thinking of having an Indian Head Massage, it is relaxing, refreshing and reviving, stimulating your senses and leaving you completely rejuvenated and revitalised.     ', '    if you suffer from migraines the best thing to do is get a desert bowl fill it with lukewarm water and put five table spoons of vinegar into the water,mix it together with the spoon to make sure its mixed together, get a cloth and dip it into the water but squeeze some of the water out so its just damp. Sessions typically last 30 to 60 minutes, no need to undress, and you can use oils or go oil-free depending on your preference. Oils like coconut, almond, or tea tree add extra benefits for hair and skin, which is a nice bonus if you’re after shinier, healthier hair.

While it’s generally safe—even suitable for babies and those with physical disabilities—people with conditions like thrombosis, heart problems, diabetes, epilepsy, or recent injuries should avoid or adapt the massage. So, always check with a healthcare provider if you’re unsure.

One thing to keep in mind: this isn’t a cure-all but a complementary therapy that supports overall well-being and helps prevent illness. If you’re looking for a natural, nurturing way to relax and promote health for yourself and your loved ones, Indian Head Massage is definitely worth exploring. Just remember to tailor it safely to your family’s needs!

If it can give them pain relief of any kind, then it must be helping rather than hurting.Take careZorena xx     ', '    Olbas oil is my saviour   Since having sinus trouble last year and trying numerous powerful over the counter drugs, this stuff was recommended to me by my father who has relied on olbas oil for years. ', '    Savlon Dry Antiseptic Spray is the perfect way to prevent infection after minor cuts, grazes and burns.It comes in a small 50ml spray can, about 5 inches tall and cost me about    3 from co-op pharmacy. The spray itself is a fine antiseptic powder. It s ideal as a  no-touch  first aid treatment. Very good for children, as they offten refuse to allow you to touch their wounds, so a spray is very convienient. What does the spray do?********************The spray forms a protective layer that helps to prevent any infection and apparently aids natural healing. I like the idea of using a spray, it makes it very easy to apply, as do sun protection sprays.What can the spray be used on?**************************** Minor cuts, grazes and burns. Friction burns from synthetic surfaces, concreate, or grass. Abrasions caused through gardening or DIY.When should it NOT be used?*************************The spray is not for use near the eyes or nose, on deep wounds or on babies under 1 month of age. Nor is it applicable to use if you are sensitive to iodine or suffering from thyroid disease.How effective is it?******************I used this when I went down a  death slide  at a theme park and got a friction burn. As I ve already said, spray s are much more effective than creams. They re easier to apply and more efficient.     ', '    I have worn glasses since I was seven, and must admit i ve never had any hassle about them. But I did feel they lowered my confidence, so about nine months ago I decided to buy contact lenses. Now this was harder than it sounds. There are so many different types around now, hard, soft, coloured, all day for three months, disposable, and the brand new all day-all night lenses that you don t have to remove. I spoke to my optician and we decided that because of my budget I would get 30 pairs a month which costs me    11. Contact lenses are great for anyone who sick of wearing glasses. Most opticians stock them now, and you should speak to yours if you are interested. Disposables are by far the best option in my opinion, because for a small amount more you can get rid of all the hassle of aftercare solutions and stuff like that. A new system at Specsavers is that you pay for your lenses by direct debit and they are delivered to your door. This is extremely conveinent for busy people who don t have time to drop in and collect themselves.Contact Lenses are available for practically any one. Even people who have special problems can have prescripton lenses specially made. Prices range from    7.50 to upto    60 depending on the prescription. Lenses are the best thing that has happened to me in a long while and I advise anyone to just give them a go.     ', '    I have battled with my weight since my teenage years, and tried every diet going, without success. After having two kids,my I went up a further two stones, and I decided the time had come to try a diet club.The only one in my area was Weight Watchers, and eventually I plucked up the courage to go along.I was immediately made welcome by the ladies running the club and the other dieters were a very friendly bunch. I chose a time to join when there was free membership (normally    9.00) which cut down on costs a bit.I chose my own target weight, and the principles of the diet were explained to me. All food is allocated points, and there is no food forbidden. There is no weighing or measuring involved, which makes things much simpler. For my weight, 11.5 stones, I was allowed 20 points a day. If I used less than twenty points, I could save up the extra points for a special treat, such as a meal out. I could also earn extra points for doing exercise, such as gardening, swimming or dancing. After the weigh-in session,which is confidential, there is a talk about diet-related issues, or a demonstration of cooking healthy meals. I found these very useful and informative.I would definitely recommend joining Weight Watchers, it is the only diet that has worked for me. Because nothing is forbidden, it doesn t seem like a diet, and it teaches you the principles of healthy eating for life.I also found it a great social occasion, and have made many good friends.        ', '    I have now been practising Yoga in a gentle way for 20 years. I was 36 when I started and my present class takes place on a Wednesday morning between 10.30 am and 12 noon.My teacher is a very pleasant woman as are all the other ladies who mostly, like me, have been attending and finding benefit for years. I can   t think of any nasty or spiteful personalities among the 30-40 women which is, I think, rare in any group. So, I enjoy the social interaction even before we start     what the teacher calls    exercising our tongues   .We always start by    shaking out    and warming up slowly.The whole emphasis is on breathing, stretching and relaxing and there is no competitiveness     everyone just works to the best of their own ability. This suits me fine as I have never been a    sporty    person. It is a treat for me to actually enjoy exercise and feel better and more energetic afterwards  It really puts a    spring in my step   . The age group ranges from 20-80   s     a real mixture and I   ve noticed that in some postures (or asanas) the older ladies are more supple. In fact, most of them look younger than their age.Yoga not only tones up the outer body but also works, more importantly, on the internal organs. I do try to do about     an hour a day at home each morning following the Rishikesh sequence of a forward stretch, backward stretch (such as the Cobra), a twist and an inverted posture (e.g. The shoulder stand) and I really miss it if I   m unable to do this or miss my class for a while.I don   t think there is any finer system of exercise than Yoga      ']

product_reviews: ['    I write this review as I am spending the day with my collie Jess who is now almost nine years old.  When my husband and I split up and I moved into rented accommodation I was told that I couldn   t really have pets and as such I sadly had to leave her with him.  I am currently thinking hard about actually requesting to my landlord that I take her on and as such having her today provoked me to write a review.Border Collies are still used by farmers to hoard sheep and I believe they are also used in some police forces due to their intelligent nature.   quot; quot;Jess as a puppy quot; quot;We bought Jess when she was around twelve weeks old.  She cost us    150 nine years ago and I am not sure what the current price would be for a collie.  We chose her in the end because she had a really cute little pink spot on her nose which she shoved to the front so we could see her.  We got her home and we were all excited to have her.  I have always had dogs in my life but had never trained one from being a puppy so it was all quite new to me never mind my then husband who had never had a dog before The training her to go to the toilet outside did take a few days and of course we had accidents along the way.  We used to put paper down for those first few days just in case she didn   t make it outside.Now I have to say Jess was possibly one of the most privileged pups I have come across  She had all manner of toys, treats and even a little racing car bed to sleep in   Thinking back it must have cost us a packet   Even though she had all those things her most favourite thing to play with was one of my old slippers and a Winnie the Pooh teddy bear.The first night we had Jess home we left her downstairs with a big teddy bear and went to bed.  Then began the howling   We let her howl for a little while but me being soft decided to go down and see to her as she was just so small   I guess here was the first mistake  Border Collies are incredibly intelligent dogs and once I had come down once she knew she had me  After this she ended up sleeping in our bedroom.  This went on for around three years until I became pregnant and booted her out again One thing that we noticed with Jess was that she had separation anxiety from us when we went to work.  I used to arrange for my mum to come and visit her, walk her and feed her whilst we were out but she still developed an anxiety being alone.  As a result of this she howled a lot and chewed anything she could-namely woodwork and the wallpaper but in a couple of instances she got hold of a camera and a mobile fun   Needless to say she wasn   t in my good books then   I know some people use dog cages to contain their pets whilst they are out but this wasn   t something I wanted to do with Jess and so we kind of had to just ride it out.  I would say this stage lasted around a year sadly. quot; quot;Jess as she got bigger quot; quot;As I mentioned earlier Border Collies are an incredibly intelligent animal. As such it was really easy to teach Jess the basics of sit, lie down, roll over and paw with just a few treats.  It hasn   t been so easy to train her not to pull though  She is strong and as soon as she sees the lead come out gets very excited and will drag you out of the door.  She is manageable but I would never let a young child hold on to her.  Jess   s favourite place to be walked is to a field where she can be let off and have a good run around chasing a stick  She is obedient and knows that she has to come back when shouted, though sometimes she will try and push her luck and make me go and get her  Again, I think this is simply an intelligence thing and she sees it as a game Jess has also developed a love for playing football   It is hilarious to watch as she will actually put her paw on the ball and    kick    in before chasing it and doing it again   Much to my annoyance though she has to bark at the ball the whole time she is playing Recently I have had a few issues with my ex and the state in which Jess had gotten into.  She developed a skin condition which meant that she was losing some of her hair.  I managed to get it under control with some regular bathing, brushing and cream and she is on the mend again now thankfully.  quot; quot;Jess in general quot; quot;Jess is an average sized collie and weighs around the 20kg mark.  She has long hair which needs a lot of keeping on top of or it can become matted underneath and just look a bit tatty.Jess has always been fed a dry food diet with the odd pouch or tray thrown in for good measure.  She is currently eating Iams when she comes to my house which she adores.  I would recommend that you get quite a heavy bowl for food and water as she can flick them around the room otherwise.  Jess is loyal and so affectionate and is great with children.  Initially when we had my son she was very aware of him and did not like the noise he made-I think she was confused at the time and as such we needed to get a baby gate just to put a bit of separation between them but she soon got over the phase and is fine with him now.I don   t know if it is a trait of the collie but Jess is very excitable when guests come and will have a bit of a jump around-this is just something to be aware of.  They do have a lot of energy and really you need to be committed to giving them the walks that they need to wear off some of this energy.  I would have no doubts at all in recommending a Border collie to someone as a pet.  They are kind, loyal and fun to own if you can give them the right kind of attention and home.     ', '    The Border Collie.I own 3 Border Collies myself called Flynn, Moby and Tess. My son has 1 Border Collie and my daughter has 2 Border Collies. Their dogs also spend quite a bit of time at my house as when they both work shifts the dogs come to mine to save them being on their own. So its quite often have 6 dogs at mine and they all get on well with each other. There are 5 Dogs   1 Bitch in total. I have owned this breed of dog for the last 20 odd years.The Dog ItselfThe Border Collie is a very intelligent and responsive medium sized dog originally bred as everyone knows to round up sheep. They are a bundle of energy which needs to be channelled in the right direction. This breed excels at obedience, agility and flyball in which they are commonly used as these particular sports are right up this intelligent dog s street. They thrive on praise, are sensitive and are very trainable. None of this is achieved without dedication from its owner. This dog likes to be well exercised and you will need to be a hardy individual who doesn t mind at least an hours walk twice a day (more if you can offer it) in ALL weathers as the dog doesn t care what the weather is like  You should take your dog to obedience classes as soon as the dog has had the full set of vaccinations even if you only do the basic classes. This dog needs to keep its brain as well as its body exercised. Flyball or agility is a useful addition for both you and the dog and you can do these classes for fun right up to serious competition level. Like any dog this breed will become a nuisance and also destructive if not given enough exercise and stimulation. These dogs are simply just too intelligent to lie around the house all day with nothing to do.Coat Type, Colour   Grooming.Their coats tend to come in two styles of a coarse thick, straight hair about 3 inches long complete with a mane and bushy tail and the other with sleek 1 inch long hair covering from head to tail.I personally think Border Collies are unique because they come in absolutely every coat colour available other than the more traditional black   white , they also come in the colours of tri-colour ( black, white   brown) red, blue-merle, red merle, tri-merle ,sable and tan. A Border Collie that is mostly white is said to be difficult to work sheep as apparently the sheep do not have the same respect as they think its one of them.As for grooming I brush them a couple of times a week by brushing them with a slicker brush. (I also check them for any lumps and bumps and give a quick check in ears   mouth). I give them a bath about twice a year unless they have rolled in something particularly nasty.TemperamentI have always found Border Collies to have a nice temperament. Like most breeds of dogs they can be snappy if not socialized properly or given enough to do. They do like to herd children and small animals (which after all is what they were bred for) which can be a nuisance if not curtailed. Most are more than happy to do anything for a few words of praise. All of the dogs I have or have had been fine with my children, cats and chickens and rabbits (although will try to round up if given the chance) Height   Weight.DOGS are around 19-22 inches tall weighing in around 30-45 pounds.BITCHES are around 18-21 inches weighing in at around 27-42 pounds although same as people this can vary.Health Problems.These dogs are generally a very hardy lot on a day to day basis but can be prone to hip dysplasia (HD), Progressive Retinal Atrophy (PRA) and an eye disease common to collies such as Collie Eye Anomaly. Anybody buying a puppy can ask if the parents have been tested for these and what the results were. Collies are also prone to epilepsy. Living Conditions.My collies live in the house and have been brought up to use crates. They simply adore these. They are always fed in these and have treats and bones in these. I always find crates essential for teaching any new puppy to toilet train and when left home alone in the first 6 months or so not to be destructive by chewing things you don t want them to chew like furniture etc. Once these habits have been attained it s hard to break so best they are not allowed to start. Border Collies are also happy to live outside in a suitably insulated kennel as long as this is not all day long with any human contact. Mine are pets and live in happily with us all using their crates overnight or when home alone. Once trained the dogs are not even shut in these crates.Exercise.As said before plenty of it  Also exercise the dog s brain too. They are so easy to train especially clicker training. I can teach any dog within 10 mins to sit   down with this. Flynn can also give paw, turn right or left, I five and now almost bow. All taught with the clicker. All my dogs will sit, down, stay, wait and paw on command. Admitted they could do even more if I wanted to train them further.Further Training.As said before these dogs adore obedience,flyball and agility and will compete to any level depending on the time and dedication the owner has.Life ExpectancyLife excpectancy is 12-15 years. CostAnything from    150 to    500 depending on breed lines.And Finally...Please remember A DOG IS FOR LIFE.Thank you for reading       ', '    I know this review is meant to be more about Border Collies in general as a breed rather than about an individual dog but I would like to share my dog Marley with other people on Ciao.It all started on 28th April  2004. She is very loyal and god knows what I   d do without her      ', '    In 1873 the first sheepdog trials were held. A training course was devised to test the skill of the Border Collie. In 1906 the International Sheep Dog Society was formed and written records were instituted. In 1976 the first border collie was show and recognised by the Kennel Club. In 1997 I was born and my name is Pudsey the puppy even though I am 6 years old. I am a black and white border collie with freckles. I am also very cute.Selecting your dog------------------Now before you decided that you would like to purchase a Border Collie, you have to take into consideration several things.1) Have I got the time to take him out for walks every day as they love walking. Our will run and run and run and come home and go to sleep for a while and would quite happily go back outside again for another walk.2) Does the dog fit into my lifestyle. If you work all day and the dog is left on its own, please do not buy a Border Collie like me as I get very bored easily and I love the company of humans. My breed has been known to chew through walls and carpets and anything that I think is amusing, although you will not be amused when you come home. Now my mum is going back to full time work soon and there will be no one with us for two whole days... Great I thought we will be on the rampage causing chaos. Then she came home today and told dad, she has got a friend who we know to come and petsit while she works.3) Do you want to show him or is he going to be a household pet. This does make a lot of difference as mum shows me but she gave up after I was very naughty one day.  I was in the show ring and I was selected for the final two rounds and it was between me and an alsation. I did not like been shown and I decided it was time to prove this to her. We were walking around the ring when I saw an agility class and I started to run very fast. Mum was not amused as she knew I could win this easy but she knew I was not happy so we decided I would be put into agility rather than just been shown. Also if you want to show your dog professionally I would suggest getting a KC reg dog. I am a farm collie from a stock of hard working parents. 4) In looking for a puppy, ask the owner about the parents health and make sure they and the puppy is in good health. If you want to breed from a pup again it is advised to see the puppys parents and ask the owner has there been any problems with litters.Types of Border Collies-----------------------Shorthaired or long hairedBlack and WhiteTri colourRed MerleBlue MerleI am a Black and white collie and I have 10 freckles on my nose and a few on my legs. My brother Caffery has got beige on him and has beige eyebrows, cute eh  My daughter is so cute, she is predominantly black with white on her.Breeding--------First of all you must not breed the two coloured merles as this can cause all sorts of complications and health issues. Always breed a merle with a tri colour or a black and white border collie.Walking/Exercise----------------I am a fun and active dog and I love going out in the car and into the countryside and running and running feeling the wind in my hair, whoops I mean fur  lol. I can out walk humans any day of the week and sometimes I have come home gone to sleep for a wee while and I am ready to and play or go for another walk. When mum is not bad she will take me to the park but I have to wear a muzzle as I am prone to nipping.Be careful if you have children, whilst I am friendly and loving, I have a herding instinct. When I was about 8 months old mum was at her friends and it was a birthday party. The children were screaming at the bottom of the garden.. I was not harming them, I was playing but if they moved out of my circle they got a quick nip. Mum and her friends were laughing and they had to rescue the children.  I love children, I will play with them all day as they amuse me and I would not hurt them in any way.Training--------I am very active and a bit boisterous and my mum sent me to puppy training classes, you can normally get a number from your local vets. Classes can be anything from a couple of pounds upwards. Why send me there? Well I need to learn who is master and how to walk properly and when to be praised and when not  I hate it when mum tells me I have been a bad boy as I am very eager to please. My ears go back and I sulk and my puppy eyes just stare at her.Toilet training was quite easy with me, first of all I saw the cats use this litter tray and I did what they did but as I got older mum put newspaper down on the floor and day by day moved it to the back door and then every morning she would take me out in the garden and tell me to wee. I became very housetrained very quickly.I was never allowed to play with slippers as mum said If I chewed an old slipper I would chew the new ones, so I was told no If you are going to breed from a border collie, it is best to do this during the second to third season when the bitch is at her best.Sleeping Arrangements----------------------A lot of people have indoor cages/kennels or let their pets sleep in the kitchen. Me I sleep on my mums bed at the bottom, ok so a lot of you might think ewwwww but its really comfy but in the middle of the night I usually go and sleep on the floor at the side of her bed. If your pet is to sleep elsewhere, make sure it has a comftable bed and drink and food nearby with toys.Intelligent-----------I am very intelligent and a quick learner. One of my favourite tricks is for mum to tidy all my toys up in the garden and then I go and take them all out of the box again.I am easy to train, I fetch mum her post every morning, normally with a few teeth marks on it. I was scolded the other week as mum left some liver on the side for tea, when she went there it had gone and it was inside my tummy ;0) I managed to jump up on the side and on my back feet I pulled the dish over with my paw. I also do this with the cats food when shes not looking.Compatibility-------------I am a fun loving dog and love people and children and other pets. My best friend is Devil cat, we grew up together and we sleep together.Home----Now I can adapt to most situations, I have lived in a flat with no garden but did not like it.  My favourite is our new house as it has massive gardens.General Care------------Brush me regulary otherwise I will get knots in my fur. I am long haired and there is a lot of fur flying around our house at the moment. Do not forget to worm me and take me to the vets for a check over and use frontline for fleas. I hate the stuff and roll over on the bed when she puts it on me but it does work. Do not forget my innoculations as mum forgot about them one year and I got kennel cough.Travelling----------I love travelling in a car but I have warned you that I am a clever dog. Mum bought a guard for the car but we learnt how to move the bars. I would advise a cage for the car or safety belts if your going to have me on the back seat. Mum was not impressed this particular day as we scratched the side panels of the car and it cost her    400 to have them replaced.Most of all I am lovely breed and a very faithful companion in the right hands.. Must go now I can smell food downstairs, She is cooking liver, my favourite, time to go and look cute at her.Pudsey the Border Collie.     ', '    I had owned other dogs before from puppies, but nothing could prepare me for owning a Border Collie.  Buffy  was bought for me last October as an early Christmas present from my sister. I went to pick her up from the Pennines and she was a beautiful little red merle at 10 weeks old (she is now 9 months old). We drove her all the way back and bought her into the house. She was so shy that she hid under the table for the whole of the night. How sweet I thought, but little did I know. THE BASICS Border Collies have an inbred tendency to work. If you do not keep them stimulated they will very quickly become bored and start to chew. You may even see your Border Collie chasing shadows on the walls   It is a sign of boredom and is something you will need to overcome quite quickly. We have lost wallpaper, shoes, chair legs etc just because we turned away for 20 minutes. We didn t find toilet training too much of a chore. Every time she messed in the house we used to pick her up and put her outside. After a couple of weeks she got the hang of it and we have had no mess since. HERDING Border Collies also have a herding instinct, which is inbred. This means that they will nip at your ankles and try to  herd  you around the house. This can be extremely painful and should be  nipped  in the bud as soon as possible. The best way that I found to stop them from doing this was to buy a spray from the pet shop, which is lemon in flavour. Dogs do not like the taste of citrus and I found that it did stop her, however, you do end up smelling like a tart s boudoir  You could try to use a consistent command like  No  or  Stop  and use it every time they try to herd you. If they are really naughty try ignoring them for a few minutes. I have found that they really do not like to be ignored and will generally stop what they are doing. It will take some time but persevere and you will get results. INTELLIGENCE The Border Collie is an extremely intelligent dog. I would even put myself on the line to say that they are far more intelligent than their owners. The trouble with this is that they will run rings around you if you let them. You must again be firm with them and get them into a routine as soon as possible and stick to it. If you usually take them for a walk first thing in the morning then keep doing this. We didn t take her one morning and she played all hell. Ran around barking, started chewing and running backwards and forwards to the door. As soon as we took her out she calmed down    EXERCISE A Border Collie can walk up to 20 miles in one day, so you can imagine how much exercise they will need to keep them in line. Just imagine how much ground they cover in one day herding sheep and you will get some idea how much you will be taking on. If you are not a person for walking your dog for 2 or 3 miles a time, 3 or 4 times a day then please do not get a Border Collie. Buffy is only 9 months old at the moment and can quite easily outwalk us. We generally have to take her across a field with a ball and run around with her for a good 45 minutes 3 times a day  When you get them home they will sleep for about 30 minutes and will then be ready to go again  TRAINING As I said earlier, the Border Collie is an extremely intelligent dog. Get your dog into training as soon as they are able to mingle with other dogs. This will keep their mind active and also will ensure that they do not become overly possessive or dominant. Local training classes are run in most areas and it is an idea to get them into an agility and obedience class. Cost of classes range up to approximately 5.00 per class. Please note that you cannot register for an agility class until your Border Collie is 12 months old as their bones are too fragile before this. BREEDING Border Collies can come in black and white, red merle, blue merle and tri colour as far as I am aware. It is important that you do not mate two merles together as you will end up with a double merle and it can cause all kinds of health problems such as eye defects. Merles should only be mated with black and white collies. INDOOR KENNELS An indoor kennel is an extremely good idea. We bought one from an early stage and she soon learnt that it was her own private space. We put a big cushion and some of her toys in it and when she wants some peace and quiet (which is not very often) she will generally take herself off into it and go to sleep. It is ideal when they are teething as you can leave them in it for up to about two hours at a time and go about your duties. A decent kennel will probably cost about 80.00 - 90.00, but just think how much of your furniture you will save. Never use the kennel as a form of punishment, as they will not go in it of their own accord. We also find the kennel useful for travelling in the car. I would like to add that having now owned one for 7 months, I would definitely recommend it. I know they have their problems and are a lot of hard work, but the rewards you get back far outcry any of the hassle they cause. They are an extremely loyal and loving pet and are (would you believe  ) desperate to please. After having Buffy I cannot imagine owning a less active dog  (I had a King Charles Spaniel before and would probably be quite bored with them now  ) So there you go. I hope you have enjoyed reading this and have learned a bit about the Border Collie.      ', '    Life for Sarah_Louise has been pretty hectic lately, what with moving to a completely new part of the country for a start.  My Ciao addiction has consequently taken another hit, hence my absense of late.  SO thanks to Duncan (torr) for suggesting I write this review - I needed some inspiriation so here I am   As many of you know, I m a huge animal lover.  I am by far the biggest animal lover I ve ever come across in fact.  Isn t it strange that, as an animal lover, the vast majority of my friends are those that just don t see the fascination?  Or indeed those who can t stand the thought of sharing their homes with an animal   Sure, I adore horses.  I ve been a keen horse rider for the past 12 or so years and have worked as a Stable hand/Groom for the past 10 or so years.  Sadly though, horses are a tad expensive.  Not only to buy in the first place but also to keep.  Have you ever looked into the price of a piece of land suitable to keep a horse on ?  Or indeed the weekly cost of keeping a horse at Livery?  Well lets just say that until I win the Lottery, I sincerely doubt I ll be becoming a horse owner anytime soon.  Dogs have always been on my number 1 of realistic pets that I wanted to get.  I ve had two cats but sadly my parents (mainly my mum) would never let me get a dog. ', '    My dad has always kept dogs. They were used on farms to help shepherds with their sheep.~*~ Buying ~*~Before even considering a Border Collie you must consider the time, exercise and effort you will need to put into this breed of dog. Remember they were bred to work on farms. Therefore they would spend most (if not all) their time with the shepherds and run miles around fields with the sheep and they will nee a similar level of exercise and time from you. That said there are a few things you should consider if you are still interested in getting a Border Collie.Firstly NEVER buy from a pet shop. Pet shop puppies can be very difficult to house train as they have not been encouraged with this as they grow up. They may develop behaviour problems as they grow up as this is not discouraged and they may have health problems.We got Magic off a friend who didn t have the time she needed. She had bought her from a pet store and although her training had helped someway with her problems she would still occasionally nip and chew the furniture and everything else in sight  As I said training will help someway towards correcting this but if the puppy has grown up without having these problems corrected it will be very hard to correct this completely after your dog has grown up.So, having said that how do you know which breeder to go for? There are a number of points to make here:1. Breeders should have had both the mother and the father tested for genetic problems. This will not mean that their puppies will not have any health problems, as there are bound to be health problems with any pedigree dog, but it will go someway in helping to prevent them.2. Breeders should only breed a dog if both parents have good temperaments. I.e. gentle, not timid, or aggressive3. The parents of your puppy should not be closely related4. The breeders should sell their dogs from their own home rather than a warehouse or pet store.5. The parents of your puppy and any other dogs the breeder has should be involved in other activities such as agility, obedience, dog clubs etc. This will mean that the dogs are not only kept for breeding and will keep them mentally stimulated.~*~ Feeding ~*~Border Collie puppies should not be fed puppy food. The protein levels are too high for them and may cause bone development problems later in life. You should choose an adult dog food that has a protein level no higher than 24 .Puppies should be fed 3 times a day until they are 6 months old when they should start to be fed 2 times a day instead (do not cut down the amount of food, just the amount of times they are fed.)For treats do not feed table scraps. Instead only use dog biscuits (preferably broken in half) it is very easy for a border collie to become overweight and this may cause problems.Magic was being fed twice a day when we got her. We continued this when we got her home. She was being fed on dried food and she had 3 cups a day (2 in the morning, 1 at night)~*~ Health ~*~I do not claim to mention every single health problem here that you may experience with your dog. I am only trying to give a brief introduction to a few problems that you may experience. So as far as health is concerned I would recommend that you get to know your dog and keep an eye out for anything unusual for him, sometimes this is the best (and quickest) way of noticing any health problems with your dog. Never be afraid to take your dog to the vet over any change. A vet would rather you took your pet over something that turned out to be nothing than you waited until it had become serious.Collie Eye Anomaly - This is a genetic disorder. It can mean that the puppies may be totally blind. There is now a test available for breeders to check for this disorder and therefore this can be easily preventedHip Dysplasia - This affects the dog s hip joint. The ball and socket do not fit together properly. Some cases of Hip dysplasia are manageable by veterinary advice and diet. Most cases are recognisable by the age of 2 years although severe cases can be recognised before this.Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis - This affects humans as well as dogs. In young dogs, the disease is recognisable by confusion, unpredictability and an inability to walk and see properly. It is often fatal. It is a genetic disease and can be prevented by breeding dogs that do not carry the gene for it.Osteochondritis Dissecans - This is another genetic disease. It is recognisable by the age of 6 to 12 months. Diagnosis is made with the aid of an x-ray machine. In mild cases rest will aid healing, in more severe cases surgery may be required.Progressive Retinal Atrophy - This is a hereditary disease. It is linked to the retina and may lead to blindness. Night time vision goes first, then dim light vision etc .The affected eye may have a  shine  to it, and the lens may appear cloudy, causing a cataract.~*~ Exercise ~*~Magic will walk for 1 hour twice a day every day. Without this she becomes very restless and get generally very excitable, chew everything and cause complete chaos in the house  She needs this exercise, it s what she was bred for  We often exercised her by having her run alongside a bike while one of us rode it, but if you attempt this please be careful of them running in front of the bike trying to herd it. This was one of Magic s favourite tricks  If you don t have the time needed to do this then maybe a Border Collie isn t for you. They are not the kinds of dogs that will be happy just running around the back garden.When exercising a Border Collie you must constantly watch for heat exhaustion. As they are working dogs they will not stop when they get too hot or too tired. They can work themselves to death (literally) if you let them. ~*~ So, would I recommend a Border Collie? ~*~Yes, they are gorgeous dogs. Having said that they do require a lot of time and exercise, they are one of the most high maintenance dogs.They must also be supervised when with livestock and children. They can be too boisterous with children and if left with livestock their herding instinct will take over and they may injure or kill the animals. So please consider carefully whether or not you re making the right choice. This is good news in that they are very ready to learn  how you would like them to behave, but bad news for a lazy owner, in that it means they absolutely require lots of exercise and  the right sort of stimulation in order to prevent them becoming bored.They are medium sized dogs, but so long as they get plenty of outdoor exercise and lots of play, they can adapt happily to life in a flat. However they will not do well in a confined area where they don t receive enough exercise or fun - in that type of environment they tend to become frustrated and soured, and as well as being unhappy, will usually become destructive and even snappy.They are not generally fussy eaters; any good quality food should be well-tolerated by their digestive system, which means they aren t particularly expensive to feed. They come in two  varieties  - one is known as bare-skinned, which actually means it has a coat similar to that of a Labrador; the other is a rough, or wavy coat. Obviously, when they moult, you have a lot more fluff around with the longer-coated type  However they are easy to keep groomed, any decent brush or dog-comb will keep your collie looking smart with just a couple of 5 minute sessions each day.Health wise, a collie getting the amount of exercise it requires and a good balanced diet usually has very little in the way of health problems, but occasionally the dreaded Hip Dysplasia crops up in this breed just as in German Shepherds, Labradors, etc. Some have it mildly; others, as in the case of one of my own bitches, have to have the entire hip joints removed. This is NOT a cheap option, as well as being something you d prefer your dog not to suffer, so if you buy a puppy, do ask about the parents  hips before you part with your cash - and your heart  - as breeders will only take care not to breed from dogs with problems if they find they can t readily sell the pups.If a collie is brought up from between 5 - 12 weeks with plenty of sensibly managed exposure to the things (e.g. children, cats, ducks or horses) which you want it to cope well with in adult life, you are unlikely to have any problems in those areas; however an adult rescue would have to be carefully assessed, as they can be very  sharp  with children if they re unused to them, and not trustworthy with other animals if they haven t learned about them.It s important to be aware, if you are training a collie, that are as quick to learn the  wrong  thing as the  right  thing - so for instance, if you unwittingly reward your collie for barking by going to it and speaking to it/reassuring it every time it does so, you will find you have  trained  your dog to bark for attention .. very annoying   If you haven t had to train a dog before, I really recommend you buy a book on training (by someone who advocates humane methods) before you even bring your collie home.Colour-wise, you can find anything from a  blonde  almost yellow Labrador colour, through red   white; white with very little colour; black   white or black, brown and white (known as tri-colour) to red or blue merle -which is a beautiful mix of the solid colour with the white, giving a smoky effect.One important warning though - if you intend to breed from a Merle, you MUST NOT breed to another Merle, only to a solid   white or a tricolour.  Something in the genetic makeup of the Merles means that a proportion of many Merle to Merle litters will be born deaf or hyper-active (that s even by collie standards ) or have their vision affected - sometimes all three in the same poor dog.If you enjoy playing with your dog, a collie is definitely a breed to consider - their skills in Agility, Flyball and Search-And-Rescue are legendary.If you would like a dog who will protect you and your property, don t rule out the collie - they will lick friends to death so to speak, but they are not to be trifled with by strangers with raised voices All in all the Border Collie is a superb friend, protector and companion for the right owner, but a total disaster for an inactive person who hasn t the time or inclination to interact with their dog, or who can t take him/her out to really run every day. If you’re considering welcoming a Border Collie into your family, it’s important to know they thrive best with owners who can commit to daily walks, playtime, and plenty of mental stimulation. These dogs are incredibly intelligent and eager to please, making them quick learners who excel in agility and obedience training. From my experience and what many owners share, Border Collies form deep, loyal bonds—not just with one person but often with the whole family—bringing immense joy and companionship. Their affectionate nature means they’re truly missed when gone, a testament to the strong emotional connection they inspire.

However, their herding instincts can sometimes lead to nipping during play, especially with children, so early socialization and consistent training are key to preventing behavioral issues. They also need ample space to run and explore; while they can adapt to different living situations, a home with a yard is ideal to keep their energy in check. Without enough exercise or attention, Border Collies may become bored, leading to destructive behaviors like chewing or chasing shadows, which can be frustrating for any owner.

Health-wise, they’re generally robust, but it’s crucial to avoid breeding two merles together due to potential genetic problems. Regular grooming is necessary, especially for long-haired varieties, as they do shed. On a positive note, many wonderful Border Collies are available for adoption from rescue centers, offering a chance to provide a loving home to a dog in need.

In sum, Border Collies are loving, intelligent companions who reward dedicated owners with loyalty and affection. But they demand time, patience, and understanding—qualities that, when given, make the bond truly special and deeply fulfilling. If you’re ready for that commitment, a Border Collie can be a remarkable addition to your family.

', '    Cif Glass   Window Wipes come in a little resealable pack of twenty and cost around    1.50 and are available in most supermarkets and Pounland and Home Bargains, where you will no doubt find them much cheaper.The cloths are quite large and stretchy and don t shred or get damaged even after you tug at one for a bit.I would not recommend these wipes at all.
