This made the job far faster and easier. All that is needed is a quick wipe with the wadding and then a polish with some kitchen towel. I was extremely impressed with the results. Without wanting to sound like a cheesy advert my toaster and kettle shone so I could see my face in them. This was what I was looking for, a shiny appearance for minimum effort.Brasso metal polish wadding costs    1.85 for 75g and in mind it is worth at least twice that price. As anyone who knows me can tell you housework is pretty near the bottom of my priority list so I am always in search of products that make a big difference for very little effort. With brasso I think I have rediscovered this magical product.     ', '    Before I start writing about this product I must apologise for the title(its really naff)I just couldn t think of anything more truthful I m afraid:)Right onto the product,I used to use powder,fairy actually and found it okay,but my whites were never really white.When you have a baby or small children they always manage to get something on their clothes  I find that spaghetti sauces and chocolate are the worst stains to get off,as well as fruit juice,its a bit of a problem and thats just me being messy(only kidding)but seriously (well as serious as you can get about washing clothes)I like my washing to look like it has actually been washed and doesn t just smell fresh  This comes in a 1,5 litre bottle and costs 3.85p depending on where you shop that is.On the bottle front it says  best ever whiteness and I have too say that I agree with this statement:)It gets all the stains out of my sons clothes and all the oil out of his daddies too.It also gets the odd coffee stain off mine and makeup marks..Its also better value for money.It may not seem like it when you look at the box and bottle price in the store but I get at least 30 washes out of the liquid compared to 10 out of a box of fairy  Its available in all supermarkets and probably some of your local shops too,I would recommend it for those of you who are looking for those extra white whites:)One last thing I will mention is that it comes with one of those roller ball thingymebobs and if you roll some of the liquid onto a really bad stain before putting it in the wash it really helps....     ', '    Rascals rewards are meaty   8216;sticks  8217; made by Felix. They come in resealable pouch s containing 12 sticks. The sticks are notched to make breaking them easier, although my cats like to chew them whole from the hand. Rascals rewards come in 3 great flavours - well  for cats  - Ham   cheese, salmon    trout and chicken   liver. The maximum daily allowance is 2 sticks for  3kg cats, 4kg - 3 sticks and 5kg 4 sticks.The treats are available from all supermarkets and pet outlets at around  79p upwards.This opinion has been written in respose to  Kens Challenge  to write a 90 word wonder opinion      ', '    Well, that s my cats opinions anyway - I haven t actually tried the stuff myself though a few of the varieties do smell very tempting  Felix canned meat cuts in jelly -mmmm,my cats definitely prefer this to any of that Whiskas stuff  Available in 400g cans, the price varies from about 40p upwards depending where you buy it but the average supermarket price seems to be about 43p per can. I lose count of the number of varieties they do - tuna, chicken, rabbit, beef, duck   heart, turkey, lamb   turkey, duck   rabbit, salmon   trout, cod, mackerel   plaice to name but a few. There are also some varities in gravy instead of jelly too but my  boys  (two ten year old ginger tom cats) prefer the jelly varieties. The cans come with those handy ring-pulls so they are easy to get into and the cats recognise that tinkling can-opening sound  The different flavours are also different colours (as are most brands) for easy recognition.The ingredients are a little bewildering - how much  true  meat is within these cans is debatable amongst the additions of  meat and animal derivatives   listed on the label. It is also fortified with essential vitamins, minerals and fibre for the cats health. Mine seem to be thriving on it anyway. One can lasts my two cats one day and they are big eaters. There is rarely any waste - they seem to enjoy licking the jelly off first then going straight in for the chunks  Felix also do other cat food such as dry snacks and treats but this is their main food.My cats recommend it       ', '    GARDEN FLEECEWhat is it?   Well you don`t have to keep sheep and I am not referring to your bestjumper. This is horticultural fleece for use by smart gardeners. It is a very lightweightfibrous material that allows light, heat and rain through and will resist about 3 degreesof frost. Moor if used doubled.Why use it?  In a nutshell to protect your plants from birds, insects and, to somedegree, from frost. It is particularly effective for keeping birds off of your newly sownpeas. Just lay it flat over the site and peg down with tent pegs, or bricks, at reasonableintervals. For late sowings drape it over half hoops and leave it there until your peasare ready to be staked and it will eliminate the pea moth.It will keep carrot fly away from, would you believe carrots, and, any number of pestsaway from any number of plants including fruit bushes. It will keep newly sown fineseed warm until the seedlings are established and, when folded makes a very soft seatfor your garden chair.Availability  Just visit any garden centre or large diy store or, for a better bargain,browse through the ads in the popular garden magazines. Considering that it is re-useable over many years the price is very cheap. It will pay for itself more than oncein the first year of use by improving the quality of your crops. It is usually available in1 metre or 2 metre widths with the lengths being variable.During the first year that I used it in my allotment it created quite a talking point andat the end of the season my results justified it`s use to the extent that the followingyear most of the other plot owners were using it. Now, several years on, it is used byalmost all of the 24 gardeners at the site.      ', '    This washing-up liquid is part of the Cussons group.  I paid 54p for a 500ml bottle.  The scent is lemon and lime and contains real citrus extract.It is powerful at cutting grease, and you only need to use a small amount in your washing up bowl to get maximum effect on both your hands and dishes.  I found it to be soft and gentle on my skin, although it does state on the bottle to avoid prolonged contact if you have damaged or sensitive skin.Amongst other ingredients, it contains more than 30  anionic surfactants, and less than 5  nonionic surfactants.  I m not sure how much of the liquid contains actual lime and lemon extracts, but even a small amount is better than nothing The smell is quite strong, and the smell of lemons does, I find, overpower the limes.  It s a refreshing smell that, after washing-up, does leave a pleasant smell in your kitchen, and on your dishes.For questions and comments, call free on 0800 581001 or write to:CussonsFREEPOST NWW13380StockportSK3 0YL     ', '    Parsley is our best-known herb, and no kitchen garden is complete without it. It is a biennial, usually grown from seed as an annual.Cultivation:Sow directly in the soil from March   8211; August. Later sowings will overwinter, for use in spring. Germination is slow, so be patient. Incorporate plenty organic matter, and keep well watered throughout the season. Pick regularly to encourage new growth.Uses:Tasty in salads, as a garnish for fish and meat dishes, and an addition to sauces, soups and stews.Recommended Varieties:Moss Curled, Favorit, Bravour.*****Note to my regular reader(s). You will be disappointed to learn that I have not discovered the art of brevity. This opinion is an entry for Ken s Challenge - to try to write a VH op in exactly 90 words. Normal rambling service will be resumed.     ', '    Parsnips are difficult to start off because of the long germination time required and it is easy to lose them in the garden because the weeds will grow first and weeding = disturbed parsnip seeds.I avoid all this by germinating my seeds in short, rolled up tubes of newspaper. Make up some newspaper tubes about an inch in diameter and 3 to 4 inches long. Fill with a mixture of peat and sand and stand them up in a seed tray. You can easily get a couple of dozen in each tray. Put 2 or 3 seeds into each tube and, when they germinate just keep the strongest. You can keep the tubes in the greenhouse or cold frame until the seedlings are a couple of inches high.Now for the second tip. Get hold of some old drainpipe preferably 5 or inches diameter and cut it up into lengths of about 15 or 18 inches. Insert them about 3 inches deep, and just a few inches apart, into the ground and fill with a mixture of peat and fine sand. (Do not use builders sand as this will itself and and may cause forking. Pop along to your favourite garden centre and get some silver sand.) Add a small amount of your favourite fertiliser but, avoid one with an high nitrogen content as this will encourage foilage as opposed to the root. Now transfer each complete newspaper tube into a piece of pipe and water in.This avoids any root disturbance and keeps your parsnips free of weeds. Do not water to much during the first few weeks as this will encourage the root to grow straight down in search of water. You should finish up with some nice, long and clean great specimens        ', '    Persil capsules are the newest thing on the market now.  They re little capsules in the shape of a UFO, with persil washing liquid contained in them.  I paid    2.95 for 20 capsules, which is 10 washes.  It s expensive, I know, but as they are new, I thought I d give them a go.  It does say on the box to use 2 capsules in a light to normal soiling wash, and 3 in a heavy soiling wash.Using them couldn t be simpler really.  All you do is place your washing into the machine, and put 2 of these capsules on top of the washing, then begin the washing cycle To look at, they are quite large in size, and can see that a decent amount of liquid is going into the machine, and, presumably, the correct amount   It does state not to overload your machine.  It also says not to break or piece the capsules.  They are not recommended for handwashing either.Well, I ve done a couple of washes with them, and so far, I m happy with them   They are stored in a plastic bag, which is placed in the Persil box.  This is handy if you do get any that leak.  The clothes smell nice, and they are easy to use.Although, I must say, I still prefer using the powder.  This way, you can use however much or little you wish to.  But, with the capsules, although you could use more, it would certainly work out more costly with the price of them.It s an ingenius idea using capsules.  It makes you wonder what they will come up with next, doesn t it?  They are handy for anyone who lives in the fast lane, and just want to bung the washing in the machine and go.     ', '    When it comes to kitchen cleaners I don t really mind what make I use as long as it cleans and contains bleach, that is until I discovered Tesco s own brand.It is on offer at the moment for 79p (500ml spray bottle). The great thing about this is that there is a black clip and when squeezed together acts as a lock so any little fingers (like my 4 year old boy) won t be able to spray it here there and everywhere. The cleaner is suitable for all types of surfaces including sinks, work tops, cookers, tiles and so on (I use it everywhere). Even though there is bleach in the cleaner there is no horrible smell (I hate the smell of bleach) and leaves all my surfaces clean with quite a nice fragrance, which doesn t last very long but as long as all germs are being killed and the kitchen is getting disinfected what does it matter. Basically all you have to do is unlock the spray, aim and fire then wipe down with a clean cloth and hey presto all is clean. Any stubborn stains like blackcurrant just leave for a few extra seconds and they soon disappear. Again as there is bleach involved you have to be careful when it comes to clothes etc (as per the bottle) but I have yet found any of mine with tiny bleach marks (unlike Flash spray with Bleach which DID mark a t-shirt of mine) so I think it is quite safe. Can cause irritation for sensitive skin (no problems with me) and there are the usual warnings about keeping away from children etc.Well worth the money and now it is the only kitchen cleaner I buy.     ', '    These little gems, are a tube about one foot long by 3  in diameter and covered in paper.  You put them into your grate and light the paper at both ends.  Once the flames catch (and they do every time) the  log  will burn for approx. 2 hours - giving off a substancial amount of heat.We have found that if you place them onto a layer of coal first before lighting this will then form the basis of a lovely roaring fire which will keep you warm all evening (just top it up with extra coal as and when) They are the ultimate in fuss free, sooty hands free, fire lighting.  They don t make too much ash either.We have so far found them in B Q, Homebase and Tesco but they may be available in more stores.  They cost between    1.50 and    1.99 depending on where you purchase.So if you use your coal fire regularly and find it too messy give Tiger Tim a try - he s GGGGRRRREAT       ', '    With a sprinkle, sprinkle here,And a sprinkle, sprinkle there,That  8217;s what it  8217;s all about Max, my new cat will not eat his dinner, even with only five teeth, if it does not have Whiskas Crunch  Topping. For some reason, Max (and the late, great Tiny) really loves the cereal, chicken, duck and turkey cat shaped biscuits. This topping seems to add an extra texture to the soft tinned, pouch or trays of wet food that other companies produce. Whiskas Crunch  Topping is highly nutritious. These biscuits also contain extra vitamins and minerals to complement Whiskas cat meals.UseIt is really simple and uncomplicated. Put wet food in the cat  8217;s dish and sprinkle the crunch over the top of the food. Place the dish on the floor for the cat to eat and digest at their leisure This 100g tub costs around 69p from Tesco  8217;s. The tub is easy to identify, being round in the corporate purple of all Whiskas products, with gold writing. The lid is plastic and easy to open. I store my pet food in a cupboard out of temptation reach, so I am not sure how easy the tub is to open for a cat A tub used twice a day, on average lasts about three weeks. That works out at 1.7p per meal on top of price of wet food. This is great value for money, if it adds to the cats satisfaction and happiness.For further information Crunch  Topping and other Whiskas products contact:Pedigree Master FoodsFreepostMelton MowbrayLeicestershireLE13 0BRTelephone Number 0800 738 800Website www.mypetshop.com     ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re after a quick fix for those pesky fingerprints and greasy smudges on your glass surfaces, Cif Glass and Window Wipes do a decent job—especially for spot cleaning. They’re like the trusty sidekick to your elbow grease and soapy water, not a full-on replacement. The wipes are handy for smaller jobs, like sprucing up your computer screen or TV without leaving that annoying smear trail behind. Plus, the resealable packaging (think baby wipe refills) keeps them fresh and ready for action, which is a nice touch for anyone who hates dried-out wipes.

That said, don’t expect these wipes to cover a large area in one go. Despite the “large” label, they’re on the smaller side, so if you’re tackling big windows, you’ll be reaching for multiple wipes—and maybe some patience. Also, while they dry quickly thanks to the fast-evaporating alcohol solution, some users have noticed smears can still show up on glass, which is a bit of a letdown when you’re aiming for streak-free shine.

In terms of value, these wipes strike a balance: they’re effective for quick, targeted cleaning and save you the hassle of mixing solutions or hauling out buckets. But if you’re looking for a one-stop, all-surface miracle worker, you might want to keep your expectations in check. For the pragmatic cleaner who appreciates efficiency and a bit of convenience (with a side of humor about the “large” wipe size), Cif wipes are a solid, if not perfect, addition to your cleaning arsenal. Just don’t forget the elbow grease for those truly sparkling windows!

product_reviews: ['    My mum bought me a black labrador when I was 11 years old, I   d gone on for ages about how much I wanted a dog and promised to walk it every day before school but that never happened  We got our Labrador, who was named Tessa when we got her and we stuck with it, from an animal shelter. She was with about 5 of her brothers and sisters and she was the smallest one and the others kept trampling on her  She definitely was the best choice  Labradors are very loyal and very affectionate. They only have one owner which in our case is my mum, as I have moved out now. It was always my mum who fed her and took her for walks and now she absolutely adores my mum. She goes crazy if she sees anybody hug my mum  Labradors are beautiful dogs, they can be white, black or chocolate colour. Tessa is a black lab with white markings on her. They are not the cleverest of dogs, for example, when we throw a ball for her it will land on the grass, and she carries on running for it as if its still in the air  They can be very naughty as well, and they always know when they have done something wrong. Tessa loves to raid the kitchen bin  You always know when she has done it as when you come home and she doesn   t greet you, she is always hiding upstairs looking sheepish  She puts on a sad look and you cant help but hug her, she is so cute  Labradors are full of energy and need lots of attention. They need walking everyday, and can walk for hours and not get bored. My mum always takes her out when the soaps go off at night, and as soon as Tessa hears the corrie sound tune she jumps up all excited  She knows she   s about to go for walkies  If you are going to get a labrador, consider getting two as Tessa loves other dogs company. She gets very sad and depressed when she can tell you are going out as she hates being on her own, she must get so bored when my mums out at work all day. My mum has got her a number of toys to keep her occupied, including one which is a ball, which you put dog treats inside. There is a small hole in the ball, and Tessa has to push the ball round the house and try and get the treats out of the hole. It gives her something to do while she   s all alone  Our labrador is also great with other animals, we have a cat and they love to sleep on the bed together. We also had two rabbits and we used to leave the dog out in the garden with them and she never bothered with them  It was so funny to see the two rabbits, dog and cat all in the garden together in the summer, none of them bothered the others  Labradors can be a little unpredictable, they are very soft and love affection, but if you go near their food or their owner they can be very possessive. They can growl and show their teeth to warn you away, and a couple of times she had gone to bite people. I would be wary of having a Labrador dog near small children, especially as kids tend to torment animals some times. Labradors can be very greedy with food  Once my mum had 3 packs of rolos in her bag for her, me and my brother. We came home one day to find Tessa had eaten all 3 packs of rolos, foil and paper aswell  She has taken countless loafs of bread of the kitchen worktop  She has eaten boxes of muffins, anything you leave out she manages to get it  Tessa is now 11 years old, and all the hair on her face is going white now, bless her  She still loves playing with toys though, going for walkies or just sitting on the sofa having a cuddle. I would definitely consider having another labrador dog again, they are so much fun, not just as puppies, as adults too  ---Also posted on dooyoo under the same name---Thanks for reading my review x     ', '    We are foster carers and Social services are very fussy about the kind of dog we are allowed to have. We have a toddler granddaughter too.We had a lab before who sadly died when he was 11 years old. We always said  never again  - the sadness is too much to bear  Then two of our friends split up-neither of them could keep their 2 year old black labrador called Buster and they asked if we would take him. We took one look at him and he melted our hearts instantly.He is just such a great character  He bounces with energy but is incredibly careful around small children. He tolerates all the games kids like to play. He brings such joy into all our lives. He will run all day when we take him out- then he is ready to go again soon as he has had a drink.If you are looking for the ideal family dog who is safe around children and who will guard your house as if he owns it then look no further. I recommend the labrador retriever to you. You will never regret the decision to get one of these wonderful dogs.I have decided (after a few requests ) to add a bit to this.Labradors come in a choice of 3 colours- black ,chocolate brown and a golden yellow. If you breed different colour adult dogs the puppies still arrive in these 3 colours. There is no such thing as a  mixture  of these colours.The puppies are ready to leave their mother at about 10 weeks. They need vaccinating before they are allowed out or in the company of other dogs.Usually 2 vaccinations 2 weeks apart, cost about    30.00.  The dog will need booster vaccinations once a year.  A good idea to ask your vet to microchip your dog-cost about    20.00 but well worth it if he/she gets lost.I have always fed my dogs on  IAMS  dry dog food. This is a pelleted food which is usually given dry but can have added gravy if changing over to this diet. The dog needs plenty of fresh water down for drinking. The  End product  of this diet is much less offensive in smell and much easier to poop-scoop  This IAMS can be bought in varios size bags, the larger you buy the cheaper it works out. It costs about    3.50 a week to feed Buster because I buy the largest size sack. He has all the suitable scraps that my family leave and he also has many treats.He is fully grown and weighs about 6 stone-kilograms?-never heard of them  He is a very strong dog and requires a lot of exercise to keep him fit and happy. He would happily run 10 miles, stop for a drink and then run another ten.Definitely a dog that needs space and preferably a garden to run in. Failing that, an owner who is prepared to give the time and energy to make sure he is taken out regularly.Love and affection?.....110 Faithful?................110 House guard?......110 Safe with kids?......110 Very highly recommended dog. He is laid at the side of me-I have read to him what I have written and he just yawned...hope you aren t doing the same....Thanks     ', '    The Labrador Retriever is an extremely popular breed.However, regardless of the popularity and reputation, this breed is not for everyone.The breed has actually became far too popular for its own good in respect that people have gone out and bought a Labrador without researching the breed first.Resulting in many Labradors worldwide being given up, as the owner has been caught off guard, completely unprepared.The Labrador was a favoured breed of mine before we bought our Labrador, Jasper. My Grandad also owned a Labrador (or did Laddy the Labrador own him?) So, here it is an opinion on the Labrador, the facts about them, and my thoughts. ~~ Some history and background ~~The Labrador Retriever was developed in England in private kennels, the aim was to breed the perfect gundog.However, the original history stems back to Newfoundland in Canada apparantly dating back to at least AD 1000. The Labrador Retriever was first ever used as a Fisherman s dog. The majority of Labradors are strong swimmers and have a love for the water.The Labrador comes from the Retriever family, of which there are curly-coated Retriever, Golden Retrievers, Flat-coated Retriever and short-haired Retriever (no doubt a few more I have failed to mention)There is only one standard breed of the Labrador Retriever, however there are actually two standard  lines  which is unbeknown to many people.There is the  show line  and the  field line .These two lines of Labrador are slightly set apart in individual area s.Both lines however will make both great pets and show great hunting skills.You will find that breeders or owners of one particular line will really favour their line over the other.If you want to own a Labrador for reasons other than a basic pet i.e showing, then get your dog from a showing breeder, and vise versa if you are interested in owning a Labrador soley for hunting/ field work. Labradors have been used as service dogs, guide dogs for the blind, and sniffer dogs. However, Springer Spaniels recently topped the Labrador as being the better sniffer dog as they are smaller and lighter. It is great that you have the choice of colouring to blend in with the land you will be working your dog on more or less. * Weight and HeightThe Labradors in America tend to be slightly heavier than ours in the UK. The top coat being quite hard, with a more lighter, fluffier under coat.The top coat helps prevent water from getting in, and the undercoat helps to keep the body warm and dry.The coat on a Labrador doesn t come in any other forms.Think of a typical Labrador Guide Dog, and this is the coat which a Labrador will bear. Anything else, and you will no doubt be looking at something from the Retriever family, rather than the Labrador Retriever as a whole. Although Labradors  shed  twice a year, they also shed throughout and in-between. There really is an awful lot of hair to contend with when it comes to cleaning.It is recommended that you hoover every day, and without a doubt I can back that up. Ensure that you groom your Labrador at least once a week, not only to keep the coat looking clean and healthy, but to also work-out and remove loose hairs.I would always say it is best to do this out doors as grooming really does become a loose-hair fest  The coat doesn t need particular attention when it comes to bathing, infact, bathing can do more harm than good as it strips off the natural colours.Jasper is coming up to a year, is groomed weekly, has never had a bath, yet he doesn t smell and has a silky coat which is commented on regularly. In the event that your Lab does have a bit of mud here and there, you can clean this off with luke warm water.I have read that bathing should be reserved for when your Labrador has really been rolling in  it  * NoseI didn t even know this myself until recently, however it is possible for a Labradors nose to change colour. Generally they are darker during the summer months, and will get lighter during the winter. They can even change from black to pink This is another thing I haven t witnessed myself, but would be a great thing to see  So don t despair in thinking your Labrador has got a disease of some sort if you were to see this happening.Although the nose pigmentation can change, the eye-rims and lips will not. Named as a  Dudley . I only mention this as when paying good money for a Labrador, or any pedigree dog, you are generally or hoping to pay for the best dog money can by in means of health. Thus, hoping that you will have very little or slight problems with your dog in the future. More on that later though.* General appearanceThe Labrador is a strong built dog, however, dependant on the line of breed, show or field line, there is slight difference in the appearance.Labradors have a broad skull, and a deep chest area.Your first impressions of a Labrador should be that they look  strong and muscular  (when fully grown) Jasper is still in the teenager category, though he is filling out beautifully. ~~~ Temperament ~~~The temperament on a Labrador can alter depending on the amount of exercise he or she gets.A Labrador who has the correct amount of physical and mental exercise can be quite relaxed, however, if this is not met the Labrador can be quite active. In the first 3 years of a Labradors life, he will be quite boisterous and always on the go. Although, again, mental and physical exercise can help slightly during these first few years.If a Labrador isn t well exercised it is known that he will go  looking  for trouble. Labradors love to be around people, they really do, through and through.So, do take this into consideration if as a potential owner, you will need to leave your Labrador on his own whilst you are out at work alot etc.When Labradors are left alone, this is where the trouble tends to start, especially with chewing. Labradors are famous for their chewing as it is, without increasing this due to being bored.Labradors are a real family dog and they have alot of patience when it comes to children.(Again remember that during the first 3 years, a Labrador may appear scary to a young child because of his uncontrollable behaviour and such like) I will mention Labrador and training further down the lines, which is a must with this breed  If a Labrador was to hurt a child, this would definitely be down to play and caused by an accident rather than a bad-tempered streak.The Labrador breed by all means doesn t make a good guard dog. Yes, the Labrador will bark in a protective manner, however in person a Labrador will not act aggressively as such. There is a famous saying that the Labrador would rather lick an intruder to death than to bite one  Having said that, I do feel safe with Jasper, when I am alone in the house. His bark definitely sounds very alarming, very deep and forceful, which is a deterant in its own way. Jasper enjoys looking out of the window, watching the world go by, and then barking if the shoe fits.Because Labradors are very intelligent dogs, it is said that Labradors can be trained to be aggressive on demand. This is of course reversing the temperament the Labrador was bred for. Though Labradors can do very well at being aggressive once trained.I would seek professional guidance however if thinking about going down this route, as there will be a specific way of training this kind of behaviour. Labradors are quite stable dogs, and not easily upset by strange happenings. I found socialising Jasper to be quite easy to date, as he seems to be inquisitive over new things rather than scared of them. ~~~ Scavanging  Traits ~~~Yes, the Labrador is a greedy dog, or is that a hungry dog?You should be extra careful not to fall foul of the typical  head tilted to the side  Labrador look, or the giving of a paw in order to seek food from you.This is an easy way for your Labrador to gain weight.A typical Labrador should not be fat, but lean and have muscles. ~~~ Lets Walk ~~~If you don t train your puppy to walk properly alongside you at a young age, when he grows and gets bigger you will find yourself having real problems. The Labrador is a strong dog, full of muscle and can pull hard enough to take you off your feet if you are of a small frame.Jasper used to pull hard enough that on my own I could not take him out.However, with training classes he has improved and I can now enjoy taking him out without a fuss.Even now however, Jasper is the kind of dog that must walk ahead of me (or anyone) and you will usually find this is the case with any energetic dog.However, when Jasper is off lead, he is never more than 15 paces ahead of me, and he is always looking over his shoulder to check on me.  Labradors once matured it is said require approximately 2 hours exercise per day. This however should be split up between different walks, training and play. They will also adapt quite well to what you can manage.Good exercise should be given off-leash, during a nice long walk.Weekends are the best times for us to give Jasper really long walks. His best being either at the beach for a few hours, or a country walk. We are lucky, as we live quite near to both.~~~ Retriever ~~~The Labrador is renown for having a strong desire to please. The Labrador also has a strong desire to work, having been specifically bred to be a gundog/ retriever. They really do have a natural desire to retrieve, I can give an example of their designed genes.* This is a true example with what our Labrador Jasper carried out only a few months back. Me and my partner were walking Jasper late at night, off lead, we came across a cat teasing an injured pigeon.Jasper ran towards the cat and pigeon, of which the cat quickly ran off. Then, Jasper picked the pigeon up in his mouth and ran towards Jonathan, and dropped the pigeon at Jonathans feet A prime example, and although we do not want to encourage this behaviour, it would have been wrong of us to tell Jasper off as this is his natural instinct. To retrieve.Do not get me wrong, Labradors don t actually kill or hurt the prey, they simply carry it in their mouths.Which is the prime example of which I have told you. At this point in time, Jasper had not even had training in this area, again showing the Labradors natural instinct.~~~ Training ~~~It is imperative that you begin training your puppy Labrador as soon as he arrives into your home.If you don t give your Labrador puppy training, you will most definitely have problems further down the line.Training will also give your Labrador mental stimulation which is extremely important for his well-being. As a puppy, we firstly introduced the basic housetraining to Jasper, and as of course, puppies aren t able to go out-doors beyond the garden until they have completed their important innoculations, some basic obedience training can begin in-doors.You will find that the Labrador picks up commands quite well, providing he is taught correctly. Bad training can easily confuse any dog, causing him not to pick up and learn at the correct pace. Your most common behavioural problem is chewing. Again, this can be caused by a number of reasons.Luckily, it doesn t last forever, generally it stops within the first few months.Correct measures can be carried out to help prevent this such as again, exercise, (exercise can still be given even while your Labrador is waiting to have the all clear to be allowed out-doors following innoculations) play games to give mental stimulation and exercise all in one go. Give him plenty of chew toys and ensure that you praise him when you return to an undamaged kitchen. Training is of course a new topic entirely, and therefore trying to stick to the desired topics, my best advice would be: Invest in a good training book Contact your Local Labrador club for any information relating to anything concerning this breed Take up Obedience training, either doing so yourself, or via a local class Join newsgroups, a great way to speak to fellow Labrador owners and swap stories, advice etc.Training is a must to keep this breed happy and under control due to their temperament. ~~~ Choosing a breeder ~~~When buying a Labrador puppy (or any other pedigree), it is important that you buy from a reputable breeder. This is because, for the amount of money you will be paying out, by buying from a backstreet breeder as such, you could end up paying amazingly high vetrinary bills due to hereditary problems in your puppy. Or other problems associated with  bad breeders .Pricing for a Labrador is usually in the region of    350 and above. The colour of Labrador does not alter pricing. Breeders really build up a good reputation for themselves, and the best way for breeders to achieve this reputation is by entering their dogs into conformation shows, or Field Trials etc. Their goal is to have a judge recognize their dog as a champion, which of course takes alot of money, time and effort on the breeders behalf. Which then brings to the question, would a reputable breeder sell his stock at a really cheap price?You need to ensure that your breeder is thorough, although not necessarily the larger the breeder the better.A good breeder will: Use a reputable stud  Ensure that the stock are x-rayed Use a quality food to ensure correct growth and health is obtained Will not raise their pup s in an unclean environmentThe last thing you want to do is to buy an unhealthy Labrador. Ask to see parents hip and eye scoring. They can certify this by presenting a document through OFA or Wind-Morgan. When both sets of hip scoring is added up, you are looking for a score which is in the region of 20. The lower the better of course  Hip-scoring is very important, as Labradors and other dogs commonly suffer from a condition called Hip Dysplasia. This is said to be hereditary too, so by carrying out a selective breeding programme (those will low hip-scoring only) should eventually and hopefully wipe out the condition.A list of reputable Labrador breeders can be obtained by contacting your local Labrador Club if you are unsure or require any help in any aspect. ~~~ Choosing a puppy ~~~Choosing a puppy isn t as simple as getting in your car and picking one up.Speak to a few breeders before making your choice, and check that the pups are living in a clean environment.Also check of course that the puppies look healthy, not too thin, and that they look stable. Check that the puppy is lively, but don t be misunderstood in thinking a tired puppy is a lifeless one.Check for mites etc, to do this brush the skin backwards with your thumb. Look for what looks like bits of dirt in the fur.Generally, a puppy in a dirty environment will be more prone to having mites so take note  Be at ease with the breeder and ask away as many questions as your heart desires.Before you speak to anyone, determine which sex and colour you would like. Of course, you may even be open minded regarding this. Though most people are favourable towards a certain sex and colour.Your breeder should help you decide which puppy is best for you, as he will know their personalities better than anyone. You wont of course be able to take your puppy home until he/ she is at least 8 weeks old, but you will be able to of course visit before they are at this age. A good breeder will also be willing to take the pup back off you if you feel you have made the wrong choice etc. The breeder will supply you with a diet sheet, and will advise you of food your puppy is currently using. This being that you should never chop and change a dogs diet, especially with puppies   Our breeder supplied us with a tub full of the food Jasper was using (in order we could wean him onto a puppy food of our choice) However, we also bought a huge supply of food from him, as we weren t quite ready or sure about food etc at that given time. Also, should you choose to purchase a puppy, ensure that you obtain the Pedigree Certificate. The certificate can inform you of some great information, as well as being an important document in certain situations. In Jaspers case, his father, grand-father and other relatives are Field Trial Champions. ~~~ Common health problems ~~~As established above, hip and elbow dysplasia are common problems in the Labrador breed. This condition is where the joints don t all fit together properly. Cataracts and arthritis also being common problems. Labradors are also prone to ear infections, as due to their  hanging ears , also some mild skin allergies which seem more prone in the Chocolate range.There is a new problem which has recently been recognized within the Labrador breed, this is a defect of the heart and its name is Tricuspid Valve Dysplasia. At this moment in time however, it is unknown as to whether this disease is inherited, nor how many Labradors have this disease. You can read up on these problems, as there are a wealth of good books available.With regards to hips, try and prevent any problems in the future by trying to make sure that they don t slip about on wooden/ kitchen floors etc.Also ensure that you keep them at their desired weight, to help deter them from having future problems.~~~ Is a Labrador right for you? ~~~When looking for a dog, it is extremely important that you choose the  correct  breed of dog to suit you and your lifestyle. Simply purchasing a dog because you like the look of it is a no go area  Research the breed thoroughly, and if in doubt, keep looking until you find a breed which matches your criteria. You definitely need to be prepared for the Labradors high-energy, again which doesn t settle down until he matures at about 3 years old.~~~ My overall thoughts ~~~We have had Jasper coming up to 10 months, and we have had our ups and downs with him.Overall, I would describe Jasper as being an extremely loving dog, full of energy and very child like, in many ways.He loves to play hide and seek, and he also loves to roll about on his back, scratching himself on nearby toys whilst making strange noises. All in good fun though as the tail never stops swinging  When it comes to play with Jasper, we can play as rough with him as we can bear to stand. He definitely isn t one for a little gentle fetch, he really likes to play and get interacting. Most Labradors are swimming lovers, Jasper being one of them. He also loves to go on long walks up in the hills, smelling all he can manage to take in.He just loves to be with people, showing his true Labrador qualities and he also loves his food with an absolute passion.He also loves running up and down the stairs too, believe you me, if I am going up or down the stairs he has to beat me to the top or the bottom.Since when did the staircase become a race? He has been a pleasure to train, although don t get me wrong, sometimes he just wants to play rather than get down to business.He also wants to play late at night which can be a nuisance when your favourite TV program is on. But since when can anyone refuse such a face?I have found Jasper to be quite hard work at times, though I must stress that this was more when he was about 3-4 months old. As he has developed, and combined with training, I have watched him calm down. Though he is still a very very lively dog, and has such a different character to what Labradors generally are portrayed to be.Anyone who owns a Labrador will agree with me, I m sure, that this breed is certainly a wonderful one, with an excellent loving temperament. One last factor I would like to mention, is that Jasper has occassionally shown what we initially thought to be authoritive behaviour. I have also heard this is common within various other Labrador Retrievers. However, this is actually something displayed with the dog feels uncomfortable or ensure in a particular situation.Example; Jasper used to do this when I tried to get him out of the bathroom (a favourite haunt for him, but I don t like him being in there for many reasons) as Jasper didn t like me reaching for his collar. Therefore, to prevent this happening, I now ask him to Sit and Come. He also gets a reward for doing so.As like any breed, try and look behind their behaviour, to try and see why they do what they do. You will almost always then come up with a common sense answer  I have tried to keep this opinion focused on the Labrador Retriever in general, therefore anyone who is seeking to buy a Labrador or any other breed, should really invest in a good book to cover the typical  dog owning  area s. However, I hope that this has given you a great insight to the breed and has also helped determine whether or not this is the breed for you. Remember, a Labrador can live up to 15 years (although their life-span is between 12-14) which is still long enough, so DO make sure that you choose wisely To see a recent and puppy photo of Jasper, have a look at my profile. ', '    This is my first review on Ciao so I thought I would write about a subject very important to me, my 2 year old Labrador.  My wife and I bought the dog as a puppy soon after we were married. We paid    300 for her and I believe that is an average price. There are three different colours of Labradors, Black, Yellow and Chocolate. Our dog is a beautiful chocolate colour. The hair on the Labrador is short with a harder coat outermost with a softer coat closer to the skin. This helps the dog keep both warm and dry. Because the hair is short, it will not need much cleaning but will need to be brushed at least once a week.Labradors belong to the gundog group and are often used in field trials and as guide or hearing dogs.A Labrador will grow to about 22 inches and will weigh approximately 30 kg. They are described as medium sized. I personally think this makes them on the large size. Something that should be considered with small children. The dog could easily knock them over,  Their tails are long and are quite strong in their movement. Labradors generally have a gentle and friendly temperament. They like to be play and be petted. They do need quite a lot attention. If left they will become bored and chew things.They are also quite boisterous and will need quite a lot of exercise. They have a good deep bark and will greet people noisily. They are not aggressive though and will not make a particularly good guard dog. They have a good appetite and can be a little greedy so you have to be careful not to overfeed them. A Labrador will cost about    5 a week to feed. The Labrador is quite hardy but like any dog they are susceptible to some disease including hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, epilepsy Cancer, Metabolic Liver Defect and ear Infections. Overall, the Labrador makes a great family pet but they will need regular exercise and grooming to keep them healthy and happy.     ', '    Well as you may have guessed I have a gorgeous dark yellow (I say ginger but apparently that s not possible) Lab.  Well she isn t mine, she s the whole family s - but I m sure I m here favourite This might not be considered a good op - but all I want too do is tell you how great my dog is We argued and argued on names for her, and for some god forsaken reason this was the best (how bad were the others you ask I hear you ask )  She came to us in February 1998 on my brothers 16th birthday, apprently the  unwanted  out of the litter - well that was it - love at first, second, third etc sight She shares the same birthday as my mother deceased brother - which in a way makes her that extra bit special.  We were not a  dog family  apart from brother no2 and the whole point of the visit was to prove that - now? Pah I have always had a fear of dogs after been chased by a pack of five dogs (all different breeds - apart from labs) at the age of seve, bitten by a sheepdog on the face, narrowly missing my eye at the age of three and again at five on my arm.  SO obviously I didn t feel comfortable with dogs.  And my father, who grew up on a farm didn t see the point of cats or dogs unless they were  working  animals.  And well Mum, and bros no 1 3 just complete CBA about the whole pet thing.Anyway - home with us she came, a nervous little bundle with beautiful big brown eyes.  The first night I stayed up with her as the poor little thing whined all night.  After a couple of days she settled in though, becoming a bit more adventurous her tail (which may I point out is bloody painful when it wacks you) waggling away knocking everything over.  Mum wisened up to this and moved all valuables to window or mantlepiece level.She was housetrained within a couple of days.  Responding well to compliments and hugs when she did right.  No need for heavy handedness with tese beautiful beasts A little probs with labs is they looooove chewing shoes - one of each pair if possible - but so what I love her (I did love those russel and bromley cow skin mules - but she did me a favour they went out of fashion so quickly )A massive plus is  HOW FRIENDLY?????   She is fantastic with kids.  Coming from a large extended family I have cousins that are younger than 5.  THey tug at her ears and drag her round the garden and she loves it.  A couple of kids that have been petrified of dogs feel very comfy  playing rough  with Pooch, putting their hands in her mouth and letting her climb over them.  If they nap, she will lie as close as possible to them, jumping to attention to the slightest movement.She loves her sunday dinners, and will not beg on sundays because she knows she ll get hers once it cools down.  She is now 6 years old and still has the innocence of a puppy.  If all labs are like my baby I would highly recommend them as a family pet      ', '    About 3 years ago I set off in my car to Devon. I returned    200 lighter and with a bundle of brown fluff  Yes, I d bought a chocolate Labrador.The Labrador is one of the most popular breeds of dog. It makes an ideal family pet.Originally it was bred as a working dog. These days you see them used more frequently as guide dogs and search and rescue dogs.The breed originated in the early 1800s when fishermen from europe travelled to Newfoundland. There they found a large heavily built breed of dog, known as the Newfoundland, and a lighter built smooth coated dog - the Labrador Whilst making excellent pets, Labradors are a large breed. This means that they need a great deal of exercise, eat a lot of food, and should be trained well to enable control over the dog. As with any breed, the Labrador can be expensive to keep in terms of food and vets bills. I have found it wise to take out insurance on my boy, just in case The most common health problem that I know of with Labradors is that as they get older they can have problems with their hips and eyes. To combat this, a lot of breeders have hip and eye scores done on the parents. This shows how likely the offspring are to have any problems.All in all, my Labrador is fantastic (but then, i m biased). His great qualities are that he is friendly, obedient and a great companion. His not so great points are that he is full of energy (we come back from a two hour walk and he s raring to go again ) and he eats his way through mountains of dog food each week  I would recommend Labradors to most people. However, they would not really be suitable in a small flat. They are fantastic with children and adults alike and if my partner would let me, I d have a housefull of them      ', '    I have a 5 year old Golden Labrador called Polly.  She is the best dog that any family could ever own.Labradors are kind and gentle with everyone especially young children.  I trust my labrador 100  with my 5 month old baby daughter.  I know she would never become aggressive even whilst having her ears pulled by my baby, being sat on by my 2 year old and being chased by my 5 year old.Labradors can have problems, they are well known for having arthritus in their hips.  They are tested for this as puppies.  My labrador sadly has developed epilepsy, which I have now discovered can be another problem that occurs in labradors.We bought our labrador from a breeding kennel in Hampshire.  I would never recommend anyone to by a puppy from a place like this as I believe there can be too much in breeding (mothers with sons etc) and I feel that this may be why my labrador has epilepsy.  If I ever bought another labrador I would buy one from a reputable breeder, visit the puppy at the breeders home and make sure that I saw the mother with her puppies.  My husband and I were shown the mother of our labrador, she was brought to us and then taken away again.  Our puppy was also brought to us in a room and we never saw them together and we never saw where she was kept.I have found that female labradors can become protective over their toys but only with other dogs.  Our dog would never become agressive with my children and I would have no problem with them removing her toys from her mouth whilst playing.  I would not trust any other dog to be like this with my children.  Labradors will spend hours chasing a ball and bringing back.  Unfortunately sometimes she brings back other dogs toys instead.  They then develop jaws of steel and a good grip and lots of treats are required to retrieve the ball or toy.My dog is a yellow labrador (golden) but you can also get black and chocolate labs.  I believe that the chocolate labradors can be slightly more expensive to buy because of their colour.Labradors can cost    300 to    350 to buy from a breeder but I know that there is a labrador rescue centre in Sussex that rehomes all age labradors that have lost their owners or who are sadly unwanted.Remember, if you purchase a puppy they will remain very lively for the first 18 months.  They will chew everything, slippers, furniture, carpets, absolutely anything    After 18 months they suddenly calm down and spend most of their time sleeping.Labradors make extremely good guard dogs as they have a really deep bark that will ward off unwanted visitors and postmen A labrador is classed as a large dog and will therefore require a lot of food. My labrador eats tinned meat and mixer biscuits but many owners give their dogs the complete biscuit mix.  They are also prone to becoming overweight so do not overfeed.  They will eat any scraps on offer so try to resist dropping the leftover pieces of toast from the kids plates into the dogs bowl because your dog is looking at you with its big brown eyes.  I absolutely love labradors because they are just the best family pet anyone could ever own.     ', '    Labradors are a breed of gun dogs. They usually make excellent swimmers and live on average between 10 to 12 years. Labradors are loyal loving dogs and are well known for their friendly and gentle characteristics. Female Labradors should weigh between 25 and 32 kg. Male Labradors should weigh between 29 and 41 kg.The Labrador retriever comes in long hair and short hair varieties. The only difference between the two is the coat. The long hair retriever needs regular brushing where as the short hair type only needs brushing occasionally. The Labrador retriever is the most popular breed in the world for family pets. This is due to their easy going nature. Labradors by nature are gentle with children and other pets and extremely loyal to their owners. Labrador Retrievers are also known as very playful dogs. They usually enjoy tug of war, ball games, seeking games. They have a very good sense of smell and absolutely love food so treat reward games are always a hit. They will eat almost anything which means you must keep a close eye on their weight as they can easily become too heavy. They will often eat food from the streets or parks unless you can train them well to leave.Labrador Retrievers are intelligent dogs and are therefore very easy to train. They also enjoy learning new tricks and usually pick commands up quite quickly.Labradors need quite a lot of exercise, at least 1 hour a day, but they do better with more. They can use energy quickly on playing, running or swimming and they can maintain stamina on a long country walk as well. They are very sociable animals and enjoy being part of a pack, so they more family they have, human or animal, the better.When they are puppies like most breeds, they can be quite destructive. This will become worse during a bitches season. Do not worry, this phase is short lived and with plenty of exercise and the right training you will have a wonderful dog by about 10 months old. You can get Labradors in 4 colours, Black, Yellow (Golden), Chocolate and Red. The first three are common and can be found quite easily via the internet or papers. The Red Labrador is actually a dark ginger colour and is not quite so common, but can be found. There is no difference in characteristics for each colour, only appearance. Labradors are medium to large size. They have webbed paws which makes them good swimmers. They usually have a round rib cage and stomach and if they are a healthy weight, their waistline should go slightly inwards just above their rump. They have floppy ears and can shed regularly and significant amounts so don   t get a Labrador if you like your house to always be spotless.Summary: Labrador Retrievers suit a variety of people. They get along well with children so can join young families. They are usually gentle with other animals and friendly to all adults. The more exercise they can have the better, so if you have no time to walk them then don   t get this breed. They love cuddles and human attention. The more they get the happier they are. They can sometimes before fearful of other dogs and need lots of socialising from a young age to avoid this. This is probably the friendliest breed of canine you could get and if you want a four legged best friend, then this is the breed to get. I have only met two unfriendly Labradors whilst walking my dog and hundreds of friendly one s. Any negative behaviour in this breed is usually due to the owner and training classes can fix this.I think this breed makes the perfect family pet and because of their characteristics will remain the number one breed of dog for the unforeseeable future.     ', '    We decided to get a labrador as we have heard they are great dogs to get along with kids.When we got him we paid    220 for him when he was 8 wks old got his papers and a diet sheet for him. He settled in very quickly and our then 2 yr old although was scared of dogs soon took to Prince after a couple of hours. Prince has been a great puppy we have had him chewing, whinging, whining, barking when we are out, dragging us along the streets on walks, and he barks when we are on the phone or hoovering up for some reason or other, but like i say he is a puppy so to be expected.Prince is very friendly and loyal to us, he really is a great dog and he loves the kids they can go up to him and sit on him being young kids we have and he sits there and licks them to death, i dont think he would ever bite anyone he doesnt even bark when someone knocks on the door   The kids more often then not sit with him and talk to him and stroke him and he sits there listening to them as if he can make sense of them which he probably can as Labs are very intelligant, he loves walks and swimming and generally easy to maintain, and he only costs us    8 per mth to insure as well which covers most things. I would say anyone that wants a loyal and loving dog would be best to get a lab especially if you have kids that come round or you have kids at home young or older.      ']

If you’re considering adding a Labrador Retriever to your family, here’s a balanced, down-to-earth overview based on what many owners have found helpful. Labradors are famously friendly and well-natured, making them wonderful companions and great family pets. Their affectionate nature means they rarely show aggression, which is a huge plus if you have kids or other pets. However, don’t expect every Lab to fit the textbook description—each dog has its own unique personality, so be ready to adapt and learn as you go.

One interesting tidbit is that Chocolate Labradors are rarer and often come with a higher price tag, so if you’re drawn to that beautiful coat color, be prepared for the extra cost. Speaking of costs, Labs are not the cheapest dogs to keep. Their large size means they eat a lot, and food bills can add up quickly. Plus, regular vet visits are essential since Labs can develop health issues like hip dysplasia and eye problems as they age. It’s wise to budget for these potential expenses upfront.

Labradors are bundles of energy who thrive on daily exercise and playtime. They need plenty of space to roam and a firm hand in training—clear boundaries are key to managing their exuberance and ensuring they grow into well-behaved adults. If you’re someone who enjoys active walks and outdoor time, a Lab can be a perfect match. But if your lifestyle is more sedentary or space is limited, you might find their energy a bit overwhelming.

In short, Labradors offer loyal companionship and lots of love, but they require commitment, both in time and money. If you’re ready for the responsibility, their joyful spirit and affectionate nature will more than repay your efforts. Just remember to plan for their needs realistically, and you’ll have a wonderful furry friend for years to come.

product_reviews: ['    When walking through Tesco a few days ago, I saw this on special offer and as Cillit Bang is a trusted brand - thought I would give it a go. Background If you have ever watched the tv, you would of heard of their advert. As I mentioned in my title their catchphrase is  quot;Bang and the dirt is gone  quot; ... ringing bells? For some people they love the advert, others hate it. You could call it a Marmite advert I guess  But now moving onto the product.The PackagingThe actual product is very recagnizable and I don t think would be hard to find on the shelf. Like I have always remembered it, it has a deep purple background colour and the red and yellow background on the label. And like normal it has all the gem about how wonderful the product is and so on - I won t spend half the review talking about that  With it being a trigger it does also have the useful gadget of the on-off nozzle. You simply turn the end square and it will either halt the spray coming out or let it flow free. Basically a child lock - very useful for some people  So - Does it work? Well, yes  Although the dirt doesn t completly glide off (what cleaner can do that? ), it doesn t take too much elbow grease. More off a wipe just to help the grime on it s way. I also find that it isn t too strong a smell. I have experienced some where the smell is so strong I have too open the window - this didn t happen with Cillit Bang. Another good plus for me. I can also say that a 750ml lasts a long time as you only need a brief spray for it to be really effective.How to useYou simply spray it on the area that you want to clean, leave it for up to about a minute and then wipe away the stains. Then wash off with water - I find warm water the most effective.Avalibilty and PricesI know it is avalible in Tesco, Sainsburys, Asda and Morrisions. I am pretty sure that it is in Iceland and Co-op as well. As for prices, if you really want to give it a go, get down to Tesco who are doing it for    2 (where I got it from ). Otherwise I think the general price is around    3.05. So all together I give Cillit Bang Power Cleaner 4/5 stars. It would of got 5/5 stars but it is quite expensive when not on offer.Thanks for reading  Please comment and rate  x     ', '    When it comes to household cleaning I must confess that I am a little lazy, so anything that promises to make such a chore a little easier is likely to catch my eye. Something that comes packaged in a bright purple trigger spray bottle with a shocking pink top is even more likely to grab my attention.And so I parted with my    2.98 in Asda and decided to give it a try         .The 750ml bottle looked pretty large but it certainly wasn t the cheapest product on the shelf. The label on the front had a pale orange background with the words  Cillit BANG power grime and lime cleaner (the BANG on this label is in capitals, no it s not my caps locked on) and beneath this there are three different pictures. The first of these portrays a bath with the word Grime beneath it, the second image in the middle shows a sink with the word Stains beneath it and the third picture a shower cubicle with the word Limescale beneath.And so  I put my new purchase safely away at the back of the cupboard, out and sight and out of mind, whilst the Stains and the Grime and the Limescale on my bath accumulated            .It was last Saturday afternoon when I was panicked into taking drastic action. Some friends had  invited themselves to stay over, which I had apparently agreed to after a pint or two (sorry if any of you ever read this - honest )I got out my dishcloths and filled a bucket with hot soapy water and off I set in the direction of my bathroom, armed only with my basic no frills proprietary cream bathroom cleaner, which I squirted around the bath. After a few minutes of scrubbing  I suddenly remembered my Cillit Bang, tucked away at the back of  the cupboard and I foolishly imagined that those days of hard labour and elbow grease were over. I would simply need to give my bath a good spray and all of the Grime and the Stains and the Limescale would disappear like something from a tacky Paul Daniels trick from the 1980 s whilst Debbie Mghee looked on amazed      .My first surprise was how the product resembled something rather familiar, the soapy water in my bucket.  It is not an abrasive cleaner , which I have become familiar with, but instead it is a liquid, a very nice smelling liquid, but nonetheless a soapy liquid which ran down my bath and straight down the plughole.The instructions on the back of the bottle advised me to hold the bottle upright and approximately 12cm away from the surface, to spray directly onto the area which was to be cleaned, wipe with a cloth (or sponge) and leave for one minute. These instructions I followed to the letter with baited breath but alas to no avail.It is true to say that  the stains did eventually vanish, but it wasn t anything to do with the Cillit Bang (or Paul Daniels and Debbie Mghee for that matter) it was down entirely to the good old fashioned elbow grease that I had to apply  afterwards and I felt robbed for having parted with my hard earned cash when my usual cleaner at a third of the price was equally as effective.On a positive note it did leave my bathroom smelling much cleaner and fresher than my usual cleaner but I think that this a high price to pay for something that leaves my bathroom visually the same as something far cheaper and without any reduced effort. If you’re tackling the kind of grime that laughs in the face of your average cleaner—think ovens, hobs, BBQs, and extractor hoods—Cillit Bang Power Cleaner Degreaser is your new best mate. product_reviews: ['    Let me tell you about what I use to do my least favourite chore, washing up. Ok so I don  8217;t like ironing, am not to keen on vacuuming, or dusting. Dearly beloved does most of it anyway, I cook (I like doing that) but let me tell you about Ecover washing up liquid.I try to use some products that do little or no harm to our environment. Ecover seems to be produced in a factory in Belgium that seems to be using environmentally sound resources and methods where they can. I explored their web site www.ecover.com and was quite impressed ok I was supposed to be I do think they seem to be heading in the right direction. Shame there is not a bottle refill centre near here that I know of.The bottle caps and label are all biodegradable. Costs    1.58p for 1 litre but it does last a fair time.Happy washing up      ', '    Our dishwasher is out of action. It s sitting in the garage feeling rather lonely. One day, when I ve sorted out the conservatory/extension/outhouse, and it s become the laundry, and there s room in the kitchen, our dishwasher will be pressed into service once again. Until then     and at the Murphy rate of house improvement it may be some time     we are back to washing up by hand. Hard work, isn t it? Guess which washing up liquid we re using?Ecover.Ecover are probably the most famous of the  environmentally-friendly  manufacturers of household detergents. Among their products you will find: cream cleaners; multi-surface cleaners; washing powder; fabric conditioner; bathroom and toilet cleaners; dishwasher tablets. They ve been making them since 1979. And they ve been making them in the world s very first ecological factory. It s made largely from wood with a grass     yes, grass      roof. They ve even won a seal of approval from the United Nations, who added Ecover to their global roll of honour for outstanding environmental achievement. So, you can see, they re a sound company  If you want to find out more about them you can, at their open and honest home in cyberspace, www.ecover.com.To the liquid, then MacDuff.Easy enough to find on the supermarket shelves, the Ecover washing up liquid is packaged very prettily. Look for the almost opaque bottle with a lovely picture of a camomile leaf on it. Look on the shelf with the large sizes. Although they make it in both 500ml and 1 litre sizes, I ve only ever seen the larger one in either Tesco or Sainsbury. It s plain but pretty, and in comparison to the garish offerings by the likes of Fairy, Persil and Morning Fresh, I think it looks rather sophisticated. Not that washing up is a particularly sophisticated activity, mind you. Ecover s packaging is 100  recyclable; made from polypropylene and polyethylene. Sadly, in the UK, plastic recycling is patchy to say the least, so your bottle may well end up as landfill anyway. Check out www.wastepoint.co.uk to find your nearest recycling site. Mine is miles away in Chard. Sigh.Ecover washing up liquid is promoted as a  green  detergent. How does it arrive at this claim? Well, it s all to do with its active ingredients. The active ingredients in washing up liquids are  surfactants . Surfactants act to dissolve grease, oils and fats. They hold them dispersed and suspended in water so that they don t settle back onto the surface of whatever it is you re trying to clean. The surfactants in most washing up liquids are made from petrochemicals. The surfactants in Ecover s offering are made from plant-based sources. Plant-based surfactants biodegrade more quickly, so causing less environmental damage. And they can be produced with less harmful pollution as a by-product. Ecover s washing up liquid is safe to use if you have a septic tank, for example, something most of its competitors cannot claim. The petrochemical industry has an ever-shorter lifespan as its resources dwindle. Clearly then, Ecover is the choice if you re concerned about such things as global warming and the pollution of rivers and seas. Ecover also have a comprehensive policy on animal testing     including the standard  five year  rule for its suppliers which is about the best a cleaning product can promise you under current laws     so it s also the least unsound for any anti-vivisectionists out there.What else is there to tell you about the soundness of this product? Ah yes. Fairy may well claim to be  kind to your hands  but I know, prone to eczema as I am, that I d not use it without washing up gloves, for my hands would become dry and chapped very quickly. Not so with Ecover. Its lack of petrochemical ingredients and the addition of camomile and milk whey mean that I find I can wash up using Ecover with absolutely no ill effects whatsoever. Hurrah  If you suffer from sensitive skin or any form of dermatitis at all, you ll know what a huge advantage for Ecover this is.So, it s made by a non-polluting factory, it s in a pretty bottle, and its ingredients are as sound as a detergent s ingredients could possibly be. It won t damage your hands either. So far, so good. But the ultimate question is; does Ecover clean dishes efficiently? All of the fine things we ve found so far will be pointless if it fails that test. You ll be glad to know that yes, it does clean dishes efficiently. It cuts through grease as well as any other liquid I ve used. It copes wonderfully well with most Murphy Dirty Dishes, including such nasties as roasting pans, teacups with tannin stains, and Tupperware containers stained with tomato-based sauces. I find that Ecover cleans as well, if not better, than the emergency bottle of Fairy I bought from our local Spar a few weeks back. And it cleans this well at water temperatures I can put my gloveless hands into. If you tried some of the very early  green  detergents and weren t satisfied with their cleaning power, I d urge you to give Ecover another go. These second generation products really do compete in efficiency with the multi-national brands. Even the worst of tannin tea stains, or most baked-on of casserole dishes will come clean with a short soaking. With the bottle of Fairy I bought, I found that neither of these filthiest of kitchen dishes would come clean with any less than an overnight soaking.One thing to remember when washing up with Ecover: you need only a tiny squirt of it to clean your dishes. The plant-based surfactants we spoke about earlier do not form lots and lots of suds, unlike their petrochemical counterparts. You won t have a frothing, foaming, bubbletastic bowl of washing-up water at all. It s quite a shock when you first begin to use it. Fear not though; these suds are merely cosmetic and you really don t need them at all. Your few Ecover bubbles will do the job of your zillions of Fairy bubbles equally well, I promise. Don t defeat the object of all this green-ness and use half a bottle of the stuff at a time And is there a price to pay for all this eco-conscience? No  Hurrah  Ecover not only works as well as all those other nasty, polluting brands but it s no more expensive  In some cases, it s cheaper, too. I hadn t looked at its price before writing this opinion because if I think something is  better  or  the right choice  then I just buy it. And I arrived here, at my last paragraph, prepared to try a bit of gentle persuasion on my readers that it would be only right to pay a premium for Ecover, given its many advantages, only to find there is no premium  Below, you ll find pasted current rates for washing up liquid at www.tesco.com     you might be as surprised as I was Ecover 1 litre         @    1.35Fairy 1 litre          @    1.58Persil 500 ml          @    0.74Morning Fresh 500 ml   @    0.66Tesco Own Brand 500 ml @    0.64Good, huh?There is little I find to criticise with Ecover. And what there is, I guess is largely out of their hands. I d like to see the major supermarkets stock the 500ml bottle size, but they do not. I d like to see them stock the lemon-fragranced product as it s suitable for vegans, but they do not. I d like to see the supermarkets offer a service to refill the Ecover bottles, but they do not. I d like to see this product available in the modern corner shop     the convenience stores such as Spar and Londis, but it rarely is. My local health food shop stocks all these items and will allow me to refill my bottle too. So I m buying Ecover there from now on. And I ll be telling Tesco why, too. Bloody supermarkets. Oh well, at least they actually sell it.I m so pleased with Ecover s washing up liquid that I ve decided to put the DIY on hold. The dishwasher can continue to languish in my garage, and the conservatory/extension/outhouse can continue to function as a greenhouse. The only thing remaining to do is to teach the children how to wash up. Ha. Some chance      ', '    Ecover Washing Up Liquid is available widley in most supermarkets I have been to and costs around    1.68 for a litre sized bottle.The bottle is the usual shape you would expect for a washing up liquid but the colour is light / off white instead of the usual green.  It has a flip top lid and is easy to dispense.It is fairly thick in consistency but you do need a nawful lot before you get any decent bubbles with this liquid.It is not as good as Fairy Liquid, by any means.  It does not remove grease and grime or baked on food from pots and pans with any real efficiency and even after soaking dishes for a long time it is still very hard to remove food debris.It is also quite harsh on the skin and I find it very drying, so rubber gloves are a necessity when using this product.The smell is also not pleasant and has a strange almost sulpher-like smell to it that is difficult to explain.It seems to be weak and watery and although I bought it originally for ethical reasons, and I have had the same brand washing powder which I have used with some degreee of success, I would not recommend this product unless I was pretty desperate, which is a real shame as I was hoping for great things.     ', '    I don t generally tend to write reviews on mundane household products unless I find one that stands out from the crowd.  Ecover Washing Up Liquid does just that in my view so I thought I would put  fingers to the keyboard  to tell everyone what makes this washing up liquid different from the rest.Why try the product?To be honest I can t really remember what it was that prompted me to buy my first ever bottle of this washing up liquid. I guess I must just have been having one of those days when I was trying to be a little  green  and protect the environment so I picked up a bottle and took it home with me.The next time I did the washing up I put a squirt of this into the bowl and tried it out.  The first thing I noticed was there weren t anything like as many bubbles in the water. Ecover was founded in 1980 in Belgium and is now an international company.  Ecover   s progressive environmental policy is not only demonstrated by the products it sells, it is also an integral part of the company   s business operations.  Their mission statement saya  quot;Ecover strives to provide effective, sustainable solutions for the hygienic needs of people. quot;  I certainly think that they achieve this,  having started with their washing up liquid I have tried other products and none of them have disappointed. I think the cleaning power is far superior to the products I have used previously and it is kinder to the environment.     ', '    ECOVERCleaning up The WorldAs anyone who has read any of my reviews will know, I m a big fan of natural. Natural colours, natural fabrics, natural stuff in general, and in particular natural cleaners. Doesn t matter whether we re talking recycled loo roll, plant based face wash, or opening a window instead of spraying half a tonne of fake air freshener, it s all the same to me. Natural. To say a big. Loud NO to all the companies out there that have got us hooked on chemical based, toxic products to clean our homes within an inch of their red-brick little lives.******************************************************************************************************************************************Who are Ecover?Well, they are the revolutionaries who first stood up and said  wait, there is another way   In Belgium, in 1980, Ecover was founded, as a pioneering company, selling phosphate free products. As a company, Ecover is very concerned about environmental issues and in 1992 they opened the world s first ecological factory - it has a green  live  roof  This product is actually made at this factory.Every part of their business is covered by ecological policy, not just the products and production of them, but everything else, like marketing and sales (for example, they will refill your old bottles of washing up liquid, collecting them and delivering them back, free of charge. I think it compares very favourably financially, and it is certainly my first choice when it comes to buying washing up liquid. So go on. Save the world - buy Ecover Thank you  for reading, Kate x     ', '    Ecover Ecological Washing Up Liquid has been available for many years. However, the Ecover for company has not been content to rest on its laurels.No, they have researched and worked on (for over 20 years, mind ) not only expanding their range of green, eco-friendly products, but on also improving the quality of the products they already make.The first thing you will notice is that there is no absolutely unnecessary garish colouring in the Ecover Ecological Washing Up Liquid.
