Petrochemicals are used in making most washing up liquids, as are a number of other chemicals which aren   t good for plant, marine or animal life, and Ecover clearly state on their product that this doesn   t contain any petrochemicals, and that no chemical residue will be left on your plates etc. when you use it.Now I don   t know about you, but I   d never really thought about what residue is left on my dishes by my washing up liquid until someone pointed it out to me (which I   m hopefully doing now for you of course), the thing is, I don   t really want to be ingesting chemicals that are harmful to animal life as that presumably means they can   t be particularly good for me either   I   d much rather use something that isn   t going to do me any harm at all, and this is where the Ecover comes in handy again    it   s harmless  It   s biodegradable (there is a difference between    degradable    and    biodegradable        look it up ), it has minimal effect on marine life etc. too.Cost wise, its pretty good.  You can buy this in a wide range of sizes.  500ml @    1.23, 1 litre @    2.03 (these are pretty standard sizes you   ll find most washing up liquid coming in), 5 litre @    9.86, and 15 litre refill box @    28.60.  So, if you want to make the biggest savings, buy the 15 litre refill from somewhere online such as big green smile as this works out cheapest (the prices quoted are from Big Green Smile, but they   re similar from other places).I suppose, these days, if I   m honest, I prefer to buy Earth Friendly Dishmate     I like the scent better, it   s just as environmentally friendly and I personally think it works a bit better.  However, I have to buy it online as I haven   t found any supermarkets or other stores locally who sell it.  If I have to buy my washing up liquid in a shop, then I will choose Ecover.  It   s the easiest environmentally friendly option to find and it does work plenty well enough.  I don   t need to worry about rinsing everything over and over there   s not residue left, it cleans well and I   m not putting nasty stuff down my drain or into me.  Overall I   d say it compares well cost wise to most of the big brands that it   s competing with, and it   s just as good as most of them too.     ', '    Ecover Washing up liquid comes simply bottled in plain white plastic ,but the packaging goes one step further,the bottle and label are made from polyethylene and the cap is made from polypropylene,both of which are 100   recyclable.What Ecover say about the product :The liquid is freshly perfumed and made from plant ingredients.It cleans and degreases efficiently and is kind to your skin.The liquid leaves no residue and it is possible to get a refill for your bottle.Refills are available from many health food shops and your bottle will refill over 50 times before it needs replacing.Ecover deliver the washing up liquid to the Health food shops in large drums that are also recyclable.I sent for a free sample of lemon Ecover washing up liquid from HotDealsUK ,like many of us I just love a freebie.I had forgotten all about it by the time it was delivered in the little brown jiffy bag.I decided to trial sample after supper,when I not only had plates,but dishes,glasses,cutlery and pots and pans too.I filled the basin with hot water and gave my mini ecover a good squeeze.Nice lemony smell ..but hardly any bubbles.The glassware washed well and shone afterwards,the plates I washed but then rinsed again,they still felt a little bit grainy.The serving dishes were cleaned easily as were the pots and pans.I did the cutlery last of all in fresh water and Ecover worked its magic yet again.So my trial bottle gave me good insight into how well Lemon Ecover washing up liquid performs.Overall it performed exceptionally well.It degreased well,made a good job of the cutlery and the glassware.the plates just needed that extra rinse.But the one thing I missed were ..BUBBLES   A 500ml bottle of Lemon Ecover washing up liquid costs 97p in Tesco.     ', '    I used to use fairy to clean my dishes but last year I discovered that proctor and gamble test products on animals. Now, I wouldn t state I m any kind of animal activist, or a warrior for fair trade...I don t go vigorously seeking products to boycott, and I don t do a great deal of investigation into the products I buy. That said, if I learn a product I often use is animal tested, I would endeavour to discover a superior and kinder alternative. That s how I ended up using Ecover. Ecover is the lone non-animal tested and environmentally friendly product I was able to locate on my supermarket shelves, and was suggested to me by a friend who s very exacting on which products she will allow in her house. They produce other cleaning products as well: cream cleaners; multi-surface cleaners; laundry products. I went on the Internet to investigate them a little, and Ecover was established in 1979 and was the first company to manufacture ecological and animal friendly cleaning products on a large scale. They ve also been added to the United Nations list of companies with exceptional environmental achievement, as well as many other awards, such as most innovative product and a corporate conscience award. The product is straightforward enough to find in large supermarkets, and in Holland and Barratts, but you re unlikely to find it in your corner shop. Made in 500ml and 1L sizes, and available in either Chamomile and Marigold or Lemon and Aloe Vera varieties (the lemon being vegan), the packaging is attractive .The bottle is almost opaque, although you can still see the liquid through it. The bottles are quite chunky, and the chamomile one I ve been using has a pretty picture of the chamomile plant on it. There is an Ecover logo on the front, eco in blue and ver in green. It s simple but attractive, and compared to the bright gaudy packaging of other brands; it stands out as being both the pl ainest and the most attractive packaging. The packaging is made from recycled materials, and is recyclable itself, The bottle and labels are made of polyethylene; and the cap of polypropylene. I ve never seen a plastic recycling point near me, so mine unfortunately ends up in the bin anyway. Ecover is a very environmentally sound product. The main ingredients in washing up liquids are surfactants, and they dissolve grease easily. While most companies use petrochemical surfactant, Ecover use plant based one s, which are much more biodegradable, and cause less pollution when being produced. It s also less harmful once it s released back into the rivers. The top brand washing-up liquid is 40 times more toxic to fish than the Ecover detergent. The fragrances used in the products come form essential oils, and are not synthetic in any way. With regard to animal testing Ecover do not test their products in animals. That in itself isn t too remarkable, but Ecover also refuse to buy or use ingredients that have been tested on animal in the last five years, which for a cleaning product is great. While this all sounds good, the most important thing is whether or not it actually works. Well, yes, it does. Brilliantly in fact. One tiny squirt will be enough for a sink of dishes, and will clean them easily and efficiently without leaving any trace of grease. Tougher dishes may need an overnight soak. It has a lovely chamomile scent, soothing and relaxing me as I use it. It doesn t froth up as much as other brands, but it cleans just as well, and you don t need as much. I have quite dry skin on my hands, and find that a lot of products irritate them when I m washing up. But not Ecover. It doesn t affect my skin badly in any way, and I personally think it s actually softened my skin (must be the chamomile) It s not very expensive either. It s actually cheaper than fairy. Fair y costs about    1.60 for a litre, and Ecover is about    1.30 for the same amount. Would I recommend this? YES, BUY IT. Basically anyone wants their washing up liquid to do the job well, which this does, with the added bonus of being environmentally and ecologically sound, and not tested on animals. The fact that it costs less than fairy is just the icing on the cake  They have a great website at www.ecover.com, which gives more detail about their company policy and their products, and is well worth a look. Thanks for reading.      ', '    I have to admit that I have noticed that some of our  environmentalist  friends used this product and I always thought it had to be completely ineffective if it was good for the environment.  So I have always stuck to my big brand varieties but at the same time I have been quite aware about the number of chemicals that we have in our kitchen cupboards but to my shame had done nothing about it.So when we went on holiday and the cottage we stayed in used all Ecover products I felt like I was getting a free sample so I test drove the products and was particularly impressed by the washing up liquid.  So much so that when we got home and I needed to buy some more washing up liquid I thought I would ge this product and see how well it lasts.I have to say that I have been extremely impressed by this product     it has a wonderful camomile and citrus smell which is light and yet does not linger on your crockery.  As far as I can see it does what it claims to with the minimum of fuss.  According to the information on the back of the bottle it says:   Cleans and degreases efficiently using the power of nature.  Kind to your hands thanks to plant based ingredientsNot based on petrochemical ingredientsNo residue of unnecessary chemicals left on your dishes    To test this I did arrange a pan test (merely to satisfy my husband that this product does actually work and I wasn   t jumping on the environmentalist bandwagon) with the remainder of our well known branded washing up liquid versus the Ecover.Using two dirty saucepans from the night before I put the Ecover in the dirtier of the two and the well known brand in the other.  We then put some very hot water in each pan.  The Ecover pan only required a little rubbing with the sponge to get the dirt off whereas the well known brand needed a bit of scouring help.  Also the Ecover made the saucepan lovely and bright     it looked properly clean.  Was this because of the lack of residue you have to ask.I suffer from eczema on my hands and for years (or so I tell my husband) I haven   t been able to wash up due to my hands becoming irritated.  The only downside then to this product for me is that I now have to do the washing up because it doesn   t irritate my hands   But I have no complaints with its cleaning ability and would not hesitate to recommend this product to anyone.  And not just anyone with an environmental conscience but anyone who wants an effective washing up liquid.How much do you need and how long does it last?You don   t get a lot of bubbles with this product but you   re not supposed to     you just get effective cleaning.  One squirt is enough for your average bowl of washing up but for more stubborn, dried on dirty dishes a little soaking is required in very hot water.  As for how long does a bottle last we have just finished our first one which was bought 3 months ago (please note this is based on two people who wash up straight after dinner so dirt isn   t allowed to dry on much and whose main source of    burnt on    dirt is a cast iron griddle pan which has a protective coating).Are there any other benefits?Yes all of their products offer the best levels of biodegradability which far exceeds legislative requirements.  The bottles and labels are made from polyethylene, the caps are made from polypropylene both of which are easily recyclable in a low energy process.  Refills are available although they are not  widely available but you can check here for your nearest refill supplier http://www.uk-marketingdatabase.com/ecover/ECOVER.search.show_parms).  You can refill your bottles up to 50 times - again positively impacting on the environment.Because the products are plant based there is minimal impact on aquatic life.Ecover are against animal testingAnd you can use this product in your septic tank (if you so wish ).Where can I buy this? It is becoming more popular with supermarket chains but can also be found in some health food shops.  Here is a link to Ecovers stockists http://ecover.reference.be/gb/en/WhereToBuy/Price wise it was    1.74 in our local Sainsbury for a 1 litre bottle.  I was a little taken aback by this but then 500ml of our usual brand was    0.89 so it was about the same price per litre.  You can buy it in a 500ml bottle for    0.99 so in that respect it is a little more expensive but as I soon discovered well worth that little bit extra.  The only thing is the products don   t seem to be on offer as much as the standard brands so that is where the standard brands win in value terms.  But for quality and effectiveness without ruining the environment, this product wins hands down.Ingredients (from the back of the bottle with a couple of extra notes)>30  water5-15  aniomic surfactants (which are plant based)Milk whey (does contain a small amount of animal product), Extracts of camomile and marigoldCitric acid (plant based)Table saltPerfume (type: camomile, contains Limonene)Preservative (0.02 ):2-Bromo-2-Nitropropane-1,3-diolWho are Ecover?This review has been of this particular product but if you are interested in finding out more about the company click herehttp://ecover.reference.be/gb/en/About/     ', '    Ever since stumbling over ecover in the supermarket it has been the only product i use - for dishes clothes and the toilet, there should be more products like it and people should be more aware of the damage done to thier environment through all the chemicals they use just to clean thiemselves and thier house. Just look at the household isle next time your out shopping and think about all the chemicals on the shelves going down the plug - and then where to?Please if you already use this product recomend it to your freinds, i have tried. Ecover is great and all the product i use have been great so far, the orignal washing up liquid did smell a bit strange and the bottle did look too similar to the laundry liquid but the new product have resolved these problems and now look and smell great.With the Fragrance of camomile and marigold it makes washing up a pleasure.This product may be slightly more expensive than the leading brands but what is a few pence when you consider the implications for future generations.There is not much you can say about washing up liquid, but a lot you can say about the environmont.     ', '    Ever since my awesome night walk in the rain forest of northern Australia a few years back which included a talk on how we can all make little changes to the way we live and help preserve the environment we live in. I have been keen to do whatever possible to be kinder to the environment myself :o)Therefore slowly but surely I have been changing the products my family uses in the home from good old household names to Ecover a brand I have known only a short while but one I wouldn t be without.I have already successfully changed to Ecover washing powder and thought why not give Ecover ecological washing up liquid a go too.You can chose from camomile and marigold or lemon and aloe Vera. Both of these I have tried and liked. It comes in 2 sizes, 1 litre or 500ml. The plastic bottle is clear with the words Ecover written in blue and green, it also has an image of a green plant. The flip up lids are either green or blue. A list of ingredients and instructions for use can be found on the reverse.Its performance has been as good as my previously used brand Fairy. The consistency of the liquid is nice and thick and the aroma fresh and pleasant. It lathers nicely and allows me to wash my kitchenware   s brilliantly leaving no residue. My skin is pretty sensitive and as yet no nasty reaction has occurred since using.The two most important reasons for me choosing and using this:(1) It has an optimum level of biodegradability that by far exceeds the legislative requirements which means it is kinder to our environment :o)(2) It is made using plant based ingredients, which are kinder to us :o) Some supermarkets do seem to price this product higher than other brands, but I was lucky enough to find it in my local Tesco store (Brighton) for the same price as the leading brand I used to choose. Approx    1.50 for 1LPersonally it makes me feel good to use something that is kinder to the environment and does exactly what is required of it. That s why I shall continue to use Ecover washing up liquid.Why not give it a try Cheers for reading :o)     ', '    I recently went to the supermarket and found they were out of my usual brand of washing up liquid.  As was I.  Being totally desperate for some (not that I love washing up you understand ) I looked at the other brands available, comparing prices.  I noticed that Ecover washing up liquid was a comparable price to many leading brands, yet was an environmentally friendly product.  It also came with a coupon to send for money off vouchers for other Ecover products, so I decided to give it a try.For cleaning power, this product is very good, I don t need to use any more of it than I would of my normal product, so it will last a good length of time too.  It has no trouble tackling even the nastiest grill pan (my pet hate).  I have also noticed that it seems kinder to my skin. Since using Ecover my hands have improved a bit and it is certainly not making it worse.  An added advantage with this product is that it is kinder to the environment.So, will I buy this product again - probably not.  Why?  Well, when I first used it, I was aware of a faint aroma of indian cooking.  I thought it was one of the neighbours (though this is not a common cooking aroma where I live). Hey, at least I get the washing up done a bit quicker      ']

If you’re like me—someone who values a clean home without compromising on eco-friendliness—Ecover Washing Up Liquid is worth a close look. On the downside, while the price is reasonable given its quality and eco-credentials, it might be a bit higher than some conventional brands. But considering its effectiveness, safety, and sustainability, I find it a worthwhile investment. Overall, Ecover Washing Up Liquid strikes a great balance between practical performance and environmental responsibility—perfect for anyone who wants a clean kitchen and a cleaner conscience.

', '    To be honest with you I absolutely hate housework, if I can find myself something more interesting to do trust me I will sounds quite bad really but that   s life. Features:No loss of suctionLifetime filtersNo bags (what a result no more dust flying around in the air )All tools attach to the top of the HooverSelf adjustable head8.4 meters of cableInstant hose (for those hard to reach places)It comes in a wonderful lime green colour and as stated in the features it has no loss of suction, so it does a fantastic job of cleaning up that awful cat hair in less time. Its also light weight so if you do have back problems you won   t have any trouble moving it. As I said before I had previously borrowed a Dyson from my mum, and she has now got a Dyson Animal so if you have a big house and it   s like a train station then I would recommend this as it has some real hefty power behind it, but if you are like me and have a small family then the DC04 its just right for the job.So happy Vacuuming          ', '    Or did it? When we opened the box containing our newly purchased DC04 Dyson vacuum cleaner, I expected to see little green men climbing out of it   The combination of yellow knobs and purple borders and cable was quite a sight. We nearly reached for our sunglasses   Anyway, enough of the frivolity  A few years ago, I never would have believed that I would buy a Dyson or in fact, write an opinion on one. However, two years ago my old Hoover broke down. This my father had bought for me when I was in shared accommodation over 10 years ago for about    15. My husband happened to be working at Comet at the time, and managed to get about    100 pounds off since this particular machine had been a show item, and was a lot more expensive than it is now. So there we were in possession of a Dyson DC04, which was supposed to be the be all and end all. So here we go. What is all the fuss about?DescriptionIt is an upright model with a purple cable and yellow knobs. A very colourful object which definitely can t be missed. There is a see through cylinder at the front into which the dust and fluff goes. On the part of the handle under which the detachable see through cylinder resides, there is a help line phone number and it states that this line is available 7 days a week from 8am and 8pm. The cylinder is easily detachable by pushing the yellow sliding switch inwards and hey presto, the cylinder comes off and you can empty its contents. No bags are needed which saves money also. On the body of the cylinder it says   8220;The world  8217;s first vacuum with 100  suction 100  of the time  8221; followed by   8220;The most powerful upright cleaner and no loss of suction - Dyson MEMA lifetime filters TM -  High efficiency airways (patent pending) - Easy airway inspection   8211; Protected belt - Brush control (patent pending)  8221;. Just above this description there is a gray slide, which shows you how to remove the filter on pushing the slide, and how to clean it. Beneath the description there is a sticker saying,   8220;Bags kill suction  8221; showing a picture of clogged pores in a carpet, and a picture beside it showing the way the Dyson works with the comment   8220;No loss of suction   8211; Dyson Dual Cyclone   8211; TM  8221;.  Below the see through cylinder, the base of the machine is the brush mechanism. The top covering states:   8220;Adaptive brush control   8211; patent pending   8211; the clutch mechanism allows you to turn off the brush bar for rugs and smooth floors. Because of this, the brush on the DC04 should never need replacing.  8221; Then there is the yellow knob which has three settings marked D, P and N, and above this these are explained:   8220;N   8211; manual brush off for delicate rugs and floors  8221;   8220;B   8211; brush off when upright  8221; and   8220;D   8211; auto brush on for normal cleaning  8221; followed by protects belts and protects flooring. On the very bottom just above floor level it says   8220;Self-adjusting head   8211; pivots on two axes to keep level on the floor for any carpet thickness  8221; Then it explains safety features:   8220;Brush bar stops when obstructed and gives ratchet warning   8211; release valves (patent pending)   8211; protects children from powerful suction   8211; cable life extender   8211; thermal cut-out   8211; brush bar off upright position  8221;. On the front face at the bottom it says   8220;ABSOLUTE +   8220;   8220;HEPA filter + bacteria killing screen  8221;All the different sections are clearly marked and it is quite obvious for a novice to take it apart and reassemble it.AdvantagesWell, these are spelt out in the many descriptions on the machine itself. I can  8217;t help thinking that if there was a cataclysm on this planet, and most of life was wiped out, if any remaining humans found a Dyson, they would be able to understand how to use it    It is very good at its job, and the amount of dust and fluff that we get in the cylinder is greater than what we ever got in the Hoover bag. The technology works. The idea of the ratchet noise going off when the brush bar is obstructed is a good idea. It is then a good time to turn the knob to the   8220;manual brush off  8221; setting. It is great for floors as well as carpets, and saves time having to sweep up separately. The purple cable is very long, so in a small flat like ours, you don  8217;t need a cable extension. It is easy to maneuver because of the self-adjusting head. Cleaning the filter is easy, and unblocking the airway is also not hard. So all in all it is very versatile and useful.Customer service - The help line is a very good idea since it fell over, one day, and then would not work. I rang the help line in a panic only to be told,   8220;- oh that  8217;s deliberate so that it doesn  8217;t overheat  8221;. We had a Dyson repairman comes to the house the very next day to fix it, and then everything was back to normal.There are also three attachments, which you can use to clean round the edges of a room, the walls and upholstery. The arm, or stem, of the machine detaches, and you just fix the attachment to its end.DisadvantagesOoh   That ratchet noise, when you have forgotten to change the setting to   8220;manual brush off  8221;   It drives me mad since we have a rug with tassels and the Dyson hates it. But does it have to sound so upset? I always feel like I am upsetting it as if it was a small child   Maybe I am going slightly mad    I would also like to have been warned that it would refuse to work if it falls over, so that I didn  8217;t think that I hadn  8217;t killed it    It is also rather heavy, and a little awkward, and when I had tennis elbow, I had to get my husband to use it   SummaryWould I recommend it? Yes, definitely, although I believe there are lighter and more efficient models now. James Dyson found a niche and very cleverly exploited it. He deserves his wealth and success for the patience, perseverance and for producing such a good machine.       ', '    The title of this could be misconstrued. I also feel there are a few issues with the early wear and tear on the tools, which I had expected to last considerably longer, particularly due to the price of the product. I hope you found this useful and would thank you for bearing with me.This review was posted on Dooyoo on 30 August 2010 under my same user name. I finished my living room and then turned it of. Inside the clear bag less canister was the result, it was full  I was shocked how much dirt there was in my carpet especially when I had only vacuumed a couple of days ago. Plus it was only from my living room. I then cleaned the bedroom and again the canister was full of dirt and happy with the results I found emptying the canister really easy too but most of this dirt was cat fur so I had to put my hand in side to get the odd bits of fur out ( yuk ) After emptying the canister once more, I did the bathroom and hall way, and spare bedroom. That filled the canister with enough cat fur to require another emptying, but the job was done. I am very, very impressed with this new vacuum cleaner. Aside from performance, the cleaner has some good features. It has a filter system that prevents 99  of pollens and other particles from being recycled into the air. The back saver handle is also a very good. It is tall enough so I don  8217;t have to stoop to clean. It has on-board attachments, including a crevice cleaner and an upholstery brush, along with a 2-1/2 foot extension tube to reach tall places. It also comes with a 25   8211; foot lead much longer than my other vacuum had. This is good because you don  8217;t have to keep un plugging it to go into another room, it  8217;s a real time saver. I would definitely recommend this Dyson vacuum, although it  8217;s a bit expensive it does its job well.       ', '    I have just bought a new house so needed a vacuum for the first time. I searched the stores and was recommended the Dyson over and over again. It is a bit expensive at over    200, but not a problem when you have loving grandparents The DC04 absolute is great - it s very satisfying to see the dirt you vacuum up, and seems to suck up the majority of my dust. However, the hose does not extend as easily as I had hoped - the hose keeps falling off the wand. Also it isn t as easy as I had hoped in terms of maintenance, but the fact you never have to buy bags again is a definite plus. My hair is very long and still gets wound around the brush - if anyone ever finds a vacuum where it doesn t, let me know      ', '    It would be wasting time to list all the merits of the Dyson. Many are on record doing just that.   But I m on my second and still singing their praises.    I don t have any allergies but I do value a dust free environment when I am doing my housework.   Dyson certainly lives up to their promises in that direction.I bought my first Dyson when they were introduced to the vacuuming market. It was, without a doubt, a new experience in cleaning. Super suction, easy to empty - no fiddling around with bags - and bright and cheerful (grey and yellow) compared to the more mundane vacs on the market. Why do manufacturers always assume that because we use them for cleaning up dirt they have to look dreary? When my son left home and moved into his own flat I gave him my Dyson as a blatant hint that he should keep his new home clean. I replaced in with the newer model DC04. Apart from snazzier colours than the original, it also comes with a special tool for getting under things and, amazingly, has even more suction power. It is just a wee a bit disconcerting to see my new carpet being gradually sucked up into the clear plastic  dust tube  but it s a price I m prepared to pay for the supper efficiency of my new machine  It is a rather heavy piece of equipment to lug upstairs to do my bedrooms (the extra long hose and special tool actually takes care of the stairs themselves) and I am now debating on whether to break into my son s flat to steal back my old model or, even more painful, cut out chocolates so that I can afford to by another DC04.      ', '    You can   t be enthusiastic about a vacuum cleaner can you?  Now, come on, I   m not a train-spotter and I don   t even own an anorak, so why write a review of the Dyson DC04?To tell you the truth, I really hate vacuum cleaners; they make a horrid whining noise and you have to lift your feet up to let the wife vacuum under them    but the Dyson DC04 has actually got me at the controls, pushing it around and getting others in the family to lift their feet for me I have owned a few vacuum cleaners in my time, and have never found such an efficient machine.  A friend recommended that we get one, and reluctantly I capitulated and parted with the cash.To test it properly, I insisted that we vacuum the office thoroughly with the old vac.  The carpet looked fine, so then we started with the Dyson.  Miraculously, the transparent receiver filled up, time after time with dust, dog hair and fine grit that the other machine had left behind.We have some old rugs, and I was worried that a vacuum cleaner with such power would pull out all the tufts - the Dyson doesn   t; it just gets the dust out.With the built-in hose and tools, even vacuuming cobwebs off the ceiling and getting crumbs off the furniture is a doddle.The hose is long enough to reach up the stairs, with is a boon as we have three staircases in our house Overall, this is a well-designed bit of kit, and at the risk of being called an anorak; I would recommend it to anyone, but don t tell my friends - they will really tease me about it so, by writing this review I m really Dyson with Death      ', '    I bought a Dyson DC04 about just under a year ago. I had recently moved to my new home, whose previous inhabitants had consisted or a couple of rats, a few cats, and a hamster. I just could not get those hairs out of the carpet. It seemed as though I was constantly struggling with my old vacuum cleaner and I was going through the bags as if they were going out of fashion. I decided to take the plunge and splash out on the latest technology; a Dyson.My decision was primarily based on the bagless issue. I had looked at the alternatives, such as the electrolux bagless model. I decided that as Dyson was the first they must be the most advanced. The DC01 although cheaper still had filters to change, so I decided that if I am going to pay that sort of money anyway, that I d pay more and irradicate that problem too. So the DC04 it was My mum had bought the same model, so whats good enough for my mum is good enough for me. As I got it home I was amazed at the amount of dirt an dust and most of all hairs, that came out of my carpets. I thought to myself what a dream. My only niggle was that I was exhausted each time I used it; it was so heavy as I, myself am only five feet tall.Almost a year on now I am not quite as happy. Initially I thought that having a place for each of the tools was great. My opinion now is that their placing is rather annoying. After all, each time I use the Dyson I am guaranteed to knock one of the tools off. In addition to this I have had the wand and the hose replaced. My problems consisted of a split hose, the hose lock had broken, and the floor tool clasp had snapped. Although these are relatively minor problems they are problems that I would not expect when paying over    200 for a vacuum cleaner.On the up side, it is great not having to buy bags and filters. Mechanically it works as well as the day I bought it. The most positive thing is the after sales service that Dyson provide. As you can see on the vacuum they have placed their phone number, should you need it. You are provided with a list of the parts with the serial numbers and prices should you need them. If you do experience problems as I did there are no quesions asked and your problems are solved. My replacement tools were sent to me within a week of me contacting them.To sum up. I am not convinced that the DC04 is worth the price that I paid and it does not quite live up to the hype that surrounds the brand name. My advice is that if you can easily afford it, then why not. If however you would be stretching yourself, then look at the cheaper versions, made by other companies. Perhaps my experience is rare. I hope it is. Come to think of it, I have yet to see a second hand DCO4 advertised in my local classifieds....     ', '    I saved up and bought a Dyson with the idea that it was the best vacuum cleaner about.  When I first hoovered upstairs I thought it was wonderful, all this dust that I could see in the tube  wow  It even caused a grapple with my boyfriend cause he wanted a go with it.  BUT...... when I used it as instructed on the stairs, I felt a bit deflated, it wasn t half as good as it was on the floors.  It didn t get up the cat hairs as well, the suction was less and although you can leave the Dyson at the bottom of the stairs and take the attachment all the way up the stairs, it seemed a little cumbersome.I m still pleased with it, just thought it would be better on the stairs.     ', '    ^^Summary^^My Dyson DC04 has been completely reliable, it picks up everything including cat hair and it is easy to empty and maintain. On the flip side the Dyson brand has reliability problems, its noisy and some of the plastic fittings may not fit very well. ^^Introduction^^I bought my DC04 from Powerhouse back way back in May 2000, I paid    269.99 and it came in a coloured box. To get the box in the car I only had to put one side of the rear seats down (Model used 1992 Vauxhall Cavalier Saloon). I had just bought my first house a tiny one bedroom terraced place with stairs and nice thick carpets. I had heard how wonderful the Dyson vacuum cleaners were and a liked the bright yellow colour. I picked the DC04 as it had the minimal amount of attachments and I didn   t need the extra cleaning and filtering of the higher spec    models.^^The Vacuum Cleaner^^The DC04 is an upright cleaner, it is bagless with a large clear plastic container for the collected detritus, the rest of the cleaner is also plastic and is coloured light grey or bright yellow. It has a handle for upright use that also converts to the extension hose and it has three cleaning attachments available to go on the end. All this came in a large box with good clear instructions so I had no problem in putting it together and using it.^^Cleaning Experience^^This cleaner is powerful it works really well on carpets and lino floors. It picks up everything including cat hair, building waste such as small lumps of plaster and the occasional Monday morning cornflake explosion. The DC04 has an extension hose for cleaning stairs, nooks and crannies, however on stairs it will not reach right to the top step. The extension hose is much better than other cleaners of the time, as they had a separate hose mounted on the side. A push of a yellow button and the handle lifts up, there is a yellow cap that flips open and you can attach one of the three nozzles onto the end. Two of the nozzles are located above the plastic container in shaped recesses, the other thin nozzle is attached to the handle and all stay on the cleaner when I   m using it around the house.The only problem I have had is the flexible extension hose always comes away from the metal extension pipe. I guess the plastic clip doesn   t fit or work very well. It has never been much of a problem as I hold the plastic end of the hose when using the extension and it is not in an uncomfortable position. It is also a very noisy cleaner, making the cats dash out of the house every time it starts up. It is slightly heavy to carry up stairs, but when is an upright easy to get upstairs? I solved this problem by moving to a ground floor maisonette.^^Emptying^^To empty the cleaner is very easy, push a yellow button and the collector comes away in one large chunk. Place it on the floor near the bin and unclip the top filter housing from the collector and empty the collector into the bin. It   s easy and you don   t have to find a new paper bag and attach it on. Yes you get a little kick back of dust, but you get that from the old bags when you put something on top of them in the bin. I tend wash out the clear collector every other empty to wash away the dust stuck on the inside.^^Maintenance^^The cleaner has numerous little plastic items that can be removed for maintenance. The filter on the top needs removing and washing every six months and I tend to take apart the extension hose and some detachable bends and wash them out once a year. I do this as dust can get clogged on the bends and in my view looking after something is better than paying for an extended warranty.^^Warranty^^ The DC04 came with a two year warranty, I   ve had no need for this as everything so far has held together. Dyson offered me an extension to the warranty for up to five years, but I didn   t bother with it as I think warranties are a waste of money. If any thing goes wrong it is usually within the first year or two and the manufacturers warranty should cover it. I my view there should be no need to pay for any warranty s, they are not worth the paper they are written on, particularly if the item needing repair is not covered by the small print.^^Conclusion^^For me this has been a good vacuum cleaner, true I have looked after it, but I do the same to any appliance in the house. It has given me nearly five years of trouble free use and I haven   t spent a single penny on paper bags or getting it fixed. I would definitely buy another Dyson, despite what people say about the brand being unreliable and noisy. It does a very good job picking up the mess and it is very easy to maintain. Thanks for readingCad     ', '    Whoaarr     What a cleaner   It sucks like a bitch  Got a bit carried away there but boy oh boy I  8217;ve got a DC04 De Stilj which is a beautiful shade of purple and red with a subtle addition of a bit of yellow.I have never known anything like it. The machine itself is very tactile, it is flexible and responds to the touch well. The directability of the appliance is impressive. For a big machine it exhibits a nimbleness that Nureyev would have been proud of. The addition of a number of tools adds to the flexibility of the product. You  8217;ve got a nozzel to get into those tight little cracks, a firm head to reach those difficult corners and a palm sized soft bristled bushy brush for doing the curtains.As a cleaner, it has been pushed as never losing it  8217;s sucking capacity. This is achieved by a complex series of vortices (currents of air). Add to this, the lifetime guaranteed filters that can reduce all pollutants such as pollen and house dust-might and the reinforcing nature of a revolutionary product you will never go wrong with the DC04. The De Stilj model also comes with a more traditional head attachment found on cylinder cleaners. This is great for doing the stairs   If you have got the money spare   8211; Go invest in a Dyson It s now Jan 2002 - I am still in love with my Dyson  Another year with my trustworthy filly. She has not let me down. The things she can do  Although, I still rate it s performance, I have been a tad irritated by the tools dropping off whenever you move the thing. It is still remarkably quiet though it doesn t even wake the baby and the action - well is still mindblowing       ', '    You can clean your carpet with a dust pan and brush.  Invest in a Dyson, they do cost more than conventional vacuum cleaners, however the performance, style and sheer convenience can justify this extra cost.The main advantage it is wonderful cleaning power, the powerful suction collects dirt that you didn t know you had, especially pet hairs.  A satisfying result is that all the dirt is collected in the see-through drum, this can be quite embarrassing when using a Dyson for the first time   There is a whole collection of accessories fitted to the vacuum allowing easy use of these. The  bag  really fills up fastand is easier to empty using two hands. However there is a tendency for these to fall off during vigorous vacuuming.Overall my Dyson has turned vacuuming from a chore to a pleasure     ', '    I had been used to having little bagged hoovers and they were never brilliant they picked up but i still wasnt satisfied then when i got some money there was a local cash and carry called Tradex doing cheap Dyson s for    129.99.I set my heart on one and begged my husband for one he didnt think they would be as good as i thought they were.Anyway we got it home and put it all together and i kept looking at it without the cylinder on saying is this all this hoover is it cant be that good as it looks like a basic shell without the cylinder.I turned it on and whoosh i was amazed as i was going over my beige rug was it was changing from a murky brown colour to its true colour i was so impressed and even my husband had his mouth hanging open    Teh amount of dirt that was collected as well it goes to show how much actually lurks in your carpets as i had half a cylinder full.This hoover is good for carpeted flooring and it comes with washable filters so they are lifetime lasting so no more buying filters, and also its bagless so no more buying bags.The handle you press a button and pull it up and its your hose and the top flips across on the pipe and you add your attachment to it, so no more pipes hanging off your hoover. The hose also stretches upto 6 times its length so no carry the hoover as you hoover the stairs as it stretches all the way up. Also has on board tools. This hoover even when the container is full continues to suck as well as it would if it was empty.It also picks pet hair up like a dream. The hoover also comes apart so you can get to your filters easy to wash them and the cylinder can be washed as well to keep it clean all very easy to do.This hoover is very easy to push about but can be heavy to lift up the stairs to hoover upstairs, trhis is deffinatly the best hoover investment i have ever made and although they are quite expensive to buy in the first place there is no need to keep buying filters or bags so it saves you money in the long run       ', '    The Dyson works with a recently devised system in a similar way to a tornado, that is a fan spins creating a centripetal force which causes an airflow which, in turn sucks up the dust from the carpet.  Unfortunately the Dyson has so many  easy to (dis)connect  parts that it leaves a similar amount of debris as a tornado.  Suction:Despite having to rebuild the thing several times it is still possible to vacuum a floor in relatively quick time thanks to the amount of suction power the thing packs, and although this is an old model it has enough suction to clean a floor in a few sweeps, any more is just  indulgence.  When I switched from the old vacuum to the Dyson I realised I could spend about half the time doing the same amount of cleaning because more suction equals less sweeps and less sweeps equals less time wasted getting that annoying dusty mark off the floor where some clever person dropped a bag of crisps.Operation:Simple - Plug in, press the big colour switch on the top and move across floor, unfortunately this model doesn t have the handy automatic plug reel-in feature that some have but there are a sweet little bunch of gadgets on the thing.  Includes an extension tube for getting behind the sofa and up the stairs and it can stretch up a whole flight (I ve tried) although stretch it more than about 2 metres and it begins to feel like a tug of war, anyway the extension tube has different heads which are interchangeable for hard floors, rugs or sucking cobwebs off the ceiling.  The vacuum itself can be altered for hard floors or deep piles and has a beater bar in case it is needed.The best innovation in this system (apart from the suction) is that, along with most other modern Dysons it has no bags to change, buy or get annoyed at when they tear and cover your carpet in dust.  With the simple system you just press the eject button on the front, grab the transparent plastic storage cylinder and tip the contents in the bin, then just click the cylinder back in place and carry on cleaning.  You don t need a degree in mechanics to operate this thing but you do need a little patience when it begins to fall apart on you, then again all you need to do is snap it back together and carry on. Reliability:For the 2 years we have had the Dyson we have not needed to take it to the mechanics or even have a bit of a fiddle with when it stops working.Would I recommend it?Yes.Simple answer which is appropriate because simplicity is the name of the game with this thing, simple to operate, simple to store and hardly ever requires any complex mending.  Ideal for a busy individual with little time for cleaning, or indeed a lazy individual with no time for cleaning.     ', '    About 2 years ago my family bought a Dyson vacuum cleaner. Well, it was the  in  thing for household items, wasn t it? So we bought the thing all shiny and... grey, and for the first four months it did the job pretty well. Well done Dyson, although this is where my first problem with the product arises: the stupid filters. The main gimmick that the Dyson held was that it didn t need bags to constantly re-use. However it needs these damn filters that need constantly replacing (albeit not quite as much as bags), and they re about the same price as bags.The months went by, the house got cleaned well by the Dyson and everything was fine and dandy. Fine that is, until the motor burnt out. I was fairly annoyed at this, after all; a new motor shouldn t just burn out, especially not on a space age product such as this. The vacuum was returned where upon I was invoiced    75 for a new motor.   75  Because the Dyson was still well under warranty I ignored this letter, but then I got several more letters from the company, the last of which was rather threatening and wanted legal action to get the    75 off of me. After reading the manual for the DC-04, I found that a thermal cut-out which was meant to save the motor was actually either missing or evaporated from my vacuum  When I politely informed Dyson of this mishap, they discontinued to press for my hard-earned cash. Amazing  I can only assume that if I was a bit more gullible then the company would have tried to go the whole ten yards. How worrying.So, I m left with my repaired Dyson, all nice and shiny, motor repaired although relationship with maker certainly not. Another eight happy months passed without incident, until the mains on-off switch gave up the ghost. Again, one of the last things you would expect to go wrong on a vacuum. I repaired this myself, but ever since the DC-04 hasn t wanted to pick up as well as it did. One more qualm with the Dyson is that the attachments are far from helpful at what they are meant to do- clean the nooks and crannies of your home. Do not buy this thing  Even if it is the coolest vacuum cleaner (if there is such a thing) if not for the fact that mine didn t work, then because the company tries to fleece every one of their customers.      ', '    well, the amount of opinions on this product speaks for itself really, but another one wont hurt. I have had a little henry hoover for a while and decided to put him into retirement. So of I went to Tyrell   Greens  to buy a Dyson. They price matched Letsbuyit.coms price of    235 , which, lets face it, is a lot of money for a vacuum, but it has been worth every penny. On trying it on the rug in the lounge it must have lifted about a kilo of really fine grit out of it, it was embarrassing  I keep mine upstairs and have to say it is rather heavy to lift downstairs and im a 35yo male. I could imagine it being a problem for some people. The extended hose is great for cleaning the stairs and the attchments are good for curtains etc. especially with the  reduce suction  feature. I have used it on the matresses on the beds, it quite frightning really to see how much dust is around. I did recommend this to my mum, she bought one and is delighted with it. She does think its heavy but lives on one level so shouldn t really have to lift it.     ']

If you’re weighing the Dyson DC04 for your cleaning arsenal, here’s a practical rundown based on solid user insights that should help you decide. First off, the DC04 scores well on performance—it’s genuinely effective on both carpets and hard floors, tackling dust, dirt, and even pet hair with ease. The automatic height adjustment is a nice touch, making it simple to switch between floor types without fiddling around. Plus, the suction power holds steady even as the dust container fills up, which is a big plus for consistent cleaning.

Assembly is straightforward thanks to clear, illustrated instructions, so you won’t waste time puzzling over complicated setups. The included hose and attachments are thoughtfully designed to reach tricky spots like stairs and corners, enhancing overall usability. And if you’re concerned about ongoing costs, the bagless design means no extra expenses there, making it a good value for money given its cleaning performance.

On the flip side, some parts—particularly the hose and smaller brushes—can feel a bit brittle and may break if you’re heavy-handed or use them frequently. This durability issue is worth considering if you expect rough daily use. However, Dyson’s customer service is responsive and helpful, which can ease worries about replacement parts or repairs.

In summary, the DC04 is a reliable, no-nonsense vacuum that delivers strong cleaning results and user-friendly features. It’s not perfect—watch out for fragile attachments—but if you prioritize effective cleaning, ease of use, and solid support, it’s a smart investment that balances performance and value without unnecessary bells and whistles.

product_reviews: ['    One of the less satisfactory aspects of writing opinions on   8220;hardware  8221; in general, is the fact that, with the way technology moves on, you  8217;re either writing a long-term report on something that is now an obsolete model, or you are writing about a recent product, which, whilst still a current model, precludes you from commenting on long-term reliability. Either way, you are limited in how useful you can be to potential buyers.The Dyson DC-01 bucks both trends by being something that I have owned for two years, AND is a current model.The DC-01 is the lowest priced upright vacuum cleaner in the Dyson range. No, it doesn  8217;t come in a wide range of funky colours, nor does it have ultra-fine   8220;HEPA  8221; filtration. It  8217;s just a vacuum cleaner, no more, no less.Is it fit for purpose? I  8217;ll say it is  As many of the other writers have mentioned, first use fills up the drum so quickly, that it leads you to wonder whether the previous incumbent, some Electrolux model, was working at all. Oh well, you know what they say -  Nothing Sucks Like Electrolux  (No wonder that ad campaign wasn t used in America )One thing, which is immediately prominent on the Dyson by its absence, is a height adjuster. Dyson doesn  8217;t need one. The front of the cleaner hinges down to follow floor contours, although it isn  8217;t too keen on going back UP the bumps that it just dropped down, and needs a bit of assistance if, for example, you are going from wood-block up to carpet as you move from room to room.Emptying the   8220;dual cyclone  8221; drum is easy enough - it tilts upwards and forwards. Don  8217;t go away thinking that you never need to change anything. There are still two filters, which need regular renewal, roughly quarterly   8211; they  8217;re not expensive though.Failing to change them on time gives the motor more work to do, and in extreme cases causes the heat cut-out to operate   8211; not a serious occurrence but worrying when it first happens, as it takes about 30 minutes to reset itself. When it does this, you may as well pass the time by changing the filters The filters can need more frequent changing if your recent cleaning has been on an industrial scale, like when hoovering, (or should that be  dysonning ) the dust from sanding wood or other decorating activities.Used sensibly, i.e. for cleaning everyday dirt off floors the Dyson is admirable and its ability to adjust to floor-tiles means that most of the detritus on the kitchen floor can be sucked up before resorting to mop and bucket.Niggles? Well, the built-in attachment hose is only barely long enough and kinks quite badly where it leaves the machine if you double the hose back on itself to pick up dirt from the floor, but that  8217;s about it really.Well done, Mr. Dyson, you do make exceedingly good cleaners.I bought mine from John Lewis at Brent Cross for    200 which qualified me for two year s guarantee. ', '    Ten years on, and it s still recognised as a design classic  Yes - 1993 was the year James  Dyson released the world s first popular bagless vacuum cleaner - the original cost was around    200.Which is funny in an ironic sort of way, because in spite of the claims it wasn t revolutionary, nor was it the first Industrial plants had used the  double cyclone  principle for settling dust and solids out of a rotating column of gas or fluid for years, (so *not* revolutionary) nor was it the first implementation in a domestic context (Dyson s  Cyclon  model 1000 was introduced in 1983)Since then, Dyson has bought out a couple of new models every few years - they currently market three upright (the DC03, 04 and DC04) and three  drag along  models (DC05, 08 and 11  telescope )So then - with all this choice, why might you stick with an original DC01?To start with, they work every bit as well now, as they always did Yes they have the annoying habit of having the exhaust airflow pointing forwards, so if you are trying to suck up something light, like dust or feathers, you have to draw the cleaner backwards over the floor instead of pushing it forwards, otherwise you end up in a blizzard My solution to this is to tape a piece of card to the front of the cleaner which forces the airflow upwards, much to the amusement of my children, and ridicule of my wife, but that s a small price to pay.Part of the reason for their longevity is the cleaners are practically indestructible, there s only three moving parts; the motor, the belt and the brush assembly.If your motor burns out, there isn t a lot you can do, you require special tools to get inside the housing, and the cost of a replacement would make this uneconomical, anything else, however, is pretty easily sorted.The nearest I came to killing my DC01 was when I tried to clean up some plaster dust, after about five minutes, the motor cut out (I thought I d goosed it) but in fact the thermal cut-out had simply tripped.After half an hour I replaced the filters, and emptied the bin, and it worked fine. If the filters *do* get blocked, the motor will overheat and it will shut down - I learned my lesson.One respondent has suggested that this is the least reliable of all the Dysons, all I can say is from limited personal experience, beyond the motor overheating once, I ve never had any serious problems. Filtration was another issue which was mentioned, the later models used rather more sophisticated ways of keeping dust out the gubbins, and it s fair to say, the originally supplied disposable filters were a pain. Dyson now sells reusable ones online.We ve used the same set of reusable filters for about four years now (pop them in the washing machine, and place them on a radiator overnight)Spare parts are still valuable from the Dyson online shop, I ve used them a coupe of times, and found it to be an absolute paradigm of electronic trading.There was only ever one serious design fault on the DC01 - the  wand  (which forms the handle, and can be used for attaching accessories) has a cylindrical hole at one end to accept tools, on two occasions, a plastic lug inside this hole has broken, and in spite of trying to glue the broken part in, it never stuck for very long. A replacement is    25.Even if you do get fed up with your DC01, it still has value.In reasonable condition, you could expect to get    40 on ebay for one, more if it is refurbished.Given the choice between an all-new singing and dancing cleaner with a bag, or a second hand DC01 (and keeping a few  beer vouchers ),  I d take Dyson every time Even if it doesn t work, stripped down, you could expect a tenner for the wand, and about the same for the hose. The wheels fetch about a pound, you get the idea.A friend of mine was getting rid of theirs, left it beside the wheelie bin, and it was gone within 20 minutes, no, on this occasion, it wasn t me  (I have a reputation round these parts for pulling things out of skips and selling them on Ebay)The message is clear; keep the filters clean, don t allow fluff to build up in the internal ducts, and keep the brush assembly free of matted hair, with a little care you should keep your DC01 working for ages.     ', '    Well this review is a bit of a two sided coin really. I have 2 sons one is coming up 9 and the other is just 1. Obviously at Christmas my eldest son is a lot more expensive than my youngest. (Even though I ve only had it for a week).I ve never known a vacuum cleaner so effective at picking up pet hair, and the hose that reaches right to the top of the stairs is an absolute godsend.  The hose is built in and retracts very neatly.  The tools are all extremely handy, and I like the way that they can all be stored on the machine, along with the hose, so there s no more looking for tools when you need them, they re always right at hand.The machine is extremely easy to use, and very light and manoeuvrable. ', '    We had a Sanyo Hoover which was about two to three years old, and we had immense trouble in trying to find the bags to fit the Hoover.  The only shop that sold them locally closed, and when we ordered the bags via another shop they were far too expensive to continue ordering, it would have worked out cheaper in the long run to invest in a new Hoover     which is what we did.Having heard good reports form friends we soon decided on a Dyson, and after looking online we chose the DC07i model.The model is an upright Hoover and coloured yellow and purple, and cost about    200.When the Hoover arrived we struggled to take it out of its box, but eventually managed. I picked up the paperwork that came with it, there was a warranty form, instruction manual and a few    useless    bits of info on small pieces of paper.First I had to assemble the Hoover and this is where I began to curse, I didn   t feel the instructions were particularly well written and although they were accompanied by some illustrations I still find it quite difficult to follow. Now whether this was because it was the end of a rather long day or simply that I am not the brightest button on the shirt     I   m not sure. Assembling the Hoover involves taking the pipe and inserting the tube into the pipe and then placing in the correct slots, clipping other catches together. Eventually I managed to complete the task and the Hoover was up and running.I decided that I would be the first to have a go on our new Hoover and promptly hoovered our small hallway, which is roughly 20 foot long by 2 and half foot wide. I was totally amazed by what the Hoover picked up, the results were stunningly visible within the clear Perspex case that    was    the Hoover bag. What shocked me most was that the hallways had recently been hoovered with our old Hoover and there was me thinking our house was at least fairly cleanHoovering stair cases is far easier, a hose that is attached to the handle of the machine is simply lifted out and the hose is long enough to do the entire stair case. No more lugging the heavy hoover upstairs with you while trying to clean them. The tools are easily attached to the hoover to ensure easy access when needed, although there are just two on this model: a brush and nozzle.The hoover has obvious ends that flip the dirt into the track of the hoover which in turn means edge to edge hovering is easier.Emptying the    dirt box    is as easy as pie   This manoeuvre involves the following moves     release    dirt box    by clicking button, press button under handle to release dirt into bin. However the dirt release button is tucked away in an easy to    misuse    place so beware you press it at the correct time over the empty bin and not a minute before. It is advised that you should empty the    dirt box    when it reaches the marked line, though we currently empty it after every use as it does tend to get around half full every time (well the two or three times we have used it anyway).So are there any draw backs? Just a few; apart from the one mentioned already the catches on the hoover don   t seem as sturdy as they perhaps should be, which does make me wonder about their longevity? The hoover has a    pushing    handle and a    lifting    handle, and you shouldn   t pick the hoover up with the    pushing handle   . Taking the hose out to clean the stairs, although fairly easy can be a little awkward due to the nature of the manoeuvre, though it has to be said it   s really not a major hurdle. Apart from that at present I can safely say no other problems have come to light.~~Overall~~The first and most prominent  thing we noticed was the dirt collection, we keep our house as clean as we can and it gets hovered regularly, but with the Dyson it shocked us as to how much    extra dirt    it collect. The suction is the most powerful I have ever seen, and the result of hovering is quite evident. Despite a few problems along the way, we are thoroughly happy with our new purchase. Emptying the dirt box is so easy and much easier than our old hoover, and simply requires a click.The colour of the Hoover is attractive enough, and although it is quite heavy in weight the suction and fact you have a hose long enough to do the full length of the stairs is an added bonus.Highly recommendedThanks for reading - Dave     ', '    I have two adorable cats that I love to bits, but I do wish they wouldn  8217;t be quite so generous  They love to leave me little gifts strewn all over the house, dead birds and feathers, clumps of their own fluff/fur which glues itself to carpets and furniture and have even been known to bring me the odd squashed moth or butterfly or two for good measure.I also have a husband, this one doesn  8217;t bring me pressies as such (sob ), but he does like to leave as much mess as it is possible to create. Biscuit crumbs, crisps, dust and general clutter and I generally find myself clearing up after him non-stop. The joys of being a cat and man owner After hearing me moan and groan just once too often for his liking, hubby decided to reward my somewhat unenthusiastic cleaning efforts with a thoughtful gift. No, not chocolates or flowers, but a new vacuum cleaner  But to be honest I was overjoyed because this particular vacuum cleaner is by far the best and most efficient I have ever tried. The Dyson DC01 is an upright cleaner, and its first big advantage is that it needs no bag thus saving you a fortune in replacements. Instead, the dust, crumbs and general household yuk are sucked into a large cylinder, which can then be emptied at your leisure. Or in my case, about three times a day  The machine has a very powerful suck (ahem) and it can often be very disconcerting to find that one quick hoover over the smallest carpet can generate enough fluff in that cylinder to create three more cats  It is by far the most powerful vacuum cleaner I have used, and removes even the most stubborn of cat fur and fluff from carpets and furnishings.The Dyson comes with a dual cyclone action, which you can actually watch whizzing around as you happily push it back and forth. Be prepared to be horrified at how quickly the thing fills up with dust and dirt, but emptying the container and cleaning it is simplicity itself. You just release the catch and the thing slides towards you ready for emptying. In fact, the machine is very easy to maintain and keep clean and everything slots together simply.The long hose that you attach various brushes to for stair cleaning and so on is actually an integral part of the hoover. It just needs to be unclipped and pulled out when needed. You don  8217;t have to worry about attaching ends to anything as it  8217;s all done for you It also comes complete with lots of attachments to allow you to vacuum corners, stairs and so on more easily. These all sit neatly on the back of the machine so are very convenient, no more trekking backwards and forwards to the understairs cupboard to find the right attachment  Although you do no longer have to buy replacement bags, you will need to purchase replacement filters for the machine quite regularly. There are two different types of filter. The first is an anti bacterial filter that kills nasty bacteria and demons thus making it an excellent choice for those who are prone to asthma and allergies. This should be changed every three months or so unless you live in my house, in which case every six weeks seems more appropriate  In addition, a Hepa filter is provided which needs to be changed once a year and this keeps the inner workings of the machine free from dust and so on which could prevent the machine from working properly if not changed regularly.  One thing I have found though, is that if you so much as catch a tassel on a rug, or try to pick up a length of cotton, you can wave goodbye to the belt as it practically melts  8230;  8230;  8230;you can smell that awful burning rubber straight away and know you have a problem. Extra belts (and filters) can be bought from many DIY and hardware type shops but the belts are fairly expensive. I seem to be replacing mine every five minutes  Appearance wise, I guess you could say it  8217;s quite attractive. It looks very hi-tech with it  8217;s yellow and grey trims (no other choice available with this model ) and is a good size without being too heavy that pushing it around is difficult. It can also cope with any type of floor, be it carpeted or tiled, as the Dyson has an automatic height adjustment setting. We bought our Dyson about 20 months ago, at a cost of    199 but I believe the price has come down a bit since later models have been introduced. Expect to pay somewhere around    150 to    180.Overall, it  8217;s the best I have personally tried, its suction power is immense and it can cope with just about any level of dirt and dust you care to throw at it. Seeing all your household dirt whizzing around the clear cylinder can be a little disturbing but at least you know it  8217;s doing the job and can see at a glance when it needs to be emptied. It  8217;s a wonderful cleaner and I wouldn  8217;t be without it       ', '    James Dyson, the inventor of the bagless vacuum cleaner. He not only deserves recognition for his achievements but also for his incredible perseverance.  It was through his own disappointment with his current cleaner that he embarked upon the long and arduous task of inventing a cleaner that provided 100  suction.~~~~ THE MAN HIMSELF ~~~~ Well before the invention of the first Dyson Vacuum (DC01) James Dyson had a talent for creating new and innovative products. While he was studying at The Royal College Of Art in 1970 he invented the    Sea Truck    it has sales to date of over  500 million. Most of us will not have heard of this but I am familiar with the award winning    Ballbarrow    which can apparently go where no other barrow has gone before  It is a red/orange colour with a large ball where the wheel of a Barrow normally is. Now I   m not a regular wheelbarrow user but I know they can be difficult to handle and tip over, the ball at the front eliminates that. It was in 1978 while he was in the Ballbarrow spray-finishing room that he noticed that the air filter was constantly clogging up with powder particles, just like the bags do in vacuum cleaners.As a result of this he designed and built an industrial cyclone tower which removed the powder particles by exerting centrifugal forces at more than 100,000 times more than those of gravity (information from the Dyson website)The question was, could the same principle work in a vacuum cleaner? 5 years and 5127 prototypes later the worlds first bagless vacuum cleaner from Dyson arrived.~~~~ THE BIRTH OF THE DC01 ~~~~The first bagless cleaner was launched in 1991 in Japan and was seen as a status symbol. It was named    G-Force    and retailed for around  2000, so was out of most peoples reach. Using the income from the Japanese licence    James Dyson    decided to manufacture a model under his own name in Britain. This was the DC01 and it was released in 1993 as the first in a range of cleaners to give constant suction.~~~~ HOW IT ACHIEVES CONSTANT SUCTION ~~~~The bag was replaced by two cyclone chambers, which cannot clog with dust. The traditional bag clogs with dirt and as it acts like a filter, it   s suction power reduces when it becomes clogged. Even other bagless cleaners that use filters lose suction to around 70 . With Dyson the dust is kept away from the filters and thus the suction remains. The outer cyclone spins out the larger particles and the inner one removes the minute health-threatening ones so as well as keeping suction it can help with allergies.  The newer models now have 8 cyclones making them very efficient indeed.~~~~ THE MACHINE ~~~~My main reason for choosing my DC01 was the bag free feature and the fact that it claimed to pick up more dirt and dust and thus be better for asthma/allergy sufferers. I liked its design and the facility to use a wand for cleaning stairs and it appeared to have plenty of attachments for upholstery etc. There are three versions of the DC01, a cylinder vac and a yellow and blue upright; I am going to focus my op on the standard upright yellow model. The Dyson is constructed of sturdy plastic and is primarily grey with some yellow features. It has cord storage at the back of the machine but you have to manually wind this up when not in use. Although the cleaner does not have a bag it does have two s-level submicro filters, these are supposed to be very efficient at collecting dust particles. One is placed underneath the clear plastic drum (where all the dirt is collected) and one is encased in a filter holder down the side of the machine. They need to be replaced after 3 months, as it will affect the performance if you don   t. It is very easy to do and they are very accessible. You can order them from the website at a cost of    8.00 for 8 filters or from most major retailers. You can buy none Dyson products but of course they don   t recommend it. I have used cheaper filters from time to time and they still do the job. One of things I like about the Dyson is that all the attachments fit snugly on to the vacuum and it is a simple process to use them. At the bottom of the vac you will see two storage posts on each side of the drum. Here you will find the necessary attachments stored. There will be a tool adapter, a long crevice tool, an upholstery brush and one for removing pet hairs etc. When you wish to use one of these it couldn   t be simpler. You remove the wand from the back of the machine by lightly depressing a large yellow button that is flush with the handle and located at the front. All the attachments fit easily on to the end of the wand. The wand is long enough to reach the top of most staircases and this saves having to carrying the vac up and down and trying to balance it on the steps.It has a self-levelling cleaner head so if you move from one room to another with a different height in flooring it will adjust automatically.  It has the traditional roller brush and a belt so you need to be careful that you don   t run over the cord when vacuuming. If there are any loose carpet threads or fringes on rugs make sure they are either removed or you clean the area with the wand. If you accidentally run over anything like this there is a good chance that the belt will snap as the fibres wrap around the brushes. The belt is fairly easy to replace but you have to get down on your hands and knees, undo some screws and it can be a mucky job. I have found putting back together a bit tricky on the odd occasion as I   m trying to hold the belt in place and click the brush back in. ~~~~ CLEANING ~~~~In addition to replacing the filters you will need to clean the drum and the shroud. The drum is easily removed and you can empty the contents in to a bin. You don   t need to wash it every time and it tells you not to use strong detergents. You must ensure that the drum is thoroughly dry before replacing it. The drum as I call it is referred to as the bin in the instruction manual but I prefer to call it a drum so as not to confuse matters  If I tell you to check the bin, you might wonder what I   m asking you to do, lolThe shroud is a long yellow tube that is like an upside down triangle covered with holes and you can see it clearly inside the drum. This needs to be cleaned from time to time as it gets clogged up with dust. I usually use the brush attachment and dust it off in to the drum. When you do this either wear a facemask (not from Lush) or ask someone else to do it if you have asthma/allergies. You are kind of defeating the object if you go wafting a load of dust under your nose and it can really get on your chest. I often leave this job for my husband. Periodic checks should be made of the soleplate to remove any blockages. The same applies to the flaps that are at the back of the vacuum. When my Dyson wasn   t working properly it was due to a blockage in one of the flaps. A second hand Dyson that I bought for use upstairs was depositing debris all over my carpet after I had vacuumed. This was again due to the soleplate and flaps being blocked and it looked as if the machine had never been cleaned at all. Once the blockages were cleared and the filters replaced it was as good as new.Occasionally the wand may need clearing, you should look down the wand to check for daylight (don   t do this at night  lol) and clean with a stiff wire if necessary. The brush bar will need threads removing regularly as if left unattended it could damage the vac. You simply need to cut them with scissors but be careful as they can be wrapped around pretty tightly. ~~~~ PERFORMANCE AND HANDLING ~~~~I have been very impressed with the reliability and performance of my DC01.
