I had vacuumed in the morning and then we went to Macro to buy the DC01 after my mother-in-law said they were on a special deal.  When I came back and assembled the vacuum (which was a piece of cake - even for me ) I decided to quickly whip it around the living room as a test run.I could not believe how much extra the Dyson picked up.  I didn t know there was that much hair could come from one dog - surely he should be bald with all that hair missing..   I went round the entire house and I filled the  dust-collector-container  twice over.The container is simple to empty - just press a catch down and pull the container out.  Pour into the bin (outside   ) and then just push the container back into place - simple stuff.Everyone knows that the  bagless  system should save you money since you are not forking out for bags every month, but you don t save that much since you have to buy the filter pads every two-or-three months anyway.  At least just about every electrical shop and/or superstore sells the filter pads so you can shop around for a good price.  I think we get two filter pads (all the filters on the Dyson are the same size) for about three quid - I ll post a comment later if my wife tells me this is wrong.The DC01 is extremely easy to push around and it s  pick-up-ability  is second to none.  The extendy bit which allows you to get to places where the sun doesn t shine is verrryyyy long (designed to reach the top of a normal flight of stairs) - and all the extras (even that brush one - what s that one for??) come attached to the vacuum cleaner so you don t have to carry them around.  The handle and head even go 180 degrees (flat) so you can push the vacuum right under the bed.. The only problem we have with the DC01 is that my wife is small and the vacuum cleaner is a little too heavy to pick up and carry up the stairs.This product comes with a very high rating from me - just vacuum your living room and then borrow someones Dyson and vacuum it again, you ll see what I mean.  If you ve got a pet that sheds hair like our dog does then the Dyson is a very cleverly disguised gift from God..      ', '    My DC01 Upright is 7 years old and it still works as well as day one. Yes I ve changed numerous bits, the hose twice, a new bumper and a hose part, but it is wonderful. I love cleaning, I especially love hoovering bizarely. It s calming and therapeutic. But it s not any fun when it s a struggle. Every hoover I ve known before my Dyson was heavy, dusty and so time consuming. With the Dyson however it is light on the move, however very heavy off, not for the weak, although the cylinder is exceptionally light. One more thing on cylinders and uprights is that cylinders are better with hard floors, still great on carpets, but perfect for hard floors, especially the new ones(tried lots) and the uprights are amazing one carpets, not so practical with floors. The cylinder is also better with stairs.They pick up everything, I remember the first 2 weeks with it, it collected so much that I felt amazed that all of it was in the carpets. It soon tapered off, but I couldn t believe what it picked up and how it made the fibres of the carpet stand up.Recently my friend brought the newest cylinder in mint green, I thought that after 7 years that mine would have lost some of its power, so I was really excited to get hold of hers for an afternoon (Man how sad am I) again I was amazed, it did not work any better picking up wise anyway than mine, although I was impressed with how well it did the stairs. If anything the hose annoyed me, I have a small house and it kept getting tangled, but I knew I would have got used to it and found my own way.A big, big, big plus, with a dyson you get a 2 year warrenty, in that time you can send your dyson FOR FREE to be serviced. They will pick it up, clean it, service it and make it all shiney again and delievered home in 3days. (yes how did I manage for 3 days...it was murder) The customer care is amazing and then you can get a really cheap extended warranty and carry on getting it serviced.So I guess to summerize I would say that the newer ones are smarter, they have gagdets and are very kool. Mine is grey and yellow not so kool. But it works just as well and I know the prices of the DC03,4   5 are really cheap, sometimes around    150 and they do the job as well as the really expensive ones.Well dya think I like it? Make the next vacuum a Dyson, you won t regret it  :-)I have recieved some post feedback on this review, on tool and cleaning of it, in appreciation of this I would add that there are 3 tool, they are okay, to do a carpetted stairs isn t so easr as the head provided to go with the extended hose isn t very good at picking up as the cylinder hoover is, there is also a little brush that I hardely ever use and a pointy edge tool for skirtings and so on.Cleaning is very easy, empty the bucket and its done although it does need a good clean ever 3 months when I change the filters, although the newer ones do not require replacement filters.I hope that is clearer, thankyou for all feedback recieved.     ', '    unfairly labelled as this years american pie,  this is a comedy of far more substance and humour. whereas american pie had slushy love undertones throughout road trip plays it straight for laughs from start to finish.A guy tapes himself having sex with a horny blonde babe (excuse the sexism ladies) and then the tape is accidentally sent to his girlfriend on the other side of america, thus ensues the road trip to try and retrieve the tape before his girlfriend gets to see it, some of the funniest moments include a pensioner watching mtv babes on then getting high, and watch for the dog scene, Im still laughing three days later, if you have ever somked anything illegal you will love this film, and even if you havent, its still one to watch     ']
filtered_hist_vote_written: ['    I bought a Dyson nearly five years ago because my previous vaccuum cleaner,(an electrolux)spent more time being repaired than it did working.I might add that the electrolux was my second vaccuum cleaner in five years. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re juggling pet hair, dust bunnies, and the occasional mystery crumb (because who knows where those come from?), the Dyson DC01 might just be your new best friend. This vacuum packs a punch with its dual cyclone technology, which means it doesn’t just suck—it *really* sucks, maintaining strong suction to tackle carpets, upholstery, and even those sneaky corners where pet fur loves to hide. As a fellow pet parent, I appreciate how efficiently it handles fur without losing steam halfway through the job.

One of the standout features is the antibacterial and HEPA filters, making it a solid pick if allergies or asthma are part of your household drama. Just a heads-up: these filters need some TLC—antibacterial ones every three months and HEPA annually—to keep performance top-notch. Think of it as a little spa day for your vacuum, ensuring it keeps your air cleaner and your sneezes at bay.

Maintenance is refreshingly straightforward. The transparent dust container lets you eyeball when it’s time to empty, so no guessing games or surprise messes. Plus, the bagless design saves you from hunting down replacement bags and keeps costs down—a win for your wallet and your sanity. Clearing blockages and swapping attachments is a breeze, which is great because who wants to wrestle with their vacuum after a long day?

Speaking of attachments, the DC01 comes with handy tools for stairs, curtains, and upholstery, making it versatile enough for every nook and cranny. It’s also relatively lightweight and adjusts its height automatically depending on your floor type, so you’re not stuck fiddling with settings mid-clean.

On the customer service front, Dyson scores high marks for prompt and effective support—because even the best machines need a little TLC now and then.

In short, the Dyson DC01 is a practical, powerful, and pet-friendly vacuum that balances performance with ease of use. Just keep up with those filter changes, and you’ll have a trusty cleaning sidekick for years to come.

product_reviews: ['    I m quite lazy when it comes to cooking, a consequence of being almost literally banned from the kitchen for over 20 years whenever my dad cooked dinner, and then three years at university, when, well I didn t have the time or inclination to eat well (though I did often manage to cook vegetables unlike most typical students )So when I finally flew the family nest a couple of years after finishing university, living out on my own and with a full time job, well I found I d become quite dependent on my dad s healthy cooking  If I attempted to eat fast food or anything pre-prepared more than a day or two at a time for instance, I d quickly become lethargic and ill.So what to do? I couldn t be bothered to learn how to cook - too time consuming, risky and often inevitably involved too much washing up - and I definitely couldn t afford to hire a cook. However, I remembered that my dad used to steam most of our dinners, using an extraordinarily large metal bowl part filled with water, with a separator thing keeping a dish of meat and vegetables above the water while it boiled. Well I wasn t about to buy the same thing - I m too likely to accidentally knock the whole bowl with boiling water over, or scalding myself while trying to lift food out. But I thought of another possibility... an electric steamer.Turning to my trusty Argos catalogue, I picked out the cheapest steamer I could find from a brand I trusted: Tefal s Steamer Aqua Timer for    24.50.---- Physical details ----The steamer consists of a white base to which a non-detachable electrical cord and plug is attached. This is where you fill up water, and there are both internal and external water level indicators so you can see how much time the water you put in will provide (up to 60 mins), or how much time is left. There is also an indicator on the front to show when the steamer is switched on. However, there isn t an on/off button on the base, you need to switch it on at the electrical mains. A heating element inside the base heats up the water when the appliance is fully assembled.Next a turbo ring is put in, and then a juice collector to collect, well, juice from the vegetables and meat you cook and stop them from getting into the base.On top of these, you can place one or two transparent 3 litre oval steam bowls. The bowls measure about 23 x 19.5 x 9.3 cm high, and contain holes in the bottom to allow steam through. They also contain  integrated egg holders , indented bumps downward that allow you to place eggs upright for steaming.You can also use a 1.1 litre rice bowl, which is simply placed inside one of the steam bowls. On top of all this, there is a lid with three ventilation holes. The lid can also be used upside down to carry a steam bowl to another table without having water drip everywhere.----What can it cook? ----As a general rule, anything that has been grown, freshly picked and boilable can be steamed. For instance it ll cook most vegetables like fresh broccoli, potatoes, and carrots, but you wouldn t use it for onions (not normally boiled), pasta (not grown), baked beans (not fresh and has tomatoey sauce that will go funny) or tinned sweetcorn (also not fresh and usually has salted water that will mess up steamer ). It ll also cook vegetables that may have been frozen, like peas, cauliflower and French beans, useful if you find a shortage of decent fresh vegetables in your local supermarket or grocers.It can cook white meats such as salmon steaks and chicken fillets/breasts... and while it doesn t suggest it in the instruction booklet, I also use it to steam pork shoulder steaks or spare rib steaks, though you might find this leaves the meat tasting too bland compared with grilling or oven baking.Apart from keeping its nutrients and vitamins, I find the best reason for using a steamer is that unlike boiling, the food will retain their flavour even if you accidentally steam them into a soggy mess (as I occasionally do and definitely do while boiling ) Quite important for me as I rarely use sauces, and will usually just plonk a bit of margarine on top of my vegetables when they re ready. But also important if you re forced to eat a bland diet... as I realised when I risked feeding a friend who d suffered through a fairly long period of diarrhoea and stomach infections and was fed up with boiling food all the time as they ended up tasteless. You wouldn t believe how grateful she was to receive steamed chicken fillets, broccoli, carrots and potatoes, and promptly ate it all without any sauce, salt, pepper, herbs or complaints Another thing is that I m able to cook whole meals using the steamer without any additional pots or pans. For instance, I often steam a pork shoulder steak with maybe potatoes and broccoli, using one steam bowl, and the meal I cooked for my friend and myself used just one steam bowl too. I ve also used it for a whole rainbow trout with similar vegetables. This saves on a lot of washing up, as well as space, and means I don t have to watch over the cooker constantly to make sure it s not on fire And of course it s pretty quick... oven cooking chicken fillets could take 25-30 mins, but steaming just takes 20 mins, and you don t have to wait for the steamer to  preheat  as you do an oven, as steam appears within 15 mins of switching on. In general, steaming a whole meal for one or two people doesn t generally take longer than 25 mins, at which point the vegetables have become a bit tenderer than I d normally have them anyway. And another thing, when switched on, you don t have to watch over the steamer at all as you do with boiling. You can just wander off and wait until it s finished Vegetables can be placed directly into the steam bowls, but if you re cooking meats, I d recommend placing them on a saucer to make sure the juices don t block the holes in the bottom of the bowls. When I first attempted to cook pork shoulder steak in this, I found the meat juice would solidify, and block some of the holes, while others would successfully end up in the juice tray and cook there. Not pleasant to wash It s also not a good idea to place anything like salt, sugar, dried herbs, or olive oil in the steamer as they can mess up the steamer. However it should be safe to scatter lemon slices, spring onions etc over the food while cooking.---- Inconveniences ----One thing steaming doesn t work well for is rice. I like my rice fat, fluffy and dryish, however I find steaming rice leaves it looking pathetically small and soggy, and it takes longer to steam than to boil  Also, the rice bowl takes up all the useable space in one of the steam bowls, meaning that you can t squeeze in other food around the container as I like to do. So although steaming rice would be easier, well I m afraid I prefer the old fashioned method If you like to time your food to cook at different stages so that they re all perfectly cooked at the end, this is pretty hard to tackle. Generally you will have to steam all your foods together and just cope with a few overcooked foods. The only way around this is to switch steamer off at the mains after something has been cooking a while, lifting the lid and dumping more food in, putting lid back then switching steamer on again. I usually take the rather unsafe method of trying to lift lid off carefully while steamer is still on to drop more vegetables in, and often end up being scalded by the steam This particular model doesn t seem to switch off automatically. Well actually the instruction booklet seems to think it does when it runs out of water, but I find the steamer usually makes a low but long, loud burring sound about 5 mins before the end of cooking. The sound will then stop briefly, but will resume again within a minute. It s the most annoying sound possible, and I often don t have the patience to wait for the water to run out completely before it can  automatically  stop. Still, at least the reminder is there to switch it off.Which brings us to another point, if you suddenly find you haven t placed enough water, you d have to switch the whole steamer off at the mains, then move steam bowls and juice collector off the base before you can add more water, argh  So make sure you have enough water first ---- Cleaning ----The steam bowls, rice bowl, lid and juice collector are all made of plastic, and easy to wash. However, it s recommended that the base be descaled every 7-10 times it s been used. Oops I ve used it nearly a year now and still haven t descaled it, but it still does its job well Thankfully you don t need to buy a separate descaling product, you just need white wine vinegar... which I ve still had to buy separately as I don t normally use it  Fill the base to the 50 min level, switch base on until liquid disappears, then rinse.---- Conclusion ----There are obviously better models with more functions available on the market, (ie ones where water can be topped up, timer can be delayed etc,) but as a basic steamer it does its job more than well enough. Would I recommend it to friends? Oh definitely  It s made life far easier  After washing and chopping up vegetables, then dumping them along with meat into the steamer, I can simply relax until everything is cooked. And I ve been doing that for most of my evening meals for nearly a year now.I d even suggest it would make a better investment for students than a sandwich toaster or microwave... although they probably wouldn t really want to eat that healthily      ', '    Whilst visiting the outlet centre in Swindon over last weekend - I saw the Tefal Aqua Steamer for sale at    19 which is substantially less than the Argos price at Christmas when I bought one for my son  So I bought it direct from Tefal with a one year warranty.When I got home I unpacked it,washed it out and started to cook chicken and vegetables topped with a savoury white sauce. Except it wasn t like cooking - there was no need to stand over it. I set the time added the food and stood around for a while wondering what to do next   Got it  While the food was steaming I went for a nice steamy bath too and when I went back to the kitchen the food was cooked and ready to serve. What an excellent buy with time for me too      ', '    My mother-in-law bought the Tefal Steam Cuisine 1000 Turbo Diffusion for herself, but felt it wasn  8217;t worth using for just one person (her husband doesn  8217;t eat vegetables ) so she kindly gave it to me :-)I had previously thought about getting myself one, but always assumed that they were expensive, I was wrong, this one only cost    32.95 from Argos.  I also thought you could only cook vegetables in them. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re looking for a versatile, health-focused kitchen gadget, the Tefal steamer is worth considering. One standout feature is its flexibility: by simply removing one of the grids, you can steam a whole chicken, which is a neat trick for larger meals. Beyond poultry, it handles a wide range of foods—from vegetables and fish to sausages, rice, pasta, couscous, and even fruit and sauces. I particularly appreciate that sauces can be prepared simultaneously in the rice bowl while other ingredients steam, making meal prep more efficient.

Steaming itself is a big plus here, as it preserves nutrients and flavors far better than boiling or frying. The rice steaming function is especially foolproof, which is great if you want consistent results without fuss. The three-layer design, complete with removable inserts and a divider, lets you cook two portions or different foods at once, saving time and energy.

From a usability standpoint, the Tefal steamer scores high marks. The clock and settings buttons are clear and intuitive, and the delayed cooking program is a practical feature for prepping meals ahead. Safety is also well thought out, with a water low warning beep and an auto cut-off that switches to keep-warm mode once cooking finishes. Plus, the see-through tiers let you check progress without lifting lids and losing steam.

It’s compact enough to fit comfortably in most kitchens and surprisingly easy to assemble and clean—even without instructions. Minimal lingering smells after use are a nice bonus. On the downside, while the steamer is recommended for most users, the pricier Tefal models might not offer enough extra benefits to justify the cost unless you have very specific needs.

Overall, this steamer strikes a solid balance between functionality, health benefits, and convenience—making it a practical addition for anyone serious about nutritious, hassle-free cooking.

I say little, but it s not really, it s a huge puddle being such a huge dog   Of course I would do my best to clear it all up using kitchen rolls and Dettox etc. but I never felt I was doing all I could to get rid of it.  After a while I decided that I needed something more to help, so I started looking at carpet cleaners.  I d had one years before, but it was a cylinder carpet cleaner and it was such hard work using the tools to clean the carpet.  I noticed the Bissell Pro Heat Cleaner in one of my catalogues first of all.  It wasn t cheap at    240.00.  I could have bought it cheaper through another outlet, such as QVC, but this suited me better as it was on a Buy Now Pay Later basis and also I would then be able to pay off for it monthly.  I decided to order one to see if it was all it was cracked up to be.  When it came, I spent a while putting it together - well, that is attaching  the handle to the body of the machine - then reading through the instruction leaflet thoroughly.  It all seemed straight forward, and it was.  I tried it on what I thought was a slightly grubby part of the carpet near the door.  When I emptied the container of dirty water, it was filthy   Now, I am perhaps not the World s most diligent housewife, but I do like to keep the house clean and tidy and I was shocked at how much dirt it had taken up from the carpet.  When you start using the machine, you have to fill up the special conatiner bottle with the Bissell fibre cleaning formula, fill up the other bucket type container with warm water, put them back on the machine, set the right settings, then you re away.  It s really as simple as that.  Because it s an upright cleaner, you literally use it like a vacuum cleaner, going backwards and forwards slowly over the part of the carpet you want to clean.  It washes the carpet with the solution, then sucks up the excess water, leaving the carpet damp, not soaking wet.I can t say just how brillian I think this machine is.  It s definitely one of the best things I have ever bought for the house.     ', '    That   s what you could end up with if you invest in one of these and use it on a regular basis.One of the features I liked best about investing in a brand new property was the fact that I could also buy brand new carpets, where man nor beast had ever walked before.  Previously when buying my houses, I had had to rely on the quality and choice of the previous owner and a good steam clean courtesy of my dad and the local rental outlet whilst I was at work.However, after two years of teenage feet, numerous hidden spills, a few early puppy accidents and mucky paws I had had enough; the entrance to my living room was looking like the local nursery floor when it hadn   t been cleaned for a week.My trusty old Daewoo hoover kept the bits at bay, but nothing could shift the stains and the musty look the carpet had developed around the doorway.  I asked around, no-one I knew had a steam or wet and dry hoover, looked like I was at the mercy of my local Comet store again.Perusal of the store found Dysons in every shape and size, bagless and bagged cleaners, wet and dry VAX machines, where the hell was I supposed to start?Then to the rescue came my maiden in shining armour in the shape of a Comet sales assistant, extolling the virtues of the Bissell machines, assuring me there was nothing better on the market, and that it coped admirably with the Ribena stains of her two under 5   s, with two models in the shop, one priced at    169, the other at    238.99, I bet it did.But the young lady was sooooo convincing, Martin rolling his eyes at the prospect of me investing extortionate sums of money in something that might not work, and me erring towards the pricier machine because it apparently also worked on ceramic and lino floors, I was convinced.It was at this point I realised there was no credit on my Timecard owing to their ridiculous process of frontloading non-existent interest, however, luckily for me, Comet are ditching Timecard from October and moving over to G E Capital, so it was time to open a new account, all this does is give some breathing space of about 6     8 weeks, as at 29.4 APR, not being able to pay by the due date means you really shouldn   t be using it.SO WHAT DID I GET FOR MY MONEY?A beast is the simplest way to put it with three free bottles of cleaner, two for the carpet, one for ceramic floors, and a bottle of Scotchguard protector.It quickly became apparent in the shop that this beast is not light (it actually weighs around 10Kg/22lbs), I opened the box to discover that the top half of it, and all the accessories had to be self assembled.  Knowing Martin   s track record of handling plastic, I decided to give it a go myself, what they don   t warn you of in either the shop or on the box, is that you require a PhD in applied engineering to work it all out, for that price surely it should be    plug and go   ?Basically, the Pro-Heat, Protech cleaner is a    deep    floor cleaner, with a pipe attachment that offers a variety of different attachments including a number of different shaped brushes, a turbo brush and a skirting board style cleaning attachment that allow you to work on any stubborn stains before you use the actual floor cleaner.There is a computer scanner on the front of the machine that offers two interfaces,    Too Fast    and    Best Cleaning   , and very simply relates to how fast you are actually moving the machine across the carpet (this is only relevant to floor cleaning).The machine has the facility to Scotchguard carpets, and a built in heater that keeps the water at a constant 25C whilst plugged in.  If you leave the machine standing for two minutes you will find the area of the carpet underneath it has turned lovely and warm.  You can also use it to clean upholstery, curtains and most non-carpeted floors with the exception of wood     although the book does recommend that you check your manufacturer details for synthetics to ensure they are not dry clean only.  In addition, there are large typewritten warnings in the handbook advising that Berger carpets should not be deep cleaned.SO HOW DOES IT WORK?Once you have pieced the machine together, you will discover it has what is called a    tank in tank   .  Clean, warm tap water is placed into the inner bag and then replaced in the machine.  The cleaning fluid is placed into a small dispenser bottle that sits on the other side of the machine (this bottle can and does leak, so be very careful about making sure the lid is on securely, and that when the machine is not being used, that the tank is empty, if leaving the machine for short periods of time, ensure that the fluid can   t leak out on to anything easily damaged or tarnished).  Once you have filled up all the necessary compartments (the machine will not work correctly unless fluid is present in both).  Then, seek out your stains, and scrub them after setting the dials to pre-treat/tools and heavy duty.  There is a spray button on the arm of the hose which will spray out a carefully measured dose of water and carpet cleaner; when not spraying, the hose will adopt a suction action.Once you have worked on the stains, give it a couple of minutes to work, switch the dials over to floor cleaning and normal treatment and hoover your floor.  There is a button on the handle of the machine to again allow you to dispense a combination of water and cleaning fluid, once you stop squirting, the machine will again adopt a suction action, and you should keep moving back and fore over the affected area until there is no fluid being visibly drawn up into the machine through the glass screen on the front.  The dirty water is drawn back into the outer rim of the    tank in tank   , with the expandable inner tank bag reducing in volume and size to accommodate it.The book advises you to perform a final clean after this process, repeating the above procedure, but with the dial set to dispense water on its own, this apparently allows you to take advantage of the machines and the chemicals full cleaning properties.SO DOES IT WORKAs with anything involving chemicals, it is always advisable to perform a    patch    test on an inconspicuous area first to ensure it doesn   t bleach / stain / ruin your carpet beyond repair, so it was firstly tested out on my rugs which were remaining off-cuts from the original carpet that had been bound and supposedly used as carpet protectors, but were actually in better condition than the carpet I was targeting, and bearing in mind that anyone venturing into my living room with shoes on was threatened with severe pain, I didn   t expect them to be too bad..  I followed the process to letter in the booklet provided, and was stunned to discover that the water was, to say the least, gruesome.  In addition, there were piles of warm wet hair accumulating at various places on the rug, it was quite scary.A quick check at 7am in the morning, established that the rugs were dry, still in one piece and looking pretty pucker, I just had time before going to a friends funeral to tackle the stains in the doorway.  You are advised in the book to plan your    escape    route before starting work, however, in this instance the problem was the escape route and therefore I had no option but to walk barefoot across the treated area, even when followed up with a clean water treatment, my feet felt quite sticky, I still had time to spare before getting ready and opted to try out the ceramic cleaner.  This requires an additional piece to be fitted to the base of the cleaner, and this is not a straightforward process.  You should also ensure you are using the correct cleaning fluid, else you will find yourself with a floor resembling the local skating rink.  Despite months of bleach mopping, my tiles came up cleaner than I have ever seen them, and the floor dries just as quickly as a mop and bucket, just in time for Hally to come in with her mucky paws. THE RESULT?When I returned from the funeral, the stains were gone, and the carpet was looking as good as the day it was laid, and is now really nice underfoot     a result.  This particular carpet has quite a deep pile, and it took around 10 hours to dry fully, and also requires a brush over to make it fit in with the rest of the room, but thankfully there was no discolouration.  Once you have finished the process, you will need to remove any muck from the screens and brushes, and also empty the dirty water tank and clean it out to remove any surplus muck that has found its way through the filter system, if you have pets, expect this to be a fair bit, particularly if using the machine for the first time.  ADVANTAGES    If you are prepared to put the work in, it will produce superb results on your carpets    It is cheaper than a Kirby, or at least the ones I have seen demonstrated    It cleans stains AND deep cleans    It cleans ceramic floors and upholstery    The computerised interface tells you when you are hitting optimum cleaning levels    Quite a pleasant, fresh and not too strong smell once cleanedDISADVANTAGES    It is heavy and cumbersome, and definitely not suitable for those with limited mobility or bad hearts    It is very noisy    I found it quite stressful to assemble    At    238.99 it was not the cheapest product on the market (we actually discovered that its real price was    279 and it had been incorrectly marked up, but Comet honoured the price tag)      It does not double up as a standard vacuum cleaner    The cleaning fluid tank can leak    A thick piled carpet can take around 10 hours to dry    Computerised interfaces have a habit of going wrong    You can only use Bissell cleaning fluids,    6.59 for a bottle of fibre cleaner,    5.97 for a bottle of ceramic cleaner (otherwise Bissell advise your warranty will be invalidated - how they know is anyones guess)    It is messy and fiddly to clean upDO I REGRET IT?I must admit I do begrudge paying this amount for a cleaner, and would far rather have spent the money on an XDA, a new TFT screen or some additional software, but needs must, and looking at my lounge carpet now, it is cheaper than replacing it when I know that in two years time I would be in the same boat again     the kitchen rug got    done    this evening, and it is off to Tasha   s room over the weekend, the subject of far too many teenage makeovers and facemasks.     ', '    Bissel Carpet cleanerAfter years of struggling to keep my carpets clean with an unwieldy two piece carpet cleaner I decided it was time for a new one  Imagine if you will my dusky rose pink carpets, only laid 3 years ago, and the incessant tramping of 16 assorted sized paws, 6 regular sized feet plus the visitors we have had over the years, plus the various spills and accidents that occur through everyday life with a 2 year old. All this adds up to a very grubby looking carpet  I used to use the old carpet cleaner at least once a month in the heaviest traffic areas, which used to take up to 2 hours PER ROOM  I thought the carpets were clean  Enter the beast  8230;  8230;  8230;  8230;  8230;  8230;.The Bissel beast as I have affectionately named it, looks very similar to a regular upright vacuum cleaner, with the exception of the two-water/fluid tanks. It is incredibly easy to fill each tank. To fill with cleaning fluid (450ml supplied as a trial size). Remove the fluid cartridge by pulling upwards gently, unscrew the top and pour the required amount into the chamber. Replace the screw top, and replace cartridge in the machine. This is the easiest encounter I have ever had   8211; no mixing or diluting required, just put the neat cleaning fluid into the chamber, no spills no mess.Filling the bucket with water is just as easy   8211; remove the bucket using the built in handle, remove the lid and place bucket under the hot water tap until the desired level is reached. The bucket itself holds 1 gallon of water   8211; not very much really but just enough to do one room. This may not sound like labour saving if you have to fill the bucket in each room, but believe me the combined weight of the machine (10kg) plus the water is VERY HEAVY Once you have loaded water and fluid into the machine, select which option you want the machine to perform either carpet cleaning or the tool option. The tool option is fantastic as you can clean your suite, stairs, and car upholstery and carpets. The hose is the longest I have seen, even on cylinder models   8211; this causes the only drawback the hose tends to flop about when using the machine to clean the carpets. This although a minor problem could be rectified with a better more secure on board clip feature.To utilise the carpet cleaning setting of the machine, select the   8216;type  8217; of clean you require either water only,   8216;normal  8217; or   8216;heavy soiling  8217;. I used the heavy soiling option as I hadn  8217;t cleaned my carpets for a fortnight and thought they could do with a good clean.You first have to vacuum the area to be cleaned, this I did with the almighty Dyson, of which I have already extolled its virtues in a previous op.I manouverd the machine into position   8211; switched on, using the plastic coated power switch and away I went. There is a conveniently placed trigger mechanism on the handle to release the water and cleaning fluid onto the floor. This fluid is then   8216;brushed  8217; into the carpet using the   8216;power brush  8217; situated on the underside of the machine. As I drew back the machine to suck up the water I was horrified.If anyone has used a Dyson for the first time, they will know exactly what I mean. The water that was sucked out of the carpet was that tell tale filthy brown colour  After one   8216;sweep  8217; of the cleaner I could see a BIG difference in the colour of the carpet. I don  8217;t mean a bit of a difference, I mean the carpet looked like new, another sweep brought MORE dirt out of the carpet. A third sweep brought nothing up but clean water   It took me 30 minutes to clean the carpet in a 14ftx14ft room, 90 minutes less that with my old cleaner. The carpet looked so clean proved by no more muck coming out of the carpet  As I said before I used the whole one-gallon tank of water and all the fluid in just one room. This isn  8217;t that excessive, bearing in mind the amount of muck removed. The cleaner has cleaned so deeply it appears to have    8216;refreshed   8217; the pile in the carpet -  8211;making it look brand new, and leaving it smelling really fresh.Emptying the container is just as easy as filling it. Remove the water bucket from the machine, again using the handy handle to avoid spillage. You can see through the opaque plastic what has been removed from your carpet. To remove the foul water, simply tip the bucket and it will come pouring out, over the handy built in lip.  The foul water is sucked back into the same bucket as the clean water, although the two never mix. The clean water is contained within a bladder, which empties with use, the used water is sucked back into the container   8211; replacing the space the clean water leaves. I was amazed at what cam out of my carpets   8211; not just the   8216;mud  8217; but sand, animal hair and so on. I thought the Dyson was removing it all  All in all if you are looking for a new carpet cleaner, I can  8217;t recommend this highly enough. It is easy to use, easy to fill, easy to set up. You will be amazed at the amount of dirt lifted out of your carpets, and the amazingly quick time it takes to do also. The carpets are slightly damp after use, but several passes with the cleaner just using the suction will dry it out in no time. No more getting up at 5 to clean the carpets and keeping the kids and animals out all day whilst it dries  The cleaning fluid provided with the cleaner is Bissell  8217;s own   8211; surprise surprise, this is the recommended cleaning fluid for use. I haven  8217;t tried any other cleaning fluid, but non-foaming fluid for 3 in 1 machines should be ok. Having said that I will continue to use the Bissel fluid   8211; widely available from Argos stores priced at    6.99 for 950mls. The trial size was 450mls, which was a reasonable amount, as I used the whole bottle for the downstairs rooms in my house. The cleaner itself cost me    240 from a catalogue, but I have since seen it in Curry  8217;s for    229. It may seem a lot to pay for something only used every few months, but in my eyes an absolute bargain The machine was a beast in the bedroom, banished stains and marks in the bathroom, drove dirt out in the dining room and lapped it up in the lounge not to mention killing germs in the kitchen      ', '    This carpet cleaner is the last in a very long list of carpet shampooers that I have used, but comes out top every time. I have four kids, each in their own right, messy, accidental spillages are a common occurance in my house. Althought I rate the bissel very highly as a carpet shampooer, it is nt much use when there has been a slight accident. It is a very bulky machine to get out of the cupboard just to suck up a bit of juice. When it comes to cleaning the carpet thoroughly, say once a month, it absolutley lives up to its name. The one downfall with this machine is that its not very easy to clean after use, and if not cleaned out properly and left to dry out thoroughly, it will smell like stagnant water. Compared to other shampooers on the current market, this machine is great value for money. I got mine from bissel direct, it was a refurbished model, but came with the same gaurentee that a brand new model would, only half the price.     ', '    Bissell Little Green Portable Deep Cleaner 17201After just moving into brand new military housing, I was faced with the stress of keeping the house at 100 percent all the time. The first ones in new housing are always the ones who pay the most when they move out. So needless to say I didn   t want to pay. I went out and bought the Bissell portable deep cleaner from our local Army Air Force Exchange. I thought that this little guy would be easy enough for me to move around the house and tough enough to deep clean. So far, it has done everything imagined  I have used my Bissell cleaner on the stairs in my house, which I was amazed at the amount of dirt it had picked up and we had been in this house for little time. It appeared that the construction workers had a field day on the carpet. The next place I used it was on my sofa and loveseat. This furniture has never been cleaned since we first bought it. Now it looks almost brand new again and no longer smells of cigarette smoke. Then as a child with a new toy I began to look for more things to use my Bissell on. So, I went to the car. The Bissell was small enough that it was a breeze to steam clean the carpets and seats in my car. The smell of the Bissell cleaner made my car smell much better then when the factory gave it to me. Now that I am done bragging about this little guy, let me tell you a little bit about the machine itself. First you can buy one of two series, either the 1720, which is the one I have or the 1725 which comes with a built in heater and turbo brush. My basic cleaner comes with a 25 foot power cord that conveniently wraps around the base of the cleaner for storage, a four inch wide cleaning tool and six inch window cleaning tool. The Bissell cleaner is easy to use with a simple on/off switch and detachable parts for easy clean up. The tanks are self explanatory and tell you how much solution should be in the cleaner side and how full the dirty side can be before you should empty it. I fully recommend this product for anyone with stairs or small areas to clean. With its powerful suction and deep cleaning solution, the Bissell Little Green Steam Machine is definitely worth buying. For more information on this excellent product and to find out about Bissells full line check out: www.bissell.com or call 1-800-237-7691.      ', '    I feel it necessary to begin by saying that I can t be accused of having a past where cleanliness has featured top of my list in life s priorities, however enough was enough  With a BIG dog, a cat and frequently not enough time to notice their legacy around flat, I would be caught out on occasions with a whiff of  animal  and a grimy looking floor looking back up at me. Having spent a number of days on my hands and knees.....cleaning that is   Wearing a pair of Marigolds (which incidentally are not available in ANY colour that suits me) and a scrubbing brush, I soon ran, screaming for the nearest shop that sold electric carpet cleaners.Having found a great deal on a Bissell  Power wash  Deluxe with rotating brush (approx    100), I was convinced, bought the thing and without delay, got it to work.First impressions...very easy to fill with separate clean/dirty water tank both in one container. The  self explanatory  cleaner got to work straight away with it s push button feature to apply the water and added Bissell solution, while you then release and  vac  over the patch which sucks up the shampoo stuff, whilst the rotating brush gives those carpet fibres a good ol  seeing to. The Power wash also features a added separate  hose  which is attached to the back and can be used for those stubborn or  got to get rid of that mark  moments, with it s own applicator and brush too I was a bit worried about what happens with pet hairs and other  bits and bobs  that may not have been vacuumed up first (which is advised) but was reassured when I discovered the very effective filter which stops anything that shouldn t get into the machine, getting in to it. This Bissell is also very easy to clean afterwards too, an empty and rinse of the  bucket container  and a wipe with a damp cloth and your done  Bliss   It s worth mentioning that if used correctly, carpets (or hard floors too ) are left very nearly dry and those old whiffs are gone too Downs?? Well, I must admit, along with the dog and cat, I was a bit taken aback with the noise, a bit like an aircraft warming up...then again, I wasn t planning washing my carpets at midnight, so what the hell. The other potential difficulty is that I could imagine this machine being a bit on the  difficult  side to manoeuvre for anyone with issues around mobility. It is quite heavy and as such, may prove troublesome for anyone needing to get it into those corners or around small areas...though the attached hose can do those jobs for you without effort You also need to be aware that although a bottle of Bissell carpet shampoo does go a long way (one bottle cleans my 2 bed flat approx 2-3 times throughout) you do need to keep purchasing more. This is not a  big  issue though as you will spend more on Marigolds and scrubbing brushes, as I found out  ( I don t recall exactly how much they are, but less than a    5)Finally, on the down side, you will need a storage space as it is as clumpy as a large upright vacuum, not a problem though if you care to make a feature of it, as I do:)All in all, this machine has taken the hard work out of trying to keep my flat smelling clean, with the ease and grace of a vacuum cleaner (well, not far off) and I now don t swear at the animals for...erm...being animals .     ', '    Over the years, I have tried and tested quite a few carpet cleaners but  from now on, I will not use anything other than my Bissell Carpet Cleaner.It is lightweight, with easy to understand instructions.It is so easy to use, with the water and carpet shampoo in the same compartment.The suction is so  powerful, the cleaning fluid is delivered and removed in no time and  the carpets are almost immediately dry enough to walk o. When you compare the prices of the Bissell Carpet Cleaner with comparable carpet cleaners, in my opinion, it comes outwell ahead of its leading  rivals. A realy good product from a well established company, a company you can depend on. I would recommend this product.     ', '    I am a VERY big fan of all Bissell products. It s really economical to run and apparently uses less water than washing up by hand.  All of the dishes come out sparkling - no scraps of food left on plates - even when they have been left overnight without soaking.  It s a brilliant time saver and if you hate washing up like me it s a godsend   Although there s only 2 of us, it has a half load option so you don t have to use water for a full load. ', '    I came across this in the cocoa section, but having bought one last christmas for my step daughter, thought I would give my opinion on it.We spotted these in Toys R Us while hunting for presents for the awkward 13 year old.  What to buy   Well as soon as she spotted this, I thought, what a cool idea.This machine cost me    29.99 in Toys R Us.  It comes in a wicked pink colour, is battery operated and also comes with battery charger.  You simply put in your sugar as per instructions, put the lid on the machine and press the button.  You don t get a great deal but it is certainly tastes as good as the stuff at the fairs.  We added some blue food colouring to ours which made it look really cool - literally.However, like most novel things, the novelty wears off, as it did very rapidly with this toy.  It has been used exactly three times since Christmas.     29.99 well spent - not.It was very expensive for what it is - I suppose you are paying for the novelty factor.  It does what it says its going to do, there is no disappointment there and if you know someone who is going to eat candy floss regularly then this would be a great pressie. Otherwise, I would say don t bother.  On the other hand - I know where there is a second hand one going cheap....     ', '    Gone are the days of clinical white household appliances that show up every dirty mark and stand out like vicar in a psychedelic boudoir. Here comes style with the usual features that Hotpoint are renowned for.The WM33 comes in 3 colours, white, beige and silver (well ok, not bright colours but it  8217;s getting there). So you can now make a fashion statement of your washing machine.The buttons and knobs look pretty technical and have options such as   8216;rinse  8217;,   8216;rinse hold  8217; and   8216;one  8217; (for washing one item only, which can be handy for last minute clothing dilemmas). The one thing I had difficulty finding was the economy button, until I read the instructions (  8220;daft cow  8221;, you say) and then found out that the washing machine will monitor how much you load up and alter the water amount accordingly (shame it doesn  8217;t iron as well ). It also comes with temperature and spin speed adjustment knobs. I  8217;m still trying to fathom out when there are so many programs to choose from.At a rrp of    429 it is pretty hefty, but does do a good wash, and the spin facility (with a maximum spin speed of 1300) drains clothes more than I  8217;ve seen any other washing machine do.The main disadvantage with a non-white appliances is that it might be more difficult to match into new kitchen revamps and that colours can go out of   8216;fashion  8217; and look old before their time very quickly. But hey, it  8217;s only a washing machine we  8217;re talking about      ', '    After always wanting a breadmaker, i got a wonderfull surprise one day after coming in from shopping my partner had bought me a special present in a big brown cardboard box.once i managed to open the box, there it was a lovely chrome breadmaker, i set to work on making my first ever loaf of bread within seconds. Following the instruction manual was easy enough, and no fancy ingredients were needed as every thing you need is available in all super markets.The good thing about the bread maker is you dont just have to make bread in it, you can make whole range of things ie :-Jamcakesmuffinsdoughnuts ( no need for the seaside trips to get your doughnuts)The average time to make a loaf is around 3 hours depending on the size of the loaf you want to make.Theres a variety of breads you make ie :-brown whitesoftgraingranaryitalian herbcheese  n  onionfrenchand my favorite CHOCOLATE BREADThe best things ive found about using the bread maker area) its easy to programmeb) the outer casing stays cool ( ideal for when there are children about the house)c) its very easy to clean as everything is dishwasher safe.d) it makes your house smell lovelye) its got a window in the lid so that you can monitor the progress of the loaf.f) Fresh bread whenever you want it.g) It even has a timer so that you can set it before you go to bed and wake up to fresh bread.Theres not many dissapointments with it, however its a little on the noisey side and it cost about    80.The only other problem is beating everyone else to the freshly baked loaf as it only lasts about an hour in my house       ', '    I actually have 2 of these. The first I bought was a Remmington but when we moved house I misplaced it. I definitely had to have one but was unable to find another Remmington and bought a different make from Innovations.  Needless to say I found my old one soon afterwards. This is a very useful little gadget for shaving the bobbles that develop on items of clothing such as; socks, T-Shirts, jerseys and tracksuits.  It has saved me from throwing away some items of clothing I thought were beyond it. After giving them a shave they were almost as good as new. I use it when I am doing the ironing. It  8217;s quite fun shaving the bobbles off and I do sometimes get carried away.  A little light entertainment in the sheer drudgery of housework.By one, I definitely find it difficult to do without it.Unfortunatley I cannot remember how much the Remmington was but the other make from innovations is about    5.99. See if you can source one elsewhere as innovations are rather expensive. I originally bought the Remmington from Argos but have not seen it in their catalogue again. If I come across one elsewhere I will update this site with the name of the company.     ', '    I have had the Tefal Steam Cuisine for approx six months now . Previously , sauspans by the hob full were used for cooking our veg etc..Now all is cooked via the steamer . Obviously corners have to be cut , and different veg. etc have to share the available tiers .This said flavours are not mixed , and the end product is of better , fuller taste . Additional benefits arise from saved fuel costs . Most veg can be cooked between 10   20 minutes , depending on your preferences. The timer does allow for a full hour of steaming , allowing for items such as rice , fish etc. The time is clockwork , and very acurate , and a fairly loud Ping can be heard upon timer ending.  Setting up is easy , and the maximum water level line is easy to see . For those safty consious , the Steam cuisine has a automatic cut off , should all water be used up .On the negative side , a slightly bigger water reservoir would be useful ,thus saving on topping-up  for such items as rice. Also the drip tray is a little clumsy . Obviously such water is hot , but there is no easy way to lift up the tray to re-use this water ( eg for gravy ) . I personnaly use a baster to suck up this .     ', '    Having not had a dishwasher before, you really don  8217;t know how much they can make life easier until you actually have. I have always preferred Philips as a make, as I have a few other electrical appliances and the seem to be very good. I bought the Whirlpool Dishwasher for    300 it was originally    400 but I got it in the sales. I have to say that I am so glad that I bought it, it  8217;s easy to use and setting up and getting the hang of it was no problem. The dishes more importantly are cleaned and there  8217;s no more arguing who  8217;s washing up turn it is. ', '    You can   t be enthusiastic about a vacuum cleaner can you?  Now, come on, I   m not a train-spotter and I don   t even own an anorak, so why write a review of the Dyson DC04?To tell you the truth, I really hate vacuum cleaners; they make a horrid whining noise and you have to lift your feet up to let the wife vacuum under them    but the Dyson DC04 has actually got me at the controls, pushing it around and getting others in the family to lift their feet for me I have owned a few vacuum cleaners in my time, and have never found such an efficient machine.  A friend recommended that we get one, and reluctantly I capitulated and parted with the cash.To test it properly, I insisted that we vacuum the office thoroughly with the old vac.  The carpet looked fine, so then we started with the Dyson.  Miraculously, the transparent receiver filled up, time after time with dust, dog hair and fine grit that the other machine had left behind.We have some old rugs, and I was worried that a vacuum cleaner with such power would pull out all the tufts - the Dyson doesn   t; it just gets the dust out.With the built-in hose and tools, even vacuuming cobwebs off the ceiling and getting crumbs off the furniture is a doddle.The hose is long enough to reach up the stairs, with is a boon as we have three staircases in our house Overall, this is a well-designed bit of kit, and at the risk of being called an anorak; I would recommend it to anyone, but don t tell my friends - they will really tease me about it so, by writing this review I m really Dyson with Death      ', '    Haden corded jug kettle.  The builders, bless their cotton socks broke my kettle and they replaced it with this Haden corded kettle I am not ever so happy about it but at least they replaced my kettle without being asked.This white auto jug kettle cost about    18. The guarantee is for 12 months. A plug is already fitted to the lead. I find the cord/lead a little short .I am sorry I can find no info on the length and I can not find a measuring tool its about 30 cm long I guestimate .This kettle is a tall jug with a water level gauge on the side. Generally this is an adequate kettle, simple does its job. (it  8217;s had plenty of use while the builders are here working.)Thanks for reading. I shall go and use it now to make another cup of tea     ', '    I hate DIY, I also hate washing up, or in my case drying up. The reason I went for this, is it looked quite good  It has a grey and metallic gold finish   I also did some research on the web. (I had seen it in the Argos catalogue)I really wanted something to get deep into the carpet.  The added bonus is that I can clean the two sofas (the dogs like a cuddle now and again )  and maybe even the car upholstery.** Who are they?**As a company, Bissell have been in existence for over 125.  Apparently the first cleaner by them was patented in the US in the 1870   s.  Bissell have been active in the UK for about 100 years.  Even Queen Victoria insisted that her palaces be    Bisselled    every day ** What is it meant to do?          Pictures      ', '    I have had this breadmaker/homebaker for some years. I bought it when I was in new gadget mode and seemed to have most of the ones that most people have and this seemed a brilliant idea.Then after getting it home, unpacking it and making several loaves of bread, we realised that in this house we actually don t eat a loaf of bread a week. So there it sat atop the microwave, because we don t even have room for it really, for about three years. Every so often I gave it a wipe, thought I really ought to use it more often, but otherwise it didn t feature very highly in our lives. When the children came to visit my husband was heard to make jokes about all the gadgets we have and whether he could find something else as useless as the breadmaker for my next shopping rush.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~So  What is this wonder machine that gathers dust?I bought it in Curries, it is a Hinari breadmaker, it makes loaves of bread, cakes and even jam. What a wonder machine.I paid about    29 for it and have just looked on Amazon to see and they have them for    29.97. I am not sure if they include delivery in their prices, but leave the link for anyone who wants to buy one for themselves.http://www.amazon.co.uk/exec/obidos/ASIN/B0002HDMPQ/ciaouk-feed-21/ref 3Dnosim/026-1345950-0349267~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Then what happened?Well, some of our children with a grandchild came early in January to live with us, this is a great thing and suddenly from being a middle aged couple, we are part of this large extended family. If you’re looking for a practical and efficient carpet cleaner that fits smoothly into a busy home—especially one with pets—the Bissell Carpet Cleaner stands out for its user-friendly design and thoughtful features. One of the biggest wins here is how easy it is to clean after use: a simple rinse and wipe down gets it ready for the next round, which is a real time-saver when you’re juggling multiple chores. The separate clean and dirty water tanks are another smart touch. They’re straightforward to fill and empty, making the whole cleaning process less messy and more hygienic—something I appreciate when dealing with pet stains and odors.

From a functionality standpoint, the Bissell does a solid job tackling typical household messes, including those stubborn pet spots. While it may not replace professional deep cleaning, it offers a reliable, convenient solution for regular maintenance without the hassle. The design feels well thought out, balancing performance with ease of use, which is exactly what I look for in home appliances.

On the flip side, if you’re someone who expects ultra-quick drying times or a super lightweight machine, this might not be the perfect fit. It’s a bit bulkier than some handheld models, so storage could be a consideration if space is tight. Also, while the cleaning tanks are easy to manage, they do require regular attention to avoid any lingering smells—nothing deal-breaking, but worth noting for those who prefer low-maintenance gadgets.

Overall, the Bissell Carpet Cleaner offers solid value for money, especially if you want a dependable, no-fuss machine that handles pet-related messes with ease. It’s a practical addition to any home cleaning arsenal, combining thoughtful features with straightforward operation—just what you need to keep your carpets fresh without extra headaches.

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re diving into Eminem’s *Marshall Mathers LP*, brace yourself for a rollercoaster of raw emotion, sharp lyricism, and some seriously controversial content. Eminem’s knack for stirring the pot—both through his provocative image and clever marketing—helped this album skyrocket commercially, especially among teenagers, though it’s not exactly tailored for the hardcore hip-hop purists out there.

Lyrically, Eminem continues to shine with his original, hard-hitting style that blends rhythm and wordplay in a way that still sets him apart from many contemporaries. Tracks like “Stan” stand out as haunting masterpieces, delivering a dark, emotional punch that’s as memorable as it is depressing. On the flip side, songs like “Kim” are so intense and disturbing that they might make some listeners squirm—definitely not your casual listen, but it’s part of what makes the album so brutally honest and grounded in reality.

The album’s guest appearances—from D12 and Dr. Dre to Snoop Dogg and Dido—add a nice variety, preventing the sound from becoming too one-note. And for a bit of cheeky fun, the UK version swaps out “Kim” for “Kids,” a catchy, humorous track that lightens the mood.

One thing to keep in mind: some of Eminem’s lyrics have been wildly misinterpreted thanks to media sensationalism, so it’s worth listening with an open mind to appreciate the individuality and confidence he encourages in his fans. That said, the album does recycle some familiar lyrical and musical formulas from his earlier work, so if you’re looking for groundbreaking innovation, you might find it a bit repetitive.

Overall, *Marshall Mathers LP* is a must-listen for those who crave music with emotional depth and cultural relevance—just don’t expect a sanitized, radio-friendly ride. It’s messy, intense, and unapologetically real, much like Eminem himself.

product_reviews: ['    It s been a good year for film, franchises revived, big screen blockbusters, small low budget gems. I have seen more movies in 2007 than any single year, and I have found myself so many times writing  quot;This is my film of the year  quot; Now thankfully with a few days of the year left I can again say about Stardust that this IS my film of the YEAR  Stardust is a film I kept putting off, not for any dislike, but simply because I felt I might enjoy the movie and that personally I feel it was released at the wrong time.  I suspected that Stardust would be a Christmas film, and having just finished watching it, I feel my original view was correct. Stardust is a magnificent movie for the whole family, it does not matter whether your an art-house fanatic, and action aficionado, or a horror hoarder, if you watch Stardust and don t enjoy at least 75  of it then you really don t have a pulse.When Dunstan Thorn decides to defy the rules that their village runs by in respect to a wall that surrounds it and cross through, his quest for the unknown and adventure lands him nine months later with a child called Tristan. Now an adult Tristan (Charlie Cox) too has a quest for adventure, his adventure however is restricted to his village; Tristan has a pain in heart otherwise known as love. Victoria (Sienna Miller) is the girl in the village that everyone wants, and someone way out of Tristan s league. This little fact has no impression however on Tristan, and he sets himself the task of trying to seduce her.Across the wall in a more mystical world the death of a king leaves the sons fighting to become the rightful heir. Their quest begins as a star alls from the sky, and a battle to become the last man standing, plus of course a jewel sent out into the stratosphere causing the star to fall.On the other side of the wall Tristan makes a vow to Victoria, that he will return a week from that day, with the star they have just seen fall on the other side of the wall.  If Tristan succeeds he will win the hand of Victoria in marriage. What Tristan of course never knew what lay beyond the wall; a world with feuding princes, a trio of witches with plans to be immortal, sky pirates, and a star delivered to the world in human form. Tristan finds himself battling evil worse than he could imagine, all for love, but what if love existed in places he never expected?At just over two hours in its running time Stardust is an adventure in every sense of the word, those put off with long run times should not have any fear here, and there is seldom chance to catch your breath. Stardust echoes the great family classics of the past, with traits of the present. Aiming its sights at all areas of the audience from young to old, it blends seamless jokes and anecdotes to all areas. There is love and romance, plus more than a parting glance of action and adventure. Stardust features all the things that make these adventures great, we have always loved magic and witchery and this is the basis of the movies heart. Let s be honest however realistically Stardust is nothing new, its storyline echoes 25 year old movie The Neverending Story in more than a handful of ways. You can also draw similarities with Harry Potter, Star Wars and the Sinbad adventures. Stardust is just a new way of turning out a series of older and highly successful movies and merging them into one solitary piece. What in my mind separates Stardust from these other movies is the fact that those obvious little plot passages that a story takes, normally saved for the ending are more often than not addressed no sooner has the thought  quot;I know where this is going quot; entered your head. As a result you end up questioning the impending predictability of the movies finale, while you clearly realise that everything will be fine in the end, exactly how it will end stays a mystery.Another point of interest is that despite the American funding, Stardust is very much a British outing, all of its executive roles are UK based individuals its script writer none other than Mrs. Jonathon Ross, Jane Goldman. Its casting is also majorly British, a wealth of popular British comedy actors fill more than two dozen roles in the movie everyone from David Walliams to Ricky Gervais. The movies sets so British, you can almost smell it. So it s a phenomenal tribute that Stardust was box office gold the world over, proving that Britain still has what the world wants.There are some big name American stars filling some of the principle roles Michelle Pfeiffer is just astounding as Lamia the leader of our trio of witches. Looking stunning for her almost 50 year age, she reclaims her crown as leading lady in the role of the movies big villain. And even though her character is as cold as you can be, you cannot help but love Lamia, or are you in fact loving the actress as opposed to the character. Unafraid to face the future Pfeiffer s character ages dramatically as the movie progresses, having initially started old but using an element of an old conquest to reclaim a temporary youth. Robert DeNiro acts his most jaw dropping role as a reknown pirate type character with a penchant for fashion and all elements that might make him appear a little femme.  A scene in which this one time Hollywood hardman dons make up, a dress and performs an impromptu can-can is so terribly wrong that it s right. It s amazing to see an actor of this status not take himself too seriously and to be able to really let go.Relative newcomer Charlie Cox is great as the movies lead performer, charismatic and charming you like the guy no sooner has he appeared on screen for the first time. The journey of Tristan is carried out with you his passenger; you are literally living the adventure in a not dissimilar manner to the relationship between the Neverending Stories two leads, except this time it s you that s on the journey rather than an eleven year old boy carrying out a depiction, a representation of you.I won t linger on this review because there is only so much you can say about a film without weakening its impact. I knew very little about the film before watching it, and in fairness that s the best way to see it; less most certainly is more here. But I d like to end be reiterating my opening remarks, this movie is of exceptional quality, a real epic, you ll laugh, you ll be on the edge of your seat, and you might well cry.Stardust is still at Cinema s doing matinee screenings of the bigger cinemas. For those eager waiting for the DVD however US releases are imminent and a DVD release is scheduled in time for Easter 2008.     ', '    This is perfect for anyone who wants a fairytale with a difference.Charlie Cox as Tristan goes from an awkward, love sick young boy to a hero throughout the story, accompanied by Claire Danes who plays star Yvaine. The chemistry between the two isn t really apparent until later in the story, but both act their parts well.Michelle Pfieffer is excellent as evil witch Lamia who is desperate to get Yvaine so she can eat her heart and regain her lost youth. The performance of Mark Strong as Prince Septimus is also good, and he perfectly fits the profle of the moody, good looking and determined prince who will do literally anything to get the crown of Stormhold. However, it is Robert De Niro who steals the show with his interpretation of a gay pirate. In his role he both perfectly grasps the funny and slightly feminine nature of his character as well as the side which must pretend to be manly infront of his crew. The CGI is excellent, with a whole host of ghost princes, a magnificent castle, magic spells and of course, a star.This is a must see for anyone who wants a fairytale which isn t all smiles and happy endings.     ', '           About the film  Stardust, a fantasy film, was released in 2007. It is rated PG due to some fantasy violence and is 128 minutes long. The script was written by Jane Goldman (Jonathan Ross s wife) and Matthew Vaughn and the narration is by Sir Ian McKellen. The film had a  70 million budget and went on to make over  135 million at the box office world wide.  Plot  In a town called Wall, (because of the huge wall spanning the length with a guard preventing anyone from crossing over) a young man is desperate for adventure and manages to get across the wall. He meets a woman that has been kidnapped by a witch and they manage to spend 1 night together. 9 months later, a baby boy is left on his doorstep. 18 years later, the baby is all grown up. Tristan has fallen deeply in love with Victoria, the town beauty. One night a star falls from the sky and he vows to bring it to her for her birthday, so long as she will marry him. The star fell on the other side of the wall but Tristan fails to get past the guard. His father gives Tristan the Babylon candle his mother left him as a baby, he decides to find his mother with the candle but as he lights the candle and it transports him to the crater where the star fell in Stormhold because he was thinking about that instead. Instead of what Tristan was expecting, the star is actually a woman. Yvaine (the star) is beautiful and immortal. Tristan connects himself to Yvaine with the enchanted chain that his father gave him and promises to return her to the sky after taking her to Victoria first. As easy as this sounds, it doesn t turn out that way. Three old, haggared witches are also looking for Yvaine so they can cut out her heart and use it to keep their youth. As well as Mormo, Empusa and Lamia (the witches), the Princes of Stormhold are also looking for her because at the same time the star fell, he threw his ruby into the sky and it fused with Yvaine. The King states on his deathbed that  he of Royal blood  who finds the ruby will succeed him. On the way back to the wall, Tristan and Yvaine meet some interesting characters who both try to help and hinder their mission. Will the witches and the princes catch up with them, who will succeed the King, and will Tristan get his girl?  Cast  Charlie Cox - Tristan Thorn Claire Danes - Yvaine Michelle Pfeiffer - Lamia Robert DeNiro - Captain Shakespeare of the Caspartine Mark Strong - Septimus Nathaniel Parker - Dunstan Thorn Ben Barnes - Young Dunstan Thorn Kate Magowan - Una Sienna Miller - Victoria Foresster Peter O Toole - King of Stormhold Jason Flemyng - Primus Joanna Scanlan - Mormo Sarah Alexander - Empusa Rupert Everett - Secundus Ricky Gervais - Ferdy the Fence  What I thought  Stardust has a fantastic mix of American and British actors and it just goes to show not all of the great films only come from America. Even though Claire Danes was great as Yvaine, and im glad the other 2 actors turned down the role, she wasn t my favourite. It was nice to see the main girl not be a typical damsel in distress and she showed her fiesty side every chance she got. Michelle Pheiffer was great as Lamia. I thought she played the crazed, youth hungry witch really well and as well as being quite serious in her role, she came across as very comical when things didnt go her way. The effects and make up were really imaginative and I loved seeing how Lamia changed every time she aged a little bit more. I loved Robert De Niro s character, Captain Shakespere. He plays a great pirate with a secret and he had me laughing all of the way through his scenes. I m glad the part went to De Niro instead of Jack Nicholson because the part was made for him. As most of the film was filmed in many different locations around the UK, it has a great British feel to it, unlike some American films that try to get the British feel and atmosphere wrong. As well as being mainly shot in the UK, one of our biggest boy bands, Take That wrote the theme music  Rule the world  after seeing a cut of the movie before it s release. The song went on to reach  2 in the charts. Before watching this film, I thought I was going to hate it, thinking it was just a kids film. I was very wrong. Stardust is exciting, interesting and emotional. I even cried at one point. There is a fair bit of fantasy violence throughout and because of this it might not be suitable for young children but other than that, it is pretty much a family film. Although there is some romance in the film, it isn t over done so it isn t just a chick flick. I know quite a few guys that were suprised by this film and liked it more than they though.      ', '    When I read the description of this film I truly expected to hate it with a passion. Then I saw the trailers. Unlike most films where if you ve seen the trailer you ve already seen the best bits, Stardust has a lot more to offer than just it s trailer contents. A LOT more. Running over 2 hours if it s supposed to be a movie for kids then they are going to fidget through this. It s overly long for the sake of it in places. Based on a book by Neil Gaiman I assume the film is long to stay as true to the book as possible.Surely they should know you have to cut a lot for pacing. There are a lot of big names attached to this although the main 2 lead parts are played by unknowns (to me at least). You can tell this was a film that Terry Gilliam should have done (he turned it down) but it doesn t suffer for his absence. Take all the Gilliam classics like Time Bandits, Brazil, Fisher King   Baron Munchausen and this film would easily slot right in there with that very excellent and extremely prestigious company.It has all the makings of a cult classic but could very easily do extremely well in cinemas as well.  Michelle Pfeiffer plays a wicked witch very well, Peter O Toole as a dying king, Robert De Niro as the very camp pirate. There are many recognizable faces especially for the British audience like Ricky Gervais and several of the deceased brothers. The effects and locations are fantastic. The film is only spoiled by how long it is and would truly benefit from a harsh cutting of about 20 minutes or so. Still it is a very enjoyable movie which will stand up well to several viewings.     ', '    I am a big kid at heart, I still love to watch Disney and animated films. When I saw the trailers for Stardust on television I was captivated, a smattering of famous faces, tales of far away lands and treasures, right up my street. Although I didn t really plan to go and see it, lack of time, money and motivation. But I was pleasantly surprised when my boyfriend called me on Thursday morning and asked if I wanted to go to the Premier of Stardust that evening at 5.15pm. It was a bit of a push but I finished work a bit earlier and headed off to the cinema, The Plaza in Truro. Luckily my boyfriend had booked the tickets because when we arrived the queue was out the door, cinemas always seem to start all their films at the same time. But we didn t have to wait we just went to the ticket collection point, this is a slightly worrying idea like the Tesco self service checkouts used to be, you simply but you card into a slot, them remove it and out pop your tickets. The other annoying thing was that everyone had chosen to seat right in the middle of the cinema, so to get to our seats we had to hustle past lots of people with long legs or bags on the floor, lovely   So, anyway we finally got seated and sat down to watch the trailers of forthcoming attractions film, I just wanted to mention this as the first one they showed was for Stardust, how silly. Nevermind, after about fifteen minutes of this tedium the film started      The film starts many moons ago, the film begins in a small called Wall in England, the village is given this name for the long wall which surrounds it. There is, of course, a gap in the wall which is guarded 24 hours a day, the guard claims this gap is a portal to another world, but through some clever trickery a young man does manage to pass through.
