But while the witch is away the princess may play. Nine months after his enchanting trip the          Pictures of Didgeridoo Dreamtime - Mark Atkins     ', '    I have not written many movie reviews simply because there are plenty of people writing on here that do a really great job in this category and to be honest I really don t get the time to sit and watch many films. I mainly end up seeing films with the kids and having 2 boys aged 9 and 11 they are not really anything a women would really be into  Last year there was a lot of films that my boys really wanted to see, 2007 seemed to be a really good year for kids films we had Shrek 3, Harry Potter, Transformers, The Simpson s movie and Pirates of the Caribbean. Lucky me I got to see them all  Then I saw adverts for this film and really fancied seeing it but as it looked more like a fairy tale the boys weren t that keen and by the time I got around to persuading them the film was gone from the cinema. So I decided to get it on DVD and watch it on my own in peace and quiet, this has happened to me once before with the film Nanny Mcphee and It ended up with me starting to watch it and then having an audience, the boys suddenly decided that they really wanted to watch it and now that DVD is in their room never to be seen by me again  So did the same happen with this film or did I get to keep it to myself?THE PLOTThe film starts with a narration from none other than Sir Ian Mckellan setting the scene, he explains about the mysterious and magical town of Stormhold and the English town of Wall that is next to it. The town of Wall has surprise surprise  a wall separating it from Stormhold, along this wall is a gap that is guarded 24 hours a day by a funny little man who keeps anyone curious away.The story begins with a young man called Dunstan Thorn he decides to get through the gap in the wall and tricks the old man, having finally found Stormhold he encounters a young lady who tells him she is really a princesses enslaved by a witch, they have a brief encounter (you know what I mean ) and Dunston goes back to Wall a happy young man. That is until 9 months later the funny little old man turns up at his door and hands him a basket with a baby boy in it.The story then goes forward and you then meet the baby who is now grown into a young man, his name is Tristan and the narrator explains that this story is how Tristan became a man. Tristan you begin to realise isn t the most popular 18 year old in the town and doesn t seem to have had much luck especially with the ladies, he has set his sights on the most popular girl Victoria but she has eyes for the more popular and arrogant Humphrey. The one thing Tristan has got going for him is he doesn t give up and a week before Victoria s birthday takes her for a champagne picnic, while there they see a shooting star and Tristan makes her a promise that he will bring the star to her as a birthday present, she agrees that if he succeeds she will marry him and not Humphrey.After a failed attempt to cross the wall his father tells him about his journey over the wall and gives him a letter and a candle that his mother left for him in the basket, the candle is a magic candle and transports him straight to the star but all is not as it seems and the star turns out to be not what he expects in fact the star is a girl and a very pretty one at that, so begins the journey back to Wall with his star to give to Victoria for her birthday. Meanwhile in Stormhold the king is dying and summons his remaining sons to sort out who will next be king, the king had 7 sons and 1 daughter but now only has 4 remaining living sons the other 3 sons have been killed by their brothers in the pursuit of the throne and the daughter has mysteriously disappeared. The king enchants a jewel on a chain and tells the remaining brothers that whoever finds the jewel and turns it red will be the king he then magically shoots it into the sky. Problem is it was this jewel that knocked the star out of the sky so she ends up wearing it, one of the brothers then finds out that if he has the heart of a star he will be immortal and rule forever so he obviously starts hunting the jewel and the star. Oh and just to let you know as the brothers die they become ghosts that follow the journey of the living brothers, these are quite comical at times and include David Walliams and Rupert Everett.Another person to see the shooting star fall to earth is a witch called Lamia she gets very excited about this and informs her two sisters. The reason they are very excited is because they need the heart of a star to become young and beautiful again. They found the last star to fall to earth and took her heart but there is very little left so they have become old. These are dark witches and will do anything to get the star, Lamia sets off to get to the star and so the film becomes a sort of three way story all leading to the star.I have give a special mention in this review to Robert De Nero who usually plays the tough sort of guy and I have loved ever since I saw the film Once upon a time in America, in this film it appears at first that his role is another tough guy role being that he is the captain of a sky pirate ship. Until we glimpse him away from his crew the tough image disappears and he becomes a bit on the feminine side complete with dresses and the can-can  THE CASTCharlie Cox as Tristan Thorn Claire Danes as Yvaine ( the star )Michelle Pfeiffer as Lamia Robert De Niro as Captain Shakespeare Mark Strong as Septimus Nathaniel Parker as Dunstan Thorn Kate Magowan as Una Sienna Miller as Victoria Foresster Peter O Toole as King of Stormhold Jason Flemyng as Primus Joanna Scanlan as Mormo Sarah Alexander as Empusa Rupert Everett as Secundus Ricky Gervais as Ferdy the Fence Mark Heap as Tertius Adam Buxton as Quintus Julian Rhind-Tutt as Quartus David Walliams as Sextus Melanie Hill as Ditchwater Sal Ben Barnes as Young Dunstan Thorn David Kelly as Guard Mark Williams as Billy Dexter Fletcher as Skinny Pirate Henry Cavill as Humphrey Ian McKellen as Narrator Jake Curran as Bernard The best bit about this cast is the fact it has a very English film feel, As you can see from that list there is a few faces that you should recognize including Melanie Hill who was Avaline in Bread  Also Ricky Gervais to be honest he more or less played his part the same as most of his parts so can t say he stretched himself  But it really felt as if the film was mainly English.I felt all the parts were acted well, I thought the Michelle Pfieffer was great and looked absolutely fantastic for her age and even though she played a evil witch I couldn t help but warm to her for some reason (maybe it s the witch in me ) I also enjoyed the performances of the main characters Claire Dane (little women   Romeo and Juliette) who played the star was feisty and not always the usual damsel in distress. Also Charlie Cox who I think this is his first big movie-leading role is also believable and has lots of personality and makes the transformation from clumsy young man to hero believable.OTHER BITSThe film was originally a book written in 1998 by Neil Gaiman and was adapted into a screenplay by Matthew Vaughn (layer cake, lock stock and snatch) and Jane Goldman (wife of Johnathon Ross). I can t honestly say if the film stays true to the books, as I haven t read them.Robert de Nero s role was either going to be offered to himself or Jack Nicolson and Claire Danes role was originally offered to Sarah Michelle Geller (her of Buffy fame ) but she turned it down.The filming locations are mainly British including the Scottish highlands and the Isle of Skye and look stunning in the film.Take That wrote the song Rule the world for the film, and this gave the film some extra hype.The film lasts for 130mins but isn t bum numbing and once the action starts the time flies by  This has also been given a PG cert as there is some violence, but to be honest from what kids see today its quite tame.The special effects are really good but nothing you haven t seen before if you have seen Harry Potter, there is a great sword-fighting scene near the end that really looked fantastic.I just bought the cheaper version so sorry can t report on any DVD extras as there isn t any.MY OPINIONYou can proberly tell from this review that I did like this film actually I loved it  I really managed to lose myself in the film and laughed a lot. I felt all the actors enjoyed their parts and this seemed to show, I didn t even stop the film for a cuppa, which for me is a miracle  For me this is the perfect film for Sunday afternoons to curl up with the kids and enjoy a good family film. I can also report that again I have lost this DVD to my boys as they really enjoyed it and actually had the nerve to question why I didn t take them to the pictures to see it  There was enough action to keep them interested and for them the lovey dovey bits were not over long so they could just about stand them      ', '    The cast Charlie Cox ... Mark Atkins’ *Didgeridoo Dreamtime* offers a fascinating dive into the rich, meditative soundscape of the didgeridoo, an instrument far removed from the typical pop or rock fare. For a listener like you—curious and open-minded, with a penchant for musical depth and storytelling—this album presents a unique opportunity to explore a genre that prioritizes atmosphere and tradition over conventional song structures or lyrical narratives.

Musically, the album excels in its authentic, organic instrumentation. Atkins’ mastery of the didgeridoo creates a hypnotic, almost trance-like experience that feels both ancient and timeless. The production is clean and immersive, allowing the instrument’s deep drones and subtle overtones to resonate fully. While the album lacks lyrical content, it compensates with a profound emotional texture that invites reflection and a connection to Indigenous Australian culture. This can be especially rewarding if you appreciate music as a form of storytelling beyond words.

However, the album’s meditative style may challenge listeners accustomed to more dynamic or lyrically driven music. Its repetitive, minimalist approach might feel limiting if you seek melodic variation or narrative progression. From a collector’s perspective, owning a physical copy—especially vinyl—could enhance the experience, as the tactile engagement complements the album’s earthy, spiritual vibe.

In sum, *Didgeridoo Dreamtime* is a compelling artistic statement that broadens your musical palette and offers a sonic journey into a deeply rooted cultural tradition. While it diverges from the lyricism and compositional complexity you often favor, it rewards attentive listening with a rare, immersive sound world. If you value artist growth and exploration, this album stands as a testament to the power of music to evoke memory and emotion without words, making it a worthy addition to a thoughtful, diverse collection.

It doesn t have any particular novelty value - it s just a collection of (mostly) good songs, and that s how I m going to review it here.The first thing to note is that this album is - as its title would imply - exclusively made up of songs which reached number one in either the UK or the USA. That means that there s no place for many of the Beatles  finest works, either because they only appeared on albums (Lovely Rita, for example) or because they didn t reach the top of the charts. The most infamous example of the latter qualification is Strawberry Fields, which was kept off the summit by - of all things - Please Release Me.So, to the songs. The 27 tracks can reasonably be split into three roughly equal groups: early, middle and late. They re not perfect breaks, but they ll do. Which is rather handy for reviewers such as yours truly - cheers, Fab Four  So, without further ado, let s get on the case.=====EARLY SONGS===========1) The Beatles  very first number one was, of course, Love Me Do, which only achieved the top spot for one week, and then only in America, but was, as it turned out, the beginning of a legend. (Yes, yes, I know, the Quarrymen, Hamburg and all that - I m talking about the mass market.) It s fair to say that Love Me Do isn t the most memorable song ever released, and might well have long since faded into obscurity were it not for the identity of its artists. I happen to be a mouthorgan fan, though, so I rather like it.2) Next up is the group s first British number one, a position which it held for no less than seven weeks. Yes, it s From Me To You, a song which, though it retains the mouthorgan ornaments from Love Me Do, sounds considerably more recognisably  quot;Beatley quot;. It s here that the Fab Four s trademark harmonies really come to notice for the first time.3) The third track,  quot;She Loves You quot;, gets my vote as the best of the Beatles  early numbers. It s an uptempo, happy song that can t fail to bring a smile to your face, one of the most joyful of all their hits. It was at No. 1 for six weeks in the UK, but seems to be much less regarded these days. A very underrated song in my book.4) This is followed by  quot;I Want To Hold Your Hand quot;, another relentlessly cheerful, feelgood tune ( quot;and when I touch you I feel happy inside quot;). Maybe it s not the most original piece of music ever written, but who cares? Just get out there and dance the night away 5) Can t Buy Me Love, for anyone who s seen the film of A Hard Day s Night (of which more anon) inescapably conjures up images of John, Paul, George and Ringo fooling around on fire escapes in the middle of a field. Many people tend to play it too fast - one interesting thing about the Beatles  songs is that their tempos are often not what you might expect from reading the lyrics.6) As promised above, we now move on to A Hard Day s Night. This is a bit of a turning point - it has a little bit more of an edge to it than the earlier songs. It might be considered the point at which the Fab Four started to shed the  quot;generic Sixties pop group quot; label and hint at something much bigger and more interesting.7) I Feel Fine, though, returns to the feelgood mode of She Loves You, though the slightly Oriental effect of the opening chord is hardly conventional. This is another song which is often played much too fast - it s a happy song, yes, but in a reflective way rather than a shout-it-out way. The sort of song that many of today s clubbers could never cope with - after all, the melody is louder than the drums and it s slower than 180 bpm....8) Eight Days A Week (yep, slower than you d think, yet again) also experiments with the opening bars, but after that it s all rather conventional. It wasn t released as a single in Britain, and to be honest I don t think that was a great loss as it really isn t especially memorable.9) Ticket To Ride has a very interesting guitar track - it s not at all what you d expect from an archetypal pop group of the era. It also has the  quot;twiddly chorus quot; ( quot;She oughtta think right, she oughtta do right by me quot;) so apparent in many of the later songs. And it also fades out rather than ends cleanly - something that I generally dislike, but still... and with that, we leave the early years behind and move on to:*****************************=======MIDDLE PERIOD=============10) Help  is the song that kicks off this section. It can be read in two ways: either as a straight song, as which I really don t think it s all that interesting, or as an autobiographical comment about what fame has brought on the group, which is a much more engaging idea. Lyrics such as  quot;and now my life has changed in oh so many ways quot; and, especially,  quot;my independence seems to vanish in the haze quot;, would seem to point to the truth of the second hypothesis.11) And so we come, inevitably, to Yesterday. It s hard to say what I can say about this song which hasn t been said a million times already (except that this one is often played too *slowly* ). It came as quite a surprise as a child to discover that this was a Beatles number - even by the early eighties it had become an established standard. Can t say I find it *that* involving, though I realise many people beg to differ.12) Ah, Day Tripper. Winner of the  quot;best intro in the history of the world ever quot; competition. I once attended a concert at Liverpool s Albert Dock, given by a guitarist on a floating stage. The performance was, shall we say, not going too well, with many people preferring the delights of the jellybean shop. Then that famous riff sounded out... and the transformation was instant, with smiles breaking out around the dock. Needs to be played LOUD, this one :-)13) We Can Work It Out is an interesting one. Could it be seen as an early indication of tensions within the Beatles? Personally, I don t think so, but that s just a gut feeling. It s another  quot;two-piece quot; song, with an insistent, almost pleading chorus reminding us that  quot;life is very short quot;, and an uptempo verse which shows a more positive attitude ( quot;we can work it out quot;).14) The exact halfway point of  quot;1 quot; is marked by Paperback Writer, and that s quite appropriate as it shows elements of both early and late Beatles styles: we have both the traditional  quot;poppy quot; features of the early years and the later innovative harmonies and inventive lyrics. It s just a shame that it isn t a more memorable song.15) Yellow Submarine was another of my  quot;oh, is that really the Beatles? quot; childhood discoveries. It s the first really psychedelic song on the album, pretty much impossible to categorise and the sort of thing only a supremely gifted and confident group could get away with. If anyone else had put this out, they d have been laughed into oblivion; because it was the Fab Four people write studious critiques of it (like this one ).16) In Liverpool, there is a bench on one street, on which sits a cast figure of Eleanor Rigby, dedicated to  quot;all the lonely people quot;. A very introspective work, this one, with an overpowering sense of melancholy. The most poignant words,  quot;died in the church and was buried along with her name quot;, perhaps (and this is just me shooting in the dark, but what else do you expect?) hint at a worry about what will happen to the Beatles after they are gone and forgotten - as it turns out, something which is unlikely to be a problem any time soon.17) When I lived in Liverpool, I used to pass the end of Penny Lane regularly - and yes, the barber is still there, as is the  quot;shelter in the middle of the roundabout quot;, though by the time I was a resident it had become a bistro. This is one of my favourite songs of this era. It proves that the really great musicians can write wonderful songs on pretty much any subject. Although I d question how you can have  quot;blue suburban skies quot; and  quot;pouring rain quot; at the same time - the latter was generally my experience  Penny Lane displays a common later-Beatles trait, that of making weird noises (technical term there, ladies and gents) on the outro. Here we have what sounds like a lion roaring with about 30 seconds to go - I really have no idea whatever why.*****************************=====LATER SONGS===========18) The start of the  quot;late Beatles quot; period on this album is most definitely marked by the famous  quot;Marseilles quot; intro to All You Need Is Love. It must also have one of the longest outros of any song - well over a minute - taking in snatches of music drawn from as far apart as Glenn Miller and Greensleeves. Well known as the song chosen for one of the first satellite broadcasts of pop music, this one is clearly of the  quot;peace and love, man quot; school - the single was also the first one to show (in some versions) John, Paul, George and Ringo in moustaches and long(ish) hair. From now on, the straight pop thrash would no longer be a part of the Beatles  vocabulary.19) Hello, Goodbye seems at first listen to be a return to more traditional poppery (my spellchecker tried to change this to  quot;popery quot; ), but if you actually listen to the words, you ll discover that they re anything but conventional. There s no explanation of what s going on, there s generalised weirdness going on on the backing track and the song has no real shape to it. Another one with an odd outro - 40 seconds of folk-style stuff that keeps threatening to turn into You Are My Sunshine....20) Lady Madonna has a good claim to be my favourite among the later songs on this record. A strong rhythm, not *too* much strange studio trickery for the sake of it, and excellent lyrics - especially the very clever way in which  quot;see how they ll run quot; is made to fit on the end of two very different verses.21) Hey Jude, though, is not on my top songs list. There s nothing too much wrong with this slow ballad in itself, and the harmonies are interesting (especially  quot;better better better better quot; - if you haven t heard it, you ll have to take my word for it that this *does* make sense ). The problem is that it s far, *far* too long. At over seven minutes, you might call it the Beatles   quot;Bohemian Rhapsody quot;, except that it s not nearly so interesting. A three-minute version would have been excellent; this drags badly.22) Get Back. Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear. Apparently this song was at the top of the charts for six weeks here and five in the US. All I can say to that is: why, for heaven s sake? It s a tremendously feeble effort by the Fab Four s standards, with possibly the least interesting melody of anything they ever put out. Frankly, this song is a disgrace to the group: overindulgent, repetitive and - yes - boring. Skip it.23) The Ballad Of John And Yoko is probably the least well known number on  quot;1 quot;, and that s rather a shame, I think. Despite its fairly regular use of a certain religious word beginning with  quot;C quot;, it can t seriously be classified as offensive, so the fact that many radio stations (especially in the US) still don t allow its play is slightly absurd. It s a bit of a throwback in some ways, eschewing the mixing-desk madness characteristic of the late period Beatles and returning to an earlier age of bouncy tunes and simple lyrics. Well worth a listen.24) Something, the next track, is a total break with what precedes it. A dreamy, reflective piece, it s probably George Harrison s best song for the Beatles. If only he d been able to resist those blasted sitars more of the time, there might have been more as good as this one. Very few words, but then it doesn t need them.25) Come Together is an acquired taste, and I must admit that I haven t acquired it. If you didn t know better, you might not think this a Beatles song at all - it could quite easily have been written for a mid-Seventies film soundtrack. I m sure it has all kinds of hidden meanings, but to be honest they re way over my head.26) The penultimate song on the album is, unfortunately, the horribly mawkish Let It Be. If we *have* to have John Lennon playing the piano in this style, then I suppose Imagine would be preferable, though even that I feel is somewhat overrated. But not so much as this one - please tell me, what is so great about it? It s just four minutes of semi-religious drivel; the sort of mindless good intentions that achieve nothing.27) And so we come to the end, and appropriately it s The Long And Winding Road, a fitting way to go out. By this time (1970) it was clear to all and sundry, not just the group themselves, that the Fab Four s days were numbered, and listened to in that context it s a very poignant piece - the Beatles themselves are coming to the end of their own  quot;long and winding road quot;. *****************************============That s the songs dealt with - what of the packaging? The front cover is striking though dull, but the back cover has pictures of the four Beatles alongside the track list. Three are in negative, but one is not. Yep, you ve guessed it - it s Paul. He s also carrying a white bird, which *clearly* indicates that he was assassinated with a poisoned hairgrip in 1969 by a deranged Abbey Road traffic warden, and replaced by the spawn of Beelzebub....The insert booklet is very well done. There aren t any lyrics, which is a pity, but instead we get a page for each track detailing dates of recording and of hitting the top spot in either country; and also a fascinating selection of record sleeves for each song, many of them from foreign editions ( quot;Los Beatles quot;). One very nice touch is that they re pictures of *real* records, complete with dog-eared corners and writing on the sleeves, rather than clinical PR shots.So, there you have it. Twenty-seven songs tracing a path through eight of the most extraordinary years in modern musical history. Listen to Love Me Do and All You Need Is Love and you d be hard pressed to tell they were from the same outfit. By 1970, the world of pop music had changed enormously, and these four men had played perhaps a bigger part than anyone in that. Okay,  quot;1 quot; isn t breaking any new ground, and it doesn t contain any great revelations, but as a guide to the way popular music changed, 1962-1970, you can t beat it. To quote Slade s Yuletide anthem,  quot;Does your Granny always tell you that the old songs are the best? quot;.  These songs may be between 30 and 40 years old, but they wiped the floor with the competition.Enough said? Still, it is an interesting song, persuading a friend not to be shy and  quot;go out and get her quot;At the time John found it very encouraging to his relationship with Yoko Ono. 8/1022) Get back: Awful.  quot;Get back quot; appears to be about American Wild West Transvestites.  quot;Jojo was a man who thought he was a women, But she was another man quot;and so on As has already been said on this site, over-indulgent, rambling,over-long, pointless, and boring. Paul s singing wavers around a lot as well, and the only good bits are the guitar riffs and Ringo s drumming.   3/1023) The ballad of John and Yoko. John s account of a chaotic honeymoon. It covers the bed-in, bagism, and their acorn craze.John seemed to have gone mad but not realised quite how bonkers he was.   quot;the newspaper s said, she gone to his head quot;The blaphemous chorus  quot;Christ, you know it ain t easy quot; is not quite as bad as you might think, for both Christ and John struggled to get the message across. (Although Christ had a far less gimmicky message). Bouncy and fun.  8/1024) Something:  quot;Something quot; is a true timeless classic by George, expressing how he feels about this girl, who has some hidden charisma. Will his relationship last? a touch of doubt, beautiful first line, and dreamy singing, easily put this up here with  quot;Yesterday quot;. Were it released today it would probably hit No. 1 just like it did back then.  9/1025) Come together: Actually written by Timothy Leary but taken by John. Meaningless song really. What is it about? Sex? Rousing rally-round to unite the Beatles?There s not enough of the rockin   quot;middle eight quot; either.  A few clever lyrics though, like  quot;whaaaan an whaaan an whaaaaaan is three quot; and  quot;feet, down, below his knees quot; keep it from true mediocrity.  6/1026) Let it be: This song is sickly and saccharin, with no deep meaning whatsoever. They ran out of things to say half way through, and just resorted to saying  quot;let it be, let it be, oh let it be, let it be quot; and then an out of place guitar solo.  4/1027) Although this was actually no way near the last song they ever recorded, could of been. Does it seem like McCartney s vocals are drowned somewhat by the choir and everything?. Blame it on Phil Spector, who gave the  quot;Let it be quot;  album all the added instrumentals. Despite the controversial absence of  quot;Strawberry fields quot; (it only ever reached No. 2, pipped by some rubbish by Englebert Humperdinck quot;) and the lack of  quot;Sergeant Pepper quot; this CD is VERY good value for money, yes, there are a few bum tracks, but they had to have every No. 1 included , not just the best ones.The album cover, with closer inspection, looks like it was cobbled up on Microsoft Paint. It s quite effective though. Inside the booklet is a little intro by the one and only George Martin and a page donated for each of their single covers from different countries. Quite interesting.Overall, No. 1 is  solid, and great value for money. If you already own all the albums, don t bother. But if you are just getting into the Beatles and don t know which peirod you will like best, or are just wanting to start a Beatles collection, this (along with Sergeant Pepper) would be the ones to own.Hope you enjoyed reading this  Please rate me as I like to know what you think of my first album review  : )     ', '    What do you buy a miserable old git who never appreciates anything that you get him anyway? It is that time of year again, my Dad is 51 and I am struggling to get him a present. Usually I get him a bottle of Whiskey or some other cop out present. The thing is that my lack of originality has started to be noticed by my family. Now as I am already considered the black sheep and as they are getting on a bit and they will soon be finalising the Will (OK this is a joke and if they do pop their clogs soon I will feel bad so please no comments calling me a heartless swine) I feel it is time to make an effort.So I embark on my shopping trip on Thursday 3rd May, two days after my father  8217;s birthday, there is nothing like getting off to a good start. Thursday night is late night opening so I go straight from work, this will give me a whole hour of shopping before the shops shut. More than enough time to find a present for someone who has no hobbies or interests. Then suddenly it hits me. Ouch My father has never bothered to update his music collection to CD. Therefore all I need to do is to remember what he likes and buy that. So I went into the nearest CD outlet and look for some country music (hey he is old and strange). Then on my way to the counter I spy Beatles   8211; 1. My dad keeps going on about how he has original Beatles vinyl and how much it is worth. Figuring that he is too tight to actually play them in case the value drops I decide that this would make a far better present than Willie Nelson Sings About Tax Evasion which I promptly throw over my right shoulder and forget about.OK less background more opinion I think.This is a fantastic album. Firstly there are 27 songs on it. I know that the Beatles have notoriously short songs but try to find another CD that has 27 songs. Then there is the fact that this album only has those Beatles songs that went to number 1. OK it might have been number 1 in Botswana but at least each song was considered good enough for single release. This means that you weed out all the guff that you find on the original albums (hey I like the Beatles but I do not see them as the god like geniuses that many seem to). The next thing is the price. Most Beatles CDs I have seen in the shops range from    13.99 to    18.99 and then the double CDs and special editions cost more. Bearing in mind that most of these will only have about ten songs on them (restricted by vinyl  8217;s limits) this works out at a fair whack a song. You do the maths. This means that you are actually getting this for less than half the price of an original Beatles album and missing out all the average album tracks.So is there a problem with this. This all depends. It has all the Beatles tracks you know and love (you know the songs which is why I am not reviewing them but rather I am doing the album as a whole). This however means that the average Beatles fan will already own these songs on other albums.It does have to be remembered why I bought this album though. It is a present for my Dad. My Dad is a Beatles fan, an original Beatles fan. This means that he has these songs but not on CD. This is perfect for him. He does not want to play the vinyl because it is worth money and sounds crap (I am not saying vinyl is crap just his record player), he will not go out and buy his vinyl collection on CD as they are around    15 a pop. So in this CD he has all the songs he loves in one place, it is cheap (hell it is free for him) and the quality is great.This may be another case of the Beatles releasing the same old stuff to make more money. In fact we all know that it is the Beatles trying to make more money as Paul McCartney is down to his last 387 Trillion quid. The fact is though it is one of the better deals around, if you only own one Beatles album make it this one.     ', '    For Christmas I got The Beetles  No. 1 . What a great present  Although my all time favourite Beetle song is  Strawberry Fields  (was not a No. 1) the rest was great.   And it s true what Paul McCartney said:  quot;it s not our best work quot;.  I think it s great that the group are still making money, seeing as they were the original boyband, and a great idea to release it in memory of John Lennon.  Even if your a new fan, or a long time lover, this album will start and complete your Beetles collection perfectly.     ', '    We all know that if you ve never heard of The Beatles before you ve either lived in an underground enclosure for 40 years, or your under ten years old. But, just because they re back again doesn t mean we have to get fed up of them. Anyone with great talent should never fade, and if they re not appreciated, it s because of jealousy  Well maybe.  Although these songs have all been heard before,  a compilation of all 27 of their number one hits can t be all that bad if all those copies have been sold.  Favourite after favourite roll out of this hit cd helping to prove that sometimes the old songs are the best. They even sound good quality, which is good to say they are all a fair few years old and some of them were recorded even before television sound effects came about   The songs seem to follow on from each other in style, but how the sadder songs come to be bunched up together near the end wasn t too clever in my opinion.  The price of the album was not more than most today which is good, and even some places were doing great deals on it s price even being as little as    8  or     9.  So we can t really grumble. It s simple -they re good.  Very good.     ', '    It has been a hard days night - since the Beatles brought out there last song and although they are without doubt the best british band of all time, I personally feel there was no need for this album to be released.It has been 20 years since the Beatles brought out a song and all the songs on this album are on the 20+ other Beatles albums that have been release.My verdict is buy if you are a Beatles fan - leave well alone if your notthere are plenty more albums which may be worth your hard earnt cash     ', '    You probably think that The Beatles are an old peoples group, don t you? Think that this is the kind of album that your mum would like for her birthday, but isn t your thing? Well, you d be wrong. So, so wrong...The material on this album doesn t sound half as dated as you might think, in fact it s surprising to hear just how little Oasis etc. have actually diverged from the style of The Beatles. The album itself contains all 27 of the band s UK and US Number 1 singles, arranged chronologically, so you can hear the progression from the simpler rock and roll style of their earlier material, to the softer, more ballady style that characterised their later songs. Most of the songs on here you ve probably heard before (or, at least, heard of) and if you haven t then you should be ashamed of yourself The inlay brochure itself is also a great thing for fans, as it reproduces all the US and UK covers for all the songs on the album, along with a full list of dates when each song was in the charts. A bit anorak-y, perhaps, but the kind of thing that fans will go nuts over.It s not a perfect album, though. Since the album only includes Number 1 singles, there are a lot of songs that aren t on here (Strawberry Fields, Roll Over Beethoven, I Am The Walrus, to name but a few) but then again, a full collection of all the groups hits would span many, many discs. And, of course, die-hard fans will probably be sick to death by now of the endless  quot;Greatest Hits quot; compilations. Anyway, this is a great album. Obviously, if you re more into thrash metal or speed garage, then you probably have very little interest in proper music like this. (Relax, I m only joking...) But if you think that dirge like Coldplay is God s gift to the world of music, then buy this album and see where all the  quot;new wave quot; got their ideas from, 40 years ago. Throughly recommended.     ', '    This has got to be one of my favorite albums in my extensive collection.  The Beatles - 1 has no less than 27 of their number1 singles all on one CD. You just can t go wrong with it. I can t get it out of my player  I truly do believe that everyone should add this album to their collection, regardless of whether or not they are a big Beatles fan, lets face it few people actually dislike their musicThis is by far the best greatest hits album i have ever heard.     ', '    The Beatles were and indeed still are one of the most influential bands in recording history, in just 8 years they had countless hits and changed the way many looked at the music industry.This album is a collection of the Beatles  number 1 hits from the UK and American Charts and is a selection of their best material. Everyone should have this in their CD collection, whether a Beatles fanatic or not this album has wide appeal, play this to almost anyone and they will enjoy it. In a word this album can only be described as  Brilliant  .The only thing against it is that most Beatles fans will already own all of the songs on this album, but i dont see that as a major flaw as this album brings all the best material together on one album and would be a good addition to any beatles CD library.The accompanying inlay book is also colourful and informative giving information on each of the tracks and showing the covers of every realease of each single from all over the world.     ', '    So, the Beatles. Quite a well known brand they ve got there, isn t it?  This album is frankly amazing; not for its musical content, which is a succint summing up of almost the entire recognisable Beatles range, but for the way it swept to number 1 in the album charts and outsold everything in sight.Who bought it for  lt;BLEEP gt; s sake? I would have though that any Beatles fan would have either the Red and Blue albums, the Anthology, all the albums, or at least a fair proportion of the material - certainly all of the tracks on this album. As for non-Beatles fans... this album isn t really for them  OK, so younger people may not have the original Beatles albums, and that accounts for a fair chunk of the sales... but to outsell everything in sight? With material which hasn t been released *once* before, but at least 3 times? Truly a marketing miracle.The album itself is great, and I would recommend it to anyone who, like me, like the Beatles a bit but not enough to have splashed out on a larger compilations, such as the red and blue albums (whatever they were called).Miraculous in two ways then:1) It manages to compress years of quality music into 80 minutes or so.2) It managed to sell enough discs to... I dunno.. make a fortune for the remaining Beatles.     ', '    Most people will allready have all theses songs any way but this is certanly a must for anyones collection. Without doubt the most influential and importtant band ever and this has most of their best songs handily packaged on one album. Okay there a songs they did whcih are better than some of the ones that are on hear, but it is, as allready proved, impossible to put all the best beatles songs on one album, you really have to get all their albums, but this is expensive and not everyone will want them all so this is an ideal album.The fact it is chronolgical order is very interesting as well as you can hear how much they progressed as a band from the early songs like  quot;she loves you quot; and  quot;Cant buy me love quot; to songs they did towards the end of their careaer like  quot;Let It be quot; and  quot;Come together quot;. Listening to this you also hear how much of an influence they had on bands such as Oasis and the stereophonics. If you are allready a fan and have most or all of their stuff buy it because it has most of thir best songs on one cd. If  you don t own any beatles stuff buy it because it is pretty exstensive collection of some of the best songs ever written.     ', '    After 30 years or so The Beatles return with their new album, which includes all their greatest hits such as  quot;Ticket to Ride quot; and  quot;Eight Days a week. quot; This album is a must have for your CD collection and is well worth purchasing.This album is fairly expensive at your local music store, but you can buy it cheaper over the internet, which is what I did.I recommended this album to my friends but they were more interested in more modern bands  Although one of my friends bought his Dad the album for Christmas, and there was a slight fault on the song  quot;Yellow Submarine quot; so the album had to be returned, but I don t know anyone else who had this problem.This album is aimed at just about any age group, and for people who like The Beatles  music.     ', '    My Mother and Father are the greatest fans of the beatles, when this album came out there was great competition between my parents and I to get this album, seen as tho I had been brought up on the beatles I thought all 27 no1 s on one album would be worth something in years to come so behind there backs I went and boughht it, boy    it was the best    13 I had ever spent  Just sat there wrapping all the presents up listening to it was Bliss This album is one for the youth, it gives them all an insight to what our parents listened to, I thought it was a different to listen to some class music for once rather than todays music.     ', '    I recently bought this, as probably most of you have for a chistmas present for my father.  So you are probably want my opinion.  Well My father loves it but more importantly I LOVE IT           .  This CD is for people of all ages and it is recemmened by an 18year old.  Its got all there number one hits, Which are of course incredible, When they were recorded and alittle about the beatles themselves.  This has to be an excellent choices for a birthday present.  If you BUY IT YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPOINTED        .     ', '    This is an absolutly great album. No matter who you are what your music tastes are this is fantastic. Whilst i normally hate to go with the masses as so many of then are twats in this case the majority are correct this is a fornominal album. Go and bye it no I dont care if you already own it get it again its great every cd system in your house should have one.  Whilst it doesnt have some of my favorites on such as little better (or something like that) it has everything most people could want any cd that has over 20 good tracks is worth the money but this one has over 25 increadible value go bue it now.... well go on then.      ', '    anthology was good because there were loads of demos and different arrangments of songs on it, but 1 is just the same songs that most of us have already got but repackaged in a different sleeve. A hardcore beatles fan would have all these tracks already in fact most of us have all these songs already, there is twenty seven songs squished onto a compact disc but the beatles actually had 17 number one singles. Its just lucky that the beatles songs are so good that I ll never get sick of them the way Im sick to the teeth of abba. Abba is comming at you from all angles.     ', '    The Beatles are the biggest selling musical group of all time. Their undoubted success however surprises me due to my belief that they are a totally mediocre musical group. Looking back at some of the talents that have graced the world of music through time (such as Andrew Lloyd Webber, Mozart, Eminem, Tom Jones) I find it difficult to comprehend to overall storm that is the Beatles.It is tru to say that the four relatively handsome chaps from Liverpool had some style and were marketed fantastically, but does that mean that they were talented musicians? I think not. The overall  package  of the Beatles made them popular- like groups such as Steps or Five in today s charts. Lennon was always a musical genius and a total eccentric, this shone through as the band were watched and listened to. However, the other members of the group developed to between average and good musicians as time went on They are the most successful group ever, and I believe the most over-rated because of it. They found a niche and exploited it to full effect- good entrepeneurial vision all round      ', '    At last an album with all of my favourite Beatles songs on it  For years i ve enjoyed listening to the Beatles by sneakily pinching my dad s albums when he wasn t looking but never invested in an album myself as i could never find one that had all of my favourites on it.Finally  quot;1 quot; has filled the gap in my CD collection and hasn t been off my stereo since i bought it.This album is great for people like me who like the Beatles but are not obsessed enough to go and buy all of their albums just to get the songs they like.This is very much a cheerful, boogie around the room singing at the top of your voice album.  Lets face it everyone knows the words to the number ones.  Also a good party album.     ']

If you’re dipping your toes into the vast Beatles ocean, *1* is a neat little raft that sails you through their chart-topping hits from 1962 to 1970. It’s like a greatest-hits time machine, showcasing their evolution—from the early, infectious harmonies of “Please Please Me” (catchy and joyful, no doubt) to the more emotionally complex and inventive songwriting gems like “Eleanor Rigby” and “Penny Lane.” You get 27 number-one singles packed onto a single CD, which is impressive value for money, especially with the well-designed booklet that includes recording dates and original single sleeves—though, fair warning, it’s a bit stingy on lyrics, which some fans might miss.

Now, if you’re a Beatles aficionado who’s already got the original albums, *1* might feel like déjà vu with a side of “been there, heard that.” It’s a convenient collection for casual listeners or newcomers but offers little fresh material for the seasoned fan. Also, don’t expect to find “Strawberry Fields Forever” or “Please Please Me” here—both iconic but absent because they never hit number one. So, it’s a bit of a chart-centric tunnel vision that leaves out some culturally and musically significant tracks.

In sum, *1* is a solid, well-packaged introduction to the Beatles’ biggest hits, perfect for those who want a snapshot of their musical journey without diving into the deep end. Just don’t expect it to replace the rich experience of the original albums or satisfy the craving for the band’s full artistic range. For a first-timer or a casual fan, it’s a joyride through pop history; for the Beatles die-hard, it’s more like a greatest-hits greatest hits.

product_reviews: ['    I   d imagine I was probably one of only a few Ciao members who had head of Snow Patrol before the recent release of the third album    Final Straw    and come to think of it I   m probably still one of only a few members to have heard of the band since as well. The first two albums weren   t the best but since then Snow Patrol have undergone a slight personnel change and have changed direction slightly with the help of a new producer and new record label. The band originally met at Dundee University after lead singer Gary Lightbody had come across from Northern Ireland to attend and met Bass player Mark McClalland on the first day there. After a lot of early praise they proceeded to tour with the likes of Travis and Belle and Sebastian as they became one of the darlings of the Scottish music scene. However after debut effort    Songs For Polar Bears    and second album    When Its All Over We Still Have to Clear Up   , Snow Patrol have taken to their Scottish roots and come up with this masterpiece of an album. From the albums opening track    How To Be Dead    the tone of the album is set. A guitar intro dies out before a keyboard brings the song back to life and the guitar suddenly stars up again providing a slow mellow introduction. The vocals come in soon afterwards and although the lyrics are a bit bizarre they really do sound superb complimented well by the guitars and a slow drum beat in the back ground. A good solid start that mixes a nice steady beat with a nice melody and really emphasises the vocals. The pace of the track varies slightly but it really is a good start to the album. The second track really picks up where the first left off and    Wow    starts with some guitars obviously being tuned before a beat really starts up. The drum beat stays constant throughout picking up the pace from the beginning making this a fairly medium paced track. The guitars sound amazing and really compliment the vocals well, which again work well with some clever lyrics. The slower parts of the track don   t really last that long and still have a real edgy feel to them as the guitars repeat the same chords while the drum beat changes slightly from the rest of the track. A touch of distortion added to the vocals works really well and adds a little something extra to the overall feel of the song.    Gleaming Auction    is the shortest track on the album and again continues the gradual pace build up already displayed in the previous two tracks. Rather than the casual intro the guitar starts straight away with the drums and vocals coming in pretty shortly after. This leads the first verse into the chorus where the pace and sound changes completely as a heavier guitar really leads the way and the pace of the drums picks up a touch. The vocals again have changed in tone and sound from the previous 2 tracks but still sounds as good if not better, which adds a refreshing touch to the album as they don   t sound the same. That   s followed up by    Whatever   s Left   , which in all honesty starts in a very similar way to    Gleaming Auction   . Although this helps to keep the consistency of the album and helps it to flow along a lot easier than it would have changing the style with every track. The bass brings it in but is joined very quickly by the drums, vocals and guitars, for a good solid intro building steadily into a more upbeat faster track that really keeps the album going. The vocals again sound good and are actually quite catchy complimented well by the guitars. The first single to be taken from the album,    Spiting Game   , didn   t really get a lot of airplay and seemed to really slip by without anyone noticing it. A fast paced start with the guitars and drums coming in from the opening note for a short introduction before the melody changes slightly and the vocals start up. The rhythm of the track stays consistent all the way through with the vocals really taking the forward role but the drums and guitars really complimenting them well and really giving the feeling that they are keeping the song and the album moving along. The vocals sounds slightly different again to any of the other tracks and this adds good variety to the overall feel of the album. The next track is one of my favourites and also includes the album title as part of the lyrics.    Chocolate    slows the pace of the album down to a more mellow level but it works well and really signifies the start of the mellower middle section. A slow guitar intro, joined fairly shortly afterwards by the drums gets the track underway and sounds perfect for a middle of the album interlude. The vocals come in fairly soon afterwards while the drum beat continues all the way into the chorus, where the pace and melody change slightly but keeps the same pace and beat. The lyrics are well written and Gary   s vocals really bring out the best in them. It   s then the current single and the track that   s really got the band the acknowledgement and praise they deserve.    Run    is another slower track and the middle of the three mellower songs on the album, this one is probably the slowest of the lot. A slow guitar opens before the drums come in at a similar slow meandering pace before finally the vocals come in. The slow pace of the vocals mean they are almost spoken but the lyrics really set your mind off thinking about the songs content of lost love. It   s a little different from the rest of the album in terms of pace but sounds totally amazing. Coming to the end of this mellower segment the final song of the three is    Grazed Knees   . It has a very haunting opening with the keyboard really opening it up before the guitar comes in followed shortly after by the vocals. The guitar really builds upon this haunting feeling as it slowly builds up in the background and when we finally get to the chorus the full effect of this can be felt as the backing vocals also provide an echo like effect to the main vocals. Although fairly short it is really good and gets inside your head again really making you think about things, however saying that its just as easy to switch of and enjoy it as just a mellow track. Another favourite of mine on this album is    Ways and Means   , which starts to pick the pace back up again. The opening drum beat is a little faster and more purposeful as is the guitar creating a quiet intro gradually getting louder the closer to the verse it gets. The vocals have a slight echo effect to them and again spark a little bit of thought with the lyrics. The repeating tune carries on for the verse before the pace and melody chances for the chorus and this really works well as the vocals really continue to lead the sound of the track and the album as a whole. The musical element stays consistent throughout, not really varying a great deal but enough to keep it sounding fresh. The pace really has been picked up and    Tiny Little Fractures    just carries this on. The guitars open it up with a pretty fast paced but repetitive riff before the drums come in to lead the song into the verse. The pace settles with the introduction of the vocals, which again sound brilliant and are complimented very well by the guitars. Musically as well the track works very well and although maybe a little quiet in places the drums and guitars seem to compliment each other well and keep the faster pace of the track moving along. If this isn   t a future single I   d be very surprised. With only 2 tracks of the album to go,    Somewhere A Clock Is Ticking   , which actually slows the pace down again a little. But from the opening notes of the guitar it starts well and the vocals come in quite quickly to accompany it. The slow start builds up nicely as the track goes on and the backing vocals accompanying the lead again adds a little something to the track. The lyrics again are well written and the changes from the quieter sections of the track to the louder parts are done very well, all of which helps to make this one of the better albums of the year so far. The final official track on the album and also the longest    Same    is another mellower track that opens with a piano loop and the vocals coming in shortly afterwards. The slow pace is carried on as the drums and guitars come in to lead the song along. The correlation between the drums, guitars and vocals really make the song what it is. The vocals mixed with good quality lyrics really round off a good track. However when I say it   s the longest track, that   s because they leave a couple of minutes of dead CD time, which is something that really annoys me on albums. The reason for this couple of minute gap is a couple of UK only bonus tracks, both of which are very good, but I   ll let you find that out for yourself if you buy the album. Overall it   s the best album from the band so far and that   s not normally something that can be said for a third album. The sound really goes back to the mid 90   s and captures the best parts from a lot of recent Scottish bands, Idlewild, Travis et all. It   s certainly one I   d recommend although if your not keen on    Run    then I   d advise against it. Available from www.cd-wow.com for    8.99     ', '    I first heard of Snow Patrol about six months ago, as they were a band that had been championed by the same people who had previously championed Belle   Sebastian.  I expected when the album came out therefore, something of the B S ilk: tuneful, lively, and with songs interspersed with piano, woodwind and strings.What it turned out ot be is an album sounding a little like an early nineties guitar band.Don t get me wrong, Snow Patrol are a good band, and Final Straw is a resonable breakthrough album.  It isn t however, my particular favourite cup of tea.There s a little too much jingly-jangly guitars for my liking, and although the lyrics are thoughtful and often clever, in my opinion they do not project through the music - which sounds like it s all been done before.  The most notable pieces on the album, for me, are the commercial  Run  and  Spitting Games , and although there are no tracks that I feel the need to skip past on my car stereo, there are none either that I want to rewind and play over again. It s good background driving music, but the CD will stay in my car.If you are into guitar based Brit-Pop (such as Travis, The Coral or Starsailor), you ll warm to this album quickly.If you re into anything harder, pop or dance, this will probably not be your sort of thing. ', '    This makes the 22nd review on Ciao on this album.  What can I possibly have to say that hasn t already been said, and probably far better ?  I m no good at all that technical description stuff - can t tell a bass guitar note from a drum machine. So the answer is quite possibly, I can add nothing.  However, it hasn t deterred me from wanting to write a review on it.  Quite simply, this album is one of the best I have heard for years so I really wanted to put pen to paper and share it with you. ~ BAND BACKGROUND ~The band was formed back in 1994, by two young students from Northern Ireland studying at Dundee University - Gary Lightbody (vocals and guitar) and Mark McClelland (bass and keyboards).  Originally intending to call themselves Polar Bear, they swiftly renamed themselves Snow Patrol after a threatened lawsuit from ex Jane s Addiction guitarist Eric Avery who had already earmarked the name.  Whilst touring in their hometown of Belfast, the duo signed up the third member of their band - Johnny Quinn (drums).  A record deal swiftly followed and their first album  quot;Songs for Polar Bears quot; was released on the newly formed Jeepster label in 1998.  A second album followed in March 2001  quot;When It s All Over We Still Have To Clear Up quot;.  Neither album did huge things chart wise and when the relationship with Jeepster broke down, Snow Patrol moved on.  The third album  quot;Final Straw quot; was two years in the writing and was eventually released by Polydor in 2003.  By this stage, the Snow Patrol line up was complete in the form of its fourth member, Nathan Connolly (guitar).~ FINAL STRAW ~So really - what s so good about  quot;Final Straw quot;? Well it was nominated for the Mercury Prize as album of the year and it s been described as  quot;Something special quot; by The Times and  quot;A musical masterpiece quot; by the Sunday Post. For me it is quite simply a collection of some of the best music I ve heard in years. ', '    At the time of this albums release in 2003, many people thought Snow Patrol were a  new  band and that this album was their debut. In fact,  Final Straw  is the third offering from the band who formed at Dundee University ten years previously, although most members hail from Northern Ireland, including the band s frontman and lyric writer, Gary Lightbody.I discovered Gary Lightbody in 2001 when he formed Scottish Indie band  Reindeer Section  as a sideline, consisting of members of Idlewild, Belle   Sebastian and Teenage Fanclub amongst others. This prompted me to listen to Snow Patrol s second album, the 2001 release  When It s All Over We Still Have To Clear Up . A decent album, but sadly did not give the band the recognition they were seeking. So it was back to the drawing board and in 2003, after changing label and producer, the band finally achieved success with the release of  Final Straw .Produced by Jacknife Lee who has produced albums for U2 and REM amongst others, Final Straw saw the band come up with a more layered sound. In short, it s basically descriptive of what people accuse groups of doing when they switch to a major label from a smaller one, but personally although I prefer their cleaner sound here, I do believe that the band retain some of their original sound to keep fans of their earlier work happy.Tracks :-1. How to Be Dead2. Wow3. Gleaming Auction4. Whatever s Left5. Spitting Games6. Chocolate7. Run8. Grazed Knees9. Ways   Means10. Tiny Little Fractures11. Somewhere a Clock is Ticking12. SameThe most recognised track is the album s centrepiece  Run  which was later covered by Leona Lewis. As a fan of the original, I cringe when I hear her version, though it did ensure many sought out the original, thus giving the song a new popularity. I am not against cover versions - Roxy Music s  Jealous Guy  I actually prefer to the original - but Leona Lewis s version of  Run  does nothing for me, though I accept the girl can certainly sing. Run  was probably destined to be the anthem it has become. Along with  Chasing Cars  from the bands subsequent album, the two songs see the crowds singing along from start to finish when the band play live. I saw Snow Patrol here at Newcastle Arena last year and Gary Lightbody appeared humbled by the reaction to these two songs, as well as noting there were a few watery eyes in the crowd. It must be an amazing feeling to see something you have written, move people in that way. Run  is indeed one of the best tracks on the album, the emotional lyrics such as : quot; You ve been the only thing that s right in all I ve done quot; reach out and touch your soul, as the song builds slowly to its powerful chorus and instrumental break towards the end, before it comes back down and ends in the mellow way it began. How To Be Dead , is a good choice for the opening track as it manages to bridge the gap between old and new Snow Patrol perfectly and paves the way perfectly for the rest of the album. One of the quieter tracks and also one of my favourites here, it is nonetheless strong, as the bands new fondness for big sound past the halfway point features again as Lightbody tells of the frustration and hesitancy of an argument, where one side is pleading for a chance to be heard :  quot;You ve not heard a single word I have said... quot;What comes next, is a block of tracks leading up to  Run  which starts with  Wow  featuring layers of guitar and also some distortion familiar to their earlier work, which also seems to be repeated on the next two tracks,  Gleaming Auction  and  Whatever s Left . Whilst solid enough and featuring some interesting moments such as the slide guitar effect on  Gleaming Auction  I do tend to think of the latter two of these tracks as filler.I particularly enjoy the lyrical theme running throughout the album, which in turns gives the sense of abandoning all hope of love and then offering a tentative sense of optimism. The brilliant  Spitting Games  with its strong guitar and drums, embracing both, as Lightbody tells of  quot; Lonely written words for company quot; and also the poetic :  quot;My heart is bursting in your perfect eyes quot;. Chocolate  is another of my favourites. Containing the lyrics which give the album its title, it s catchiness sticks in your mind, along with its stop/start feature. Although upbeat, the lyrics again tell of mistakes, self-reflection and promises as  quot;A simple mistake starts the hardest time, I promise I ll do anything you ask...this time quot;I loved the accompanying video for this even though it was quite ironic when contrasted with the lyrics. Set in New York, it features an hourglass counting down and signifying the end of the world as everyone begins to panic. When the song has ended, Lightbody inverts the hourglass and throws everyone into a second panic. It remains one of my favourite videos.The end section of the album throws up a couple of great tracks : the understated  Grazed Knees  and the brilliant, atmospheric  Somewhere A Clock Is Ticking  adding a more melancholy feel.Whilst there aren t any tracks I dislike, there are one or two which can be described as filler. The standout tracks here more than make up for any weaker moments though.Above all, the utter helplessness felt at times in Lightbody s lyrics are expressed perfectly when he sings them and contrast well with the albums more upbeat moments. His words pick you up, then gently put you back down again. The raw quality of his voice adds so much to the songs.Snow Patrol are invariably compared to Coldplay and it is easy to see why. I do like Coldplay also, but the humble appeal and expression of Gary Lightbody appeals to me more than Chris Martin. Whilst Lightbody has certainly grown in confidence since this album and enjoyed increasing success with subsequent releases, Snow Patrol have never shown any signs of arrogance or taking things for granted and I am pleased their  final straw  began to give them the success they deserve.*Review also appears on dooyoo under same user name     ', '    Snow Patrol: Final StrawReleased: 2003 on Polydor RecordsSnow Patrol are an alternitive rock band that hail from Northern Ireland/Scotland.The band formed in 1994 going by the name Shrug, by members Gary Lightbody and Mark Mcclelland while they were studying at the University of Dundee and played gigs at the Uni and local bars and pubs. In late 1995 they changed their name to Polarbear but had to change this as it was being used by another artist, a friend of the band had always dubbed them Snow Patrol while they were officiallly named Polarbear so it seemed logical to go with this name, so in 1997 the band we know as Snow Patrol began their long journey to the top. It was in 1997 that a permanent drummer was found, Johnny Quinn from Northern Ireland, and the band were signed to Jeepster, an independent record label and released 2 albums,  songs for polarbears  in 1998 and  when its all over we still have to clean up  in 2001, and though these albums were critically aclaimed, commercialy they were failures and the band were dropped by jeepster. At this point a new guitarist joined the band Nathan Connolly and the band were signed to polydor records.With this came the release of the bands first album under Polydor,  final straw  in 2003, and what an album it is. I remember the first time i came across snow patrol, i had being living with a friend and he came home one day and said i have to listen to this album he bought, so he put it on, got us a couple of beers and we sat and listened from start to finish, the first 6 tracks i was really impressed with, especially  how to be dead ,  spitting games and  chocolate .............then track 7 started.........a track called  run .........WOW, this was possibly one of the greatest songs i have ever heard, the lyrics, the bass, the vocals, the lead guitar, it was all perfect..........i always say that an album with just one classic on is worth buying, well this had 11 fantastic tracks on and 1 that has to be one of the greatest songs of all time.There aren t many people who haven t heared  Run , but if you haven t i urge you to buy this album for this track alone.Final Straw is just one of those defining albums, i will always remember the first time i heard it and will never get bored of listening to it, this truley is a classic.FINAL STRAW TRACK LISTINGHow To Be DeadWowGleaming AuctionWhatever s LeftSpitting GamesChocolateRunGrazed KneesWays   MeansTiny Little FracturesSomewhere A Clock Is TickingSameWe Can Run Away Now They re All Dead And Gone (UK Bonus Track)Half The Fun (UK Bonus Track) Summary: A CLASSIC ALBUM THAT CONTAINS POSSIBLY THE GREATEST SONG OF ALL TIME  RUN THIS REVIEW IS ALSO POSTED ON DOOYOO BY ME UNDER THE SAME USER NAME     ', '       Final Straw    is the 3rd album from Snow Patrol and was released on 2nd February 2004.  Although it is their third album it is the first album that has any significant commercial success through the popularity of singles such as    Run    and    Chocolate   .The band is made up of four members: Gary Lightbody on vocals, guitar, keys and glockenspielNathan Connolley on GuitarMark McClelland on Bass and keyboardJonny Quinn on DrumsTrack List1. How To Be Dead2. Wow3. Gleaming Auction4. Whatever   s Left5. Spitting Games     Released as a single 12/07/20046. Chocolate     Released as a single 12/04/20047. Run     Released as a single 26/01/20048. Grazed Knees9. Ways   Means10. Tiny Little Fractures11. Somewhere A Clock Is Ticking12. SameBonus Tracks13. We Can Run Away Now They   re All Dead And Gone14. Half The FunI, like many others, bought this CD on the back of    Run   .  I do a lot of commuting and as a consequence of this listen to a lot of radio.  This song was really pushed by the stations I was listening to and while I was not instantly a big fan of it, over the course of several miles it grew on me to the point where I was prepared to buy the album.As with the single, the first couple of times I listened to the album I was not convinced.  On the surface, this album sounds a lot like the material released by Coldplay and Travis over the last 5 years.  Given the success of these bands over that period, this shouldn   t be considered a bad thing, but it did lessen the impact this album had of me.  Having resisted the temptation to simply add this CD to the pile and not listen to it again for a couple of years, I have really grown to like this album.There are very few week tracks on this album.  Obviously, not very track would stand up as a single as    Run    and    Chocolate    have done, but as album tracks, they are good songs.  The style of the album is very much in line with the singles that have been released, so if you like    Run    and    Chocolate    then you will like this album.There have been lots of comparisons made between Snow Patrol and various other bands.  At times in this album there are bits of Idewilde, Coldplay, Travis and Radiohead style lyrics coming through.  What remains constant is the emotion and the power of the lyrics and the fact that the tracks tend to be focused on soft lyrics and guitars.One of my favourite tracks on the album is    Grazed Knees   .  This is a very subtle song.  The lyrics are soft and the music softer.  It is a very relaxing track.  I love it.The only thing that I can find on this album that I really don   t like is the ending to    Same   .  The song itself is around 4 minutes long, yet the track on the CD is nearly 7 minutes long.  Once the song finishes there is a 3-minute silent pause.  I know a lot of bands have done this over the year and added another song after the pause.  On this album there is no other track at the end of the pause.  I tend to listen to CD   s on shuffle or random so it is really annoying for me when I am faced with a 3-minute pause.  Also, on the special edition version, there are two bonus tracks so even if you listen to the album in order, you have to sit through the pause before the bonus tracks.  Obviously, you could use skip and this is a small feature but it is something that I just don   t like.If you are a Snow Patrol fan from before their rise to fame then I (as yet) haven t heard any previous material so can t tell you how this album compares.  Having grown to like this album I will definitely be checking out their older material.  This is an album that you make not like immediately, but if you are a fan of similar music or the singles and are prepared to give it a couple of listens before making judgement then I   m sure you will like it.     ', '    I first heard of Snow Patrol on the local radio at home at Christmas of 2003.  I had been away at university for 3 and a half months and I hadn t listened to Xfm for months so I wasn t as up on new music as I like to be.  I heard this and was gutted to be going back to Leicester.  However, when back in Leicester I constantly nagged my girlfriend that there were a few bands that were great and should make it on the basis of their quality.  These were one, and thankfully they have started to gain recognition.I wasn t aware that this was their third album until recently but this should not be put against them - Blur became much bigger after the release of their third album (a certain Parklife).  Also, a bit of a random fact, the lead singer is the only man that Colin (from Colin and Edith on Radio 1) has ever snogged...Anyway, on to the songs:1.  How To Be DeadA gentle intro that warns you they are capable of nice melodies that leave you humming their songs even if you haven t heard it for ages.  Certainly a nice introduction but obviously written as such, as it would never be a single.2.  WowNow I like this song.  It has a slightly desperate tone to it and the line  If it looks like it works and it feels like it works then it works  is a line that I love and has been stuck in my mind for ages.  It is reasonably fast so if you have only ever heard Run from this band then hearing this song will relieve you from worrying that they would only be capable of playing slow songs as some British bands of the last 5 to 7 years are guilty of.3. Gleaming AuctionAnother strong song, probably best remembered for it s very simple yet effective guitar riff.  A reasonably fast song that has a verse with little guitar playing other than small tapping which contrasts nicely to the chorus which is rich and heavy.  A very abrupt ending.4.  Whatever s LeftSimilar to Gleaming Auction in that it contains light (although not quite so light as the guitar contains more gain and bass) guitar tapping on the verses and a much thicker chorus.  This time there is not so much of a guitar lick (if it can be called that) as a memorable part of the chorus.  However, it is replaced by the lead and backing singing of the line  You must know that I ll follow you .  Once again, however, it is a strong song which fits the singers voice well.5.  Spitting GamesQuite a light sounding song about trying to attract girls e.g  i find it easier to sit and stare, than push my limbs on towards you right there.  My heart is bursting in your perfect eyes, as blue as oceans and as pure as skys .  The theme may not be original and you may have heard the  blue as oceans  phrase a few times but at least it is done well.  Spitting Games reminds me of The Boo Radleys with this light and summery guitar song.6.  ChocolateI believe this is the new single, as I heard it played on Radio 2 this morning (more my mum s choice of radio station than my own but never-the-less it still plays the odd quality song).  Now I think this is another good song not least because it has a thumping drum beat.  Has there ever been a bad song with a thumping drum beat? The Doves  Pounding and The Stone Roses  I am The Resurrection are other fine examples.  Also contains the chorus where the name of the album comes from.  I doubt it will make number 1 but a very good song regardless.7.  RunThe song that brought this band to prominence, certainly in my eyes.  Funny, in ways this song doesn t really fit in with the rest of the album.  It is beautiful, haunting and exciting in one.  The verse echos of a weak man under the spell of love only to come to a chorus full of spirit and determination even in adversity.  A song full of emotion that fits the strong Irish accent well.  The best part is when it goes into the guitar instrumental, which doesn t really prove they are the best at their instruments but this song really wouldn t have been good with a Dan Hawkins from the Darkness solo.  The violin ending is good and fitting.8.  Grazed KneesA quiet song comprised of finger-picking guitar, violins and harmonic singing with only light drumming.  After the fantastic Run, this was a perfect song to follow.  It continues the slow theme well.9.  Ways   MeansA third slower song, but this picks up the pace and uses guitars and violins in a way that reminds me of The Verve pre-Urban Hymns.  A great song in that it fits the eery violin playing on the beat with guitar effects and a loud chorus.  10.  Tiny Little FracturesNot like the last three, this song is proud to be a typical guitar song of era 1994.  It is refreshing to get back to this after the slower songs and you can imagine jumping in a crowd to this at their gig with everyone shouting  waaooaaaooaaaooww yeah  11.  Somewhere A Clock Is TickingA great song that emphasises their ability to write a decent slow track.  Reminds me of a Coldplay type of track in that it makes you sit back and think.  Uses the backing singer as a second singer in a small capacity and is a nice song to just sit back and listen to. This song may or may not get released but if it doesn t you should be buying the album to get this.12.  SameA slow song again, this time using piano.  Once again competing in the same musical market as Coldplay.  A really good song to end, although I thought Somewhere A Clock Is Ticking could have been equally as good.  It retains the tradition for strong slow songs that are good to listen to whether in the background or as part of relaxation.There are also two bonus tracks on some editions.  This is a really good album that is definately worth buy.  It may not be the most original album but it s tracks are consistently strong and the positions of the songs are perfect.  The generally quick starting songs are slowed down by the excellent Run, which is followed by two more great slow songs.  The pace is picked up again and ends with two slow songs that are different in approach to Run etc.  Definately an album to buy      ', '    Snow Patrol have been around since 1994, beginning life under the name of  Shrug , later changing their name to  Polar Bear  before finally becoming Snow Patrol due to the name  Polar Bear  also being used by the side project band of the bassist from Jane s Addiction. Having said that, there is nothing on this album that I feel is not deserving of a place here as each and every single one of the tracks is beautiful both in it5646051', '    By the time Final Straw was being recorded, Snow Patrol were fed up. After releasing two albums that had been met with a general feeling of    nobody cares    by critics and the public alike, they were on the verge of splitting up. Although loved by their fanbase, and popular within musical circles, they decided that if Final Straw failed then that would be it; Snow Patrol would split up and be no more. Lead singer Gary Lightbody, guitarists Nathan Connolly and Mark McClelland, and drummer Jonny Quinn gathered together for what could be their last recording session ever, and went for broke.
