After years of being old fashioned and fuddy duddy, the Co-op has finally moved into the 21st century or at least I think they re trying.My local store offers a wide selection of magazines, books, CD s and newspapers which could compete with any newsagents. It has an off licence with great savings on booze and best of all it has a chemist right there in the store. This alone makes it number one for me. All other local chemist shops entail parking your car (which costs extra money) and possibly walking some distance once you leave your car. The Co-op chemist has great car parking facilities at no extra cost and whilst you are waiting for your prescription to be filled you can do your shopping. The food selection has improved greatly as has the instore bakery. The deli isn t the best I ve shopped in but you can t have everything. The staff are polite, friendly and extremely helpful but the real icing on the cake is the blood pressure monitor placed strategically near the entrance/exit of the store so that you can check your blood pressure after you have seen how much you have spent  Good or what   Honestly, if you haven t been to a Co-op for years try one I don t think you will be disappointed.      ', '    I feel no  quot;pity quot; for America, I feel no  quot;pity quot; for G.Bush or American Politician. I feel immense sorrow for the friends, Family, and all those who are directly affected by the loss of lives in this Tragedy. America supply s weapons to the Israel s who then murder innocent Arabs with them. So why are people shocked to see  quot;Arabs quot; dancing with joy when America gets attacked. For people to hate America enough to be willing to kill themselves and thousands of others just to vent this anger shows that the American government needs to review it s policy s on international conflicts. There is no excusing what the terrorists have done, but then people only do such things when desperate, and only in the hope it will improve things. I personally can see no way in which killing 5000 people can improve anything, but then surely that shows just how desperate these people were. I realise this is not going to be a popular opinion, yet I feel it needs to be said, for if America doesn t change some of it s polices then these people will get as desperate again sometime and another tragedy of this size could be the result.I hope, despite what G.Bush has said about those harbouring being as guilty as those who did it, I really hope, that America doesn t simply revenge blood with blood.     ', '    Co-op is a store that I only use to buy the small products, the main reason is because the prices are high and I don  8217;t always find that I find everything their as sometimes products are not their or have not been stocked up. I  8217;m not slagging the Co-op store off, as they probably are really good but this one, isn  8217;t the best. The majority of the times there are products missing, which is a little annoying.They employ teenagers who chat amongst themselves, and when it comes to paying at the checkout, out of all the places to pay, only one is open, which means you have to queue for ages before your turn. On the plus side, the store is useful for products that you forgot to buy from the supermarket or you need urgently. I would recommend you don  8217;t do all your shopping here, as it would cost you quite a bit. You  8217;ll find one of the supermarkets to be cheaper than this store.     ', '    our local has just been refurbished- and badly. they usually have two electric sliding doors operating, but they ve blocked one off, for no apparent reason, with a basket stand. their own brand food is dire, especially the bread, which is like eating recycled cardboard. the shop now looks like a cheap, dodgy discount warehouse, and for quite a while had no proper roof. the staff are mainly 16 year olds, who obviously would rather be anywhere else but in that shop. co-op : pull your socks up AS AN EXTRA NOTE, A DUDE NAMED MASCARASNAKE [ HELLO] HAS TOLD ME TO BE A BIT MORE OPEN- MINDED IN MY REVIEW AND TO TAKE INTO ACCOUNT THE CO-OPS SERVICE AIMED AT THE WORKING CLASS SAYS HE. HE SYMPATHISES WITH MY LACK OF CONSIDERATION AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE CO-OPS HISTORY AND ITS OBJECTIVES- HE BLAMES MY LACK OF UNDERSTANDING ON MY AGE. BUT THIS is ABOUT OUR OPINIONS- WE RE NOT HERE TO ADVERTISE. I MAY NOT HAVE BEEN VERY CONSTRUCTIVE IN MY OPINION, BUT I ONLY SPEAK A TRUTH, AND WHY WOULD IT BE INTERESTING TO READ A FACTUAL OPINION, ANYWAY?THANKYOU FOR LISTENING, DON T MEAN TO OFFEND- TA-RA        ', '    It is really incorrect to place a single heading  quot;Co-op quot; for all the co-ops in the UK. The Co-Op is a co-operative society which, to put it simply, the people who shop there own, and the more you shop there the more of it you own. let me explain.There are many hundreds of co-operative societies. Some are co-operatives for farmers, some are manufacturers co-operatives, some are retailers co-operatives and the list goes on. The Co-op to which this opinion refers is a food co-operative of which there are many different ones in the UK, for example Yorkshire Co-op, Lancashire Co-op, Manchester Co-op, Scotland Co-op but these do not have a monopoly in the area, for example Yorkshire Co-op covers all of Yorkshire and parts of Lancashire, yet Leeds (within Yorkshire) has a co-operative aswell (the aptly named Leeds Co-op) yet Yorkshire Co-op still operates within Leeds. My opinion is on the Yorkshire Co-op which is the one that serves me.The Co-op does not have a wide selection of goods like Morrisons or tesco s, and nor are their prices so keen, however they do  quot;Fairtrade quot; items which are things like chocolate and coffee which are fair to the workers in Economically less developed countries which produce the coffee bean or the cocoa or whatever. The result is slightly more expensive but more ethical products.Now when you shop at the Co-op, if your purchase is over I think it is    1, then you will be asked if you want your stamps (if not, ask for them). I am not sure on how many stamps to the    1 or whatever, but each stamp you receive (in either  quot;5 quot; or  quot;40 quot; units) is effectively a share certificate in your Co-operative society (some societies use a card and the  quot;stamps quot; are loaded onto that). You then stick those stamps into your stamp book which are located at the bottom of each till and then you can  quot;spend quot; that stamp book in a Co-op store. In Yorkshire, the completed stamp book is worth    1 at a Sunwin department store (the Yorkshire Co-operative s department store) or    2 at a Sunwin motors. However, if you get these stamps on triple-stamp days and redeem them on double-book days, they are then effectively worth six times as much as the stated value, and your quids in  And in case you  8217;re wondering, yes, this is pretty similar to a store  8217;s loyalty card except as the Co-op makes no money, you get it all back as opposed to say the Tesco  8217;s Clubcard where the shareholders make the money. If you shop at the Co-op, you  8217;re a shareholder. If you shop at Tesco  8217;s you  8217;re a customer.And, in case you  8217;re wondering, if you buy something (eg a TV) in a Sunwin department store, yes you do get your stamps for it So   8211; do I recommend shopping at the Co-op? Yes, I do but not for your weekly shop but if you run out of something then they  8217;ll probably have an equivalent one that  8217;s fair to the cocoa workers. Or something.Ciao      ', '    I was always a regular at Sainsburys when we got a bit financially tight, so we decided to try our local Co-Op. To my surprise we found it to be very good, alougth the range of foods isn t so large with no fresh meat or fish counter we still manage to get everything we need for our weekly shop, they sell meat off the shelf and a limited amount of fish, and they have a bakery and deli counter, but what we noticed was the price our weekly shopping used to come to around    70 but it rarely goes above    35 now and we also get 5  back on Co-Op goods when you join their loyalty card the Co-Op Dividend.All in all it s worked out very well for us and it s well worth us doing our shopping there.     ', '    Have you overdone it this Christmas? alwats searching for a diet that works for you? Kelloggs Cereals are starting their 2 week challenge again on January 8th. This challenge involes eating a bowl of Kelloggs cereal with skimmed milk for breakfast and then another bowl for lunch or dinner for 2 weeks. If you can meet this challenge then you should be able to lose up to 6lbs. in 2 weeks. This has been tested by nutritionists at Queen Margaret University College in Edinburgh. Kelloggs ran this challenge last summer. There is an associated website at www.2weekchallenge.co.uk Why not make it one of your new year resolutions ?     ', '    As a student I have a Part-time job at the local Co-op store in Frinton,   8220;Frinton Fiveways  8221;.  It  8217;s not exactly classed as a supermarket but it has a fine range on food for the customers to choose from.Recently the Co-op has started to close down its in-store butcher  8217;s service, and yesterday, Frinton Fiveways had its Butchers made redundant   8211; the job no longer existed.This now means that all meat produce will be prepared and packaged off site in Thetford where it will then be loaded onto lorries and delivered to the various Co-ops.I would say that it is unfortunate that the Co-op has had to lose the butchery workforce. I wrote to the nice Co-op peeps and they sent me a list of everything that they stock that is Vegan  Even better than that they have a little green box thingy on all their own brand stuff that tells you that it is Veggie or Vegan. Luckily I live only 2 miles from a small town, that has facilities such as doctors, newsagents, post office, hairdressers, DIY shop, and a supermarket called Rainbow food store.Rainbow is part of the Co-op chain, and to be honest it is definitely not the lowest priced supermarket, and they don t tend to sell a big range like the larger supermarkets. In January my local Rainbow, underwent a serious refurbishment, the main reason for this is that the former army barracks are being converted into low priced starter homes. Therefore, the supermarket had to expand in order to cope with the extra demand.Rainbow expanded it s floor space, by about a quarter of the original size, they upgraded the out of date tills, installed five extra checkouts, put in a new Deli counter, installed a separate news stand. They started to introduce household items, such as toys, gardening equipment, tools, electrical goods, and a well stocked supply of the latest books, videos, CD s and some budget prices PC games and software.They even put in separate Ladies, Gentleman s, and Disabled toilets.The outside was also upgraded, the pothole filled car park was re-surfaced with tarmac, new lighting was put in, and extra parking spaces were created, included five disabled spaces, and new trolleys were brought.You would imagine that the prices soared after all this work, but they didn t. In fact, they introduced many special offers, on everyday products. At the moment, there are quite a few special offers. For example, all videos in a basket are    2.99, and CD s are    1.99. There are many buy one, get one free deals, on Virgin Cola, Smoked Ham, Mighty Strong Cheddar, Pork Pies, Rathbones Bread, Bacon, Cod Portions, Scones, Pasta, Felix Cat Food, Strongbow Cider, Crunchie Ice Cream Bars and many more. There is also money off lots of items.With today s rising petrol prices, Rainbow have introduced a petrol saving scheme, if you spend over    50 on groceries you will receive a voucher from the cashier, offering you 4p off per litre of petrol. This voucher can be redeemed at the adjacent Rainbow filling station.They also have a Christmas saving scheme, where you can purchase saving stamps, and if you cash the stamps, in December you will receive    2 worth of stamps free.Since the refurbishment, the range of groceries has dramatically increased, the freezer selection is good, there is quite a range of organic foods, and even specialised East Anglian foods. Obviously, Rainbow could never rival the big well-known supermarkets, but you will be surprised at what they have to offer.When you shop at the big supermarkets, that personal service is gone, but Rainbow has still retained that friendly, personal service, that is now hard to find.If you have a Rainbow near you, why not pop in, and see what you think. I m sure you will find it a pleasant experience, and who knows you might pick up a bargain.     ', '    I don t live near any big supermarkets, so anything I ve forgotten I have to get at a Co-op - big mistake.  It isn t the fact that they re expensive, or badly stocked, or even their range of goods isn t large - it s the staff.  These people are nice enough but have had no training whatsoever.  Who would put an under 18 year old at the alcohol checkout?I bought some parsnips in there once (hubby had to have them ) and for 2 reasonable sized ones it cost me over two pounds - how can that be justified?However, it is the convenience or where they are that takes me back to them - how often do people forget things or nip to the shop for a packet of ciggies and end up buying more?Of course - I could be better organised, but as I mentioned before, it s not the price.     ', '    The co-op is a class supermarket. What people have to remeber is that the coop was teh creator of the so called super market. I work for the coop part time and as an employee i am treated very well. I m a student but still i am entitles to sick pay and holiday pay. Maybe we can t compete with Tesco and asda prices but we are still a quality supermarket branch. If you’re weighing up whether Co-op hits the sweet spot between ethics, quality, and price, here’s a no-nonsense breakdown. Co-op stands out for its genuine commitment to ethical policies—no irradiated foods here, and a solid backing of fair trade produce. For shoppers like us who care about where our food comes from and how it impacts communities, that’s a big tick. Plus, their environmental efforts, like using degradable plastic bags and supporting local causes, show they’re not just paying lip service.

Price-wise, Co-op plays the middle game. It’s not the cheapest on the block, but you won’t be paying premium supermarket prices either. Essential items are generally reasonably priced, and their fresh meat, dairy, and hot food options often come with competitive pricing compared to the big players. That said, some products can be pricier than at larger chains, so it pays to keep an eye out and compare. On the bright side, their frequent special offers—BOGOF and half-price deals—help stretch your pound further, especially when combined with their dividend card and saving stamp schemes.

Quality-wise, Co-op’s own brand products often surprise with better taste and higher quality than many rivals’ equivalents. They also clearly label dietary options, which is a boon if you’re vegan, vegetarian, or have other specific needs. Customer service tends to be friendly and helpful, making shopping a less stressful experience, and their refund and replace policy adds a layer of reassurance if something doesn’t meet expectations.

What really sets Co-op apart is its community spirit. Unlike many chains that shutter smaller stores for profit, Co-op keeps local shops open, supports local charities, and even offers free local delivery and personalized assistance. For anyone who values accessibility and a store that genuinely cares about its neighborhood, this is a rare find.

In summary, Co-op offers a balanced mix of ethical sourcing, decent pricing, and community focus, though you might want to shop around for the best deals on certain items. If you appreciate a supermarket that’s more than just a place to buy groceries—one that aligns with your values and supports local communities—Co-op is worth a serious look.

', '    well i have to be honest, i do not use safeway that often, but when i do, i have to say the offers they have on are very impressive.Ok let me start by talking about the shop itself.The one near us, here in Lincoln, is in a very good place, it is not so close as to other supermarkets, but it is near 2 big Living Estates, which is a good thing, as a lot of people will not want to go far for there weekly shopping, so they have a simple 2 minute journey to get there. Often the best comes with    desensitisation    work, that is helping people overcome their anxieties by gradual exposure to their problems, in my line of work usually the community.. This could be going to the supermarket, caf   , using the bus or even a walk in the park. It is for this reason I find myself finding an inordinate amount of time in the Safeway in Fishponds in Bristol. However my service user is now at the point where she can go around the supermarket on her own and I can go and sit in the caf   , thus observing Safeway in its entirety.Lord alone knows what the staff think as this big 5    8   , bright red haired pierced woman trailed around this little old lady  At any moment I expected the security to come and clap me on the shoulder, accusing me of getting ready to pinch her handbag  But this way I get to observe her from a distance.The first impression I get whilst walking into Safeway   s, particularly this one, is one of complete and utter chaos  As you walk into the    foyer    you are greeted by a big panel of swipe machines (more about them later), a broken pay phone covered with sticker, a rack with a bike chained to it, and another rack with    free    magazines. Its crowing glory is stuck right in the middle and it   s a pile of bakery products, usually with a few empty packets as less than scrupulous people seem to regard them as a freebie as they leave. When you finally get into the supermarket it looks like an assault course  The dry cleaners/photo booth is to the right, alongside fridge units containing drinks, sandwiches, etc. To the left is a massive display of hot cross buns (a bargain at buy, one, get one, free), right in front of you is a huge rack and display of flowers, bulbs, and seed, etc. The ensuing crush usually reaches its peak at lunch times with the office workers coming in.But then you get past the hustle and bustle, its like stepping into an oasis of calm, clean wide aisles stretch in front of you, all see able clutter is behind you.Obviously all branches of supermarkets are different but this is a large store so the stuff in it has to be very typical. The fruit and veg section is quite varied with a small range of organic goods. What I   m beginning to really dislike are these open salad bars, and Safeway has a great one which includes a wide range of olives. Its just that people like to dip their fingers and taste the produce, as the toilets are by the entrance to the store I don   t know where they   ve been  Some covers would be appreciated As for the lazy buggers who cant be bothered to cook is a curry    bar   , freshly made pizza (not on site), and again the rotisserie which seems to be springing up in all stores. I   m always astonished at how my idea of a large chicken differs with theirs  They have a large delicatessen counters, which is sadly much underused. A large amount is taken up with exactly the same produce that is in the salad bar, they have some impressive pies though  The cheese counter is quite pitiful, a wider range would be appreciated, a much underused, valuable space. They do have an instore bakery, which makes better use of its space, a good range of breads and cakes can be found here. Unfortunately its not a continuous baking process like Asda so by the end of the day some of the bread can be a little too    crusty    Their little donuts with the chocolate covering are absolutely divine There is a good raw meat section, although they could probably do with a butchers in store, there are a lot of elderly people living in Fishponds and since the local butchers a lot of people come here, unfortunately all the produce is sold in packs of two or more, putting a lot of people off.There   s the usual cooked meat, cheese, yoghurt, etc. In fact there is everything you want to see and buy in a supermarket so it would be ridiculous just to list them all. So I   m going to talk about some more pertinent things you look for when you go shopping.Firstly prices and quality of their own brands. The prices I have to say are on a par with all supermarkets, except Somerfield who are more expensive. But it   s the bargains that are especially appealing  A 6 pack of Wotsits for 39p  An 18 pack of Walkers for 99p. 2 packs of Chicken Kiev   s for the price of 1  And the list goes on and on  These are a supermarket that does place a restriction of how many of the products you can buy at one time, its usually 3 though. But nonetheless its an excellent place for bargains. I have to be honest and say I only have limited knowledge of their own cheap brand, I   m not impressed, watery beans, toilet tissue is a bit scratchy,( at least it doesn   t fall apart in your hands ), but then I   m one of those people who prefer to pay the bit extra for what I know is a decent good.Next, the store itself, well you have these wonderfully bright bits, very neat, very clean and tidy, then you turn a corner or into an aisle, and its goes a bit crap  At the end of each aisle is the    bargains    that can be had, unfortunately they are usually piled up in their cardboard boxes, so the place ends up looking like a scrummage at Lidls. Some parts of the store are also completely neglected, with goods and seconds piled up, even Aldi wouldn   t stand for it  The checkpoint also look a bit of a muddled mess, with good piled up, and the cream and bright green of the checkpoints obviously don   t get cleaned very often so end up looking a bit grubby, in fact a lot of the store looks like it could do with a lick of paint and a good tidy  up  The cigarette counter is another such area, a lot of the shelves have things missing, and although its very popular usually only 1 cashier as other people there usually have reams of paper work spread out on it. Its also difficult to find the customer service desk because of all the crap piled up on it But of course, you could bypass all this by opting for the handheld swipe thingy, the idea behind this is that you would go around and swipe all the goods yourself, then go straight to the till and pay, thus cutting out all the queuing whilst poor other souls have to wait and some really slow cashier swipes the stuff for you, how this deters people from not paying for some of their goods I have no idea. So you   ve rushed round, swiped it all and then gone to the    special    till, just one problem. There is never anyone on thee tills, so you then have to get the attention of one of the customer service staff to come over and do it for you, sometimes these new gadgets just aren   t worth the bother The staff are either really helpful or just completely disinterested, Safeway has a fully inclusive recruitment policy which I support whole heartedly. The security is  very lacking though, you   d be hard pushed to find a security guard and when you do he   s usually got a mobile phone glued to his ear. I do find this quite surprising in an area like Fishponds, I don   t wish to generalise, but Fishponds doesn   t have the best reputation in the area, its also very close to some deprived area and the shoplifter do like to make a quite bus ride up to the place. It doesn   t help the local Social Security office is just down the road so when the junkies cant scam the money to buy drugs they just come up to Safeway to nick food and handbags to sell instead, never a good idea to let your bag out of your site.And lastly the caf   , the only really positive side to it is the staff who are really helpful. Unfortunately like the rest of the store, its beginning to look old and tired, certainly the windows that run alongside it don   t look like they   ve been washed in years, the tables and chairs are faded and many slightly wobbly. But it   s the food that is the piece de resistance..because its awful, I don   t mind a cup of coffee and a slice of cake, but there   s no way I   m setting a fork near that grey cottage pie and watery vegetables, I   d rather have a nice tub of poo infested salad  The staff do try and keep the tables nice and clean though, although a few extra mops of the floor wouldn   t go amiss I   m still not sure on Safeway   s, I don   t think I would go for the things that have been touched by other human hands, salad bar, deli etc and definitely not the cage. BUT the bargains sometimes outweigh my negative thinking, I wouldn   t do my weekly shopping here, but I   m happy to pop in to see what bargains they have. The best thing to do with this store, is close it down, refurbish and revamp the whole, and the brand new Lidls being built right next door its something they are going to have to think about pretty damn soon      ', '    Safeway supermarkets seem to be trying to brighten up their image and project themselves back onto the stage as serious players in the supermarket game.  Once the bastion of all that was bad with cheap and cheerful inner-city supermarkets now Safeway is presenting a more upmarket image.I have a Safeway store close to where I work (Barbican) and a new store has opened up where I live in Woking.Safeway s have ditched their loyalty card scheme (that went a year or so ago) ABC Card in favour of store-wide discounts that everyone is entitled to.  Along with this they have created for themselves a new, bright and exciting image.  Fresh fruit and veg are presented in lit barrow-type displays, butchers counters and deli-counters have been introduced along with expanded bakeries.  New take-away style food counters have been added selling pre-cooked chicken, ham and ribs, pizzas and oriental food.  The store in Barbican even has a sandwich counter where you can have your sandwiches made to order.  The atmosphere is now not at all down at heal and is instead much more pleasant.  There is a quality feel to the stores.Floor space in the stores is often limited (Barbican was never very big and the new Woking store is far from huge) and as a result available products are often limited.  Shelves are not stacked with row upon row of the same product, instead there is a little of everything.  Safeway have developed a system whereby if a product has truly run out they will add a dot to the bar code on the shelf, thus, if a product is not on display and there is no dot on the barcode, chances are they will have some  quot;out the back quot; and a member of staff will be more than happy to get it for you.The Woking store filled an immediate need in the community.  Whilst there is a branch of Sainsbury s in the town centre it is far from large and the large store is about 3 miles away.  Tescos have a store about 6-7 miles away.  The new Safeway, cited just outside the town centre, had to break into the established market and it has accomplished this with ease.The meat and fresh produce is far better that Sainsbury s.  I have yet to have a  quot;just OK quot; piece of meat, it has all been full of flavour and very fresh.  Safeway also stock less  quot;own-brand quot; products (although they do have a Savers range) and so you can often get some of the more obscure items here.The pricing policy is what really makes the difference and is far better that Sainsbury s or Tesco s.  Products are generally priced in line with competitors and are occasionally a penny or two more expensive.  However, there are around 30 or so products that are on offer every week at heavily discounted prices.  The discounted products are actually everyday items and not just the luxury stuff and so everyone benefits.  This week there is an offer on bananas at 39p/lb, eggs at 29p for 6 and Ski yoghurts at    1.50 off a 12 pack.  For beer lovers a 24 pack of Peroni comes at    10 off, and wine at    1-2 discount.  Fresh bread is often on buy one get one free and there are offers on frozen foods and cleaning products.  Purchases are limited to three per customer but they do not stop you going with another family member and buying 6 or going back the next day Store-wide promotions are run every now and again, we have just had one on Italy where there were major discounts on all Italian products and over the Bank Holiday weekend there has been a major promotion on alcohol     This is also the place to come for petrol.  The pump price is cheaper than any around and if you spend    40 in store you get a voucher for 5p off every litre of fuel valid for the next 7 days   Well worth it if you have a big tank.The Woking branch also has a restaurant attached to it and unlike many supermarket cafes this actually feels like a restaurant.  There is even live music and outside garden seating As the Woking branch was new and they wanted to attract custom there were a number of opening offers that were well worth it.  Free meals in the restaurant (we had dinner one Friday night, three courses for two people and it cost us    2.00 (the price of the drinks ) instead of the bill price of    30).  Bottles of wine, cases of cola (cans) and chocolates were all given away free with spends of    30 in the store.Customer service in second to none and if there is a price query (which has happened to me twice) I just got the item for free   On one occasion at the beginning there was a promotion on pre-cooked chicken which meant that it was cheaper than the uncooked version.  Only problem was they ran out of whole chickens so suggested that I have some chicken pieces instead for the same price.  When I got to the till I presented the voucher but noticed that I was charged the full price for the chicken less the discount on the voucher.  When I queried this I was told that the counter had made a mistake and that they were not authorised to do this.  I said that I did not want the chicken in that case and the manager authorised the voucher anyway so I got    2.50 off the bill.  On my way out of the store the manager came running after me and gave me the chicken that I hadn t bought by way of apology.  I got a free dinner and money off my shopping   Bargain Every week we get a leaflet drop on a Tuesday telling us what products are on offer starting the next day (Wednesday) - this makes planning a shopping trip easy Only complaint I have with the store is that they do have a very poorly laid out car-park which is too small to navigate if cars are travelling in opposite directions.  There is also a lack of trolley parks (although plenty of trolleys by the store).  The packing area at the end of the checkouts is also a little too small.  8230;oh yes, and they NEVER have a large box of regular Tampax I have switched to Safeway s for all my shopping now.  My bill is reduced and the produce is better.  I just hope it stays that way CLAIRE s BOTTOM TEN TIPS for grocery shopping1 - Make a list of what you want and stick to it, deviating only if you see something very good, or they are out of what you want - it will prevent your bill from escalating.2 - Use your freezer, it is often cheaper to buy fresh produce in larger quantities which can then be spilt and frozen.3 - Make the most of special offers, if your regular washing powder is on offer it won t go off so bulk buy.4 - Select produce with the latest sell/use by date it will be fresher.5 - Think what you are going to do with a product, if you want a beef stew no need to buy rump steak but if you want a steak don t get stewing steak.6 - Load the conveyor belt carefully so that you can easily separate your shopping.7 - Pack heavy items first to prevent damage.8 - Look out for money off coupons in papers and magazines and do fill in those shopper surveys as you will often be sent coupons as a thank-you.9 - Select frozen produce last and consider taking a cool bag to stop it melting.10 - Please be considerate - if you don t need them don t park in the disabled or child-friendly spaces, don t block the aisles with your trolley and don t barge  8230;.there s no food crisis yet Claire 300801     ', '    Since joining Ciao, I have written reviews all for 4/5 star products. This began the weekly fight for the special offers being ran instead. Meanwhile prices on other goods began to slowly climb. Not sure on Head Office s idea behind all this, did they think that we the shoppers were going to be too stupid to notice?I carried on shopping there, more out of loyalty and pure laziness than anything else. I DIDN T WANT TO BLOODY STEAL ONE...just do my shopping  lt;sobs gt;I have no idea why I didn t just abandon trolleys there and then and go home  Well actually I do...I felt this had the makings of a darned good review for Ciao ;-) I soldiered on...all in the name of consumer research of course  It was then I discovered the real reason they ve moved over to smaller trolleys...over half the shelves were empty. All in all, we didn t even fill the little trolleys. Heck we could have got away with just taking the one round. Now I m not blaming what I call the  front line  staff here. I personally blame the managers..wherever the hell they ve all cleared off to. I mean, if the stock isn t being ordered properly? ? ? ?  It s almost like they are deliberatly trying to run the shop out of business. I wonder if it has anything to do with them losing out to Tesco in the bids to build a new  superstore  in the town. All I do know is that right now it s like rats leaving a sinking ship. Even the customer telephone is broke, has been for weeks..with no sign of that ever being repaired/replaced. I m off to Morrison s. Yes it s further for me to go (it s around 4 miles away), but hopefully it will restore my sanity  Would I go back to shopping at Safeway? Not if you paid me a million lol     ', '    Before I start, I would like to say that I am an Asda fan, but as Safeway have a store right next to my house, I find myself in there a couple of times a week picking up the odd item, and to be honest, I can only afford to pick up the odd item, because excluding their weekly special deals (which I will come to later), Safeway are very very expensive, and the variety of products on offer from the likes of Asda and Tesco just cannot be rivalled by Safeway. Safeway would not dare do this, as they would have to tell some huge lies to make it look good. If you’re like me—someone who’s been around the Safeway block a few times—you’ll appreciate how this store has really stepped up its game. The fresh fruit, vegetables, and meat here consistently outshine competitors; I swear their apples last longer than my last relationship! Their produce isn’t just fresh; it’s the kind of quality that makes you want to cook something fancy instead of just grabbing a frozen pizza. And speaking of cooking, their expanded bakery and deli counters are a godsend for those “I forgot to meal prep” days, offering everything from crusty bread to ready-to-go meals.

Safeway’s layout remains that comforting, familiar maze where you don’t need a treasure map to find your favorite snacks. Plus, the store feels more upmarket now—like it’s had a little makeover and put on its Sunday best. This isn’t your run-of-the-mill supermarket anymore; it’s a pleasant, convenient place to shop, with a wide variety of products that cover everything from dry cleaning to electronics. Yes, electronics—because why not grab a new phone charger while picking up your groceries?

Customer service here deserves a shout-out. Staff are friendly, helpful, and often go the extra mile—like the time they resolved a price query in my favor without me even asking twice. Checkouts are usually well-staffed too, so you won’t be stuck in a line long enough to memorize the entire Safeway weekly leaflet (which, by the way, is a brilliant tool for planning your shopping and snagging those weekly bargains).

Now, not everything is perfect. Some loyalists grumble about the Morrisons takeover, feeling it’s a bit like inviting a new roommate who rearranges all your stuff. But honestly, the weekly discounts and the wide range of branded and obscure items keep me coming back. Safeway manages to balance quality, variety, and value in a way that feels both familiar and fresh—kind of like that reliable friend who’s always got a good deal up their sleeve.

product_reviews: ['    I started working for Morrisons about three months ago, but dont worry, im not going to bore you with a rant about how i hate my job, thats a whole other opinion, i am going to tell you a little more about the store. The store in question is in Stamford, Lincs, my humble town, we dont have a lot here, except estate agents and pubs (apparently there are over 50 pubs, not bad for a town with only 20,000 people ) but anyway back to the point, we have a very small tesco s on the High Street, and a very terrible Somerfield s just outside the centre, so as you can imagine, i, like most other Stamfordians choose to do my weekly punishment and good old Morrisons.The Car ParkObviously this is the first thing you notice when you drive in, it is very big and litter free, there is a Petrol station just as you come in, then the car park, then the store, there are 6 or 7 trolley bays which means you never have to go far to take it back, it also has the usual disabled and mother/toddler spaces situated closer to the store, next to the pick-up point, or  quot;i ll be quick, just need a lottery ticket quot; point and a motorbike space or two. The car park is almost always getting to be full, i go to work at 8 o clock, the store opens at 8 o clock and there are always at least 20 cars waiting, very strange i personally think, but hey ho. I dont myself drive but if i did im sure i would have no problems with the car park except maybe a lack of spaces at peak times.The StoreWhen you first walk in you enter a little foyer area, with a post box and some baskets, although not many people use these, there are also a couple of benches and a childs Noddy car or something.Then through the next automatic doors and you are into the store, sort of, there is a large cigarette and lottery kiosk and the paper section, very handy if that is all you need, then the entrance to the cafe on the right, and the store straight on.Through the automatic gate you go and straight into the world of flowers, a large selection of plants, flowers and other such accesories (baby bio etc), then we go onto the produce section, rows and rows of most types of fruits you can think of and probably never heard of, vegetables too, my trolley is still usually empty at this point :) On the right then is the fish bar, i love this place, as i love fish, there is a display of fish of the front of the counter covered in ice, and always looks good, you can see the staff working behind the counter gutting etc. and they are happy to help at all times, they sell all fish that i have ever wanted, and can order in most other things if they dont have it. Directly next to that is Salad bar, you know the things, made famous by Pizza Hut i think, four different sized boxes, i think most people do the same thing though which is to get the smallest box and try to fit the contents of a big box into it, saying that, i have just discovered that there is sellotape next to the counter to help, ingenious  Then past the potatoes and the pre-packed cakes we come to my department, the bakery, obviously the best department in the store as i work on it, the department has a large selection of loaves, baps, cobs, rolls and bloomers, some covered with all sorts of wonderful things, cheese and onion, sesame seed, poppy seed etc. There is also what is called the continental range, which is what i refer to as the yuppy bread, this includes the organic loaves, rye bread etc. There is also a large selection of muffins and doh-nuts, hand filled by me if you re lucky (or not so )Then we move around to cake shop, this is where they make all of the delicious yummy trats that i m not allowed, danish pastry, egg custard, flapjack, cookies, mousse, im getting hungry just thinking about it, lets move on quickly. Onto the Butchery department, on here they sell the main meats, chicken, turkey, lamb, pork and beef, you can buy a joint, a steak, a chop, diced virtually however you want it, they also sell weird stuff such as diced pigs liver and a variety of other things which im sure only people over a certain age like. Like the fish bar you can clearly see the butchers working, which is a refreshing sight, making sure they re not kicking it around the floor  Then the Oven fresh counter, this is where you get the hot chickens, sausage rolls etc, the chicken is very nice from here with a nice french stick and a tomato, yummy yummy, (i knew this op was a bad idea on an empty stomach), the  pastie  side of it sells a range of sweet and savoury pies. The chicken side of it sells, obvoiusly, the chicken, along with potato wedges, cooked ribs, cooked pork and even crackling.Then to my favourite department, the deli, first of all meat, ranging from hams to turkey all nicely sliced up and ready to eat, then the best bit, CHEESE    all sorts, edam, cheddar, gloucester and my favourite, smoked, the deli is quite pricey, but belive me, its worth it  All of the departments i have covered so far are reffered to as  Market Street , this is supposed to go back to when Sir Ken Morrison used to sell these products on his market stall all of those years ago, and try to offer a  Market place  under one roof. These departments all cover the sides and backs of the store, there is a row of freezers and fridges, which obviously stock everything from your pizza to your ice-cream, there is then a row of aisles which contain all of the rest of the stock, at the furthest end is all of the toiletries and shampoos etc, then things such as crisps, cereals, soups and biscuits until we nearly end back up at produce. But there is one more department, the audio bar, they sell the top 20 DVD s, Video s, PS2 games and Audio CD s all at very low prices, they are actually the cheapest place to buy these from in town, then opposite his there is the magazine rack, which houses almost every interest known to man   a small birthday card and paperback section and we re at the checkouts. I think there are about 40 checkouts in all, and on a Saturday, they are all open, there are 4 basket ones, two of which are cash only and wide for disabled people, then there are a few more wide access tills dotted around so you are likely to find one if you need it. Once you are through the checkouts you enter the cigarette area again and are free to leave, for another week at least  The CafeI don t go into the cafe much now, but did quite a lot as a student, they do a mean breakfast, all of the food is cheap, but you dont get that much, there is a good selection of kids meals, and they also stock a number of cakes, sandwiches that are made in the store, there are plenty of seats and a smoking area. Be warned though, it gets very busy, and i mean VERY busy, every Thursday they run coach trips for the pensioners to do their shopping (seriously), they always go into the cafe for a natter and a teacake, also Sundays, i went a couple of months ago and ordered a Sunday lunch, they said it would be about an hour and a half, i could nearly go round the shop, buy the stuff, go home and cook it in that time, but of course you can go around the shop while you are waiting.Overall the store is a very pleasant and friendly store, it gets very busy, i think its in the top three stores in the country for sales, which isnt bad considering the population of the town. On the notice boards we are told the number of offers available this week, it is 1800 this week, that is an awful lot of offers, every end of every aisle there are offers, there are promotional tables everywhere with buy one get one free stock on, my average shopping bill for me and my partner is    50 per fortnight, we save on average    15 each time with all of the offers.All of the staff, except me, are polite and are willing to help, there are plenty of managers lurking around aswell if you ever want to .. cough.. complain about anything. All in all a very good shop, i think the layout of our store, and certainly the offers, are pretty similar in every store, so if you havent already i suggest you give it a try.Thanks for reading, i know it was a slog, but we got the in the end  :)www.morrisons.co.uk , and ask for Ken       ', '    Morrison s is a chain of supermarkets with their head office based in Bradford.  As you might expect from a Yorkshire based company they offer a range of goods at competitive prices without all the frills of the  southern softies  such as Waitrose et al.Morrison s stores do not have bag packers for example, or valet parking or cloakroom attendants either.What they do offer is a wide range of products, not as wide as some others, no foie gras here but they do sell everything your average family would need or want.  The prices are very good and the special offers (3 for 2 etc) are frequent and on products which you would usually buy anyway.I recommend trying their own brand products which do offer excellent value and are also of reasonable quality.They do seem to struggle to recruit enough staff though, I recommend steering clear during peak hours, but then again the same goes for most supermarkets really.The salad bar and  pie man  shops are very good, a wide range of fresh items to choose from and they also sell freshly roasted chickens with different flavourings which makes a change.If you are looking for quality on a budget then try it.  If money is no object the send me some      ', '    i find morrisons always has what i want and are very friendly. i definately think thier meat is better than other places i.ve tried. fruit and veg are great quality and all in all i tend never to shop anywhere else when it comes to groceries. they always have buy one get one free from week to week on different items.they also have 50  extra free on certain items which is usuallydiffernt every week.and so with a family you get valued fresh goods and can save to.they have a great variety on houshold goods as well as childrens things and if you have a computer they running a graet deal on three packs of cdr s,plus other computer cartridged as well as paper etc     ', '           Where Are Morrisons? You will probably see Morrisons more frequently in your national tabloid paper or on the television more frequently than anywhere else as the advertise their 2 4 1 bargains with national celebrities such as Alan Hansen, Lulu and Gabby Logan, or in the paper with 2 shopping trolleys bulging with goodies, twice as many as their competitors.My local Morrisons is in Basingstoke. They are not as common a sight as Tesco or Sainsbury s and they do not have the smaller convenience stores over running the country, but they have superstores packed to the rafters with everything you could possibly need in your house hold shop and they are the 4th leading UK supermarket.My most recent experience of Morrisons and the one I write of was following a move into a new flat away from my parents. My flat mate and I took her car and went shopping. The Carpark. The Morrisons Carpark in Basingstoke is plenty big enough and there is always a choice of spaces when I attend. Unfortunately it is two way - something most supermarkets seem to be nowadays and in my opinion a ridiculously unsafe design. It is home to several shopping trolley bases where you can leave your trolley once emptied, instead of returning to the shop front. The Carpark is easily accessible from the major routes into Basingstoke and also features a large petrol station where you can collect petrol points amounting to a money saving coupon.The StorePrior to entering the store you will walk under a roofed section to collect a trolley. You will have the choice of a deep normal shopping trolley, a shallow smaller trolley or a basket. The deeper trolley s have child seats at the front. The trolley s are    1 each; refunded when you link the trolley back up at the end of your visit.The store is designed as most supermarkets are with the fruit and vegetable section immediately ahead of you once you enter the store. There is a tobacconist area to the left and toilet and baby changing facilities to the right. There is also a fish section next to the fruit and veg, something I despise and hurriedly rush past every time I go there.  WARNING:  you will be tempted with cake offers on entering the shop as stands are conveniently placed to draw your attention. However the cake section is further on and has much more choice.The aisles in Morrisons are wide enough to pass other trolleys or for wheelchair access and still enough room to manoeuvre a trolley round. The store is divided into two sections with an aisle down the centre and then aisles separating each row as well. On one side is the dry foods, toiletries, home essentials bread and cereals and at the far end the beverages both alcoholic and non alcoholic. On the other side is the frozen stuff, tinned food and books, CD, magazine and gifts section as well as party essentials.I have never been to Morrisons in Basingstoke where I have felt it was badly maintained or not clean. The aisles are always clutter free and the staff endeavour to make sure the items are in their correct locations.   Bargains all the way  Down the aisles, as well as the BOGOF items and there are plenty of them there are many items reduced and on offer such as 2 for    3.I was impressed that in the meat section I picked up 2 meat items, diced chicken and a pack of chicken breasts for    6. They re trying too hard to make their stores into some kind of romanticised theme park based on a bygone era where old women pottered around the cobbled streets of Yorkshire buying black pudding and lard.I can t see how this format will work in former Safeway stores in the more affluent parts of the South of England. They may have even  enjoyed paying slightly more in the belief they were getting that certain  je ne sais quoi  (or should that be  joie de vive ?). Yes, it s consumer snobbery, but it s also a business reality and it works for Sainsbury s and Marks   Spencer.Customer service at my local store has also taken a nosedive since the men from Yorkshire came along. I always check my receipts with eagle eyes, and worryingly I have been overcharged on my last five consecutive visits to Morrisons. Mostly this was down to the checkout operator failing to notice the yellow  quot;reduced for quick sale quot; sticker, but the most unacceptable incident was being charged    1.93 for two loose baking potatoes. Not a single one of my subsequent trips to the customer service desk earned me an apology or the slightest whiff of concern as to why the mistake happened. If you’re considering Morrisons for your weekly shop, here’s the lowdown from someone who’s poked around the aisles with a keen eye and a slightly sarcastic grin. First off, the bakery is a real winner—fresh, tasty, and wallet-friendly, which is a rare trifecta these days. Their fresh foods—think fish, veggies, fruits, meats, and cheese—are consistently high quality, making it a solid spot for family meals that don’t scream “instant regret.” Plus, the variety is impressive, with specialty counters that add a nice touch of choice.

Now, onto the less rosy bits. Customer service is a bit of a mixed bag. You might get a checkout clerk who looks like they’d rather be anywhere else, lacking even the basic courtesy you’d expect. On the flip side, some staff are genuinely helpful, so it’s a bit of a lottery. If you hit a snag, local stores can be dismissive, but the head office tends to step in with sympathy and sometimes compensation—so keep those receipts handy!

Navigating the store can be a bit of a challenge, especially after recent revamps. Narrow aisles and cramped layouts mean you might find yourself playing a real-life game of “dodge the trolley,” particularly during busy times. Thankfully, the stores are generally clean and tidy, and there are trolleys in various sizes, including options for families and disabled shoppers, which is a thoughtful touch.

One notable downside: no online shopping or home delivery, so if you’re used to clicking your groceries into your cart from the couch, Morrisons might feel a bit old-school. Prices are reasonable, with decent bargains if you keep an eye out, making it a good choice for those who enjoy the in-store experience and value fresh, quality produce without breaking the bank.

', '    I have used a few Anti virus programs in my x years using a computer, and I have found one thing that seems to be true through all of them. ', '    Being a careful sort of person, with a husband who is something of an expert on computer security, we ve always had some kind of virus protection installed on the family computers.  For a while we paid for McAfee, which seemed to do its job; I didn t get involved, and we had no problems.  It was supposed to be updated every so often but I didn t worry about that too much - and when our subscription expired, we had become blas    and didn t get around to renewing.  Viruses even six years ago were mostly restricted to those passed around on diskettes, and new ones only appeared rarely.  Moreover they didn t seem to do a lot of damage:  they were just irritating.  However within the past few years, a couple of things have happened.  Firstly there was an influx of cleverer viruses spreading around, and they began to be passed via email and the Internet.  These viruses ranged from the merely irritating to the ones which would gradually infect and destroy files around the system, eventually requiring a complete re-format of the hard drive, and probable loss of files.  At the same time, more and more people began using email, many of them unsuspicious and trusting, and they became an easy target for malicious viruses.  So we decided we needed better virus protection, and decided at first to pay for another year s McAfee. The best thing about it seemed to be that it was free. AVG has a professional version as well as the free one, and the links to the paying version are - not surprisingly - a little more prominent.  The free version is linked immediately above the search box on the left. product_reviews: ['    My husband is a computer geek and can probably tell you all the additional features and list all the technical changes that have been introduced for Windows ME. Well I am not a computer geek and I am not filled with Jargon so I will simply tell you what a user of the new Windows system has noticed.The first thing I notice is that the system loads quicker, leaving me a little less frustrated. I have a musical file that plays immediately on setup and was surprised at the change to the player that is bundled with Windows.The player seems to take longer to load but has a lot more features. Each tune is accompanied by some neat graphics that move in relation to the music (there are about fifteen different variations.). The player has added options that allow you to play music from the web. The player is much improved from the one included in Windows 98.We recently bought a web cam and although I have used it I found it difficult to edit my movie files. Windows ME offers a comprehensive video package that allow you to edit the movie, add titles and text and reduce the size to make it small enough to email. My husband tells me that the new system gives the user more options to control digital equipment such as a web cam and things like scanners etc. (I told you he was a computer geek )The look and feel of Windows is exactly the same. I noticed a significant improvement in the speed I download from the web although my husband feels this may have been due to problems with our installation on Windows 98.My husband gave me a great deal of reasons why we should spend the  53 to upgrade from Windows 98, and I must admit to not understanding many of them,All I can say is that there are a few nice touches added, the system generally seems to run quicker, and so far the system hasn  8217;t crashed. It used to crash at least once a day.When my husband installed the software there was no swearing so I assume the process is easy.I haven  8217;t really noticed much different apart from the above and apologize for not including any technical details or even a list of new features. I just thought it would be nice to have a non computer literate user  8217;s view on Windows Me. Should you upgrade? I will not answer that question, I suggest you find a computer that already has it installed and try it first. If I had not been married to a computer geek then I would definitely not bought the upgrade. I thought long and hard about a rating, and came to the conclusion that I can only rate on what I know. All I know is that hardly anything seemed to change for  53. My husband says that perhaps he should have waited for the next version, but as long as it keeps working then I don  8217;t really care Please don t be too hard on me, I don t profess to be an expert.     ', '    If you are one of the owners of the most common aged computers out there (about 3 or 4 years), I can predict that the majority of you will still be clumping away on Windows 98. While it has done its job well, It may now be time to upgrade as Microsoft are stopping the support of this operating system this year. Bet you did not know that did you? Ok, maybe you did. So you want support for your computer but where do you go? Your computer is a few years old now and will not be happy sticking Windows XP or 2000 on it. Why is that? Well, 2000 and XP require huge amounts of resources to function properly. In fact, unless you have a brand spanking new computer, you could run into all sort of incompatibility upgrading to these 2. Then you will be stuck in eternal limbo without an operating system  So you have an older computer but what support. What is the solution? Enter Windows Millenium Edition or Me for short. This combines an improved performance with a more compatible and level-headed system that will work with most older technology. Let me tell you of my experiences with it. Installation. 2 Choices here. Upgrade (updating the original System with the new one without losing most of your files) Clean Install (wiping the machine and doing a fresh install. My experiences with both of this has been quite frustrating. I attempted to upgrade my mother s windows 95 machine to Me without a fresh install. Checking the installation guide which is pretty thorough, I decided to upgrade. The problem with this is that on an older machine that is starting to become slow, the entire upgrade process is delayed and slowed by a slow read and write. It is much simpler to do a clean install. You dont get half of the problems that an upgrade can cause. I tried 4 times to upgrade the machine before losing patience and wiping it. Time spent trying to upgrade = 4.5 hours. Time spent trying to Clean install = 1.25 hours. You tell me which is the best  To clean install you need to insert the supplied boot disk with the software. This stops the normal boot up sequence when the computer starts and gives you a few options. What you need to do is type  format C:  at the prompt. This then asks you if its ok to format the drive. Say yes and this takes about 5 mins. Then restart the machine. This time it should start with 2 options. With or without CD rom support. You have a CD with the software on so you need to select the WITH option. Then just follow th e onscreen instructions. Simple. Whole process should not take more than 75 mins from start to finish. So installing from Fresh gets 8 out of 10. Upgrading scores a miserable 0 out of 10  Performance improvements. Well, it claims to start up and shut down much quicker. As your hard drive becomes more cluttered, shut down takes longer anyway so a reinstall of any system would seem quicker. However, Me does seem MUCH quicker than the previous software, even on my mum s old PC. It can now also rest your machine to a previous state  This is a brilliant function and available on XP too  What doe sthis mean? How many times have you bought a piece of software or hardware and tried to get it working only to find it has wrecked your machine? Myself, I have lost count  However, the ability to turn back time has now arrived. You can set your computer to make a back up at a particular time of day so that if you have trouble, you can roll back any changes. It truly is like time travelling on your computer. Obviously any files you change since the rollback date will be lost but if you make these snapshots often enough, you should never lose too much data. It does also claim to be more stable than previous releases. The memory leaks and terminal failures do seem to be greatly reduced. I dont seem to be needed to answer question by my mum as much as I used to. I was forever recieving phonecalls asking  Its doing this,blah blah blah....  or  It is aking me to do this  or  it wont work  So well done to microsoft for improving stuff. It also has greater ranges of included multimedia software. The later version of Media player are much better suited to playing movies and audio form the web which makes it a true Internet ready PC. What I didn t like. What I didn t like were the amount of drivers I had to go hunting for to get some of the peripherals to work. The Printer and scanner were both produced before Me was released so their included drivers did not cater for Me. I then had to scour the internet for drivers to make the devices work. This took ages and proved fruitless for the Printer. It just isnt supprted and meant buying a new one. The scanner was ok though. I also did not like the fact that some games and bits of software no longer worked. It is always sad that software writers spend so much time making the stuff work with the latest computers that they totally neglect backwards compatibility. Overall its not a bad operating system but it needs improving on the compatibility. Good for upgrading older machines.      ', '    When it comes to computers my knowledge is limited. Please do not expect this opinion to be technical. It is not. My computer knowledge is very small  I only purchased my first computer three years ago. It was second hand and used Windows 3.1. At the end of the second year degree course, I managed to blow it up, due to the sheer volume of essays it had to process (it waved a little white flag, sighed and died ). I then decided to have my second computer custom made. Being really naive about computers I chose to have Windows 95/97 installed. This was fine until I wanted to add new programmes or explore the Internet in more detail. This January I choose to have Windows ME installed instead. Having read reviews and reports but what really convinced me was when I tried my mother-in-laws system. I just had to have it  To buy the system and have it installed cost around    100.00. Being a novice I felt unable to remove Windows 95 and then install ME. I would not have known where to start if it had gone wrong. Boy, it is fast, but it is easier enough to use even for me  The speed and stability of the system is great. If I make a mistake it corrects it for me. I do not have to reboot my system as I previous did. The system does not seem to crash; well I haven t managed it yet or even  get its nickers in a twist   I am still plodding though the manual. It is great bedtime reading. I am usually asleep within five minutes of reading it. The learning process is slow as a result  I find that my Internet access is quicker, than for Windows 95. I could be wrong but that is how it appears. I can also visit a few more sites and I do not keep on being asked if I want to up grade this system or that. I love to play the programmed games, particularly when I am tired. I am now hooked on Pinball. Yes,  small things please little minds , but I have to admit I am addicted. Then there are the Internet games. I haven t mastered them yet, but watch out when I do. There will be no stopping me. Then there is the media player. Compared to Windows 95, ME is out of this world. I can spend hours watching the different patterns being created by the music. Sad, I know but on me, it has a hypnotic effect. Well, so far that is, all that I have to say about Windows ME. Compared it to Windows 95/97. It blows my mind away, but I am still learning. I will edit this opinion if I come across any problems or great point. It will soon be time for dinner so I had better finish. Just time for one more game of Pinball       ', '    Windows ME did it to me again.  Up popped the little box telling me there was an update, so silly me decided to let it happen.  Fool, she cried, I should have learned from before   Woe is me for being such a trusting soul.  Within minutes, my online radio no longer played, then pages started freezing and finally, the whole blooming system just decided it had had enough.  I guess that was kind of about the same time as I was having similar thoughts   I guess I just expected them to be updating with something to FIX the screw-ups in the programme, not to create MORE So, back I went and refreshed the system back to an earlier date - how many times is that that I ve done this now?  It gets a bit tiresome, you know.  I think Microsoft should have worked out ALL the bugs before this operating system was installed in new computers for us - the unsuspecting consumer.  My computer actually has a Windows sticker on it that states  Designed for Windows 98 .  Duh?  So why, then, did it come with Windows ME pre-installed?  I guess that s something only Microsoft and the computer manufacturer know.  I m just the idiot who bought the machine ...     ', '    Seems I m not as impressed by this as some of  the other reviewers.  Unfortunately, it was installed in our brand  new computer ...and I had misgivings as soon as I realised that.  I remembered all the hassles we d had with a beta version of Windows 95 all those years ago.  My husband tried to offer reassurance and uttered words of comfort in my ear.  Things were so far advanced now, they ve been doing this so long, they KNOW what they re doing.  In fact, I agree with that last sentence. When you first boot up the machine the start up process can take a lot longer than it  8217;s predecessors but when it does finally load it looks quite similar to what I am used too.  One of the most annoying thing I found with Windows ME is that the good old CD-player has been replaced with the new and improved version of Media Player which takes a lot of the system memory which slows the machine right down.  Also the items on the start menu are constantly being hidden.  In my opinion unless your desperate leave ME alone.      ', '    Microsoft s 2000 home version of Windows - the  Millennium Edition  offers very little progress over previous versions and can only really be recommended to those using Windows 95 or earlier. The improvements are too small and the added features too trivial to make it a particularly outstanding piece of software. The bold promise  Let ME Entertain You  - Microsoft s marketing campaign for their 2000 operating system - is hardly justified by the enhanced multimedia features Windows Millennium Edition offers. The most well known of these features is Windows Media Player 7, previous incarnations of which have been rather dull and forgettable. Version 7 promises CD-ripping and MP3-recording capabilities, access to reference media through the Internet, support for a large variety of video and audio formats and extensive visualisation and skinning variations. In short, this is Microsoft s answer to RealVideo and RealJukebox, (both of which can be downloaded free of charge from www.real.com). Media Player 7 fails in many areas. The MP3 encoding does make use of variable bit-rate technology to deliver a superior quality of sound without making the resulting MP3 file excessively bulky. To be fair, it does this very well - the MP3 sizes it produces are generally slightly larger than typical 128 bit rate MP3s but the sound quality is markedly better for the majority of the time. However it insists frustratingly on encoding the MP3 files so that they are unrecognisable to any player other than Media Player 7, and cannot be distributed via Napster. This is clearly to prevent any litigation from anti-MP3 cases, but as is typical of Microsoft it has been executed in a way that makes documents created with their product incompatible with the products of other manufacturers. But this is only the beginning of Media Player s flaws. Aesthetically it is unnecessarily large, taking up about a half of the screen even in minimized mode, making it about five times larger than WinAmp. The visualisations - colourful patterns moving to the rhythm of music being played - vary between very good (especially the  Ambience  ones) to extremely poor (notably the  Musical Colours  set). Full-screen playback is possible but it can cause the software - and sometimes Windows entirely - to crash. In fact, many, many things make Media Player crash. Importing certain file formats, especially RealVideo ones, makes it crash. Recording MP3 files very often makes it crash. Navigating the online media section while playing a song makes it crash. The crashes usually take the form of .dll (i.e. driver) errors and persist so frequently that the software is unusable. The ideal solution is to uninstall Media Player 7, then go to real.com and get RealPlayer 8 Basic and RealJukebox 8 Basic - they are far more flexible and tend not to crash at all, as proper software should. While you re at it, get RealDownload 4 as well (or one of the many variations: GoZilla or Download Accelerator), for Microsoft are yet to update their own download software. Yes, in this modern MP3-swapping, Internet video-playing utopia that Microsoft apparently envisage, download utilities that allow you to resume downloading if the connection fails are apparently not necessary. Downloading is a basic necessity of Internet use and it s laughable that in this supposedly multimedia-friendly new version of Windows a decent download program has not been included. Internet Explorer v5.1 is bundled in but even this is not free from mysterious, unprovoked failures. It is, however, probably the best Internet browser available until Netscape can get Navigator v6 sorted out. It is highly intuitive, flexible and flicks back and forth through pages quickly and efficiently. But, of course, it can be downloaded for free anyway (www.microsoft.com), so having the new version of Explorer isn t really an incentive to purchase Windows ME. Two more seemingly pointless utilities are included in Windows ME. The first of which is the  Scanner And Camera Wizard  in the  Accessories  section. I fail to see the necessity of this utility - such image input hardware as it promises to support are invariably easy to install anyway. Such programmes as Adobe Photoshop, Corel Print House and Paint Shop Pro interface directly with the scanner or camera s software anyway. Having a wizard present to detect these items is a waste of time. That said, when I plugged my scanner in, it remained dormant. I suspect that was a blessing. The second utility is  Windows Movie Maker , a very limited piece of video editing software that allows you to editing together various pieces of footage and a small number of effects. It is no substitute whatsoever for a dedicated piece of video editing software, and it is far too fiddly to use even for quick editing jobs. The final products can only be saved as Windows Movie Maker Files, and therefore are pretty much useless anyway. The flashy multimedia face of Windows ME is therefore only superficial - mere window dressing. After the definite improvement in speed and stability that Windows 98 Second Edition brought I hoped for impressive feats from the new version. The truth was in fact quite disappointing. Let s begin with the good news at least - Windows ME does improve start-up and shutdown times considerably. It does so by a notable margin, too - you won t need to get a stopwatch out and measure the two to notice the difference. As with Windows of old, though, adding start-up programmes such as virus checkers slows times markedly. Nonetheless the signs are good. The promises of better stability, however, are utter nonsense. If anything Windows ME crashes more frequently than its  predecessor which is frankly unacceptable. It frequently hangs while trying to shutdown, and more often than not fails to shutdown entirely and displays the message  Windows Protection Error - Please Restart Your Computer . Windows ME is little more comfortable at multitasking than its  predecessors - attempts to run more than two or three programmes at once (my usual combination is Microsoft Outlook, RealPlayer, Word and Norton AntiVirus) cause endless problems usually resulting in crashing or programmes failing due to mysterious .dll errors. The standard system utilities are decidedly lacking in power. Scandisk now runs under Windows at start-up, which is an improvement, but the software itself is no better. Indeed Scandisk and Disk Defragmenter seem to work in an irritating pass-the-buck system where Scandisk claims data problems require Disk Defragmenter to run before Scandisk can be used, but Disk Defragmenter blames disk surface errors and won t run until Scandisk has fixed them. Another peculiar issue is that Windows consistently claims that I am using more space on my hard drive even after I ve deleted several large files. Norton Utilities can sort these problem out, but you shouldn t have to spend    59.99 on buying software which should come as standard with an operating system and function correctly. The desktop remains very similar to that introduced with Windows 95. The start menu has been tidied up a little bit, and deleting icons gives a beginner-friendly warning that this action will not delete the programme itself. In general, however, the desktop has hardly changed at all from Windows 98 to Windows ME. Windows Millennium Edition is really not worth upgrading to if you have either version of Windows 98. Though it does run notably faster than previous versions of Windows in certain areas, the frequent and inexplicable crashes suffered only waste more time anyway. The additional software is generally either useless or, like Media Player 7 and Internet Explorer 5.1, can be downloaded free of charge from the Internet. Perhaps realising that Windows ME is a worthless upgrade for Windows 98 users, Microsoft are selling a Windows 98-only upgrade for    42.99 (www.reserve.co.uk). I strongly advise against taking them up on this offer - it is a complete waste of money. Upgrades from other versions of Windows cost    74.99 and are worthwhile for the greater Plug-And-Play and USB support that came with Windows 98. Windows Millennium Edition is hardly the operating system for the 21st century that Microsoft would have us believe. It is volatile, unreliable and offers little real improvement over previous versions.      ', '    When Windows ME was out on the shop shelves, i went out and brought myself a copy, Windows 98SE was running fine and smoothly for me but lots of reviews have been saying it s a good OS and lots of improvements have been made. ', '    The newest version of Microsoft Windows is out and this time it   s interestingly called Windows Me. At this current time I   m not sure if windows Me is something that everyone should run out and buy just because it the new thing, but it is good and hasn   t (yet) crashed      ', '    What can i say? Windows ME (Millennium Edition) was hyped upo by the press and by Microsoft to be the only choice for an operating system. But the many glitches, bugs and problems drag this product back to the dark ages.   One most notible problem is it s  superiority . It is regarded so highly, that Microsoft have removed DOS from their system. This means many popular games are unplayable, and some disk facilities are unavailable.
