', '    IntroductionMillennium Edition is a new operating system for the home user, the one now supplied the new computers and is available as upgrade for existing systems.  Based on Windows 98, ME offers enhancements for digital cameras, sound, Internet Explorer exploration and interactive help.Featuresautomatic update feature gives itself could buy automatically downloading enhancements from the Web.interactive help and a new Windows help centre will answer all your problemssystem restore a feature to allow you to backtrack to a time before you had problems.seamless integration with Explorer for the net and beyond.smoother interface especially with latest technologies.allows home networking easily.Installationinstallation is NOT straightforward.  If you re upgrading from previous version of Windows there can be a lot of conflicts during the install.  A clean installation is recommended, meaning one from DOS and that ME does not use DOS, you have to create a start-up disk.  There is an option to save your previous version of Windows please do this.  When all is working about 60 minutes later you have your new version of Windows.The Benefitsa firmer tighter control system comes into operation.  For example your last used programme is immediately accessible from the start menu.  Image files and open in a browser window.  The overall feel all feels like a well-developed machine.  The help is good and easy to solve problems.  Simple problems  fixed themselves.The Problemsthe extra feature slowdown Windows.  If you re used to Windows 98 second edition you will feel frustrated by the delay.Many of my old programmes would not work on the millennium Windows.  These were not old programmes the new programmes spent hard money on.  These include Norton Utilities 2000 Clean Sweep WinFax pro and Epsom printer software.  This was incredibly frustrating trying to find downloading fixes, which were unavailable.  Windows Millennium on my machine crashed a number of times.  Working for any length of time on programmes which is Paint Shop Pro causes the dreaded blue screen.  After number of weeks I d uninstalled windows millennium and reverted back to Windows 98.ConclusionI personally would not recommend the upgrade whether it was a configuration my machine that cause problems, the disadvantages were outweighed by the advantages.  However there may be still some promotional upgrade at available at 39.99.  And despite it may be worth the risk trying it.  I will probably reinstall Windows millennium when the first service pack is available and a number of software fixes are available.ME Alone UpdateA new machine with ME cleanly installed at first had fewer problems than the update.However installing older software pre 1998 ie Via Voice causes malfunctions.     ', '       If this isn t cashing in on something that made it big then I don t know that is.  Windows ME is exactly the same as windows 98 with just a little changed to make it look as if they have done something.  The price now is    40 and I don t feel that it is a good thing to charge people over the top prices for something that is a complete waste of money.  I wouldn t touch this peice of trash with ten foot barge pole.  So my advice to all you little customers out their is not to go out and buy this because it is a comlete waste of money.         ', '    Same old story as all the other OS from M ...WinMe is just Win98 with all new driver updates and windows update run on it. In fact it runs slower than Win98. What is the Point????It seems to me anything with the word  Millenium  attached to seems to fail- Millenium Dome/Bridge, so all you marketeers out there, don t use it  Why can t M  just create a new style and start from scratch to create an operating system worthy of some of the brilliant machines out there Overall WinMe is an ok product but the public are expecting more and to be honest M  are doing less and less        ', '    With the new feature of Windows ME, like System Restore, Automatic Registry checker and more drivers, the system isn   t very stable  I used the upgrade kit from Windows 98 to ME; my original Windows 98 worked fine no problem and reasonably stable. But when I upgraded to ME the problems kicked in. Firstly when installing the system crashed and took many hours to sort out, I spent about two days just trying to get the system working with all the drivers etc. I can see that it could be a very useful Os system but only if you are lucky enough to get all the hardware working first time round. The reason I think this is because once I forced it into using the correct drivers the system sorted itself out and automatically resolved small errors. This would be useful for people of no or little knowledge in computing. ME was running fine although took some time adding components as the Soundcard and Video card were fighting over the same resources. Just recently my system has had the registry altered in some way that it does not like, and hence every time the system is restarted the registry is set back to the first time ME was installed, also all the devices have to be found again  There is little room to maneuver around this problem. Also the system restore is a very good idea from Microsoft, it returns your computer back to a point saved previously and hence saving your precious work. But this did not work for me as only one restore point was allowed to be saved, and hence every time something went wrong the system goes back to this point and I loose all of my settings, like backgrounds, start menu, and everything that   s customizable.So basically I have had a lot of problems with Windows ME, which I didn   t even get a glimpse of on Windows 98.     ', '    I have recently installed windows ME (millennium edition) and it deffinately wasn t worth it.Microsoft seem to have a very strange definition of upgrade.  Getting rid of all the old bugs and adding new ones     Seems to be the problem with all of their upgrades, windows 98 was just as bad.My machine has slowed down dramatically, I keep getting stupid errors.  My sound card stopped working, I seem to have fixed that though.  And really there is no added features on here it looks and feels exactly the same as windows 98.  What was the point?  Personally I don t see one.Oh you get a new game called spider solitaire, so much fun, lets all run out and buy windows ME for a new game.Sorry I know it s cheap but if you re happy with windows 98, then stay with it, spend your money on something else.Rob     ', '    Sadly its here - a successor to Windows 98 that really doesn t do the job   I used many different operating systems on a day to day basis, and I m very glad to say that this isn t one of them A friend of mine wanted to upgrade from Windows 95 and asked me to reinstall everything from scratch with just ME on the computer.  I was curious to see what the new OS was like, but could hardly stop laughing when it crashed during installation Eventually I managed to get it installed, and booted for the first time - another cheesy logo from the software giant, but who cares if the OS underneath is good.  A fresh start in ME reveals nothing more than a 98 GUI with the odd few  improvements  -  could be worse  I thought   The first step was installing the CDRW drivers which hadn t been detected at installation, and as usual a reboot was required before anything could continue.  It was no surprise that a reboot later, Windows crashed whilst loading Adaptec s CD writing software   Blame it on Adaptec?  Surely an OS should be able to cope with a badly written piece of software (if thats the case) on a fresh installation Stick with 95 (or 98 if you re so disadvantaged) and go straight to 2000 with a PC that ll run it properly.  A far more stable OS, 2000 will do everything ME will but quicker, more reliably, and even occasionally with a touch of class.     ', '    Windows ME is basically an extension of the Windows 98 core, a bug fix/service pack thing if you like. I will take you through my experiences of the product to give you an idea as to what its like. Firstly the setup. You get the customary startup screen although with this one you get a short movie that shows a number of the new features incorporated into ME. A little similar to the dialogue you get when setting up Win 95/98. Once the movie is over you receive a number of choices where you can learn about the new features in ME. From a visual point of view, ME is largely similar to 98 with just a few subtle changes and new features. In my opinion it is made to look more like its moving away from 98 to 2000. However, if like me youve been using 98 for what seems like an eternity (that being a good thing or bad thing im not entirely sure yet) then you ll slot straight into ME no probs. Right in terms of when your in the new system. As I said before it is largely the same as 98 (just a lot stabler hopefully, as i ll come onto later). The help system certainly seems to have been rejigged to make the OS more user friendly. A significant addition to ME over 98 is the mass expansion of the Internet Sharing system, allowing multiple machines to share one internet connection over a LAN. There is now a step by step guide to set this up and to setup a home network in general which 98 didnt have, continuing the theme of user friendliness. A helpful addition is the new registry restore setup. Before if your computer packs in after an installation (people with PCChips boards will find this particularly useful ), you had to go into safe mode and run the various registry programs like scanreg and regedit to solve your problems. You can now restore from a GUI much in the same way as it works in 2000. I have seen some benchmarks for the software on websites around the internet and I will now try to evaluate them. I wont quote actual figures as to not confuse people and also because they use an extortionately powerful system (P3 900 and 64Mb GeForce 2 ). Incidentally its ME compared with 98 SE. Winbench CPU Marks - ME better by 0.1 in total of 82.3(insignificant) Winbench FPU marks - Dead even Winbench High end graphics - 98SE quicker by 40 in total of 1170 Winbench business graphics - 98SE quicker by 8 in 421 I will quote figures for the following as it is easiest with Win 2k scores coming in now: Sandra CPU marks - 2000=2577, 98SE=2453, ME=2451 Sandra FPU marks - 2000=1265, 98SE=1258, ME=1254 Sandra MMX - 2000=2941, 98SE=2497, ME=2453 Sandra SSE - 2000=3967, ME=3933, 98SE=3923 Sandra CPU memory - 2000=323, 98SE=319, ME=317 Sandra FPU memory - 2000=353, 98SE=344, ME=342 For the principal of not overcrowding this article with uninspiring benchmark results, I will summarise the 3D Mark scores. 3DMark if you didnt know is an indicator of raw gaming performace. Win 2000 as id expect bombs out big style here. Both 9X based OS s thrash it by twice in some cases so as we knew, 2000 isnt a gaming OS. However the 9X based systems again remain very similar, maybe 98 just edging it, but not significantly enough to ruin ME. The 2 9X based OS s are very similar. Speed is one thing that shouldnt inspire you to upgrade to ME, what about stability. From my own personal experience ME is far far more stable than 98. Ive had no significant crashes thus far with ME whereas they were commonplace with 98. This is the big point, stability. Speed shows little difference based on the figures ive seen so stability is a big point because 98 is atrociously unstable. Overall there a significant steps made in this OS but are they significant enough to warrant the spending of your hard earned money...... Thats a decision that your going to have to take im afraid.     ', '    I m a home user, mostly playing games on my system or doing coursework. I m not a company, so I can write a review for all those people who just want it for home. And maybe to show off. Jokes aside, yes it is. Having now been officially released, we purchased the upgrade and shifted from Windows 98 SE up to Windows 98 Called Millennium. :-) And yes, I m more than happy with it. For those devout Windows 95 users, it will not appeal, because it is basically Windows 98. But looking so much better. More fluidity and more stable I think, you can tell quite a bit of work has gone into it. And although it shouldn t, I don t doubt it has more bugs than an ant-farm, but you get that with every OS. It loads beautifully fast on my system, which is hardly the best, and no problems running any programs so far. Lots more ways to edit both movie and sound, and it bundles in Internet Explorer 5.5 and Windows Media Player 7, both fantastic pieces of software alone. And it is hardly expensive  Upgrade to Windows Millennium now, it certainly made ME happy. Ho-ho.     ', '    My computer has been changed so much for the better since I replaced Windows 98 with Windows ME. Don t get me wrong in terms of features Windows 98 was a very good operating system, as would be verified by the massive worldwide sales that turned it into the industry standard. The problem that I had with Windows 98 is a similar one to most people. This was stability. The amount of times I was forced to restart my machine through explorer crashes was absolutely ridiculous. It got incredibly annoying and left me wondering how a company could release software that was obviously poorly tested. Despite the fact that that ME is built on the Windows 9X core, it is a massive improvement. It has all the features of 98 plus a whole lot more and the key is that it is 100  more stable. I have hardly had any crash and i ve been using it for months now it really is a breath of fresh air. I have to congratulate Microsoft on this because this stability hasn t been seen since Windows 3.1x   There are many new features in Me, the best one being the advancement of Internet Connection Sharing. It is so easy to setup internet connection sharing so 2 computers can share 1 connection by the use of a network, that a child could set it up. Me and my son have linked our machines and we can now go online at the same time and at our own machines. There is very little speed difference between the 2 operating systems. All my games run at the same speed on ME as they did on 98 or at least if there is a difference it is unrecognisable to me. Overall if your still on 98, if you can afford it goto ME because it is worth it for the extra features and particularly the extra stability. Well worth the money.        ', '    Having had Win98 wth a variety of bug fixing patches attached I decided to upgrade to the new Windows ME. Windows 98 was never going to be the stable operating platform I was looking for, so I had nothing to lose. Win ME is vastly better than I had hoped for, it s much more than just a bug fixing excercise. Upgrading to this has many benefits, these are instantly recognisable unlike the swap from Win95 to Win98. The installation was a dream, no problems there, worked first time with all devices etc recognised. From here things also get better. I am still finding nice little extras with this program, but here s the mani ones:- Better support for importing photos from scanners and cameras. Automatially preview rather than having to load up Paint shop etc. Pictures can also be stored thumbnail in a documents folder for easy retrieval. Win media player 7 is included. This is more geared up to the web and organising / customising music on your hard drive. System restore allows you to revert back to a working pc in the event of a major failure. Particularly usefull when new programes refuse to work. Home networking is easier to set up with Win ME. Devices such as printers, modems etc are more straightforward to set up. Menus are clearer to use, the start menu s are staggered on one screen. Previously having multiple applications meant scrolling into the next screen to find what you wanted. In addition to this theres IE 5.5, MSN Messenger and many other of the latest files that you re likely to use. It s been on a week now and I can t fault it, at last a Windows to be recommended ?     ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re considering Microsoft Windows Millennium Edition (Windows ME), here’s a practical rundown based on key user insights that should resonate with your curious yet pragmatic approach.

Windows ME introduces some genuinely handy features that improve everyday usability. For instance, the **Internet Migration tool** simplifies moving your Internet settings between machines—a real time-saver if you juggle multiple PCs or upgrade often. The **System Restore** function is another gem, letting you roll back your system to a previous state if something goes awry, which is a comforting safety net for anyone who’s ever felt the sting of a botched update or software glitch. Plus, the **Hibernate feature** lets you save your session and power down quickly, perfect for those moments when you want to pause without closing everything.

Hardware setup is smoother too, thanks to improved **Plug and Play** support, making adding or removing devices less of a headache. And for multimedia fans like yourself, the new **Thumbnails view** makes browsing photos more intuitive—no more guessing which file is which!

However, it’s not all sunshine. A notable downside is that many programs designed for older Windows versions may not run properly on Windows ME. This could be a dealbreaker if you rely on legacy software or classic games, so it’s worth testing compatibility before fully committing. On the bright side, the **Support Automation** feature helps you troubleshoot common issues without diving into complex manuals, which aligns well with your preference for accessible support.

In summary, Windows ME offers practical improvements in usability and system management, but its limited backward compatibility might require some patience or workarounds. If you value ease of use and innovative features but need to keep older apps running, weigh these pros and cons carefully. It’s a solid step forward, just with a few quirks to keep in mind.

', '    Available for free from http://www.grisoft.com ( AVG Free Edition  on the left hand side menu). ', '    I have used a few Anti virus programs in my x years using a computer, and I have found one thing that seems to be true through all of them. ', '    Being a careful sort of person, with a husband who is something of an expert on computer security, we ve always had some kind of virus protection installed on the family computers.  For a while we paid for McAfee, which seemed to do its job; I didn t get involved, and we had no problems.  It was supposed to be updated every so often but I didn t worry about that too much - and when our subscription expired, we had become blas    and didn t get around to renewing.  Viruses even six years ago were mostly restricted to those passed around on diskettes, and new ones only appeared rarely.  Moreover they didn t seem to do a lot of damage:  they were just irritating.  However within the past few years, a couple of things have happened.  Firstly there was an influx of cleverer viruses spreading around, and they began to be passed via email and the Internet.  These viruses ranged from the merely irritating to the ones which would gradually infect and destroy files around the system, eventually requiring a complete re-format of the hard drive, and probable loss of files.  At the same time, more and more people began using email, many of them unsuspicious and trusting, and they became an easy target for malicious viruses.  So we decided we needed better virus protection, and decided at first to pay for another year s McAfee.  But our copy was so out of date we were unable to do that easily, and in trying to solve the problem we came across several recommendations for AVG.  The best thing about it seemed to be that it was free.  Cynical as ever, we wondered how a free anti-virus program could possibly compare with the commercial ones, but we read several reviews, and we also discussed it with email friends - and eventually decided to try it.  * Where to find AVG *The main site is http://www.grisoft.com which has a simple layout - news in the middle describing recent updates, links to descriptions of the latest viruses on the right, and the main links down the left-hand-side.  AVG has a professional version as well as the free one, and the links to the paying version are - not surprisingly - a little more prominent.  The free version is linked immediately above the search box on the left.   Clicking this link leads to a page which informs the reader that the AVG Free Edition is available for all single-use non-commercial home users.   It also explains that there is no technical support available for the Free Edition and that the interface is basic.  Don t be put off by this.  We wondered if we would find it too limiting and need to upgrade to the commercial software, but it s been fine.  It also tells you that it cannot be installed in a networked environment.  What this means is that it will only work on one computer.  If you have two or more computers at home which are networked (as we do) then each one needs its own version. But the network as such does not cause any trouble.There s a standard licence agreement to agree with, and a basic registration form where you have to give your email address (that s where they send your registration code, so it s important to give a valid address:  their privacy policy is good, however, so this shouldn t lead to any problems).  The actual download is around 6 megabytes, which could take up to an hour and a half on some computers but may well be quicker.  * Installing *Installing AVG is very simple.  The downloaded file is an executable one, so double-click it and then follow the instructions.  While the download was happening, you should have received an email giving your unique registration code:  type this in when you re asked for it, and everything should go smoothly.  When the installation is finished, you ll need to re-start the computer.* Configuring *This is fairly self-explanatory.  AVG should appear as a little four-coloured square in your  system tray  at the right of your task bar.  Double-clicking this brings up the AVG Control Center (sic) box.  The Resident Shield tab should be set to check all three kinds of virus, and the email scanner to check all messages (and certify them if you wish, although this only works on some email clients).  The Update Manager allows you to decide how often you want to check for updates to the virus database, and at what time.  We used to set this to check every 14 days, then every 7 days... new viruses appear so often now that we have ours set to every 3 days, and find this to be sufficient.  If you hear of a new virus you can always click the  update now  button to see if a new database has come out. ', '    A few years ago a program called Napster came onto the scene and revolutionized the way we downloaded files, they made it free   apparently record bosses didn t like this idea, and made it not free   But relax, for Kazaa is here   Now I don t know if this is entirely correct, but i believe this is how it works; a person downloads the Kazaa application for free (with a regular 56k modem it takes roughly an hour), they then install it onto their computer, once this has been done it searches your computer for all files which can be uploaded, e.g. Mp3, Jpeg, Mpeg files and then puts them into  My Shared Folder  which is stored on your hard drive. The Kazaa application is then used to search for files in other users  Shared File  and download any files you find usefull, thus being the concept of file sharing, like i said i m not sure if the technical details are entirely correct, but its the general idea Within the program there are options to Search, View Traffic, Search the Web and  My Kazaa . Search is obviously the place where you can search for files, the categories of search vary and include audio, video and software. Once you have made your search it come up with a list of all files which match you choice, it also tells you information such as the size, quality, integrity (the rating the user has given the file) and the estimated download time, you then simply right click on the file you wish to have and click on the  download  option.The files you select to download can be viewed in the  Traffic  section, here it tells you how fast it is downloading, a progress bar and the estimated time left, along with the file name etc. With a 56k connection it takes roughly 10 minutes to download a decent quality Mp3 file (audio file, e.g a song) and up to 2 days to download a decent quality Mpeg file (video file, e.g a movie), obviously with an ADSL/Broadband connection the download times are decreased dramatically. My Kazaa lists all of YOUR files in different folders such as audio, video, i don t use this part of the program, or the web browser very often.Because of the sheer volume of people downloading and using the application, i think it was 3.5 million last week ( it also boasts being the most downloaded program on the net), it makes it very likely you will be able to find the file you are looking for, making it usefull for finding songs that have been  deleted  or that you just can t find in you local Woolies.I find the software very easy to use, it is very self explanatory and you can t really go wrong with it, however if you do there is a very usefull online help service. Another advantage of this version (V 2.1) is that you can re-connect to a download if you get cut off for any reason, without having to start all over again    It looks quite attractive and doesn t strain the eyes too much, plus you can download more skins for it, some of which are very groovy  Of course with all these good points there are bound to be some bad ones too, first of all porn, for virtually every search you make there will be a pornagraphic file in there somewhere, which is great if thats what you are looking for, but gets a bit boring when you search through and endless list to find what you are REALLY looking for  Viruses are also a big problem, because your internet connection is open for a sustained period of time to the same address it makes you very suceptable to hackers, and some cheeky monkeys even put viruses onto files just to really hack you off. Two further problems are people mislabelling their files so you can spend hours, sometimes days downloading something for it not to be what you thought and have to start all over again, and  Spyware , this is installed onto your computer when you install Kazaa, and too my knowledge it doesn t harm your computer, it just creates annoying pop-ups and finds you e-mail address so companies can bombard you with more spam. Finally, the biggie, the law, i m not quite sure where the law stands on this application, but i m sure somebody would have a problem with people downloading pieces of software, which retail at over    300, for free, an activity which i, of course, have never taken part in, nor condone.In conclusion this is a great application if it is used correctly and all precautions are taken, i would thoroughly recomend this program to you, but would also highly recomend downloading a decent firewall system ( zonealarm.com do a good free one) and virus scanner. Have fun, and remember, keep sharing   Download from www.kazaa.com     ', '    I will give some brief details of what Kazaa has to offer, but if its an in depth opinion of this program then I am sorry you will have to read other reviews. This is more a case of my personal experience and hopefully a warning to others.Firstly Kazaa is a file-sharing program that enables any two computers that are using this program to share all files on their computers. In other words they can swap anything, software, music (MP3 etc), video, pictures. So if you want something and it is on another PC you can download it. On an average day their are upwards of 2.5 million users online at any given moment. With that in mind the chances of finding what you want is more than a probability. With Kazaa you also get bullguard, which is an anti virus program.I decided to download the free version of Kazaa, I did briefly read all the notices and was aware that I would get pop ups, well I have got used to a certain amount of those. All I wanted was a software program, in fact it was an old freeware program, so using Kazaa seemed the ideal tool to use. Having downloaded the program I searched for the program, to my surprise I never did find it. Still now I have got it I might as well have a look around and see what it can do. Well yes it can and does download from other users, I tried a music file, a picture and a funny video, and they all downloaded and were perfectly ok.With so many users certain adult content type videos can be downloaded, but Kazaa does have a filter and can be password protected to stop children from accessing such things. With Kazaa you also have the choice of what if any files you wish to share with the outside world. So if Kazaa is your type of program so far so good. Now I am one of those people who clutter up their computers with all sorts of stuff. If I am honest I cannot remember what a lot of the things do. Having said that I do try and keep my pc running as smoothly as possible. Yes I do have anti virus stuff and yes I use it and keep it updated. Having had Kazaa for a few days I noticed that Kazaa itself was not too stable and would often do an illegal activity and shut down  (I don  8217;t know what it did, but it kept on doing it and shutting down). Then I was finding my PC would totally freeze on me. I would not be able to connect to the Internet without restarting the PC. A lot of this I blamed on my poor PC housekeeping. That was until I tried to do an Internet search and found I was being given strange results, for instance I wanted some train times and got places where I could buy toy trains. If I was a new user then I would have thought it was the search engine, but I do know a little better than that. A closer look and I realised although I was using the MSN search bar on Internet explorer the results were coming back from a search engine called my shopping. That was not down to me. I tried to reset my settings on the PC, but still I would find my searches hijacked.Things got worse I was soon finding strange programs trying to access the Internet. Pages were taking longer and longer to load although my hard drive seemed to be working its socks off. Now if I had broadband I might not have noticed the slow down, but having a dial up connection that is slow at the best of times I really did notice.Then Internet Explorer became more or less unusable. At this point I started to put two and two together and realised that it must have something to do with Kazaa. In fact the problem is not Kazaa itself, its all the other programs that are bundled with the free version. Add to that the fact that downloading from other computers can also mean you download spyware programs and other programs that are called thiefware.My solution was not that easy to achieve, it involved firstly deleting Kazaa, then downloading a program (I will write an opinion on the program I used) to help me trace all the programs that should not be on my PC, getting rid of them and finally resetting and downloading updates to try and get my PC working as it did prior to my flirtation with Kazaa.So for any of you thinking of using this program do be aware there is no such thing as a free lunch. Kazaa do offer another version without the add on programs, but you have to pay for this. I personally have had too bad a time to consider using it, so I cannot tell you what it is like. want, but please be careful if you do, as to the ammount of Viruses that are on there.Mickeyxx     ', '    I   m sure virtually all of you who have an interest in computers have heard of KaZaA in some shape or form, because of the publicity it   s been getting lately, good and bad. But for those who don   t know, KaZaA is an online peer-to-peer service. This basically means that you can share any files you wish with other users - you can make a copy of their stuff, and in return they can copy yours. (Don t worry, your files can t actually be altered or  stolen  ) There s quite a few of these programs out there these days, but KaZaA is the most popular of these programs with nearly 150 million users to date, and allows you to search for MP3 audio files, software, documents, images or videos. It has a huge user base as I   ve mentioned, and it   s highly configurable as to which files you wish to find (and which files you don   t )Getting hold of KaZaA is easy. It   s completely free, and is available from www.kazaa.com or any download site worth its salt. The install is fairly small, about 4 megabytes I think. This should take about a quarter of an hour on a normal modem connection, or a couple of minutes if you re on broadband like me (gloat ) After this all there is to do is to choose a user name and which of your files you wish to share, and you   re running. For those of you who don t like to provide personal information, I can assure you I ve never received any junk mail from KaZaA, and I have a suspicion that user names don t even have to be unique So you ve got KaZaA, and started it up. KaZaA loads quite slowly, but when it s loaded it remains in the system tray (the area next to your clock) which makes it appear faster in the future. KaZaA has a pleasant, uncluttered user interface. It can be customised with skins, but as of now there are not many available and they   re hard to use compared to the original. It works by means of six different tabbed sub-screens.    Web    opens up when you start KaZaA, this basically shows the KaZaA website, promoting some of its advertised downloads, and offering news and advice for KaZaA members.    My KaZaA    is where you   ll manage all your shared files; from here you can specify details for your files, rate their integrity and put them into custom playlists. (Files with higher integrity can be easily picked out from your searches, so you can find the best quality files possible.)    Theater    allows playback of any media you ve downloaded such as songs or videos, although you   ll probably be better off using your normal media player for this purpose as Theater is a bit limited.    Search    is fairly self-explanatory -  from here you can (guess what) search for files you wish to download. Normally it s easy to find what you want, simply by entering the name in the search box, but if you can t turn up anything or you wish to search more specifically, there s a  More Options  button. When this is clicked, as if by magic a number of options appear, allowing you to search by specifying the type of file (Anything, Audio, Video, Software, Images) and a number of properties (title, artist, quality, size, et cetera.) After performing the search in the left pane, results appear in the right hand pane, and can be downloaded with a double-click. You can also sort the results in just about any order you like.    Traffic    is where you keep an eye on the files entering and leaving your computer, and the speed at which they   re doing so. If you re not happy with the speed, you can attempt to find more users who have the same file, as KaZaA allows you to download the same file from up to eight users at the same time. This works by downloading a different part of the file from each user, and then piecing them together at the end. This method can speed up your downloads quite significantly.   Shop    is a (for me) largely useless feature which allows you to purchase CDs and merchandise. (Oh, and there   s the standard button which screams at you to    Tell A Friend     about KaZaA.)KaZaA has some other very useful features. First and foremost, for family users there s an  adult filter  which can be set (and password-protected) to remove any objectionable material from your search results. It s not 100  accurate, though, and due to the sheer volume of this material on KaZaA some will undoubtedly get through.It   s very easy to use already, but KaZaA has a very comprehensive online help file covering a wide variety of subjects. If you wish, the integrated virus scanner will scan everything you download, but I   m inclined not to rely on it and still use Norton AntiVirus. If you like a file, you can search for files by the same artist or off the same album, or alternatively from the same user. By rolling your mouse over an item, a pop-up will display extensive information about the file.If you have any questions about files you re thinking of downloading, you can save yourself some time by sending a message to the user who has the file. Most users are courteous and will reply to your messages.The latest version of KaZaA has a new feature. It s designed to promote the fact that KaZaA is after all a  sharing  program as opposed to a  stealing  program. Users who allow other users to download lots of their files are given a higher  Participation Level , from 0 to 1000. The benefit is that if two users want the same file, it goes to the user with the higher Participation Level. KaZaA appreciate that users on slower connections might not be able to afford to share many files, so the program allows you to set how much of your bandwidth (connection) you want to use for sharing files - useful if you re on a modem.KaZaA is a hugely popular program, but there are three main issues which put people off it. The first is the inclusion of the so-called    spyware    with the program. KaZaA being a free service, creators Sharman Networks had to make some revenue somehow, and the way they chose to do it was by bundling smaller programs with KaZaA. Most of these mainly pop up irritating adverts, such as Cydoor. Some of these can be turned off during the installation procedure, and others disabled by other means, but there will always be the allegations of violation of privacy. If you   re not comfortable with organisations recording information such as your surfing habits, you might want to avoid this and go for less    bugged    software like WinMX.The second issue is that of copyright infringement. When Napster, the first file sharing program, came out, there was a collective uproar from record companies, who instigated a court case alleging that file sharing had a detrimental effect on their profits. The big American companies eventually won the battle and Napster was closed down. KaZaA obviously faces this threat     its creators claim that it is intended for users to share files for which they hold the copyright, but the reality is that there   s an overwhelming amount of    stolen    material on KaZaA, ranging from the latest Kylie album to any software package you desire. This may be unethical, but it   s very much alive and kicking. Finally, there is a considerable amount of material on KaZaA that some may consider objectionable. The adult filter reduces this, but only to an extent. As well as files with unsuitable content, viruses are also a worry - there was a particularly nasty episode a little while ago when malicious users attempted to fool people into downloading viruses by naming them after popular songs and programs. This, like copyright infringement, is not specific to KaZaA but common to all programs of this type. Really you have to consider whether the benefits outweight the potential issues - it   s up to you whether you want to get involved.So what of my experience of KaZaA? Well, I have to say I ve found it unbelievably useful. The easy-to-use interface and massive user base allows me to quickly and easily find what I   m looking for. Files download quickly, and are usually accurate and problem-free. I   m not particularly bothered about organisations tracking my surfing habits; however, if you are, or you   re worried about joining a service which potentially infringes copyright, this might not be for you. For me, though, it   s brilliant. Thanks for reading,Matt (age 15).PS. Oh, nearly forgot to mention .. might be worth a look at www.kazaalite.com too - they claim to offer a version of KaZaA minus the privacy-invading spyware. Good luck      ', '    I tried them all, no, I really did. Fileshare, E-Donkey, Win MX, I-Mesh, Bearshare, Rapigator as well as other unmentionables and then over a year ago I chanced upon KaZaA. Since I first found KaZaA I have uninstalled all other P2P s because I quite simply stick with the best.     ', '    What is KaZaA?KaZaA in short is a FREE peer-to-peer downloader application.  This actually translated into English is a file sharing community allowing you to access a massive shared distributed database of files (well .. almost English).  The software allows you to search for files that other members are willing to share meaning that the files are not situated on some remote server, but actually sitting on their hard disks ready for you to download directly from them.  Similarly you as a member also have the  option  of sharing files with other members allowing them to access part(s) of your hard disk (read-only) for them to download from.  Some of you by now will probably be saying ..  dodgey ..  but as i said it is optional as to whether you wish to share or not.What can I download?The search facility currently allows you to search for Audio, Video, Images, Documents and Software but also allows you to search under the heading of Everything in case you are not sure what category the file will qualify as.  I will discuss the search facility more in the Features section.Signing UpOnce you have downloaded this software (just install KaZaA, the rest is not worth bothering about .. trust me ), simply run the application and you are presented with the sign-up screen which is a straight forward process of you supplying them with your requested username, password and your e-mail address.  There are currently 99,362,235 members at the time of writing this sentence so you will need to be patient when trying to get your required username.  Do not worry about being spammed with e-mails, I have been using this software for roughly 2 years now and have had no problems at all.FeaturesOK, you have now logged on and you are ready to use this cool piece of software that nice Mr Wolfie has recommended to you   The interface is very intuitive and presents you with an Internet Explorer style screen with the KaZaA home web page on the Start tab - these tabs are at the top of the screen under the menu.The search tab will allow you to search for the file of your choice in the category that you specify, there is also a  more options  filter that will help you narrow your search which differs depending on what type of file you are looking for - an example being if you are looking for MP3 audio, you can choose the title, artist, quality bits-per-seconds, etc.. then simply hit the  Search Now  button and wow lots of files are listed to choose from, to download one of these just double-click on it and the download begins.You can check the progress of your download by going to the Traffic tab, this will show you the current progress of all the files that you are currently downloading aswell as those being downloaded from you.  If you think a download is too slow you can right click on the items and choose  find more sources , this will then hunt down people with the same file and download it from them, also to be noted is that a file can be downloaded from a number of people at the same time, in which the file is broken up into at most 8 pieces from which a single piece is download from each person.  You can also log-off from the web at any time and resume your downloading next time you want to go online.Under the My KaZaA tab you can manage the files that you want to share with others - this shows all the different types and amount of files in each category that you are currently sharing and allows you to add/remove directories from your sharing list. Kazaa Downloader is a mixed bag, especially if you’re like me—keen on easy file sharing but wary of security pitfalls. On the plus side, Kazaa shines with its straightforward interface and simple search functionality, making it easier than some rivals like Emule or Audiogalaxy to find music, videos, and software. The onboard media player is a neat touch, letting you preview files before committing, which is handy given the occasional mislabeled or damaged downloads you’ll encounter.

However, the security concerns are hard to ignore. Kazaa’s free version notoriously bundles spyware and adware, leading to annoying pop-ups and potential privacy headaches. Worse, it can hijack your browser settings and install unwanted programs without clear consent. This isn’t just a nuisance—it can seriously compromise your system’s stability, causing crashes and slowdowns, especially if you’re on a dial-up connection or older hardware. The bundled software is also a pain to remove and can even prevent Kazaa from running properly if you try to uninstall it.

Another red flag is Kazaa’s sharing model: it exposes your IP address to third parties, which could land you in hot water over copyright infringement. So, if you’re cautious about legal risks, this is a major drawback. The participation rating system, meant to improve download quality, often backfires by slowing things down for some users, which can be frustrating when you just want a quick download.

On a brighter note, Kazaa does offer some parental controls, like filtering and password-protecting adult content, which is a thoughtful feature for families.

In summary, Kazaa is user-friendly and functional for file sharing but comes with significant security and performance trade-offs. If you’re willing to experiment and take precautions—like running strong antivirus software and carefully managing what you install—it can be a useful tool. But if you prioritize a clean, stable system and legal safety, you might want to explore alternatives or paid options that don’t carry these risks.

However, Microsoft s Internet Explorer still beats it by miles.     ', '    I changed my ISP to NTL in November, and ever since then I have had nothing but problems with IE5. This was the main reason I had tried Netscape... I went to my first site, logged in and there was the applet, YES..SUCCESS . I have no idea how, or why, Netscape helped but I am sure glad that it did.     ', '    Having played about with the Beta Versions of Netscape 6, it looks as though my asks may have been fulfilled. The new browser, whilst I am not sure if it is quicker than IE5.5, given that it tends to load pages only upon completion, rather than incrementally like IE5.5, is certainly a looker. As well as the classic interface, with the somewhat tawdy boxy look, that it familiar to users of previous incarnations of NN/NC can be replaced with a Modern skin, and apparently other skins are also available for this browser. Whilst undeniably a skin should not be a major talking point of a browser, it at least gives you the impression that this is a  new  browser, rather than a bug fix as has hitherto been the case. The security options for the browser are a marked improvement, and the biggest omission of previous versions was a component for saving passwords, with is becoming evermore a necessity. Furthermore the printing options have been further improved from previous versions of the browser and the interface is compact, whilst still offering a wide range of functions. The collapsible left menu (this appears where the History Bar appears in IE5.5 contains more features, and the integration with AOL Instant Messenger has been cleverly integrated into this menu, saving yet more space, adn meaning less trips to the sys tray. From having done a continuous all day test (10 hours surfing), the browser has proved to be more resilient than IE5.5, and more stable, not having crashed so far. A further improvement is in the mail function, where you can control multiple e-mail accounts easily from within the mail programme, something that had hitherto presented problems. Overall this is a return to form after some very lacklustre browsers from Netscape, although I doubt whether this latest offering will really make much of an in road in the dominant IE. For a web designer it is a must, as sites must be compatible with all browsers. On a closing note, it seems to be a good countermeasure against bloatware, being of course entirely recoded, and therefore not full of bad code that has been so guilty of cause application sizes to soar.     ', '    Having giving 4.75 an extended trial and being disappointed with the results, I thought that I would give the Netscape 6 Beta 2 a bit of a try out. My first impressions were taht considerable changes were affot. This was noticeable especially considering the fact that my computer let it install itself alongside Netscape 4.75, thus indicating completely new programming rather than an upgrade.A few features caught my eye, and there do appear to be signs of life and promise at Netscape - Firstly from the weak NN4.75, the page loading is a lot quicker, although not as quick as IE5.5- If you use Netscape as a e-mail programme, then you can for the first time manage multiple accounts from it - this is a definite plus, as you can t in Outlook Express.- There is a provision made to save your passwords, like in IE5- It takes up less space on the harddrive and uses less RAM- there is a new ICQ imitation called the BuddyBar - name sounds poofy but this is one of a host of new features on the retractable sidebar...- Radical new design. This is on the whole a plus, moving away from the tired NN look, although this can initially be a bit annoying, as it takes a while to get used to.- Poor support for Viewbars, alladvantage.com (for what it is worth...) is just about supported, but hopefully work will be done on this for the release version- Bookmarks are not fully transferred from previous versions.On the whole it is a step in the right direction, but still lags behind IE5.5     ', '    After seeing reviews and comments on Netscape 6, I decided to give it a try. I went to the site, and downloaded it (which took an absolute age, because there are multiple files, which are a large size (about 5 mb each)), then installed it.The stupid thing is that it keeps on nagging you to sign-up to their netscape services, so that they can essentially e-mail you offers and ads. If you decide not to sign up, then every time you open the program, it will ask you.So, I signed-up and got into the program itself (it just holds on one screen for about 20 seconds for some reason before loading the program). The first impression is that it looks so nice, that it has to be good. In some ways it is, because it has AIM integrated into it and a spell checker for checking your emails, which you can also send from the Netscape program.Although after a while, it just feel horrible to use, mainly becasue it runs so much slower than IE. You get the distinct impression that they are trying to get kids and women to use it because it has a nice layout, with schemes that you customise by downloading extra buttons for the navigation bar, thus forgetting to make it memory efficient and fast.There are quite a few little niggles that put you off, like when you click the address bar with IE, it will highlight all the text, and you just press Delete and type in the address of the place you want to go to, but in Netscape it doesn t highlight it all, so if you have a long URL in your bar, then to get rid of it and type in a new one, you have to scroll along, Delete, scroll a little more Delete. This can be very annoying. Plus there are shortcuts with IE like typing something in, and press enter while holding ctrl, and it will wrap the  http://www.  and the  .com  around your phrase. Netscape doesn t seem to have any user-friendly shortcuts like these.If you are accustomed to IE, then there is no way that you will be able to use this program, because it is sloppy, and the fact that you would need *at least* 64MB RAM to run it with any joy. This is a miss for me.     ', '     Firstly, I ll confess that I m a bit of a Microsoft fan.  I know its not cool to admit that these days, but I find that their software is in general OK - just incredibly expensive sometimes  Perhaps that means I shouldn t be writing an opinion on Netscape, as I d obviously hate it anyway, but my feelings on this one are so strong that I have to write about it. The intention of these is probably to let you get access to the information you want, whenever you want. BUT IT S SO SLOOOOOOOWWWWWWWW           It takes ages, and ages, and ages to load even simple pages, and if you click on a checkbox in something like hotmail to select a message to delete, then go away and have a bath, have a coffee, do our shopping, then it MIGHT have realised you ve clicked on it.  Sometimes when it s loading a page with a script on it, it sort of  pushes  the layout all over the place - making it impossible to read the page until it s fully loaded. Want to scroll down a page? If you’re curious about Netscape 6 and how it stacks up in today’s browser landscape, here’s a no-nonsense rundown based on what users have found helpful. On the plus side, Netscape 6 does improve website rendering compared to its older versions—pages generally look better, which is a relief if you’ve been stuck with the clunkier Netscape 4.x. Plus, it offers some neat customization options like attractive skins and a sidebar you can tweak with useful features, which is a nice touch for those who like to personalize their browsing environment.

However, don’t get too excited just yet. Netscape 6 is notorious for being a resource hog—it has significant memory leaks that can slow your system down, especially if you’re running multiple apps. It’s also quite buggy and prone to crashes, which can be a real headache if you rely on stability for your workflow. Page loading and responsiveness are painfully slow, making it feel like you’re stuck in dial-up days rather than surfing the web at modern speeds.

When you put it side-by-side with competitors like Opera or Internet Explorer, Netscape 6 falls short in both speed and stability. If you’re someone who values a smooth, reliable browsing experience without constant freezes or crashes, you might find Netscape 6 frustrating rather than fun to explore.

In summary, Netscape 6 shows promise with better visuals and customization, but its heavy system demands and instability make it a tough sell for practical daily use. If you’re a tech explorer who enjoys tinkering and don’t mind some rough edges, it’s worth a look. But if you need a dependable, fast browser, you’re probably better off sticking with the more polished alternatives out there.

product_reviews: ['    Now try not to faint when I share this with you    My partner does not have a mobile phone. He s never had a mobile phone. And he must be the only adult in his 30s who doesn t know how to text. Now with a baby on the way the time has come for him to join the mobile race. After all it would be quite nice to be able to get hold of him when the time comes rather than rely on a local cab. So it could not have been a more opportune moment for the  man from T Mobile  to ring me and offer a free upgrade (worth    250 he said), so I could hand my old phone onto the other half. Now I ve never bought a phone without seeing it in the shop so it was a bit of a risk. The most important thing for me is size (I don t know why it s coming back into vogue to have a phone the size of a brick again just so you can e-mail from a field) and I do like to be able to flip the phone shut so I don t call my parents inadvertently from my bag convincing my mother she is witnessing my murder over the phone. So when the Nokia 6230i arrived I was a little disappointed to find it bigger than my previous Samsung, and no flip lid so I toyed with the idea of giving it to  him indoors  and holding onto my old one. But it only weighs 99g and when I turned it on I started appreciating all the upgrades and advances. Now, I m probably only ever going to use about 1/8 of this phones gadgets and subsections, so if you re expecting a 100  run down and regurgitation of the phone s handbook you re going to be disappointed and probably grade me as  somewhat helpful but marks off for not being very thorough . For a techie / anorak s view, please stop reading now and read the other reviews. For a  user friendly  opinion please feel free to read on. First of all the address book allows far more information to be stored, if you can be bothered to enter it all in. You can nominate a general number, home / mobile / office / fax numbers; you can pop in their e-mail address; web address; even postal address; user ID; Notes about them; and even an Image taken by your smart new photo camera in portrait mode. Add to this that in your secure  briefcase  you can enter all the details of your credit and store cards - it could be argued that you don t need to carry anything anymore apart from your trusty mobile, (and an army of personal assistants to upload all the info for you). The other feature I use regularly is texting. Not so user friendly here. I keep hitting  back  if I make a mistake and exiting in one move the whole texting area. Luckily my message is still hanging around when I return but this is getting very annoying. There s predictive text and even a complete predict the word mode. And helpfully if the phone has no idea what you re trying to type in it offers up a  spell and then Save  option allowing you to add words to the dictionary and saving you from changing from predictive text mode. There are loads of templates for you to choose from  I m late, I m busy, I m in a meeting or even  I love you too  which I guess could be useful if you re the gregarious type or a serial bigamist with no time to waste on individual texting. Now I don t really download - I m always worried how much it s going to be costing me, so I rely on a few good ring tones, something Samsung never provided making me dive for my phone to save the world from my phone s pitiful rendition of Greensleaves. The Nokia has some pleasant ring tones, 3 different simple telephone rings (bliss ), and the most gentle alarm clock to prize you from slumber in the morning. The factory settings provide you with a little bubbly noise for a text which is inoffensive. And if you re fussy there are hundreds of tones to warn or alert to choose from. Now as you may have been able to tell - I am a girl, and for your information I don t chew my fingernails. But even with a good manicure I find the keypad fiddly. God help any of you guys with big digits. The central button that controls almost all of the menu and the up / down / right / left controls are blooming difficult to use accurately. Is this handset designed for under 8s only? I m currently growing my left thumb nail for improved mobile dexterity but this layout is always going to annoy me. My other phones have had cameras - the Samsung had a camera attachment which I never bothered to keep. Technical progress has definitely helped the quality (1.3 mega pixels) but I wouldn t try to take anything too precious with this phone. There s a  night mode  but no flash. You can zoom in, use the self timer and change to video mode but for me the only useful thing about it is the comical trick of having a photo of the person who s calling come up on the phone, or of course you could attach amusing images of inanimate objects to the phone numbers of friends and family, just try not to let them find out. There s a music player so you can listen to audio files through headphones or the speakers, and a radio too - but the quality s never going to match a real radio or MP3 however much you fiddle with the equalizer. There s a little 32MB memory card that comes in the box too for extra video shooting potential. There are all the usual games, calendars, stopwatches, reminder lists etc. The battery life has 3-5 hours talk time, 150- 300 hours standby which is impressive. It charges quickly and doesn t seem to be too affected by being turned on or off to charge. There s blue tooth available if you ve got the gizmo to stick in your ear and do your best Star trek impression. I m on T-Mobile - the only network that works where we live and reception is OK, although usually I can hear the caller better than they can seem to hear me. You can make the phone a hands free speaker if you want all around you to hear your conversation, and there s voice dialling which has been around for a while but could have its uses. I ve managed to figure out how to lock the handset within 10 seconds so I won t be calling my Mum from my back pocket. And the size doesn t seem to bother me anymore so I ll be holding onto this upgrade. Now I have the technology I just need to teach the other half  texting for beginners  before the baby overtakes him in mobile dexterity.      ', '    This is basically one of the coolest mobiles I have owned. Like most of the Nokia branded mobiles, it is simple to use and does not have to many complications like the modern mobiles of today. I know that I have owned more than eight different mobiles in the last seven years which is quite a low and is not good for the environment. This Nokia 6230i just happened to be in the midst of these mobiles and it is a shame that it left me before I was fully satisfied which is more of a shame really. I actually bought this mobile on the beginning of the year 2006. Quite a shame that I dropped the mobile in juice and it stopped working. That is why I bought my Sony Ericsson K750i. This mobile is not heavy at all; it only weighs about 95 grams and the looks of it are cool. One of the things I like about this mobile is that you can change the facial cover, memory stick and it has both Bluetooth and Infrared connection. The keys of the mobile are very soft to the touch and so as to the press. The keys are quite easy to note as they have big black prints on them. The lay out of the keys on this Nokia 6230i makes it easy to navigate through out the whole mobile. Everything is quite simple to use, therefore if you are a first time buyer this might be the mobile for you. The battery life of this mobile is quite good actually. I once talked to my mate more than four hours before the battery ran out. Therefore the talk time of the mobile is just over four hours which could even be five hours if the battery was fully charged. It also has over 200 hours of stand by time which is very good for those who don t use their mobiles a lot. ----------MEMORY----------When I bought this mobile it had a 32 MB MMC memory stick with it and already has a 32MB internal memory. 32MB holds about eight MP3 songs. The memory can however be extended by buying a 256MB or 512MB, MMC memory stick from many electrical shops. ----------PRICE   PACKAGING----------The Nokia 6230i comes in a small pictured box. In the box you will have you mobile, the battery, mobile charger, the manual (also in other languages), Software to run into you PC, USB connection, head set, sim card and your memory card. Last year when I bought this mobile it cost me    120 from Argos. I actually remember that it was on special offer as I bought it at the beginning of the year period were all the sales are fuming in every shop. ----------GAMES----------This Nokia 6230i comes with three games for you to enjoy. Sadly the Nokia 6230i does not come with Nokia classic snake game which has been there forever. It was not much of a disappointment to me really because they just had to move on from the old generation of games to the new generation, though some other Nokia modern mobiles still have the Snake game. The games included with the mobile are the Backgammon game which I actually learnt how to play with my previous Nokia mobile. The 3D golf game is one of the games which I find boring really; maybe it is mainly because I never accepted golf in my fun sports list. I have played the Golf game and the graphics are quite good really, the game is mainly based on how to maintain the striking power on the golf ball. However, if you are a golf fan you would enjoy the game more than I did. Street Racer is the third game that comes with This Nokia mobile. The game is of two cars racing together and you have to control one of them. It is quite hard to win n the game for the reason that when you play against the computer in never crushes on other cars on every journey which gives it an advantage because whenever I play the game I crush at least two times onto other cars or swerve out of the main road which slows my vehicle down. The game is easy to play as you only have to use the right and left navigation keys. With the game settings you can however chose to turn on or off the sounds, change the game level (easy, medium, difficult) and to turn on the shakes (vibrate). If you want more games you can download loads of Java games from your network provider WAP r the internet. You might have to pay for most of the games unless stated  free ----------MEDIA----------This mobile has a lovely 1.3 mega Pixel camera. It might not sound a lot but the picture quality is actually quite good. You can either set the picture to High resolution (bigger and sharp image) or low Resolution (small and low pixel image).The camera is fairly easy to access; you can go on the main menu and chose camera or you could use the right navigation key to access the camera from the main page. I used to find this very useful really because it saved me time. When I was fiddling with the mobile I actually realized that you could change to access the camera from the right navigation key to the left, up or down navigation. Therefore you can access the camera which ever key you.With the camera it comes with editing clip arts and picture frames which make your picture look cool or funny. I found it very easy to print my pictures by taking my MMC memory stick to a picture processing shop; I mainly used to go to boots for some reasons. Using the 1.3 Mega pixel resolution you can also take video with the mobile. You can edit your videos via the mobile if you want or you can use more advanced editing via your computer if you want. Whilst taking the video you of course have two choices, either to take a high quality video which takes up more space or to take a low quality video which uses less memory but has bad quality picture. The video will be recorded in a 3GP format which can be played via windows media player if you transfer the video to your computer. ----------CALLS-----------You can divert your calls to other numbers or your voicemail if you want.-You can call up to five people at the same time. I always used to call three of me friends at the same time; it s quite a cool feature to be honest.- You can choose to hide your number when calling other mobiles. - It has call timer, (calculates how long the call has lasted) and keeps it in record.-It stores up to 20 last dialled, missed calls and received calls.  ----------MESSAGING-------------With the Nokia 6230i you can send SMS which is the normal text messaging with letter or symbol characters. When writing an SMS you could use the integrated dictionary---You can send MMS which includes all you media (pictures, voice recording, videos and MP3 songs). This tends to take at least a minute to send to other mobiles as the files tend to be of big size in terms of memory. The mobile automatically resize the image if it is too big to send. ---You can e-mail your friends via the mobile and you can also read you e-mails on the go. ----------CONNECTIVITY----------With this mobile there are various ways of connecting to other sources such as mobiles, internet or your computer. You can connect to other mobiles when transferring data, pictures, videos or music by using infrared or Bluetooth. Bluetooth could however be the easiest and fastest way of transferring the data. With infrared the two mobiles have to be very close to each other and have to be turned. With Bluetooth you can be ten metres away and still transfer the data quicker. Bluetooth is also easy to transfer to computers though I find it easier to transfer to the computer via the USB connection. The Nokia 6230i comes with the USB connection. If you want to use this to synchronize documents to your computer it is best you use a USB 2.0 port on your computer as it makes the transfers quicker.  This mobile has WAP and GPRS therefore you can connect to the internet and browse thousands of mobile beta pages (websites suitable o be viewed on mobile screens). I used to mainly use the internet to talk on msn with my fellow mates or just browse for games and latest news in the world. The mobile also has PoC (Push to talk) which lets you use the mobile as a walkie talkie. I never actually had the chance to use this feature, but I m sure it s a good one. ----------APPLICATIONS-------------ConverterThis mobile has a converter which converts money (selected currencies), weight (pounds, stones, KGs), length (KM, centimetres, Inches) and temperature (degrees, Fahrenheit). I did found this feature useful a couple of times when I had to convert pounds to stones as I do not really know how much a stone is, in pounds. --- The mobile has a dictionary which translates basic words to languages like French, Dutch, Spanish and Italian. It also has an English dictionary. ----------EXTRA FEATURES-------------FM Radio this mobile comes with an integrated FM radio which is quite cool to listen to if you want to hear the news or if you are bored from listening to your old songs. You could put the radio to loudspeaker or use the headset. You can save some of your radio channels onto the mobile so that you won t have to look for them every time you want to listen to the radio. ---Like any other mobile, this Nokia 6230i also comes with a calendar which lets you set reminders e.g. anniversaries, meetings and things to do during the whole day. The calendar feature of this mobile is actually a bit different from other mobiles I have owned as it lets you view the calendar in weekly format. ---The mobile has a world clock which lets you navigate the earth as globe and when you click on an area it tells you the GMT time of that country comparing to the London time. If you are going to a holiday which is out f the country this could be a useful to use as it tells you how many hours you are going to change your watch. I used the feature when I was going to France and yes it was all good, didn t have to ask a dozen people to find out the French time. ---The mobile has an integrated speaker which means if someone calls, you can put them on loud speaker if you do not have your headset or if you just can t be bothered to hold the mobile. ---With Nokia 6230i of course you can change your display picture, screen savers and ring tones. You can use your mp3 songs as ring tones or you can download them from the internet. With screen savers and main display picture you can both use the pictures and screen savers which come with the mobile or you can use your own personal pictures. ---The mobile has a Tri-Band meaning you can use it in many countries including European, American and some African countries. ----------NOTE---Run the software provided if you want extra features such as picture and video editing tools to your computer. If your computer was made before the year 2000 you might also have to run the software so that you computer recognise the mobile when it has been connected. If you have lost your manual you can still find it o the software. This mobile is not touch screen like some nowadays mobile---Do not I repeat  DO NOT  let the mobile get in contact with any fluids. I dropped mine in juice and now it is no more   61516; If you drop it in juice and you do not have insurance on the mobile it will probably cost you more to fix it than buying a new one. That is exactly what happened to me so I bought my K750i. Do not forget that water damages are not included in the manufacture s warranty. ---The automatic answer only works if you have your headphones plugged into your mobile. ---The speed dial only keeps nine contacts. ---Like modern mobile this mobile is not a touch screen I m afraid, so if you are looking for touch screen mobiles this isn t the one for you. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
If you’re after a solid, no-nonsense phone that balances practicality with a surprisingly rich feature set, the Nokia 6230i is worth a close look. Weighing in at just 99 grams, it’s delightfully lightweight and compact—easy to slip into a pocket without feeling like you’re hauling around the Starship Enterprise. The design clearly prioritizes comfort and portability, which is a big plus if you’re on the move.

Navigating the phone is refreshingly straightforward thanks to its simple, user-friendly menu system. No labyrinthine menus here—just quick access to what you need, which is perfect for those who want efficiency without fuss. The address book is impressively robust, letting you store multiple numbers, emails, web addresses, notes, and even images per contact. For someone who likes to keep detailed info handy, this is a practical boon.

Connectivity-wise, the 6230i shines with fast USB transfers and reliable Bluetooth that won’t suck your battery dry. Plus, voice dialing and voice control work well, making hands-free calls genuinely useful rather than gimmicky. If you’re into media, the built-in MP3 player and FM radio deliver excellent sound quality, and the expandable memory (starting at 32MB and upgradable to 512MB) means you can stash plenty of tunes and photos without fretting over space.

The 1.3-megapixel camera won’t win any awards, but it’s a handy feature for casual snapshots. Overall, the phone scores high on functionality and reliability, packing a wide range of features without overwhelming the user.

On the flip side, if you’re expecting cutting-edge specs or a powerhouse camera, this might feel a bit dated. But for those who value straightforward usability, solid connectivity, and good media options in a compact package, the Nokia 6230i delivers dependable performance with a touch of charm.

First stop Woolworth s I have seen they have a large choice of phones. Closer inspection soon revealed that all the lower priced phones seemed unavailable. I then visited some of the main phone shops including Vodafone and to be honest here I was greeted with prices way beyond my budget. I was in Argos making another purchase, when I saw phones that appeared to be on the Vodafone network and priced between    39.95 and    69.95. I like the small size and design of the phone, it has the option of having the vibrating battery on or off. The reception of this phone has as yet not let me down.It is a nice compact design, with most of the standard features that are found on other mobiles..choice of ring tones,date and time,volume control,calculator etc To find a complaint it would be that having used a Nokia for so long the text messaging is fiddly and awkward.Also if you take the battery out you need to reset the date and time. I have found that the battery comes away from the phone very easily and it has on more than one occasion done so whilst in my pocket. Another downside although not high on my personal list is it does not have any of the games that are found on the Nokia  8217;s.The phone holds its charge very well, but the vibrating function can soon use up the charge. I would therefore recommend that you only use the vibrating function when you need to keep your phone switched on but do not want an audible sound.
