', '    I am not the type of person who needs to have the latest technology, so I bought this phone from someone who no longer wanted it.  However, she had lost the charger, and finding a new one was a nightmare. I think I went to about 25 mobile phone shops in London looking for a new charger for this phone. I went to the Sagem website, but the only charger they sold came with a leather carrying case and a contraption that enables the charger to sit on your desktop-- extra stuff I didn t want to pay for. But eventually, I had to shell out the    22 to get their over-priced packaged deal. The Sagem company wants you to buy an entire new phone if you lose the charger. --Customer Service-- I accidentally entered the wrong expiration date on my credit card when I ordered the charger online, so I had to call the company. They put me on hold for several minutes and the people didn t speak English very well. They assured me that my charger would arrive in one week (five business days). A week and a half later when it didn t arrive, I called again and they claimed it had been shipped. I emailed the company a bunch of times, but they didn t reply to my emails. When I called, they just said,  Oh, we got your email.  The charger finally arrived about 2 and a half weeks after I had ordered it. And it was a French plug  (i.e. 2-pronged, as opposed to the three pronged British plugs.) Aaargh  I have converters, so it wasn t a problem, but, on principle, I was annoyed that they had sent me the wrong product. --Using the phone-- The girl who I bought the phone from had also lost her owner s manual, so I had to play around with the phone a lot in order to make it work. You can download the user s manuals from the website, but they are largely unhelpful and are for 4 or 5 different types of phones, and are, thus, very general   So, it says things like,  your phone may have this feature...  and it is really confusing. To start using the phone, you press the downward arrow key that takes you to the first of 8 menus, which are: 0) PayT (pay as you talk) Menu 1) Directory 2) Messages 3) Calls 4) Ring and Beep 5) Settings 6) Security 7) Accessory When you get to the one you want, you press  OK  and it takes you to another list, etc. etc. Other phones I have seen are less time consuming. There are, however, at the top, three buttons that you can program to do things that you most often do. For instance, mine are  Call message center  i.e. check voicemail, put silent mode on or off, and  read message.  I won t go into all of the features, but I will say, in general, some of the ways you have to go about using the phone seem rather counter-intuitive. For instance, replying to a text message. When you finish reading a text message, it will ask you if you want it to  clear.  You have to say  no  and then back all the way out of the read message function and go to  Send Message  and then to  Send existing message,  which takes you back to the message you have read. Then you press OK and scroll down to reply. This makes no sense   and is very annoying. --Talking-- Talking on the phone is fine. It is small and light and has good sound. To change the volume, you press the memory buttons (the furthest right makes it louder and the left softer). To activate speaker phone, press the pick up the phone button again. It has caller ID and tells you if you have missed a call, etc. etc. Standard features.  One strange thing is that if you have a voicemail, it will say that you have missed 6 calls, even if only one person called.  --Texting-- This phone was definitely made with talking in mind. Texting is very difficult and time consuming as compared to Nokias that I have seen others using. Instead of pressing the same button twice in a row to get to the next letter or symbol, you have to HOLD IT DOWN. This is annoying because you really have to pay attention to what you are doing in order to hold down the button for the exact amount of time necessary to make it an  R  and not an  S.  Also, when you receive a text message from someone, even if they are in your directory, it just gives their number and not their name   When you are done with a message and want to send it, it says  Addressee  and gives you spaces to fill in their number. The Vodaphone people told me that you actually have to enter the number every time. But, it turns out (one of my mates has this phone, as well) that if you press  OK  when it asks for the number, it will take you to your directory and you can enter saved numbers. Again, this feature is not obvious and it is difficult to figure out how it works since the owner s manual is so poorly done. --Battery-- The life of the battery is pretty good. I am extra careful with keeping it charged, so I m not sure how long it lasts. I usually keep it on all the time and charge it every other night.  The talk-time is not very good, however.  The phone sometimes starts to run out of batteries after talking on it for only an hour and a half or so. I don t usually have very long conversations, so it s ok.     --Durability-- There s dust under the screen and the numbers are starting to wear off some of the buttons. Also, it is really hard to hold down the     key which is what you need to do punctuation for texting. But I ve dropped it a couple of times and I keep in in my pocket sometimes, so it is in relatively good shape. --Vodafone-- Once you buy a phone, you are stuck with the network it comes with. I didn t want a Vodafone because most people I know are on Orange, I m stuck with it for now. So, even though it costs me a bit more to call other networks, the money I saved in buying this phone for    10 makes up for it. Plus, I also don t like Vodafone because it is on the shirt of Manchester United  So, every time I Top-Up my phone, I think,  Eeew, this money is going to support Man U.  --Conclusion-- This phone was really cheap, so I can t really complain. It is smaller than a lot of the other  pay as you talk  phones. It s also relatively nice-looking. (It looks better than the one in the photo on Ciao, and mine is greenish-grey). Talking is fine, but texting is a pain.     ', '    After months of moaning to my fianc   , I was graced with the pleasure of owning a new phone. If you’re considering the Sagem MC 920, here’s a down-to-earth take based on what really matters. First off, the phone scores well on basics: it’s small, light, and fits comfortably in your hand or pocket—perfect if you dislike bulky devices. Signal quality and call clarity are excellent, and talking on it is generally pleasant with good sound. Plus, it’s durable enough to survive drops and rough handling, which is a big plus if you’re prone to accidents.

On features, it offers the essentials: dual-band support, speakerphone, vibrating alerts, programmable keys, and multiple built-in ringtones. The Vodafone PAYT smartstep tariff pairs nicely with this phone if you’re a frequent caller or texter, keeping costs reasonable.

However, don’t expect much customization. The ringtones are limited and can’t be added or personalized beyond what’s built-in. Also, if you’re coming from a Nokia, beware: it won’t accept pictures or logos from Nokia phones, and texting is a slow, frustrating affair. You’ll be holding down buttons forever to get the right letters, and the menu system is confusing enough to make you wish for a simpler interface. Unfortunately, the owner’s manual doesn’t help much—it’s confusing and makes setup more of a chore than it should be.

Another practical downside is the rubber buttons—they wear out quickly, with paint peeling off and some buttons becoming almost invisible or non-functional over time. Battery life is decent on standby but disappointingly short during calls, so keep a charger handy if you’re a heavy user.

In summary, the Sagem MC 920 is a solid, no-nonsense phone that delivers on core functions and durability but falls short on user-friendliness and customization. If you value straightforward calling and a tough build over flashy features or smooth texting, it might do the job—just don’t expect it to be Nokia-smooth or stylishly customizable.

Hope this review was helpful.oh yeah nearly forgot the important bit, available on contract for free or nearly free in most stores or on pay as you go for    179.99      ', '    Have just got a new mobile phone, it   s a Sony Ericsson T630.Normally im a Nokia kinda girl, but I thought why not have a change and go for the Sony Ericsson. Polyphonic RingtonesWasn   t that impressed with the ring tones, My 2 children on the other hand dance to them. There more dance ringtones. In all there are 32 to choose from. You have a ringtone composer which ive only quickly looked at. Im now on the look for a ringtone I like.One of the first things I looked for on the phone when it arrived was a auto lock, with having kids, I didn   t want no calls to 999. so I was glad when I found it did have auto lock it went straight on.It displays the time and date, and you can pick your wallpaper design, which you have a few to choose from. Plus screen saver pictures can be added if you wanted them, you have ones which are already on the phone but you can use your pictures you take from you camera as them too.My Sony Ericsson came with the instructions and the battery charger plus a CD which have the drivers on for the computer to transfer data from phone to computer. Thanks for taking the time in reading my reviewTanya     ', '    So this is it. Phone number five in under a year. So far I have managed to write a review for each of them, and this is going to be no different. Now, as anyone who read my (recently updated) NEC 338 review will know, I was severely dissapointed bu the lack of features which are often considered standard on most modern mobile phones. I dispised the picture size, and the low sound quality. I was gutted to learn it had neither Bluetooth, nor infrared. I was annoyed that I had payed out so much money for such an under-advanced phone. After putting up with it for about a month, I started trying to find excuses to get a new phone. Indeed, the only reaxson I hadn t returned it to the store within a fortnight was because I dropped it on my way to work, whilst biking, leaving it with a mahoosive scratch down one side, rendering it useless for a refund.Then along came a small package of gold, in the form of an O2 genie sim card. See, my girlfriend decided that buying two of them would be great, as the 300 free texts that it offers would be perfect for staying in touch. The only problem (if you can call it that) was that the NEC couldn t be unlocked. So, unfortunately, it looked like I would have to get a better phone, eh?So off I trotted to the city centre once again. My experiance form last time told me that the Link was a good place to go. I looked around for what felt like hours but was unable to find a phone within my    90 budget.So I left the store to go home, feeling slightly dismayed and a bit daft. It was then I noticed the Carphone Warehouse practically next door.I had already decided that the Carphone Warehouse is a good place to buy phones, as that was where I had been helped out greatly buying my A835. I also knew they had a massive selection of phones, and that they are a lot cheaper than many other places. Proof of this is the fact it took less than five minutes to find a small, cheap-ish, attractive phone, with all the functions I wanted.My dad had a T610 for a long, long time. I really liked it as well, since it was one of the first camera phones with recognisable quality. I had wanted one for so long you wouldn t believe it  So the fact I was about to buy one better had me feeling very excited, with high hopes.After parting with eight thousand, nine hundred and ninty nine Great British pennies, I walked out of the store, once again considerably poorer but yet another phone richer than before. Bus home, yada yada, open the box, and so on.First impressions were actually not that great. There was a huge and blatant attempt to make money in the from of a CD containing software to transfer sounds, pictures, and the like from the phone to the PC. What s the problem with that, you cry? Easy. There is no data cable included  How s that for cashing in? Well, dispite that, the software is usually expensive, but never the less this annoyed me. You know, as if parting with ninety quid wasn t enough The charger was there, but no hands free kit, which I was also a little dissapointed at since the last three phones I owned came with one... and they were a damn sight cheaper than this phone I can tell you  There was also a lot more leaflets than I have ever seen in any phone. As well as the O2 promotion ones, there were also leaflets promoting Sony Ericsson  As well as this, there was an exceptionally chunky instruction booklet... which I used purely to find out what buttons to press. I decided that since I didn t fancy a sleepless night of reading the instruction manual I would teach myself what does what.But to the thing you are reading this review for... the phone. Sitting in a snug little cardboard bed, it gleams slightly as the light hits the shiny lamination of the buttones and screen. Very nice first impressions. There is an internal aerial, and the sides are a different colour to the front and back. In the centre of the back is a small silver capsule-shaped oval, housing the camera and view finder. The buttons on the side have clear marks indicating what their functions are. The phone itself is small and light, even with the battery in. So all in all, good so far.Putting the SIM card is was, it has to be said, a bit of a mission. It is basically touch and go as to whether you get it right, since it involves sliding a really small and stiff metal panel back and forth to hold the card in place. The battery sits over the lot and is held very securely in place by a slide on battery cover. Very safe, no chance of it popping off and you losing your SIM card anywhere.After plugging it in to charge, I turned it on. This is done Nokia-style, with a button on the top of the phone as opposed to the increasingly popular method of holding down the hang up button. The screen flashes on nice and bright, displaying the Sony Ericsson logo. But the best part about turning it on is the sound. A loud, sharp, crystal clear tone sounds out, pounding the puny NEC 338 sound capabilities into the ground. It isn t as loud as the A835 but it is far clearer.The main screen consists simply of a wallpaper, time, date, and all the usual expected info such as battery life and reception quality. There are no shortcut pictures, asides from the soft keys to access recent calls and the quick menu, which includes the options to check your number, put the phone on silent, and lock the keypad. This leaves the main screen looking very neat and tidy, and since the quick menu features the most used functions it doesn t really matter that there aren t any shortcuts.The joystick in the middle of the phone acts as a button and also as the navigation for the phone. From the home page, you can either press it as a button to access the main menu, push it left to write a new text (Straight to the typing.... very fast indeed ), push down to access contacts, press right to access the main menu (for some reason), or push up to view your friends. This annoyed me a bit as well.... the only friend you have at first is, apparantly, yourself  Not nice to feel rejected by a phone, Sony Ericsson The next thing to do was to add all of my old contacts onto my phone, as it was a new SIM card. However, to share photos and the like it also supports bluetooth and infrared. These allow you to exchange photos and sounds between other bluetooth and infra red phones for free  This feature is becoming more and more popular, although the T630 was one of the first phones to support bluetooth.The phone comes with several games. Built in are four games to play from the start, and there are a few that can be downloaded for free through the phone. So if you want a phone, go out and buy this one Links--------http://www.myt630.lasyk.net/ - An absolutely brilliant idea for a website  Without any signing up or paying, you can browse a load of pictures, wallpapers, games, and ringtones.... and then download them for free  This does not even need you to hand out a phone number or pay any money at all. Check it out      ', '    When my Nokia 7210 failed to work on me and since I d bought it just over a year ago it was beyond repairable, it was time for me to buy a new phone.As Athens was just a couple of days away  it was the perfect opportunity for me to upgrade my phone. ### User Profile Summary

**Personality Traits:**
- **Analytical Thinker:** The user demonstrates a methodical approach to evaluating products, often weighing pros and cons in detail.
- **Pragmatic:** They prioritize functionality and practicality over aesthetics, focusing on how well a product meets their needs.
- **Detail-Oriented:** The user pays attention to specific features and performance metrics, indicating a thorough evaluation style.

**Core Interests:**
- **Telecommunications:** A strong interest in mobile technology, particularly in the functionality and usability of mobile phones.
- **User Experience:** Values ease of use, intuitive interfaces, and efficient navigation in technology products.
- **Budget-Conscious Choices:** Shows a preference for cost-effective solutions that provide good value for money.

**Expression Habits/Style:**
- **Descriptive and Informative:** The user provides detailed descriptions and explanations in their reviews, often elaborating on both positive and negative aspects.
- **Balanced Perspective:** They maintain a balanced tone, acknowledging both strengths and weaknesses of products, which suggests a fair and unbiased viewpoint.

**Evaluation Priorities:**
- **Functionality:** The user prioritizes practical features such as battery life, ease of use, and connectivity options (e.g., Bluetooth, internet access).
- **Design and Usability:** They appreciate sleek designs and user-friendly interfaces, but not at the expense of functionality.
- **Performance:** Consistent performance, especially in terms of reception and reliability, is crucial for their evaluations.

**Shopping Behavior:**
- **Research-Oriented:** The user conducts thorough research before making a purchase, often comparing different models and seeking recommendations.
- **Value-Seeking:** They look for products that offer a good balance of features and price, often opting for budget-friendly options without sacrificing quality.
- **Brand Loyalty:** Shows a preference for specific brands (e.g., Sony Ericsson) based on past positive experiences, indicating a tendency towards brand loyalty.

**Aspects of Products Interested In:**
- **Camera Quality:** While not a primary concern, they do consider camera features, especially in terms of usability and quality.
- **Connectivity Features:** Strong interest in Bluetooth and other connectivity options for seamless integration with other devices.
- **User Interface:** Values intuitive menu systems and ease of navigation, indicating a preference for products that enhance user experience.

### Summary
This user profile reflects a telecommunications enthusiast who values practicality, functionality, and user experience in mobile technology. They express their opinions in a detailed and balanced manner, focusing on the performance and usability of products while being mindful of budget constraints. Their reviews suggest a strong inclination towards brands that have previously met their expectations, particularly in the realm of mobile phones.

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
The Sony Ericsson T630 stands out as a practical and budget-friendly mobile phone that delivers solid performance in key areas important to users seeking reliable functionality. Its battery life is notably impressive, lasting several days under moderate use and only showing moderate drain even with heavy Bluetooth activity, which is a significant advantage for users prioritizing endurance. The phone’s menu navigation is fast and logical, aided by an intuitive joystick that enhances overall usability—this aligns well with those who value a smooth and efficient user interface.

Reception quality is another strong point, with the T630 maintaining excellent signal strength even in locations where other phones falter, ensuring dependable connectivity. Speaking of connectivity, the inclusion of tri-band support, infrared, Bluetooth, and GPRS/WAP makes this device versatile for travel and data transfer, catering well to users who need flexible communication options.

On the downside, the phone’s limited memory—capable of storing only about 20-40 text messages and quickly filling up with photos and games—may frustrate users who require more storage capacity. The camera, while easy to use and equipped with various modes and effects, produces average-quality photos, especially in low light, and suffers from a noticeable delay between pressing the capture button and the actual photo being taken. This suggests it’s more suited for casual snapshots rather than serious photography.

Voice dialing and control features work reliably, and volume control during calls is conveniently accessible; however, the maximum call volume may be insufficient in noisy environments, which could impact call clarity in certain situations. The phone also includes standard organizer tools like calendar and alarm clock, adding to its practical appeal.

Overall, the Sony Ericsson T630 offers a well-rounded package for budget-conscious users who prioritize battery life, reception, and ease of use, though its limited memory and modest camera performance are worth considering depending on individual needs.

product_reviews: ['    Now try not to faint when I share this with you    My partner does not have a mobile phone. He s never had a mobile phone. And he must be the only adult in his 30s who doesn t know how to text. Now with a baby on the way the time has come for him to join the mobile race. After all it would be quite nice to be able to get hold of him when the time comes rather than rely on a local cab. So it could not have been a more opportune moment for the  man from T Mobile  to ring me and offer a free upgrade (worth    250 he said), so I could hand my old phone onto the other half. Now I ve never bought a phone without seeing it in the shop so it was a bit of a risk. The most important thing for me is size (I don t know why it s coming back into vogue to have a phone the size of a brick again just so you can e-mail from a field) and I do like to be able to flip the phone shut so I don t call my parents inadvertently from my bag convincing my mother she is witnessing my murder over the phone. So when the Nokia 6230i arrived I was a little disappointed to find it bigger than my previous Samsung, and no flip lid so I toyed with the idea of giving it to  him indoors  and holding onto my old one. But it only weighs 99g and when I turned it on I started appreciating all the upgrades and advances. Now, I m probably only ever going to use about 1/8 of this phones gadgets and subsections, so if you re expecting a 100  run down and regurgitation of the phone s handbook you re going to be disappointed and probably grade me as  somewhat helpful but marks off for not being very thorough . For a techie / anorak s view, please stop reading now and read the other reviews. For a  user friendly  opinion please feel free to read on. First of all the address book allows far more information to be stored, if you can be bothered to enter it all in. You can nominate a general number, home / mobile / office / fax numbers; you can pop in their e-mail address; web address; even postal address; user ID; Notes about them; and even an Image taken by your smart new photo camera in portrait mode. Add to this that in your secure  briefcase  you can enter all the details of your credit and store cards - it could be argued that you don t need to carry anything anymore apart from your trusty mobile, (and an army of personal assistants to upload all the info for you). The other feature I use regularly is texting. Not so user friendly here. I keep hitting  back  if I make a mistake and exiting in one move the whole texting area. Luckily my message is still hanging around when I return but this is getting very annoying. There s predictive text and even a complete predict the word mode. And helpfully if the phone has no idea what you re trying to type in it offers up a  spell and then Save  option allowing you to add words to the dictionary and saving you from changing from predictive text mode. There are loads of templates for you to choose from  I m late, I m busy, I m in a meeting or even  I love you too  which I guess could be useful if you re the gregarious type or a serial bigamist with no time to waste on individual texting. Now I don t really download - I m always worried how much it s going to be costing me, so I rely on a few good ring tones, something Samsung never provided making me dive for my phone to save the world from my phone s pitiful rendition of Greensleaves. The Nokia has some pleasant ring tones, 3 different simple telephone rings (bliss ), and the most gentle alarm clock to prize you from slumber in the morning. The factory settings provide you with a little bubbly noise for a text which is inoffensive. And if you re fussy there are hundreds of tones to warn or alert to choose from. Now as you may have been able to tell - I am a girl, and for your information I don t chew my fingernails. But even with a good manicure I find the keypad fiddly. God help any of you guys with big digits. The central button that controls almost all of the menu and the up / down / right / left controls are blooming difficult to use accurately. Is this handset designed for under 8s only? I m currently growing my left thumb nail for improved mobile dexterity but this layout is always going to annoy me. My other phones have had cameras - the Samsung had a camera attachment which I never bothered to keep. Technical progress has definitely helped the quality (1.3 mega pixels) but I wouldn t try to take anything too precious with this phone. There s a  night mode  but no flash. You can zoom in, use the self timer and change to video mode but for me the only useful thing about it is the comical trick of having a photo of the person who s calling come up on the phone, or of course you could attach amusing images of inanimate objects to the phone numbers of friends and family, just try not to let them find out. There s a music player so you can listen to audio files through headphones or the speakers, and a radio too - but the quality s never going to match a real radio or MP3 however much you fiddle with the equalizer. There s a little 32MB memory card that comes in the box too for extra video shooting potential. There are all the usual games, calendars, stopwatches, reminder lists etc. The battery life has 3-5 hours talk time, 150- 300 hours standby which is impressive. It charges quickly and doesn t seem to be too affected by being turned on or off to charge. There s blue tooth available if you ve got the gizmo to stick in your ear and do your best Star trek impression. s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
The Nokia 6230i stands out as a solid, practical choice for users who value reliable functionality over flashy design. Weighing just 99g and featuring a compact, business-like form, it’s easy to carry and built sturdily—though it lacks trendy flip or slide features. Network reception is generally strong, though naturally dependent on your provider, and call sound quality is good with easily adjustable volume, ensuring clear conversations.

For multimedia enthusiasts, the 6230i offers respectable features: it supports MP3 and AAC music playback, along with MP4 and 3GP video formats. The included 32MB memory card and support for upgrades mean you can store plenty of music, pictures, and videos. The 1.3-megapixel camera delivers decent photos with zoom capabilities that don’t degrade quality much, and the night mode helps in low light—though the absence of a flash limits its effectiveness after dark. Video recording is available without strict clip length limits, but expect basic quality.

Connectivity is a strong point here, with reliable Bluetooth and Infrared that don’t drain the battery excessively. Fast USB file transfers are supported, though you’ll need to source the cable separately. The user interface is straightforward and typical of Nokia’s user-friendly menus, but the keypad and central navigation button can feel fiddly, especially if you have larger fingers. Text messaging can be frustrating at times due to the ease of accidentally exiting the texting area, though predictive text and a customizable dictionary help smooth the experience.

Organizational features like a calendar, voice recorder, and an extensive address book (storing multiple numbers, emails, and notes per contact) add practical value. Customizable themes, caller ID with images, and a variety of pleasant ringtones—including a gentle alarm clock—round out the user experience nicely.

In summary, the Nokia 6230i is a dependable, feature-rich phone that delivers good value for money. It’s ideal for those who prioritize usability, solid multimedia support, and connectivity over trendiness or cutting-edge design. Just be prepared for some minor quirks in texting and navigation controls.

', '    Ok, its silver, and not much bigger than a penny chew, and flips open to reveal a dual-band phone almost identical to its predecessor the v3688. So what have those guys at Motorola been doing for the last couple of years apart from a quick respray in silver?Quite a bit, it would seem. My first ever mobile, 3 years ago was an  mr201  on Orange (a d140, to the rest of the world, I believe), and most Motorolas I d seen since then had varied very little, including my v3688 I had 2 years ago, which feature-wise was almost identical to the mr201. Not so with the new V50, which seems to have been completely redesigned on the inside.Instead of each option taking up the whole screen and you scrolling (or  wading ) through them with the arrow keys, the menus are now presented three options per screen and you scroll up and down. This is all very tasty, and the smooth scrolling between options is very posy, but not at all practical, as the scrolling is very slow, and pressing the arrow key 4 times doesn t necessary mean it will scroll 4 options down. This can cause much frustration until you discover the  Animation  option under phone set-up, and realise you can switch it off. This cures the posy  smooth scroll  on the menus, but you still get the fancy animated graphics when you make and hang up calls, and a very nice flying envelope when you send and receive text messages.Features========The familiar menu headings of the older models are still there,  Phone Book ,  Call Related Features ,  Messages ,  Phone Setup ,  Call Timers  and the like, so anyone whose used older Motorolas will find no problem finding their way around the phone.The most obvious new feature is the one on the top of the menu,  Access Internet . This leads to a WAP mini-browser. You both scroll the screen and highlight links with the left and right arrow keys, and the MENU and OK buttons get allocated functions on the bottom row of the screen, giving you four lines of text for the internet.Although fine on the whole, the browser is slow responding to keypresses, entering text can be fun as the letters don t seem to appear for a few seconds after you finish typing, then appear all in a bunch, like London buses. Bizarre. Ok if you don t type too fast. Or too often. Which at 10p a minute on most networks you probably won t be anyway...Text entry on the V50 is much improved since older models, and now has Motorola s answer to Nokia s predictive text input, which they call  iTap . (Not in the WAP browser though). As anyone whose used predictive text will know, you enter words pressing each key once; thus  STOP  would be typed 7867 and not 777786667. If more than one word matches the combination you typed, a list of possible words is shown at the bottom of the screen and you just scroll along to select the right word.Saying that, though, the dictionary doesn t have all the words you might expect in it, and although it knows some big clever words you d never use, it will fall over on some simple things. It does let you correct any hopeless guesses and enter unknown words in iTap mode by scrolling to choose the  correct  letter at any point along the word. You don t have to go into a separate  insert word  mode like on the Nokias, which is nice. As well as iTap there is a  TAP  (standard) and  numeric  mode. It also says in the manual that it automatically capitalises names from your phonebook, but it doesn t seem to do this for me  They also reckon it will learn words you enter manually on a regular basis.Text message reading is nice too, with a menu showing the first 10 or so letters of each message. You can scroll up and down these, and the selected message at any point will scroll round the first few lines of itself, making it very easy to quickly find the message you re looking for. You can also select  switch view  for the conventional message-per-screen view.The  Quick Access  menu has been improved, and provides an icon-based menu of 9 popular features, fired off by a key with a very non-descriptive arrow icon on it. You can choose and allocate the entries in the menu yourself, and can assigning them to a keypress, e.g.  ^4  for  read messages .You can also assign voice tags to commands, so you can stab the  ^  button and shout  Vibrate  and it switches vibrate mode on or off (unless you assigned the word  vibrate  to something else, of course ). Again you can choose these from a list of commands. This is also possible with entries in your phonebook so you press the middle button on the side of the phone and shout a name, and you re off  It says the name back to you before it dials, so if it gets it wrong, press the button again and it will give you its next best guess. Be warned also though that it does also shout out any names it knows when you display or scroll past that entry in the phonebook, so if you re trying to send a discrete text message from somewhere quiet, you might be best off typing in the number rather than look it up in the phone book unless you want it hollering the recipient s name out. Holding your thumb over the earpiece actually makes it louder, not quieter, which is odd Other new features include  Voicenotes  - which let you record snippets (upto a total of 3 minutes) from a live call, or just notes from the microphone. You can play these back to yourself, but not to another caller. Very handy when your caller says  have you got a pen  and you haven t This also integrates with the alarm clock, which will take 5 alarms with date and time. These can be daily, weekly, mon-fri, mon-sat, or one-off, and you can assign just an alarm, or a text reminder, or attach a voicenote which will be presented for you to play when the  alarm  goes off. I challenge anyone to sleep through the alarm. It is a very annoying beeping which sounds... like an alarm clock.Which brings me onto ringtones. The best thing i can say here is that there is a built in  music tone editor , which is just as well with the selection of tunes provided, all of which were obviously composed by a deaf chimpanzee on an out-of-tune xylophone. You can send compositions by text message between  compatible Motorola  phones, but I haven t met anyone else with one yet and it comes out as right rubbish if you send to a Nokia The weirdest part of the phone is the part in the manual which describes a calculator function with lots of features, and currency conversions and all sorts of useful things. Yet then it says,  Calculator feature may not be available in all countries . Hmm. I guess the UK is one of those where it isn t, as I have no  calculator  on my menu Finally, for any bored moment, there are three games,  Towers of Hanoi ,  Baccarat  (an odd card came I cant understand), and  Bricks  which is your classic bat n ball, which no phone should be without.Summing up==========All in all its a good phone and its odd points are far outweighed by its features and facilities, and its ability to be put in that small pocket in the front of your jeans which nothing else fits  There are a few odd quirks here and there, but no more than any other phone, and certainily nothing that gets in the way of everyday use of the phone - providing you switch off those animated smooth-scrolling menus Just as a quick aside, it is a bit of a pig to get the v50 into a carkit designed for the v3688 (as mine was, for my old phone), as the v50 has a raised  M  logo on its back cover, which sticks out and pushes the bottom of the phone forward in the cradle so it doesnt line up with the connector. Push it in and slide it down onto the connector and you re stuffed, but clip the top in and then move it slowly back till the connector lines up and you re fine. It s just a knack, and anyone with a carkit will soon find out how to do this.     ', '    A little while ago I owned a Motorola StarTac 85 and I was very pleased with it.  However I d had it for just under 12 months when I experienced problems with charging. ', '    The phone thats small, stylish and sexy, but is it all that its supposed to be? I can t really say its very bad but it is in a league of its own. ', '    I have had my phone for over a year and a half now. I bought it to replace my ericson mobile which was stolen. I chose it because it looked stylish and was very small and light and had was a flip-top phone. It is also WAP enabled.Although a great looking phone, I had hoped that its functions were as good as it looked. Phone sales people are anything but helpful. I was assured that it was a great phone, but truthfully it was just a standard phone.The phone comes in two colours silver and blue, although the shop only had silver available. However I have also seen a black phone. The black phone was an older version and not WAP enanbled.The phone is extreemly light, very stylish and rather pretty. I think it makes an excellent phone for women. It does need alot of TLC, as it can get damaged rather easily. I dropped it while playing with it at table, onto the table and it picked up a dent from that small fall. If you drop it onto the floor, chances are that the back opens and the battery falls. Cannot be too good for the phone. Everytime you drop it, the phone will have a scar or two to remind you how clumsy you are. DO NOT BUY THIS PHONE if you ill-treat your phone. DO NOT keep this phone in your pocket with other things, as it will get scratched. Scratches on this phone look awful, and if like me you bought it to look stylish, it will soon be redundant to you  I take lots of care of my phone, but like an normal user have dropped it a couple of times. A year and a half on, it looks really scruffy. I get upset about it, because my brothers phone (ERICSON), which is around 3 years old still looks brand new. Towers of Hanoi, Baccarat and Bricks. Not excellent games, but if you really have nothing to do, will occupy you for a few minutes The phone is a dual band phone. I wish I could explain it further but I cannot. I do think that it means it is suitable for roaming around the world except for the states, where you need a tri-band phone.The phone also has a network selection. If you are not tied in with a contract, you can pick and chose the cheapest provider. However, I do not know anyone who is not somehow tied in the UK. It makes sense when travelling overseas to see who is the cheaper provider and use them to keep costs down.The battery seems to last for ages. You can easily do 5 days on standby. And it can easily last a couple of hours on talktime. However, it goes down to the last bar rather quickly, but then can last for another 2 days  So there is no need to panic just because your battery  is on the last bar.Call meters.You have a minute beep, which I find useful so that I can make sure my bills do not get too high. It reminds me that I have been chatting for ages.You can find out how long you were on your last call, and also on your total calls. These can be reset. Great if you have one tariff and want to keep track that you are being billed correctly. There is even a lifetime timer. How good is that It has an alarm clock, which is really great. You can set several alarms. You can even set them to go off daily, one off or when and as you wish. You can even have a message attached, so when the alarm rings, you remember why you set the alarm in the first place. Great for remembering meetings. You can even set it by date for some time in the future.Volume control. You have volume control over the level of the call, which is great when you have low voiced speakers as you can raise to volume to hear without having to ask them to raise their voice and repeat. You can also lower when someone is shouting so it does not hurt your ears.You also have control over the ringer. If like me, you keep losing your phone (and with this one its easy due to its size), keeping it on high means you will find it time and again. A note of caution, high is actually much higher than most mobiles, and can be rather attention grabbing if it rings somewhere quiet. Although you can chose your ringer volume, you cannot have the volume increase slowly as in some other phones. Nor can you have vibrate and ring tone simulatenously. Ideally my phone will first vibrate, then whilst vibrating begin to ring louder and louder with every ring. Its a pity this cannot do that A weekness of this phone is the flip-top part of it. If you drop it a few times, there is a join which breaks. This quickly deteriorates the stableness of the phone. This has not happened to my phone, but it has to a couple of my friends who also have the phone. BE CAREFUL.There are short cuts on the phone, but i have found the short cut to not really be a short cut so use the full method. I believe, one can also have quick dial buttons but as you will need to rely on memory as to which ones you actually programmed, I do not use it There are a few other features, but I am not very aware of them and really hardly use them. But the above mentioned are the most common and frequently used features.On the whole, it is very useful as a phone. It does not have all the extras that say a NOKIA may have, but it does its job as a phone very well. Its not a great phone for texting (except for compiling), it can get rather scruffy but as a phone I just cannot complain. However, despite what I just said, next time I think I ll go for a different phone as my previous phones did alot more, and stay very presentable.     ', '    The V50 by Motorola is a fantastic phone. Although it may not have as many glitzy features as other phones, it serves its purpose well. It is an update of the V3690 and it is availiable in silver or dark blue. Depending on your contract, you can get it for a range of prices, up to no more than    149. It is not availiable on pay as you go - or so I believe. The V50 has WAP capabilities, and although I don t use this feature, it may prove useful to others. Similarly, I choose not to use the ringtone composer as a wide range of tones are pre-set. However, you can easily make up your own or download them from the internet. Texting people is very easy and Motorola have improved on their previous model by allowing the user to see who has sent the text - it s frustrating not being able to see. You have a choice of predictive text or standard input. Having got used to the predictive text, I find this the easier setting.Games are also a new feature. They re fun or a while - one of those novelties which gradually wear off. But the games on the V50 are much more fun than on other phones  The signal you recieve it comparitive to others. And the reception is good. The battery lasts for about 3 days if you use it occasionally every day but it obviously varies with your use. It take about an hour and a bit to charge from empty to full power.In such a small phone from the outside, you would think the screen would be small. This is not the case and the text is very clear. I was surprised at how easy it was to read  The buttons are average size too, although the size of the phone is downsized, the features within the phone itself are still a good size.The phone is small and very light. A definate bonus. Also, it is extremly scratch resistant and seems to surivive a few knocks and bumps here and there If you buy a motorola phone and something goes wrong (my microphone speaker temporarily stopped working - a real nusicance) then the customer survice you recieve is excellent. You phone up the company, explain the problem and give the a few numbers from the back of the phone. Hey presto  The next day, a courier picks up your phone and when it has been checked and fixed (free of charge) it is returned to you by special delivery  I was amazed at their helpfulness. Definattly a thing to remember when buying a new phone.     ', '    A couple of weeks ago I decided to upgrade my ageing Nokia 7110 to a Motorola V50.It took time but now ive realised that this was a good descision. At first when you start to use the V50 it seems very fiddily, especially compared to the 7110 I had been using. The message writing method seem to take forever, however with time it became second nature.The phone has a host of features which amazed me as I started looking through the brick of a handbook that came with the phone. The phone has a three min dictaphone which allows you to record snipits of converstations or from moments of inspiration. The phone also has a huge capacity for storing all those phone numbers plus a voice recognition system for dialing your family and friends.The V50 also comes with three games which are : Bricks, Baccarat and Tower of Hanoi, with the latter being my favourite.Obviously the thing which I think drew me to the phone in the first place was its size and design. The slick silver design is just perfect for all those posers out there and its tiny size means you totally forget its in your pocket (now dont loose it )I have found the reception quality and the standby of the battery to be of good quality and average length respectivley.So over all i am very happy with the purchase of my phone, however it did take me a week or so to get used to its small size after I had been used to the chunkier Nokia.     ']

s5_annotated_personalized_summaries:
The Motorola V50 stands out as a compact and stylish flip phone, available in sleek silver and blue, which will appeal to those who prioritize design and portability. Its small size is complemented by a surprisingly large screen and buttons, making it easier to handle than one might expect. The phone’s build quality is solid, featuring a chunky aerial that some users find reassuringly sturdy, and its durability is notable—it resists scratches well, which is a definite plus for anyone rough on their devices.

Functionally, the V50 covers the basics well. It stores up to 100 contacts in its memory plus another 100 on the SIM card, and it keeps a call log for the last 10 calls in each category. However, the missed call tracking can be unreliable, which might frustrate users who rely on accurate call history. The phone also offers voice dialing and voice notes, though voice dialing demands precise pronunciation to work effectively.

On the downside, texting on the V50 is less intuitive compared to Nokia phones. The menu navigation is cumbersome, requiring multiple steps to access messages, and the space input feels awkward. While it supports predictive text (iTap), this feature can be hit-or-miss, especially with unusual words, which may slow down typing rather than speed it up. The phone lacks the richer feature set found in competitors, missing out on diverse ringtones and fun extras.

Internet access via WAP is available but slow and potentially costly, so it’s best seen as a basic option rather than a highlight. Volume controls are straightforward, though you can’t have vibrate and ringtone active simultaneously, which limits discreet use options despite the presence of a vibrate function.

Overall, the Motorola V50 is a practical choice for users who want a stylish, durable, and affordable phone focused on essential calling and basic texting. If you’re after advanced features or seamless messaging, you might find it lacking, but for straightforward use with a touch of flair, it holds its own.

', '    Having recently been on my first fly-drive holiday to the U.S.A.  I was interested to see what quality of vacation I would have driving around America instead of flying. ', '    After a last minute visit to friends in the US was arranged, it was quickly decided that I would need some form of transport when I got there, as the US is rather big  So I jumped on Google and started checking out car rental companies. Those of you that have found yourselves in a similar situation will be aware that there are rather a lot of rental companies out there, fortunately I was spared the agony of deciding between Thrifty, Alamo, Hertz, Avis et al by one deciding factor   . My age  Very few car rental companies in the US will rent to anyone under the age of 25, and only one of these had an office in Providence, Rhode Island. So it was that I became a customer of Dollar Rent A Car.THE WEBSITE and MAKING A RESERVATIONThis will most likely be your first point of contact with Dollar so they want to make a good impression right? Well, yes actually  The site is nicely laid out, with the  Rates and Reservations  screen displayed by default. From here you can select your pickup and if different, drop-off, point. Although I am reviewing my experience with Dollar in the United States, it is worth knowing that they do have sites throughout the world in a good selection of locations.Anyway, once you have chosen your location(s) you then select your dates, times and car type. In the USA, you are given the choice of Economy, Compact, Intermediate, Full Size, Premium and Luxury cars with Economy cars at the lower end of the market - think Hyundai Accent etc, moving up to Luxury cars such as Daimler-Chryslers mighty 300C. As expected Economy cars are the cheapest option at around  20 (   12) a day + fees and taxes moving way up the scale to  250 (   145) a day + fees for a Luxury vehicle.Also available are Minivans, Convertibles and SUV s, all at a higher rate than a standard car.A box on the right hand side of the screen shows you the cost of your choice including fees and taxes, and a link is available to display a comprehensive breakdown of said fees.Below this box is a link titled Important Local Policy Information, which I would strongly suggest you check out as it contains all sorts of useful information about driving restrictions and other terms and conditions   it was here and only here that I found out about the  30 a day surcharge for 21-24 year old drivers When you are happy with your selections, click proceed to continue. You will then be asked for your name, phone number and email, but not a credit or debit card at this point. Once you have provided your details, you are ready to make your reservation by clicking the green  Reserve Now  button. You are then given your confirmation number and rate breakdown and details of your itinerary are emailed to you. I would suggest you print a copy of this and take it with you, just in case.THE PICKUPArriving at Providence Airport, I was directed toward the Dollar rental office by the main entrance (not all offices are located within the airport building, check before you leave ) a friendly and efficient clerk asked for my name and confirmed my reservation - I didn t need my printed copy but better safe than sorry - I was then asked for my Driving Licence and credit card which I duly provided. At this point, the clerk asked if I would consider an upgrade from an Economy to a Compact, which I declined as I was on a tight budget as it was  Having confirmed all my details, the clerk got on her 2 way radio and asked for a Hyundai Accent to be made ready for me. A garbled response came back followed by a lengthy pause during which many buttons were pressed on my clerks computer   it turned out there were no cars suiting my needs available. I was not best pleased to say the least, but I was swiftly placated by a free upgrade to a Compact Dodge Neon, coincidentally the car my mother owns in the UK  Having confirmed there was a Dodge Neon available, I was then offered the  Gold  insurance package, covering me against every possible eventuality including uninsured drivers. I would have liked to have taken this but at  49 a day it was beyond my means. I was then offered the  Silver  package which wasn t so comprehensive but still covered me for collision damage. At  25 a day this was still beyond my pathetic budget so I had to take the  11 a day  Liability  insurance. This is mandatory in the US and is equivalent to our Third Party Only cover. This meant that if anything were to happen to the car, I would be liable and would have to pay a  350 excess, fair dinkum, I d just better be careful. At this point I was also advised that I would be charged a fuel surcharge of  40 but this would be deducted if I returned the car with a full tank of  gas . My card was then swiped on a manual card machine (one which takes a physical copy of the card on a sales voucher rather than electronically.) This is because your account is not debited until you return the car and an inspection is made.Paperwork signed off, the clerk told me to wait outside the airport where I would be met by a driver. After 10 minutes waiting, with no sign of my blue Dodge, I went back inside to ask what was occurring, only to find out  was being met by a bus driver who would take me to the Dollar Rental lot and office. How stupid did I feel  Stepping back outside I now got on the bright yellow Dollar bus I had somehow failed to notice  After a couple of minutes drive I was dropped off at the Dollar sales office proper. Handing the clerk my paperwork, I was given the keys  and a map of the local area and left to get on with it Getting into the car my first thought was  Right, where s the steering wheel gone  Getting into the correct side of the vehicle enlightened me somewhat and I had a look round to get myself familiar with things. Fortunately I knew where everything was as my mum s car was pretty much exactly the same, albeit with the steering wheel on the proper side  This car was an  05 model 2.0 Auto in metallic blue and was spotlessly clean inside. There were a few marks on the bodywork but I had been assured that they had already been noted and I wasn t going to get the blame for them Setting off proved to be a bit of an adventure - I kept looking for the rear view mirror above my left shoulder instead of my right and kept opening the door instead of pulling up the handbrake  Driving on the left also took some getting used to, especially at the first junction when I totally forgot what way the traffic would be coming from and ended up looking both ways about 20 times to be sure the road was clear, god knows what I must have looked like  After the first drive on alien territory, things started to fall into place, and it started to feel natural being on the wrong side of the car, on the wrong side of the road I had the car for a week, and in that time put over 500 miles on it. Not a massive amount I know, but for my first time it was enough  THE DROP OFFAfter a thoroughly enjoyable week tooling around in this nippy auto it was time to take the car back to Dollar. At some point in the week a largish gouge had appeared on the rear bumper of the car so I was freaking out, expecting a  350 bill on top of my  560 rental charge. When I returned the car I reversed into a parking space, went into the office and gave the clerk behind the desk my mileage, fuel report (full tank) and the keys. He smiled nicely, accepted the paperwork and printed off my receipt   for  560  I made no mention of the damage, and he didn t ask. Result  The big yellow bus was waiting outside to take me back to the airport and I hopped aboard. The driver pulled away, only for me to yell at him to Stop  I had left my luggage in the  trunk  of the car  Running back to the office, I was dismayed to find the car gone already. Explaining my predicament to the smiling clerk, I was told to wait at the far end of the car park by a roller door. This was raised and there was  my  car, already washed and dried  The valeter popped the  trunk  and I reclaimed my baggage, all too aware of the gouge in the now very shiny bumper. Still no mention was made and I was free to get back on the bus. Somehow I had gotten away with it. Either they didn t care that much, or they weren t aware of the condition of the car before I took it. Whatever the explanation, I was one happy bunny CONCLUSIONAll in all, I had a very enjoyable experience with Dollar, the staff were friendly and efficient, the choice of cars was very good and the booking process was hassle free, with no hidden costs other than the insurance which I should have expected. Definitely recommended for everyone, especially younger drivers.     ', '     I have used Dollar Car Rental twice now and have had absolutely no problems whatsoever.The first time was back in 2000. We were heading to the States to do a road trip and I was looking for a three week rental that wasn   t going to charge the earth. On all my searches, Dollar came up consistently cheaper than the other nationwide companies. Sure there were heaps of cheaper options but I wanted to steer clear of the mum and pop type deals so only concentrated on nationwide companies.                                                   I booked an economy car, unlimited miles  over the net using the Dollar website and while there, noted a coupon promising me an upgrade. I printed it off and tucked it in with all my travel papers.We arrived at LAX very early morning after a tedious long haul from New Zealand and found our way to the free-phone to the Dollar depot. They said to wait out front and the shuttle bus would be along soon to pick us up. We seemed to wait for quite awhile but eventually we spied the Dollar shuttle and signaled to the driver. We jumped on board and off we went to the depot.We were the only customers at that early hour so we were dealt with promptly and courteously. I remembered my upgrade coupon and pulled out the page I had printed off, this was accepted without a word and we were upgraded to a compact car.We asked directions to our booked accommodation and the attendant printed off a map for us showing us exactly which route to take     such service We were pointed in the general direction of the garage and told where our car would be. We found it okay but had an initial moment when we discovered it was locked     after a while it dawned on us that we were trying the passenger door and the keys were in the ignition, ready and waiting on opposite side of the car   The car was spotlessly clean and we jumped in, with map and hand and headed off for three weeks of fun and adventure. Driving on the right took a little bit of getting used to, sorting out the indicator lights from the windsceen wipers took a bit of effort but it all clicked in the end. One essential piece of advice we received was to remember this catchy saying to remind us which side of the road to stay on .... Loose Left, Tight Right. This helped immensely in the early daysd of our trip.We drove over 4000 miles without a hitch, the car caused us no problems whatsoever and apart from giving us some electric shocks when we were in the hot desert regions, we had no complaints.The feature I like the most about the car ( a Dodge Stratus) was the automatic locking system. A few minutes after getting into the car, all the doors would automatically snap locked if we hadn   t locked them ourselves, a great safety feature I thought, especially with the back doors in mind.Returning the car was a breeze; we pulled up to the depot and followed the signs for the returning vehicles. We were directed to the place to stop by a worker who immediately looked over the car, we were given the all clear and the car was driven to where there was another group cleaning and grooming all the latest returned cars.Easy We signed off the credit card payment in the office and then took the free shuttle bus to LAX for our flight home.The bill for the 3 weeks came to  1800 (NZ) which was pretty reasonable considering the appalling exchange rate at the time.  1 (NZ) was only worth about .40c (US) so it wasn   t a bad rate. This included all the insurance coverage which we took as well, we made sure to take the works as we didn   t fancy being sued if something went wrong.                   ====================The second Dollar experience was just as satisfactory. We were in Waikiki, Hawaii on a five night holiday and decided we wanted to rent a car for a few days to get around the island a bit. We came across the Dollar Car Rental yard and headed on in straight off the street. There were a few cars on the lot ranging from small cars to 4x4 jeeps . We booked an economy and were given yet another dodge. I can   t quite remember the model we got this time round but it was about the same size as the Stratus. A small 4 door sedan, automatic and a cinch to drive.Once again, the attendant didn   t bother going over the car at all, just pointed us to the car and off we went.Returning the car was again simple, we were directed to the washing area, a guy gave the car the once over and we went to the office booth to sign off on the credit card.The bill was  216.60 (US) for the three days, once again with the full complement of insurance. You never can be too sure when in the States I guess. This came to  386.43 (NZ), the exchange rate was slightly kinder to us this time around as our dollar was worth about .66c (US)                                   *** Overall ***I wouldn   t hesitate to recommend Dollar Car Rental to anyone and would use them again without question.No problems with either of the cars we had, they were both spotlessly clean and ran well. The service was good both times. The front desk folk were friendly and efficient at doing their job. We missed the opportunity to get a discount in Waikiki via a coupon in one of the many tourist giveaway brochures and booklets. I hadn   t bothered looking through them till we got home     silly I know but there you go     I will know better next time.Website ... www.dollar.com     ', '    I have to say that when in Florida I have always used Dollar Car Rentals, usually opting for the Airport Pick up and Drop off...We ve used them at Tampa, Orlando and Kissimee..Everyone hates paying those extras, and that   including free car hire  that we keep getting thrown down our necks everytime we pick up a Florida Brochure is very misleading until you ve read the small and smaller print..On average a Family of say four people will pay around    400 for a two week car hire on top of their holiday price, and that is for an intermediate sized car or midsize, don t forget in the USA they may have bigger everything except for the Boot..you will get your car it will probably have a big engine, and you will have been told that it is a four or five person car..I bet you wont get 4 or 5 peoples luggage in the boot..it is always worth considering an upgrade, sure it will cost you more, but in the end for two weeks it will  be more comfortable..Dollar make things very easy and they have always thus far helped us as much as we have ever needed a helping hand, we prefer Dollar and always hold out when offered an upgrade ( usually because we have booked the car we need) .. One of the favourite tricks in Florida is to try and get the passenger to upgrade to a slightly better car...this is often done even if they do not have the car you originally booked, because if you agree to upgrade they can get more money out of you, however, if you say no thanks I prefer the car we have already paid for..then the chances are you will be given a bigger and better car at no extra cost, if they don t have your original vehicle in stock and believe me it happens quite frequently..so stick to your guns and hold out...you can always upgrade your car after a day or two, if you want to pay for it   ..Most of all enjoy you holiday ..Florida is a great place to drive...and the people are friendly...     ', '    This is not a review it is our experience with dollar car hire.Some people like to rent a car when they are on holiday and recently I have been on holiday in California (I actually wrote this review in California but I forgot to type it up.) so when we got to California we decided to rent - a - car from a place called Dollar rent a car, we had been traveling for over 48 hours already (from Liverpool to Heathrow and to LA.) But before we went my Mum had booked a car for 50.80 pounds that was not including insurances. When we had arrived at dollar hire head quarters in LA we had brought a slip of confirmation this showed basically that she had paid for the car over the internet. When we got there she asked for a quote on how much the car and all the insurances would come to, after all of everything it came to about  420 which is about equivalent of about 210 pounds these was with insurances these covered all sorts of things really:  149; If you got hit by another car  149; If an uninsured car hits you.  149; If you kill someone (In an accident)  149; If your car gets stolenBut the person in dollar car hire who was serving us didn t give us much option about which insurances to take and practically forced us to go for the more expensive one so we had to pay for that  So after that eventually we got the car and we was on our way to the hotel.One week later my Dad arrived in LA so it was back of to the dollar car hire place to get him insured to drive the car. Once we had explained to him about the amount of money we had to pay for our insurances he had a bit of a row and cancelled a few of them off. So our purpose of going back is to get my Dad insured to drive the car BUT oh no we have to get a new contract because you cannot add people on to the contract which is fair (I suppose.) Eventually after all that they said that we hadn t paid for the car which set off a big argument you may think that we had the confirmation slip but we gave that in. So we had to dig out another  420 dollars and after that we were so tired and just agreed with them.As I had mentioned at the start this is not a review of dollar car hire but just our experience in conclusion we think dollar car hire are one of the worst companies.Thanks for reading     ste231191     ', '    Last week a colleague and I were sent to Boston on business and my company arranged for us to collect a rental car at the airport. They chose to use Dollar, a company I d never heard of before.Things started well, the courtesy shuttle bus was easy to find, they helped us on with our luggage, and dropped us at the office. There we received the all American, over the top, polite and friendly greeting, and proceded to state our business. They immediately located the booking, and printed out the rental agreement for me to sign. No problems so far, up to this point I was impressed with the efficiency.After signing all the necessary, we were told where to find the car, and off we went. This is the first time I have rented a car in the US, but I was a little concerned that they hadn t carried out the pre-drive away check, that other rental firms do, where they make a note of any existing dents and scratches and both parties sign. This caused me to look at the car in horror as we approached it. I don t know who d had the car in the past, but I think they may have entered a demolition derby  OK so that is an exaggeration, but it would have taken considerable time to mark them all down on a diagram of the vehicle. Then we spotted the tyres, two of which were practically bald  It would have been dangerous to drive and we returned to the office to request another car.The car was replaced and on initial inspection everything seemed ok. Off we went, still amazed that they would try and rent us such an unroadworthy vehicle, but happy that this car was in better nick - until a light came on in the dashboard later that day. It was not immediately obvious what the light was for, but it was clearly a warning as the word  check  appeared under it. We popped into a gas station and the chap there thought it was probably low on coolant, but after topping that up (it was very low) the light did not go out, so it was back to Dollar to request yet another car.They were always very helpful, and even gave a free upgrade to a better class of car, in view of all the problems, but my concern is that they obviously do not check the condition of the vehicles before they rent them out. The car we ended up with was practically brand new, only 300 miles on the clock, so we felt fairly confident that we were safe, but I shudder to think what may have happened, had we accepted the first car. At best, a fine from the traffic cops for an unroadworthy vehicle, at worst, I may not have been writing this op.     ']

', '    Independance hall is located in the Independence National Historical Park which is part of the Old Arts district and sometimes referred to as centre city, (The skyline of centre city itself closely resembles Canary Wharf in London s East End).At the park which is set in some 45 acres you can see the Liberty Bell exhibit, and Independence Hall,  where both the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution were created, (Also one of the scenes in the recent movie  National Treasure  with Nicholas Cage).The park also depicts the events and the lives of the population during the years when Philadelphia was the capital city of the United States around 1790 to 1800 (I think). ', '    Manikata - A small country village in MaltaManikata is a small typical Maltese village. The main industry of Manikata is farming. The music isn t too loud and plays mainly in the public bar.  there are entertainment machines but they are unobtrusive.  http://www.redlionswanage.co.uk/     ', '       **** What is Earthwatch? ****Earthwatch is a diverse community of scientists and volunteers who work together to promote worldwide conservation through research. Earthwatch was founded in Boston in 1971 and there are now offices in the United States, England, Australia, and Japan, in addition to 20,000 global members, 4,000 eager volunteers each year, 50 collaborating conservation organisations, and 50 corporate partners. **** My Project ****In the Summer of 2001 I travelled to Washington State and to a city called Ellensbugh. Here you can find Fashion, Electrical, Household, Perfume and           Pictures of The Oracle, Reading     ', '    As you probably all know I have not long returned from holiday.After browsing the internet for a cheap deal,we finally decided on Kos,Kefalos in particular,as it was stated to be a quieter part of the island.So after a bit of pondering we booked it through Thomson.co.uk.The few weeks soon passed and we were whisked away to the airport,as chauferred by my Dad.Luckily for us there were no delays and our flight departed on time from the glorious Luton airport.Goodbye Cloudy old England..as we flew into the sunset.By this point I was so excited I was almost at exploding point.Not only do i love flying,and insist on getting as drunk as I can whilst on board,but I just love travelling.I am like a wide eyed five year old,its just always new and exciting for me.Anyway,after the luggage carousel breaking down twice ,and the little Greek man coming out and swearing at it,we were hearded onto our tourist buses and taken to our designated resorts.The transfer to the Zeus is roughly fifteen minutes from the airport.So no long bus journey which was really nice.We then arrived at the hotel at 2:30am local time.We were greeted by a happy smiling face,given our key,and we then proceeded to our room.So what then did we do next? If you’re a budget-savvy traveler like me, Dollar Rent A Car Worldwide often stands out with consistently lower prices compared to other nationwide rental companies—definitely a win when you want to stretch your travel funds without sacrificing coverage. Their nationwide presence means you can pick up and drop off almost anywhere, which is super convenient for spontaneous road trips or multi-city adventures.

That said, here’s the practical scoop: Dollar’s vehicle condition can be a bit of a mixed bag. Some cars arrive spotless, comfy, and with all the expected extras like working air conditioning—perfect for those long drives through scenic routes. But others might show signs of wear or maintenance issues, so it’s crucial to channel your inner detective and thoroughly inspect the car before driving off. Make sure to document any scratches or dents upfront; otherwise, you might end up in a “he said, she said” over damage later.

The staff at Dollar generally bring a friendly and efficient vibe to the pick-up and drop-off process, which helps smooth out the experience. Plus, if your reserved car isn’t available, they sometimes throw in free upgrades—nice little surprises that can make your trip feel a bit more special.

On the flip side, watch out for the upselling tactics at the counter. Dollar tends to push insurance packages and car upgrades, which can quickly inflate your total cost if you’re not careful. It’s worth weighing these extras against your own travel insurance or credit card coverage to avoid paying more than necessary.

Returning the car is usually hassle-free and quick, with efficient processing and cleaning, so you can get back to your adventures without delay.

In summary, Dollar is a solid pick for travelers who prioritize value and nationwide access, but a sharp eye and a bit of patience will help you dodge the occasional vehicle hiccup and upsell trap. Happy travels!
